Ryco performance research — re-check

2026-10-15 · all 263 findings of the 2026-10-11 report (written against f1be4abc7) re-checked against Ryco ec250e386 and ryco-hub origin/main 5f656ad · one auditor (Sonnet) and one adversarial verifier (Opus) per finding · read-only

SummaryBy scenarioRegressions and defectsOpen workImplementation planImplementation resultsNeeds a decisionAll findingsMethod

Summary

Most of the original report has shipped. Of 263 findings, 169 are fully done, 86 are partly done and 8 are not done. The work landed in Ryco #710, #714 and #715 and ryco-hub #163, which also pins the hosted client to the #715 merge.

The verifiers were deliberately adversarial: they corrected 64 of the 263 first-pass audits and moved 37 findings from done to partial, mostly because a fix missed a second caller, a mobile path or a proposal part. They also found 7 serious defects introduced or exposed by the shipped fixes, listed below. The most important: Claude has not been receiving Ryco's system-prompt additions at all; the reused composer shares one undo stack across threads; frame batching can cut assistant text; and a Stop during the pre-turn baseline wait no longer cancels the turn.

Of the 94 open findings, 4 are high value, 38 medium and 52 low. 32 need a product, security or cross-repo decision (E2EE and relay protocol, hosted lifecycle ownership, Hub changes); their safe, no-decision parts are scheduled anyway. The implementation plan groups everything else into 19 work packages.

Regressions and defects in shipped fixes

Found by the adversarial verifiers while checking fixes marked done. Severity is our assessment. Each is scheduled in the work package shown unless marked as a decision.

SeverityProblemFindingPlan
seriousClaude never receives Ryco's system-prompt additions. ClaudeAdapter passes them as a top-level appendSystemPrompt; Claude Agent SDK 0.3.296 only reads systemPrompt.append (checked in sdk.mjs). Since #710 that drops the attachment-delivery instructions, and it has always dropped the project custom system prompt and token-mode instructions. ClaudeAdapter.test.ts asserts the wrong field.#140 #143WP01
seriousThe composer editor is now reused across thread switches with one Lexical undo stack. After switching A→B, Cmd+Z in B restores A's prompt and persists it as B's draft, so A's text can be sent to B's agent. Send continuations that finish after a switch can also mark the newly shown thread busy or roll back into it.#128WP10
seriousFrame-batched detail events: coalesceOrchestrationUiEvents can cut assistant message text when a streaming delta and an empty-text completion of the same message land in one frame.#119WP11WP14A
seriousA Stop pressed while the turn start waits for the pre-turn checkpoint baseline (up to 5 s) no longer cancels the start; the turn runs anyway. The baseline-timeout activity is also filtered out of the work log.#144WP02
seriousEvent-driven history recovery no longer repairs a dropped turn.completed on a live runtime while the thread stays open; the turn stays "running".#254WP02
seriousA prewarmed provider session can be claimed by a computer-use turn that needs to start with the computer plan staged.#141WP02WP10WP14A
seriousHosted Hub CSP forbids WebAssembly, but diff workers now select the Shiki WASM engine there; the workers fail to start and highlighting falls back to the main thread.#153WP13
warningSplit draft storage: with two tabs open, one tab's index write can drop the other tab's new draft; it is lost on reload (and swept by the next boot).#88WP10
warningStatistics client cache is not scoped by environment: after a hosted node switch or in-page account switch, Activity shows the previous node's/account's data until the new one answers (forever if it fails).#184WP06
warningA transient repository-identity probe failure (1 s timeout, spawn error) is persisted as "no repository" for up to 24 h across restarts, and clients regroup the project.#201 #44WP05
warningProject skills: a probe timeout/failure is cached as a successful empty list, replacing a good list.#179WP01
warningProject icons disappear after the icon TTL or LRU eviction and only come back on reconnect or remount (web and mobile).#245WP12AWP14B
warningShutdown fallback closeAllConnections() does not close upgraded WebSockets, so a peer that never answers the 1001 close still holds shutdown open.#32WP03
warningHosted boot gate awaits HostedHubRoot (and the RootAppShell graph) even on /pair and /native/authorize, which render only an outlet.#213WP12B
warningLocal-changes review: the batched intent-to-add can replace a tracked temp-index entry when a path changed between file and directory.#159WP07A
warning/ws/device-frames negotiates permessage-deflate although the device-frame code says it must not.#117WP03decision
warningStatistics stale-while-revalidate: a race can leave the background-refresh marker set, so later opens never refresh.#47WP06
warningHub read-cache publisher can upload thread bodies the bounded index does not list; the Hub rejects them with 409.#56WP05
warningAn empty git worktree list answer (git failed) is cached under a valid fingerprint.#43 #106 #202WP05
warningThe relay-ticket minor-version fallback memo never resets for the lifetime of the client.#225WP15
warningAn agent's request to open a device pane is lost when the user is not viewing that thread at the time.#110 #96WP15
warningWith Agent Control disabled, the automations badge still opens a refused subscription; turning Agent Control on later does not reopen it until reload.#101WP12A
minorMissing server entry or bootstrap pipe still restarts forever behind the splash (skips the failure policy).#0WP04
minorOld rotated logs .7–.10 (from the former maxFiles=10) are never pruned, up to 80 MiB.#258WP04
minorMCP settings: the refreshing state can stick when a mutation lands during a load.#187WP12A
minorOpening the Statistics Limits view fetches the Activity statistics snapshot it does not show.#191WP06
minorMobile Thread route prewarm is a no-op since inline requires were enabled.#238WP14B
minorSome lazy dialogs and the PR Files tab have no load-error path; a failed chunk throws.#60 #186WP12B
decisionTurn-start lease handoff skips the admission check against a pending project relocation (deliberate and tested; needs owner confirmation).#148decision
decisionHosted connectionRecovered arms the 30 s session-sync deadline while the directory is stale (inside the hosted lifecycle owner).#212decision

Implementation plan

Each work package runs in its own detached worktree at the base commit. An Opus implementer works from the verified finding (evidence, remaining work, implementation sketch) and adds tests. An independent Opus verifier then reviews the diff adversarially and re-runs the checks, and the implementer fixes what the verifier confirms. The packages are then merged onto one branch, conflicts are resolved, and the full repository backstop runs (bun fmt, fmt:check, lint, typecheck, bun run test, build, the web browser suite, build:desktop), because the change set is cross-cutting. Nothing is pushed.

Rules for every package: fix the root cause in the shared module rather than adding local workarounds; keep hosted lifecycle ownership, E2EE and auth semantics unchanged; do not extend the frozen web phone tier; never weaken an existing test to make a change pass.

Implementation results

All 19 packages were merged onto one tree (local branch perf3/recheck-2026-10-15, 20 commits, 553 files) and validated together. 5 files needed manual merge resolution; an independent review of every file touched by two packages found no interaction bugs; a final verifier pass against this plan returned APPROVED on all five acceptance criteria.

CheckResult
bun run fmt:checkpass
bun run lintpass (0 errors; 779 warnings vs 786 on main)
bun run typecheck (all packages)pass
bun run test (16 packages, 8,281 tests)pass (one shutdown test needed bun install to re-apply the changed @effect/platform-node patch)
bun run buildpass
web browser suitepass, 245/245 files (a known order-dependent ContextPickerButton flake passed on rerun; one new test had a wrong baseline and was fixed)
bun run build:desktoppass
release:smokenot run (no release-workflow change)
merge with current origin/main (#729)clean

Behaviour changes worth knowing

  • Claude now receives Ryco's appended system prompt (attachment instructions, project custom system prompt, token-mode instructions) through systemPrompt.append; it previously received none of it.
  • Adopted Claude/OpenCode provider snapshots stay valid for 6 h; their usage limits are still re-read every 5 minutes, but without starting a Claude SDK session or opencode serve. Codex is unchanged.
  • A Stop pressed while a turn waits for its pre-turn checkpoint now cancels the start; a lost turn.completed is repaired by a bounded, liveness-triggered history read while the thread stays open.
  • The server keeps the idle provider sessions of up to 4 viewed threads for up to 30 minutes; unviewed threads keep the 5-minute reaper, and a session is re-checked for an active turn right before it is stopped.
  • Desktop: a missing server entry or bootstrap pipe stops after 3 failed starts and shows the error dialog instead of retrying forever; the renderer origin port is recorded in userData right after selection.
  • The live command model keeps only the activity kinds it reads and no checkpoint file lists; after a restart a pending checkpoint revert blocks turn starts until it is recovered, as it already did while running.
  • A failed or timed-out project-skills read keeps the last good list and retries after 30 s instead of caching an empty list.
  • Terminal history is persisted append-only (full rewrite only on clear, restart, close or compaction). Subprocess activity checks no longer run every second during output: Linux reads /proc without spawning; macOS and Windows still spawn ps/PowerShell, but only on edges and the 5 s idle sweep (foreground-process detection was not possible through node-pty).
  • The tiny-chunk merge (#61) was measured and rejected: every variant regressed the RootAppShell gzip budget or file count; only the guard shipped.
  • Existing checkouts need bun install after pulling, because the @effect/platform-node patch content changed.

Desktop cold boot (17)

Done#0 Deterministic backend start failures are retried forever while the window stays on the splash (reliability bug)

desktop-boot:backend-fatal-crash-loop · original impact High, effort S · Reliability WP04

Current state

Confirmed DONE (60633eff3, #710). The scenario from the finding now stops. A downgraded binary meets a newer DB, fails migrations with Migrator.MigrationError kind BadState, and the error reaches cliMain unwrapped through Sqlite setup and Layer.launch. cliMain classifies it, prints one line, writes {type:'fatal',code,message} on fd 4 and sets process.exitCode = 78. NodeRuntime's default teardown leaves a successful exit alone, so 78 survives. The desktop halts at once on exit 78 or a fatal frame. Any other pre-ready exit restarts at most twice (500 ms, then 1 s) and halts on the third. On halt, windows that loaded early are sent back to the boot page and a Retry / Open Logs / Quit dialog appears. Readiness cannot be marked early: the http-serving frame is written only after the runtime graph (migrations) builds, 'Listening on' is never logged, and the gate holds /.well-known/* until the router attaches. I found no defect in the core fix. The leftover gaps are small: two pre-spawn restart paths that skip the policy (as the auditor said), a dev-only bug in readiness bookkeeping, and the CLI node service units, which do not respect exit 78.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations.ts:655 Schema-too-new still fails with Migrator.MigrationError kind BadState. It is the only BadState producer in the repo.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/Sqlite.ts:60 runMigrations runs inside the setup layer through trackStartupPhase (acquireUseRelease). The error is not remapped and not orDie'd, so the Fail cause reaches Layer.launch (server.ts:844) and then cliMain unchanged.
  • apps/server/src/cliMain.ts:40 catchCause classifies with classifyFatalStartupError, prints 'Error: <message>' and sets process.exitCode = reportFatalStartupFailure(...) = 78. The effect then succeeds. NodeRuntime.runMain (platform-node-shared 4.0.2) calls process.exit only when code !== 0, and defaultTeardown returns 0 on success, so 78 is kept. No other server code overrides process.exitCode.
  • apps/server/src/startupFailure.ts:28 BadState maps to database-schema-newer, ConfigError to invalid-config, and BootstrapEnvelopeUnavailableError to bootstrap-envelope-missing. Line 55 writes the fatal frame and returns 78. Covered by startupFailure.test.ts.
  • apps/server/src/diagnostics/DesktopResourceTelemetry.ts:88 fd 4 is an unref'd Socket, so it cannot keep a failed backend alive, and it is attached as the lifecycle channel. A small pending pipe write still flushes. Exit 78 alone is enough for the desktop to halt.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:833 HttpServerLive (bind) is built before RuntimeServicesLive (line 830, migrations), so http-bound arrives before the failure. The http-serving frame (server.ts:721) is written only after the router serves. httpStartupGate.ts:258 holds /.well-known/* until the router attaches. The desktop's 3 s HTTP fallback probe therefore cannot mark a migrating backend ready, and the gate's patched close() answers held requests with 503 Connection: close so server.close() completes.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendStartup.ts:138 createBackendFailurePolicy halts on a fatal frame or exit 78 (lines 154-161). Otherwise it halts after 3 consecutive pre-ready exits (lines 166-173). A post-ready exit restarts and resets the count. Unit tests are in backendStartup.test.ts:93-137.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3299 handleChildGone returns early-loaded windows to the boot page (line 3313) and consults the policy (line 3314). It restarts only on 'restart'; otherwise it calls haltBackendStartup (line 3326). A fatal frame that arrives after the exit event still fills readiness.fatal, because handleFrame sets fatalFrame before fail() and the telemetry cleanup does not remove the data listener.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3061 haltBackendStartup sets backendStartupHalted, cancels the readiness wait and clears the restart timer, then shows the dialog after the child closes (500 ms fallback). showBackendStartupFailure (line 3081) offers Retry / Open Logs / Quit; Retry resets the policy and backoff. scheduleBackendRestart (line 3000) and startBackend (line 3205) both honour the halt flag.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3222 Remaining gap (auditor was right). A missing server entry (line 3222) and a missing bootstrap pipe (line 3273) call scheduleBackendRestart directly. They skip backendFailurePolicy, so they retry every 10 s with no limit.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1796 Gap the auditor missed, dev only. ensureInitialBackendWindowOpen returns under isDevelopment, and ensureDevelopmentInitialWindowOpen (line 1666) runs only when no window exists. After the first dev backend, restarted children never reach waitForBackendWindowReady (line 1599), so recordReady() and backendReadyChild are not updated. Their crashes, even hours after serving, count as pre-ready failures. The third such crash halts with a misleading 'stopped 3 times in a row before it was ready' dialog.
  • apps/server/src/service/nodeService.ts:137 Related gap outside desktop scope. The CLI node launchd plist uses KeepAlive=true with ThrottleInterval=10 (lines 137-140), and the systemd unit uses Restart=always with RestartSec=10 (lines 170-171) and no RestartPreventExitStatus=78. A downgraded CLI node still respawns every 10 s, although startupFailure.ts:4-8 says service managers can stop on EX_CONFIG.
Defects in the shipped fix

The core fix has no defect for the desktop loop described in the finding. Minor leftovers: (1) apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3222 (missing server entry) and main.ts:3273 (missing bootstrap pipe) call scheduleBackendRestart and skip backendFailurePolicy, so a corrupted install retries every 10 s behind the splash forever. (2) Dev only: restarted backend children are never recorded as ready, because ensureInitialBackendWindowOpen no-ops under isDevelopment (main.ts:1796) and the dev path runs only with no window (main.ts:1666). backendReadyChild stays on the first child, so later post-ready crashes count toward the pre-ready limit, and the third such crash, however far apart, shows a misleading halt dialog. (3) Hardening only: when a fatal frame arrives, the desktop relies on the child exiting by itself. Nothing kills a child that wrote 'fatal' but hangs in teardown, and in that case the readiness rejection is only logged (main.ts:1817). I judge this unlikely: the startup gate answers held requests on close and fd 4 is unref'd. (4) Outside the desktop scope: the CLI node service units (service/nodeService.ts:137-140 launchd KeepAlive=true, :170-171 systemd Restart=always) ignore exit 78 and keep respawning every 10 s after a downgrade, contrary to the startupFailure.ts header comment.

Implementation sketch

Optional cleanup, no product decision needed. (a) In apps/desktop/src/main.ts startBackend, send the missing-entry and missing-pipe cases through the policy instead of calling scheduleBackendRestart directly. Example: a helper recordPreSpawnFailure(details) that calls backendFailurePolicy.recordExit({reachedReady:false, exitCode:null, fatal:false}) and either schedules the restart or calls the halt path. haltBackendStartup needs a variant that takes no child, e.g. make child optional and show the dialog immediately. A missing server entry can also be treated as fatal at once. (b) Dev readiness bookkeeping: at the end of startBackend, under isDevelopment, start a lightweight wait, e.g. backendReadiness.promise.then(() => { backendFailurePolicy.recordReady(); backendReadyChild = child; backendRestartBackoff.reset(); }). Better, move recordReady/backendReadyChild out of waitForBackendWindowReady into a per-child readiness hook, so packaged and dev share it. (c) Optional hardening: in handleBackendFrame case 'fatal', arm a 5 s timer that SIGTERMs the child (it is not marked expected, so handleChildGone still halts with reason fatal), and clear the timer on exit. (d) Separate change, low priority: add RestartPreventExitStatus=78 to renderSystemdUserUnit (service/nodeService.ts:170). For launchd, which has no equivalent, either accept the 10 s throttle or raise ThrottleInterval. Tests: extend backendStartup.test.ts for a no-child halt helper; add a nodeService test asserting RestartPreventExitStatus=78 in the rendered unit; the dev-mode bookkeeping can be covered by extracting the per-child readiness hook into backendStartup.ts and unit-testing it.

Done#1 Backend spawns ~320 ms after process start; spawn it from desktopEntry before loading the 2.27 MB main bundle

desktop-boot:spawn-backend-before-main-bundle · original impact High, effort M · Waterfall

Current state

Confirmed DONE. The packaged desktop spawns the backend in desktopEntry.ts before desktopMain.cjs is required, and desktopMain adopts the child and writes the envelope later. The single-instance lock moved into the entry, the envelope wait is 10 s, the spawn args come from one shared launcher, and the computer-use bridge is loaded lazily. Real launch logs from the installed 0.1.31 app (~/.ryco/userdata/logs/desktop-main.log, five launches on 2026-10-14) show 'desktop.backend.spawn ... early=1' about 56-65 ms before the desktop.launch mark. That is roughly 80-100 ms after process start, against about 320 ms before. Backend 'listening' now lands 246-383 ms after desktop.launch on warm launches, against a 1.59 s p50 spawn-to-listening before (compile-cache work also contributed). I found no fix defects. One leftover, not a defect: the envelope arrives about 170-190 ms after the early spawn on warm launches. It needs Electron ready, the main-bundle load, the port probe and computer-use start. The backend reaches its envelope read about 130-170 ms after spawn with the compile cache (measured standalone with `bin.mjs --version`). So the backend now waits roughly 0-50 ms for the envelope instead of the envelope hiding behind a 550 ms module load. Envelope-to-first-backend-log gaps of 23-35 ms on every launch fit that.

Evidence
  • apps/desktop/src/desktopEntry.ts:150-177 Packaged launch: enable the compile cache, claimPrimaryInstance(), applyCachedShellEnvironment(), startEarlyBackend(), publishDesktopLaunchRecord(), then require desktopMain.cjs. A failed require discards the early child.
  • apps/desktop/src/desktopEntry.ts:55-60 setPath(userData) runs before requestSingleInstanceLock(). A refused instance calls app.exit(0) before loading the main bundle. main.ts:4635-4641 skips its own request via hasSingleInstanceLock().
  • apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts:32-54,70-114,129-152 desktopBackendSpawnArgs, createDesktopBackendChildEnv and spawnDesktopBackend are the shared launcher used by both the entry (desktopEntry.ts:99-114) and main.ts launchBackendChild (3186-3202). Early spawn errors and EPIPE on fd 3/4 are recorded, not thrown. The args include --mode desktop --no-browser.
  • apps/desktop/dist-electron/main.cjs The built entry (5.9 KB) requires only electron, node builtins and small shared chunks (desktopPaths, shellEnvironment, compileCacheDirectory, rolldown runtime). The launch record and launcher live in the shared desktopPaths chunk, so the entry and desktopMain see one module instance. Symbol.for on globalThis would also cover duplication.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3204-3289 startBackend adopts via takeEarlyDesktopBackend() and replaces a child older than 8 s (isEarlyDesktopBackendStale). It handles a child that errored or exited before adoption (goneBeforeAdoption, then handleChildGone), and writes the envelope through writeBackendBootstrapEnvelope (3135-3184).
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:2166-2180,3370-3374,4877-4882 handleFatalStartupError, stopBackendAndWaitForExit and before-quit all call discardEarlyDesktopBackend(), so an unadopted early child is not orphaned. If the parent dies, the closed fd 3 pipe makes the server exit with BootstrapEnvelopeUnavailableError.
  • apps/server/src/bootstrap.ts:42-57; apps/server/src/cli.ts:497-509 readBootstrapEnvelope defaults to 10_000 ms. With no envelope on an explicit fd, the server fails with BootstrapEnvelopeUnavailableError instead of booting on defaults. applyBootstrapShellEnvironment runs right after, before any layer is built. No top-level process.env captures were found in apps/server/src or packages/shared/src.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4803-4870 bootstrap(): port probe and startDesktopComputerUse() run in parallel, then exposure mode, then the shell environment (cache hit already applied by the entry), then startBackend. The window opens inside startBackend. IPC, menu, protocol and updater are deferred after it.
  • ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/desktop-main.log + server-child.log (runs 2713c0d2abd7, d2e02080aa02, 2c9d7783bd64, 5e1dd6a776c6, b1b8af618599) Every packaged launch logs early=1 with spawn at elapsedMs -56..-65 (-199 on a loaded post-login launch). The envelope (APP SESSION START) is at +117..+126 ms, and the first backend log line follows 23-35 ms later (72 ms on the loaded launch). Listening is at +246..+383 ms (+955 on the loaded launch).
  • apps/desktop/src/desktopEntry.test.ts:126-202; apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.test.ts:151-205; apps/desktop/src/desktopMainBundleSplitting.test.ts:110 Tests cover a refused second instance (no bundle, no backend), early spawn with and without a cached shell environment, a missing server entry, single adoption, discard, stale replacement, and keeping the entry free of the main bundle and heavy dependencies.
Defects in the shipped fix

None verified. Checked these and found them clean: identical env, cwd, executable and compile-cache hook between the early spawn and launchBackendChild for packaged builds; no process.env mutation in main.ts before startBackend except the shell environment, which the envelope covers on a cache miss; child stdout/stderr and telemetry buffered until adoption; cleanup on fatal error, quit and parent death; the 8 s adoption limit against the server's 10 s wait. Minor, harmless: on Windows the entry now takes the singleton lock before configureAppIdentity() calls app.setName(), so the lock name is the package default rather than 'Ryco (<stage>)'. Every new instance does the same, so this is consistent. The refused second instance also no longer writes the 'second instance refused' log line.

Partial#2 Real-world boot is dominated by 3–15 s backend stalls before 'Listening'; the listener waits behind provider creation and migrations

desktop-boot:backend-listen-stalls-real-world · original impact High, effort L · Blocking I/O WP03decision

Current state

PARTIAL is correct. Current code does proposals 1 (16-thread pool), 2 (lazy, async, bounded maintenance probing) and 5 (stall monitor). It also does the static half of 3: the port is bound before the runtime graph, the gate holds requests and serves the static shell and desktop document, and drivers are built only after markHttpServing. So the measured four-driver 3-15 s stall is now off the listener path. Still open: auth/session, RPC and WS wait for the whole RuntimeServicesLive graph, there is no health or status route, and there is no 'upgrading data' state. Migrations and data repairs still run inside the SQLite setup layer before HttpRouter.serve, and four data migrations added since the report (085-088) made that path heavier on large databases. Two corrections to the auditor. First, the 9.5 s and 27 s repairs were one-time; the pr_terminal_at repair is PRAGMA-guarded and will not recur. The recurring exposure is each new full-table migration. Second, proposal 5 is only partly done: the projector replay, the read-model load and the Agent Control listener are not named phases. That is exactly where the unexplained 13 s 'reconcile 863 ms, listen 13170 ms' gap sat.

Evidence
  • apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts:68 DESKTOP_BACKEND_UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE = "16". Set at :102 only when the user has not set it; used by main.ts:666 and desktopEntry.ts:108.
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerMaintenance.ts:378-453 The maintenance probe uses resolveCommandPathAsync plus a timed realPath, and runs lazily in a scope fork with a timeout and fallback. The fallback passes resolvedCommandPath: null, so the sync resolveCommandPath at :300 is skipped.
  • packages/shared/src/shell.ts:489-565 resolveCommandPathAsync has a 1 s bound per PATH entry and skips locations whose earlier check is still stuck.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts:124-213 The registry starts empty and drivers are built only after gateReleased. ProviderService construction (ProviderService.ts:1020-1025) lists only built instances, so it does not release the gate early.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1153-1157 markHttpServing releases the provider boot gate, after HttpRouter.serve has attached.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:830-834 Build order: StartupStallMonitorLive, then HttpServerLive (the bind), then RuntimeServicesLive, then HttpRouter.serve(makeRoutesLayer) at :807. Every API, auth and WS route still waits for the whole runtime graph.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:266-299 The gate's early handler serves static assets only (the desktop also gets the document). There is no health, auth/session or startup-status route early, and the codebase has no health route at all.
  • apps/server/src/httpStartupGate.ts:36 Held requests get a 503 after 10 s. The client retries 502-504 for at most 15 s (packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.ts:93-95), and the desktop reloads at ready after 9 s (apps/desktop/src/backendAppWindowLoad.ts:30).
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/Sqlite.ts:60 runMigrations still runs inside the SQLite setup layer, ahead of the router. It is only wrapped in trackStartupPhase.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations.ts:663-760 The ledger pass and the full post-ledger repair list still run before the router. pr_terminal_at (:282-317) is PRAGMA-guarded and one-time, so its 27 s stall does not recur.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations/085_ProjectionThreadActivityKindIndex.ts:42 New since the report (60633eff3). CREATE INDEX on (kind, thread_id, sequence, created_at, activity_id) on the largest table. sequence and created_at come after payload_json in the row (005_Projections.ts:49-57 and 008), so building it reads every activity payload's overflow chain, before the router, on a 9 GB DB.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations/088_LegacyActivityPayloads.ts:50-55 New (36760bffd). length(CAST(payload_json AS BLOB)) scans every payload and rewrites large rows, before the router. It runs once, guarded by a marker.
Remaining

1) Auth/session, RPC and WS still wait for the full RuntimeServicesLive graph (apps/server/src/server.ts:807,830). There is no health or startup-status route, and only static files are served early (server.ts:266-299, httpStartupGate.ts:310-345). 2) Migrations and data repairs run before the router (persistence/Layers/Sqlite.ts:60, Migrations.ts:663-760), with no 'upgrading data' state anywhere. Since the report, 085 (an index build that reads every activity payload, 085_...ts:42), 087 (a per-thread backfill, 087_...ts:216) and 088 (a payload scan and rewrite, 088_...ts:50-55) joined that path. So the first boot after an upgrade on a large DB can again exceed the 10 s gate hold and the 15 s client retry, and fall back to the desktop's reload at ready. 3) Stall attribution has gaps. Projector replay and read-model load (OrchestrationEngine.ts:601-602), auth and the Agent Control listener start (AgentControlMcpServer.ts:183-199) are not trackStartupPhase phases. Migration phases are never sent to the desktop as frames, because recordDesktopStartupPhase is only called at four milestones. 4) Nobody has measured real-world p90 since the change. 5) Optional: sync resolveCommandPath remains in CursorAgentCommand.ts:49-63 and CopilotAdapter.types.ts:123.

Defects in the shipped fix

No blocking defects in the implemented parts. The 'proposal 5 done' claim is overstated: the monitor cannot name the layers that held the unexplained 13 s pre-listen gap. Because the window loads at http-bound, a backend slower than 9-10 s fails its first API calls. The client's 15 s auth retry then fails, the desktop reloads at ready, and the user may briefly see an error. That is a known trade-off, not a regression.

Implementation sketch

A) Attribution (S, no decision needed). In OrchestrationEngine.ts:601-602, wrap projectionPipeline.bootstrap in trackStartupPhase('orchestration.projection.bootstrap') and getCommandReadModel in trackStartupPhase('orchestration.read-model.load'). Wrap AgentControlMcpServer startListener as 'agent-control.listener.start', and wrap the Auth layer build. Alternatively, add a small helper trackLayerBuild(name, layer) = Layer.unwrap(trackStartupPhase(name, Layer.build...)) and apply it to the big RuntimeServicesLive members in server.ts. Have trackStartupPhase write a desktop 'startup-phase' frame for phases that last more than 1 s, so the desktop log and apps/desktop/scripts/boot-report.mjs capture them. Tests: extend startupStallMonitor tests so a slow fake engine bootstrap shows up in the reported phases. B) Visible upgrading state (S-M, decision). Emit a phase-begin frame from trackStartupPhase for 'persistence.migrations.*'. In main.ts handleBackendFrame, forward it to the window over IPC (preload bridge, not a new HTTP route). The renderer's connection/boot UI then shows 'Upgrading data...' instead of a stalled connect. While a migration phase is running, let the gate extend the hold, or have the client treat 'Ryco is starting' 503s as non-fatal, so long one-time upgrades do not end in an error and a reload. C) Move data backfills off the pre-router path (L, decision). Split runMigrations into a schema pass (DDL, cheap column adds, marker checks) that stays in Sqlite.ts, and a data-upgrade pass (085 index build, 087 backfill, 088 reprojection, the summary backfill). Run the data pass after markHttpServing, gated before signalCommandReady or behind the read paths that depend on it. 087 readers need a fallback to subqueries until its marker is set. 088 is already safe to run late, because readers bound payloads. 085 holds the SQLite write lock for the whole build, so it must finish before the command gate opens. Test with a synthetic multi-GB DB that HttpRouter.serve attaches before the data pass completes and that snapshots stay correct. D) Optional (S): switch CursorAgentCommand.ts:49-63 and CopilotAdapter.types.ts:123 to resolveCommandPathAsync via Effect.promise. E) After a week of use, re-run the boot-log parser on server-child.log to confirm listen p90 and read the 'startup stall' warnings.

Needs a decision

Two product and boundary choices. (1) Whether to show an 'upgrading data' state, and whether the gate and client should keep waiting past 10-15 s during known one-time migrations instead of failing and reloading. (2) Whether to defer data backfills behind the router. That means accepting degraded or fallback read paths until the backfill finishes, or reordering the command gate. Serving auth/session or a status route before the auth layer is built would also touch auth semantics. The attribution work (A) and the async Cursor/Copilot resolution (D) need no decision.

Value medium · effort M · risk medium

Done#3 No V8 compile cache for the Electron main process or the backend child (T3 Code ships one)

desktop-boot:v8-compile-cache-backend-and-main · original impact Medium, effort S · Build config WP03

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. DONE is right: the cache is on and working. The auditor was wrong to report no fix defects and to call the inherited variable harmless. RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR is never stripped, so every terminal, provider CLI and agent shell started by the desktop backend inherits it. apps/server/src/bin.ts honors it in any Ryco server or CLI process, so other Ryco instances started from inside Ryco Desktop write into Desktop's per-version cache. Those instances can come from the dev checkout, worktrees, smoke scripts or a Bun-run dev backend. Pruning only removes other version directories, so those entries are never cleaned up while the version stays the same.

Current state

Implemented in #710 (60633eff3) and working on this machine. The cache is enabled in the Electron main process (compileCache.cjs is required before desktopMain.cjs), in the early and restarted backend (via --require), in the MCP bridge child, and in bin.ts for the stdio proxy, device host and MCP bridge helper modes. It uses a per-version directory under userData, is skipped for AppImage and dev builds, and is flushed after backend startup. I checked the installed app's cache. ~/Library/Application Support/ryco/compile-cache/0.1.31/v24.21.0-arm64-8c6a5e03-501 holds entries keyed to app.asar/.../desktopMain.cjs (CJS key 626ff022) and to file://.../app.asar/apps/server/dist/bin.mjs (ESM key bcd02a4f). So both the main process and the backend persist bytecode. One minor side-effect defect: the variable leaks into foreign processes. The same directory also holds 4,761 Node entries (101 MB) in a second subdirectory keyed to /Users/laurinfrank/Code/ryco/apps/server/dist/*.mjs and that checkout's node_modules, plus a Bun 1.4.3 subdirectory (131 files, 37 MB). That is about 138 MB of the 198 MB total, and none of it is pruned while the app version stays 0.1.31.

Evidence
  • apps/desktop/src/desktopEntry.ts:35 enableDesktopCompileCache sets RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR and requires compileCache.cjs before desktopMain.cjs is required (line 172). It is called on the bridge path (132) and the normal path (150).
  • apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts:40 In Node mode the backend args include --require <compileCache.cjs>. The early backend (desktopEntry.ts:99) and the restart path (main.ts:3187-3195, COMPILE_CACHE_HOOK_PATH main.ts:330) both use them.
  • apps/desktop/src/desktopEntry.ts:135 The MCP bridge forwarder spawns its Node-mode child with --require compileCache.cjs.
  • apps/server/src/bin.ts:34 enableCompileCacheBestEffort() runs before the dynamic imports of the stdio proxy, device host, external MCP bridge and cliMain. It honors RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR in any process (apps/server/src/compileCache.ts:22-46), so the stdio proxy that cursor-agent spawns (CursorAdapter.ts:603, ProviderInjection.ts:289) is cached.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1147 flushCompileCacheBestEffort() runs once startup completes, so the cache survives a backend that is later SIGKILLed.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1623 pruneStaleDesktopCompileCaches runs on the first backend ready. It removes only sibling version directories and never touches entries inside the current version directory.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts:70 createDesktopBackendChildEnv copies process.env and does not delete RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR. TERMINAL_ENV_BLOCKLIST (apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:105) blocks only PORT, ELECTRON_RENDERER_PORT and ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE. Terminals, provider CLIs and agent shells therefore all inherit the variable.
  • ~/Library/Application Support/ryco/compile-cache/0.1.31 (on-disk, read-only check) This directory is 198 MB and holds three subdirectories. v24.21.0-arm64-8c6a5e03-501 (1,450 entries, 60 MB) contains Desktop's own entries: desktopMain.cjs and the app.asar bin.mjs. v24.21.0-arm64-964aae3f-501 (4,761 entries, 101 MB) contains entries whose crc32 keys match file:///Users/laurinfrank/Code/ryco/apps/server/dist/*.mjs and that checkout's node_modules/.bun, so those are dev-checkout servers run from Ryco-spawned shells. v1.4.3-aarch64-c6da4a4d3-501 (131 files, 37 MB) was written by Bun 1.4.3, the repo's pinned Bun, which Desktop never runs in packaged mode.
  • apps/server/src/compileCache.ts:34 The doc says the API is 'Absent under Bun', but the Bun-tagged cache subdirectory shows Bun 1.4.3 implements module.enableCompileCache and honors the directory. The comment is stale.
Defects in the shipped fix

This is a minor defect that costs disk space, not runtime speed: RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR leaks into foreign processes. Desktop sets it in its main process env (desktopEntry.ts:42), and createDesktopBackendChildEnv (backendLauncher.ts:79) passes it to the backend. Neither the backend env, the terminal env blocklist (terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:105) nor provider spawns strip it. bin.ts:34 then honors it in every Ryco server, CLI or helper process, including copies from other checkouts or worktrees and Bun-run dev backends (a dev desktop launched from a Ryco terminal inherits it). Those processes write entries keyed by their own paths into Desktop's per-version directory. pruneStaleDesktopCompileCaches (compileCacheDirectory.ts:43) only deletes other version directories, so these entries pile up until the version string changes. On this machine about 138 MB of the 198 MB cache came from such processes in two days. A related issue: the server bundle has hashed chunk names, so local rebuilds that keep the version (this machine runs repeated 0.1.31 builds) add a new set of entries on every build. Release updates bump the version, so pruning bounds this for normal users. A smaller nit: the 'Absent under Bun' comments in apps/server/src/compileCache.ts are stale.

Implementation sketch

1) Stop the variable from reaching processes Desktop does not own. In apps/server/src/compileCache.ts, have enableCompileCacheBestEffort return the directory it resolved. In bin.ts, delete process.env.RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR right after enabling, so terminals, provider CLIs, git and agent shells no longer inherit it. The desktop main process can keep it, because restarts pass it through backendChildEnv. 2) Keep the stdio proxy on the Desktop cache by passing the captured directory explicitly in the ProviderInjection stdio-proxy mcpServer env (apps/server/src/agentControl/ProviderInjection.ts:291), only when it was set. Alternatively, let the proxy fall back to Node's default tmpdir cache, which still gives the speedup. 3) Optional, to bound same-version rebuilds: add a build identity (commit or build id from the packaged package.json) to resolveDesktopCompileCacheDir, so each rebuild gets a fresh directory and the old one is pruned. 4) Update the stale 'Absent under Bun' comments. Tests: compileCache.test.ts should assert the variable is consumed (removed from env) after enabling. Add a ProviderInjection test that the stdio-proxy env carries the directory when set. Add a terminal Manager or backendLauncher test that spawned terminal env lacks RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR. Manual check: launch the packaged app, open a Ryco terminal and confirm `env | grep RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR` prints nothing.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Partial#4 Renderer origin follows the first free port from 3773, which T3 Code also uses; origin flips split caches and localStorage

desktop-boot:renderer-origin-port-flips · original impact Medium, effort S · Caching WP04decision

Current state

PARTIAL is correct. #710 (60633eff3) is the only change in this area since f1be4abc7. It adds a Ryco-specific default port (7926) for fresh installs, persists the last served port in desktop-settings.json, refuses to persist one-launch fallbacks, and logs flips as a warning. Existing installs that already have a 'Local Storage' dir still start at 3773, the port T3 Code also uses, so they keep flipping to 3774/3775 whenever T3 Code starts first. That is the author's measured case, about 5.6% of launches. The app document is still loaded from http://127.0.0.1:<port>, so the origin is still tied to the port. A flipped launch now loses more than before: the primary last-known-shell IndexedDB cache from 45f7a9be6 is origin-scoped too, so the boot-paint shortcut goes cold. I found no other implementation: no Hub-side, renamed or ryco://-origin path. The auditor's fix-defect is real and somewhat broader than stated. The port record lives in ~/.ryco/userdata/desktop-settings.json, but the state it guards lives in Electron userData. Resetting or wiping ~/.ryco, an unreadable settings file, or a fresh install that never reaches backend-ready moves a 7926 install back to 3773. In the reset and never-ready cases it then persists 3773 for good.

Evidence
  • apps/desktop/src/backendPort.ts:11 DEFAULT_DESKTOP_BACKEND_PORT = 7926. Fresh installs no longer collide with T3 Code's 3773.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendPort.ts:16 LEGACY_DESKTOP_BACKEND_PORT = 3773 is still the start port for every install that already has renderer state.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendPort.ts:53-64 hasPriorDesktopRendererState is only existsSync(userData/'Local Storage'). resolveDesktopBackendStartPort returns the persisted port, else 3773 when that dir exists, else 7926.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendPort.ts:80-88 shouldPersistDesktopBackendPort persists only when the preferred port served, or on a fresh install. A one-launch fallback to 3774 is deliberately not remembered, so the next launch retries 3773, and that launch's origin differs.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4676-4709 selectDesktopBackendPort probes 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0 and :: (main.ts:377-378) upward from the start port and logs 'warning: preferred backend port ... in use'. This covers the 'log the flip' part of the proposal.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1618-1619 persistDesktopBackendPort runs only from handleBackendReady, after the app was already loaded at bind time (loadPackagedBackendAppWindowOnBind, main.ts:1766-1770). Local Storage can exist before the port is recorded.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1636-1654 Persistence is skipped when desktopSettingsUnreadable is set or the write fails.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:531-549 An unreadable desktop-settings.json falls back to defaults with backendPort null. A 7926 install then starts at 3773 and its origin flips.
  • apps/desktop/src/desktopPaths.ts:30-35 desktop-settings.json (the port record) is under ~/.ryco/userdata. Local Storage is under Electron userData (resolveDesktopUserDataPath, set at main.ts:4614). The record and the state it protects live in different directories and can be reset independently.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1757 window.loadURL(backendHttpUrl), also at main.ts:4587. The renderer origin is still http://127.0.0.1:<port>.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:338-349 ryco:// is already registered as a privileged standard, secure, codeCache scheme. Its static file handler (main.ts:2196) and isDesktopAppUrl (main.ts:645) exist, but only the boot page is loaded from it. A port-independent origin is technically available but unused.
  • apps/web/src/composerDraftPersistence.ts:36-44 Composer drafts are still in origin-scoped localStorage, with attachment bytes in IndexedDB. A flipped launch still hides drafts.
Remaining

1) Existing installs still flip. An install with userData/'Local Storage' and no persisted port, or a persisted 3773, starts at 3773 (backendPort.ts:58-63, main.ts:4683-4690). When T3 Code holds 3773, Ryco serves on 3774 and does not persist it (backendPort.ts:80-88). That launch has a different origin, so localStorage drafts and UI state (composerDraftPersistence.ts:36-44, uiStateStore.ts:435), the IndexedDB attachment bytes, the primary shell cache (primaryShellCache.ts:72-95), and the HTTP and V8 caches are all cold or hidden. This is exactly the author's measured case. 2) The origin is still derived from the port: window.loadURL(backendHttpUrl) at main.ts:1757 and main.ts:4587. The long-term decoupling has not been done.

Defects in the shipped fix

The port record is stored apart from the state it protects, and it is written late. resolveDesktopBackendStartPort trusts desktop-settings.json (~/.ryco/userdata, desktopPaths.ts:30-35) and uses existsSync(userData/'Local Storage') as the legacy signal (backendPort.ts:53-55). Any of these moves a post-#710 install from 7926 back to 3773 and strands its 7926 localStorage, IndexedDB and caches: (a) the user wipes or resets ~/.ryco, or uses a different RYCO_HOME, while Electron userData survives; (b) desktop-settings.json is unreadable, because defaults with backendPort null are used (main.ts:531-549) and persistence is skipped (main.ts:1640); (c) on a fresh install's first launch the app loads at bind time and creates Local Storage, but the backend never reaches handleBackendReady (main.ts:1618), so the port is never written. In (a) and (c), the next launch that serves 3773 persists it as preferred (backendPort.ts:86), so the move is permanent. Low frequency, but it is silent data loss of drafts on exactly the path the fix was meant to protect.

Implementation sketch

A. Fix defect (S, low risk). Keep the origin record next to the state it guards. Add readRendererOriginRecord/writeRendererOriginRecord in apps/desktop/src/backendPort.ts, backed by a small JSON file in Electron userData (e.g. app.getPath('userData')/renderer-origin.json, {version:1, port}), written atomically with mode 0600. In selectDesktopBackendPort (main.ts:4676), resolve persistedPort as record ?? desktopSettings.backendPort, which keeps the #710 field as a read fallback. When `persistable`, write the record synchronously right after selection, before any loadURL, instead of in handleBackendReady (main.ts:1618, 1636-1654). Then a crash before ready, a ~/.ryco wipe or unreadable settings can no longer reclassify the install. Optionally, keep mirroring into desktop-settings.json. Tests in backendPort.test.ts: the record overrides settings; a record present with an absent settings port still yields 7926; the legacy path applies only when there is no record and Local Storage exists. B. Migrate existing installs off 3773 (M, medium risk; product decision). Do a one-time renderer-state export and import so legacy installs can move to the persisted Ryco port (7926). (1) Add a desktop bridge IPC pair, e.g. desktop:origin-state:export and desktop:origin-state:take, in apps/desktop/src (preload plus main), with a size cap. (2) In apps/web, in a desktop-only early module run before the zustand persist stores rehydrate (before composerDraftStore and uiStateStore are imported in main.tsx/__root), do this on a legacy-origin launch flagged by main: serialize all localStorage entries plus the composer attachment-bytes IndexedDB store, and send them to main. Main writes userData/origin-migration-v1.json (0600) and sets the renderer-origin record to 7926 for the next launch. Do not migrate the primary shell cache or the HTTP/V8 caches; they rebuild. (3) On the next launch at the new origin, the same early module calls take(), writes only keys that are absent, re-puts the attachment bytes, acks, and main deletes the bundle. If the import fails, keep the bundle and retry, and never delete the old origin's data. Tests: unit tests for the export/import merge (absent-only, size cap, idempotent ack) in apps/web/src/persistence; backendPort tests for the record transition; one desktop smoke test that a draft written on 3773 is visible after the move. C. Long-term (L, needs decision). Load the shell from ryco://app instead of loadURL(backendHttpUrl) at main.ts:1757 and main.ts:4587. The scheme is already privileged and has a static handler (main.ts:338-349, 2196). The renderer would then reach the backend through the bridge-provided httpBaseUrl/wsBaseUrl. This needs backend CORS for ryco://app, auth that does not depend on same-origin cookies (bearer/ticket), CSP review, and the same one-time migration as B. After that, port flips only affect API and WebSocket traffic.

Needs a decision

Moving existing installs to a new origin is a product trade-off about user data: drafts, UI state and attachment bytes must be migrated, or they are stranded. #710 deliberately chose not to move them. The long-term ryco://app origin changes same-origin, cookie and CORS assumptions between the desktop renderer and the backend, which is an auth-semantics change that needs review. Part A, the defect fix, is low risk and needs no decision.

Value medium · effort M · risk medium

Partial#5 Startup timing misses main-module load and time-to-usable-shell; proposed measurement plan

desktop-boot:startup-measurement-blind-spots · original impact Medium, effort S · Other WP03

Current state

PARTIAL holds. (1) and (2) are implemented, and the user's own production desktop-main.log confirms it: launches on 2026-10-14 log processUptimeMs, entryStartMs, mainModuleLoadMs, then desktop.window.app.shell-usable and shell-painted with every ryco:startup:* mark. (5) also exists as perf:boot-report. (3) covers only 4 coarse frames (http-bound, command-gate-ready, http-serving, complete). Migrations, per-instance provider create and the server.startup.* phases never reach desktop-main.log. The user's own logs show why that matters: on 2026-10-13 one launch had an 18.2 s gap between backend.http-bound (serverMs=208) and backend.http-serving (serverMs=18405) with nothing attributing it in desktop-main.log. The cause (persistence.migrations.ledger 18036 ms, migrations 87/88) appears only in server-child.log, and only because a 1.3 s event-loop stall warning happened to list the in-flight phases. (4) requires shell-usable, but nothing integrates a seeded DB or a packaged run. The auditor said nothing seeds a large DB, which is wrong: perf:fixture-home exists. The smoke script also has two practical defects when run against a packaged build or a fixture.

Evidence
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:220-233 (1) DONE. desktop.launch now logs processUptimeMs (the performance.now origin at process start), entryStartMs, mainModuleLoadMs and compileCache. In the user's packaged logs (16 launches) processUptimeMs has p50 150 ms and max 3781 ms, and mainModuleLoadMs has p50 63 ms and max 205 ms.
  • apps/desktop/src/desktopEntry.ts:30 entryStartedAtMs is taken first thing in the entry and published at desktopEntry.ts:163. mainModuleLoadMs therefore also counts the entry's own pre-require work (lock, compile cache, early spawn). Measured, that is about 3 ms, so the label is effectively accurate.
  • apps/desktop/src/startupMarks.ts:84-160 (2) DONE in a different form. A PerformanceObserver in the preload (preload.ts:95-99) reports on every launch with no env flag, at primary-shell-usable and again at primary-shell-painted, bounded by a 5 s timeout. There is a unit test in startupMarks.test.ts.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3412-3423 The IPC handler validates the report and always calls markDesktopStartupPhase('desktop.window.app.<phase>'). That writes to desktop-main.log in packaged builds (main.ts:1510-1516, 1885-1902). In the real log, shell-usable carries primary-ws-open, primary-shell-frame-received, primary-shell-snapshot-*, primary-shell-usable and more.
  • apps/server/src/desktopLifecycle.ts:39-45 (3) PARTIAL. recordDesktopStartupPhase sends only {name, ms-at-end}. It has 4 callers: server.ts:296 (http-bound), server.ts:722 (http-serving), serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1030 (command-gate-ready) and serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1145 (complete). desktopLifecycle.ts did not exist at f1be4abc7.

  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/Sqlite.ts:60 trackStartupPhase('persistence.migrations') and Migrations.ts:665-669 (ledger, repairs) are only stall-attribution registry entries (startupStallMonitor.ts:77-86).   • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderInstanceRegistryLive.ts:268 Per-instance create is wrapped in trackStartupPhase with no fd-4 frame. Correction to the auditor: its duration is already logged at INFO ('provider instance registry entry resolved ... durationMs', lines 306-312, also present at f1be4abc7) into server.log and server-child.log. It is not in desktop-main.log, so boot-report cannot aggregate it.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:509-516 runStartupPhase spans (server.startup.*) and the runMigrations span are persisted to the always-on server.trace.ndjson. On this machine those files rotate through about 110 MB in about 2 hours, so per-launch startup spans are gone within hours and are not tied to the desktop run id.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderRegistry.ts:545 trackStartupPhase is also used for provider.probe:<id> on refreshes long after startup. A blanket forwarding hook in trackStartupPhase would flood fd 4 and desktop-main.log, so it needs a startup-window gate.
  • apps/desktop/scripts/startup-timing-smoke.mjs:23-31 (4) Half done. REQUIRED_PHASES now includes desktop.window.app.shell-usable, SUMMARY_PHASES adds backendBound, shellUsable and shellPainted, --max-shell-usable-ms was added, and TIMING_RE accepts negative elapsed times.
  • apps/desktop/scripts/startup-timing-smoke.mjs:182-195 Defect (pre-existing, but it blocks the seeded-DB use case). readNewFileContent starts every log at offset 0 (fileOffsets is a new Map at line 275). With a reused --base-dir, such as a fixture home run twice or a real ~/.ryco, the previous run's desktop-main.log lines satisfy REQUIRED_PHASES on the first 100 ms poll (line 284). finish(0) then reports stale timings.
Remaining

(3) Server phases are still missing from desktop-main.log. - persistence.migrations, .ledger and .repairs (Sqlite.ts:60, Migrations.ts:665-669) are not forwarded over fd 4. - Neither is provider.instance.create:<id> (ProviderInstanceRegistryLive.ts:268), nor the server.startup.* phases (serverRuntimeStartup.ts:509-516). - Only http-bound, command-gate-ready, http-serving and complete are forwarded (server.ts:296/722, serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1030/1145). - The frame schema has no duration (desktopResourceTelemetry.ts:123). - Real impact: an 18 s bound-to-serving gap on 2026-10-13 was unattributed in desktop-main.log. (4) No seeded or packaged integration. - The fixture generator exists (perf:fixture-home), but startup-timing-smoke.mjs has no option to copy a fixture into a fresh RYCO_HOME. - It re-reads existing logs from offset 0, which gives stale results with a reused --base-dir (lines 182-195, 275, 284). - A packaged --app run fails while the user's Ryco is running, because the single-instance lock is keyed to ~/Library/Application Support/ryco (desktopEntry.ts:55-57). - Nothing runs it in CI or release. (5) Minor gaps in boot-report.mjs. - PHASES (lines 17-27) omits processUptimeMs and mainModuleLoadMs from desktop.launch and every backend.* phase. - Its percentiles are relative to desktop.launch (line 169), not process start.

Defects in the shipped fix

There are no functional defects in (1), (2) or (5). The always-on reporting works in the user's production logs. Two startup-timing-smoke defects undermine the 'packaged build with a seeded large DB' goal of (4). Both are pre-existing, not regressions. (a) Stale-log parsing from offset 0 when --base-dir already holds logs. The script finishes instantly with the previous run's numbers and exit code 0. (b) A packaged run cannot start while the installed Ryco is running, because the single-instance lock ignores RYCO_HOME. The script reports only 'exited before startup completed (code=0)'. boot-report percentiles exclude pre-main time (processUptimeMs). On a cold launch that was 3.8 s that the report does not show.

Implementation sketch

1. Forward server phase durations (apps/server, packages/shared, apps/desktop): - packages/shared/src/desktopResourceTelemetry.ts: add an optional `durationMs` to the startup-phase frame. Parse it as an optional counter so older frames still parse. Extend desktopResourceTelemetry.test.ts. - apps/server/src/desktopLifecycle.ts: add `recordDesktopStartupPhaseDuration(name, startedAtPerfMs, endedAtPerfMs)` that writes {type:'startup-phase', name, ms: end, durationMs}. - Add a module-level `startupForwardingOpen` flag, closed by recordDesktopStartupPhase('complete') or after a 60 s cap. Also cap frames per process (e.g. 128), so provider.probe refreshes and hot-reload creates after startup are not forwarded. - apps/server/src/startupStallMonitor.ts: in trackStartupPhase, take performance.now() at begin and end. In the release step, call the duration recorder when forwarding is open and the name matches an allowlist: 'persistence.migrations', 'persistence.migrations.*', 'provider.instance.create:*', 'provider.registry.*' / hydration phases, and 'server.startup.*'. This covers Sqlite.ts:60, Migrations.ts:665-669, ProviderInstanceRegistryLive.ts:268, ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts:131/191 and runStartupPhase without touching each caller. - apps/desktop/src/main.ts handleBackendFrame (~3029): append `durationMs=` when present. sanitizeStartupPhaseName already maps ':' to '_' and caps names at 64. - Tests: in apps/server/src/startupStallMonitor.test.ts, attach a PassThrough through attachDesktopLifecycleChannel or detachDesktopLifecycleChannelForTests. Assert that one frame is emitted per allowlisted phase, none after 'complete', and none for provider.probe. 2. boot-report.mjs (apps/desktop/scripts): - Parse desktop.launch details (processUptimeMs, mainModuleLoadMs). - Add rows for preMain and mainModuleLoad, and a derived shellUsableFromProcessStart = processUptimeMs + shellUsable. - Aggregate backend.* durationMs by phase name. Collapse provider.instance.create_* into one row plus the worst instance, and print the top phases by p90. - Add a small fixture-log test, e.g. scripts/boot-report.test.mjs next to the existing *.test.mjs scripts. 3. startup-timing-smoke.mjs: - Before spawning, set each log's offset in fileOffsets to its current size, or track the run id from the first new desktop.launch line and ignore other runs. - Add `--fixture-home <dir>`, which copies the fixture (fs.cpSync, including state.sqlite -wal/-shm) into a fresh temp RYCO_HOME per run. Document using it with `bun run perf:fixture-home --out <dir>`. - When the child exits with code 0 before launch on macOS with --app, print a hint that an installed Ryco instance holds the single-instance lock. Do not add a user-data override to the app; that would be a behaviour change. - Optionally add a workflow_dispatch macOS job that builds the desktop app, generates a fixture and runs the smoke with --max-shell-usable-ms. Validation (focused): - `bun run --cwd packages/shared test -- desktopResourceTelemetry` - `bun run --cwd apps/server test -- startupStallMonitor` - `bun run --cwd apps/desktop test -- startupMarks` - Run boot-report against a sample log.

Done#6 Electron main eagerly loads the whole Hub/E2EE/relay stack, the contracts barrel, effect and electron-updater before 'ready'

desktop-boot:main-process-eager-module-graph · original impact Medium, effort M · Bundle size WP04

Current state

Confirmed DONE. The finding's main cost is gone and the measured gain matches the estimate. In plain Node 24, everything evaluated before main.ts's own body now takes 78-85 ms uncached and about 53 ms with the compile cache, against 172-185 ms in the finding (whole bundle). Done: (a) the Hub/E2EE/workspace, SSH, tailscale, guide and Computer-use stacks sit behind import(), and SSH IPC uses deferred stubs; (c) electron-updater is a lazy require; (d) the port probe is plain node:net with the same EADDRNOTAVAIL semantics as before; (e) there is a source-graph guard test. What remains is about 50 ms (cached) of eager code. About 40 ms of it is effect/Schema, needed by the contracts schemas, clientPersistence and desktopHubControl. Another 10-15 ms is contracts module evaluation, about 3-7 ms of which is Hub-only and Computer-use-only schemas placed in the entry chunk. Proposal (b), narrow contracts imports, is only partly done. The guard test checks only the relative source graph. It does not follow @ryco/* packages, inspect the emitted chunks or set a size budget, so it passes while Hub-only schemas are evaluated before ready.

For a user with a stored Hub session it loads right after startBackend via prepareDesktopHostedIdentityResume (main.ts:1279-1291, 4857), which is after ready. That costs about 30 ms cached and 48-66 ms uncached of main-thread time, in a microtask after window creation.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1991 loadElectronUpdater() is a lazy CommonJS require. desktopMain.cjs:13268 is its only electron-updater require. Only `import type` remains at main.ts:50.

This implements the proposal's 'register IPC eagerly with a stub' step. The SSH chunk still requires the effect barrel and platform-node, but only on the first SSH use.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendPort.ts:31 canListenOnHost is plain Net.createServer().listen()/close() and treats EADDRNOTAVAIL as available. That matches the old shared/Net.ts:102-119 behaviour (git show f1be4abc7). No Effect runtime per probe any more.

This happens before startBackend, registerIpcHandlers and the first window. The work is needed because the envelope carries computerUseBridge (main.ts:3166). The chunk cost moved from before ready to after ready but stays on the boot path.
  • apps/desktop/dist-electron/desktopMain.cjs:15291 143 `exports.*` for the lazy chunks (built 21:45, after HEAD, clean tree). 96 are referenced nowhere in main's own body: all NativeIdentity*, PublicSignup*, PasswordLogin*, ExternalIdentity* and ActiveSpaceSwitch* schemas and paths, RelayFrame, RelayProtocolVersion, RELAY_SUPPORTED_VERSION_RANGE and cborg decode$1. desktopHubStack consumes 193 `require_desktopMain.*` references and desktopStack 51. Eager prefix: 78-85 ms uncached, about 53 ms with NODE_COMPILE_CACHE. Within it, effect/Schema takes 46 ms (about 40 ms cached), and all contracts regions about 10-15 ms (settings 2-4, orchestration/threadFork 2-4, environment about 1.5, hostedIdentity about 1.4). Remaining

Only polish remains; the finding's main cost and its estimated gain have been delivered. Leftovers: (1) Hub-only and Computer-use-only contract schemas are evaluated before ready. Rolldown hoists modules shared with the lazy chunks into desktopMain.cjs: 96 chunk-only exports, mainly hostedIdentity.ts native identity schemas and the relay frame schemas in environment.ts, pulled in through desktopHubControl.ts:1-23. Cost is about 3-7 ms. (2) Proposal (b) is only partly done. Barrel imports remain at main.ts:34 (EnvironmentId, used only at main.ts:3823) and clientPersistence.ts:4-11. settings.ts pulls the orchestration schema tree, about 296 KB of contracts eager, about 10-15 ms uncached. (3) effect/Schema, about 40 ms cached, is still required before ready by contracts, clientPersistence and desktopHubControl. Defects in the shipped fix

None that cause a behaviour problem. Gap in the guard (proposal e): desktopMainBundleSplitting.test.ts only walks relative source imports and denylists 5 externals. It passes even though desktopMain.cjs exports 96 Hub- or Computer-use-only schema bindings that the entry evaluates before ready. That is the shared-module hoisting from the eager desktopHubControl.ts import of @ryco/contracts/desktop-native-node-claim, which pulls in hostedIdentity.ts. It also has no byte budget, so 'fails if the eager graph grows' from the proposal is not implemented.
