Partial#7 Renderer cannot fetch or parse any app JS until the backend listens; the ryco:// origin with codeCache is registered but unused

desktop-boot:renderer-serialized-behind-backend · original impact Medium, effort L · Waterfall WP04decision

First-pass audit said PARTIAL; the verifier corrected it. PARTIAL is right, but two of the auditor's claims are too strong: that "the core serialization is gone" and that there is "no concrete defect". (1) The app document and assets are still served by the backend process. The early static handler runs on the backend's event loop, and migrations run synchronously there (node:sqlite DatabaseSync). So a stall while the runtime graph builds still stops the renderer from fetching any app JS. The user's own desktop-main.log after #710 shows 2 of 16 launches where the early-loaded document took 15-18 s to reach dom-ready (server-child.log: 'persistence.migrations (18040 ms, in flight)' plus an event-loop stall). During those stalls the 45f7a9be6 last-known shell could not paint. (2) The bind-time load usually starts about 65-75 ms after the boot page load and aborts it before it commits: boot dom-ready never fired in 14 of 16 launches. During a stall, the reveal fallback then shows a blank window (run 2a6031c40a6b: 'reveal-fallback urlKind=blank' at 428 ms, app dom-ready at 15188 ms). Before #710 the boot splash was visible during stalls. (3) The 9 s staleness heuristic counts from the load request, not from the document's commit, so a document that loaded fine just before ready is reloaded anyway (same run: app dom-ready at 15188 ms, reload at 18386 ms). The auditor's point that 'a slow spawn or bind shows only the boot page' is also inaccurate: the boot page usually never commits.

Current state

Implemented differently, and only in part. The packaged window now loads http://127.0.0.1:PORT when the backend sends `http-bound`, and the backend serves the static shell from its startup gate. The backend is spawned from desktopEntry before the main bundle loads. Together these remove the wait for 'Listening' on normal launches: in the user's logs, window.create to bind is about 100 ms (82-242 ms) and bind to serving about 20-170 ms. The ryco://app proposal was not implemented. The ryco:// scheme is still registered with codeCache through the deprecated registerFileProtocol and is used only as a boot-page fallback. The origin is still http://127.0.0.1:PORT (3773 legacy for existing installs, 7926 for new ones). The shell document still comes from the backend process, so the proposal's main benefit is not achieved: painting cached state through backend stalls. Real launches after #710 show 15-18 s migration stalls on update launches, during which no app document was served. The bind-time load also introduced a blank-window regression during such stalls, plus a redundant reload at ready.

Evidence
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3035-3039 The `http-bound` lifecycle frame calls loadPackagedBackendAppWindowOnBind(), so the app load starts when the port is bound, not at ready.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1717-1771 loadPackagedBackendAppWindow(…, moment) still does window.loadURL(backendHttpUrl) at line 1757, so the document comes from the backend process. The load is gated on rendererCacheMaintenance (line 1752), which waits up to 1.5 s for clearCodeCaches on a version change (line 4773).
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:276-299 The early static handler (desktop mode serves `/` and assets) runs on the backend's own event loop while the gate is closed, and writes the `http-bound` frame at line 295.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/NodeSqliteClient.ts:7,257 Migrations and SQLite access use synchronous node:sqlite DatabaseSync on the backend main thread. A heavy migration blocks the same loop that must serve the early shell.
  • ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/desktop-main.log runs 2a6031c40a6b, 57fddc1a1b24 (outside repo) Run 2a6031c40a6b: bound 243 ms, app load-request 243 ms, reveal-fallback urlKind=blank at 428 ms, app dom-ready 15188 ms, listening 18386 ms, a second app load at ready, dom-ready 18459 ms. Run 57fddc1a1b24: app dom-ready 16005 ms. In server-child.log the same run shows migrations 087/088 taking 18040 ms with an event-loop stall warning.
  • ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/desktop-main.log, 16 runs after #710 (outside repo) In the other 14 runs: window.create to http-bound median about 100 ms (82-242), bind to serving 21-441 ms, launch to shell-usable 534-1442 ms. The boot page never reached dom-ready before the bind-time load replaced it in 14/16 runs.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4553-4556, 2483-2499 The boot page load is followed by a 250 ms reveal fallback that reveals the window even when urlKind is 'blank', which is what happens when the early app navigation aborted the uncommitted boot page.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendAppWindowLoad.ts:30,44-56 EARLY_APP_LOAD_MAX_HOLD_MS = 9 s is measured from requestedAtMs, not from document commit, so a document that loaded late but correctly is reloaded at ready.
  • apps/server/src/httpStartupGate.ts:26; packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.ts:93; packages/client-runtime/src/connection/fetchWithDeadline.ts:11 Held requests get a 503 after 10 s. The client gives up control-plane bootstrap retries after 15 s with a 5 s per-request deadline. Stalls longer than this need the desktop reload at ready.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:236 primary-shell-usable (which the desktop uses as shellUsable) is marked only when a live snapshot is applied. A cached-shell paint does not count, so a failed early boot is reloaded rather than reconnected. This is correct.
  • apps/desktop/src/desktopEntry.ts:158 The early backend spawn happens before desktopMain.cjs loads, which shrinks the remaining window.create-to-bind gap to about 100 ms.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:337-350, 2196, 4375-4382 ryco:// is privileged with codeCache but registered through the deprecated protocol.registerFileProtocol. It is used only as a boot-page fallback. The boot page loads through loadFile (file://).
Remaining

(1) Biggest residual: the renderer document and boot graph are still served by the backend process (apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1757 loads backendHttpUrl, served by the early handler at apps/server/src/server.ts:276-299 on the backend event loop). An event-loop-blocking stall in the runtime graph, such as synchronous node:sqlite migrations on the first launch after an update, still stops the renderer from fetching or parsing any app JS. The cached primary shell (45f7a9be6) therefore cannot paint during exactly the 15-18 s stalls the finding targeted (2 of 16 logged launches after #710). (2) On normal launches the app load still starts at bind, about 100 ms (82-242 ms) after window creation. The window starts on a file:// boot page and swaps to a cross-site http renderer (main.ts:4375-4382 → 1757). (3) The origin is still http://127.0.0.1:PORT (backendPort.ts). The ryco:// codeCache privilege and the deprecated registerFileProtocol (main.ts:337-350, 2196) are effectively unused. (4) Related: on a version change the first app load waits up to 1.5 s for clearCodeCaches (main.ts:1752, 4773).

Defects in the shipped fix

(a) Blank window during stalls: in 14 of 16 launches the bind-time loadURL (main.ts:1757, about 65-75 ms after the boot load request) aborts the not-yet-committed file:// boot page. If the backend then stalls before serving the document, schedulePackagedBootReveal (main.ts:2483-2499) reveals a blank window. Run 2a6031c40a6b stayed blank for about 15 s (reveal-fallback urlKind=blank at 428 ms, app dom-ready at 15188 ms) instead of showing the boot splash it showed before #710. (b) Redundant reload: isAppLoadRequestCurrent (backendAppWindowLoad.ts:44-56) ages the early load from requestedAtMs. After a stall longer than 9 s, ready reloads a document that committed seconds earlier and whose held requests cannot have hit the 10 s 503 yet (same run: dom-ready at 15188 ms, reload at 18386 ms). The cost is about 250 ms plus a re-boot and a flash. (c) The 'bound' path is skipped in development (main.ts:1768), so dev builds never exercise it. That is minor but worth a test hook.

Implementation sketch

Step 1 (S, no decision needed), fix the early-load defects in apps/desktop/src/main.ts and backendAppWindowLoad.ts. (i) Keep a pending app navigation from leaving the window blank: when the reveal fallback fires with urlKind 'blank' while appLoadRequestedFrom has a current request, or when the app navigation has not committed within about 750 ms (track 'did-start-navigation'/'did-navigate' for backendHttpUrl), stop it and call loadDesktopBootPage(window). Delete the appLoadRequestedFrom entry so `ready` loads the app, reusing returnEarlyLoadedWindowsToBootPage's logic. An alternative that keeps the early load is to delay the bound-time loadURL until the boot page's dom-ready, capped at about 100 ms. That costs 0-50 ms on normal launches but keeps the splash visible, because Chromium keeps the committed boot page during the pending navigation. (ii) Age early loads from document commit or dom-ready, not the request: record committedAtMs in AppLoadRequest from 'did-navigate', and treat the request as current while now - (committedAtMs ?? requestedAtMs) < EARLY_APP_LOAD_MAX_HOLD_MS. Add cases to backendAppWindowLoad.test.ts, and assert in boot-report.mjs and startup-timing-smoke.mjs that 'desktop.window.boot.reveal-fallback urlKind=blank' never occurs. Step 2 (M, needs a decision), decouple the shell document from the backend process. The recommended option keeps the origin: in registerDesktopProtocol, use protocol.handle('http') on the default session (Electron 44) only during boot. Serve GET `/`, `/index.html` and `/assets/*` for exactly backendHttpUrl's origin from the bundled static dir, sharing resolveDesktopStaticPath and the path-safety checks with the ryco:// handler. Pass everything else through net.fetch(request, { bypassCustomProtocolHandlers: true }). Call protocol.unhandle('http') at http-serving so steady-state API traffic never hops through main. WebSocket traffic is not intercepted. With that in place, call loadURL(backendHttpUrl) directly from createWindow, so there is no boot page in the normal path. The cached primary shell (same origin, same localStorage/IndexedDB) paints during migrations. Primary bootstrap requests get ECONNREFUSED or are held and retried (primaryAuth retryTransientBootstrap). Extend the desktop path so the renderer keeps retrying, or rely on notifyRenderersToReconnect at ready, instead of failing after 15 s. Test with a fixture home that forces a slow migration, and check shell-usable, primary-cached-sidebar-committed and the absence of a blank reveal in desktop-main.log. Step 3 (L, optional; switching to ryco://app is what fixes the origin): implement the original ryco://app plan. Switch the scheme handler to protocol.handle. Allow ryco://app in browserApiCorsLayer and the WS upgrade origin check. Use bearer/DPoP for the desktop primary environment. Run a one-time migration of origin-scoped storage (composer drafts, primary shell cache, UI state). Drop the codeCache privilege and registerFileProtocol if it is not pursued. Optionally move the version-change clearCodeCaches off the first-load path (main.ts:1752).

Needs a decision

Step 1, the blank-window and redundant-reload fixes, needs no decision. Decoupling the shell from the backend does: either intercept the http backend origin in the Electron session during boot, which is a new security-relevant request path in main, or move to ryco://app. The latter changes desktop primary-environment auth (cookie to bearer/DPoP), adds a CORS/WS origin allowlist entry and needs an origin-storage migration, which calls for a security review and a product trade-off against modest normal-path gains (about 100 ms) and stall-only benefits (update launches with heavy migrations).

Value medium · effort M · risk medium

Done#8 The desktop backend's local trace file writes ~280 KB/s under agent load, 75% of it full SQL text spans

desktop-boot:server-trace-file-volume · original impact Low, effort S · CPU WP16

Current state

Fixed in 60633eff3 (#710), and the fix is confirmed on the running install. LocalFileTracer drops SQL statement spans (any span with db.query.text) that succeed in under 50 ms by default, before they reach either the NDJSON sink or in-memory diagnostics. Failed and slow statements are kept. db.query.text is collapsed to one line, and RYCO_TRACE_SQL_MIN_DURATION_MS=0 turns full SQL tracing back on. Effect's sql Statement sets db.query.text through span.attribute(), which goes through the override, so real SQL spans are matched. In the current ~/.ryco/userdata/logs trace files, server.trace.ndjson.1 has 25,613 records and 0 SQL spans (183 s, 55.8 KB/s); .4 also has 0, and .8 has 3 slow statements, which were kept as intended. The report measured ~250-280 KB/s with 75.8% sql.execute bytes, so the expected ~-200 KB/s and -75% is achieved. Two optional proposal items were not done: a statement hash or id, and a higher trace level or sampling for other high-frequency spans. The core cost the finding described is removed.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/observability/LocalFileTracer.ts:27 DEFAULT_LOCAL_TRACE_SQL_MIN_DURATION_MS = 50 is on by default. ObservabilityLive (server.ts:835) is the only tracer construction site, so the desktop-spawned backend gets it too.
  • apps/server/src/observability/LocalFileTracer.ts:89-101 end() calls spanToTraceRecord and push only when keepsLocalRecord() is true. A db.query.text span that succeeded under the threshold is dropped. Failure, including interruption, is kept. A threshold of 0 keeps everything.
  • apps/server/src/observability/LocalFileTracer.ts:103-112 attribute() stores db.query.text normalized to one line. The OTLP delegate still receives the original redacted value.
  • apps/server/src/observability/Layers/Observability.ts:48-57 diagnosticsSink.push writes to both the file sink and diagnostics.recordTraceRecords. Dropped spans skip JSON.stringify and the in-memory push.
  • apps/server/src/observability/Layers/Observability.ts:23-25 RYCO_TRACE_SQL_MIN_DURATION_MS (Config.Int, default 50) is the opt-in for full SQL tracing, documented at docs/observability.md:515. It is read directly here rather than through ServerConfig/cli.ts like the other RYCO_TRACE_* settings.
  • apps/server/node_modules/effect/dist/sql/Statement.js:738-745 withConnectionSpan sets db.query.text with span.attribute() after creation, which goes through LocalFileSpan.attribute(). Spans are named 'sqlite' or 'sql.execute' depending on db.system.name, but the filter keys on the attribute, so it covers both.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/SqliteReadClient.ts:378-385 The read-worker client builds Statements on the main thread through Client.make, so its spans pass through the same tracer and filter. No second tracer exists in a worker.
  • apps/server/node_modules/effect/dist/internal/effect.js:2709 When TracerTimingEnabled is false, startTime and endTime are 0n (also line 2770). Every successful SQL span is then dropped regardless of threshold. The default is timing on (cli.ts:306), so this does not affect the default path.
  • apps/server/src/observability/LocalFileTracer.test.ts:119-181 Tests cover fast SQL dropped, slow (40 ms against a 25 ms threshold) and failed SQL kept, whitespace normalization, and threshold 0 keeping everything.
  • (local, outside repo) ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/server.trace.ndjson.1 Live check on the current install: 25,613 records, 10.48 MB, 0 db.query.text spans over 183 s (55.8 KB/s, 140 rec/s). .4 matches (57.6 KB/s, 0 SQL); .8 has 3 kept slow statements. The largest remaining spans are orchestration.command.thread.activity.append (1.35 MB), sql.transaction (1.21 MB, 2,292 records) and 7 per-command projector/decider spans of about 0.75 MB each.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationEngine.ts:532 The residual volume source (out of scope for this finding): each dispatched command creates orchestration.command.<type> plus decideOrchestrationCommand (decider.ts:516), applyProjectorsForEvent (ProjectionPipeline.ts:2510), per-projector spans (for example ProjectionPipeline.ts:828 and 2261) and runAttachmentSideEffects (ProjectionPipeline.ts:530). That is about 9 spans and about 3.8 KB per activity-append command.
Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defects found. Minor notes: (1) normalizeSqlText runs eagerly in attribute() (LocalFileTracer.ts:103-110) on every statement, including ones dropped at end(). This is a microsecond-scale regex. (2) With RYCO_TRACE_TIMING_ENABLED=false, all successful SQL spans are dropped whatever the threshold, because durations are 0n. This is acceptable but undocumented. (3) The threshold is a bare Config.Int in Observability.ts:23 rather than part of ServerConfig, unlike the sibling RYCO_TRACE_* settings. An invalid value fails the observability layer at boot, as the sibling ints do. (4) sql.transaction spans carry no db.query.text, so the filter does not cover them. They are about 11.6% of the current trace bytes. (5) The proposal's statement hash or id, and the higher trace level or sampling for high-frequency non-SQL spans, were not implemented.

Done#9 Readiness depends on a stdout log substring plus a 100 ms HTTP poll that lands in the server's pre-listen dead window

desktop-boot:structured-ready-signal · original impact Low, effort S · Reliability WP04

Current state

Implemented in #710 (60633eff3). The server writes http-bound, http-serving, startup-ready, startup-phase and fatal frames on fd 4. Desktop parses them with the shared parser and feeds them into BackendReadinessTracker. The stdout 'Listening on' match stays as a fallback, the HTTP probe only starts after 3 s, and fatal frames or exit code 78 halt the crash loop. The httpStartupGate removes the dead-window hang that made probes cost 1 s. The user's real desktop log confirms that normal boots now fire no HTTP probes. Nuance: in practice the stdout line still wins the race by 0-3 ms on all 16 post-#710 launches (source=listening every time), so the frame works as an always-present backstop rather than as the signal actually used. The robustness goal still holds: if the log line goes away, readiness falls through to the frame about 1 ms later instead of to the HTTP poll. The edge-path issues left are minor.

Evidence
  • packages/shared/src/desktopResourceTelemetry.ts:119-160 DesktopBackendLifecycleFrame union (http-bound, http-serving, startup-ready, startup-phase, fatal) and parseDesktopBackendLifecycleFrame; DESKTOP_BACKEND_FATAL_EXIT_CODE=78.
  • apps/server/src/diagnostics/DesktopResourceTelemetry.ts:86-97 fd 4 Socket created and attachDesktopLifecycleChannel called; invoked from cli.ts:510-512 once the bootstrap envelope says desktop mode.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:280-296 http-bound written after bind; the startup gate is installed before listen (server.ts:258) and the early static handler serves the shell.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:715-724,805-811 http-serving written by httpServingLayer, which is provided by HttpRouter.serve, so it only runs after the handlers are attached (and after Effect's withLogAddress has logged 'Listening on').
  • apps/server/src/httpStartupGate.ts:106-254 Requests and upgrades that arrive before the handlers exist are held and replayed (503 after 10 s or overflow), so a probe no longer hangs in the dead window.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1028-1030 startup-ready is written when the command gate opens.
  • apps/server/src/cliMain.ts:45-52; apps/server/src/startupFailure.ts:55-58 Deterministic failures write a fatal frame and exit 78.
  • apps/desktop/src/desktopResourceTelemetry.ts:101-118 The fd-4 reader passes non-sample frames through the shared parser to onFrame.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3024-3054,3249-3256 handleBackendFrame records phase marks, sends http-serving and fatal to readiness.handleFrame, and loads the window on http-bound.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendStartup.ts:41-120 BackendReadinessTracker: settles on http-serving (with a port check), keeps ServerListeningDetector as the fallback, rejects on fatal.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:326,1599-1615 BACKEND_HTTP_READINESS_FALLBACK_DELAY_MS=3000 is passed as httpFallbackDelayMs.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendStartupReadiness.ts:56-84 The HTTP probe is deferred by the delay and cancelled when the tracker settles.
Defects in the shipped fix

Minor, edge paths only: (1) The no-tracker path still polls HTTP from t=0. waitForBackendStartupReady (apps/desktop/src/backendStartupReadiness.ts:20-23) runs waitForHttpReady at once when readyPromise is null. This happens when ensureInitialBackendWindowOpen runs while no child is tracked: bootstrap's call at main.ts:4872 after the adopted early child has already died (startBackend bails at main.ts:3360-3364), or app 'activate' (main.ts:4931) during a restart backoff. That boot then uses 100 ms / 1 s probes, and the restarted child's frames never settle the in-flight wait, because startBackend's own ensureInitialBackendWindowOpen returns early while that wait is in flight. waitForBackendWindowReady also captures `backendProcess` (null) at call time (main.ts:1600, 1613), so backendReadyChild is null and a later post-ready crash of the replacement counts once as a pre-ready failure. (2) Attribution only: stdout 'Listening on' is logged before the http-serving frame is written, so readiness source=listening on every real boot. The frame is a backstop rather than the primary signal, and the stdout scan still runs on every boot. (3) Fatal frames for failures before fd 4 is attached (bootstrap-envelope-missing, env ConfigError before cli.ts:511) are no-ops. Exit code 78 still halts restarts and the stderr tail carries the reason.

Implementation sketch

Optional cleanup, Effort S: (a) In apps/desktop/src/main.ts ensureInitialBackendWindowOpen: if backendReadiness === null (no live child), only call ensurePackagedBootstrapWindowOpen and return. startBackend already calls ensureInitialBackendWindowOpen (main.ts:3367) once a child and tracker exist. Alternatively, remove the immediate-HTTP branch in waitForBackendStartupReady for the packaged path. (b) Store the child on the tracker, or capture it at startBackend, and set backendReadyChild from the child whose tracker settled instead of from `backendProcess` at call time. (c) To make the frame primary: in apps/server/src/server.ts call HttpRouter.serve(..., { disableListenLog: true }) and log `Listening on http://host:port` from httpServingLayer right after writeDesktopLifecycleFrame. Older desktops keep the log line; new desktops see the frame first. Tests: add a backendStartupReadiness test for 'no tracker means no immediate poll', or a main-level unit for the guard; add a server test that the http-serving frame is written after the request/upgrade listeners are attached and before the 'Listening on' log.

Done#10 Shell-env cache has a hard 7-day TTL with a blocking refresh before backend spawn

desktop-boot:shell-env-stale-while-revalidate · original impact Low, effort S · Blocking I/O

Current state

Confirmed as DONE. readShellEnvironmentCache has no TTL. A cache of any age is a hit, and only version, platform, capturedAt, an empty environment or a shell change cause a miss. The packaged entry applies the cache synchronously before the early backend spawn. main.ts applies it on hits (dev and fallback) without waiting and schedules a refresh in the worker 5 s after handleBackendReady. A failed capture keeps the PATH already in effect. A first launch with no cache waits for one capture, but the early backend loads its modules meanwhile and gets the environment through the bootstrap envelope, which cli.ts applies before any layer builds. No other caller of the login shell on the desktop path still blocks the backend on a stale cache.

Evidence
  • packages/shared/src/shellEnvironment.ts:390-447 No age-based invalidation. ageMs is only reported. The miss reasons are unreadable, version, platform, capturedAt, environment and shell.
  • apps/desktop/src/desktopEntry.ts:66-80,160-166 The packaged entry applies the cache to process.env before startEarlyBackend.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:737-760 A hit, whether applied by the entry or here, sets shellEnvironmentRefreshScheduled and returns at once. Only a miss awaits the capture.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:767-774,1618-1620 A delayed stale-while-revalidate refresh runs from handleBackendReady and is skipped while quitting.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:695-728 A failed or aborted capture leaves the existing PATH and cache in place. A successful one rewrites the cache. Probes start from the inherited PATH, so stale cache entries are not carried forward.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4848-4856,3165 On a packaged miss the boot window is shown, the early backend is already loading, and the captured environment goes into the envelope.
  • apps/server/src/cli.ts:509 applyBootstrapShellEnvironment (bootstrap.ts:33-40) applies the envelope environment before layers build.
  • packages/shared/src/shellEnvironment.test.ts:57 Test covers an aged record still returning a hit with ageMs. desktopEntry.test.ts and bootstrap.test.ts cover the entry and envelope paths.

Current state

Both layers of the proposal shipped in 60633eff3 (#710). The preload caches a frozen bootstrap after the first complete answer. The web layer memoizes the desktop primary target per bridge in a WeakMap. After the first complete answer none of them reaches the sync IPC again. None verified. Three minor notes, none of them a defect. (1) No unit test covers the preload-level cache. Only the web-layer memo is tested. Done#13 Main window uses the default v8CacheOptions; after each update, code cache kicks in only on the 3rd launch

desktop-boot:renderer-v8-code-cache-heat · original impact Low, effort S · Caching WP04

Current state

The core fix is in place. The main window sets v8CacheOptions "bypassHeatCheck". A packaged-only, version-keyed prune clears the renderer code cache with a 1.5 s bound before the first app load. It works on the user's install: Code Cache is 46 MB (the finding saw 310 MB) and the marker reads 0.1.31. The main window is created by a single function and denies child windows, so no other window loads the Ryco boot graph with default options. Changed chunks now warm one launch earlier, as the finding proposed. Defect: the prune clears the whole code cache, which partly cancels that gain. On the first launch after each update, stable vendor chunks that used to load warm now compile cold, while the boot chunk compiles cold either way. The skipped HTTP-cache clear is reasonable: Chromium bounds that cache (773 MB now), and keeping it is what lets stable chunks stay valid. The defect is low impact, so the status stays DONE.

Evidence
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4397-4406 createWindow() webPreferences set v8CacheOptions: "bypassHeatCheck". createWindow is the only factory for Ryco app windows (callers at 1691, 1712, 2225, 2268), and setWindowOpenHandler (4488) denies child windows, so no other window runs the boot graph with default options.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4747-4771 pruneRendererCachesOnVersionChange() calls session.defaultSession.clearCodeCaches({}) on any app.getVersion() change, an unfiltered wipe that includes still-valid entries for unchanged hashed chunks. The marker is written only after success, so a failed clear is retried on the next launch.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4811-4815 The prune runs only when app.isPackaged, starts at the top of bootstrap and is bounded by boundedRendererCacheMaintenance (1.5 s, 4774-4783).
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1752-1758 loadPackagedBackendAppWindow waits for rendererCacheMaintenance before loadURL(backendHttpUrl).
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4580-4588 The did-fail-load fallback (the boot page failed to load) calls window.loadURL(backendHttpUrl) without waiting for rendererCacheMaintenance. This is a rare path with trivial impact.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/codeSplitting.ts:18-23 boot-vendor (React, router, Effect, Base UI) is deliberately kept byte-stable across app-only deploys, and lexical, markdown and Shiki get their own stable groups (lines 28-31). Their code-cache entries stay valid across such updates, but the blanket prune discards them.
  • apps/web/dist/assets/boot-vendor-BQ6g4P2-.js In the local build, boot-vendor is 707,326 bytes and boot-D36cWeP2.js is 894,988 bytes. Stable vendor code is about 44% of the boot graph that the prune makes cold on the first launch after each update.
  • apps/server/src/http.ts:50 Hashed assets are served with 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable' (applied at line 121). The HTTP cache is not cleared, so an unchanged chunk keeps its URL and response time, and its V8 code-cache entry would still validate.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4676-4709 selectDesktopBackendPort keeps a persisted port, so the renderer origin (part of the code-cache key) is stable across launches and updates. The bypassHeatCheck gain therefore holds.
  • ~/Library/Application Support/ryco (outside repo, read-only du) Packaged userData shows 'Code Cache' at 46 MB (310 MB in the finding), 'Cache' at 773 MB (Chromium-bounded; 890 MB in the finding), and renderer-cache-version = 0.1.31. The prune runs in production.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4754 pruneRendererCachesOnVersionChange and boundedRendererCacheMaintenance are referenced only in main.ts, and no test covers them. All of this landed in 60633eff3 (#710).
Defects in the shipped fix

On every version change, the unfiltered session.defaultSession.clearCodeCaches({}) at apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4760 also discards V8 code-cache entries for chunks whose content hash did not change. The web build deliberately keeps these stable across app-only deploys: boot-vendor is ~707 KB of the ~1.6 MB boot graph (codeSplitting.ts:18-23), plus the lexical, markdown and Shiki groups. Those entries would still validate: same URL, the persisted port keeps the origin stable, and the retained immutable HTTP cache keeps the same response time. Effect on the first launch after each nightly: the vendor half of the boot graph compiles cold where it used to load warm. Estimated at roughly 10-20 ms (not measured), which partly offsets the finding's gain for that launch; the gain on the second launch is unaffected. Minor: the did-fail-load fallback loadURL(backendHttpUrl) at main.ts:4587 does not wait for rendererCacheMaintenance, and the prune and bounded-maintenance logic has no unit tests.

Implementation sketch

Replace the blanket clear with a targeted one, extracted into a testable module such as apps/desktop/src/rendererCodeCachePrune.ts. 1. Write the marker as JSON {version, electron: process.versions.electron, origin, assets: string[]} instead of a bare version. assets lists the hashed /assets/*.js|*.mjs|*.wasm names from resolveDesktopStaticDir() (main.ts:2119). Read the directory once with FS.promises.readdir; it holds about 200 files. origin is the backendHttpUrl origin, so the marker is written after port selection, or the previously persisted port is recorded. 2. On launch, read the old marker and decide: - Missing or unparsable (legacy plain-text marker): clearCodeCaches({}), the current behaviour. - prev.electron !== current: clearCodeCaches({}). V8 rejects cached data from another V8 version anyway, so this costs nothing. - prev.version !== current version: compute removed = prev.assets minus current assets and call session.defaultSession.clearCodeCaches({ urls: removed.map(name => `${prev.origin}/assets/${name}`) }). Electron matches the resource URL exactly, and Chromium's remover keys by resource URL. Skip the call when removed is empty. - If the origin changed, the old origin's entries are dead; clear everything. Keep boundedRendererCacheMaintenance and the loadURL gate as they are. Also wrap the did-fail-load fallback at main.ts:4587 in rendererCacheMaintenance.then(...). Tests (vitest, in the new module): a pure decide(prevMarker, current) function returning 'none' | {kind:'all'} | {kind:'urls', urls}. Cover legacy-marker migration, Electron bump, app-only bump with partial asset overlap (only removed URLs are listed), identical asset sets (no clear), origin change, and the timeout helper resolving after the bound. To validate in a packaged build: install build N, launch twice, then install N+1 with only app changes (boot-vendor hash unchanged). On N+1's first launch, check chrome://tracing or performance 'v8.compile' / the boot-report script (apps/desktop/scripts/boot-report.mjs): boot-vendor should consume its cache (v8.compile with consume) while boot produces one. The Code Cache directory should stay bounded over several updates.

The serverBundleBoundaries test guards the closures of bin.ts and stdioProxy.ts but not bridge.ts. That residual is a small follow-up, not a reason to reopen. No functional regressions found. CursorAdapter is the only stdio-proxy caller and ProviderInjection still passes [argv1, proxy arg]. The externalSetup bridge args match bin.ts's fast-path parser exactly. The CLI has no other `mcp` subcommand that could fall through to cliMain. Current state

PARTIAL confirmed. Since f1be4abc7 (60633eff3, ecd6e206a): the credential hydrate and Hub restoreSession start at bootstrap through prepareResume and are adopted by the post-ready resume; the GitHub read overlaps setup and enrollment; one security helper serves each burst of requests (2 s idle); and desktop.hub.resume.start/end marks exist. I found no other implementation of the rest. Still missing: only #setup should wait for backend readiness, but the whole #run still starts in resumeDesktopHostedIdentityForBackend. So credentials.flush, nativeE2eeEnrollment.ensure (helper ops plus the upsert RTT) and the GitHub read all still start after readiness. The auditor also missed one step: the device catalog listNodes RTT runs strictly after #run, in DesktopWorkspaceClient.#adoptIdentity -> refreshCatalog. So 'catalog ready' after backend-ready is still flush + max(setup, enrollment, github) + cache.list + listNodes RTT + per-node trust reads. The remaining gain depends on config. With the connector enabled (background claim allowed, this user's setup), setup is about 2 Hub RTTs plus about 6 backend control calls and already hides enrollment and GitHub, so moving those earlier gains about 0. With a standby connector, setup is local-only and moving them saves about 1 RTT plus helper ops.

(1) Only #setup should wait for backend readiness, but the whole #run still starts post-ready via resumeDesktopHostedIdentityForBackend (apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1256, called at 1676/1806). credentials.flush (desktopHostedIdentity.ts:559), nativeE2eeEnrollment.ensure(accountId) (572; helper ops plus Hub upsert RTT) and #readGitHubState (569) need only the account session, yet start after readiness. The helper is reused per burst (2 s), not long-lived, so the bootstrap and post-ready bursts usually launch separate helpers. No correctness defect in the implemented parts. Checked: a prepared 'unavailable' outcome is never adopted (desktopHostedIdentity.ts:346), so an offline launch only re-restores. disconnect() awaits #idle and clears #preparedRestore before clearing credentials (390-397). Point desktop's refreshDirectory (219-221) at desktopWorkspaceClient?.refreshCatalog() or drop it, so each launch no longer pays a discarded listNodes. D. Add markDesktopStartupPhase('desktop.hub.resume.prepare') in prepareDesktopHostedIdentityResume (main.ts:1279), plus a mark when the prepared restore settles. Tests in desktopHostedIdentity.test.ts: prepareResume followed by resume() calls upsert, GitHub configuration/security and flush exactly once; an account mismatch or signed-out outcome discards the prefetch; disconnect during the prefetch prevents adoption; enrollment still runs on resume when prepare was skipped. Server process boot (14)

Done#17 Port is bound 70–305 ms before any request handler exists; requests in that window hang forever

server-boot:http-accept-before-handler · original impact High, effort S · Reliability

Current state

Confirmed DONE. On the Node path (production, desktop, `ryco serve`, and dev, which runs `node --watch`), HttpServerLive passes NodeHttpServer.layer a createServer factory that installs httpStartupGate before the platform calls server.listen(). The gate has provisional 'request'/'upgrade' listeners and a 'newListener' hook. Early requests and upgrades are parked in a bounded set (256 entries, 10 s). They are replayed on nextTick once Effect's serve attaches its real handlers. Overflow, deadline and close-while-gated all get 503 + Retry-After. This is proposal (a). An integration test proves a request sent before HttpRouter.serve attaches gets 200. I found no route shadowed by the early static path, no other in-process HTTP listener with the bind-before-handler pattern, and no Hub equivalent. The 10 s cap (shorter than the proposed 30 s) is covered by the clients: client-runtime bootstrap retries 502-504 for 15 s, and desktop re-loads an early (bind-time) window at ready when bind-to-serve took longer than 9 s. Remaining nits are low-value: the Bun branch is ungated (early requests get platform-bun's default 404), and no server-level test pins that HttpServerLive wires the gate.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:250-267 The NodeHttpServer.layer factory calls NodeHttp.createServer(), optionally the loopback compression 'upgrade' hook, then installHttpStartupGate(server). All of this runs before the platform's listen.

Handlers are attached only in serve via server.on('request'/'upgrade') at :126-127, not :117-118 as cited. Both are plain .on() calls, so the gate's 'newListener' hook sees them. The repo's platform-node patch does not touch this.
  • apps/server/src/httpStartupGate.ts:122-168 gateRequest/gateUpgrade hold early items in bounded sets with an unref'd 10 s timer. On overflow or deadline they answer 503 + Retry-After: 1. Held entries are dropped on response/socket close, so aborted desktop probes do not leak entries.
  • apps/server/src/httpStartupGate.ts:170-215 newListener marks the handler attached synchronously and replays held items on process.nextTick. Effect attaches both handlers synchronously, so both exist before the replay. The gate listeners and the close override are then removed.
  • apps/server/src/httpStartupGate.ts:219-241 If startup fails while gated, the close override answers held items with 503 first. The platform's shutdown finalizer looks up server.close at call time, so it hits the override.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:268-300 While gated, the early static handler serves assets in every mode and '/' only in desktop. It uses the same serveStaticRequest (http.ts:852-940) as the router's GET * catch-all.   • apps/server/src/httpStartupGate.test.ts:182-219 Regression test with the real Effect Node server. A GET sent while the routes layer is blocked on a Deferred, before serve attaches, resolves 200 'pong'. Unit tests at :80-158 cover the upgrade replay, overflow, deadline and close-while-gated cases.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.ts:95-135 Bootstrap control-plane requests retry 502/503/504 (and timeouts) for up to 15 s. A 503 from the gate's 10 s cap becomes a retry, not a hard failure.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendAppWindowLoad.ts:23-30 Desktop loads the window at http-bound and sets EARLY_APP_LOAD_MAX_HOLD_MS = 9 s. If bind-to-serve exceeds the gate's hold, the window is loaded again at ready, so held requests that got a 503 do not strand the renderer.

The bin shebang is node (tsdown.config.ts:60) and dev uses `node --watch`, so this is effectively unused.
Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness defects in the shipped Node path. Minor, non-blocking gaps: (1) The Bun branch at apps/server/src/server.ts:236-244 is ungated. Done#18 Synchronous interactive login shell blocks the event loop at every web/CLI boot, and its timeout cannot stop a hanging .zshrc

server-boot:login-shell-sync-path · original impact High, effort S · Blocking I/O WP03

Current state

Confirmed DONE for the described cost and bug. PR #710 (60633eff3) moved the login-shell logic into @ryco/shared/shellEnvironment, shared with desktop. The server now applies a cached PATH synchronously (measured 0 ms) and refreshes it asynchronously 3 s after start. A cache miss runs a bounded sync probe: SIGKILL, 1.5 s, cwd = homedir, stdin ignored. I measured it killing a TERM-ignoring interactive zsh at 1,503 ms (ETIMEDOUT, SIGKILL). A hanging rc can no longer stop the server from listening. Two gaps remain. (1) A shell that always takes longer than 1.5 s never produces a cache entry, so every boot repeats the blocking 1.5 s probe and still gets no login PATH. This regresses service-managed servers whose rc takes 1.5 to 5 s: they used to get PATH and now never do. (2) The win32 branch still runs PowerShell synchronously on every boot, with no cache.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:710 fixPath is still called synchronously at the top of makeServerLayer, before any layer is built. On a cache hit it only reads a small JSON file.
  • apps/server/src/os-jank.ts:129-142 Cache hit: applyShellEnvironmentCache runs synchronously. The refresh uses resolveShellEnvironmentAsync (non-blocking) via setTimeout(3000).unref() (lines 28, 52-54). Measured: the cache read on this machine took 0 ms and hit a record captured today.
  • apps/server/src/os-jank.ts:144-150 Cache miss: the bounded sync probe runs, then remember(). remember() returns early for an empty environment (line 118), and nothing is scheduled. os-jank.test.ts:297-315 asserts that no refresh is scheduled on a miss. So a probe that always times out never writes a cache, and every boot blocks 1.5 s again.
  • packages/shared/src/shellEnvironment.ts:69,289-307 SHELL_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS=1500, killSignal SIGKILL, cwd homedir(), stdio ['ignore','pipe','pipe']. The executor drops the caller's options (timeout 5000/2000 in shell.ts), so the bound always applies. Measured: `zsh -ic 'trap "" TERM; sleep 6'` returned ETIMEDOUT/SIGKILL after 1,503 ms. The real probe took 319 ms sync and 176 ms async.
  • packages/shared/src/shellEnvironment.ts:239-281,309-324 The async refresh runs off the critical path but uses the same 1.5 s bound. An rc file taking 1.5 to 5 s used to yield PATH (old 5 s timeout) and now never does.
  • apps/server/src/os-jank.ts:109-112 win32 still calls resolveShellEnvironmentSync, which runs PowerShell (pwsh.exe, then powershell.exe, possibly a second pass with the profile loaded) on the main thread on every non-desktop boot, with no cache. It is now bounded at 1.5 s per spawn, down from 5 s.
  • packages/shared/src/shellEnvironment.ts:396-469,481-489 Cache read/write and the worker body are shared. apps/desktop/src/shellEnvironmentCache.ts is deleted. apps/desktop/src/shellEnvironmentWorker.ts only calls runShellEnvironmentWorker(). Desktop applies the cache and refreshes with the same helpers (apps/desktop/src/main.ts:695-771, desktopEntry.ts:66-80). The cache path matches the server's <RYCO_HOME>/userdata/shell-environment-cache.json.
  • apps/server/src/service/nodeService.ts:25 Service units still carry no PATH, so service-managed servers rely on the probe or cache. This is the population hurt by gap (1).
  • packages/shared/src/shellEnvironment.test.ts:346-359 Tests cover the async executor's SIGKILL bound, homedir cwd and closed stdin. The sync executor has no direct test, but I checked its behaviour empirically.
Defects in the shipped fix

(1) No background retry or negative cache after a failed miss probe (apps/server/src/os-jank.ts:117-150). If the user's interactive login shell always takes longer than 1.5 s, the sync probe is killed, the environment is empty, and remember() skips it (line 118). No refresh is scheduled, so every boot pays the full 1.5 s per candidate shell. The server also never gets the login PATH. A terminal launch still has the inherited PATH and only loses time. A launchd/systemd service (units carry no PATH) runs without nvm/homebrew/~/.local entries, so provider CLIs are reported missing. Before the fix, an rc taking 1.5 to 5 s did yield PATH. The async refresh does not need the 1.5 s bound because it is off the critical path, but it uses it (shellEnvironment.ts:309-324). (2) The win32 branch (os-jank.ts:109-112) still runs one or two synchronous PowerShell spawns before listen on every non-desktop boot, with no cache. Desktop on Windows already uses the cache plus a worker. Minor and not worth reopening: a cached PATH can sit ahead of a fresher inherited terminal PATH for about the first 3 s, until the refresh, so boot-time provider probes may see a stale binary. Provider snapshots re-probe within 5 minutes.

Implementation sketch

Gap 1 (S): in packages/shared/src/shellEnvironment.ts, give createBoundedShellExecFile and resolveShellEnvironmentAsync an optional timeoutMs. Add SHELL_REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS (e.g. 10_000) and keep SIGKILL, homedir cwd and closed stdin. In apps/server/src/os-jank.ts fixPath, factor the hit-path refresh closure into a local refresh(). Use it on the hit path as today, and also on the miss path whenever the sync result has no PATH (timed out or failed). Pass the longer timeout in both cases. A slow-rc user then pays the 1.5 s block once, the background refresh writes the cache, and later boots hit it. Optionally use the same longer bound for desktop's stale-while-revalidate refresh: pass a timeout through workerData in captureShellEnvironment/runShellEnvironmentWorker, and raise captureShellEnvironment's overall timeoutMs for the refresh call only (apps/desktop/src/main.ts:695-725). Tests: in os-jank.test.ts, the sync readEnvironment throws while the injected async reader returns a PATH. Assert scheduleRefresh is called on the miss, env.PATH is updated after refresh() and the cache file is written. Replace the 'probes once' test expectation only for the failed-probe case. In shellEnvironment.test.ts, assert createBoundedShellExecFile honours a custom timeout. Gap 2 (M, low priority): on win32 in fixPath, read the cache (platform win32), apply it and refresh off the main thread. Either add an async Windows resolver in packages/shared/src/shell.ts, using createBoundedShellExecFile for PowerShell and resolveCommandPathAsync for the node check, or ship a server worker entry that calls runShellEnvironmentWorker. Keep the current bounded sync path for a miss. Add a win32 cache-hit test to os-jank.test.ts with injected readers.

Done#19 getCommandReadModel runs 3× per boot, and its actionable-activity query full-scans the activity table (0.24–2 s each on a real 9 GB DB, synchronous)

server-boot:command-read-model-scan · original impact High, effort S · Database

Current state

Confirmed DONE, verified independently, including against the real 9.8 GB state DB opened read-only. Migration 085 (60633eff3) adds the kind-led index idx_projection_thread_activities_kind_order. The actionable-activity query now plans as 'SEARCH ... USING INDEX idx_projection_thread_activities_kind_order (kind=?)' plus a temp B-tree for the ORDER BY, and returns 482 of 625,420 rows in 5-7 ms (the report measured 0.24-2 s). The DB has no sqlite_stat tables and the server never runs ANALYZE or PRAGMA optimize, so the heuristic plan the unit tests pin is the plan production gets. workspace.validate returns before reading any model when the workspace is unrestricted. reconcileOrphanedProviderSessions, RestartContinuation.dispatchPending and ThreadPurgeReactor read the engine's in-memory model through currentCommandReadModel. The only production engine (OrchestrationEngine.ts:662) implements getReadModel, so the SQL fallback is reachable only from test doubles. Partial#20 Every boot runs cold capability probes for every enabled provider: 15 child processes, ~1.9 GB peak process-tree RSS, and Claude Code credential refresh

server-boot:boot-provider-probes · original impact High, effort M · Process spawns WP01decision

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

Most of the fix is real. Construction and boot no longer probe. Persisted snapshots carry a probe fingerprint and are adopted for 6 h. Background revalidation is demand-driven, starts after the first config snapshot, runs at concurrency 2 and staggers starts by 250 ms. The Claude probe is MCP-free, OpenCode reuses its verified version, the npm latest-version cache is on disk, and the Claude OAuth refresh/writeback is deleted. Proposal 1 is not met for the most common accounts, though. Any snapshot that carries rateLimits is adopted for only 5 minutes, and the full rich probe then reruns instead of a cheap usage refresh. That covers Claude with a claude.ai login, Codex with a ChatGPT login and OpenCode with Go usage. The usage probe in the original measurement read the keychain, so the measured Claude had such a login. On that machine, any restart more than 5 minutes after the last probe still cold-probes the Claude SDK session and codex app-server once the first client subscribes. In desktop that client is the renderer at launch. Non-ready outcomes and Ryco updates also force full probes. The auditor's DONE overstates this: the fan-out is much smaller, but it is not gone for these accounts.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/makeManagedServerProvider.ts:45-50,82-87,320-331 Construction never probes: lastRefreshAttemptAtMs starts null, the settings stream is Stream.never for every driver, and refreshInterval is null in all six built-in drivers (ClaudeDriver.ts:213, CodexDriver.ts:209, CopilotDriver.ts:109, CursorDriver.ts:149, GrokDriver.ts:128, OpenCodeDriver.ts:177). The old fork at :272-275 is gone.
  • apps/server/src/provider/makeManagedServerProvider.ts:291-318 adoptPersistedSnapshot uses the 6 h window only when snapshot.rateLimits is undefined (:302-305). Otherwise it uses the 5-minute snapshotFreshness. After that, revalidate reruns the whole checkProvider (models, slash commands, account and usage). Proposal 1 wanted rich data fresh for hours, with at most a cheap check at boot.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeProvider.ts:538-552 rateLimits are attached whenever the instance uses a claude.ai login (resolveClaudeLoginStore), which covers the typical Pro/Max subscriber, so that Claude snapshot gets only the 5-minute window.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexProvider.ts:371-396 ChatGPT-backed Codex accounts always carry rateLimits, so they also get the 5-minute window and re-spawn codex app-server on a restart after 5 minutes.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/OpenCodeProvider.ts:514-520 OpenCode with Go usage carries rateLimits, so it gets the 5-minute window and re-runs opencode --version and opencode serve (739 MiB in the measurement).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderRegistry.ts:100-101 Only ready and disabled outcomes are persisted as fresh. An installed but unauthenticated Copilot (error) re-runs copilot --headless on every first subscribe. So does OpenCode with zero connected providers (warning), which re-runs opencode serve.
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerProbeFingerprint.ts:120-131 The fingerprint includes packageJson.version, so every Ryco update invalidates every persisted snapshot. The first launch after an update probes every provider, at concurrency 2 and without MCP.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderRegistry.ts:88-94,583-607,725-758,840-868 Boot reads persisted snapshots, and settleBootArrival adopts a snapshot when its fingerprint matches. Stale sources are probed only by a background pass at concurrency 2 with 250 ms staggered starts. Instances added or rebuilt by a settings change still probe at once, at concurrency 4.
  • apps/server/src/ws/providerRpc.ts:755-766 revalidateStale is forked after the subscribeServerConfig snapshot has been pulled. The desktop renderer and every reconnecting web or mobile client subscribe right away, so stale providers (including the 5-minute rate-limited ones) are probed during desktop launch and on every reconnect more than 5 minutes after the last probe. Proposal 2 said 'never at boot in desktop', and that is not met for these providers.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1153-1158 The boot gate is released in markHttpServing. Drivers are built after the listener serves, which replaces the desktop-only 100 ms sleep.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeProvider.ts:341-356 The capability probe passes mcpServers: {} and strictMcpConfig: true. SDK 0.3.296 sdk.d.ts:2313-2320 documents that this also excludes plugin and agent-frontmatter MCP servers, so proposal 3 is done.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeUsage.ts:255-277 Expired tokens yield undefined. No refresh and no keychain or file writeback remain; grep finds no refresh_token or writeCredentials in apps/server/src. Proposal 6 is done.
Remaining

1. On a typical restart, rate-limited providers still get a full cold probe. adoptPersistedSnapshot (makeManagedServerProvider.ts:302-305) gives any snapshot with rateLimits only the 5-minute window, and revalidate then reruns the whole checkProvider. For Claude with a claude.ai login (ClaudeProvider.ts:543-552) that means claude --version, a Claude SDK session process, a security spawn and an HTTPS call. For Codex with a ChatGPT login (CodexProvider.ts:371-386) it is a codex app-server. For OpenCode with Go usage (OpenCodeProvider.ts:514) it is opencode --version plus opencode serve. These start 250 to 500 ms after the first client's config snapshot (providerRpc.ts:755-766, ProviderRegistry.ts:583-607): during desktop launch, and on every reconnect more than 5 minutes later. Proposal 1 (rich data fresh for hours, only a cheap check at boot) is not implemented for these accounts, and proposal 2's 'never at boot in desktop' is not met for them. 2. Expensive non-ready outcomes re-probe on every first subscribe (ProviderRegistry.ts:100-101), for example an installed but unauthenticated Copilot (copilot --headless) or OpenCode with no connected providers (opencode serve). 3. Every Ryco update invalidates all fingerprints (providerProbeFingerprint.ts:125), so the first launch after an update probes every provider. 4. A related path outside boot: the mobile Limits tab (useStatisticsData.ts:43) force-refreshes every provider on every node at concurrency 4 just to read usage.

Defects in the shipped fix

No functional bug found in the implemented code. The adoption, single-flight, stagger, gate and fingerprint logic is consistent and covered by tests: makeManagedServerProvider.test.ts:613-760 and ProviderRegistry.test.ts:1131, 1601, 1710 and 3129-3173. Minor correctness gaps, not perf defects: - On macOS the Claude fingerprint's auth file (.credentials.json) does not change on a keychain login or logout, and the Copilot and Grok fingerprints have no auth inputs. An API-key or Copilot auth change can therefore show the old ready state for up to 6 h until an explicit refresh. - The Codex fingerprint ignores config.toml, so model or provider edits there are also not picked up for up to 6 h. - An adopted snapshot starts no enrichment, so the version advisory can be up to 6 h stale.

Implementation sketch

A. Decouple usage-limit freshness from capability freshness. - In makeManagedServerProvider, add an optional input refreshUsage: (snapshot) => Effect<ServerProvider | undefined>. - Track two windows in ProviderSnapshotState: capabilityFreshUntilMs (6 h for an adopted snapshot) and usageFreshUntilMs (checkedAt + 5 min). - adoptPersistedSnapshot always grants the capability window. - revalidateSnapshot: if capabilities are fresh but usage is stale and refreshUsage exists, run refreshUsage (single-flight, under refreshSemaphore) and publish snapshot+rateLimits instead of calling checkProvider. Otherwise keep the current behaviour. - Expose isFresh as 'capabilities fresh', plus a new isUsageFresh, so ProviderRegistry.revalidateOneSource (ProviderRegistry.ts:563-575) can choose the cheap path and skip probeSource. The cheap path must not change the persisted probeFreshness. - ClaudeDriver: refreshUsage = resolveClaudeLoginStore(makeClaudeEnvironment(...), account) followed by the existing cached probeUsage (keychain read plus one HTTPS call, no SDK session, no --version). This needs the probed tokenSource and subscriptionType persisted, either in the snapshot's auth metadata (claudeAuthMetadata already carries authMethod and subscriptionType) or as a small extra field. - Codex: there is no process-free usage path, so pick one: (a) keep 5 minutes for ChatGPT accounts but strip stale rateLimits on adoption and let usage arrive from live turns or an on-open targeted refresh; or (b) accept a codex app-server only when a usage surface asks for it. Choosing between them is the product decision. - OpenCode: refreshUsage = probeUsage(environment) (Go usage over HTTP), with no opencode serve. - Tests: - makeManagedServerProvider.test.ts: an adopted snapshot with rateLimits stays capability-fresh for 6 h; revalidate after 5 minutes calls refreshUsage, not checkProvider. - ProviderRegistry.test.ts: the background pass over a usage-stale, capability-fresh source spawns no probe. B. Optionally persist non-ready outcomes with a short window (15-30 min) when every failing input is covered by the fingerprint (missing binary, auth files), so an unauthenticated Copilot or an OpenCode with no providers does not respawn its server on every first subscribe. Change isPersistableProbeOutcome (ProviderRegistry.ts:100-101) to return a window instead of a boolean. C. Mobile Limits: in useStatisticsData.ts:42-45, stop calling refreshProviders() for all instances. Read the current providers (config snapshot or getConfig), then refreshInstance only for instances that carry rateLimits, or call a new usage-only RPC backed by refreshUsage from A. Dedupe per node and keep range changes from re-triggering it. Add a unit test that the limits tab does not call the all-provider refresh. D. Optional: replace packageJson.version in the fingerprint (providerProbeFingerprint.ts:125) with PROBE_FINGERPRINT_FORMAT plus a hash of the snapshot schema, so updates that do not change probe semantics keep the persisted snapshots. This is low priority because it is one boot per update.

Needs a decision

This is a product trade-off over how fresh usage limits must be when the UI shows them. The current 5-minute rule is deliberate: the composer and the Limits panel render rateLimits as current, and the user explicitly wants per-subscription usage there. Decoupling them means either showing usage that can be up to 6 h old, hiding usage until a cheap refresh lands, or keeping a codex app-server spawn for ChatGPT usage. Persisting non-ready outcomes is a similar staleness trade-off.

Value medium · effort M · risk medium

Done#21 Enable the V8 compile cache for the backend (desktop and CLI)

server-boot:node-compile-cache · original impact Medium, effort S · Build config WP03

Current state

Confirmed DONE. In #710 (60633eff3), apps/server/src/bin.ts became a tiny entry shim: its only static imports are compileCache.ts and stdioProxyProtocol.ts. It enables the V8 compile cache, then loads the server graph by dynamic import. The built dist/bin.mjs is 3.2 KB, and its only static import is node:module. Desktop enables the cache for the packaged Electron backend through `--require compileCache.cjs` plus a per-version userData directory. This covers both the early-spawn and the restart paths, and old version directories are pruned. The server calls flushCompileCache after 'startup phase complete'. On this machine the installed Ryco.app writes entries under its own Electron tag (v24.21.0-arm64-8c6a5e03), so the cache works in the packaged app. Two small side effects were found. (1) The desktop sets RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR in its own process.env. Every provider agent session inherits it (only terminals and side questions strip RYCO_*). Any Ryco dev server or CLI that an agent runs under Homebrew Node or Bun then writes into the packaged app's version directory, which Node never evicts. (2) The 'Absent under Bun' comments are wrong: Bun 1.4.x implements module.enableCompileCache.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/bin.ts:10-11 The only static imports are stdioProxyProtocol.ts and compileCache.ts. enableCompileCacheBestEffort() runs at line 34. Every heavy graph is a dynamic import: device host at :39, stdio proxy at :47, MCP bridge at :51, cliMain at :75.
  • apps/server/dist/bin.mjs:3 The built entry (3,226 bytes, newer than HEAD) has one static import, `node:module`. The cliMain, stdioProxy, bridge and deviceHostWorker chunks are dynamic imports (lines 46-69), so the cache is enabled before the 4.8 MB graph is compiled.
  • apps/server/src/serverBundleBoundaries.test.ts:125-133 There IS a regression test, contrary to the auditor. 'keeps the process entry free of the server graph' asserts that bin.ts's static closure is exactly {bin.ts, stdioProxyProtocol.ts, compileCache.ts} with externals ['node:module']. Lines 210-218 also assert that a current built bin.mjs has no static chunk imports.
  • apps/server/src/compileCache.ts:36-55 Best-effort enable (RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR, else NODE_COMPILE_CACHE, else tmpdir) and flush. The doc comments at :34 and :50 say the API is absent under Bun. That is false for Bun 1.4.x: `bun -e` shows enableCompileCache/flushCompileCache are functions, and Bun writes a v1.4.0-aarch64-* cache directory.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1142-1147 flushCompileCacheBestEffort() runs right after 'startup phase complete', in both the headless and browser branches. This is proposal part 3.
  • apps/desktop/src/desktopEntry.ts:35-48 enableDesktopCompileCache sets process.env.RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR = userData/compile-cache/<version> and requires compileCache.cjs.   • apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts:32-54 Shared spawn args add `--require <compileCache.cjs>` for Node-mode (Electron) backends. The main-bundle restart path uses the same helper (apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3186-3195).
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1618-1628 Stale per-version cache directories are pruned after the first ready backend. Pruning keys on the version string only.
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:905-913 Terminals strip RYCO_* env vars, but provider agent sessions inherit backend process.env unfiltered. This agent session (spawned by Ryco Desktop) has RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR=~/Library/Application Support/ryco/compile-cache/0.1.31 in its env.
  • ~/Library/Application Support/ryco/compile-cache/0.1.31 (runtime state, outside repos) There are 198 MB in 3 tag directories after about 2 days: v24.21.0-arm64-8c6a5e03 (60 MB, 1,450 entries) is the installed Ryco.app Electron runtime (verified by running its binary with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE), which shows the packaged cache works. v24.21.0-arm64-964aae3f (101 MB, 4,761 entries) is Homebrew Node 24.21 (verified). v1.4.3-aarch64-* (37 MB) is Bun. So about 138 MB were written by Ryco dev processes that agents started and that inherited the variable.
  • apps/desktop/src/compileCacheDirectory.ts:4-10 The rationale that 'third-party Node programs the backend spawns never write into Ryco's cache' holds. Ryco's own bin.ts, run from other checkouts or under Bun, does write into it.
Defects in the shipped fix

The cache is wired correctly and the described per-boot compile cost is removed for packaged desktop and the npm CLI. Minor defects: (1) The env var leaks. desktopEntry.ts:42 puts RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR into Electron main's process.env. The backend inherits it, and so does every provider agent session it starts; only terminals strip RYCO_*. bin.ts honours the variable under any runtime (compileCache.ts:22-27), so Ryco dev servers or CLIs that agents run from source under Homebrew Node or Bun write into the packaged app's per-version directory. Node never evicts entries, and pruning only happens when the app version changes. Measured here: 138 of 198 MB in the 0.1.31 directory came from non-Electron runtimes after about 2 days. Local rebuilds that keep the same version string (0.1.31 built repeatedly from Oct 12 to Oct 14) also accumulate in the Electron tag directory without pruning. (2) The compileCache.ts:34/:50 comments claim the API is absent under Bun. Bun 1.4.x implements it, so the Bun dev desktop backend and `bun` dev runs also enable a JSC bytecode cache, which the comments do not anticipate. (3) A correction to the auditor: there is a regression test (serverBundleBoundaries.test.ts:125-133 and :210-218) that fails if bin.ts gains a heavy static import.

Implementation sketch

Optional cleanup, low priority. (a) In apps/server/src/compileCache.ts resolveCompileCacheDirectory, honour RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR only when running under the Electron runtime. Add a `versions = process.versions` parameter and return undefined unless versions.electron is set. Homebrew Node and Bun processes then fall back to Node's default (NODE_COMPILE_CACHE or tmpdir). The packaged backend, MCP bridge and agent-launched stdio proxy (all Electron in Node mode) keep the shared directory. Alternative: delete process.env.RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR in bin.ts right after enabling, so descendants never see it; the stdio proxy graph is under 10 files, so losing the shared directory there costs nothing. (b) Decide whether the Bun dev runtime should use the cache. Either skip when process.versions.bun is set, or fix the 'Absent under Bun' comments at compileCache.ts:34 and :50. (c) Optionally key the desktop directory on version plus a build id (for example the server dist chunk hash or app.asar mtime) in compileCacheDirectory.ts resolveDesktopCompileCacheDir, so same-version rebuilds get pruned too. Tests: extend apps/server/src/compileCache.test.ts with cases for 'RYCO_COMPILE_CACHE_DIR ignored without versions.electron' and 'used with versions.electron'. If (c) is done, update compileCacheDirectory.test.ts.

Partial#24 Idle RSS of 340–360 MiB: V8 young generation grows to 128 MiB during boot and never shrinks

server-boot:rss-young-generation · original impact Medium, effort S · Memory WP03

Current state

PARTIAL is right. Commit 60633eff3 (#710) passes --max-semi-space-size=16 to the packaged desktop backend (both the early and the main-bundle spawn) and to the launchd/systemd units, as a runtime argument rather than through NODE_OPTIONS. Bun and dev get no flag, and tests cover all of this. Still open: (a) any server started through the CLI entry runs with the default: foreground `ryco`, `ryco start`, `ryco serve`, `npx ryco-cli`, and also the Desktop's SSH-managed remote server, which the auditor missed; (b) there is no streaming-load or GC benchmark, and the perf harness itself spawns the server without the flag. Probes run here: Electron 44.7 in node mode does honor the flag, but its default new space is 64 MiB, not 128 MiB, so the desktop saving is smaller than the plain-Node ~50 MiB. Setting the flag at runtime with v8.setFlagsFromString has no effect, so the CLI fix has to be a start-up flag: a process.execve re-exec, which cost about 27 ms here, or documentation.

Evidence
  • apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts:24 DESKTOP_BACKEND_V8_FLAGS = ["--max-semi-space-size=16"]; desktopBackendSpawnArgs (:32-54) puts it first, only when nodeRuntime is true
  • apps/desktop/src/desktopEntry.ts:99-103 early packaged backend spawn: nodeRuntime: true, so it gets the flag
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3186-3196 launchBackendChild uses the same helper with nodeRuntime = !isDevelopment, so dev Bun gets no flag
  • apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.test.ts:36-71 Tests assert the flag in Node mode and no flags for Bun
  • apps/server/src/service/nodeService.ts:100-108 NODE_SERVICE_V8_FLAGS and nodeServiceRuntimeArgs, gated on an execPath basename of node/nodeN/node.exe; nodeServiceCommand feeds both the plist ProgramArguments (:112) and the systemd ExecStart (:155)
  • apps/server/src/cliSetup/nodeSetup.ts:91 The service spec uses process.execPath, which is the real node binary under Homebrew, nvm, volta and current Debian, so the basename gate is fine
  • apps/server/src/bin.ts:34 The CLI entry only calls enableCompileCacheBestEffort(), then imports cliMain at :74-80. No flag check or re-exec, so foreground ryco/start/serve and npx run with the 128 MiB default (the auditor cited :36, which is the externalMcpArgs line)
  • packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:336-346 MISSED BY AUDITOR: the Desktop's SSH remote runner execs `node $RYCO_NODE_SCRIPT_PATH` (dev only), then `ryco`, `npx --yes ryco-cli@...` or `npm exec`. None of them passes the flag
  • packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:469 nohup launches a long-lived `serve` on the remote host through that runner. This is a Ryco-controlled long-lived backend without the cap
  • scripts/perf/serverLifecycle.ts:78-90 The perf harness spawns `node bin.mjs serve` without the flag, so lifecycle RSS numbers don't reflect the shipped desktop/service setup. scripts/perf/micro only has client-retained-size.ts. No streaming or GC benchmark exists
  • apps/server/README.md:39 Documents a foreground `node apps/server/dist/bin.mjs serve` without the flag; scripts/update-node-from-source.ts:135 prints the same hint
  • /tmp/semi_probe.cjs (verifier probe, outside repo) Node 24.21: default new_space 128 MiB; v8.setFlagsFromString('--max-semi-space-size=16') at runtime still 128 MiB; CLI flag 32 MiB. Electron 44.7 ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE: default 63.5 MiB, with flag 31 MiB, so the flag is honored but the desktop baseline is half of Node's
Remaining

1) CLI entry: apps/server/src/bin.ts:34 does not apply the cap. Affected: foreground `ryco`, `ryco start`, `ryco serve`, `npx ryco-cli` (the README quick-start), and the Desktop's SSH-managed remote server (packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:336-346 runner, launched long-lived at :469). On plain Node these run with a 128 MiB new space, the full ~50 MiB idle-RSS case. Nothing documents the flag either (README.md, REMOTE.md, apps/server/README.md:39, scripts/update-node-from-source.ts:135). 2) No benchmark checks scavenge frequency, GC pause time or throughput under streaming load with the 16 MiB cap, which now ships to every packaged desktop and node service. The perf harness (scripts/perf/serverLifecycle.ts:78-90) can't pass node args at all. 3) Minor: a node service installed before #710 keeps its unit without the flag until `ryco service install`/setup runs again (node:update does this; a plain `npm i -g ryco-cli` upgrade does not), and nothing re-renders stale units.

Defects in the shipped fix

None in the shipped code. The flag works in Electron's node mode (verified empirically) and in the units, and it never reaches provider CLIs through NODE_OPTIONS. Note on expected gain: Electron 44's default new space is about 64 MiB, not Node's 128 MiB, so the packaged-desktop saving is probably about 30 MiB rather than the ~50 MiB measured on plain Node. The code comment in backendLauncher.ts:20-22 ("128 MiB ... about 50 MiB") overstates it for Electron.

Implementation sketch

A) CLI re-exec, which covers foreground ryco/start/serve, npx and the SSH remote in one place. Move the flag list into one shared constant, e.g. packages/shared/src/serverRuntimeFlags.ts (subpath export @ryco/shared/serverRuntimeFlags) exporting SERVER_V8_FLAGS = ["--max-semi-space-size=16"], and import it from apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts, apps/server/src/service/nodeService.ts and the new shim so the three can't drift. Add a pure decision function, e.g. apps/server/src/serverReexec.ts: serverReexecArgs({argv, execArgv, env, versions, hasExecve}) returns string[] | null. It returns args only when all of these hold: argv[2] is undefined, starts with '-', or is 'start'/'serve' (never mcp, device-host-stdio, the stdio proxy, auth/config/service/etc.); versions.bun and versions.electron are undefined, and argv has no --bootstrap-fd; process.execve is a function (POSIX, Node >=22.15); no --max-semi-space-size in execArgv or env.NODE_OPTIONS; env.RYCO_V8_REEXEC !== '0'. In bin.ts, before enableCompileCacheBestEffort(), call it and, when non-null, run try { process.execve(process.execPath, [process.execPath, ...SERVER_V8_FLAGS, ...process.execArgv, ...process.argv.slice(1)], process.env) } catch { /* continue without the cap */ }. execve keeps the PID, fds and TTY, so launchd/systemd, the SSH PID file and Ctrl-C behave as before; services and desktop already carry the flag and skip the re-exec. Optionally also pass the flag directly in the dev branch of packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:337 (`exec node --max-semi-space-size=16 "$RYCO_NODE_SCRIPT_PATH"`). Changing the runner bytes restarts managed remote servers on the next connect (RUNNER_CHANGED), which is acceptable. Tests: unit-test serverReexecArgs over the matrix (serve/start/bare/flags-only yes; mcp/device-host/stdio-proxy/auth no; Bun/Electron/bootstrap-fd no; already flagged via execArgv or NODE_OPTIONS no; opt-out env no). Measure time-to-listening for `ryco serve` before and after (expect about +25-40 ms) and idle RSS at 5 s (expect about -50 MiB). Update apps/server/README.md:39, scripts/update-node-from-source.ts:135 and REMOTE.md (one line on the cap and the opt-out, and Windows, where there is no execve). B) Benchmark: let scripts/perf/serverLifecycle.ts launchProductionServer accept nodeArgs (and RYCO_PERF_NODE_ARGS) so runs match the shipped setup. Add a --require preload (scripts/perf/gcStats.cjs) that records PerformanceObserver 'gc' entries by kind (count, total and p99 duration), process.cpuUsage, old-space growth and RSS, and writes them on exit. Drive streaming load by replaying a recorded provider event fixture (thousands of content deltas plus tool events) through the orchestration/WS push path; a scripted fake provider driver works too. Compare the default against 16 (and 8). Keep 16 if GC CPU rises by no more than about 2-3% and p99 event latency does not regress. 16 MiB was Node <=20's default semi-space, so expect it to pass. C) Optional: re-render stale service units on `ryco service start/restart` when the rendered definition differs from what is on disk.
