Done#25 In web/headless mode, provider driver construction blocks HTTP listen (desktop already defers it)

server-boot:web-mode-registry-on-critical-path · original impact Medium, effort M · Waterfall WP03

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor is right that the main fix landed (60633eff3). But they understated fix-defect (1). They said a pre-gate getInstance 'only matters for early provider-intent recovery'. In fact any startup housekeeping that stops a provider session trips it: the reaper's immediate first sweep, and the orphaned-session reconcile, which runs on every restart while a turn is running. That call releases the gate before HTTP serves and builds all drivers on the listen path. This has already happened on the user's machine. In the first post-#710 boot (2026-10-12T15:16:16Z), all 6 drivers were built at .39-.445 and a session was reaped at .446, while 'Listening on' only came at .633.

Current state

Verified that the core fix is in place. Every mode now starts with an empty registry and seeds the provider list from persisted per-instance status caches (no drivers built). Drivers are built only after markHttpServing releases ProviderInstanceBootGate. Real boot logs confirm it: in 15 of 16 desktop boots and 7 of 7 dev boots since the fix, the initial reconcile completes after 'Listening on'. The fix does have one hole. The hydrated getInstance has an on-demand fallback: a configured but unbuilt instance calls awaitInitialReconcile, which releases the gate early and waits for ALL drivers. The startup fiber and the provider session reaper both run before the router serves. Their stop paths (stopSession, stopSessionBinding, findExactAdapterSession) call getByInstance just to learn that a fresh process has no live session. So on a restart with a running turn (orphan reconcile), or after an unclean shutdown with a non-stopped binding idle for more than 5 minutes (the reaper's immediate first sweep), all provider SDKs are imported and CopilotClient is spawned on the listen critical path again. That is the cost the finding wanted removed, and it was observed once in the user's logs. First-run boots without cache files show no provider rows until drivers arrive. This is cosmetic and first-run only: disabled instances are persisted too (e.g. cursor.json).

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts:124-150 In every mode, the registry is created with an empty configMap. Settings are read once, and identities are resolved through resolveConfiguredProviderIdentities (schema decode only, no driver built). The desktop-only branch and the 100 ms sleep are gone.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts:174-213 Both the initial reconcile and the settings-stream reconciles wait on gateReleased. awaitInitialReconcile = release + wait for the WHOLE initial reconcile.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts:218-226 Defect source. A getInstance call for a configured instance that is not built yet calls awaitInitialReconcile, which releases the gate even if HTTP is not serving yet, and builds every configured driver, not just the one requested.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1153-1158 markHttpServing releases the boot gate. This is the intended release point. server.ts:710-724 calls it after HttpRouter.serve.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:804-828 startOrchestrationRuntime (reactors.start, then provider-sessions.reconcile, then provider-intents.recover) runs in the startup fiber, forked while the layer graph is still being built. The logs show 'startup command gate ready' before 'Listening on' in every boot, so these phases run before the gate's intended release.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:714-726 For every thread whose projected session is still starting/running or has an active turn (any restart during a turn, including graceful ones: runStopAll only marks bindings stopped), this calls providerService.stopSessionBinding.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:910-917 findExactAdapterSession (used by stopExactBinding/stopSessionBinding at :939-983) calls registry.getByInstance, which reaches the hydrated getInstance fallback and builds all drivers just to call listSessions on a fresh adapter that cannot have the session.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderSessionReaper.ts:33-150 start() forks the sweep with Effect.repeat(Schedule.spaced), so the first sweep runs immediately at reactors.start. For every non-stopped binding idle for more than 5 min, it calls providerService.stopSession (:103), and resolveRoutableSession calls getByInstance (ProviderService.ts:~1161).
  • /Users/laurinfrank/.ryco/userdata/logs/server.log:3-18 Observed regression on a post-#710 boot (2026-10-12T15:16:16Z; both the new 'hydration config resolved' and 'initial reconcile complete' messages are present). Command gate ready at .370, all 6 drivers resolved .441-.445 (initial reconcile 55 ms), provider.session.reaped at .446 (idleDurationMs 345701), and 'Listening on' only at .633. Later boots (e.g. lines 766-776) show the intended order: Listening, then drivers.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderRegistry.ts:265-330 Persisted status-cache snapshots are seeded per configured identity (listConfigured) before any driver exists, then published at :931-934. This addresses the verifier's 'lost cached provider list' regression.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderRegistry.ts:724-758 settleBootArrival adopts the persisted snapshot or keeps it without probing. The placeholder is upserted with persist:false. Cache files still get written by later probes, including for disabled instances (~/.ryco/caches/cursor.json is current).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderRegistry.test.ts:1600-1720 Tests cover building only after the gate opens, building from the current settings at release, and on-demand building before the gate. There is no test that startup stop/reaper paths leave the gate closed. The on-demand test actually codifies the full-build fallback.
Defects in the shipped fix

The on-demand fallback in ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts:218-226 lets boot-time housekeeping release the boot gate before HTTP serves, and it then builds ALL configured drivers on the listen critical path. The finding's 95-140 ms cost comes back in exactly these boots. Triggers: (a) reconcileOrphanedProviderSessions (serverRuntimeStartup.ts:714-726) calls stopSessionBinding, which reaches findExactAdapterSession and getByInstance (ProviderService.ts:917), for every thread that had a turn running at shutdown, including graceful restarts and node updates mid-run. (b) The ProviderSessionReaper's immediate first sweep (ProviderSessionReaper.ts:103,150) calls stopSession and resolveRoutableSession (getByInstance) for non-stopped bindings idle more than 5 min, e.g. after a crash, kill or force quit. (c) Provider intent recovery or pending goal-sync replays that touch an adapter. For (a) and (b) the build is pure waste: a freshly built adapter has no sessions, so the stop returns not-found. Observed in ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/server.log on 2026-10-12T15:16:16Z: drivers built about 190 ms before 'Listening on'. Minor: before the first probe, instances with no cache file have no provider row (first run only).

Implementation sketch

1) Add a non-building lookup. Add an optional `peekInstance(instanceId)` to ProviderInstanceRegistryShape (Services/ProviderInstanceRegistry.ts). In ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts it returns the raw `registry.getInstance` with no awaitInitialReconcile fallback; in ProviderInstanceRegistryLive it equals getInstance. Expose it on ProviderAdapterRegistry as `peekByInstance` (Layers/ProviderAdapterRegistry.ts). 2) In ProviderService.ts, make the stop-only paths use it. In findExactAdapterSession (:910) / stopExactBinding (:939), when peek returns undefined, return 'not-found' (forget the stale binding and runtime activity), because an adapter not built in this process cannot hold the session. In stopSession (:2134), take the provider for metrics/annotation/directory.upsert from the binding when the adapter is not built, and skip adapter.stopSession. Keep getByInstance (building on demand) for start/send/recover paths. 3) In ProviderSessionReaper.start, delay the first sweep by one interval or until command readiness, e.g. `Effect.delay(Duration.millis(sweepIntervalMs))` before the repeat. This also removes a 700-binding listBindings scan from boot. 4) Optional: change the hydrated getInstance fallback before the gate to build only the requested instance, via a mutator method that reconciles a single entry, instead of releasing the whole gate. Turn-start intent replays then pay one SDK import, not six. Tests: in ProviderRegistry.test.ts or a new hydration test, build ProviderInstanceRegistryHydrationLive + ProviderAdapterRegistryLive + ProviderServiceLive with the gate closed. Call stopSessionBinding / stopSession for a binding on a configured instance and assert that `listInstances` stays [] and the result is 'not-found'. Add a serverRuntimeStartup.test case: an orphaned running thread at boot must not build drivers before markHttpServing (count driver create calls with a stub driver list). Add a reaper test that the first sweep does not run at start(). Validate with the focused vitest files only.

They go into the published ryco-cli package.json and into the desktop stage install, although no dist chunk imports them. Defects in the shipped fix

I found no functional defect: the bundle is correct and smaller at boot. There are two follow-up gaps. (1) The structural guards never run in CI. The 'built server bundle' suites in apps/server/src/serverBundleBoundaries.test.ts:215,264 skip without a dist, and CI never builds ryco-cli before its tests (turbo.json:116 dependsOn ^build only). Two kinds of regression would merge unnoticed: a new pure-JS dependency left external, or a tagged template with an em dash making a chunk two-byte again (that only produces a build warning). No test checks the one-byte, no-JSDoc or no-CJS invariants on built output. (2) The packages that are now bundled are still in apps/server/package.json dependencies. (a) CI guard. Move BUNDLED_RUNTIME_PACKAGES out of apps/server/tsdown.config.ts into a new module, apps/server/scripts/bundledRuntimePackages.ts, and import it from the config and from the test. Then run it in CI after the build. Either add a step to the Build job in .github/workflows/_validation.yml after `bun run build` (`bun run --cwd apps/server vp test run src/serverBundleBoundaries.test.ts scripts/latin1Output.test.ts`), or add a ryco-cli `test:bundle` turbo task that depends on build. Optionally have latin1OutputPlugin call this.error instead of this.warn when RYCO_STRICT_BUNDLE=1 (set in CI) and preserved > 0. (b) Trim dependencies. Move effect, @effect/platform-node, @effect/platform-node-shared, @effect/platform-bun, @effect/sql-sqlite-bun, mime and @pierre/diffs from dependencies to devDependencies in apps/server/package.json. tsdown bundles devDependencies by default, and alwaysBundle stays for clarity. The desktop keeps effect and @effect/platform-node through its own dependencies. createStagePatchedDependencies drops the @pierre/diffs patch automatically. Check @anthropic-ai/sdk separately (no dist chunk imports it, but it may be a peer dependency of claude-agent-sdk). Add a test that every external specifier in dist is a published dependency, a node builtin, bun:*, or one of ws's optional bufferutil/utf-8-validate. Validate with `bun run build:desktop` (validateStagedRuntimeDependencies fails on any unresolvable dist import) and `node apps/server/scripts/package-smoke.mjs` (npm pack, install and boot). (c) Update the stale CJS wording in scripts/lib/validate-runtime-dependencies.ts:87 and its test at line 133.

Done#27 Desktop mode never reads the on-disk provider status cache at boot, so providers and models are missing until each cold probe finishes

server-boot:desktop-provider-status-cache-never-read · original impact Medium, effort M · Caching

Current state

Confirmed DONE by 60633eff3 (#710), which is also in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3. The desktop-only empty registry and the Effect.sleep(100ms) reconcile are gone. Every mode now reads settings once, derives the configured identities without building drivers (listConfigured), and reads <providerStatusCacheDir>/<instanceId>.json for each one in parallel during the ProviderRegistry layer build. The validated snapshots go into providersRef before the HTTP listener exists, so the first server-config snapshot carries the last-known providers and models. When a driver arrives after the boot gate opens, its cached entry is either adopted (fingerprint match) or kept until a demand probe replaces it. It is never overwritten by a placeholder, because makeManagedServerProvider never probes or publishes on construction. I could not find another composition, caller or mode with the old gap.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts:124-150 Registry starts empty in every mode (no config.mode branch remains). Settings are read once, the map comes from deriveProviderInstanceConfigMap, and identities come from resolveConfiguredProviderIdentities (schema decode only, no driver.create).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderInstanceRegistryHydration.ts:156-243 plannedIdentities is exposed as listConfigured (230). Drivers are built only after gateReleased (187-208). getInstance forces the build on demand for configured ids (218-227). The old DesktopSettingsReconcileLive with Effect.sleep("100 millis") at f1be4abc7 was removed.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderInstanceRegistryLive.ts:157-195 resolveConfiguredProviderIdentities and resolveInstanceEnabled use the same decode and enabled derivation as buildEntry (266-275), so the seeded identity's enabled flag matches what the driver later reports.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderRegistry.ts:272-326 Boot reads listConfigured and reads one cache file per identity in parallel inside the provider.status-cache.seed phase. Identity is validated by hydrateCachedProviderFromConfig, and mismatches are logged and dropped.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderRegistry.ts:931-936 Persisted snapshots are upserted into providersRef at layer build with publish:false and persist:false, before any driver exists.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderRegistry.ts:725-758 settleBootArrival either adopts the persisted snapshot (matching fingerprint) or keeps the cached entry. The driver's placeholder is upserted only when providersRef has no entry for the instance.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderRegistry.ts:838-852 Instances still awaiting driver arrival stay in knownInstanceIds, so the prune at 892-902 does not drop cached entries while drivers build. Instances removed from settings before they arrived are dropped.
  • apps/server/src/provider/makeManagedServerProvider.ts:47-52 Construction never probes and never publishes the initial placeholder to streamChanges, so a kept cached entry is not replaced by 'Checking...' when the driver's change subscription starts (ProviderRegistry.ts:816-821).
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerStatusCache.ts:54-76 Validates instanceId, driver and enabled against the settings-derived identity, and takes displayName and accentColor from current settings.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:525-531 The only composition of ProviderRegistryLive and ProviderInstanceRegistryHydrationLive, shared by desktop, web and headless.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1153-1158 markHttpServing (called from server.ts:723 after HttpRouter.serve) releases the boot gate, so driver construction is off the listener critical path.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:1173-1175 loadServerConfig reads providerRegistry.getProviders, which now returns the seeded list. The auditor's 1160 is loadDiagnosticsSnapshot.
Defects in the shipped fix

None found. Minor non-defects: (1) No single test drives the real ProviderInstanceRegistryHydrationLive plus an on-disk cache file through to getProviders before the gate opens. Each half is tested separately (ProviderRegistry.test.ts:1601 and the fake-registry tests at 3098+). (2) A seeded snapshot that was not adopted can show cached usage limits (rateLimits carry no timestamp) until the demand pass probes it. That pass has concurrency 2 and a 250 ms stagger, so with many providers the window is a few seconds. This is an accepted last-known-state tradeoff. (3) The enabled-mismatch rejection at providerStatusCache.ts:62 falls back to the placeholder after an offline toggle, as the auditor noted. This is deliberate.

Partial#28 About 4.7 MiB of the 8.1 MiB bin.mjs is feature or protocol code evaluated at boot (Codex/ACP schemas, computer use, hub E2EE, source-control providers)

First-pass audit said PARTIAL; the verifier corrected it. 1. Hub: the auditor said HubConnectorLive and HubIdentityRuntime are import()ed after the router serves, which is true, and treated hub/E2EE as done. But httpServingLayer calls hubConnector.start unconditionally (server.ts:719-726). HubConnectorLive statically imports HubIdentityRuntime (HubConnectorLive.ts:22-26) and the NodeE2ee* modules. Forgejo: ForgejoApi, ForgejoPullRequestPageApi, forgejoDiffLines and forgejoPullRequests* (about 115 KiB in cliMain) stay eager through server.ts:79, ws.ts:13 and SourceControlProviderRegistry.ts:13. The local host has to be built on first device operation instead. 4. Wrong line: AgentControlExternalMcpServerLive is server.ts:168 (used at :622), not server.ts:122 (that is AdvertisedEndpointRegistryLive). 5. Tail sizes in the serve closure (bundle region bytes): device 157 KiB, htmlRender 103 KiB (including shared/htmlRender and htmlRenderTools), Atlassian 66 KiB, ExternalMcp 54 KiB, cli.ts plus cliSetup 140 KiB, Forgejo about 115 KiB. Current state

PARTIAL is right. The expensive time-to-listen parts are done: bin.mjs is a 3.2 KB shim, the Codex schema, effect-acp, noble, React/zustand, native computer use and the GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Azure clients are behind import(), and a guard test locks the source graph. The auditor's remaining list misses three things. (1) The biggest remaining item: the whole Hub/E2EE graph (HubConnectorLive 210 KB plus HubIdentityRuntime 483 KB with noble) still loads and evaluates on every boot, right after serve, even when hubConnector.enabled is false (the default). The finding's 'load only when enabled' was not implemented, so the RSS saving it named as unconditional for non-Hub nodes never happens. (2) The eager Forgejo API stack (about 115 KiB) is missing from the remaining list. (3) The device fix the auditor proposed (import() inside the layer) would save nothing, because DeviceServiceLive builds localDeviceHost during layer construction on darwin, linux and win32 alike. The tail on the listen path is about 0.6 MiB, not 0.4-0.5. Also, the guard's built-bundle checks never run in CI.

On every boot after serve (not on the listen path): - The Hub/E2EE graph, about 690 KB of bundle (HubConnectorLive plus HubIdentityRuntime with noble), loads even when hubConnector.enabled is false (server.ts:726, HubConnectorLive.ts:22). Still in the static serve closure (time-to-listen path), about 0.6 MiB of source: - device: localDeviceHost chunk 143 KB, built during layer construction (DeviceService.ts:19, :58). - htmlRender: 103 KiB (server.ts:155). - Atlassian and Jira: 66 KiB (server.ts:140-141). - ExternalMcp tools and listener: 54 KiB (server.ts:168, AgentControlExternalMcpServer.ts:44). - Forgejo API stack: about 115 KiB (SourceControlProviderRegistry.ts:13, server.ts:79, ws.ts:13). - CLI admin handlers and setupFlow: about 140 KiB (cli.ts:87-108, 1548-3565). Guard gap: the bundle budget and region checks never run in CI (serverBundleBoundaries.test.ts:200).

Defects in the shipped fix

No functional bugs in the implemented lazy boundaries. Gaps in the guard: - The built-bundle assertions (size budget under 7,000,000 B, currently 6,611,615 B, plus forbidden regions and no Codex schema marker) are skipped in CI, because the test job never builds apps/server (turbo test depends only on ^build). They only run when a developer happens to have a dist. - hasCurrentBuild only greps bin.mjs for 'enableCompileCache', so a stale dist can produce misleading passes or failures. - The guard does not cover the hub-disabled post-serve load, the device backends, htmlRender, Atlassian, ExternalMcp or Forgejo.

Implementation sketch

1. Hub on demand (largest remaining, S). - In HubConnectorDeferred.makeDeferredHubConnectorLive, make HubConnectorReady.await run `start` first. `start` is already idempotent. - In server.ts httpServingLayer (~:726), call hubConnector.start only when config.hubConnector?.enabled is true. - A disabled node then never import()s HubConnectorLive or HubIdentityRuntime unless a Hub route is hit (Settings > Node security, `leave`, and so on). - Why this is behaviour-preserving: a disabled connector takes no process lock (HubConnectorLive.ts:365), opens no custody (:384), HubConnector.start returns early (HubConnector.ts:460), and desktop probes only when the hub is enabled (desktop main.ts:1396). - Tests: a HubConnectorDeferred unit test where the load spy is not called until `await` when start was never invoked; a server-layer test that a disabled config never calls the loader. - Do not try to just lazy-import HubIdentityRuntime inside HubConnectorLive: NodeE2ee* would still pull noble statically. 2. Device (M). - In DeviceService.ts, replace the eager localDeviceHost(platform) with a lazy DeviceHostBackend: a ForwardingDeviceBackend-style wrapper whose first operation does `await import('../localDeviceHost.ts')` and caches the result. Keep the same host id 'local', and keep a single Android adapter instance after first load. - Run reclaimOrphanedBoots only when the boot-ownership file has entries, so a clean boot never loads the backends. - Keep SshDeviceBackend, deviceFrameRoute and the contracts eager. - Check that rolldown moves DeviceManager out of the localDeviceHost chunk (it is now exported from it) into a chunk that cliMain may import statically. 3. htmlRender and Atlassian (M). - Add a small HtmlRender facade layer whose methods import('./HtmlRenderLive.ts') (headlessChrome, PreviewBrowser) on first call. htmlRenderTools only needs the service tag. - Same pattern for JiraWorkItemService and AtlassianConnectionService. Keep the persistence repositories and migration 036 eager, since migrations must run at boot. 4. ExternalMcp (S). - In AgentControlExternalMcpServer.ts, move makeExternalMcpTools and the makeAgentControlExternalListener import into `start` through import(). start only runs when topology.current().available. 5. Forgejo (M). - Split ForgejoApi into an eager ForgejoHosts service (configured hosts plus detectProviderFromRemoteUrl, which the synchronous detection needs) and a lazily loaded request client (ForgejoApi, PullRequestPageApi, diff lines), using the existing lazyClient/loadModule pattern in SourceControlProviderRegistry.layer. - Update ws.ts:13 and server.ts:79 to depend on the light service. 6. CLI (M). - Keep Command/Flag definitions in cli.ts (needed for parsing and --help). - Move the handler bodies of pairing, session, hub, e2ee, project and service commands, plus setupFlow, into cliCommands/*.ts, loaded through Effect.promise(() => import(...)) in each withHandler, the same way loadCliRemote works. 7. Guard (S). - Run the built-bundle block in CI: add a step to the Build job in _validation.yml after the build (line ~204), e.g. `bun run --cwd apps/server test src/serverBundleBoundaries.test.ts`, with an env flag that turns the skipIf into a hard failure when dist is missing or older than src. - Add forbidden-region assertions for src/device/IosSimulatorBackend.ts, src/htmlRender/headlessChrome.ts, src/atlassian/JiraWorkItemService.ts, src/agentControl/ExternalMcp/tools.ts and src/sourceControl/ForgejoPullRequestPageApi.ts in the serve closure, once each is lazy.

Done#30 Hub connector identity runtime (sequential store loads plus keychain) is built before the router attaches

server-boot:hub-identity-gates-router · original impact Low, effort M · Waterfall WP03

Current state

Confirmed DONE. HttpRouter.serve no longer depends on HubConnectorLive. It is provideMerged with HubConnectorDeferredLive, which only gives the routes a HubConnectorReady access tag and a HubConnectorStart handle. httpServingLayer calls startup.markHttpServing, a fast Deferred.succeed plus a provider boot-gate release, and then hubConnector.start. That forks a fiber which dynamic-imports HubConnectorLive and builds it with Layer.buildWithScope in the layer's scope. So the process lock, identity custody, the keychain probe and the roughly 690 KB relay/E2EE/identity module graph are all off the bind-to-handler path. Every Hub route (http.ts, desktopNativeNodeClaimHttp.ts, localIntroductionHttp.ts, desktopHubReachabilityHttp.ts) goes through awaitHubConnector. Nothing else in the router, ws.ts or the runtime graph needs HubConnectorService. Inside makeHubIdentityRuntime the state and retirement stores open in parallel. The protected-store selection (keychain) runs at the same time as the E2EE record loads: 5 records in one Promise.all, then 3 dependent ones, joined with allSettled. The shared continuity anchor has its own single-writer leaf lock, so the parallel continuity and policy constructors are safe. Spans server.startup.hub.connector, server.startup.hub.process-lock and server.startup.hub.identity-runtime exist, the last annotated with hub.identity.{state,protected-store,e2ee-records}Ms. Three caveats, none of which reopen the finding. (1) Hub routes wait on the Deferred rather than answering 503. (2) There is a stale comment. (3) A smaller related pre-bind path remains: the desktop standby check imports the whole identity chunk before config resolves.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:809 HttpRouter.serve(makeRoutesLayer).pipe(Layer.provideMerge(HubConnectorDeferredLive)). The router no longer waits for the connector build.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:716-727 httpServingLayer runs startup.markHttpServing and then hubConnector.start, which forks the build once handlers are attached.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1153-1158 markHttpServing only succeeds a Deferred and releases the provider boot gate, so the connector start is not held behind slow work.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorDeferred.ts:43-88 The connector module is dynamically imported and built in the layer scope from Effect.forkIn under the span server.startup.hub.connector. A Deferred is resolved on success, died with HubConnectorStartupError on failure, and interrupted on shutdown. start is idempotent.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorDeferred.test.ts:42-106 Tests cover no load until start, a single build in the serve context, finalizers running with the server scope, a failed build failing only the waiting routes, and interruption on shutdown mid-build.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorService.ts:169-173 awaitHubConnector awaits the Deferred. It is the only way routes reach the connector, and grep finds no other server consumer of HubConnectorService.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubIdentityRuntime.ts:844-943 The state and retirement stores load in parallel. Protected-store selection overlaps the E2EE record loads (Promise.all of 5, then 3 dependent), joined by Promise.allSettled at :943.
  • apps/server/src/hubIdentity/NodeContinuityAnchor.ts:51-63 The anchor takes its own single-writer leaf lock, so constructing the continuity and policy stores concurrently cannot race on the shared anchor.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorLive.ts:370,408 Spans server.startup.hub.process-lock and server.startup.hub.identity-runtime. The latter is annotated with per-phase durations from onStartupPhase.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorLive.ts:381-382 Stale comment: 'Identity custody is built before the router serves'.
  • apps/server/src/cli.ts:738-749 Desktop standby resolution runs during config resolution, before the port binds, on default desktop settings (hubOrigin defaults to DEFAULT_HOSTED_APP_ORIGIN at apps/desktop/src/desktopSettings.ts:65, standby at :294).
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorStandby.ts:34-38 Dynamically imports the whole HubIdentityRuntime module (built chunk about 483 KB: @noble curves, hashes and ciphers, relay E2EE shared code, every hubIdentity store) only to call hubIdentityHoldsKeyMaterial. That function reads two small files, and on a fresh install readOrCreate writes them.
Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defect in the fix. Three minor points. (1) The comment at apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorLive.ts:381-382 ('Identity custody is built before the router serves') is stale. (2) Hub routes block on Deferred.await until custody finishes instead of answering 503/Retry-After as proposed (HubConnectorService.ts:169-173). A stuck OS credential prompt now hangs only Hub routes, and only the settings panel and desktop main use them, so this is acceptable. (3) There is an adjacent pre-bind Hub-identity cost the fix did not cover. On desktop standby launches, which is the default for a fresh desktop whose connector was never toggled, cli.ts:738-749 calls resolveStandbyHubConnectorConfig before ServerConfig exists. HubConnectorStandby.ts:34-38 then dynamic-imports the full HubIdentityRuntime chunk (about 483 KB including noble and the E2EE handshake code) just for hubIdentityHoldsKeyMaterial, which takes the state-file lock and reads two small JSON files. This happens before the HTTP port binds. It has no keychain and no process lock and was never measured, likely single-digit to about 15 ms of module parse/eval, and it predates the report. The cost is small, but it is the same class of problem. There is also no server-level test asserting that the router serves before the connector builds; only the unit test of makeDeferredHubConnectorLive covers the semantics.

Startup request black hole (10)

Done#31 The HTTP port is bound ~150-280 ms before any request/upgrade handler exists; requests accepted in that window are dropped and never answered or closed

startup-hang:startup-accept-before-handler-blackhole · original impact High, effort S · Reliability

Current state

Confirmed DONE for the Node path, which is what the finding describes and what production runs. The gate is installed in NodeHttpServer.layer's evaluate() before listen() (server.ts:253-258). It holds early requests and upgrades: at most 256, for at most 10 s, then 503 with Retry-After. When the platform's serve() attaches its handlers with server.on, the gate replays the held entries into them; the repo's platform-node patch changes only shutdown, not how handlers attach. If the server closes while still gated, held entries get 503. A real Effect regression test covers it. The desktop's loopback-compression upgrade listener is registered before the gate, so the gate correctly ignores it. The early static handler (added later) cannot shadow any router route. The desktop reloads a document it loaded at bind time if bind-to-serve takes longer than 9 s, so the gate's 10 s 503 cap does not strand the renderer. Clients also retry on 502-504. The only gap is dev-only: under `bun dev:desktop` the Bun branch has no gate, and BunHttpServer's placeholder answers 404 during the startup window.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/httpStartupGate.ts:106 installHttpStartupGate adds the gate's request and upgrade listeners and a newListener hook (:243-245). Held entries are bounded by HTTP_STARTUP_GATE_MAX_PENDING=256 (:25) and MAX_WAIT_MS=10000 (:26). Past either limit: 503 with Retry-After: 1, no-store and Connection: close (:67); raw 503 on upgrade sockets (:74). Entries are dropped when the client closes (:142, :164).

Dev-only.
Defects in the shipped fix

No defects found in the Node gate. One minor path is not covered, and only in development. Under `bun dev:desktop` the backend runs on Bun (apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3186-3200), and the Bun branch of HttpServerLive (apps/server/src/server.ts:236-244) has no gate. It also has no early static serving and writes no http-bound frame. During the bind-to-serve window, BunHttpServer's placeholder therefore answers 404 to HTTP requests and WebSocket upgrades, and primaryAuth treats 404 as non-transient. First dev boot is masked because the dev window waits for http-serving. Exposure is limited to renderer reconnects across a dev backend restart and to other dev clients (for example mobile) pointed at a dev desktop backend. It is a fast 404, not an indefinite hang.

Done#32 Graceful shutdown waits the full 20 s gracefulShutdownTimeout whenever a WebSocket (or hung request) is open; desktop sends SIGKILL after 2 s, skipping later finalizers

startup-hang:shutdown-blocked-20s-by-open-websocket · original impact High, effort S · Reliability WP03

Current state

The described bug is fixed. With a normal WebSocket client open, shutdown no longer waits the 20 s gracefulShutdownTimeout. The patched @effect/platform-node sends 1001 to every wss client before awaiting server.close(), Ryco bounds the HTTP stage at 750 ms, and the desktop now waits 3 s before SIGKILL. The patch is registered in package.json and bun.lock, and node_modules resolves to the patched 4.0.2 build. A scratch repro against the installed patched package showed a responsive ws client: the whole scope closed in 4 ms. The fix has one gap in its fallback path. server.closeAllConnections() does not close upgraded WebSocket sockets, because Node drops them from its connection list on upgrade. A client that never answers the close frame (frozen, or half-open after a network drop) is therefore not force-closed. The final wss.close() layer finalizer then waits out ws's 30 s closeTimeout. Measured: HTTP stage done at 755 ms, full scope close at 30,002 ms. Runtime finalizers (restart hints, providers, SQLite) run before that, so the reliability fix holds. Only the tail is affected: Observability trace-sink flush, logger and platform layers.

Evidence
  • patches/@effect%2Fplatform-node@4.0.2.patch:96 closeWebSockets sends client.close(1001) to every wss client, then timeoutOrElse(shutdown). On timeout the orElse calls only server.closeAllConnections(). The comment says 'past the timeout, connections are closed', but upgraded WS sockets are not in Node's connection list, so they stay open. Same hunk in src (:153-171).
  • package.json:156 @effect/platform-node@4.0.2 is in patchedDependencies, and bun.lock:429 records it. apps/server/node_modules/@effect/platform-node symlinks to the patched .bun store entry, whose dist/src contain closeWebSockets.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:205 HTTP_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT = 750 ms, passed to the Node layer (:264) and the Bun layer (:243). This is the only NodeHttpServer/BunHttpServer layer in apps and packages. The doc comment at :199-204 still says the desktop grace is '2 s'; it is now 3 s.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:824 Layer order: the HTTP drain (serve's preemptive finalizer) runs first, then the http-drained marker, RuntimeServicesLive and runtime-services-closed. HttpServerLive's own finalizers (wss.close(), then the cached server.close()) run after that, followed by StartupStallMonitor, ObservabilityLive and Platform layers. The residual 30 s wait sits in the HttpServerLive stage.
  • node_modules/.bun/ws@8.22.0/node_modules/ws/lib/websocket-server.js:196 In noServer mode with clientTracking, WebSocketServer.close() emits 'close' only once clients.size reaches 0 (_shouldEmitClose). A client still CLOSING is destroyed only by setCloseTimer (websocket.js:1323) after closeTimeout, default 30000 ms. @types/ws 8.18.2 has no closeTimeout field, so it can't be passed cleanly through the typed websocket options.
  • node_modules/.bun/@effect+platform-node@4.0.2+8fabb152f7781780/node_modules/@effect/platform-node/src/NodeHttpServer.ts:314 The upgrade release is a synchronous ws.close(code), so interrupting WS fibers does not block. It also does not force-destroy a socket already in CLOSING.
  • apps/server/src/httpShutdown.test.ts:28 The regression test covers only a responsive ws client (close code 1001, under 2 s, 10 s graceful timeout). It has no case for a client that never answers the close frame.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts:218 DESKTOP_BACKEND_SIGTERM_GRACE_MS = 3000. terminateDesktopBackendChild (:231) sends SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after the grace, with a 5 s exit wait. stopBackendAndWaitForExit (main.ts:3370-3386) uses it for quit (before-quit :4890), relaunch (:1466) and update install (:2829).
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:859 The recordShutdownHints finalizer is still in the startup layer, inside RuntimeServicesLive. It runs before the HttpServerLive tail, so it is reached on both the responsive and unresponsive paths.
  • apps/server/src/httpStartupGate.ts:226 The 'hung startup sockets' part of the finding is also covered. The gate holds early requests and upgrades, and on close-while-gated it answers them with 503 instead of letting server.close() wait on them.
  • apps/server/src/agentControl/Mcp/listener.ts:388 The other loopback HTTP listeners call closeAllConnections() before close(): Agent Control MCP, External MCP (ExternalMcp/listener.ts:269), and publicProxy, which destroys its tracked sockets. One exception: deviceToolGateway.close (providerTools/deviceToolGateway.ts:722) awaits server.close() without closeAllConnections. An in-flight device tool call at quit can hold the DeviceService finalizer. That is outside this finding's scope.
Defects in the shipped fix

(1) The timeout fallback in patches/@effect%2Fplatform-node@4.0.2.patch (orElse -> server.closeAllConnections()) does not close upgraded WebSocket sockets. Node removes them from its connection list on upgrade (freeParser -> parser.remove()). If a client never answers the 1001 close frame (frozen app, phone that left Wi-Fi, other half-open TCP), the socket stays until ws's 30 s closeTimeout. HttpServerLive's wss.close() finalizer waits for it. Reproduced against the installed patched package with a raw upgraded client that pauses and never replies, gracefulShutdownTimeout 750 ms: HTTP stage done at 755 ms, Scope.close returned at 30,002 ms. Ryco's runtime finalizers (restart hints, providers, SQLite) run before this tail and are unaffected. But a CLI or service Ctrl-C/restart then takes about 30 s, and the desktop backend ends by SIGKILL at 3 s, skipping the later ObservabilityLive trace-sink flush, logger and platform finalizers. (2) Nit: the server.ts:199-204 comment says the desktop SIGTERM->SIGKILL grace is 2 s; it is 3 s (DESKTOP_BACKEND_SIGTERM_GRACE_MS). The auditor's edge case (closeWebSockets creating the WebSocketServer during shutdown when no WS ever connected) is real and harmless.

Implementation sketch

Edit the @effect/platform-node patch (regenerate it with `bun patch @effect/platform-node@4.0.2` + `bun patch --commit`, keeping both the dist/NodeHttpServer.js and src/NodeHttpServer.ts hunks and the bun.lock entry in sync). (a) In preemptiveShutdown's timeoutOrElse, make orElse `Effect.flatMap(wss, (wss) => Effect.sync(() => { server.closeAllConnections(); for (const client of wss.clients) client.terminate() }))`. The HTTP stage then frees every socket once the graceful timeout passes. (b) As a backstop, have the wss acquireRelease release terminate any remaining clients before `wss.close(cb)`, so the final layer finalizer can never wait out ws's closeTimeout. (Passing `closeTimeout` through `websocket:` options in server.ts also works at runtime, since ws 8.22 supports it, but @types/ws 8.18.2 lacks the field, so it would need a cast. Prefer the patch.) Test: add a case to apps/server/src/httpShutdown.test.ts. Open a raw node:net client, send a valid Upgrade request, wait for the 101, then pause() and never answer the close frame. Use gracefulShutdownTimeout '200 millis' and assert Scope.close(scope) finishes under 2 s (currently about 30 s) and the raw socket gets 'close'. Also update the stale 2 s wording in the server.ts:199-204 comment to point at DESKTOP_BACKEND_SIGTERM_GRACE_MS (3 s). Validation: focused `bun run test` on apps/server/src/httpShutdown.test.ts plus typecheck of apps/server.

Done#33 Every SSH remote cold launch pays ~0.9 s: the 100 ms / 1 s readiness poller always puts one probe into the dead window

startup-hang:ssh-remote-launch-readiness-penalty · original impact Medium, effort S · Waterfall

Current state

Confirmed DONE. The root cause is fixed. The Node HTTP server, which every remote runner uses (`node`, `ryco` and `npx` all run `dist/bin.mjs` with a `#!/usr/bin/env node` banner), now installs installHttpStartupGate before listen. The gate holds requests that arrive before HttpRouter.serve attaches and replays them through the newListener hook. @effect/platform-node attaches its handlers with server.on('request'/'upgrade'), so the hook fires. In serve (web) mode, `/` is deliberately not served early (isEarlyStaticAssetRequest), so wait_ready cannot report ready before the router serves. The defense-in-depth part also landed: the remote wait_ready per-probe timeout is now 250 ms (REMOTE_LOOPBACK_READY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS), and the probe still accepts only 2xx, so the gate's 503 counts as not ready. I emulated it in memory, using the real httpStartupGate.ts module and the exact probe loop. Attach times were 145/200/280/600/1500/3000 ms and listen offsets 0/37/73 ms. Readiness lag after the router attaches was: old code (no gate, 1 s probe) min 335, median 851, max 1064 ms. Current code (gate, 250 ms probe) min 0, median 0, max 102 ms. An old remote `ryco` on PATH without the gate, probed at 250 ms, gives min 9, median 215, max 327 ms. The ~0.9 s penalty is gone. I found no real defect.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:258 installHttpStartupGate(server) is called inside the NodeHttpServer.layer factory, so before listen. Node path only. Bun never blackholed.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:280-289 Early handler: desktop mode serves the document, other modes serve only isEarlyStaticAssetRequest. So `/` (the wait_ready path) stays held until the router attaches (commit 347008e60).
  • apps/server/src/httpStartupGate.ts:201-215 newListener hook replays held requests and upgrades on nextTick once the real handlers attach. Held entries are dropped on response 'close', so a probe destroyed after 250 ms leaves no residue. Cap is 256 entries and 10 s, then 503 + Retry-After.
  • apps/server/node_modules/@effect/platform-node/dist/NodeHttpServer.js:126-127 The platform attaches with server.on('request'/'upgrade'), so the gate's newListener detection works with the real serve path. Also covered by httpStartupGate.test.ts:182 ('startup gate with the Effect Node HTTP server').
  • apps/server/src/cli.ts:514-520 `ryco serve` resolves mode to 'web' unless RYCO_MODE or a flag overrides it. So the non-desktop early-serve policy (`/` held) applies to the SSH remote.
  • packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:61 REMOTE_LOOPBACK_READY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 250. Old code substituted SSH_READY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS (1000) at the old :543.
  • packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:550 RYCO_READY_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS now takes the 250 ms constant. It feeds wait_ready (:382-383) for the cold launch (:474) and both reuse checks (:415-451).
  • packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:282-304 Probe uses http.get timeout = probeTimeoutMs and resolves true only for 2xx, followed by a 100 ms sleep. A 503 from the gate counts as not ready.
  • packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:339 The runner prefers a `ryco` already on the remote PATH. An older global install without the gate still blackholes during its dead window, but the 250 ms timeout caps that at ~330 ms (emulated) instead of ~1.06 s.
  • packages/ssh/src/tunnel.test.ts:162 Pins the 250 ms value in the generated launch script.
  • packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:739 The local tunnel waitForHttpReady keeps the 1 s default, which the finding did not ask to change. It runs after the remote is ready. OpenSSH binds -L listeners only after auth, so early local probes get ECONNREFUSED quickly and there is no dead window.
Defects in the shipped fix

None verified. Notes on trade-offs, not defects: (1) Against a gated server, a 1 s probe timeout would give ~0 ms lag, because a held probe is almost always in flight at attach. With 250 ms plus a 100 ms sleep, about 100/350 of launches land in the sleep and lag up to ~100 ms (emulated max 102 ms). The 250 ms value buys the cap for old non-gated remote `ryco` installs. (2) The idle timeout covers the held time too, so a replayed probe must get headers within what is left of its 250 ms. On a slow, busy host right after attach it may be abandoned and retried. That is bounded by the 15 s deadline and costs at most a few 350 ms cycles. (3) The same 250 ms probe now drives the 2 s reuse checks (tunnel.ts:451), which kill a managed server that fails them. A healthy server whose `/` consistently takes 250-1000 ms would now be restarted where it was previously reused. That needs sustained event-loop stalls for about 2 s, so the risk is low.

Value low · effort none · risk none

Done#34 Client descriptor/session/ws-token fetches and the WS URL provider have no timeout; one request in the window stalls reconnects indefinitely, and saved-env connects pile onto the hung attempt

startup-hang:client-control-plane-fetch-no-timeout · original impact Medium, effort S · Reliability WP15

Current state

Confirmed DONE. #710 (60633eff3) implemented every part of the proposal. A shared fetchWithDeadline (5 s primary, 10 s remote) bounds descriptor, session, ws-token and bootstrap fetches, including the body read. issuePrimaryWebSocketToken is retried and abortable. protocol.ts gives the URL provider the attempt signal and a 10 s timeoutOrElse that maps to the retried WsUrlProviderError. All direct/saved-env WsTransports on web and mobile set urlProviderTimeoutMs, except SSH, where the exclusion is deliberate. A saved-env slot timeout now aborts the attempt's controller and drops the pending entry, so a retry or Connect starts fresh. I found no unbounded control-plane fetch or URL provider left on the primary or direct saved-env paths. Two minor latent gaps remain: the mobile driver drops the supervisor's abort signal, and the web wrapper resolveRemoteWebSocketConnectionUrl does not declare `signal`. Each request in both cases is still deadline-bounded, so the described indefinite stall no longer happens.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/fetchWithDeadline.ts:53-110 Manual-timer deadline plus caller-signal merge. Promise.race on headers and body settles the caller even if the adapter ignores the signal, and controller.abort releases the socket. I read the edge cases (pre-aborted signal, unread body, repeated reads) and found no bug.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.ts:139-140,145-168,192-201 fetchControlPlane wraps every startup and reconnect call. issuePrimaryWebSocketToken(signal) goes through retryTransientBootstrap with signal-aware abandonment (118-138). The prefetched token uses the same 5 s-bounded requestWebSocketToken.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryContext.ts:78-93 fetchDescriptor uses fetchWithDeadline inside retryTransientBootstrap.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/remoteApi.ts:48-94,151-168 fetchRemoteJson uses the 10 s deadline. Session, rotate and ws-token URL resolution forward input.signal.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/protocol.ts:143,293-307,338-345 WS_URL_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_MS=10_000. tryPromise passes the attempt signal, and timeoutOrElse fails with WsUrlProviderError, which Effect.retry retries. Effect 4.0.2 timeoutOrElse→timeoutOption interrupts the loser, which aborts the signal.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts:475 WsTransport and DeviceWsTransport spread lifecycleHandlers (including urlProviderTimeoutMs) into createWsRpcProtocolLayer.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:963-998,1093-1108,1165 The primary /ws and /ws/device transports and the saved-env /ws and /ws/device transports all set urlProviderTimeoutMs. SSH is deliberately excluded. Hosted transports keep their own lifecycle.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:914-1014 There is one AbortController per pending attempt. The 60 s slot timeout calls abandonPendingSavedEnvironmentConnection, which deletes the entry, rejects joiners and aborts. supervision.test.ts:300-314 covers this.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1463,1485-1497 The web saved-env connect forwards the attempt signal to the session check and to renewal rotate/session.
  • apps/web/src/environments/remote/api.ts:35-39 Minor latent defect. The wrapper resolveRemoteWebSocketConnectionUrl declares no `signal`. service.ts:1033 spreads `signal` in, which escapes excess-property checks, and it reaches fetchRemoteJson only because the wrapper forwards the whole input object. No test asserts the caller signal (api.test.ts checks only that a deadline signal is present).
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:380-383,446,619-620; apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentActions.ts:67-68 Minor gap. The mobile driver's connectSavedEnvironment takes no signal, and the supervisor wiring (record, isCancelled) drops it, so a slot timeout on mobile does not abort the in-flight session check or renewal. The 10 s fetch deadline and the 15 s check timeout still bound both, and the pending entry is still dropped.
  • packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:880-938,992-994 The SSH loopback fetch has no deadline and the SSH URL provider has no urlProviderTimeoutMs. ServerAliveInterval=15×CountMax=3 tears down a dead tunnel in about 45 s, so this is bounded rather than indefinite. The exclusion is intentional (service.ts:1100-1106).
Defects in the shipped fix

No blocking defects. Minor latent issues: (1) apps/web/src/environments/remote/api.ts:35-39 does not declare `signal` in the resolveRemoteWebSocketConnectionUrl wrapper type. Cancellation works only because the whole input object is forwarded, so a refactor that destructures it would silently stop aborting abandoned saved-env ws-token requests. (2) Mobile does not thread the supervisor's AbortSignal (environmentDriver.ts:380-383,446,619-620; environmentActions.ts:67-68), so a slot timeout on mobile leaves its session-check and renewal requests running to their 10-15 s deadlines instead of aborting them. (3) Out of scope and unchanged: primaryAuth post/get/getHubOrNull (primaryAuth.ts:256-293) have no deadline, but they are user-initiated pairing, Hub and E2EE operator calls. /ws/device-frames (service.ts:1005) resolves without a caller signal but is still bounded by the 5 s deadline and the 15 s retry window.

I tried to refute the DONE classification and could not. All three proposal parts are on main at ec250e386. Only GET non-upgrade requests for /, /index.html, /assets/* and root-level files are served early. (b) The Node backend writes an 'http-bound' frame after the early handler is installed. (2) The saving is still unmeasured. #710 also moved provider drivers and the Hub connector after serving, so the runtime window to overlap is smaller than the 145-280 ms in the finding. (3) The Bun backend (desktop dev, which loads the Vite devUrl) has no gate or early serving. In non-desktop modes the browser opens at serving and / stays held on purpose. Both are outside this desktop finding.

Done#36 Desktop readiness depends on parsing the INFO log line 'Listening on http://'; when it is missing, the HTTP fallback costs +0.9 s on every boot

Current state

PR #710 (60633eff3) implemented the proposal. The backend writes `http-bound` and `http-serving` frames as newline-delimited JSON on the inherited fd 4 telemetry pipe, and `http-serving` is written only after `HttpRouter.serve` has attached the handlers. The desktop validates frames with the shared parser and settles readiness on `http-serving` (source 'protocol'). It also rejects on a port mismatch or a `fatal` frame. The 'Listening on' log detector stays as a second signal. The HTTP probe no longer races from t=0: it starts only after a 3 s fallback delay and is cancelled when a signal arrives. The startup gate (httpStartupGate.ts) holds early probe requests and replays them, so the old 0.9 s dead window is gone. A suppressed or changed log line (RYCO_LOG_LEVEL=Warning, disableListenLog, format change) therefore no longer delays packaged desktop readiness. I found no runtime regression. Remaining nits: there is no server-side test of the http-serving frame. The dev script boot-report.mjs still keys on the log text. In the very unlikely case that fd 4 is unusable and the log line is suppressed, the probe now starts at 3 s rather than at 0.

Done#37 markHttpListening is signalled by a layer built concurrently with HttpRouter.serve, so 'http listener ready', the ready event and pairing output can come before handlers are attached

startup-hang:mark-http-listening-races-serve · original impact Low, effort S · Reliability

Current state

I tried to refute the auditor and could not. The fix holds on the current code. The old `httpListeningLayer` sat in `Layer.mergeAll` beside `HttpRouter.serve`, so it built at the same time as serve. Commit 60633eff3 (#710) replaced it with `httpServingLayer`, which receives the serve layer through `Layer.provide`. In effect 4.0.2, `Layer.provide` (via `provideWith`) builds the provided layer fully, then builds the dependent layer. The serve layer only finishes after `HttpServer.serve` returns, and on both Node and Bun that call attaches the request/upgrade handlers synchronously at its end. So `markHttpServing`, and with it 'startup http listener ready', the `ready` publish, headless pairing output and browser open, now always follow handler attachment and the 'Listening on' log. Nothing else calls the mark; the only other `markHttpServing` references are test mocks. Desktop also treats the `http-serving` frame, written in the same post-serve layer, as its authoritative readiness signal. In 11bfda63e, Hub connector construction moved after the mark: it is forked and does not block the layer. Hub routes wait for `HubConnectorReady`, and the headless output reads the Hub origin from config only, so this does not reintroduce the race. One related point, outside the finding's scope: the proposal deliberately left `tailscaleServeLayer` concurrent. On a first boot with Tailscale Serve enabled, the headless output may probe the MagicDNS HTTPS endpoint before `ensureTailscaleServe` has finished. The link would then be left out, or a loopback-only server would print a loopback connection string. That is low value, a trade-off rather than a defect of this fix.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:715-728 `httpServingLayer` writes the `http-serving` desktop frame, calls `startup.markHttpServing`, then forks `hubConnector.start`. A comment says it is built after `HttpRouter.serve`.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:804-815 `httpServingLayer.pipe(Layer.provide(HttpRouter.serve(makeRoutesLayer,...).pipe(Layer.provideMerge(HubConnectorDeferredLive))))` is the shape the proposal asked for. `runtimeStateLayer` and `tailscaleServeLayer` stay in `mergeAll`, as the proposal said.
  • node_modules/.bun/effect@4.0.2/node_modules/effect/src/Layer.ts:1951-1970 `provideWith` does `flatMap(that.build(...), ctx => self.build(...))`, so the dependent mark layer is built strictly after the serve layer has finished building.
  • node_modules/.bun/effect@4.0.2/node_modules/effect/src/http/HttpRouter.ts:1340-1396 `serve` builds the app layer, then `Layer.merge(HttpServer.serve(handler), ...)`, then `withLogAddress`. Its build completes only after `server.serve` returns and the address is logged.
  • node_modules/.bun/@effect+platform-node@4.0.2+8fabb152f7781780/node_modules/@effect/platform-node/src/NodeHttpServer.ts:172-198 Node `serve` calls `server.on('request'/'upgrade')` synchronously at the end of the serve effect. Bun's `BunHttpServer.ts:224-226` likewise does `handlerStack.push` plus `server.reload` synchronously.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1032-1141 The startup fiber awaits the `httpServing` Deferred before it logs 'startup http listener ready', publishes `ready`, prints headless output and opens the browser.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1153-1158 `markHttpServing` (renamed, as the proposal asked) resolves `httpServing` and releases the provider boot gate. It is the only producer; the other references are test mocks (server.test.ts:1004, threadFork.fixtures.ts:238).
  • apps/desktop/src/backendStartup.ts:5,94 Desktop treats only the `http-serving` frame, written in the post-serve layer, as authoritative backend readiness.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorDeferred.ts:62-80 `start` only forks the connector build (it is not awaited in the layer), and Hub routes await `HubConnectorReady`. Moving it after the mark (11bfda63e) keeps the guarantee that requests are served or held, not dropped.
  • apps/server/src/startupAccess.ts:259-285 Headless output reads the Hub origin from config only, so it does not depend on the connector. It does call `registry.list`, which probes the Tailscale MagicDNS URL live (AdvertisedEndpointRegistry.ts:164-176). That is the related, out-of-scope `tailscaleServeLayer` concurrency.
Defects in the shipped fix

None verified. Minor gaps: (1) No test asserts the layer ordering in server.ts, meaning that `markHttpServing` runs only after handlers are attached. A future refactor that moves `httpServingLayer` back into `mergeAll` would pass every existing test. (2) Out of scope by the proposal's own terms: `tailscaleServeLayer` still builds alongside the mark. On a first boot with `--tailscale-serve`, the headless pairing output can probe the MagicDNS HTTPS endpoint before `ensureTailscaleServe` finishes, which leaves out the Tailnet link or falls back to a loopback connection string.

Done#38 With no clients, graceful shutdown still takes 1.0-1.5 s (1.7-2.8 s right after boot), close to desktop's 2 s SIGKILL; the analytics finalizer does an unbounded network POST

Current state

Confirmed DONE (PR #710, 60633eff3). The shutdown telemetry flush is now capped at 300 ms. Effect v4's timeoutOption resumes as soon as the sleep wins and does not wait for the losing fetch, and runMain calls process.exit after a signal, so the in-flight POST cannot hold the exit. An unbounded `analytics.flush` that the old provider finalizer also ran (f1be4abc7 ProviderService.ts:2402) is gone. All adapter stopAll paths run concurrently. Copilot stops are bounded at 1 s and then force-stopped; forceStop only signals and does not wait. opencode gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 1 s. Shutdown phase markers are logged, the desktop SIGKILL grace is 3 s on every stop path, and the perf harness disables telemetry. Tests cover the analytics bound, the parallel provider stop and the Copilot force-stop. What is left is cosmetic or adjacent and optional.

Evidence

Losers are only interrupted when the parent exits, so the timeout returns at 300 ms even inside an uninterruptible finalizer.

Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defect. Three comments are stale and still say the desktop SIGKILLs after 2 s, while the grace is now 3 s: apps/server/src/telemetry/Layers/AnalyticsService.ts:21, apps/server/src/server.ts:201-202 and apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CopilotAdapter.clientStop.ts:5. Done#39 After a backend crash-restart, desktop navigates the renderer back to the backend root (full app reload); this currently hides stuck reconnects

startup-hang:desktop-crash-restart-full-reload · original impact Low, effort S · Rendering WP04

Current state

Confirmed DONE. In 60633eff3 (#710), loadPackagedBackendAppWindow got a gate (resolveBackendAppWindowAction). After a crash-restart, a window that already reported a usable shell on the backend origin gets an in-place reconnect nudge (SYSTEM_RESUMED_CHANNEL) and keeps its route. loadURL(backendHttpUrl) now runs only from the boot page, about:blank, or a backend-origin document that never became usable. The client deadlines the proposal depended on are in place: fetchWithDeadline (5 s), transient retry for ws-token/session (15 s), and the server httpStartupGate. Production desktop-main.log shows the shell-usable report arriving on every launch, so the gate is live, not dormant. The optional version check was not implemented; it is moot because a crash-restart relaunches the same bundled binary. One small missed edge: a renderer whose process died keeps its usable mark and is nudged instead of reloaded.

Evidence
  • apps/desktop/src/backendAppWindowLoad.ts:61 Pure gate. Returns load for an empty URL, about:blank or the boot URL. Returns ignore at bound or for another origin. Otherwise returns reconnect when shellUsable is true and load when it is false. Unit tests in backendAppWindowLoad.test.ts:23 cover the deep-route reconnect, the unusable reload, foreign origins and bound vs ready.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1717 loadPackagedBackendAppWindow now resolves the action first. The reconnect branch (1741-1745) only calls notifyRenderersToReconnect() and returns. The only remaining loadURL(backendHttpUrl) in this path is at 1757. At f1be4abc7 the function called loadURL for any backend-origin URL.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3413 The DESKTOP_STARTUP_MARKS IPC adds the sender to appShellUsableContents (declared at 495). The preload observer (startupMarks.ts) reports only after the primary-shell-usable mark, which service.ts:236 sets once the primary shell snapshot is applied. ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/desktop-main.log contains desktop.window.app.shell-usable on every recent launch.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4426 The usable mark is cleared on every main-frame cross-document navigation start. Error pages and new documents must report again before they count as reconnectable.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:1183 reconnectAfterResume forces reconnect() on connections whose heartbeat is not fresh. It is skipped in hosted mode (1244-1246), so the new trigger does not bypass hosted lifecycle ownership. A connection whose last pong is under 15 s old (Effect pings every 8 s) is skipped. It then relies on the transport retry: the URL provider polls ws-token every 500 ms (primaryAuth retryTransientBootstrap) and the startup gate holds that request until the backend serves. The WebSocketConnectionCoordinator stall detector is the backstop.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.ts:139 The ws-token request runs through fetchWithDeadline (CONTROL_PLANE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000, fetchWithDeadline.ts:11), with transient retry on refused, timeout and 502-504 (118-137). The POST that used to hang across the restart, and that the reload used to rescue, is now bounded.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4825 The bootstrap token and port are fixed per app run, and the session signing secret is persisted (ServerSecretStore). The renderer's cookie session survives a backend crash-restart, so reconnecting in place needs no re-auth.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4591 The render-process-gone handler only marks the load request failed. It does not remove the webContents from appShellUsableContents, so a dead renderer still counts as reconnectable.
Defects in the shipped fix

Minor edge-case regression. The render-process-gone handler (apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4591-4596) sets request.failed but leaves the webContents in appShellUsableContents. getURL() still returns the backend-origin app URL. If the renderer process has died (OOM, GPU or renderer crash) when a backend crash-restart reaches readiness, resolveBackendAppWindowAction returns "reconnect" and notifyRenderersToReconnect sends IPC to a dead renderer. The window stays blank until the user presses Cmd+R. Before #710 the unconditional loadURL revived it. Not a blocker: it needs a renderer crash plus a backend crash-restart, and View > Reload is available. Not fixes, just notes: (a) the proposal's optional server-version check was not built; it only matters if files on disk change under a running app, such as a Linux deb/rpm upgrade, and the existing version-mismatch hint covers that. (b) The reconnect nudge skips a connection whose heartbeat is still fresh; the transport's own retry plus the startup gate reconnect at readiness.

Implementation sketch

In apps/desktop/src/main.ts, inside the window.webContents.on("render-process-gone", ...) handler (around line 4591), add appShellUsableContents.delete(window.webContents) so a dead document is no longer reconnectable. Belt and braces: in loadPackagedBackendAppWindow (around line 1732), pass shellUsable: appShellUsableContents.has(contents) && !contents.isCrashed(). Then readiness takes the "load" path and loadURL(backendHttpUrl) revives the renderer. To make this testable, pull the check into a small helper, e.g. isReconnectableAppShell({ usable, crashed }), in backendAppWindowLoad.ts. Add a case to backendAppWindowLoad.test.ts: a deep backend-origin route with shellUsable false (crashed) resolves to "load". Optional and low value: send a distinct backend-restarted reason, or force reconnect of only the primary connection regardless of heartbeat freshness, so a crash shortly after a pong does not wait on the transport's retry timing. Validate with focused vitest runs for apps/desktop (backendAppWindowLoad.test.ts) and a manual check: kill the backend child and the renderer process (kill -9) in a packaged build, then confirm the window reloads.

Done#40 HubConnectorLive (process lock plus identity runtime with ≥12 sequential file/keychain awaits) is built between listen() and handler attachment, widening the dead window for hub-enabled nodes

startup-hang:hub-connector-in-serve-gap · original impact Low, effort L · Waterfall WP03

Current state

Confirmed DONE by 11bfda63e, which is on main and also in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3. HttpRouter.serve now gets only HubConnectorDeferredLive (a Deferred-backed HubConnectorReady plus HubConnectorStart). The real HubConnectorLive (process lock, identity runtime, OS credential-store probe) is dynamically imported and built in a fiber forked into the layer scope. That only happens after handlers attach, the http-serving frame is written and markHttpServing runs. Every production consumer of the connector awaits the Deferred: the routes in http.ts, localIntroductionHttp.ts, desktopNativeNodeClaimHttp.ts and desktopHubReachabilityHttp.ts. No WS RPC, auth, environment or startup-phase code touches the connector or the identity, and owner auth runs before the await. So keychain and identity I/O are off time-to-first-response and off the desktop http-serving and ready signals. Shutdown order is unchanged: connector finalizers still run after the serve layer's. Build failure and mid-build interruption are handled, and HubConnectorDeferred.test.ts covers both. Spans server.startup.hub.connector, server.startup.hub.process-lock and server.startup.hub.identity-runtime, with per-phase annotations, reach the local file tracer. I could not refute the auditor, but it missed one point: there is no composition-level test for the start call. The remaining nits are cosmetic or optional.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:805-809 httpServingLayer is provided with HttpRouter.serve(makeRoutesLayer).pipe(Layer.provideMerge(HubConnectorDeferredLive)). HubConnectorLive is no longer imported statically by server.ts.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:715-727 After serve, httpServingLayer writes the http-serving lifecycle frame, runs startup.markHttpServing (line 723) and only then calls hubConnector.start (line 726). markHttpServing (serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1153-1158) completes a Deferred and releases the provider boot gate without waiting.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorDeferred.ts:43-88 Uses a lazy import('./HubConnectorLive.ts') and Layer.buildWithScope in the layer scope with the captured serve-time context. start is idempotent and fire-and-forget (forkIn). A defect is logged and the Deferred dies with HubConnectorStartupError. An interrupt-only exit interrupts the Deferred.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorService.ts:160-177 HubConnectorReady and awaitHubConnector are Deferred-backed. hubConnectorReadyLayer exists for tests.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/http.ts:41-49 Hub routes run authenticateOwner and then awaitHubConnector, so only Hub routes wait on custody. git grep shows that awaitHubConnector, in http.ts, localIntroductionHttp.ts, desktopNativeNodeClaimHttp.ts and desktopHubReachabilityHttp.ts, is the only production path to the connector. There are no WS RPC consumers.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorLive.ts:365-411 The process lock (span at line 370) and makeIdentityRuntime (span at line 408, per-phase annotations through onStartupPhase) are built only inside the deferred build. HubConnectorLive is a plain Layer.effect with no sub-layers (line 767), so the fresh memo map in buildWithScope duplicates nothing.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorDeferred.test.ts:41-106 Tests cover: nothing loads before start; a waiting route is answered after start; start runs once; the serve context is used; finalizers run on scope close; a build failure fails only the waiting routes; shutdown mid-build interrupts the waiters.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorLive.ts:381-382 Stale comment, 'Identity custody is built before the router serves'. It is now built after.

Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defects. Minor: (1) The comment at apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorLive.ts:381-382 is stale; it says custody is built before the router serves. (2) awaitHubConnector (HubConnectorService.ts:169-173) has no timeout or 503. While an OS keychain prompt is pending, /api/hub/*, the local-introduction routes, native-claim and desktop reachability hang, and the desktop hub control fetch (apps/desktop/src/desktopHubControl.ts:119) has no timeout either. This only affects Hub surfaces, and it was strictly worse before (the whole server was held), so it is not a regression. (3) Test-coverage gap: nothing asserts that the real makeServerLayer composition calls HubConnectorStart.start after serve. (4) The connector module graph (relay, E2EE, noble) is still imported on every boot, now right after serve, even for nodes with the Hub disabled. It is off the critical path but competes with early requests on the main thread. That is outside this finding's scope, which covers keychain and identity I/O in the listen-to-handler gap.

Done#41 Boot loads the full command read model 3 times before the command gate (and once per page afterwards), although the engine already holds it in memory

persistence-boot:boot-command-read-model-3x · original impact High, effort S · Database

Current state

Confirmed DONE. The engine has one production implementation, and it exposes getReadModel as Effect.sync over the worker-maintained commandReadModel. No wrapper layer drops it, so the helper never falls back to SQL in production. All three redundant boot reads use it: restricted workspace.validate, orphan reconcile (one snapshot shared by settleStaleProjectedTurns, capture and the request sweep) and RestartContinuation.dispatchPending per page. workspace.validate returns before loading anything when unrestricted. The only remaining SQL getCommandReadModel callers are engine bootstrap, CLI offline and the HTTP debug endpoint, as the proposal said. Both runtime-recovery phases that run before validate dispatch through the engine, so the in-memory model is not stale against SQL. The projector keeps the command-model shape aligned with the hydrated one: user-message anchors only, plans without markdown, activities capped while keeping milestones. The callers' field use (session, latestTurn, user anchors, activities, worktree paths) is safe. The restart pre-check now reads the same model the decider fences against, which is stricter than before. Shipped in 60633eff3 (#710), present in HEAD and in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3. The separate kind-scan cost in the remaining bootstrap hydration is tracked as finding 042.

Done#43 The first subscribeShell after boot forks reconcileAllWorktrees, which builds 2×P+1 full shell snapshots (P = projects and chats whose folders exist)

persistence-boot:reconcile-worktrees-n-plus-1 · original impact High, effort S · Database WP05

Current state

Confirmed DONE. The sweep no longer builds 2P+1 whole shell snapshots. It now reads the project list once (listProjectShells). Per non-chat project it does one PK project lookup, a stat-based fingerprint, and two indexed per-project reads that run in one short transaction. git runs only when the worktree registrations changed. The pass starts 15 s after the forking subscribeShell, its git calls run in the background process lane, and chat projects are skipped. The rows passed into ensureProjectMainWorktree remove the 2nd and 3rd per-project snapshots. Not re-reading after a main workspace is created is safe, because the planner ignores rows with a null path. There is only one production ProjectionSnapshotQuery layer, and it implements both narrow methods, so the whole-snapshot fallbacks only run in test doubles. One minor edge case is in the extra listing cache (not part of the proposal): it can store an empty listing, which can silently stop reconciliation for one repo for the rest of the process lifetime.

Then readProjectShells uses listProjectShells, a project-rows SELECT (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:865-876, 3217), not getShellSnapshot. The throttle stamp is taken before the sleep (line 915), so reconnects within 5 min return at once.
  • apps/server/src/git/worktreeReconciliation.ts:56 partitionReconcilableProjectRoots skips isChatProject before the existsSync check, so chats pay neither git nor DB work.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/worktreeOperations.ts:258-271 loadProjectWorkspaceRows prefers getProjectWorkspaceRows. The only production implementation (orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3592-3626, exported at 4538) provides it, so the readWorkspacePlacement fallback only runs in test doubles.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:1001-1029 Both reads filter WHERE project_id = ?. The thread read selects 5 columns with deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY created_at, covered by idx_projection_threads_project_deleted_created (019_ProjectionSnapshotLookupIndexes.ts:13-14). Worktrees are covered by (project_id, archived_at) (030_Worktrees.ts:28). The filter semantics (deleted threads excluded, archived worktrees included) match the old whole-shell placement rows.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/worktreeOperations.ts:767-771 Rows are read once, after git answers, and passed to ensureProjectMainWorktree (288-296), so there are no extra snapshots. A main workspace it creates is not re-read. That is safe because planWorktreeReconciliation skips worktrees with worktreePath === null (worktreeReconciliation.ts:180-185).

Chat and missing projects are skipped, and git runs in the background lane.

GitWorkflowService.listWorktreePaths (GitWorkflowService.ts:445-453) returns [] when detection says 'not a repo'. Git detectRepository returns null on any non-zero rev-parse exit (vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:493-510, allowNonZeroExit), for example on dubious ownership or a broken HEAD while <root>/.git still exists. The planner treats [] as 'git could not answer' (worktreeReconciliation.ts:158), so that project is never reconciled again until a worktree registration changes or the server restarts.
Defects in the shipped fix

No defect affects the finding's cost. One low-severity robustness edge exists in the extra worktree-listing cache added by 502adfd1e. worktreeOperations.ts:749-760 caches an empty `git worktree list` result under a valid fingerprint. An empty result only happens when git could not answer (detectRepository returns null on a non-zero rev-parse exit, for example dubious ownership or a corrupt HEAD, while .git still exists). planWorktreeReconciliation treats [] as a no-op (worktreeReconciliation.ts:158), so once the repo recovers, reconciliation for that project stays off until its worktree registrations change or the process restarts. Other negligible leftovers: the project row is read again per project (getProjectShellById, worktreeOperations.ts:736) even though listProjectShells already returned it, and knownWorktreeListings is never pruned of deleted projects (a tiny map). Projects rooted in a subdirectory of a repo always get a null fingerprint (no <root>/.git), so they still run `git worktree list` on every sweep, in the background lane only.
