Done#44 Repository identity (2 git spawns per project, 1-minute TTL, 1 s budget, chats included) blocks every shell snapshot, including the one built at boot

persistence-boot:repo-identity-git-on-snapshot-path · original impact High, effort M · Process spawns WP05

Current state

DONE is correct, landed in #710 (60633eff3), which the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3 also contains. Shell snapshots, getProjectShellById and the shell stream's project-upserted items now read repository_identity_json from projection_projects (migration 086), so there are no git spawns on the snapshot path. ProviderCommandReactor.start uses a targeted pending-goal SQL query. A background sync (startup, a 30-minute sweep, project.created and root/kind moves) skips chats and missing roots. It probes git in the background lane only when a stat-based fingerprint of <commonDir>/config changes or the entry is older than 24 h. Neither of the finding's costs remains: the 250-380 ms of boot probing and the up-to-1 s snapshot wait. I found no other first-party hot path that still spawns identity git. The remaining resolver callers are the background sync, AgentControlProjectPlans (one root per plan), and the enrichment for the legacy replayEvents/replayEventsPage RPC, which no first-party client calls. The fix has two small defects. (1) A transient probe failure is stored as 'no repository' for up to 24 h, survives restarts, and is announced to clients. (2) Remote changes that Ryco makes itself, such as publishRepository, only appear at the next 30-minute sweep.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3007 buildShell is pure SQL: 'repository identities are persisted ... so a snapshot never waits on git'. Identity is decoded from row.repositoryIdentityJson at :2646, :3129, :3227, :3267, :3364 and :3384. resolveRepositoryIdentitiesForProjects and the RepositoryIdentityResolver import are gone (git show f1be4abc7 had them at :529/:560/:2183/:2658/:2806/:2837).
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:259 toShellStreamEvent maps project.created, project.meta-updated and project.avatar-set to getProjectShellById, which reads the persisted identity. This is the main client stream path, and it spawns no git.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:3432 start() calls readPendingGoalSyncThreads. The live implementation at ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3279 uses listPendingGoalSyncThreadRows (:928): goal_json IS NOT NULL plus a json_valid-guarded json_extract(...)='pending'.
  • apps/server/src/project/repositoryIdentitySync.ts:101 syncProject skips chats and missing roots (null fingerprint) and returns 'fresh' when the fingerprint is unchanged and checkedAt is under 24 h old. Otherwise it calls resolver.refresh in inBackgroundProcessLane and records the result.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1074 repository-identities.sync runs after commandGate.signalCommandReady (:1028). runRepositoryIdentitySync forkScopes both the event consumer and the sweep, so it does not block boot.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/ProjectionProjects.ts:77 The projector upsert keeps the identity columns while workspace_root is unchanged and clears them on a move. recordRepositoryIdentity (:161) is guarded by project_id AND workspace_root.
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:135 DEFECT SOURCE: makeGitIdentityProbe turns every failure into null, whether a timeout (1 s, :97/:126), a spawn error or a non-zero exit. A transient failure is therefore indistinguishable from 'not a repository / no remote'.
  • apps/server/src/project/repositoryIdentitySync.ts:115 DEFECT: that null is recorded with the current fingerprint and checkedAt (:119-125). Later sweeps treat it as 'fresh' (:108-114) for 24 h, even across restarts, because the state is persisted. If a non-null identity was stored before, samePersistedRepositoryIdentity is false and the empty project.meta.update (:133) announces the removal to every client.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/SourceControlRepositoryService.ts:521 publishRepository adds a remote through git.ensureRemote, and GitVcsDriver initRepository runs git init. Neither triggers an identity resync. Nothing revalidates on read or on git activity, so the new identity appears only at the next 30-minute sweep (repositoryIdentitySync.ts:43). Before the fix, a snapshot or reconnect after the 1-minute TTL picked it up.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:420 enrichProjectEvent is only reached from the legacy replayEvents/replayEventsPage RPCs (orchestrationRpc.ts:473/:500), which no first-party client calls. A persisted null is ambiguous, so project.created replays for chats, non-repo projects and deleted projects still call resolver.resolve. This path is not hot, and it was already this way before the fix.
  • apps/server/src/project/repositoryIdentitySync.test.ts:136 The tests cover fingerprint gating, max-age, chat/missing/deleted skips, the moved-root guard, non-blocking event consumption and trigger selection. No test covers a refresh failure or timeout.
Defects in the shipped fix

(1) A transient probe failure becomes a sticky 'no repository' state. RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:128-135 collapses a timeout (over 1 s of process runtime), a spawn error or a non-zero exit into null. repositoryIdentitySync.ts:115-125 then persists that null with the current fingerprint and checkedAt, and :108-114 treats it as fresh for 24 h. The state is persisted, so a server restart does not clear it. If a real identity was stored before, :127-146 dispatches project.meta.update, so every client drops the project's repository grouping, remote link and hero metadata. The old code cached such a miss for 1 minute only. This is most plausible on Windows (slow spawns under Defender) or a heavily loaded machine. The first sweep after upgrade runs right after boot. (2) Remote changes made by Ryco itself go stale. publishRepository (SourceControlRepositoryService.ts:507-525, via ensureRemote) and initRepository change <commonDir>/config, but no sync is triggered. The identity updates only at the next 30-minute sweep, where before a reload after 1 minute picked it up. (3) Minor. A newly created git project first streams with a null identity, then a second upsert arrives once the sync records and announces it. This causes a brief regroup and an extra project.meta-updated event per new repository project, and after upgrade one such event per git project on the first sweep. Not done from the optional proposal step: still 2 spawns per root (rev-parse plus remote -v) instead of parsing config. That now only runs in the background, so it is negligible.

Implementation sketch

(1) Separate 'indeterminate' from 'no identity'. In apps/server/src/project/Layers/RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts, make the probe return a tagged result, e.g. {ok: stdout} | {exit: code} | {failed: cause}. Keep resolve() collapsing everything to null for interactive callers. Change refresh() to fail with a typed RepositoryIdentityProbeError when either probe times out or cannot spawn, and do not Cache.set in that case. Update RepositoryIdentityResolverShape['refresh'] in project/Services/RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts. In repositoryIdentitySync.ts syncProject, catch that error and return 'skipped' without calling recordRepositoryIdentity. The old identity, fingerprint and checkedAt then stay as they were, so the next sweep (or an earlier short retry, e.g. a 1-2 minute Schedule just for failed roots) tries again. Tests: in repositoryIdentitySync.test.ts, inject a resolver whose refresh fails. Assert that record and dispatch are not called and that a later sync with a working resolver records the identity. In RepositoryIdentityResolver.test.ts, assert that a VcsProcess timeout makes refresh fail while resolve still returns null. (2) Expose the sync as a small service, e.g. RepositoryIdentitySync with revalidateRoot(cwd), built in serverRuntimeStartup next to runRepositoryIdentitySync. revalidateRoot enqueues the projects whose workspaceRoot equals or is inside the repository root. Since it is fingerprint-gated, it costs a few stats when nothing changed. Call it after publishRepository, initRepository and ensureRemote. Alternatively hook it into VcsStatusBroadcaster.refreshStatus(cwd) behind a short debounce, which also catches CLI remote edits made through agents. Test: after a mocked publish, the project's persisted identity updates and one project.meta.update is dispatched. (3) Optional. In repositoryIdentitySync.ts, for a project.created trigger, resolve before the projector's first upsert is streamed, or have toShellStreamEvent hold project.created until the sync records it. This is low value and can be skipped.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Partial#45 Routes are served only after engine hydration and projector catch-up, while the socket is already bound

persistence-boot:engine-hydration-before-serve · original impact Medium, effort M · Waterfall decision

Current state

PARTIAL is right. Nothing makes hydration asynchronous: the engine still runs projector catch-up and command-read-model hydration inside Layer.effect construction (OrchestrationEngine.ts:601-605), and HttpRouter.serve (server.ts:807) still sits above RuntimeServicesLive (server.ts:830). The router, environment descriptor, auth/API routes and WS upgrade therefore still wait for hydration. #710 (60633eff3) added httpStartupGate, which closes the reliability half: early requests and upgrades are held and replayed, or get 503 + Retry-After after 10 s or 256 entries. 347008e60 serves static assets early in every mode and the document `/` early in desktop mode. Provider drivers and the Hub connector moved after serve, and catch-up is batched and filtered by event type. On the user's real desktop the remaining bind-to-serve window (migrations + hydration + other layers) is about 20-440 ms, typically 40-170 ms. Its end comes before the renderer's own DOM-ready, so for desktop boots the remaining perf value is now small. What is left matters mainly for web/headless nodes (document still held), for large post-upgrade projector replays, and for starting the hosted Hub connector earlier.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationEngine.ts:601 `yield* projectionPipeline.bootstrap; commandReadModel = yield* projectionSnapshotQuery.getCommandReadModel(); const bootSequence = yield* eventStore.latestSequence;` (601-605) still runs synchronously during OrchestrationEngineLive construction (Layer.effect at 685-688). git grep finds no engine-ready Deferred or forked hydration anywhere in apps/server/src.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:807 HttpRouter.serve(makeRoutesLayer) lives in serverApplicationLayer, which is provideMerge'd over RuntimeServicesLive (:830), and RuntimeServicesLive includes ProviderRuntimeLayerLive -> OrchestrationLayerLive (:503-506). httpServingLayer (markHttpServing at :723) therefore still follows hydration.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionPipeline.ts:2607 bootstrapProjectors is now batched per transaction and filtered by event type (:2654-2698), so it is much cheaper than at f1be4abc7. It is still awaited before the engine layer completes, so a large lagging-projector replay still delays the router.
  • apps/server/src/httpStartupGate.ts:106 Mitigation added in 60633eff3. The gate is installed before listen (server.ts:252-259). It holds requests and upgrades (max 256 entries, 10 s at :25-26), replays them when the real listeners attach, and answers 503 + Retry-After on overflow, timeout or close. This removes the never-answered-connection hang. I found no defect in the hold/replay/close logic.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:282 Early static handler: desktop serves `/` + assets (isEarlyStaticRequest); other modes serve assets only (isEarlyStaticAssetRequest, httpStartupGate.ts:285-291). `/` is held outside desktop because the SSH wait_ready probe polls it (packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:262-300).
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1606 The environment descriptor is a readiness probe for the desktop HTTP fallback, and also for the CLI's probeLocalServer (apps/server/src/cli.ts:3835). Serving it from the gate before the router attaches, as the auditor's cheaper step 2 suggests, would make these report ready early. That is the same objection that keeps `/` held for SSH.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Services/OrchestrationEngine.ts:33 `bootSequence: number` is a plain value on the engine shape. It is read synchronously by ProviderCommandReactor.recoverIntents (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:3538) and ws/context.ts:1249 (settleThreadDeletionCleanup). Async hydration needs this to become an Effect or Deferred-backed value.
  • apps/server/src/ws/orchestrationRpc.ts:527 Shell snapshot reads SQL projections directly (projectionSnapshotQuery.getShellSnapshot), as does orchestration/http.ts:45. These reads implicitly depend on projector catch-up having finished, and nothing gates them today because the router cannot serve before bootstrap. WS dispatch is already gated by startup.enqueueCommand (ws/context.ts:1122).
  • apps/server/package.json:23 Production runs on Node (`start: node dist/bin.mjs`, engines.node at :62; desktop launches Electron-as-Node, apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts:107-109). The gate-less Bun branch of HttpServerLive (server.ts:236-244) is a dev/test path only, so it is not a real remaining production gap.
  • ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/desktop-main.log (outside repo) Real boots on 2026-10-13/14: desktop.backend.http-bound -> http-serving = 20-440 ms (e.g. run b1b8af618599: bound 217 ms, serving 384 ms, but renderer app.dom-ready only at 552 ms and primary-ws-open later). The router is ready before the renderer can use it, so async hydration would save about 0 ms on a typical desktop boot.
Remaining

(1) Engine hydration still blocks router start: OrchestrationEngine.ts:601-605 runs inside layer construction, and HttpRouter.serve (server.ts:807) is built over RuntimeServicesLive (server.ts:830). The environment descriptor (http.ts:344-354), auth/API routes and the WS upgrade (server.ts:697-700 via makeRoutesLayer) are only held by the gate until hydration ends, and get 503 if it takes more than 10 s (httpStartupGate.ts:26, e.g. a large post-upgrade projector replay). (2) Outside desktop mode the document `/` is still not served before the router (server.ts:282, httpStartupGate.ts:285-291), so a browser opening a web/headless node right after a restart waits for migrations + hydration. (3) The Hub connector starts only after serve (server.ts:723-726), so a hosted relay attempt after a node restart cannot begin until hydration is done. Measured on the user's desktop, the whole bind-to-serve window is now about 40-440 ms and finishes before renderer DOM-ready, so the remaining cost is mostly in edge cases (large replays, headless nodes on big DBs) rather than typical boots.

Defects in the shipped fix

No defect found in the implemented mitigation (httpStartupGate hold/replay/503/close handling, early static handler). Limitations only: requests held longer than 10 s get 503 + Retry-After rather than a response, and the bound is 256 pending entries.

Implementation sketch

Option A (full fix, only if headless/large-DB boots matter). In OrchestrationEngine.ts, create `engineReady = Deferred.make<void, PersistenceError>()`. Fork `projectionPipeline.bootstrap -> getCommandReadModel -> eventStore.latestSequence` into a scoped fiber that sets `commandReadModel` and `bootSequence` and completes the Deferred. Have the worker (:607-623) `Deferred.await(engineReady)` before its first `Queue.take`, so dispatch (:645) only queues. Change OrchestrationEngineShape.bootSequence (Services/OrchestrationEngine.ts:33) to `Effect<number>` (await, then read), make getReadModel await, and update ProviderCommandReactor.recoverIntents (:3538) and ws/context.ts:1249. Expose `awaitReady` on the engine. Await it in: ServerRuntimeStartup.startup (before workspace.validate / startOrchestrationRuntime), every WS RPC handler that reads projections (gate once at the RPC route or in ws/context, not per handler; e.g. orchestrationRpc.ts:527 shell snapshot), the HTTP snapshot route (orchestration/http.ts:45), and the Hub connector's first snapshot publication. On hydration failure, fail through the existing startup fatal path (desktop `fatal` frame plus process exit). Then audit the other RuntimeServicesLive layers that do blocking work at build time, because the router only starts early if all of them are non-blocking. Readiness probes need a decision: the descriptor (desktop main.ts:1606 fallback, cli.ts:3835) and SSH wait_ready `/` would then report ready before data is ready. Either add a `ready` flag or a separate readiness endpoint, or accept the earlier signal; the desktop's primary signal (the http-serving frame) can stay tied to engine readiness. Tests: in server.test.ts, use a Deferred-controlled fake ProjectionPipeline.bootstrap and assert that, while bootstrap is pending, the WS upgrade completes and the descriptor answers, while a shell-snapshot RPC and a dispatch both wait; that after release they return caught-up data in order; and that bootstrap failure closes the server and answers held clients with 503. Option B (cheap, non-desktop document): switch the SSH wait_ready probe (packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:262-300) to a dedicated readiness path that only the router serves (keep accepting `/` for old remote servers), then let non-desktop modes use isEarlyStaticRequest in server.ts:282. Old launch scripts against new servers would report ready early, so keep `/` held for one release or version-gate it. Recommendation: Option A is not worth its risk at current measured numbers. Keep this as a deferred item, and consider Option B only if headless boot latency is reported.

Needs a decision

Making hydration async changes readiness semantics: the environment descriptor (desktop HTTP fallback, CLI probeLocalServer) and the SSH wait_ready probe of `/` would report ready before the engine is, and every projection-reading RPC has to be gated. It also brings the hosted Hub connector start forward relative to data readiness. Measured remaining gain on typical desktop boots is about 0 ms, so whether to take on this complexity and risk is a product/architecture trade-off rather than a clear win.

Value low · effort M · risk medium

Partial#46 Shell snapshot: 5.65 MiB and about 140 ms per build at 4.5k threads, with a redundant whole-snapshot Schema decode, deleted rows decoded then dropped, archived threads always shipped, and a per-subscriber rebuild on priority changes

persistence-boot:shell-snapshot-cost · original impact Medium, effort M · CPU decision

Current state

Confirmed PARTIAL. Parts (a) to (d) all landed in #710 (60633eff3). (a) The whole-snapshot decodeShellSnapshot is gone; rows are decoded once. (b) Shell-only queries filter deleted_at IS NULL, and updatedAt comes from SQL MAX. (c) coalesceConcurrentRuns makes concurrent builds single-flight, and joinPriorityLoad shares one load per priority ranking across all connections. (d) Web and mobile both opt into thread-priority deltas. Part (e) did not land. Every non-deleted archived thread is still built, Schema-encoded, relayed and decoded in each full or paged snapshot. Null and default thread-shell fields are still emitted. I found no alternative implementation: no lazy-archive capability, no archived-thread RPC, nothing on the Hub side. The client assembler also holds every page until snapshot-end, so sending archived threads last does not get the shell on screen any sooner. Small correction to the auditor: the decoded-form safety net was kept as a test, not lost.

  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:909-924 (b) readShellUpdatedAt is a single SQL MAX over whole tables instead of scanning decoded rows.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:1298-1385 The session and latest-turn shell subqueries filter only deleted threads, so they also load archived threads' sessions and latest turns.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:664-700 (c) coalesceConcurrentRuns provides read-your-writes single-flight with detached runs. It is tested at ProjectionSnapshotQuery.shell.test.ts:460.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3198-3215 (c) getShellSnapshot is coalesced; callers inside a transaction bypass it. getScopedShellSnapshot is not coalesced, which is fine because those reads are small.
  • apps/server/src/ws/orchestrationRpc.ts:518-548 (c) subscribeShell passes the coalesced projectionSnapshotQuery.getShellSnapshot() to makeReplayableShellStream.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:49-101 (c) joinPriorityLoad keeps one flight per projection query service, shared across connections.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:755-781 (d) Delta subscribers get a thread-priorities item. Legacy subscribers get one shared snapshot load but per-subscriber paging and encoding.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:294 (d) The client sends threadPriorities: "delta" whenever applyThreadPriorities is wired, and both web (apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:888) and mobile (apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:514) wire it.
Remaining

Proposal item (e) is the remaining work. (1) Archived threads are still read, built, Schema-encoded per subscriber, relayed and client-decoded in every full or paged shell snapshot: listActiveThreadShellRows at ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:878-889 has no archived_at filter; the session and latest-turn subqueries at :1298-1385 have none either; mapping happens at :3133-3172 and shipping at shellSnapshotPages.ts:55-66. The client assembler (packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/shellSnapshotAssembly.ts:51-67) waits for snapshot-end, so even the archived-last ordering does not get the shell on screen sooner. There is no capability flag, count-only mode or paged archived-thread RPC. (2) Null and default thread-shell fields are still emitted (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3133-3172), and contracts orchestration.ts:1145-1191 keeps the wire shape. With permessage-deflate on non-loopback links the wire savings are small; the CPU saving in encode, stringify and parse is roughly 15-20%. (3) Not a numbered proposal item: coalescing shares the build but not the per-subscriber work. Each subscriber still pays one JSON.stringify per thread to measure page size (shellSnapshotPages.ts:10, :61), then a Schema encode and a stringify in the RPC layer. Sequential builds are not memoized per snapshotSequence; I judge that acceptable because resumes skip the build.

Defects in the shipped fix

None that matter. coalesceConcurrentRuns is correct: detached runs, failures and interrupts propagate to every joiner, and in-transaction callers bypass it. joinPriorityLoad is correct: a flight can only be joined before its read starts, and a completed flight stays reading=true so later rankings start a fresh load. Both are tested. One correction to the auditor: the decoded-form guard was not lost. It is the test 'builds shell snapshots that are already in their decoded form' (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.shell.test.ts:81), which decodes, compares and encodes the built snapshot.

Implementation sketch

Archived-lazy (main item): (1) Contracts (packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts ~1345): add archivedThreads: Schema.optional(Schema.Literal("lazy")) to OrchestrationSubscribeShellInput. Add an RPC orchestration.listArchivedThreadShells {projectId?, worktreeId?, cursor?, limit} -> {threads: OrchestrationThreadShell[], nextCursor} to ORCHESTRATION_WS_METHODS and rpc.ts. Leave OrchestrationShellSnapshotBeginItem.archivedThreadCount as is, but in lazy mode it holds a count. (2) Server (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts): give buildShell an includeArchived flag. Add AND archived_at IS NULL to listActiveThreadShellRows and to the thread subqueries of listActiveThreadSessionShellRows and listActiveLatestTurnRows; extending scopedThreadFilter is enough. Add a COUNT query for archived live threads. Keep two coalesceConcurrentRuns instances, one per variant. Implement listArchivedThreadShells with keyset pagination on (archived_at DESC, thread_id), backed by a partial index migration on projection_threads(archived_at, thread_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND archived_at IS NOT NULL. (3) orchestrationStreams.ts makeReplayableShellStream: thread the option into the snapshot effect and the legacy priority snapshot path (prioritySnapshotFlights must be keyed per variant). In lazy mode, map thread.archived to a thread-removed item and thread.unarchived to a full upsert. pageShellSnapshot takes the count from the query. (4) Clients: wsRpcClient.subscribeShell sends archivedThreads: "lazy". Add a client-runtime archived-threads domain (paged fetch, invalidated by archive and unarchive events). Migrate the consumers: ArchivedThreadsPanel, sidebar worktree lists and archived counts, projectsModel, projectMapModel, workItemLocalLinks, desktopRelaunchGuard, sessionTabs deep links to archived threads (fetch by id), client-runtime terminal cleanup and threadNotifications, mobile homeGrouping, projectsModel, ThreadDetailScreen and environmentSnapshotCodec. (5) Tests: shell.test (lazy excludes archived, count correct, cursor paging), shellSnapshotPages.test, orchestrationStreams archive and unarchive transitions under lazy, a compatibility test that a subscriber without the flag still gets archived threads, a client store test, and a browser test of the archived panel and an archived deep link. Compact fields (optional): (1) First add Schema.withDecodingDefault(null) (0 for manualPosition) to the optional(NullOr) fields of OrchestrationThreadShell, and ship those clients. (2) Then gate server-side key omission on a subscribeShell capability (compactThreadShells: true) in the mapper at ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3133-3172 and in the thread-upsert path. (3) Add a round-trip test that compact and full decode to equal values. Cheap independent win (S): (1) Memoize pageShellSnapshot results per snapshot object with a WeakMap in shellSnapshotPages.ts, so paged subscribers that share a coalesced build do not each re-stringify every thread. (2) Add a test asserting reuse.

Needs a decision

Lazy archived threads change the subscribeShell protocol (a new capability plus a new RPC) and product behaviour across web, desktop and mobile. Archived threads would no longer be in the client store for the archived panel, sidebar counts, deep links or offline mobile snapshots, and an old-client compatibility path is needed. Omitting null or default fields changes the client-observed wire shape (null becomes undefined) and needs client-first rollout or capability gating. An alternative that only applies the unarchived part early on the client would make the shell ready from a partial snapshot, which touches the AGENTS.md rule that mutation readiness requires accepting a current shell snapshot. No Hub or E2EE change is needed.

Done#47 Statistics recompute everything (6 full reads plus about 130 ms of JS) inside a transaction that holds the only connection, and any write invalidates the cache

persistence-boot:statistics-recompute-blocks-connection · original impact Medium, effort M · Caching WP06

Current state

The auditor is right that the described cost is gone. Statistics rows are read in one transaction on the read-only worker-thread connection. In production that is Node or Electron in Node mode; only Bun dev builds fall back. Decode and aggregation run after that transaction, chunked by thread. Per-thread partials are persisted, and only threads with new thread events or changed meta are re-read. checkpoint_files_json is summed in SQLite on the worker, each token payload is parsed once, and both statistics queries use the kind and usage indexes. The writer connection is held only for a cheap revision probe and short chunked partial writes. The auditor missed one defect, which the fix itself introduced. The stale-while-revalidate bookkeeping can latch a finished fiber, after which every later request returns the same old snapshot until the server restarts. I reproduced this in isolation with the repo's effect 4.0.2. Whether a real request hits it is unconfirmed and probably rare. The auditor's two residuals also hold: every new migration forces a full rebuild, and the full-rebuild decode is not chunked.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:263 reader = SqliteReadClient (worker connection), wired at apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/Sqlite.ts:74. canUseReadWorker (apps/server/src/persistence/SqliteReadClient.ts) excludes only Bun and in-memory databases. The server runs under node (apps/server/package.json dev/start) and the packaged desktop runs it under ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, so production reads go off the writer. Only statistics and DailyRecap share the worker, so there is no new head-of-line blocking for interactive reads.
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:603-611 reader.withTransaction(readRows) runs the read only. aggregate() runs after it, outside any transaction, and calls Effect.yieldNow every 256 threads (:432). effect 4.0.2's MixedScheduler yields through setImmediate, so I/O can run between chunks. This replaces the old sql.withTransaction(cache check + computeStatistics) at f1be4abc7 StatisticsQuery.ts:731-769.
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:365-391 Dirty set: threads with aggregate_kind='thread' events after coveredSequence, plus meta changes and deleted threads. A commit from another process (data_version), a history that moved backwards, or a projection reset forces a full rebuild. I checked every writer of projection_turns, projection_thread_activities and orchestration_events. Only the projection pipeline writes them, keyed by event.payload.threadId. ThreadFork and session imports go through the engine, and the 088 repair touches only tool payloads. The invariant holds.
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:161-190 Checkpoint file totals are computed with json_each in SQL, so the JS no longer parses 8.6 MB of checkpoint JSON.
  • apps/server/src/statistics/statisticsAggregation.ts:317-321 Each token payload is parsed once and shared by every pass (proposal 5).
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations/085_ProjectionThreadActivityKindIndex.ts:42 idx_projection_thread_activities_kind_order(kind, thread_id, ...) is new since f1be4abc7. The usage index from migration 071 has stream_id as its leading column, so the scoped token reads are indexed (proposal 6).
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:616-624 DEFECT: sharedRefresh forks `refresh` with an `ensuring` that clears backgroundRefresh, then sets backgroundRefresh = fiber in a later `tap`. forkIn only schedules the child. If the parent fiber reaches its op budget at the boundary between forkIn and tap, the child runs first. A cache-hit refresh finishes synchronously (cacheLock and a sync node:sqlite readRevision). The child's ensuring clears the variable, and then the tap stores the finished fiber. /tmp/perf3/scratch047/race5.mjs uses this exact pattern with the default MaxOpsBeforeYield. It ends with backgroundRefresh holding the finished fiber for 8 of 4200 preceding-op counts (two adjacent counts per ~1023).
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:637-643 Every production call is a stale-while-revalidate call: statisticsRpc.ts always passes maxWaitMs, and `stale` is defined after the first snapshot. Once backgroundRefresh holds a finished fiber, sharedRefresh returns it, Fiber.join returns its old snapshot at once, and refresh never runs again. The web and mobile UI never show generatedAt, so the staleness is silent until the server restarts.
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:282 Residual: schemaVersion = MAX(migration_id), and loadPersistedState drops the partials when it changes (:480). Any release that adds a migration therefore makes the next first open a full rebuild. It runs on the worker, but the RPC waits for it because restored state has no snapshot (:638).
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:409-415 Residual: on a full rebuild, Schema decode of every token and turn row runs unchunked on the main thread before the 256-thread yield loop. loadPersistedState also JSON.parses every persisted partial unchunked (:491-493). Both are small next to the original 0.4-0.6 s writer stall.
Defects in the shipped fix

Latent stale-while-revalidate race added by the fix (39d17c78f), apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:616-624. backgroundRefresh is cleared in the child's `ensuring` but set in the parent's `tap` after forkIn. forkIn only schedules the child (effect 4.0.2 forkUnsafe -> scheduleTask). If the parent's op budget expires at that boundary, the child runs first. A cache-hit refresh completes synchronously, so the order is: child clears, then tap stores the finished fiber. From then on every getStatistics({maxWaitMs}) call, which is every production call, joins that finished fiber and returns the same snapshot until restart, and the UI gives no sign of it. I reproduced the exact pattern in isolation with the repo's effect 4.0.2 and the default budget (/tmp/perf3/scratch047/race5.mjs: stuck for 8 of 4200 preceding-op counts). Not shown on a real RPC path: whether a request lands on that boundary depends on the handler's op count since its last async resume, so it is probably rare. The auditor's residuals also stand: a full rebuild after any new migration, and an unchunked decode on full rebuilds. Neither is a regression.

Implementation sketch

1) Fix the race in StatisticsQuery.ts sharedRefresh (:616-624). Drop the `ensuring` clear. In the tap, set `backgroundRefresh = fiber` and then call `fiber.addObserver(() => { if (backgroundRefresh === fiber) backgroundRefresh = undefined })`. addObserver fires at once on a finished fiber, so both orders end cleared. As a guard, reuse backgroundRefresh only while `backgroundRefresh.pollUnsafe() === undefined`. pollUnsafe and addObserver are public Fiber API and are already used in ClaudeAdapter.ts:5040/5877. Better still, extract the single-flight background-refresh pattern into a small shared helper if a second user appears. Test in StatisticsQuery.test.ts: run getStatistics twice under `Effect.provideService(Scheduler.MaxOpsBeforeYield, n)` for n in 4..32, with no writes in between so the refresh is a cache hit. Then write a row and assert that a later getStatistics({maxWaitMs: 5000}) returns the new data. Today this fails for some n (n=8 latched in the isolated run). 2) Optional, low value: key persisted partials on a statistics-source schema version (bump STATISTICS_PARTIAL_FORMAT_VERSION when a migration rewrites threads, turns, activities, events or worktree rows) instead of MAX(migration_id), so upgrades stay incremental. Then add a migration-checklist note. 3) Optional: decode token and turn rows per thread chunk inside the aggregation loop, and parse persisted partials in chunks, so a full rebuild never runs one long main-thread slice.

Done#48 Projector catch-up replays one event per transaction and decodes every event even when no lagging projector consumes it: 50k events took 29 s before routes served

persistence-boot:projector-replay-per-event-tx · original impact Medium, effort M · Database

Current state

Confirmed DONE. #710 (60633eff3, an ancestor of HEAD and of the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3) rewrote bootstrapProjectors, and no later commit touched it. Replay now reads only the event types routed to lagging projectors, filtered in SQL so skipped rows are never decoded. It applies 500 events per sql.withTransaction and writes cursors with one multi-row upsert per batch. A single tail transaction moves cursors past unread events, and progress is logged at start, every 5 s and at completion. The batching gain is real: Sqlite.ts keeps the default synchronous (FULL) in WAL mode, so the old code paid a WAL sync on every event. I tried to refute the fix and found no regression. Cursor tracking is per projector and updated only after commit. The type filter matches the exhaustive routing table, which uses satisfies Record<OrchestrationEventType>, and applyProjectorsForEvent applies the same routing. A failed batch rolls back whole. Post-commit effects keep their order and run after the batch commits. readThroughSequence has only this one caller, and no other boot path replays the log per event. No migration since the report resets projection_state, so nothing forces a dense replay today. The skipped optional proposal parts (seeding cursors in a migration, running catch-up after the listener starts) were alternatives, not requirements, and are not needed for the cost this finding describes. A separate, older issue that this finding does not cover: replay re-runs filesystem post-commit side effects against today's disk. Replaying thread.reverted prunes attachments of messages sent later, and replaying project.avatar-set(null) removes the current avatar. Both behave the same in the old per-event code and only trigger if the threadMessages or projects projector lags.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionPipeline.ts:2607-2721 bootstrapProjectors: lagging projectors, projectorEventTypes(lagging), readThroughSequence(..., { eventTypes }), Stream.grouped(BOOTSTRAP_REPLAY_BATCH_SIZE), one sql.withTransaction per batch, advanceCursors once per batch (:2677), tail cursor transaction (:2702-2715), progress logs (:2628, :2688-2694, :2716).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionPipeline.ts:210-224 BOOTSTRAP_REPLAY_BATCH_SIZE = 500. projectorEventTypes is the inverse of the exhaustive ORCHESTRATION_EVENT_PROJECTORS table (:114-208, satisfies Record<OrchestrationEventType,...>).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionPipeline.ts:2510-2559 applyProjectorsForEvent: advanceCursors:false skips the per-event cursor upsert during replay. The live path (:2723-2741) still advances per event inside the append transaction.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/OrchestrationEventStore.ts:278-302 The SQL appends AND event_type IN (...) when eventTypes is set. readThroughSequence (:421-475) decodes only the returned rows. Its only caller is ProjectionPipeline.ts:2655.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/Sqlite.ts:45-55 WAL with the default synchronous (FULL), so the old per-event commit paid a WAL sync per event. Batching cuts that about 500x.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionPipeline.bootstrap.test.ts:61-186 Test with 1001 project events plus 3 unconsumed events. It asserts every replay read has event_type IN, ceil(N/500)+1 cursor writes, the tail cursor stamped with the head event time, and that a second boot reads nothing.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationEngine.ts:601-604 Catch-up still runs before the engine forks its worker and before the listener starts (an optional proposal alternative). With type filtering, a sparse new projector such as worktrees reads only its own events.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations/001_OrchestrationEvents.ts:8-42 No event_type index, so the filtered query scans the sequence range. event_type sits early in the row record and payload overflow pages are not read, so this is cheap compared with decode and commit.

Current state

Commit d6a3f6819 fixed the finding's main points. User-message anchors no longer carry text, assistant messages are not kept at all (they only bump updatedAt), plan markdown is replaced by a placeholder both live and when hydrated, hydration reads two anchors per thread by primary key with no text columns, and an id index replaced find/map. Done#50 Per-thread correlated subqueries on every hydration and shell build (user-message anchors, latestCompletedTurnAt) should be summary columns

persistence-boot:denormalize-anchors-latest-completed · original impact Medium, effort M · Database WP05

Current state

Confirmed DONE. Migration 087 (d6a3f6819) stores first_user_message_id, latest_user_message_id and latest_completed_turn_at on projection_threads and keeps them current with triggers. Hydration (listThreadRows and listUserMessageAnchorRows), shell builds and the single-thread query read the columns, so both per-thread correlated subqueries are gone. A read-only parity check on the user's real DB (791 threads, 3,569 turns, 33,924 messages, written for two days since the migration) found zero mismatches in all three columns against the original rules. Two small leftovers, neither a correctness bug. (1) The turn update trigger has no value-change WHEN guard. It fires on every projection_turns upsert, including the one each streamed assistant delta causes, and recomputes the thread twice (NEW and OLD). That adds about 25 us per upsert in an in-memory benchmark. The message update trigger is role-filtered. The session update trigger has an active_turn_id-changed guard. The turn update trigger (114-123) has no WHEN guard and recomputes for both NEW and OLD.

The thread row is already rewritten per event (ProjectionPipeline.ts:1160-1180), so the extra cost is CPU, not extra WAL pages.

Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness defects. One minor inefficiency on a hot write path. projection_turns_latest_completed_update (087:114-123) has no value-change WHEN guard, and ProjectionTurns.upsertByTurnId (ProjectionTurns.ts:79-92) always lists the watched columns in DO UPDATE SET. As a result, every assistant delta's turn upsert runs two latest-completed recomputes and two projection_threads row rewrites, the second for OLD.thread_id, which is the same thread. An in-memory benchmark (500 turns, 2 KB thread row) measured about 25 us extra per upsert. That is negligible at about 30 deltas/s per streaming thread. The message and session update triggers also recompute NEW and OLD when thread_id did not change.

Partial#52 One synchronous connection on the main thread: heavy reads block the event loop and queue behind writes, and busy_timeout=5000 can freeze the loop for 5 s

persistence-boot:main-thread-single-connection · original impact Medium, effort L · Blocking I/O WP05

Current state

PARTIAL is correct. 79b492cd6 added the short main-connection busy_timeout with async wall-clock retry, so the 5 s event-loop freeze is gone on Node. It also added SqliteReadClient, a read-only WAL connection in a worker_thread. Only statistics (39d17c78f) and the daily recap (05f67fe79) were moved onto that worker. Engine hydration (getCommandReadModel), getSnapshot, the full and scoped shell builds, message search, event replay reads and the other ProjectionSnapshotQuery reads still run in transactions on the single main connection behind Semaphore(1). So the head-of-line blocking the finding describes, such as the AgentControl lookup queued behind hydration, can still happen. d6a3f6819 and 502adfd1e made those reads cheaper but did not move them off-thread. I also found a correctness defect the auditor missed in the busy-retry part. A non-transactional statement runs without holding the semaphore. The async retry sleeps on a timer and then re-runs the statement on the shared connection, so it can land inside another fiber's open transaction.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/persistence/sqliteBusy.ts:18-44 MAIN_CONNECTION_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=25, BUSY_RETRY_BUDGET_MS=5000, backoff 5..100 ms, SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT (517) not retried.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/Sqlite.ts:40-44 busy_timeout is 25 ms on Node and 5000 ms only on Bun. The server runs on Node in dev and prod (apps/server/package.json:20,23), so the Bun path does not matter.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/NodeSqliteClient.ts:143-162 execute() catches retryable SQLITE_BUSY, sleeps with wallClockSleep (setTimeout) and re-runs attempt() on the same db/statement. It does not re-acquire the connection semaphore.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/NodeSqliteClient.ts:229 acquirer = semaphore.withPermits(1)(Effect.succeed(connection)) releases the permit as soon as it hands out the connection. effect 4.0.2 Statement.ts:1438-1440 then runs the statement as Effect.scoped(acquirer.flatMap(f)), so non-transactional statements, and now their async busy retries, run without the permit. Unchanged since f1be4abc7:222. Only the retry suspension point is new.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/NodeSqliteClient.ts:230-237 transactionAcquirer holds the permit for the whole transaction scope, and BEGIN is deferred. While fiber A sleeps in a busy retry, fiber B can take the permit and BEGIN on the same DatabaseSync. A's retried statement then runs inside B's transaction.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/Sqlite.test.ts:43-87 The busy tests cover a single INSERT against a lock-holding child process. There is no test of a busy retry running at the same time as a transaction on the main connection.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/SqliteReadClient.ts:58-62 readClientFor (auditor cited :77) keeps callers that are inside a main-connection transaction on main. It has no production caller. A grep finds it only in SqliteReadClient.test.ts.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/SqliteReadClient.ts:65-122 Inline worker source: a readOnly DatabaseSync with query_only, mmap, 32 MiB cache, busy_timeout 5000 off-thread, and an LRU of prepared statements.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/SqliteReadClient.ts:344-393 Worker client: one Semaphore(1) for the worker, falling back to main.reserve when the worker cannot start. Because the semaphore is 1, all worker reads share one queue, so a statistics recompute would block any shell builds later moved onto it.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/Sqlite.ts:74-87 SqliteReadClientLayer.layer(dbPath) is part of the production persistence layer.
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:263 Statistics reads rows through the worker (39d17c78f). Only the revision probe stays on main.
  • apps/server/src/statistics/DailyRecapQuery.ts:96-99 The daily recap reads on the worker (05f67fe79), with its own queriesOn(sql) pattern for the case where the caller is inside a transaction.
Remaining

Heavy reads are still on the main connection. Engine hydration (OrchestrationEngine.ts:602 -> ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:2716), getSnapshot (:2399), full and scoped shell builds (:3010), getWorkspacePlacement and listPendingGoalSyncThreads (:3236, :3283), message search (:1595), history-page reads, and event replay reads (OrchestrationEventStore.ts:369) all run on the single DatabaseSync behind Semaphore(1). They block the event loop for the length of their SQL and queue unrelated queries behind them. That includes the boot-time AgentControl lookup waiting on hydration, the finding's own example. Only StatisticsQuery.ts:263 and DailyRecapQuery.ts:96 use the read worker. readClientFor (SqliteReadClient.ts:58) has no production caller.

Defects in the shipped fix

Concurrency bug introduced by 79b492cd6. The main acquirer (NodeSqliteClient.ts:229) releases the semaphore before the statement executes, which was harmless while execution was synchronous. execute() (NodeSqliteClient.ts:143-162) now retries a busy statement after an async wall-clock sleep, on the same connection and without re-taking the permit. Failing scenario: the offline CLI holds the write lock, and fiber A issues a non-transactional write (for example an auth_sessions UPDATE, AuthSessions.ts:253) that gets SQLITE_BUSY and sleeps. Fiber B then takes the permit and runs a deferred BEGIN through sql.withTransaction. A's retry fires and executes inside B's open transaction. If B later fails or is interrupted and ROLLBACKs, A's write is silently discarded even though A returned success. If B already holds an older WAL snapshot, A instead fails with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT, a failure it would not otherwise hit. Reads retried this way also see B's uncommitted rows. No test covers a busy retry running alongside a transaction. Minor issues: StatisticsQuery and DailyRecap hand-roll serviceOption(SqliteReadClient) instead of readClientFor. The worker's failure counter resets on every successful start (SqliteReadClient.ts:230), so a statement that crashes the worker after it starts restarts it indefinitely rather than reaching the MAX_WORKER_FAILURES fallback. Auditor line refs were slightly off: readClientFor is at :58, not :77; the worker source is at :65-122 and the fallback client at :344-393.

Implementation sketch

1) Fix the retry race first (S, low risk). In NodeSqliteClient.makeWithDatabase, pass Client.make a borrower that holds the permit for the whole statement, including busy retries: borrower: (f) => semaphore.withPermits(1)(f(connection)). effect 4.0.2 supports MakeOptions.borrower and Statement.ts:1438-1440 uses it for every non-transaction statement, which also saves a Scope per statement. Make the remaining acquirer (stream/reserve) scope-holding like transactionAcquirer so nothing runs on the shared connection without the permit. Statements inside a transaction still resolve the transaction connection first, so this adds no deadlock. Regression test in persistence/Layers/Sqlite.test.ts, reusing spawnWriteLockHolder: hold the lock for 300 ms and fork a non-transactional INSERT. After ~20 ms run sql.withTransaction(wallClock sleep 500 ms, then Effect.fail). Assert the INSERT's row exists afterwards; today it is rolled back with the transaction. Add one more test that busy retry inside a transaction still succeeds. 2) Move the heavy readers to the worker (M/L, medium risk). In ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts, build the SqlSchema query set from a client, queriesOn(client) as DailyRecapQuery.ts:99 does, once for main and once for the reader. In buildShell, getCommandReadModel, getSnapshot, getWorkspacePlacement, listPendingGoalSyncThreads, searchThreadMessages and the history-page reads, pick the client with readClientFor(sql) and run client.withTransaction with that client's queries. Calls inside a main transaction stay on main, consistent with the existing branch at :3210. Use readClientFor in StatisticsQuery and DailyRecapQuery too. For boot hydration (OrchestrationEngine.ts:602), read the command read model on the worker after projectionPipeline.bootstrap commits; read-your-writes holds for a new WAL read transaction. Optionally read latestSequence inside the same worker transaction for a consistent pair. Move event replay pages (OrchestrationEventStore.readFromSequence) only for catch-up and replay callers, not the dispatch path at OrchestrationEngine.ts:204. 3) Avoid a new head-of-line queue on the worker. Give statistics its own worker or a small pool (two read workers), or split the queue so shell builds are not serialized behind a 0.5 s statistics recompute (SqliteReadClient.ts:351). 4) Tests: run the ProjectionSnapshotQuery suites against a file DB with the worker layer as well as main, and add parity assertions (worker result deep-equals main result). Add a SqliteReadClient test that a main-connection query completes while a long worker transaction is open. Validate with perf:external --fixture-home (d6a3f6819 generator) on a cold boot and check in the trace that small main-connection lookups no longer wait on hydration.

Value medium · effort M · risk medium

Done#53 canResumeAfter reads and Schema-decodes up to 1,001 events per resubscribed stream just to compute hasMore

persistence-boot:resume-probe-decodes-1000-events · original impact Low, effort S · Database

Current state

Confirmed DONE. PR #710 (60633eff3) replaced the two decoding readEventsPage probes in canResumeAfter. The new path is a payload-free store probe (probeResume): EXISTS on the sequence key, plus count(*) over an inner LIMIT limit+1, plus, for threads, a count over the stream index. It is wired in production because OrchestrationLayerLive is provideMerge'd in server.ts, so Effect.serviceOption(OrchestrationEventStore) in ws/context.ts resolves to Some. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on the real schema shows a rowid range search for the global count and a COVERING INDEX idx_orch_events_stream_sequence search for the stream count, with no JSON parse and no Schema decode. Threads replayed through their own stream skip the global count (limit 0). The only events decoded now are the ones the replay actually sends. One latent side effect: the old probe happened to fall back to a snapshot when a gap event would not decode. That fallback is gone. This is not observed in practice (see fixDefects).

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:688 canResumeAfter uses deps.probeResume (lines 691-722) and decides on anchored and the capped counts. It decodes no events. The old two-readEventsPage path (723-729) runs only when no probe is wired, i.e. in narrow test doubles.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/OrchestrationEventStore.ts:510 probeResume runs EXISTS(sequence = ?) and count(*) over (SELECT 1 ... sequence > ? LIMIT limit+1). For threads it adds a stream-index count capped at limit+1 (528-536). payload_json is never selected.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Services/OrchestrationEventStore.ts:109 The probeResume contract is documented as reading the sequence key and stream index and never payload_json. It is optional, which is why the fallback path still exists.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:1274 eventStore.probeResume and readStreamEventsPage are passed into makeOrchestrationStreamHelpers. The store comes from Effect.serviceOption at context.ts:207 and is provided through server.ts:505 (provideMerge OrchestrationLayerLive, which re-exports OrchestrationEventStoreLive per orchestration/runtimeLayer.ts:11-33).
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:815 The shell resubscribe path calls canResumeAfter(resumeFromSequence).
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:896 The thread resubscribe path calls canResumeAfter(resumeFromSequence, { threadId }). Its replay reads its own stream through readStreamEventsPage (944-958).
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations/001_OrchestrationEvents.ts:9 sequence is INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, and idx_orch_events_stream_sequence (aggregate_kind, stream_id, sequence) exists (line 31). A scratch-DB EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN confirmed 'SEARCH USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid>?)' and 'SEARCH USING COVERING INDEX idx_orch_events_stream_sequence'.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/OrchestrationEventStore.test.ts:245 The store test sets payload_json to 'not json' and the probe still answers, which proves it never parses payloads. It also checks the limit+1 cap and the stream count.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreamBatching.test.ts:306 The 'resume decisions' tests cover thread own-backlog resume, the snapshot over 1,000 thread events, and the fallback global scan bound. Line 237 asserts that the resume decision reads no event page.

Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defect in the perf fix. One latent robustness change, not observed in practice. The old probe decoded the gap events, so an undecodable event there made canResumeAfter return false and the client got a snapshot. The snapshot replays from about the latest sequence and skips the bad row. The payload-free probe now resumes instead: the 'resumed' head is sent, and the replay then fails with OrchestrationGetSnapshotError (orchestrationStreams.ts:556-566). That error is not retryable in wsTransport.ts:381. For thread windows, supervision.ts:658-659 resets failedWindowAttempts on the 'resumed' item, and appliedSequence is unchanged, so the client retries the same resume every THREAD_WINDOW_RETRY_BASE_MS (1 s) indefinitely. This only matters if a stored event stops decoding, for example after an incompatible schema change while a direct client was away. Hosted and hub-hosted thread subscriptions never resume (supervision.ts:562).

Done#54 SQLite runs with default page cache (2 MB), no mmap, file temp store and no PRAGMA optimize on a database that grows to hundreds of MB

Current state

The auditor is right. Commit 60633eff3 (#710) added PRAGMA mmap_size=256MiB and cache_size=-32768 to the shared setup layer, before migrations. Commit 79b492cd6 added the same two pragmas to the new read-only worker connection. Those are the only two SQLite connections the server opens on its own database: NodeSqliteClient uses a single DatabaseSync behind a semaphore, and the worker is the second. The other DatabaseSync in server src (opencodeUsageReader) opens OpenCode's external database. Every entry point (server.ts, ws.ts, cli.ts, AuthControlPlane.ts) goes through layerConfig, so the CLI process gets the tuning too. The server runs on Node in dev and in production. A test asserts that mmap is really enabled (non-zero, so node:sqlite's compile cap does not silently disable it), that cache_size is -32768, and that synchronous stays FULL. temp_store=MEMORY and PRAGMA optimize/ANALYZE were left out on purpose, with the A/B rationale in a code comment. That covers the earlier verifier's concern about plan changes. The measured gain in the finding came from mmap, and that is implemented. I found no regression. The only gaps are journal_size_limit (disk hygiene) and a missing test for the worker pragmas.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/Sqlite.ts:56-57 PRAGMA mmap_size = 268435456 and PRAGMA cache_size = -32768 on the main connection. They run before trackStartupPhase("persistence.migrations") at line 60, so migrations and boot hydration both benefit.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/Sqlite.ts:47-55 The comment records a repeated A/B: 5 runs per variant, twice, on a 5k-thread / 400k-activity database. It also records the deliberate rejection of temp_store=MEMORY and optimize/ANALYZE, and that synchronous stays at its default per docs/streaming-sqlite.md.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/SqliteReadClient.ts:69-73 The read-only worker connection sets the same mmap_size and cache_size. These pragmas are per connection, so this covers the heavy off-thread read path (introduced in 79b492cd6).
  • apps/server/src/persistence/NodeSqliteClient.ts:226-229,257 The main client opens a single DatabaseSync behind a Semaphore(1). There is no connection pool, so no other connection misses the setup pragmas.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/Sqlite.test.ts:98-118 The test 'applies the A/B-tested read tuning to file databases' asserts cache_size=-32768, mmap_size > 0 and <= 256MiB (guards against a compile-time mmap cap of 0), and synchronous=2.
  • apps/server/src/cli.ts:134 The CLI, server.ts:65, ws.ts:11 and auth/Layers/AuthControlPlane.ts:9 all use layerConfig from Layers/Sqlite.ts, so every process that opens state.sqlite gets the same tuning.
  • apps/server/package.json:20,23 dev runs `node --watch src/bin.ts` and start runs `node dist/bin.mjs`. The Bun client path (system SQLite on macOS, mmap possibly capped) is not what users run.

Defects in the shipped fix

No real defects. Minor gaps: (1) PRAGMA journal_size_limit (proposed at 64 MiB) is not set anywhere in apps/server/src. The new read worker can now hold long read transactions (whole-history statistics), which can starve checkpoints. The WAL then grows and stays at its high-water size on disk until the last connection closes. That costs disk space, not read speed. (2) No test asserts the worker connection's mmap/cache pragmas (SqliteReadClient.test.ts has none). (3) The A/B harness behind the numbers in the comment is not committed (scripts/measure-persistence-reads.ts has no pragma variants), so the figures cannot be reproduced. That does not break the fix.

Done#55 Small boot and runtime overheads: N+1 orphan-chat sweep, and every SQL statement exported as a roughly 1 KB trace span

Both parts of the finding are fixed by 60633eff3 (#710). That commit is an ancestor of HEAD and of the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3. I checked Effect 4.0.2's sql/Statement.js: it sets db.query.text through span.attribute(), so the filter does see it. No consumer of local SQL spans exists in web, desktop scripts or diagnostics. Evidence
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/ProjectionProjects.ts:177-213 listOrphanChatProjectRows: chat projects that are not deleted and have created_at < cutoff, with NOT EXISTS over projection_threads excluding rolled-back creations (deleted_at NOT NULL, trashed_at NULL, latest_turn_id NULL, latest_user_message_at NULL, lineage_source_message_id NULL). This mirrors isRolledBackThreadCreation and isNeverUsedThread in persistence/Services/ProjectionThreads.ts:83-100. The correlated subquery uses idx on projection_threads(project_id) (005:121) and (project_id, deleted_at, created_at) (019:14).
  • apps/server/src/project/orphanChatProjects.ts:88-100 One listOrphanChatProjects call. The fork ledger (2 queries) is read only when chats.length > 0. The threads repository is no longer a dependency, so no per-chat reads remain. Old code at f1be4abc7 lines 58-72 did listAll plus listByProjectId for each chat.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1028-1067 The sweep is forked (Effect.forkScoped) after commandGate.signalCommandReady, http.wait and ready.publish. At f1be4abc7 it was forked at line 896, before workspace.validate (line 906), so it competed with startup.
  • apps/server/src/observability/LocalFileTracer.ts:27,89-101 DEFAULT_LOCAL_TRACE_SQL_MIN_DURATION_MS = 50. keepsLocalRecord drops a successful db.query.text span shorter than the threshold before spanToTraceRecord and sink.push. That removes the JSON serialisation, the file write and the diagnostics ring entry. Failures are always kept.
  • apps/server/node_modules/effect/dist/sql/Statement.js:734-746,784-789 Effect 4.0.2 sets db.query.text through span.attribute() after span creation, inside withConnectionSpan, so LocalFileSpan.attributes sees it before end(). The span covers semaphore acquisition too, so statements queued for 50 ms or more are kept as slow.
  • apps/server/src/observability/Layers/Observability.ts:23-25,48-57,78 RYCO_TRACE_SQL_MIN_DURATION_MS config (default 50) is passed to the tracer. diagnosticsSink.push wraps both the file sink and diagnostics.recordTraceRecords, so both are filtered. Documented at docs/observability.md:515-517. Tests are at LocalFileTracer.test.ts:131-180.
  • apps/server/src/observability/LocalFileTracer.ts:103-112 Minor leftover: normalizeSqlText (a regex replace over the whole SQL) runs eagerly in attribute() for every statement, including the ones that keepsLocalRecord then drops. A local micro-benchmark on the largest ProjectionProjects SQL (about 2 KB) measured about 2.5 us per call, so roughly 30-40 us per 12-15-statement event commit. That is far below the serialisation and write cost that was removed.
Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defects. One small inefficiency: LocalFileTracer.ts:103-112 normalises db.query.text on every SQL attribute set, but only slow or failed SQL spans are ever serialised. Normalisation could happen at keep time instead (about 2.5 us per 2 KB statement; it is a net win either way). The proposed aggregate per-query metrics were not implemented, so locally there is no count or time for fast SQL unless the threshold is set to 0. This is an observability gap, not a perf bug. The sweep now runs after the gate, so in theory it can race with a client re-sending a first message to a chat older than 1 h. The project.delete guards (expectedUpdatedAt, expectedThreadIds: []) still fail closed, and the worst outcome is the same retired-chat error the old pre-gate ordering always produced.
