Done#56 The hub cloud thread index rebuilds the whole shell up to once per second while events flow, and throws once the shell exceeds about 2 MiB (about 1.6k threads)

persistence-boot:hub-read-cache-full-shell · original impact Low, effort M · Reliability WP05

Current state

Confirmed DONE for the case the finding measured, a node with many threads. The cloud index is now patched from domain events by threadReadCacheShellMirror (502adfd1e). The full schema re-decode became a row-limit check (502adfd1e), and a shell over 2 MiB is cut down to its most recently updated threads (60633eff3). Nodes with 1.6k to 10k threads now upload. On a synthetic 4.5k-thread shell, the remaining work per shell publish measured about 15 ms, down from the reported 140 ms. While agents stream, shell publishes alternate with content batches. The auditor missed two edge defects in the cut-down approach. A node with more than 10,000 threads (archived and trashed included) still fails every upload. A node whose project and worktree rows take up most of the 2 MiB, about 2.1k worktree rows at roughly 800 B each, gets into a Hub 409 loop: begin, conflict, a new generation that wipes the cloud cache, and again. Both are rare, and the feature is opt-in.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/threadReadCacheShellMirror.ts:78-103,117-191,193-222 Records rows per event and patches them with getThreadShellById, getProjectShellById and getWorktreeShellById. It rebuilds on unmodeled events, failures, more than 256 rows, and every 60 s. I checked the edge cases. The domain PubSub is bounded with backpressure, so no events are dropped (OrchestrationEngine.ts:180). Projection runs inside the commit transaction before publish (OrchestrationEngine.ts ~461-463, 517). No thread event writes another aggregate's row in ProjectionPipeline. Deleted rows are filtered the same way (deleted_at IS NULL) in the list query and the by-id queries. The ordering-changing events worktree.manualPositionSet, worktree.relocated and worktree.deleted fall through to a rebuild.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/ThreadReadCacheSync.ts:121,128,211-218 readShell reads from the mirror. notifyChanged records the event, and HubConnectorLive.ts:714-719 passes each event in. The feature is still opt-in (HubConnectorLive.ts:692-694).
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/ThreadReadCachePublisher.ts:51-76,101-112,196 boundThreadReadCacheShell cuts the shell down to its newest threads. checkThreadReadCacheShellLimits (three length checks) replaced Schema.decodeUnknownSync(ThreadReadCacheShell). The limit check at :196 runs on the full shell, before bounding.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/ThreadReadCachePublisher.ts:107 + ThreadReadCachePublisher.test.ts:272-280 Defect: a shell with more than 10,000 threads throws 'row limits' before boundThreadReadCacheShell runs, and a test pins this. In a simulation of the current publisher code, a 10,001-thread shell threw and a 9,999-thread shell uploaded. The bounded index would hold about 1.5k threads, well under the Hub's 10k filter, so the refusal is not needed for threads.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/ThreadReadCachePublisher.ts:224-240 Defect: recentThreads is the 512 newest threads of the full shell. Thread content is limited to indexed threads only when the shell yields (:240). When the bounded shell keeps fewer than 512 threads, a normal batch uploads bodies for threads missing from the index. In a simulation of the current code with 2,100 worktrees (795 B each) and 1,000 threads, 413 threads were kept and batch 27 sent bodies for thread-586 and others that the index does not list.
  • ryco-hub:src/threadReadCache/service.ts:124 (origin/main) The Hub rejects a thread body that the current or uploaded shell does not list with node_conflict, which is HTTP 409 (identity/errors.ts:24). The node's sync answers a 409 by calling publisher.reset() (ThreadReadCacheSync.ts:172), and the next begin clears every cached projection (docs/thread-read-cache.md:16-18). The result is a loop of begin, conflict and wipe, paced only by the 10-60 s backoff.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/ThreadReadCachePublisher.ts:84-87 This still throws when projects and worktrees alone exceed 2 MiB. Archived worktrees are included (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts listActiveProjectWorktreeRows has no archived filter). In the simulation, 2,600 worktrees threw 'exceeds the upload limit'.
  • /tmp/perf3-056-scratch/bench.mjs (synthetic) Remaining cost per shell publish at 4.5k threads of about 1.4 KB each: bound (full stringify, sort, partial stringify) 11-13 ms, a second sort 1.2 ms, body stringify about 2 ms (2.09 MB), mirror patch about 0.5 ms. Total about 15 ms, against about 140 ms before.
Defects in the shipped fix

1. Thread bodies can reach the Hub before the index lists them (ThreadReadCachePublisher.ts:224-240). recentThreads comes from the full shell, and only yield batches skip threads missing from the index. When the bounded index keeps fewer than 512 threads, normal batches upload bodies the Hub rejects with 409 (Hub service.ts:124). The node then resets, begins a new generation that wipes the cloud cache, and repeats indefinitely. This happens when project and worktree rows fill most of the 2 MiB, about 2.1k worktree rows at roughly 800 B, archived ones included. I reproduced it by simulating the current code. 2. More than 10,000 non-deleted threads (archived and trashed included) still fails every upload. checkThreadReadCacheShellLimits runs on the full shell at :196 before bounding, and the test at ThreadReadCachePublisher.test.ts:272 pins it. This undercuts the fix's own goal of showing the most recent work instead of failing. 3. As the auditor noted, the upload still throws when projects and worktrees alone exceed 2 MiB (:85-87), about 2.6k worktree rows. That is not a regression, since the old code threw for any shell over 2 MiB. 4. Behaviour trade-off, as the auditor noted: above about 1.5k threads the cloud index omits older and archived threads. The Hub treats a shell as the authoritative set of threads and drops bodies for threads it does not list. 5. Residual cost, measured: about 15 ms per shell publish at 4.5k threads, plus about 2 MB uploaded per shell publish while agents stream. Adjacent and pre-existing, not caused by this fix: THREAD_READ_CACHE_MIN_PUBLISH_INTERVAL_MS is 1 s (ThreadReadCacheSync.ts:24) and every POST needs a fresh node challenge (HubNodeProofClient.ts:253). The Hub limits node challenges to 30 per minute per client IP (Hub identityRoutes.ts:261), and its docs ask nodes to pace batches at 5 s or slower. Sustained streaming can therefore hit challenge_limit and consume the same IP's challenge budget that relay reconnects use.

Implementation sketch

All changes are on the node side, in apps/server/src/hubConnector/ThreadReadCachePublisher.ts. No Hub change is needed. (a) Limit content to indexed threads in every batch. After the shell decision in synchronize(), set `const indexed = shellThreadIds ?? publishedThreadIds;`. In the content loop, replace the yield-only check at :240 with `if (!indexed.has(thread.id)) continue;`. The first batch always carries the shell, because publishedSequence is -1 and that batch never yields, so `indexed` is never empty when it matters. Alternatively, build recentThreads from the bounded snapshot rather than the full shell. Test: give the upload mock a membership check that mirrors the Hub (it throws for a thread item missing from the last uploaded or in-batch shell). Feed a shell with about 2,100 worktrees of about 800 B each and 1,000 threads, run synchronize until idle, and assert that nothing threw and every thread item was indexed. (b) Apply the thread-count limit after bounding. Make checkThreadReadCacheShellLimits check only projects and worktrees on the raw shell. Have boundThreadReadCacheShell also cap threads at THREAD_READ_CACHE_SHELL_LIMITS.threads, keeping the newest. Change the test at :272 to expect that a 10,001-thread shell publishes a bounded index, and keep the refusal for projects and worktrees. (c) Optional, needs a product call: when projects and worktrees crowd the batch, also bound worktrees. Drop archived worktrees that no kept thread references, oldest first. (d) Optional CPU work: sort shell.threads once per publish and share the order between boundThreadReadCacheShell and recentThreads. Cache each thread's JSON byte size in a WeakMap keyed by the thread object, since the mirror reuses unchanged thread objects across patches. Then skip the full-shell stringify when the summed size is already over the limit. Separately, as a follow-up for the adjacent pacing issue: raise THREAD_READ_CACHE_MIN_PUBLISH_INTERVAL_MS to 5 s or more to match the Hub's documented pacing and its 30-per-minute challenge limit, and adjust the test 'limits sustained streams to one read per second' in ThreadReadCacheSync.test.ts.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Done#57 Usage scan cache is one JSON file (64 MiB cap) parsed whole on first open and rewritten whole after every dirty scan

persistence-boot:usage-scan-cache-monolith · original impact Low, effort M · Caching WP06

Current state

Confirmed DONE. 60633eff3 replaced the single scan-cache.json with 64 hash-keyed shard files. Shards are versioned per change, only dirty shards are rewritten (atomically, with yields between them, debounced 1 s off the request path), the legacy file is migrated once, and the cache is unloaded after 10 idle minutes. e5e676f95 shrank what is stored: per-file 15-minute slots, with keyed rows only for responses that carry a dedupe key (16-hex key plus 7 numbers). The 0.3-0.6 s single parse, the full rewrite per open and the ~500k-record oversized cliff are all gone. The SQLite proposal was not taken, but the finding's own 'shard the JSON per file' alternative is implemented, along with per-file aggregates. I found no other callers, missing persistence paths, locking races or test gaps. Lock ordering is persistLock -> loadLock with no inversion, persist snapshots synchronously, and a failed write stays dirty. Two minor residuals sit next to the fix; neither reopens the finding.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCacheStore.ts:27-41 64 shards, chosen from the first byte of the SHA-256 file key. Every cache key, including OpenCode's (opencodeUsageReader.ts:215,222,361), comes from usageCacheFileKey, so keys spread evenly.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCacheStore.ts:47-97 TrackedUsageScanCache bumps a per-shard version on set/delete/clear. restore() and unload() do not dirty anything.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCacheStore.ts:190-228 persist() captures dirtyShards() and partitions entries in one synchronous step. It rewrites only dirty shards, removes empty ones, yields between shards and marks a shard persisted only after its write succeeds. A concurrent mutation bumps the version, so that shard stays dirty.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCacheStore.ts:134-183 load() reads 64 small shards with concurrency 8 and decodes each one right after its read. Legacy migration runs only when no shard exists. An oversized legacy file is left on the first load and removed after a later load (exists check at 157-163).
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:318-337 persistLock serializes the debounced background persist, the shutdown finalizer and unload, so two persists never write the same shard at once.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:339-366 The idle watcher persists, then unloads under scanSemaphore -> persistLock -> loadLock. ensureLoaded takes only loadLock, so the locks cannot deadlock.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:609-642 An unchanged file is reused without set(), so nothing is dirtied. Only a re-parsed file dirties its own shard.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCache.ts:181-243 The v6 serialized form holds per-file slots plus compact keyed rows. Codex (dedupeKey null, codexTranscript.ts:140) folds fully into slots. The commit reports 41.5 MB -> 2.4 MB (Claude) and 41.9 MB -> 0.9 MB (Codex).
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCacheStore.test.ts:59-146 Tests cover migration, rewriting only the changed shard, unload/reload, removing a shard whose last entry is deleted, retention on load, a shared concurrent load and cleanup of a leftover legacy file.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCache.ts:509-522 Residual: capUsageScanCache still weighs entries by aggregate.recordCount. That made sense when it was added in 60633eff3 (entry.records.length), but after e5e676f95 memory scales with keys.length + slots.length. Fully folded Codex/keyless files count as if each response were resident.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:1077-1086 Every summary runs the cap. A user above 1M resident responses has the oldest files evicted after each summary. Those files are re-parsed on the next request under the per-source budget (UsageService.ts:97-99, 830-838: 100k records / 5 s), so 'All'/'90d' can keep reporting transcript-scan-budget and dirty those shards each time. Rare heavy-user case.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCacheStore.ts:173-180 Residual: on load, the 120-day retention is applied unconditionally, while all-time summaries use cutoff 0 (UsageService.ts:1082-1083). In practice this is masked: the default 30d view (apps/web/src/components/settings/StatisticsPanel.tsx:57) already prunes the same files, as the old code did at f1be4abc7.
Defects in the shipped fix

No defect reopens the finding. Minor residuals: 1. capUsageScanCache (usageScanCache.ts:509-522), called at UsageService.ts:1085 and usageScanCacheStore.ts:181, still counts recordCount against USAGE_SCAN_CACHE_RECORD_LIMIT = 1,000,000. After e5e676f95 the resident cost is keys + slots. The cap therefore over-evicts folded (Codex/keyless) files for no memory gain. Above the limit it evicts the oldest files at the end of every summary. Those files are re-parsed next time under the 100k-record / 5 s per-source budget, and coverage may never converge for 'All'. In the old code, the in-memory cache converged within a process lifetime. 2. The load-time retention prune (usageScanCacheStore.ts:173-180) evicts files older than 120 days even when the request is all-time (cutoff 0). This is masked because the default 30d view prunes them anyway. It is pre-existing retention policy, not part of the monolith cost. 3. The first usage open after startup or after an idle unload still decodes all 64 shards eagerly. That is now tens of ms, not a stall.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Web bootstrap waterfall (15)

Done#58 Ryco server serves the web app uncompressed over HTTP/1.1 (6.0 MiB on the wire to reach the composer)

web-bootstrap:serve-precompressed-assets · original impact High, effort S · Network / RTT

Current state

Confirmed DONE by commit 60633eff3 (#710). The standard web build writes .gz siblings for hashed assets, and the Ryco server (Node and Bun platforms, router route and early startup-gate route) negotiates Accept-Encoding against them. Responses carry Content-Encoding, Vary: Accept-Encoding, a per-variant weak ETag, the original Content-Type and a working 304 path, and nothing is compressed on the fly. I checked the local Oct 14 dist: all 691 compressible hashed assets of 1 KiB or more have a .gz (28,015 KiB raw, 8,137 KiB gz). The only hashed files without one are 4 .pfb fonts that fail the 10% saving rule. The CORS middleware merges Vary instead of replacing it. Icon overrides only touch unhashed top-level files, so no sibling goes stale. No relay or proxy path forwards static requests in a way that could double-decode. The deviations left are minor and deliberate: gzip by default with brotli opt-in, no HTTP/2 on the plain-HTTP server, and unhashed on-demand files (vscode-icons, index.html) are served as identity. None of these is on the cold-load path to the composer at meaningful size.

Evidence
  • apps/web/vite.config.ts:132-133 createPrecompressedAssetsPlugin() is registered only for the standard client mode. Desktop and the CLI node use this mode; the only other mode is hosted-hub.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/precompressAssets.ts:31 HASHED_ASSET_PATTERN limits siblings to content-hashed names. Siblings can never go stale, and unhashed public files (index.html, vscode-icons) get none.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/precompressAssets.ts:13 A sibling is written only if it saves at least 10%. This is why the hashed Foxit*.pfb fonts have no .gz in the dist.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/precompressAssets.ts:47-56 Brotli is opt-in by design (comment: browsers send br only over HTTPS; avoids doubling package and artifact size). The server already prefers br whenever a .br exists.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/precompressAssets.ts:100-116 writeBundle iterates the Rollup bundle. Worker outputs and the pdf.js .mjs are included, but files copied from public/ are not.
  • apps/web/dist (local build, Oct 14 21:45) 691 hashed assets have .gz siblings (28,015 KiB to 8,137 KiB). Without siblings: 4 hashed .pfb files (incompressible), index.html (4 KB), desktop-boot.html, mockServiceWorker.js, favicon.svg, and about 690 on-demand vscode-icons SVGs (3.4 MB raw in total, never loaded in bulk).
  • apps/server/scripts/cli.ts:199 fs.copy(webDist, clientTarget) carries the siblings into dist/client. The local apps/server/dist/client/assets also has 691 .gz files.
  • apps/server/src/http.ts:129 staticFileEtag adds a -br/-gzip variant suffix. The stat comes from the served sibling.
  • apps/server/src/http.ts:153 acceptedStaticContentEncodings follows RFC 9110: q=0, * wildcard, x-gzip alias.
  • apps/server/src/http.ts:257-327 staticFileResponse: Vary is set for every precompressible extension. Siblings are stat-probed in parallel and the preferred one wins. Content-Type comes from the original path, and the 304 path drops Content-Encoding but keeps Vary. setHeaders overrides the platform's own ETag.
  • apps/server/src/http.ts:910 identityOnly applies only to desktop mode plus a loopback Host. LAN (desktop exposure bind 0.0.0.0) and Tailscale Serve clients of a desktop node still get gzip.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:284 The early startup-gate static handler reuses serveStaticRequest, so it negotiates the same way.
Defects in the shipped fix

No defect in the fix. Corrections and nits on the auditor's notes: 1. Auditor defect 3 is inaccurate. The .gz siblings in the desktop artifact are used: identityOnly (http.ts:910) skips them only for loopback Hosts, and a desktop node exposed on the LAN (serverExposure.ts bind 0.0.0.0) or via Tailscale Serve (which keeps the incoming Host) serves gzip to those remote browsers. 2. HTTP/2: browsers never do h2c, so h2 is only possible over TLS. The node has no TLS listener; the existing TLS path is Tailscale Serve's HTTPS frontend, which terminates TLS in front of the node. Proposal part 4 ('consider') therefore needs no Ryco-side change unless the node gains its own TLS listener. 3. Brotli off by default is a deliberate, documented trade-off. It costs about 15% more bytes (about 1853 vs 1566 KiB per cold load) only for HTTPS (Tailscale Serve) clients. 4. Unhashed on-demand files (public/vscode-icons, about 690 SVGs of 1 KiB or more, 3.4 MB in total, largest 248 KB; index.html 4 KB) are served as identity. They are not on the cold path to the composer. Unrelated aside, outside this finding: resolveStaticCacheControl (http.ts:113) classifies some unhashed public files as immutable for a year, because their basenames are 8 or more [A-Za-z0-9_-] characters: mockServiceWorker.js, apple-touch-icon.png, favicon-96x96.png, web-app-manifest-*.png and every vscode-icons SVG. This predates the fix (same regex at f1be4abc7). desktop-boot.html matches too but is loaded through the desktop custom scheme, not HTTP.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Done#60 Click-only dialogs/popovers drag ~600 KiB (markdown + parse5 + project explorer) into the RootAppShell critical graph

Current state

The finding's four cuts from #710 (60633eff3) are in place: CommentAvatar has its own module, getEditorLabel moved to an icon-free module, and the two sidebar dialogs load lazily (preloadableLazy, mounted via useLazyComponentReady) with preload on intent.   • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:5355 ChatView mounts the same two dialogs (LazyNewWorktreeDialog, LazyLinkedWorktreeItemDialog) with onLoadError. On failure it closes the surface and calls notifyChatSurfaceLoadFailure (chat/chatViewLazySurfaces.ts:72), which shows a toast with Retry. The sidebar is inconsistent with this.
  • apps/web/src/components/worktrees/lazyWorktreeDialogs.ts:6 Its comment says the wrappers are shared by 'the chat's toolbar and header, the sidebar' and that 'a preload from any of them serves all'. Only BranchToolbar and ChatView import it.

  • scripts/perf/model.ts:276 Dist budget for the RootAppShell closure: 420 KiB gzip, with MARKDOWN_SOURCES forbidden (react-markdown, micromark, parse5 at :235). CI runs it at .github/workflows/_validation.yml:213.
  • apps/web/dist/assets/RootAppShell-DOCTs5qH.js Read-only walk of static imports in the existing dist: 103 chunks. None are markdown-stack, CommentThread, LinkedWorktreeItemDialog, NewWorktreeDialog or JetBrains chunks, and 0 of 28 JetBrainsIcons SVG paths are present. Those names appear only in __vite__mapDeps preload lists. Beyond boot (main closure): 1,198 KiB raw / 406 KiB gzip.
Defects in the shipped fix

1) Reliability regression, low probability. The sidebar's lazy LinkedWorktreeItemDialog (SidebarWorktreeList.tsx:141) and NewWorktreeDialog (SidebarProjectDialogOwner.tsx:82) pass no onLoadError to useLazyComponentReady. If the chunk fails to load (offline or flaky hosted link, or a server/node update replacing hashed chunks while a tab is open), the mount throws into RootRouteErrorView (__root.tsx:435), and clicking a PR/issue badge or 'New workspace' replaces the whole app with 'Something went wrong'. Before #710 these dialogs were static, so this could not happen. ChatView handles the same dialogs with a toast and Retry (ChatView.tsx:5355-5385). The linked-item chunk now carries the markdown stack, so it is one of the larger on-demand downloads. 2) Maintainability. The sidebar defines its own preloadableLazy wrappers (SidebarWorktreeList.tsx:253, SidebarProjectDialogOwner.tsx:25) instead of the shared worktrees/lazyWorktreeDialogs.ts, whose comment wrongly says the sidebar shares it. The result is two module states per dialog: a sidebar preload does not mark ChatView's wrapper as loaded, which costs an extra commit with no extra network. webBundleSplitting.test.ts:202 locks this duplication in. 3) Minor guard imprecision. The guard is titled 'editor icons out of the app shell', but editor-only logos from Icons.tsx still ship in the shell's Icons chunk, about 14 KB of source.

Implementation sketch

(a) Export preloadLinkedWorktreeItemDialog() and preloadNewWorktreeDialog() from apps/web/src/components/worktrees/lazyWorktreeDialogs.ts. Delete the local preloadableLazy definitions in SidebarWorktreeList.tsx (:253-259) and SidebarProjectDialogOwner.tsx (:25-31), and import LazyLinkedWorktreeItemDialog and LazyNewWorktreeDialog plus the preload helpers instead. Keep the re-export of preloadNewWorktreeDialog for SidebarProjectItem.tsx:492, or import it from the shared module. (b) Move notifyChatSurfaceLoadFailure from chat/chatViewLazySurfaces.ts:72 into a neutral module, e.g. lib/lazySurfaceLoadFailure.ts (toast plus Retry, optional threadRef). ChatView and the sidebar then share it, and the sidebar does not import a chat module. (c) Pass onLoadError in the sidebar. For the linked item: capture the context, call setLinkedItemContext(null) and setLinkedItemDialogWanted(false) (the hook clears its parked failure when wanted turns false), then notify with a Retry that restores the context. For NewWorktreeDialog: capture the target, call setNewWorktreeOpen(false) and setNewWorktreeTarget(null), then notify with a Retry that calls openNewWorktree(target.project, target.initialTab). (d) Tests: update webBundleSplitting.test.ts:202 to assert that the sidebar imports from worktrees/lazyWorktreeDialogs and passes onLoadError. Add a vitest browser test: mock lazyWorktreeDialogs with a loader that rejects once, click the badge, and assert that a toast appears, RootRouteErrorView does not render, and Retry mounts the dialog. Run standardBootGraph.test.ts and the bundle splitting tests to confirm the shell graph is unchanged. (e) Optional, low value: move the editor-only logos (Trae, Kiro, VisualStudioCode, Insiders, VSCodium, Zed, Antigravity) out of Icons.tsx into an EditorLogos.tsx that only SettingsPanels.editor imports. Optionally mount WorkspacePullRequestsPopover lazily, the first time its toggle opens, with preload on badge intent. Then confirm with bun run perf:bundle-budget that the RootAppShell gzip drops.

Partial#61 modulePreload disabled: CSS→main serialization, 4-level module discovery per phase, 93 sub-2 KiB requests

web-bootstrap:modulepreload-and-tiny-chunks · original impact Medium, effort S · Waterfall WP13

Current state

PARTIAL holds. Preloading is fully fixed. Dynamic imports now preload their whole static closure: the boot chunk's import of RootAppShell carries 102 deps and ChatThreadRouteView carries 146, which equal their closures. index.html also hints boot, rolldown-runtime, boot-vendor, main and main.css, so the CSS-before-main gap and per-phase level discovery are gone. Proposal part 2 (merging tiny chunks) is done only for the boot graph and for vendor, icon, lexical, markdown and Shiki groups. Application modules outside boot still use automatic chunking. In a fresh standard build (dist from today 21:45), the static closure of index, main, RootAppShell and ChatThreadRouteView is 173 JS files: 61 under 2 KiB, 43 under 1 KiB, 140 under 12 KiB. The finding counted 176 files with 90 under 2 KiB, and its target is under 60. The total request count to the composer has therefore barely moved, even though boot shrank from about 75 files to 5. #710 moved code out of the boot graph into the lazy phases, which now add 168 files (it was about 100). Part 3 (re-measure) was never recorded, and no test enforces a request budget.

Evidence
  • apps/web/vite.config.ts:214-217 modulePreload is { polyfill: false, resolveDependencies: resolveWebModulePreloadDependencies }. The finding's modulePreload:false is gone.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/modulePreload.ts:22-28 hostType 'js' returns all deps and the HTML host returns []. The built boot-D36cWeP2.js imports RootAppShell with a 102-entry __vite__mapDeps list and ChatThreadRouteView with 146; my static-closure walk gives 103 and 147 files, the extra one being the chunk itself. The proposal's per-phase closure preload is in place.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/modulePreload.ts:38-83 bootPreloadTags and createBootPreloadPlugin add the boot hints. dist/index.html:28-32 has modulepreload for boot, rolldown-runtime, boot-vendor and main, plus rel=preload as=style for main-*.css. The CSS-to-main serialization and the 4-level main-phase discovery are removed, and later phases are not preloaded at document start, which avoids the contention the finding observed.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/codeSplitting.ts:33-37 This comment says app modules outside the boot graph keep automatic chunking because of possible top-level side effects. That is the root cause of the remaining tiny chunks. The auditor cited :27-31 for it.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/codeSplitting.ts:39,289-293,295-318 The 12 KiB entriesAware threshold applies only to the icons, vendor, lexical, markdown-stack and shiki-engine groups, which all match node_modules paths. No group captures app modules except boot and boot-vendor (priorities 10 and 11).
  • apps/web/dist/assets (static-closure walk of today's build, read-only) index+main+RootAppShell+ChatThreadRouteView: 173 files, 4,164 KiB raw. Sizes: 61 under 2 KiB, 33 at 2-4 KiB, 30 at 4-8 KiB, 16 at 8-12 KiB, 20 at 12-32 KiB, 13 larger. RootAppShell adds 100 files (29 under 2 KiB) and ChatThread adds 68 (29 under 2 KiB). The DraftChatThreadRouteView path is 171 files with 59 under 2 KiB. All tiny chunks are app modules: useMediaQuery, kbd, label, switch, textarea, spinner, formatCount, sidebarStatusText, workItemState, pathEntry, providerCapabilities (93 B), threadLinkActivity (84 B) and others.
  • apps/web/dist/assets (chunks over 400 KiB on the composer path) boot is 874 KiB, boot-vendor 691 KiB and ChatRightPanel 637 KiB. The finding's guardrail was 'no new chunk >400 KiB'. boot and boot-vendor are both new chunks over that line; the auditor mentioned only boot. Both are deliberate (codeSplitting.ts:299-311). ChatRightPanel is a separate finding.
  • apps/server/src (git grep node:http2|createSecureServer: no hits) The standard server still serves HTTP/1.1, so the roughly 168 lazy-phase requests still queue on Chromium's 6-connection pool for LAN, Tailscale and saved-environment clients. That is the user-visible cost that remains.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/buildPlugins.test.ts:113-307 Tests cover the group matchers and preload resolver only. No test or CI budget checks the number of JS files or tiny chunks on the composer path.
  • git show -s 3ce80cee6 / 60633eff3 3ce80cee6 records hosted sign-in timings and precache counts. 60633eff3 records cold load to composer as 795 to 310 ms and 6.1 to 1.5 MB. Neither records the composer-path request count or a re-run of graph/depth (part 3).
Remaining

Part 2 for app code and part 3 are missing. Under 2 KiB, 61 app-module chunks remain, and 140 of the 173 JS files on the cold path to the composer are under 12 KiB (index → boot → RootAppShell → ChatThreadRouteView). Total requests are about 173 (171 via DraftChatThreadRouteView), against the target of under 60. apps/web/src/viteBuild/codeSplitting.ts:295-318 has no group for application modules outside the boot graph; the comment at :33-37 explains why. Merging only the sub-2 KiB chunks would leave about 112 requests. Reaching under 60 means folding most of the sub-12 KiB app subgroups too. No measurement or regression budget exists for this.

Defects in the shipped fix

None found in the preload fix. The resolver matches each import's real closure (102/146 deps against closures of 103/147 files). The HTML host gets [], and hints come from the real bundle graph with matching crossorigin mode. Preloading the full closure of every dynamic import, including idle-preloaded surfaces, is Vite's default behaviour and fires only when that import starts.

Implementation sketch

1) apps/web/src/viteBuild/codeSplitting.ts: add a group after shiki-engine (priority 0), for example { name: 'app-shared', test: isMergeableAppModule, minShareCount: 2, entriesAware: true, entriesAwareMergeThreshold: CODE_SPLITTING_MERGE_THRESHOLD_BYTES, or 24-32 KiB if needed to get under 60 }. isMergeableAppModule should reject: \0 and ?query ids; node_modules; non-js/ts files; workers; Mermaid modules; Shiki grammar, theme and WASM entries; and boot-graph modules, which boot already captures at higher priority. Add 'app-shared' to MERGED_CHUNK_GROUP_NAMES (:257-265) so filenames stay short. 2) Side-effect safety is the real design question, because the merge threshold folds a module into a chunk that other entry sets also load and evaluate. Option (a), the conservative one: gate the test on a vetted allowlist of side-effect-free paths (components/ui/*, hooks/use*.ts, *.logic.ts, *Presentation.ts, pure lib/ helpers). Add a build-time assertion in a small plugin that fails if a captured module's code contains top-level statements other than import, export, const/let/function/class declarations, or calls to an allowlisted pure helper. Option (b): declare apps/web/package.json "sideEffects" as an explicit list of the side-effecting files and CSS, then gate the group on ctx.getModuleInfo(id).moduleSideEffects === false (ChunkingContext exposes ModuleInfo). This changes tree-shaking, so audit it first. Option (c): rolldown 1.2.7 output.strictExecutionOrder:true, which wraps module bodies so they run only when imported, regardless of chunk placement. This removes the hazard but grows every chunk with init wrappers, including boot. The cheaper experimental.onDemandWrapping is marked hidden/not ready, so use (c) only with measurements. 3) Add a regression budget to buildPlugins.test.ts or a post-build script reusing viteBuild/bundleGraph.ts. Walk the static closure of index → main → RootAppShell → ChatThreadRouteView and DraftChatThreadRouteView, and assert JS file count < 60 (or a calibrated ceiling) and sub-2 KiB count <= ~5. Also check that no chunk other than boot, boot-vendor and ChatRightPanel exceeds 400 KiB. 4) Re-measure cold load to the composer on the throttled HTTP/1.1 profile (40 ms RTT, 20 Mbit), and on loopback to confirm no regression from extra bytes evaluated per phase.

Done#62 Every client boot/reconnect opens a device WebSocket and makes the server spawn ~4-5 Xcode/simctl processes

web-bootstrap:eager-device-socket-and-simctl · original impact Medium, effort S · Process spawns

Current state

I confirm the fix. On a current server, a client boot or reconnect no longer lists devices and no longer opens /ws/device, and the server spawns no Xcode or simctl process on connect. Connections only register their device client. The device event stream starts once a thread view or the simulator pane holds the device runtime (ensureDeviceRuntime, released 60 s after the last holder lets go), and it runs over the main /ws socket, which now serves the device RPCs. Subscribing only adds a manager.onEvent listener. The only inventory read left is SimulatorPanel's refresh, and the pane mounts only while the simulator tab is active. That read is cheaper too: xcode-select and xcodebuild results are cached and shared, and a 2 s reuse window gives one simctl list per read instead of two. No other client or server path runs simctl, xcode-select or xcodebuild on connect.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:323-326 The connection only calls registerDeviceConnection. reconnect() at :360-370 only calls deviceBinding?.reconnecting() and lists nothing.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/device/runtime.ts:22-62 bindDeviceConnection subscribes to events only. It has no list or refreshInventory call.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/device/runtime.ts:112-182 registerDeviceConnection binds only while something retains the runtime. ensureDeviceRuntime is ref-counted and unbinds after DEVICE_RUNTIME_IDLE_MS = 60 s.
  • apps/web/src/components/device/useDeviceRuntime.ts:11-16 This hook holds the runtime. Its only callers are SimulatorPanel.tsx:166, ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:128 and DraftChatThreadRouteView.tsx:95.
  • apps/web/src/components/device/SimulatorPanel.tsx:209-224 The only client inventory read is a parallel list() + getThreadState(), run on mount or when the generation changes. ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:1536-1538 mounts the pane only when activeMode === 'simulator'.
  • apps/web/src/lib/devicePromptContext.ts:83-90 Its getThreadState call runs only when a prompt looks like a device task, never on connect.
  • apps/server/src/ws.ts:68-97 /ws serves WsHostedRpcGroup, the app group merged with the device group, using the device layer. /ws/device stays only for older clients.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/deviceRpcClient.ts:139-273 createDirectDeviceRpcTransport: RPCs and the event stream use the main socket. The dedicated socket opens only for requestBulk (screenshots) or after an 'Unknown request tag' answer, and closes after 60 s idle. A non-retryable stream failure, such as unsupported-platform on Linux, calls onError once and does not loop (wsTransport.ts:381-395).
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:988-1009, 1159-1180 The primary and saved-environment clients create DeviceWsTransport only inside the lazy openDedicated callback. The hosted path (:959) shares the relay transport.
  • apps/server/src/ws/deviceRpc.ts:122-135, 376-386 subscribeEvents only registers manager.onEvent and spawns nothing.
  • apps/server/src/device/IosSimulatorBackend.ts:83-90, 1055-1081 DEVICE_LISTING_REUSE_MS = 2 s, with one shared listing promise. boot re-reads with fresh:true (:518) and shutdown clears the cache (:537).
  • apps/server/src/device/IosSimulatorBackend.ts:1119-1180 xcode-select -p is cached for 60 s and xcodebuild -version for 5 min, as shared promises. A non-Xcode path or an unaccepted license is not kept.
Defects in the shipped fix

No blocking defect, and nothing brings back the per-connect cost. The auditor's three deviations are accurate: the stream starts on thread-view mount, the reuse window is 2 s rather than 30 s, and a failed listing is reused for 2 s. Two more small notes. (1) A reconnect bumps the device generation twice, once in deviceBinding.reconnecting() (connection.ts:362) and again on the stream's onResubscribe (runtime.ts:35-37). With the simulator pane open, that runs two list() + getThreadState() refreshes. The 2 s listing reuse and HostDeviceBackend single-flight usually merge them into one simctl run on the server. It costs nothing when the pane is closed. (2) The Android backend (AndroidEmulatorBackend.ts:211-341) has no listing cache. availability() is cached for only 5 s, and listDevices() re-runs emulator -list-avds, adb devices -l and two adb calls per running emulator. On hosts with the Android SDK, each pane refresh therefore spawns several adb/emulator processes. That code is unchanged since f1be4abc7 and runs only on pane open, never on connect.

Done#63 Bootstrap and ws-token fetches have no timeout: a request that is never answered hangs boot or WS reconnect forever (reliability)

web-bootstrap:bootstrap-fetch-timeouts · original impact Medium, effort S · Reliability

Current state

I checked this independently and the auditor's DONE holds. PR #710 (60633eff3) added fetchWithDeadline, a 5 s deadline that covers both headers and body. It races the fetch, so it still works when an adapter ignores the abort signal, and it avoids AbortSignal.timeout/any so it runs on React Native. All four boot and reconnect control-plane fetches now go through it: session, bootstrap exchange, descriptor and ws-token. The deadline error is named TimeoutError and counts as transient. issuePrimaryWebSocketToken is now wrapped in retryTransientBootstrap and honours the attempt signal. protocol.ts bounds the WS URL provider with Effect.timeoutOrElse (10 s), which interrupts the provider (its signal aborts) and fails with WsUrlProviderError, so the reconnect schedule keeps advancing. The web primary, device and saved-direct transports plus mobile all set it. Once the 15 s budget runs out, the root beforeLoad rejects into RootRouteErrorView, which offers Try again (invalidates the router and re-runs beforeLoad, with the cached promises cleared) and Reload. I looked for gaps the fix might have opened. One candidate: the desktop now loads the renderer at http-bound, and the server startup gate holds API requests for up to 10 s, so a slow runtime build of more than ~16 s fails the boot reads. The desktop covers this by reloading at ready any app load requested more than 9 s earlier, so it is not a regression. Device-frame URL resolution passes no signal, but its fetches go through the same deadline-plus-retry path, so it is bounded at about 16 s.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/fetchWithDeadline.ts:53 fetchWithDeadline: a manual timer plus a 'stopped' race covers headers (:89-92) and body (:97-103). Caller abort settles early (:79-85). Deadline error is named TimeoutError (:20-28). No TDZ, unhandled-rejection or leak issues found; a timer that outlives an unread non-ok body just aborts the finished request at 5 s.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.ts:118 retryTransientBootstrap treats TypeError, AbortError/TimeoutError and 502-504 as transient, with a 15 s budget (worst case ~16 s with 5 s attempts) and a caller-signal abandon check (:123, :131, :135).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.ts:139 fetchControlPlane uses fetchWithDeadline for fetchSessionState (:145), requestWebSocketToken (:156), exchangeBootstrapCredential (:202). issuePrimaryWebSocketToken (:192-201) is now retried and signal-aware. The boot prefetch (:303-307) has the same deadline.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryContext.ts:78 fetchDescriptor uses fetchWithDeadline inside retryTransientBootstrap.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/protocol.ts:294 withUrlProviderTimeout uses Effect.timeoutOrElse (Effect 4.0.2 interrupts the source, which aborts the tryPromise signal) and fails with WsUrlProviderError, which the retry at :351 retries. WS_URL_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000 at :143.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:984 The primary /ws transport sets urlProviderTimeoutMs, as do the dedicated device transport (:996) and saved direct environments (:1106; desktop-SSH deliberately excluded). apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:357 does the same.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:250 Boot awaits the descriptor and auth gate. A rejection reaches errorComponent RootRouteErrorView (:85, :435), whose Try again calls router.invalidate (:511-513). pendingReadyRootContext, bootstrapPromise and descriptorPromise are all cleared in finally, so a retry issues fresh requests.
  • apps/server/src/httpStartupGate.ts:26 The server gate holds API requests for up to 10 s (then 503 Retry-After). The client's 5 s deadline plus retry cycles through it, and the 503 counts as transient.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendAppWindowLoad.ts:30 EARLY_APP_LOAD_MAX_HOLD_MS = 9_000: at ready, the desktop reloads a window whose early app load is older than 9 s and has not reported a usable shell. This covers a slow runtime build exceeding the ~16 s client budget, so the deadline does not strand the desktop on the error view (wired at apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1728-1757).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.test.ts:158 Tests: a hung ws-token is retried (:158), an abandoned attempt stops retrying (:173), the session read is bounded (:190). fetchWithDeadline.test.ts:34-118 covers deadline, body, success, ignored-abort and caller-cancel. wsTransport.test.ts:335-352 checks that the URL-provider timeout aborts the first signal and starts a fresh attempt.
Defects in the shipped fix

None verified. Out-of-scope observations only: (1) the generic get/post/getHubOrNull helpers (primaryAuth.ts:256-293) still call httpClient.fetch with no deadline. They serve user-initiated settings and Hub panels, not boot or reconnect. Their doc comment at :279-281 (pre-existing since 7a1f42bf5) wrongly says they inherit the transient-bootstrap retry. (2) Device-frame URL resolution (service.ts:1005) passes no signal, but it stays bounded at ~16 s by the deadline plus retry. (3) During an outage, each 10 s URL-provider window now polls ws-token every 500 ms, instead of once per backoff step. These requests are tiny and the change is harmless.

Partial#65 Shell code, WebSocket handshake and thread-route code load strictly one after another

web-bootstrap:serial-shell-ws-thread-phases · original impact Medium, effort M · Waterfall WP12B

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. Auditor's DONE overstates it. The early connection does not carry the welcome or config subscriptions; they still start after shell commit from ServerStateBootstrap. So on the '/' redirect path the thread chunk, thread prewarm and redirect start at commit + 1 RTT, and the auditor's suggested fix (observe the early connection's welcome) would need the lifecycle subscription moved first. The path is also narrower than implied: bootstrap redirects only happen for non-headless web-mode servers (autoBootstrapProjectFromCwd), not desktop or headless nodes.

Current state

Proposals (a) to (d) are in the code. The shell chunk and deep-linked page chunks preload alongside auth. The ws-token is prefetched with the session check. The primary socket and its shell subscription open from beforeLoad. Only one ws-token is issued at boot. Welcome-time and idle thread-chunk preloads exist, and defaultPreload is 'intent'. Most of the described cost is gone. One gap remains that the auditor described wrongly. The early connection carries only the shell subscription. The lifecycle (welcome) and config subscriptions are still opened by ServerStateBootstrap's passive effect after the shell commits, because the primary connection has no onWelcome/onConfigUpdated. On the measured '/' bootstrap-redirect path, the welcome-driven thread-chunk preload, the thread-detail prewarm and the redirect all start at shell commit plus one WS round trip. They do not overlap the shell download, so the intent of (b)+(c) is only half met. The auditor's idea of observing the early connection's welcome from beforeLoad cannot work, because no welcome is requested early. This path exists only in web mode: the server sends bootstrapThreadId only when autoBootstrapProjectFromCwd is set, which defaults to true only for non-headless web mode. Desktop and headless nodes land on the index and rely on idle or intent preloads. The low fetch-priority part of (c) was not done, but it hardly matters now. Remaining value is small: about one RTT plus shell eval and commit on slow links, tens of ms locally.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:163 (a) Shell (or HostedHubRoot) preload plus preloadMatchedRouteChunks(pathname) start before the auth fetches. Awaited after auth through withRootSurfaceLoaded (127-137). /pair and native authorize are skipped.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:249 (b) prefetchPrimaryWebSocketToken runs with the session check. It is discarded at 258 when not authenticated. startPrimaryConnectionEarly() runs at 254-255. Hosted-hub (195-202) and hosted-static (214-223) return before this, consistent with AGENTS.md.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:342 startPrimaryConnectionEarly only calls connectPrimaryEnvironment(). It does not start server-state sync, so welcome and config are not requested early.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:178 shouldObserveLifecycle/shouldObserveConfig are true only for saved connections or when onWelcome/onConfigUpdated are passed. Primary connections pass neither (service.ts createEnvironmentConnectionHandlers), so the early socket carries only subscribeShell.
  • apps/web/src/components/ServerStateBootstrap.tsx:22 startServerStateSync (client-runtime rpc/serverState.ts:162-176: subscribeLifecycle + subscribeConfig) is called only from this passive effect. It mounts inside RootAppShell (RootAppShell.tsx:90), so after the shell chunk loads and commits.
  • apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:286 (c) The welcome handler calls preloadRouteChunk(THREAD_ROUTE_ID) and prewarmThreadDetailSubscription before ensureEnvironmentConnectionBootstrapped. Because welcome arrives only after ServerStateBootstrap subscribes, this runs at shell commit + 1 WS RTT. The redirect navigate (324) is gated the same way.
  • apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:175 (c) ShellIdlePreloads warms the thread and draft chunks after primary-shell-painted plus idle. lib/shellIdlePreload.ts:15-23 skips data-saver and non-4g links, so on slow profiles only the welcome path warms the thread chunk on '/'.
  • apps/web/src/router.ts:15 (d) defaultPreload 'intent', defaultPreloadDelay 50. The thread route uses lazyRouteComponent (_chat.$environmentId.$threadId.tsx:33). Sidebar rows also warm through threadNavigationIntent.ts.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.ts:179 The prefetched token is taken once (60 s max age). A failed prefetch yields null and the socket requests again. Covered by primaryAuth.test.ts:205-280.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/deviceRpcClient.ts:175 The dedicated /ws/device socket and its ws-token open only on demand (acquireDedicated), so boot issues one ws-token (65af92766).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:894 connectPrimary returns the existing connection and disposes a duplicate candidate. start() (1218-1265) reuses the early connection, so ownership stays safe.
  • apps/server/src/cli.ts:639 autoBootstrapProjectFromCwd defaults to mode === 'web' (false when headless). serverRuntimeStartup.ts:413 sets bootstrapThreadId only under that flag, and RootAppShell.logic.ts:24 redirects only on '/' outside the phone tier. The residual applies only to web-mode CLI boots.
Remaining

In standard web mode on '/', with a server bootstrapThreadId and outside the phone tier, the welcome and config subscriptions start only in ServerStateBootstrap's passive effect (apps/web/src/components/ServerStateBootstrap.tsx:22-25 -> packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/serverState.ts:162-176), after the shell chunk loads and commits. The early primary connection (apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:342-348) does not subscribe to them (connection.ts:178-179). As a result, the welcome-driven thread-route chunk preload and thread-detail prewarm (RootAppShell.tsx:284-288) and the bootstrap redirect (RootAppShell.tsx:324) start at shell commit + one WS RTT instead of overlapping the shell download. The ~100 KB config snapshot is also serialized behind the commit. The proposal (c) low-fetch-priority sub-item was not done, but it is moot because the remaining preloads already run after the shell. Adjacent and outside this finding's primary scope: saved-environment connections also start only from start() after shell commit (supervision.ts:1235-1242), so deep links into a saved environment's thread still put their connect chain behind the shell.

Defects in the shipped fix

No bugs found in the implemented parts. Minor: connectsEarly (__root.tsx:245) also prefetches a ws-token on /pair and on every unauthenticated boot. That is a guaranteed 401 POST, harmless because the route has no rate limit (apps/server/src/auth/http.ts:181-193). The auditor said the '/' thread chunk 'starts at shell commit' and proposed 'observing the early connection's welcome from beforeLoad'. In fact it starts at commit + ServerStateBootstrap effect + one lifecycle RTT, and the early connection never requests welcome, so that idea needs the lifecycle subscription moved first.

Implementation sketch

1) packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/serverState.ts: make startServerStateSync reference-counted per client, e.g. retainServerStateSync(client). The first retain opens subscribeLifecycle + subscribeConfig and the last release closes them, so two holders never open duplicate streams. ServerStateBootstrap.tsx uses the retain unchanged. 2) apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx startPrimaryConnectionEarly: after connectPrimaryEnvironment() returns a connection, take a retain on connection.client.server (standard mode only, already guaranteed by the call site). Release it once ServerStateBootstrap has taken its own, or after a bounded timeout if the shell never mounts. 3) In the same early path, register a one-shot onWelcome (serverState.ts:138). If location is '/', shouldApplyBootstrapThreadRedirect({pathname:'/', tier:getPresentationTier(), hostedHome:false}) holds and payload.bootstrapThreadId is set, call RootAppShell.preload().then(() => preloadRouteChunk('/_chat/$environmentId/$threadId')) and prewarmThreadDetailSubscription(environmentId, bootstrapThreadId). Sequencing after the shell module avoids taking bandwidth from the shell graph, and the prewarm is idempotent and deadline-bounded. EventRouter stays the sole owner of the navigate. 4) Tests: serverState unit tests (two retains -> one lifecycle/config subscription; last release unsubscribes). A root/early-boot unit test (welcome with bootstrapThreadId on '/' triggers the chunk preload and prewarm once; not on deep links, phone tier, hosted-hub or hosted-static). Run the existing ServerStateBootstrap.browser.tsx. Confirm with the startup perf harness on a throttled web-mode profile that the thread chunk request and welcome precede root-shell-module-ready + commit, and that the 'usable' timing does not regress.

Done#67 No workspace package declares sideEffects, so barrels (@ryco/contracts, client-runtime) keep every re-exported module

web-bootstrap:workspace-packages-sideeffects · original impact Low, effort S · Build config

Current state

Confirmed DONE. #710 (60633eff3) added "sideEffects": false to all three workspace packages the web app imports: contracts, shared and client-runtime. The Hub-vendored Ryco (7bc39eec3) has it too. Those packages resolve through node_modules symlinks and package exports (the web tsconfig maps only ~/*), so rolldown applies the flag. The current dist (built 21:45, after HEAD ec250e386) shows it pruning. The contracts hostedIdentity/nativeE2ee schemas are only in the lazy hosted api-*.js chunk, not in boot, and the contracts computerAudit module is gone from every chunk. I parsed all 409 non-test modules of the three packages with @babel/parser. I found no side-effect-only imports. I found no module-scope global writes, listener or service-worker registrations, Effect.run* calls, subscriptions or polyfills, so a blanket false is safe. The only top-level statements with effects are a constant-consistency throw guard (relayE2eeInitiator.ts:285), Object.freeze on module-local constants (draftStore.ts:464-467) and static assignments on a local class (qrCode.ts:984-985). As the earlier verifier noted, the boot-time schema cost is a different finding: rpc.ts still statically reaches 48 of 70 contracts modules through wsTransport, which is still in the boot chunk (the storage.scan tag is in boot-*.js).

Partial#68 Hosted Hub boot: three sequential dynamic imports, then 2 Hub RTTs, then the 1.8 MiB HostedHubRoot download, then the reveal throttle

web-bootstrap:hosted-hub-boot-waterfall · original impact Low, effort S · Waterfall WP12B

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor says the boot now waits one Hub RTT instead of two. That holds only for authenticated boots. Signed-out and expired-session boots still wait for the session 401 and then bootstrap-status (state.ts:776-788). The auditor says the HostedHubRoot download overlaps the access check. That is true, but the RootAppShell graph, which the finding counted inside the 1.8 MiB, was split out and starts only after the account answer (bootGate.ts:45-53), contrary to the gate's own comment. Brotli is not unverified: Hub origin/main precompresses brotli q11 and negotiates br (5dc12a4); only deployment is unknown.

Current state

Most of the finding is fixed. The hosted gate's state and read-cache modules are now static, so the logging chunk round trip is gone. HostedHubRoot starts loading when the root beforeLoad begins. An authenticated boot waits only for the account answer, with the directory read sent alongside it. Both hosted surfaces are preloadableLazy and are loaded before commit, so the reveal throttle no longer applies. Brotli is also done on the Hub side. Two serializations remain in the same gate. (1) The workspace shell is the RootAppShell graph. In the current standard dist it is about 343 KiB gz of the roughly 475 KiB gz that the finding counted as the HostedHubRoot closure. It still starts loading only after the account answer, although the gate comment says otherwise. (2) Signed-out and expired-session boots still wait for two sequential Hub requests: the session 401, then bootstrap-status. Each costs up to one Hub RTT, so the remaining worth is low.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/bootGate.ts:1-2 Confirmed: readCache and state are static imports. The root imports the gate statically (__root.tsx:21), and standard builds resolve it to the inert sibling (clientModeSeams.ts:29-37). webBundleSplitting.test.ts:77-96 pins this.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:163 Confirmed: HostedHubRoot.preload() starts at the beginning of beforeLoad, and :199 hands the same promise to the gate. HostedHubRoot is a preloadableLazy (:41-43), and withRootSurfaceLoaded (:127-137) holds the context until it is loaded.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:749-773 Confirmed for authenticated boots: restoreSession and the directory prefetch go out together. accessSettled at :772 releases bootstrapAccess (:659-662) before the directory commit.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:776-788 Not fixed for signed-out or expired sessions. On a 401, getBootstrapAvailability (:784) is sent only after the session answer, and accessSettled is never called on this path. bootstrapAccess therefore settles through bootstrap()'s finally (:628-633) after the second Hub request. The code at f1be4abc7 was the same. The sign-in surface still waits two sequential Hub RTTs.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/bootGate.ts:23-31 The comment says the workspace shell downloads while the access check is on the wire. Only the small hostedRootAppShell wrapper module is imported there. LazyRootAppShell's import (hostedRootAppShell.tsx:15-17, :28-30) runs from :52, after the await at :45, and only when the account is authenticated or a read preview is possible.
  • apps/web/dist/assets (standard build of HEAD, read-only closure walk) HostedHubRoot beyond boot: 28 files, 132 KiB gz. RootAppShell adds 83 files, 1,025 KiB raw and 343 KiB gz beyond boot plus HostedHubRoot. For thread deep links, prefetchHostedRouteCode (hostedWorkspaceOwners.ts:69-72) covers all but 22 files (151 KiB gz) of that. For a '/' landing nothing prefetches it before the account answer.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/readCache.ts:56-62 The read cache is opt-in (default false). Most returning users therefore wait on the network side of the race at :624-674, not on the local restore.
  • apps/web/src/pwa/buildArtifacts.ts:331-350 The service worker serves the boot document and fingerprinted chunks cache-first. For installed returning users, the shell residual is the service-worker fetch plus evaluation of about 1 MiB of raw JS after the access check. A full network download only happens without a service worker.
  • ryco-hub:scripts/build-static-manifest.ts:57-131 Hub origin/main (5dc12a4) precompresses JS and CSS with brotli q11 and gzip. src/http/staticAssets.ts:119ff negotiates br, then gzip (docs/coolify-deployment.md:297-304). The brotli part of the proposal is implemented in code. Whether it is deployed is unknown.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/modulePreload.ts:15-20 Leaving HostedHubRoot out of the index.html modulepreload list is deliberate: earlier preloads caused measured contention. Accepted as not needed.
Remaining

(1) For a cold authenticated boot that lands on '/' with no read cache, the RootAppShell graph is loaded only after the account answer. It is about 343 KiB gz, or about 1 MiB raw JS to fetch from the service worker and evaluate. The load starts at apps/web/src/hostedHub/bootGate.ts:46-53, after the await at :45, so it does not overlap the session request. The cost is up to one Hub RTT, or the shell's fetch and evaluation time if that is shorter. (2) For a signed-out or expired-session boot, the gate waits for GET /api/auth/session (401) and then GET /api/auth/bootstrap-status, at packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:776-788. This adds one Hub RTT to the sign-in surface. That matters most for returning signed-out visitors whose chunks are already cached by the service worker. Optional and not needed: adding HostedHubRoot to the index.html modulepreload list (rejected on measured contention).

Defects in the shipped fix

Documentation defect only. apps/web/src/hostedHub/bootGate.ts:23-27 says the workspace shell downloads while the access check is on the wire. Only the hostedRootAppShell wrapper module is imported there, and the RootAppShell import starts at :52 after the account answer. No functional bugs found. Prefetch failures are swallowed and then reported again by the route's own preload or render. The workspace owners only call into the single hostedHubController. The read-cache race still holds bootstrapPending correctly now that the network leg settles at the account answer.

Implementation sketch

(1) Shell overlap for likely-authenticated boots. Add a non-secret localStorage boolean hint, for example 'ryco:hosted-signed-in:v1'. Set it from a hostedHubStore subscription when accountStatus becomes 'authenticated'. Clear it on 'signing-out', 'session-expired', or a published 'signed-out'. Extract the existing subscription in readCache.ts:630-652 or add a small hostedHub/bootHints.ts. In runHostedBootGate, when the hint is set or a remembered read-cache account exists, call hostedRootAppShell.then(s => s?.preloadHostedRootAppShell()) before the await at :45. Keep the call after the check for boots without the hint, so first-time visitors still never fetch the shell on the sign-in path. Correct the comment at :23-27. Tests: a vitest for bootGate.ts with the dynamic imports and hostedHubController.bootstrapAccess mocked. Assert that with the hint the shell preload starts before bootstrapAccess resolves, and that without the hint it starts only after an authenticated answer. Check the root-before-load-ready mark on a hosted build at 150 ms RTT. (2) Signed-out RTT. In packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts #restoreAccess, start the bootstrap-status read next to restoreSession in cookie mode, the same way #prefetchDirectory works: hold getBootstrapAvailability(operation.signal) as a promise with a catch that returns null. On isSessionFailure, use the held answer, and fall back to a fresh read when it is null. On success, ignore it. Bearer mode keeps the sequential read to avoid an extra DPoP mint on native. Tests in state.test.ts: a signed-out cookie boot sends both requests concurrently and bootstrapAccess settles without a second sequential request; an authenticated boot publishes the same state as today; an aborted operation publishes nothing. Cost: one extra public, in-memory GET per cookie-mode boot (Hub rate limit is 60 per minute per IP, authRoutes.ts:535-538).

Value low · effort S · risk low
