  • apps/web/src/components (static scan) Every class defined in the moved sheets is used only inside its feature directory. RollingText's base rules stay in index.css:3017+, and only the crown overrides moved. No @keyframes name or selector duplicates index.css, and the moved files have no @apply, @layer or @reference, so changing cascade order and processing them separately is safe.
  • apps/web/dist/index.html Modulepreload hints for boot, rolldown-runtime, boot-vendor and main JS, a style preload for main CSS, and a font preload for dm-sans-latin-wght-normal-Xz1IZZA0.woff2 with crossorigin. The woff2 matches the URL in main CSS. Main JS no longer waits for the CSS download.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/bootFontPreload.ts:32-60 createBootFontPreloadPlugin injects the hashed font preload through transformIndexHtml post.
  • apps/web/vite.config.ts:129-134 The font preload is registered only when resolvedClientMode === 'standard'. The comment justifies this with 'the Hub surface has its own typography'.
  • apps/web/src/viteConfig.test.ts:126-134 The test pins that hosted-hub builds do NOT get ryco-boot-font-preload.
  • apps/web/src/index.css:506-507 --font-family-sans defaults to "DM Sans", and body uses it at index.css:722-723. No :root[data-surface="hub"] rule overrides the font. Hub components (components/hostedHub/**) set no custom font family.
  • apps/web/index.html:34-43 The boot <style> in the shared index.html sets body font-family to "DM Sans" in hosted builds too.
Remaining

Hosted-hub builds have no DM Sans preload: vite.config.ts:132-134 registers createBootFontPreloadPlugin only for standard builds, and viteConfig.test.ts:133 pins that. The hosted index.html (app.ryco.space) therefore finds DM Sans only when the shell commits text, and cold loads such as a first visit or a new browser get the post-paint font swap the finding describes. Warm hosted loads are largely covered by the service-worker precache of the font (buildArtifacts.ts:395-400), which serves it from Cache Storage within milliseconds. Also minor: in all builds the preload is unconditional, so users who picked another sans face (Geist, Inter and so on) download 36 KiB of DM Sans for nothing.

Defects in the shipped fix

The CSS move and the CSS/JS waterfall have no functional defects. The defect is in the font preload: the comment at vite.config.ts:129-131 says the Hub surface has its own typography, but the hosted surface renders in DM Sans (index.css:506, index.html:34-43, buildArtifacts.ts:144), so the hosted build was wrongly excluded and a test (viteConfig.test.ts:133) locks the exclusion in.

Implementation sketch

1) apps/web/vite.config.ts:127-134: register createBootFontPreloadPlugin() for both client modes and keep only createPrecompressedAssetsPlugin() behind resolvedClientMode === 'standard'. Rewrite the comment (CDN compression is still a valid reason for the precompressed plugin, but not for the font). 2) apps/web/src/viteConfig.test.ts:126-134: expect ryco-boot-font-preload in pluginNames('hosted-hub') too. 3) Check that the hosted index.html transform in pwa/buildArtifacts.ts (inline-script hashing, boot document, offline.html) accepts an extra <link> tag; 3ce80cee6 already adds modulepreload and style-preload links to hosted builds. Check that the preload href (config.base + fileName) equals the precached bootDocumentAssets URL (pathAtBase(publicBase, fileName)), so the service worker serves both from one cache entry. Optionally add the same preload to renderHostedPwaOfflineDocument. 4) Validate: build hosted mode into a scratch worktree (VITE_RYCO_CLIENT_MODE=hosted-hub bun run --cwd apps/web build) and assert dist/index.html carries <link rel=preload as=font type=font/woff2 crossorigin href=/assets/dm-sans-latin-wght-normal-*.woff2>. Re-run the 150 ms / 1.6 Mbps and 10 Mbps hosted sign-in profile from 3ce80cee6 (4.81 s / 1.33 s baselines) and confirm the DM Sans request now starts at document start, the sign-in text paints without a swap, and sign-in time does not regress from 36 KiB of high-priority bandwidth contention. 5) To reach users, a Hub vendor-pin bump and deploy. 6) Optional: emit the preload from the inline head script only when the persisted appearance preference is the default sans face, so non-default users don't pay 36 KiB.

Needs a decision

Including the hosted build reverses a deliberate, test-pinned exclusion. It changes the hosted index.html that app.ryco.space serves, so it only reaches users through a Hub vendor-pin bump and deploy. It also trades about 36 KiB of early high-priority bandwidth against the boot chain on slow links, where the hosted team has measured sign-in carefully. That trade-off should be confirmed with the slow-link profile before shipping.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Done#70 Sidebar auto-animate and FLIP hooks measure layout during initial population at boot

web-bootstrap:boot-list-animation-measurement · original impact Low, effort S · CPU

Current state

Confirmed DONE (60633eff3, #710). Sidebar project/thread/worktree/chat lists and the inbox no longer observe or measure while they populate at boot. useSidebarListMotionReady keeps motion off until some environment has a live snapshot (bootstrapComplete), then turns it on one rAF later and latches. Cache-hydrated rows (primary shell cache, desktop workspace cache, hosted read cache) also populate with motion off, because hydration leaves bootstrapComplete false. While disabled, attachSidebarAutoAnimateNode never calls autoAnimate(). That matters: in auto-animate 0.10 a disabled controller still calls getCoords() in add()/remain() before its isEnabled check, so creating controllers and disabling them would not have been enough. useInboxListMotion skips every layout read when enabled is false. Its ResizeObserver stays attached but does no row reads while signatureRef is null. When motion turns on, the first read uses duration 0, so nothing flashes in. useFlipLayout's trigger effect now has [ref, trigger] deps and returns early when the trigger is unchanged. Resting positions come from a ResizeObserver and MutationObserver set up once per element, and a browser test (useFlipLayout.browser.tsx) checks that commits which leave the row alone call no getBoundingClientRect. Residual nits only, none of which undo the fix: (1) the latch fires on ANY environment's first live snapshot, as the proposal specified, so a second environment's population can still be animated and measured. With the per-environment caches this is mostly limited to cache/live differences. (2) After latching, the hook still subscribes to selectAnyShellSnapshotApplied, so Sidebar re-renders whenever all environments demote and recover. (3) Turning motion on changes the ref-callback identity, so the memoized sidebar subtree re-renders once, one frame after first paint. This only happens when the list is under the thresholds. (4) The hook has no unit test. Separate pre-existing issue, not part of this finding: pruned auto-animate controllers are never destroy()ed (Sidebar.tsx:167-175), so the library's 2-second per-child poll timers and IntersectionObservers keep running for detached lists.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useSidebarListMotionReady.ts:6-47 Latch: true once any environment has bootstrapComplete, then setReady one requestAnimationFrame later (setTimeout fallback). Module-level motionReadyLatched keeps it on for the session.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:2144 bootstrapComplete is set to true only by the live shell snapshot apply path.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:3786-3806 hydrateEnvironmentStateFromCache leaves bootstrapComplete false, so rows from the primaryShellCache, desktopWorkspace and hosted readCache paths populate with motion off.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:1053-1071 shouldAnimateProjectLists and shouldAnimateThreadLists are gated by listMotionReady before shouldEnableAutoAnimate is applied.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:191-213 No autoAnimate() call while disabled, so no MutationObserver, ResizeObserver or per-child getCoords exists during population. The ref callbacks (1073-1081, 1106-1114) change identity with enabled, and the memoized children (SidebarProjectList:570, SidebarProjectThreadList:234, SidebarWorktreeList:174, SidebarChatList:163) use default shallow memo, so they re-attach.
  • node_modules/.bun/@formkit+auto-animate@0.10.0/node_modules/@formkit/auto-animate/index.mjs:498-505 add() and remain() call getCoords() before checking isEnabled, so a disabled controller would still measure on mutations. Not creating the controller is the right approach.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:1560 motionReady={listMotionReady} is passed to ConnectedInboxSidebar, which spreads its props into InboxSidebar (ConnectedInboxSidebar.tsx:97-98).
  • apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/InboxSidebar.tsx:215-225 motionEnabled = (props.motionReady ?? true) && shouldEnableAutoAnimate(...).
  • apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/useInboxListMotion.ts:179-186 When !input.enabled, the effect returns before getClientRects and offsetTop reads. When the inbox is first enabled, it reads with duration 0 because signatureRef is null, so nothing animates in.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/useFlipLayout.ts:26-69 Trigger effect deps are [ref, trigger] with an early return when Object.is says the trigger is unchanged. At f1be4abc7 it was dep-less and called recordResting on every commit.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/useFlipLayout.ts:74-81,91-116 Observers are set up once per element. Positions are recorded on DOM mutations and resizes of the row, not on every commit.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/useFlipLayout.browser.tsx:33-48 Browser test: five rerenders that leave the row untouched call getBoundingClientRect and getAnimations zero times.
Defects in the shipped fix

No real defect in the fix. Minor nits: (a) useSidebarListMotionReady.ts:23 keeps the store subscription after latching, so Sidebar re-renders whenever every environment's bootstrapComplete flips false and back (disconnect, then reconnect). That is a negligible extra render during a reconnect. (b) The latch uses ANY environment's first live snapshot, so later environments still populate with motion on. Every boot path hydrates all environments from cache first, so in practice this mostly limits measurement to cache/live differences. (c) Turning motion on changes the ref-callback identity, which re-renders the memoized sidebar subtree once. This is bounded by the thresholds and happens after first paint. (d) There is no unit or browser test for useSidebarListMotionReady or for the sidebar's 'no autoAnimate before ready' behaviour.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Partial#71 No route-level code splitting: every route module and its imports (stores, wsTransport, contracts) are fetched and evaluated before auth starts

web-bootstrap:route-modules-eager-boot-graph · original impact Low, effort M · Bundle size decision

Current state

PARTIAL is right. Since f1be4abc7 the route bodies have been split by hand with lazyRouteComponent (60633eff3/451f35925), PreviewFileNavigationGuard is lazy, and the boot graph shrank from ~2,023 KiB raw to ~1,566 KiB raw (boot 895 KB + boot-vendor 707 KB, ~478 KiB gzip). The cost the finding describes is still there: the root beforeLoad auth (/api/auth/session plus the descriptor) starts only after the whole boot chain has downloaded and evaluated, and that chain still holds the connection runtime, wsTransport and the stores. Three of the auditor's details are wrong. (1) The BOOT_ROOT_MODULES views do not evaluate lazily: the boot chunk scope-hoists them, so they run at boot. (2) The rpc barrel in main.tsx is not a real edge to wsTransport, because client-runtime is sideEffects:false. (3) The edge cuts alone shrink nothing while BOOT_ROOT_MODULES stays, because ChatIndexRouteView imports environments/runtime directly. Since #710 the shell chunk already downloads during auth, so the remaining gain is small. Worth: low.

Evidence
  • apps/web/vite.config.ts:108 tanstackRouter() still runs with defaults (no autoCodeSplitting). vite.config.ts:220-225 passes BOOT_ROOT_MODULES as boot roots.
  • apps/web/src/routes/_chat.tsx:15 Bodies are lazy via lazyRouteComponent in _chat, _chat.index (:15), thread (:33), draft, projects, pull-requests, statistics, diagnostics, native.authorize and settingsRoute.ts. The route files are thin, and webBundleSplitting.test.ts:12-180 guards them. These parts of the proposal are done without autoCodeSplitting.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:47 PreviewFileNavigationGuard is lazy. That proposal item is done.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:239 Auth still starts here: dynamic import of the primary module, then Promise.all(ensurePrimaryEnvironmentReady, resolveInitialServerAuthGateState) at :250-253. That happens only after main has evaluated, which needs boot and boot-vendor to have run. The #710 mitigations at :159-165 (shell and route chunk preload), :249 (ws-token prefetch) and :255 (early connect) overlap the work after auth, not the wait before it.
  • apps/web/index.html:128 The inline module script only marks the start and imports /src/main.tsx. There is no early session or descriptor fetch.
  • apps/web/src/lib/utils.ts:4 This is the dominant chain to the runtime. utils (imported by ui/button in __root, ui/input, and RycoLetterMark/AppBootLoadingSurface) imports composerDraftStore, which leads through composerDraftPersistence, composerFileUpload, platform/attachmentUpload, environments/runtime/index, service.ts, rpc/wsRpcClient and client-runtime rpc/wsRpcClient to wsTransport. This comes from a binding-aware static walk (oxc parseSync, client-mode seams applied).
  • apps/web/src/routes/_chat.$environmentId.$threadId.tsx:5 This is a second, independent path, new in 60633eff3. It goes through lib/threadDetailPrewarm.ts:3 to environments/runtime/service.
  • apps/web/src/components/auth/PairingRouteSurface.tsx:5 This is a third, independent path: eager pair.tsx:3-7 leads to addSavedEnvironment from environments/runtime (service plus catalog). environments/primary at :6-10 is lean now: its own closure is 16 files / 49 KB source with no wsTransport, so auth itself no longer needs the runtime.
  • apps/web/src/main.tsx:19 This is not a meaningful lever. packages/client-runtime/package.json:6 sets sideEffects:false, so the export * in apps/web/src/rpc/wsConnectionState.ts:13 bundles only client-runtime rpc/wsConnectionState. Cutting main.tsx:19/38 removes about 3 files / 15 KB source. The walk results: main closure at HEAD is 281 files / 2.55 MB source. Cutting any one or two of the three paths above leaves runtime and wsTransport in. Cutting all three leaves 91 files / 0.54 MB.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/codeSplitting.ts:277 BOOT_ROOT_MODULES (ChatLayoutRouteView, ChatIndexRouteView) join the boot group, because the walk queue includes the roots (:176). ChatIndexRouteView.tsx:10 imports environments/runtime directly. The main+roots closure is 342 files / 3.04 MB, and still 340 files / 3.04 MB after all three cuts. The edge cuts alone therefore change nothing in the boot chunk.
  • apps/web/dist/assets/boot-D36cWeP2.js The local build is from 21:45, after HEAD at 21:40. The roots evaluate at boot, not on first use: `var KCe=e({ChatLayoutRoute:()=>XCe})` is hoisted to the top level, and the route component is `Promise.resolve().then(()=>KCe)`. rolldown-runtime exports only __commonJS/__export/__toESM, and no lazy ESM init exists. Sizes: boot 894,988 B (261 KB gz), boot-vendor 707,326 B (229 KB gz), main 922 B. RootAppShell is 341,660 B and is fetched after boot.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/codeSplitting.ts:271 This comment and standardBootGraph.test.ts:170-172 claim the roots 'evaluate on first use', which is wrong given the dist. codeSplitting.ts:147 refers to a non-existent HOSTED_BOOT_ROOT_MODULES. The auditor repeated the 'evaluate lazily' claim.
Remaining

The root beforeLoad auth (apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:239-253) still waits for the full boot chain (~1.57 MiB raw / ~478 KiB gzip) to download and evaluate, and that chain contains the connection runtime, wsTransport, contracts and stores. Three independent static paths put them in main's closure: lib/utils.ts:4 -> composerDraftStore -> ... -> environments/runtime -> wsTransport; routes/_chat.$environmentId.$threadId.tsx:5-8 -> lib/threadDetailPrewarm.ts:3 -> environments/runtime/service; and routes/pair.tsx:3-7 -> components/auth/PairingRouteSurface.tsx:5 -> environments/runtime. All three must be cut to remove them. Even then the boot chunk does not change, because BOOT_ROOT_MODULES (viteBuild/codeSplitting.ts:277-280) pulls the same closure back into boot through ChatIndexRouteView.tsx:10, and those modules evaluate at boot. index.html:128-131 has no early session fetch. The seed call at main.tsx:19/38 is not a real cost. Since #710 the shell chunk downloads during auth, so the user-visible gain left is about min(auth RTT, boot download+eval). That is a few ms on loopback, up to one RTT on a remote standard node with warm caches.

Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defect in the route splitting. Three doc/guard defects: (1) codeSplitting.ts:271-272 and standardBootGraph.test.ts:170-172 say BOOT_ROOT_MODULES 'evaluate on first use/when the router first renders them', but the build scope-hoists them into boot and evaluates them before auth. The measured trade-off comment therefore misdescribes its own cost, and codeSplitting.ts:147 cites a non-existent HOSTED_BOOT_ROOT_MODULES. (2) The new eager threadDetailPrewarm import (thread route :5-8) adds a third independent path to environments/runtime/service, and no boot-graph rule catches it. (3) The await import() calls at __root.tsx:203, :215, :244, :276, :316 and :343 target modules that sit inside the boot chunk, so they split nothing. This is cosmetic, but it only becomes a real split once the paths are cut.

Implementation sketch

Option A, cheapest. Standard builds only; never hosted (AGENTS.md hosted lifecycle owner), never Electron, never with VITE_HTTP_URL set. - apps/web/index.html:95-132: in the inline module script, when VITE_RYCO_CLIENT_MODE !== 'hosted-hub', the page is same-origin http(s) and not desktop, and the pathname is not /pair and does not start with /native/authorize/, start fetch('/api/auth/session', {credentials:'same-origin'}) and the primary descriptor request that ensurePrimaryEnvironmentReady makes. Catch errors to null and stash {requestedAt, session, descriptor} on one global. - packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.ts: add an optional deps.takeBootSessionPrefetch(). The first fetchSessionState inside bootstrapServerAuth (:239-255) adopts it exactly once, mirroring prefetchPrimaryWebSocketToken/discard at :303-312. Accept only ok and fresh responses; fall back to the normal retrying fetch on null, non-ok or stale. Do the same in the descriptor bootstrap. - The web platform adapter provides the take function; the hosted adapter does not. - Tests: unit tests for primaryAuth adoption (adopted once, 401/500/network fallback, reset clears it); a build test that the hosted index.html contains no prefetch; a browser test that a standard boot issues exactly one /api/auth/session. Option B, structural. Needs fresh measurements on both the hosted 150 ms/1.6 Mbps profile and standard loopback. - Move the DraftId schema out of composerDraftStore into a dependency-free module and fix lib/utils.ts:4. - In the thread route loader, reach retainThreadDetailSubscription through a tiny registry module that dynamically imports environments/runtime/service. Keep releaseThreadDetailPrewarmsExcept synchronous. - In PairingRouteSurface, load addSavedEnvironment with await import('../../environments/runtime') inside the submit handler. Keep environments/primary static, since it is lean. - Then stop grouping BOOT_ROOT_MODULES into boot, or make them a separate chunk preloaded with low priority. Without the cuts and this change, the cuts gain nothing. - Guard it in standardBootGraph.test.ts with forbiddenChains('main.tsx', [environments/runtime/(service|connection).ts, composerDraftStore.ts, client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts]). First make the walker skip pure re-export barrels of sideEffects:false packages (as createBootGraphMatcher already does), or have main.tsx import seedWsConnectionOnlineStatus from a narrow module. - Add the same patterns to the boot forbiddenSources in scripts/perf/model.ts. In either case, fix the comments at codeSplitting.ts:147 and :271-272 and standardBootGraph.test.ts:170-172 so they say the roots evaluate at boot.

Needs a decision

A real gain needs one of two things. One is reversing the measured BOOT_ROOT_MODULES trade-off (+0.35 s hosted sign-in, ~30 ms standard paint), against document-start preload contention that is also measured. The other is issuing the auth session/descriptor request from index.html, outside the client-runtime auth owner, which must stay standard-only under the hosted lifecycle rules. Since #710 the remaining benefit is a few ms locally and at most one RTT on remote warm-cache boots, so the owner should decide whether it is worth doing at all.

Because of the fix, a first click on a header PR, issue or Jira badge now waits on about 120 KiB gzip of chunks with no visual feedback. This is a small UX regression on slow or hosted links. (c) SidebarWorktreeList.tsx:253-259 and SidebarProjectDialogOwner.tsx:25-31 keep their own preloadableLazy wrappers instead of the shared lazyWorktreeDialogs exports, which contradicts that module's documented 'one module state per dialog' design. The effect on behaviour is negligible: one extra commit when the chunk is already cached. (d) Not a defect, but a trade-off to know about: on wide desktop threads that have messages, the overview (78 KiB gzip) now loads only after ChatView mounts. Nothing preloads it in parallel with the route chunk, so on a cold cache the crown appears one request round later than before (its slot width is reserved, so there is no layout shift).

Implementation sketch

1) Guard (S): in scripts/perf/model.ts, lower the ChatThreadRouteView maxGzipBytes to about 760 KiB and update the comment with the 2026-10-14 figure (724.5 KiB). Add forbiddenSources to that closure so the deferred surfaces cannot come back transitively. CI builds with RYCO_WEB_SOURCEMAP=hidden, so module attribution works. Patterns: ^apps/web/src/components/(chat/ChatOverviewPanel\.tsx|PlanSidebar|GitActionsControl|overview/crown/CrownOverview|SideChatPanel|chat/ContextHandoffInspectionPanel|chat/ComputerBetaPreview|chat/ExpandedImageDialog|PullRequestThreadDialog|worktrees/(NewWorktreeDialog|LinkedWorktreeItemDialog)|agent-control/AgentControlApprovals|workItems?/WorkItemDetail), plus ^node_modules/parse5/. This is a stronger guard than a per-chunk ≤600 KiB raw rule, because the chunk name 'ChatRightPanel' is just rolldown's naming of the shared chat chunk and is not stable. Optionally also add per-chunk maxRawBytes support to scripts/perf/bundleBudget.ts. Extend scripts/perf/bundleBudget.test.ts with a fixture for the new rule. 2) Phone tier (S-M): add preloadableLazy wrappers (next to chatViewLazySurfaces, or a shell/phone/lazyPhoneSurfaces.ts) for PhoneThreadAppBar, PhoneThreadDock, PhoneSessionPolicyControl, PhoneModelSheet and MessageActionsSheet. Mount them only when useLazyComponentReady(component, presentationTier === 'phone') is true, and preload when the tier is phone. Make ChatThreadRouteView use a lazy PhoneWorkSurfaceSheet the same way, which also makes LazyPhoneOverviewSheet effective; otherwise delete LazyPhoneOverviewSheet. This only lazy-loads frozen-tier code and does not extend or delete it (AGENTS.md). Add the specifiers to chatViewBundleSplitting.test.ts for ChatView.tsx, ChatComposer.tsx, ComposerFooter.tsx, ProviderModelPicker.tsx, MessagesTimeline.tsx and ChatThreadRouteView.tsx. 3) Make TranscriptSelectionActions (mount when a selection exists), ThreadMessageSearchBar (when search is open), DraftDeviceProjectDialog and ProjectScriptDialog (open state) lazy in the same way, with notifyChatSurfaceLoadFailure for errors. 4) Fix defects: pass onOpenLinkedItemIntent={() => void LazyLinkedWorktreeItemDialog.preload()} from ChatHeader through ChatHeaderBar to WorktreeSourceControlBadges. Replace the private wrappers in SidebarWorktreeList.tsx and SidebarProjectDialogOwner.tsx with LazyLinkedWorktreeItemDialog and LazyNewWorktreeDialog from worktrees/lazyWorktreeDialogs. Add a test that only lazyWorktreeDialogs.ts contains import('…/LinkedWorktreeItemDialog') and import('…/NewWorktreeDialog'). 5) Optional: in the thread route loader (non-preload navigations) or at ChatThreadRouteView module scope, call LazyChatOverviewPanel.preload() when the overview opens by default (wide, non-phone, server thread), so the crown chunk loads in parallel with the route instead of after mount. Verify by building with RYCO_WEB_SOURCEMAP=hidden and running `bun run perf:bundle-budget`, the vitest chatViewBundleSplitting and preloadableLazy tests, and the apps/web browser test perf/LazyComponentReady.browser.tsx. Then compare the ChatRightPanel size; expect about 590 KiB or less.

Partial#73 Sidebar re-renders and re-derives everything on every store commit (whole environmentStateById subscription + new settings object each render)

web-boot-cpu:sidebar-rerenders-every-store-commit · original impact High, effort S · Rendering WP12A

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

The two root causes named in the finding are fixed in 60633eff3 for the standard and desktop builds. Sidebar no longer subscribes to environmentStateById: it uses useShallow(selectCacheHydratedEnvironmentIds). The grouping settings are selected field by field and memoized. Sidebar compiles under the React Compiler (I re-ran the compiler in memory: Sidebar, FrozenWhileHidden and SidebarThreadJumpHintController compile with 0 errors). A browser test asserts zero Sidebar renders for 30 streaming thread.message-sent commits at 2,000 threads. Two gaps keep this from DONE. (1) Fix (3) does not hold. renderProjectRow is wrapped in useCallback, but one of its deps, handleNewThread, is a new function on every Sidebar render. It comes from useNewThreadState, which the React Compiler skips ('Unsupported declaration type for hoisting', the same at f1be4abc7), and that hook still uses the object-returning inline useSettings selector this finding flagged. So every legitimate Sidebar render re-renders SidebarProjectsContent, all memoized SidebarProjectItems, the SidebarWorktreeLists, SidebarChatList and SidebarPrimaryActions. A legitimate render happens, for example, on each coalesced shell upsert, at most 4 Hz per streaming thread. (2) The hosted (Hub web) build has a separate path with the same symptom. The hosted coordinator subscribes to every store commit and republishes a brand-new HostedWorkspaceSnapshot at most every 100 ms. Sidebar subscribes to the whole snapshot. inboxEnvironments and deliveryUnknownThreadKeys therefore get new identities, and InboxSidebar rebuilds its model up to 10 times per second during streaming, even when nothing the sidebar shows has changed. The browser test covers neither case: it runs only in projects mode (the default is inbox), only in the standard build, and only on unrelated commits.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:349-356 Confirmed fix (1): useStore(useShallow(selectCacheHydratedEnvironmentIds)) plus a memoized Set replaces the whole environmentStateById subscription. selectCacheHydratedEnvironmentIds is at packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:3422-3428.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:240-249, 369-380 Confirmed fix (2): module-level field selectors, and projectGroupingSettings is a useMemo over the two fields. useLogicalProjectSnapshots.ts:47-54 uses the same pattern.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:3300-3343, 1730-1871 The slice-memoized selectors keep the projects, sidebarThreads and sidebarWorktrees identities when a thread.message-sent commit only touches messageByThreadId, threadTurnStateById or threadShellById. The test therefore discriminates: commitEnvironmentState still creates a new environmentStateById, so the old subscription would fail it.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts:85, 96-99, 228-232, 412-421 Defect in fix (3). useNewThreadState fails React Compiler compilation (an in-memory babel-plugin-react-compiler run gives 4x 'Unsupported declaration type for hoisting' at :85; the same happens at f1be4abc7 and 60633eff3), so it runs uncompiled. Its useSettings((settings) => ({...})) inline selector returns a new object on every render (see useSyncExternalStoreSelector.ts:37-48), and handleNewThread's useCallback lists projectGroupingSettings as a dep (:419). handleNewThread is therefore new on every render. useThreadActions.ts:121-126 even says handleNewThread is 'inherently unstable'.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:382, 656-664, 1414-1460, 1532 handleNewThread from useNewThreadHandler is a dep of renderProjectRow (:1453) and is passed directly to every SidebarProjectItem (:1428) and to SidebarChatList (:1532). startNewThreadFromSidebar, which goes to SidebarPrimaryActions as onNewThread, also depends on it. The comment at :1414 says renderProjectRow is 'Stable so SidebarProjectsContent (memo) and its sortable rows skip re-rendering', but that is false whenever Sidebar renders. In SidebarProjectItem the new handleNewThread flows into createThreadForProjectMember and createThreadInWorktree (useSidebarThreadActions.ts:316, SidebarProjectItem.tsx:341-351, :524), so each git project's SidebarWorktreeList re-renders too.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/constants.ts:35 Shell thread upserts are now coalesced to 250 ms per thread, so Sidebar legitimately re-renders up to about 4 Hz per streaming thread. On each of those renders the unstable handleNewThread re-renders all 30 project items instead of only the affected one.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/hostedConnectionCoordinator.ts:283-286, 845-877, 912 Hosted path with the same symptom. useStore.subscribe(scheduleLiveSnapshotPublish) fires on every store commit. Within 100 ms it rebuilds each machine's metadata snapshot (readWorkspaceMetadataSnapshot is O(threads), and an IndexedDB cache.replace follows) and calls publish(machines). publish always builds a new snapshot object, including buildUnifiedWorkspaceIndex and a new demand object. publishHostedWorkspace notifies every listener without an equality check. The same code is in 7bc39eec3, the Ryco revision the Hub vendors.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:437, 466-603, 604-620 Sidebar reads the whole snapshot with useHostedWorkspaceState(). inboxEnvironments lists hostedWorkspace as a dep, and deliveryUnknownThreadKeys depends on hostedWorkspace.workspace.threads, which is a new array on each publish. Both get new identities at up to 10 Hz on unrelated commits. They feed ConnectedInboxSidebar, so the InboxSidebar.tsx:123-150 model rebuilds, and they also feed SidebarPrimaryActions. The finding measured that rebuild at about 14 ms warm at 2,000 threads, and inbox is the default mode (uiStateStore.ts:140).
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.renders.browser.tsx:136-205 Coverage gap. The test forces sidebarMode 'projects', runs only the standard build (where useHostedWorkspaceState is the signed-out stub), and asserts only that Sidebar does not render on unrelated commits. It does not check that children stay memoized when Sidebar renders legitimately.
  • apps/web/src/perf/reactCompilerCoverage.test.ts:13-52 The compiler guard covers Sidebar, the inbox components and useSettings, but not useHandleNewThread.ts (useNewThreadState) or useThreadActions.ts, which also fails ('Cannot access refs during render' at :112, though its callbacks have stable deps). Both are hooks that Sidebar calls on every render.
Remaining

(1) handleNewThread from useNewThreadHandler (apps/web/src/hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts:85-421) is a new function on every render. The cause is the compiler bailout plus the inline object selector at :96-99, with projectGroupingSettings as a dep at :419. This invalidates renderProjectRow (Sidebar.tsx:1416-1460) and the handleNewThread props at Sidebar.tsx:1428 and :1532. Every legitimate Sidebar render then re-renders SidebarProjectsContent, all SidebarProjectItems, their SidebarWorktreeLists, SidebarChatList and SidebarPrimaryActions. (2) In the hosted build, scheduleLiveSnapshotPublish (hostedConnectionCoordinator.ts:845-877, subscribed at :912) republishes a fresh HostedWorkspaceSnapshot at up to 10 Hz on any store commit. Sidebar.tsx:437 subscribes to the whole object, so Sidebar re-renders and rebuilds inboxEnvironments (:466-603), deliveryUnknownThreadKeys (:604-620) and the InboxSidebar model on commits that change nothing it shows. (3) The browser test does not cover inbox mode, the hosted build, or child stability on legitimate renders.

Defects in the shipped fix

Fix (3) is ineffective. renderProjectRow's useCallback (Sidebar.tsx:1416-1460) depends on handleNewThread, and handleNewThread changes identity on every Sidebar render because useNewThreadState (useHandleNewThread.ts:85) is skipped by the React Compiler and builds projectGroupingSettings through an inline object-returning useSettings selector (:96-99). The comment claiming renderProjectRow is stable is therefore wrong. The original verifier's correction that the SidebarProjectItems get stable props was also wrong for the same reason, but at the time it only mattered on unrelated commits, which no longer re-render Sidebar. The hosted republish path is a code path the fix did not cover. The auditor's 'None seen' is incorrect.

Implementation sketch

A. Stabilize handleNewThread (S, low risk): In apps/web/src/hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts, replace the inline useSettings object selectors in useNewThreadState (:96-99) and useHandleNewThread (:492-495) with module-level field selectors combined by useMemo, the same pattern as Sidebar.tsx:240-249/369-380 and useLogicalProjectSnapshots.ts:22-54. Fix the compiler bailout in useNewThreadState. The likely culprit is the self-recursive named function expressions inside useCallback (useCallback(function handleNewThread(...) { ... return handleNewThread(...) }) and likewise handleNewChat). Recurse through an inner local helper defined inside the callback body instead. Bisect against the in-memory compiler run until useNewThreadState reports CompileSuccess. Add { file: '../hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts', functions: ['useNewThreadState', 'useNewThreadHandler'] } to HOT_COMPONENTS in apps/web/src/perf/reactCompilerCoverage.test.ts. Optionally fix useThreadActions' render-time ref write (:125-126) with a useLayoutEffect, like ConnectedInboxSidebar.tsx:56-62, and add it to the guard as well. Extend Sidebar.renders.browser.tsx: add usePerfMark('SidebarProjectItem') in SidebarProjectItem (the existing mock already counts labels). Then apply a shell change to one thread, e.g. syncServerShellSnapshot with thread-7's updatedAt bumped, or a thread-upserted shell event. Assert that Sidebar renders once and that SidebarProjectItem renders at most once, for project-7 only. B. Hosted narrowing (S, low risk, UI-only): In apps/web/src/hostedHub/hostedConnectionCoordinator.ts, add useHostedWorkspaceSelector<T>(selector, isEqual?) built on apps/web/src/hooks/useSyncExternalStoreSelector.ts with the existing listener set. Add a matching export to hostedConnectionCoordinator.standard.ts that returns selector(SIGNED_OUT_WORKSPACE), keeping the pinned signature. In Sidebar.tsx:437, select only status, machines, demand.queuedEnvironmentIds and the delivery-unknown thread keys. machines is identity-stable across live publishes because scheduleLiveSnapshotPublish passes hostedWorkspaceSnapshot.machines through. queuedEnvironmentIds is stable between coordinator applies (:156, :174). For the delivery-unknown keys, select a sorted string[] compared with a shallow array equality. Rewrite the inboxEnvironments and deliveryUnknownThreadKeys deps to use these values. Do not dedupe inside publish(): it also drives hostedMutationLeaseAuthority.update with the snapshot generation, which is hosted-lifecycle territory. The same narrowing would help ChatView.tsx:639, useHandleNewThread.ts:524 and ProjectSwitcher.tsx:92, which also re-render at up to 10 Hz in hosted mode. Test: add a variant of Sidebar.renders.browser.tsx, or a focused test that mocks hostedConnectionCoordinator with a controllable listener set. Publish a new snapshot object that reuses machines and queued ids, and assert zero Sidebar renders. Also add an inbox-mode run of the existing streaming test.

Done#74 Streaming amplification: every 32 ms delta becomes 2 store commits plus O(all threads) UI sync work

web-boot-cpu:streaming-per-event-on-work · original impact High, effort M · CPU

Current state

Confirmed DONE. All three parts of the proposal are in main through 60633eff3 (#710), and 8fb94df00 adds shared reads on top. (1) A shell thread-upserted for a known thread now does an O(1) seedThreadVisitedAt. The O(threads x drafts) syncThreadUiFromStore and the global draft promotion run only for new threads, removals and snapshot reconcile. (2) Shell items and thread-detail events are batched per environment and animation frame. Each batcher is a store mutation barrier, the old 10-events/ms threshold is gone, and derived UI sync runs once per batch. (3) The server shell feed coalesces message-sent, activity-appended and proposed-plan-upserted per thread over a 250 ms window with a 250 ms flush tick. That gives about 4 upserts and SQL re-reads per second per streaming thread instead of about 30. Message text on the thread-detail stream is never coalesced. I found no correctness regression: ordering is preserved, the projection tracker only needs monotonic sequences, resume replays held events, and the hosted generation gate runs at enqueue time. Draft promotion is still covered through the thread.created batch path. Only minor efficiency leftovers remain, listed under fixDefects; none of them brings back the per-delta O(N) cost the finding describes.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/environmentStateSink.ts:78-102 thread-upserted: syncThreadUiFromStore and markPromotedDraftThreadByRef run only when there is no previousThread. A known thread gets an O(1) seedThreadVisitedAt. previousThread is read from threadShellById, so no full Thread is derived.
  • apps/web/src/uiStateStore.ts:969-988 seedThreadVisitedAt returns the same state once the thread is seeded, so zustand does not notify.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/environmentStateSink.test.ts:109-141 Test: a second upsert of the same thread does not call syncThreads or markPromotedDraftThreadsByRef again; it seeds only the single key.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/draftStore.ts:2432-2455 markPromotedDraftThreadsByRef indexes drafts once, so the remaining global callers (snapshot reconcile, thread-removed) are O(threads + drafts).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:1026-1077 Shell items go through createEnvironmentEventBatcher, which makes one applyShellEvents commit per environment and frame. After-hooks then run per event.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/eventBatching.ts:42-141 Frame batcher with a 100 ms fallback, a flush at 512 pending events, and registration as a store mutation barrier, so ordering against snapshots and removals holds.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:4078-4118 createShellEventCoalescer always frame-batches. The 10 events/ms gate from the old store.ts:3636 is gone.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:727-814 Thread-detail events are frame-batched through threadDetailEventBatcher. applyRecoveredEventBatch runs syncThreads only for thread.created, deleted, trashed or untrashed, and syncProjects only for project events.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationEventCoalescing.ts:62-77 orchestrationShellFrameKey keys message-sent, activity-appended and proposed-plan-upserted per thread. Every other event returns null and flushes held frames first, in sequence order.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:606-648 runLiveFeed runs a per-subscription coalescer plus a flush tick every coalesceWindowMs, so about 4 (at most about 8) shell upserts per second per streaming thread.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:831-838 The shell live feed uses orchestrationShellFrameKey with ORCHESTRATION_SHELL_THREAD_COALESCE_WINDOW_MS = 250 (constants.ts:35).
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:926-933 The thread-detail feed keeps orchestrationProgressFrameKey, which never keys thread.message-sent, so streaming text is not coalesced.
Defects in the shipped fix

None of these blocks the finding or regresses correctness; all are minor efficiency leftovers. (a) sharedThreadShellReads.ts:56 keys shared reads by (threadId, sequence), but each shell subscription coalesces with its own flush-tick phase and drain timing (orchestrationStreams.ts:636-640). During streaming the subscribers therefore emit different sequences for the same thread and almost never share a read: K subscribers cost about 4K shell reads/s per streaming thread instead of about 4. The finding's own target (about 30 down to about 4 reads/s per subscriber) is still met. (b) In hidden documents, scheduleStreamBatchFrame (service.ts:791-797) falls back to a microtask, so a minimized or occluded window still makes one commit plus a React render per thread-detail delta. (c) Mobile's thread-detail path (apps/mobile/src/connection/threadDetailEvents.ts:61) is not frame-batched; it is outside this web finding. evictIdleThreadDetailSubscriptionsToCapacity per upsert is bounded at 32 entries and now runs at about 4/s, which is negligible.

Partial#75 The inactive sidebar mode (inbox or projects) is fully mounted and recomputed while hidden

web-boot-cpu:hidden-sidebar-pane-mounted · original impact Medium, effort S · Rendering WP12A

Current state

The core problem is fixed in 60633eff3 (#710). Sidebar now mounts a pane only the first time it is shown (mountedSidebarModes starts as the persisted mode, read synchronously from localStorage, so boot mounts only the active pane). Each mounted pane is wrapped in React 19.2 <Activity mode=visible|hidden> plus FrozenWhileHidden, so a hidden pane neither re-renders on parent commits nor keeps effects or store subscriptions alive. buildInboxSidebarModel runs only inside InboxSidebar, and no other caller builds it. What remains is the proposal's last bullet, mode-specific parent inputs. In inbox mode (the default) Sidebar still derives sidebarChatRows (used only by the projects pane) and the project tree (sortedProjects, projectTreeRows, and per-project tree structures via visibleSidebarThreadKeys). The tree cannot simply be gated on sidebarMode: visibleSidebarThreadKeys also drives thread traversal and Cmd+N jump shortcuts in inbox mode, which today follow the invisible project-tree order. Also, SidebarThreadJumpHintController still re-renders the Sidebar on modifier-key hint flips in inbox mode, although no labels are shown there. The remaining cost is small: a one-off structure pass at boot plus incremental per-project recomputes, and the hidden-pane row/model cost the finding was about is gone.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:1462-1474 mountedSidebarModes = new Set([sidebarMode]); the other pane mounts only on first switch. sidebarMode comes from readPersistedState() at store creation (uiStateStore.ts:430-466, 1620), so no async hydration mounts both panes at boot.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:1505-1570 Both panes are wrapped in <Activity> + <FrozenWhileHidden>. The f1be4abc7 className="hidden"/inert wrappers were removed in 60633eff3.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:269-286 FrozenWhileHidden returns the element captured at hide time, so hidden subtrees bail out. The context providers above them (projectTreeCache from useState, the SidebarProjectDialogProvider actions useMemo) are stable, so no context propagation reaches the hidden pane on ordinary commits.
  • apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/InboxSidebar.tsx:123-125 This is the only buildInboxSidebarModel call site outside tests (grep). It is not reached while the inbox pane is unmounted or frozen.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:669-679 Remaining: sidebarChatRows (filters all 2,000 threads with a scopedProjectKey each) is built in every mode but consumed only at :1530 in the projects pane.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:845-892 Remaining: sortedProjects (spreads every visible thread; the sortProjectsForSidebar comparator re-reduces per-project threads) and projectTreeRows run in inbox mode.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:1015-1050 Remaining: visibleSidebarThreadKeys calls projectTreeCache.structure for every expanded project in inbox mode. At boot in inbox mode this is the full structure pass, which c64c1a29f measured as part of 6.2 ms at 2,000 threads/30 projects. After that, the per-project caches limit it to changed projects.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:1123-1245 In both modes, threadJumpThreadKeys and orderedSidebarThreadKeys (= visibleSidebarThreadKeys) feed the window keydown handler for traversal and jump. So in inbox mode the shortcuts use the hidden project-tree order. The list is therefore not purely mode-specific.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:1573-1578 SidebarThreadJumpHintController is mounted in both modes. Hint flips re-render the Sidebar body even in inbox mode, where visibleThreadJumpLabelByKey is consumed only by renderProjectRow (projects pane).
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:466 inboxEnvironments is not mode-specific. SidebarPrimaryActions passes it to SidebarOmnifield in both modes (SidebarPrimaryActions.tsx:97-101, SidebarOmnifield.tsx:105).
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.logic.ts:432-434 Thread prewarm is already limited to projects mode.
Remaining

Parent-level derivations for the inactive (projects) mode still run in the default inbox mode. (1) Sidebar.tsx:669-679: sidebarChatRows is computed although only the projects pane (:1530) reads it. (2) Sidebar.tsx:845-892 and :1015-1050: sortedProjects, projectTreeRows and visibleSidebarThreadKeys (a full per-project tree-structure pass at boot) run eagerly. In inbox mode their only consumer is the keydown handler (:1170-1245) for thread traversal and jump shortcuts, so they could be computed lazily. (3) Sidebar.tsx:1573: the jump-hint controller re-renders the Sidebar on modifier hint flips in inbox mode, where no hint labels render. All of this is low impact now that the hidden pane's model build, row renders and effects are gone and the per-project caches absorb repeat commits.

Defects in the shipped fix

No real defects found. Minor or by-design points: (a) after both modes have been visited, the inactive pane stays in the DOM as a display:none subtree. This costs memory only; it is not styled or laid out. (b) In the render that hides a pane, FrozenWhileHidden returns that render's children once before freezing, so the hidden pane can reconcile one last time with fresh props. Harmless. (c) Consumers of rarely changing outer contexts (for example the useSidebar context on open/close) can still re-render inside the hidden Activity at offscreen priority. Negligible. No test asserts that the inactive pane is not mounted at boot or is not re-rendered while hidden. Sidebar.renders.browser.tsx only counts Sidebar renders for streaming events and picker toggles.

Implementation sketch

In apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx: 1. Move the mountedSidebarModes/projectsPaneVisible block (now at :1462-1474) above the derivations. 2. Gate sidebarChatRows on projectsPaneVisible: `projectsPaneVisible ? buildSidebarChatRows(...) : EMPTY_CHAT_ROWS`. A hidden projects pane keeps its frozen props, so the empty value never reaches it. 3. Make the project-tree traversal list lazy outside projects mode. Extract the body of visibleSidebarThreadKeys (plus its sortedProjects/projectTreeRows inputs) into a pure helper in sidebar/sidebarVisibleThreadKeys.ts, e.g. computeVisibleSidebarThreadKeys({sidebarProjects, visibleThreads, maps, folders, expanded, caches, ...}). In projects mode keep the eager useMemo, because jump labels, the thread-list auto-animate threshold and prewarm need it. In inbox mode skip the memo and have the keydown handler call the helper on demand: put the inputs in a ref synced in a layout effect, or use a small memo cell keyed on input identity, so repeated keypresses reuse the result. threadJumpThreadKeys is derived the same way (first N of the lazy list). The existing per-project caches keep the on-demand call cheap. sortedProjects.length in shouldAnimateProjectLists/ThreadLists can use sidebarProjects.length, or be computed only when projects mode is active. 4. Render SidebarThreadJumpHintController only when projectsPaneVisible, or make it a no-op outside projects mode. Tests: extend Sidebar.renders.browser.tsx. With sidebarMode='inbox' and 2,000 threads, assert that no SidebarProjectItem or project-tree row renders at boot (for example via a perf-mark or Profiler id on SidebarProjectsContent) and that thread traversal and jump shortcuts still navigate in the same order as before (compare against the projects-mode order). Add a test that toggling to projects and back keeps InboxSidebar local state (settledOpen and similar) and does not re-render the hidden pane on a store commit. Unit-test the extracted helper in sidebarVisibleThreadKeys.test.ts. Validate with focused vitest and browser tests for apps/web only.

Done#76 useTheme re-applies the theme (style rewrite, change event, forced style read) in every consumer, including every ChatMarkdown

web-boot-cpu:use-theme-applies-per-mount · original impact Medium, effort S · Rendering WP12A

Current state

Confirmed DONE (60633eff3). useTheme no longer has a mount effect. One module-level controller applies the theme on module load, through the setters and through one shared matchMedia/storage/registry listener set. The snapshot is cached and invalidated by events, custom-theme parsing is cached by the raw string, and the appearance sheet is moved and rewritten only when needed. ChatMarkdown and the other 7 consumer files now cost a subscription per mount, with no style rewrite, change event or forced style read. No other code path applies the theme per mount: the remaining applyAppearancePreferencesToDocument and applyThemeToDocument callers are user actions, environment changes or editor previews. The fix leaves one narrow behavioural gap compared with the old per-mount apply, described under fixDefects.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useTheme.ts:296 useTheme is useSyncExternalStore plus derived values only. The old per-consumer useEffect(() => applyTheme(theme), [theme]) (f1be4abc7 useTheme.ts:226-228) is gone.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useTheme.ts:174 The module-load applyThemeChange(getStored()) is the only apply that is not tied to a change. The module loads at boot for every route through the dynamic import in apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:377 (RootRouteView).
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useTheme.ts:240 attachDocumentListeners installs one matchMedia, one storage and one registry listener per document on the first subscribe and keeps them for the document's lifetime. handleSystemColorSchemeChange (215) and handleThemeStorage (220) apply once rather than N times.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useTheme.ts:202 getSnapshot is cached via snapshotStale and invalidated by invalidateAndEmit, by subscribe, and by read-through while there are no listeners.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useTheme.ts:117 The transition guard does not force a synchronous reflow. syncBrowserChromeTheme runs in the next rAF on suppressed applies.
  • apps/web/src/themes/appearancePreferences.ts:374 The textContent write is skipped when the text is unchanged. ensureAppearancePreferencesStyleElement (~745-752) moves the element only when it is not the last element in <head>. None of the lazy CSS chunks (projects, automations, pullRequests, overview, xterm) define :root vars that overlap the appearance sheet, so moving it less often changes nothing visible.
  • apps/web/src/themes/registry.ts:189 Parsed custom themes are cached by the raw stored string. setCustomThemes and setActiveThemeId (207, 250) notify subscribeThemeRegistry (219), so the cached snapshot stays correct for same-tab writes, including importThemeFromFile and the AppearanceSettings paths.
  • apps/web/src/themes/themeController.browser.tsx:32 The browser test mounts 25 consumers and asserts 0 head mutations, 0 appearance events and 1 storage listener. A toggle produces exactly 1 appearance event and the guard lifts without a forced reflow.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatMarkdown.tsx:635 The per-message consumer now only subscribes. The other useTheme consumers are ChatView, DiffPanel, DiffWorkerPoolProvider, PreviewPanel, FilesTab, SettingsPanels and AppearanceSettings, and none of them apply anything on mount.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useTheme.ts:253 Fix defect. The first-consumer catch-up only compares appliedTheme with the stored mode and the .dark class, so cross-tab changes to the active theme id, custom themes or appearance prefs made before the first consumer mounts are never applied. The old per-mount applyTheme picked them up.
Defects in the shipped fix

One minor regression compared with the old per-mount apply. The document listeners are installed lazily on the first useTheme subscribe (useTheme.ts:269-273 -> attachDocumentListeners at 240). The catch-up at 253-261 only re-applies when the stored light/dark/system mode or the .dark class differs. The module loads at boot for every route, but routes such as Projects, Overview, the PR list and Automations mount no useTheme consumer. Suppose a tab has been on one of those routes since load and another tab changes ryco:active-theme, ryco:custom-themes or the appearance preferences. No storage listener exists yet, so nothing happens then. When the user later opens a chat (ChatView mounts useTheme), the catch-up sees the same mode and dark class and skips the apply. The tab keeps the old palette or appearance until a reload or the next real theme change. The old code re-applied on every mount, so it would have corrected this. Impact is very low because it needs a cross-tab change before the first consumer mount. Negligible leftovers: subscribe() sets snapshotStale = true even when the cache is already fresh, so each ChatMarkdown mount runs one readSnapshot (a few localStorage reads, one matchMedia query object, small array copies). This costs microseconds, not a style recalc. applyThemeToDocument (registry.ts:299-310) still rewrites identical theme text, and applyAppearancePreferencesToDocument still always dispatches its event, but both now run only on real changes.

Implementation sketch

Optional hardening in apps/web/src/hooks/useTheme.ts: install the document listeners together with the module-load apply, i.e. call attachDocumentListeners() inside the `if (typeof document !== "undefined" && hasThemeStorage())` block at line 174, right after applyThemeChange(getStored()). Keep the call in subscribe() so that re-attaching after __resetThemeControllerForTests still works. With listeners attached from boot, cross-tab and system changes are applied even on routes without a consumer, and the catch-up comparison at 253-261 can stay as a safety net or be removed. Optionally, in subscribe() only set snapshotStale = true when listeners.length was 0 before the push, which drops the per-mount readSnapshot. Test: extend themeController.browser.tsx to load the module with no consumer mounted, dispatch a StorageEvent for ryco:active-theme with a non-default theme id stored, and assert that the #ryco-active-theme style element appears. Run the focused browser test with bun run --cwd apps/web test:browser -- themeController.

Done#77 composeSidebarTree is O(worktrees × threads) with per-pair path normalization, and runs twice per project

web-boot-cpu:compose-sidebar-tree-quadratic · original impact Medium, effort M · CPU

Current state

The fix holds. composeSidebarTreeStructure now assigns threads in one O(T+W) pass using Map lookups on directory key, then linked node id. Path normalization is memoized, sortWorktrees runs once, and dedupe no longer calls JSON.stringify. A per-project cache shares one structure between Sidebar.visibleSidebarThreadKeys and SidebarProjectItem, which only decorates it. I copied the f1be4abc7 module out of git and benchmarked it against HEAD in Bun (JSC, not browser V8). Fixture: 30 projects, 30% of threads on unique worktree paths. At 2,000 threads the old composeSidebarTree took 8.0 ms and the new structure pass 0.82 ms (1.05 ms with decoration). At 8,000 threads it went from 109 ms to 3.9 ms, which scales linearly. With shared worktrees it went from 3.8 to 0.4 ms. Old and new trees came out identical on both fixtures. No other caller has a quadratic path: PhoneHome, useProjectMapCheckouts and the mobile app share the linear code or have no copy. What remains is optional, linear and small.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useSidebarTree.ts:388-431 assignThreadsToWorktreeNodes buckets threads by Map lookup. Matching on directory key or linked node id is the same as the per-pair rules. A thread whose directory is not covered can only match nodes without a directory, so the per-pair belongsToWorktree fallback runs only over nodesWithoutDirectory, or over all nodes when the thread's key is null. That is effectively never, because project.cwd is the fallback.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useSidebarTree.ts:528-542 Bounded memo for normalizeWorktreePath (4,096 entries, cleared when full).
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useSidebarTree.ts:157-237 The structure pass. sortWorktrees runs once (:212). Archived threads still go through synthesis, merge and assignment (:174, :194-210).
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useSidebarTree.ts:666-686 synthesizeWorktreeForThread sets archivedAt to null. A node synthesized only from archived threads therefore lands in the active worktrees list, so skipping archived threads would remove rows. That makes it a behaviour change, not a pure perf change.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/sidebarProjectTreeCache.ts:73-116 One structure per project. Identity fast path first, then an element-wise fallback after merging drafts and sorting (sortThreadsWithPinned).
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:386-394 The Sidebar builds its own pinnedThreadKeys Set.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useSidebarProjectThreadPresentation.ts:45-53 The project item builds a separate pinnedThreadKeys Set, so the two consumers never pass the same identity.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx:770-777 The Sidebar's per-project thread arrays come from groupByLogicalProjectKey and shareGroups. The item's come from selectSidebarThreadsForProjectRefs (SidebarProjectItem.tsx:121-129), a different array identity.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useSidebarProjectThreadPresentation.ts:153-160 The item calls cache.structure() on every render, outside a memo, including for collapsed projects. SidebarWorktreeList still mounts with an empty visible set (SidebarProjectItem.tsx:515-517), while the Sidebar skips collapsed projects (Sidebar.tsx:1024).
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/sidebarVisibleThreadKeys.test.ts:147-176 A cache test covers a second consumer with its own arrays and its own pin Set getting the same structure. The useSidebarTree.test.ts:301 test is a fixture test, not an old-vs-new oracle. My ad-hoc parity run matched.
Remaining

Nothing blocking. Optional, all linear: (1) Archived threads still go through the full structure pipeline (useSidebarTree.ts:174, 194-210). Benchmarked, deferring them would save about 0.4 ms at 2,000 threads. It would also drop worktree rows synthesized only from archived threads (useSidebarTree.ts:666-686, archivedAt null), so it is a behaviour change. (2) The Sidebar and SidebarProjectItem always pass different pinnedThreadKeys Sets and different thread-array identities. The identity fast path (sidebarProjectTreeCache.ts:75-84) therefore never serves the other consumer: each time the last caller switches, the cache merges drafts, re-sorts and runs sameElements before reusing the structure. That costs about 0.25 ms per call at 2,000 threads in one project, about a quarter of a rebuild. (3) SidebarProjectItem builds the structure for collapsed projects that show nothing (useSidebarProjectThreadPresentation.ts:153-160), so collapsed projects still pay one linear build at boot. (4) When a summary changes during streaming, that project's whole structure is rebuilt in O(T_p). Incremental reassignment is a separate topic.

Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness defects found. Old and new trees came out identical on unique-path and shared-worktree fixtures, and the per-pair rule parity holds by inspection, duplicate node ids included. One correction to the auditor's minor point: the cross-consumer cache miss is not conditional ('if they hold different array identities'). It is structural and happens on every alternation (Sidebar.tsx:386 vs useSidebarProjectThreadPresentation.ts:45 for pins; Sidebar.tsx:770-777 vs SidebarProjectItem.tsx:121-129 for threads). The structure itself is still built once, so the cost is only the re-sort. The cache Maps (selectors, structures) are never pruned for removed projects, which is negligible retention.

Partial#78 Shell snapshot re-application replaces every thread object; AI-Focus ranking changes push a full snapshot

web-boot-cpu:snapshot-no-structural-sharing · original impact Medium, effort M · Rendering WP14A

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

The client half is done and correct. syncEnvironmentShellSnapshot now keeps the previous shell, session, turnState, summary, project and worktree objects and the containers when nothing changed. The equality helpers cover every field of those types, and the cross-environment selectors return the same arrays. The server half is only partly wired: the server sends a small thread-priorities item to clients that ask for it, and web, desktop and mobile direct connections ask. The mobile hosted (Hub relay) primary connection does not pass applyThreadPriorities, so it never sends threadPriorities:"delta". It still receives a full, paged shell snapshot for every AI Focus ranking batch over the E2EE relay. Structural sharing keeps that from re-rendering rows, but the transfer, decrypt, decode and O(n) compare per batch remain for that client. Two nearby paths still rebuild every row without sharing: demoting an environment to cached state, and re-hydrating a hosted read cache that has the same capturedAt.

  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:2064-2213 syncEnvironmentShellSnapshot reuses the previous projects (plainDataEqual), worktrees, shell, session, turnState and summary objects, then the containers through reuseUnchangedIds, reuseUnchangedIdsByKey and reuseUnchangedRecord.   • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:603-776 threadSessionsEqual, sidebarThreadSummariesEqual, threadShellsEqual and threadTurnStatesEqual compare every field of ThreadSession, SidebarThreadSummary and ThreadShell (types.ts:196-275), apart from environmentId on summaries, which is constant per environment.   • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:3304-3412 createSliceRowsSelector and createAcrossEnvironmentsSelector are memoised on container identity, so reused containers return the same row arrays.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/storeStructuralSharing.test.ts:104-176 Tests cover an identical re-apply (all containers identical), a single-row change, and dropped rows.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:761-782 priorityStream sends {kind:"thread-priorities"} (only threads with a usable ranking) when threadPriorities==="delta". Every other client still gets a full (paged) shell snapshot for each ranking.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:62-65,294 applyThreadPriorities is optional, and the connection sends threadPriorities:"delta" only when the caller supplies it.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:821-925 (888) All three web and desktop createEnvironmentConnection calls (1289 primary or hosted, 1349 desktop Hub relay, 1551 saved) spread createEnvironmentConnectionHandlers, which includes applyThreadPriorities. Web and desktop are covered.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:514-515 Mobile direct (saved) connections pass applyThreadPriorities and opt in.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/primaryConnection.ts:60-67,243-289 UNCOVERED CALLER: HostedPrimaryConnectionDeps picks only applyShellEvent and resetShellProjection, plus syncShellSnapshot and pushSequenceMonitor.   • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3107-3109 (getShellSnapshot updatedAt folds in priority rankedAt) A ranking batch moves the snapshot's updatedAt forward, so on mobile hosted classifyProjectionSnapshot marks the priority-driven full snapshot as "newer" and applies it. Remaining

The equality helpers are field-complete, null sessions and own-key lookups are handled, and applyThreadPriorities correctly keeps unchanged summaries.

Not done#79 Main-thread Effect Schema decode of the whole shell snapshot, including archived threads

web-boot-cpu:shell-snapshot-decode-archived · original impact Medium, effort M · CPU decision

Current state

Not done. I tried to refute the auditor and could not. Every non-deleted thread, archived ones included, still goes over the wire as a full OrchestrationThreadShell. The client RPC layer decodes each one with the full Effect Schema on the main thread: Schema.Trim ids and titles, the ModelSelection transformEffect, and the withDecodingDefault fields. The client applies everything atomically only at snapshot-end. The one related change is d2aa947a3. It pages the snapshot into messages of at most 1 MiB and sends archived threads last, in their own messages. That shortens individual long tasks, but total decode, JSON.parse and store work stay the same. The client also never uses the archived-last ordering. The RPC client decodes each snapshot-threads page against the full schema before shellSnapshotAssembly sees it, and the assembler holds every page until snapshot-end. The pageShellSnapshot doc comment says a client 'can show the unarchived shell ... without decoding the archive first', but no client does that. I found no Worker decode, no trusted codec, no slim archived form, no excludeArchived option and no Hub-side change. The Hub relay never parses shell items. Two things make the cost larger than when the finding was written. First, #722 (46f0f6cd0, ThreadTrashRetirement) moves every conversation that was in Trash, previously excluded from the shell because deleted_at was set, into Archive, so they now ship in every shell snapshot. Second, hosted connections never resume the shell (apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:857 requires hostedGeneration === null), so every hosted reconnect pays the full archived transfer, relay decrypt and decode again.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:878-889 listActiveThreadShellRows filters only deleted_at IS NULL plus an optional scope. Archived threads are included.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3133-3170 buildShell maps every row to a full OrchestrationThreadShell (modelSelection, latestTurn, goal, session, lineage, priority) whether or not it is archived.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/shellSnapshotPages.ts:27-80 pageShellSnapshot splits threads into unarchived and archived and starts a new message for the archived ones. The pages carry the same full shells, so this only bounds message size (1 MiB, constants.ts:54).
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:747-753 shellSnapshotItems turns each page array into one stream chunk, which is one RPC message.
  • packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:1293-1296 OrchestrationShellSnapshotThreadsItem.threads is Schema.Array(OrchestrationThreadShell), so archived pages are fully decoded by the RPC client.
  • packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:1145-1190 OrchestrationThreadShell is unchanged since f1be4abc7: TrimmedNonEmptyString title/branch/worktreePath, ModelSelection, and withDecodingDefault on interactionMode, goal, archivedAt, settledOverride and settledAt.
  • packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:123-157 The ModelSelection Schema.decodeTo + transformEffect still runs per thread.
  • packages/contracts/src/baseSchemas.ts:4-5 TrimmedString = Schema.Trim and TrimmedNonEmptyString = Trim plus isNonEmpty.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/protocol.ts:517 This is the RpcSerialization.layerJson wiring; the auditor's line 472 is wrong. It is still plain JSON plus full RPC schema decode on the main thread. The client-runtime and web clients use no Worker for RPC; the only Workers are the diff parsers.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsRpcClient.ts:1077-1100 subscribeShell always requests snapshotDelivery "paged" and feeds the already-decoded items into the assembler.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/shellSnapshotAssembly.ts:36-67 The assembler concatenates every page, archived ones included, and emits a single snapshot only at snapshot-end. archivedThreadCount is never read on the client; git grep finds no consumer.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:272-283 syncShellSnapshot and bootstrapGate.resolve() run only after the full snapshot, archive included, has been assembled. Shell readiness therefore also waits for the archived pages to arrive and decode.
Remaining

The full cost described in the finding remains. ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:878-889 and :3133-3170 put every archived thread into the shell as a full OrchestrationThreadShell. shellSnapshotPages.ts:27-80 sends them as full shells. The client decodes each page with Schema.Array(OrchestrationThreadShell) (orchestration.ts:1293-1296) on the main thread via the RPC layer (protocol.ts:517, wsRpcClient.ts:1077-1100). shellSnapshotAssembly.ts:36-67 applies them atomically with the live threads at snapshot-end, which gates shell readiness in connection.ts:272-283. The archived-last ordering from d2aa947a3 is unused on the client. The hosted read cache (apps/web/src/hostedHub/readCache.ts) and the primary shell cache only paint from bounded metadata and only trim archived threads under budget pressure, so they do not change the live path.

Defects in the shipped fix

No fix exists for this finding. One inaccuracy in related code: the doc comment on pageShellSnapshot (apps/server/src/ws/context/shellSnapshotPages.ts:20-24) and on OrchestrationShellSnapshotDelivery (orchestration.ts:~1266-1272) says a client can show the unarchived shell before decoding the archive. No client can do this today, because the RPC layer schema-decodes every page before the assembler runs and the assembler waits for snapshot-end.

Implementation sketch

Preferred: an opt-in slim archived form plus on-demand full shells. (1) In packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts, add OrchestrationArchivedThreadStub: id, projectId, title, createdAt, updatedAt, archivedAt, worktreeId, branch, worktreePath, latestUserMessageAt and lineage. Use cheap leaf schemas where safe; the server already trims. Add a stream item kind 'snapshot-archived-threads' with threads: Schema.Array(OrchestrationArchivedThreadStub). Add an optional input field archivedThreads: Schema.optional(Schema.Literal('stub')) to OrchestrationSubscribeShellInput. Older servers ignore unknown keys. Do not widen the 'paged' literal, because old servers would reject a new literal value. (2) In apps/server/src/ws/context/shellSnapshotPages.ts, when the subscriber asked for stubs, emit the archived threads as stub pages. Thread the flag through orchestrationStreams.ts:747 shellSnapshotItems, priorityStream and orchestrationRpc.ts:542. (3) Add an RPC orchestration.getThreadShells({ threadIds } | { projectId, archived: true, cursor }) backed by the existing scoped buildShell (ProjectionSnapshotQuery getScopedShellSnapshot, which already supports a threadIds scope from 502adfd1e). Page it under the relay cap, reusing ORCHESTRATION_SHELL_SNAPSHOT_PAGE_MAX_BYTES. (4) In client-runtime, have shellSnapshotAssembly.ts accept stub pages and pass them through in the assembled snapshot as a separate archivedStubs array, or as shells marked detail: 'stub'. state/threads/store.ts stores stubs so the sidebar archived section, the archive settings view, lineage and the command palette keep working without a fetch. A later thread-upserted (unarchive sends a full shell) replaces the stub. Opening an archived thread already loads full detail through subscribeThreadWindow. Any consumer that needs a full field (modelSelection, goal, session) calls getThreadShells on demand. (5) Audit every archivedAt consumer and confirm stub fields are enough: useSidebarTree, sidebarTreeAdapters, archivedSettings, CommandPalette.logic, threadLineage, terminal/cleanup, workItemLocalLinks, agentThreads.logic, projectWorkspaces.logic, sessionTabs.selectors, mobile projectsModel, threadHeaderModel, environmentSnapshotCodec and workspaceMetadataProjection/primaryShellCache. (6) Tests: shellSnapshotPages.test.ts (stub pages; unarchived-only page bytes), shellSnapshotAssembly.test.ts (stubs plus threadCount accounting), store tests for stub-to-full upgrade on thread-upserted and archive-to-stub downgrade on re-snapshot, an orchestrationRpc compat test (old client without the flag still gets full shells), and a mobile environmentSnapshotCodec round-trip. Re-run the report's bench-decode-split at 2,000 threads with 60% archived. Expect decode close to the unarchived-only 39-40% plus a small stub cost, and roughly 50-60% fewer shell bytes on hosted reconnects. A cheaper variant with no product change: send the archived pages as Schema.Array(Schema.Unknown) behind a flag and decode them in idle slices. That only moves work off the critical path and does not reduce total CPU or bytes. Emitting the unarchived snapshot before the archive arrives would make the store drop and re-add archived threads; avoid it unless the store gains an additive 'archived-threads' apply. Longer term, use a Worker or trusted codec for shell pages.

Needs a decision

Slimming archived threads or fetching them on demand changes product behaviour. The archive view, the sidebar archived sections, lineage and delegated-child lookups, search and terminal cleanup would work from stubs or wait for a fetch. It also adds a contract and RPC shared by server, web and mobile. Using cheaper leaf schemas for stubs relaxes client-side validation of node-supplied data, which a hosted or E2EE path may want reviewed. Any variant that publishes the unarchived shell before the archive arrives would change when hosted shell readiness and mutation capability are granted, which falls under the AGENTS.md hosted lifecycle rules. No Hub protocol change or Hub deploy is needed, because the relay treats shell items as opaque.

Done#80 React Compiler silently bails out on the hottest boot components

web-boot-cpu:react-compiler-bailouts-hot-components · original impact Medium, effort M · Rendering

Current state

Confirmed DONE for the six components the finding names. I ran babel-plugin-react-compiler read-only with a logger, using the same default options as the build's reactCompilerPreset(). At HEAD, Sidebar, SidebarProjectItem, InboxSidebar, ConnectedInboxSidebar, ChatComposer and BranchToolbarBranchSelector all report CompileSuccess with zero CompileError, and their output imports react/compiler-runtime. Run against the f1be4abc7 sources, the same harness reproduces every original bailout at the finding's own lines: Sidebar:248 hook referenced as a value, SidebarProjectItem:72 ref accessed during render, InboxSidebar:57 value block inside try, ConnectedInboxSidebar ref writes, ChatComposer:425 ref writes, BranchToolbarBranchSelector:104 value block inside try. So the source-level guard test added in 60633eff3 (#710) is a faithful detector, and it fails CI on any CompileError or PipelineError in the listed files. The fixes are semantically sound: the moved ref syncs (useLayoutEffect) are only read from event callbacks, never during render. The auditor missed one thing. The report's file-level sourcemap heuristic could not see bailouts of single functions in files where other functions do compile. The same render-time ref pattern still silently disables the compiler for the streaming hot path: MessagesTimeline itself, UserMessageBody, useStableRows and ChatMarkdown's RenderedChatMarkdown. These predate the report and the guard does not cover them.

  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProjectItem.tsx:155-159 The ref sync moved to useLayoutEffect. First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

The core of the finding is fixed. Since #710 (60633eff3), useSettings uses a selector-aware useSyncExternalStore with Object.is over a merged-settings snapshot cached per (server settings, client settings) pair. Provider-status pushes keep config.settings, so useSettings consumers (SidebarProjectItem, InboxThreadRow, useGitStatus) no longer re-render on them, and a browser test covers this. The amplifier the finding also named is not removed for provider-status pushes. Sidebar's inbox model now depends on config.providers instead of the whole config. Every provider delta creates a new providers array, so it still rebuilds the whole inbox model (buildInboxSidebarModel over all threads) and re-renders every inbox row, and inbox is the default sidebar mode. The model only needs provider.driver and provider.models, for the model label, and status-only deltas keep the models array identity. ProjectFavicon still subscribes to the whole serverConfigAtom; the auditor missed it. It renders in every non-resting inbox row and every sidebar project header. DeviceIcon and ThreadPriorityRefreshBridge also still re-render or re-run on every provider push. Boot pushes are now much rarer (#710 persists fingerprinted probe results, and the server debounces and dedupes deltas), so the remaining cost shows up mainly after server or binary updates, provider settings changes and explicit refreshes.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useSettings.ts:168-226 Fixed. mergeSettings is cached in a WeakMap keyed by (ServerSettings, ClientSettings). useSettings subscribes to serverConfigAtom and client settings and selects through useSyncExternalStoreSelector, so re-renders follow the selected value. The doc comment is now accurate.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useSyncExternalStoreSelector.ts:8-48 The selection is memoized per snapshot and keeps the previous value under isEqual. Inline selectors (a new reader per render) stay correct and do not loop.

Defects in the shipped fix

(a) scripts/perf/gitComparison.ts:60 always builds compared refs with RYCO_WEB_SOURCEMAP=0, overriding the environment. perf:compare --cpu-profile can never produce the per-source summary that docs/performance-testing.md:159-161 and the cpuProfile.ts header describe.
