Done#84 Boot loader serializes main CSS download before starting the main JS import

web-boot-cpu:loader-css-before-js-waterfall · original impact Low, effort S · Waterfall

Current state

Confirmed DONE. The CSS and JS for the boot chain now download in parallel from document start, so the waterfall the finding described is gone. Since 3ce80cee6, index.html carries modulepreload links for every chunk in the boot chain plus a style preload for main's stylesheet, with crossorigin set to match. Separately, build.modulePreload now hands every dynamic import its full static JS closure, so the preload helper starts the JS fetch alongside the CSS. Before, it fetched the CSS first and the JS only after it loaded. The current dist (built after HEAD) shows the hints. The Hub vendors 7bc39eec3, which contains 3ce80cee6, and builds with this same Vite config, so hosted gets the fix too. The one remaining serialization is deliberate: import(main) still waits for the stylesheet's load event (the FOUC guard). The CSS (515 KB raw) has been in flight since document start alongside about 1.6 MB of boot JS, so it is not on the critical path.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/modulePreload.ts:38-58 bootPreloadTags: rel=modulepreload crossorigin for the boot-chain JS (entry excluded) and rel=preload as=style crossorigin for the stylesheets; hrefs come from the emitted bundle via resolveBootAssets.

  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/bundleGraph.ts:111-129 resolveBootAssets walks the entry's static imports plus the src/main.tsx chunk's static closure (no dynamic edges, no assets), splitting the result into modules and styles.

  • apps/web/index.html:128-131 The loader still calls import('/src/main.tsx') right away. The boot-shell-first-paint intent is kept: the shell is inline and preload links do not block rendering.
  • apps/web/dist/index.html:27-33 Built Oct 14 21:45, after HEAD (21:40). Contains the entry script, then modulepreload for boot, rolldown-runtime, boot-vendor and main, then preload as=style for main-DQhFpc47.css.

Remaining

selectDelegatedChildThreadsForThreadRef at packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:3499-3517 is still unmemoized. It runs a flatMap with a 1-element array per candidate thread, then a filter and a toSorted, on every store commit, through DelegatedThreadsSection.tsx:28-35 (mounted at ChatView.tsx:6018 on every non-phone thread view). On draft thread views the candidate set is every thread in the environment (3509-3511). That costs about 55 us and about 2k short-lived allocations per commit at 2,000 threads, and is frame-rate during streaming. It was part of the finding's cited range (old store.ts:3136-3200) and matches its per-project proposal: it is keyed by threadIdsByProjectId[projectId] plus the summary record.

Defects in the shipped fix

store.ts:3451 selectSidebarWorktreesForProjectRef uses `?? []` instead of EMPTY_WORKTREE_IDS. For every project without worktrees, each call allocates a new key array, a new result array and a dead WeakMap entry, and returns a new identity. For multi-checkout projects (createProjectRefsRowsSelector, 3460-3474) the parts comparison then fails on every commit, so the flat-and-compare runs every time. This affects SidebarProjectItem.tsx:130-138, PhoneHome.tsx:439, ProjectWorkspacesSection.tsx:412, useProjectMapCheckouts.tsx:143, useProjectDiskUsage.ts:102, NewThreadWorkLocation.tsx:96 and AgentsSection.tsx:46. useShallow still sees [] equal to [], so nothing re-renders; the cost is allocation and GC churn only. 1) store.ts:3451: replace `?? []` with `?? EMPTY_WORKTREE_IDS`. The existing comment already says results are read-only. 2) store.ts:3499 selectDelegatedChildThreadsForThreadRef: build the candidates with the memoized slice selector instead of flatMap: `const candidates = selectSidebarThreadRows(candidateIds, environmentState.sidebarThreadSummaryById)`. For the no-shell fallback, use the existing env-filtered per-environment selector (selectEnvironmentSidebarThreadRows) or the same shared selector keyed on threadIds. Then memoize the filtered and sorted result on (candidates identity, parent key), for example `const delegatedChildrenCache = new WeakMap<readonly SidebarThreadSummary[], Map<string, SidebarThreadSummary[]>>()` keyed by candidates, with an inner map keyed by scopedThreadKey(ref). Pass the result through reuseIfSameElements against the previous entry, and return a shared empty constant when there are no children. An unrelated commit then costs O(1). 3) Optional: in apps/web/src/hooks/useCheckoutResolution.ts:37, add a `threads === lastThreads` fast path before the O(N) every(). 4) Tests in packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/storeStructuralSharing.test.ts ('slice-memoized selectors'): assert toBe across the existing `unrelated` commit for (a) selectSidebarWorktreesForProjectRef on a project without worktrees, (b) selectSidebarWorktreesForProjectRefs with two refs where one has no worktrees, and (c) selectDelegatedChildThreadsForThreadRef with a fixture child whose lineage is {relationship:'delegated', parentThreadId}. Also assert the result changes when a child summary is archived. Done#86 One IntersectionObserver per sidebar and inbox row

web-boot-cpu:per-row-intersection-observers · original impact Low, effort S · Rendering

Current state

Confirmed DONE. #710 (60633eff3) replaced the per-element `new IntersectionObserver` in useHasIntersectedViewport and useIsIntersectingViewport with one module-level observer per rootMargin. Each observer has a Map<Element, Set<listener>> and dispatches entries by entry.target. The hook APIs are unchanged; useIsIntersectingViewport only gained an optional hysteresis argument. Every caller uses the default '160px 0px' margin: SidebarThreadRow, InboxThreadRow, SidebarProjectHeader, and ProjectFavicon, which #710 newly made lazy. All of them share a single observer, so the ~400 constructions at boot are gone. No other boot-scale per-row IntersectionObserver or ResizeObserver remains. The remaining `new IntersectionObserver` sites are one-off surfaces such as Mermaid, browser preview, device stream and project detail. codeHighlightQueue was already shared. The Hub vendors Ryco at 7bc39eec3, which contains 60633eff3, so hosted builds get the fix too. Only latent hardening and test gaps remain.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useHasIntersectedViewport.ts:17-77 sharedObservers Map is keyed by rootMargin. observeViewportIntersection lazily builds one observer per margin and dispatches by entry.target. It calls observe() only for a node's first listener. When the node's last listener goes it calls unobserve(), and when the observer's last node goes it calls disconnect() and deletes the entry. Dispatch iterates the Set, which tolerates self-removal.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useHasIntersectedViewport.ts:91-114 useHasIntersectedViewport registers through the shared observer. The old f1be4abc7 code built `new IntersectionObserver` per node.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useHasIntersectedViewport.ts:116-176 useIsIntersectingViewport registers through the shared observer. It processes every entry in order, where the old code used find() and took the first.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarThreadRow.tsx:133 Default margin, so it uses the shared observer. The ref is attached at :479.
  • apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/InboxThreadRow.tsx:195 Default margin, so it uses the shared observer. The ref is attached at :365.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProjectHeader.tsx:85 Default margin on the header div. The inner ProjectFavicon (:123) observes its own separate node, which is redundant but cheap.
  • apps/web/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:82 useHasIntersectedViewport was added in #710. ProjectFaviconImage observes exactly one node at a time, either the fallback or the img, so no node carries two listeners.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useHasIntersectedViewport.browser.tsx:7-35 The test harness has no unobserve(). No test checks that N rows build one observer or covers the unobserve and multi-listener paths. This is a test gap, not a defect.
Defects in the shipped fix

No current defects. Latent hazard: a second listener added to a node that is already observed gets no initial entry, because observe() runs only for the first listener (useHasIntersectedViewport.ts:58-63). An already-visible static node with a second hook would read false until it crosses the margin. No node has two hooks today. Test gaps: no test asserts a single construction across many rows or exercises unobserve, and the hook harness has no unobserve().

Implementation sketch

Optional hardening, low value. In observeViewportIntersection (apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useHasIntersectedViewport.ts:58-63), when a node already has listeners, call `current.observer.unobserve(node); current.observer.observe(node);`. Re-observing makes the browser queue a fresh initial entry, which every listener on that node receives, so the new listener gets its initial state. Repeat entries are harmless for both hooks. Add browser tests to useHasIntersectedViewport.browser.tsx with a counting stub that implements observe, unobserve and disconnect: (1) mount 3 probes and expect exactly one constructor call and three observed targets; (2) unmount one probe and expect unobserve for its node only, with no disconnect; (3) unmount all and expect disconnect, then a fresh mount builds a new observer; (4) put two hooks on one node and expect both to get state after an emit.

Partial#87 Root-level style invalidations are expensive with the 587 KiB stylesheet; avoid toggling root classes or variables at runtime

web-boot-cpu:root-level-style-invalidation-cost · original impact Low, effort S · Rendering WP12A

Current state

PARTIAL is right. 60633eff3 removed the forced reflow between adding and removing the guard, gave the document a single theme controller (one apply per real change), and skips appearance style writes when the CSS is unchanged. caa5f8576 added the themeRecalcMs harness metric with a regression threshold. Two things remain. (1) registry.ts applyThemeToDocument still rewrites the theme <style> unconditionally. (2) The no-transitions guard on <html> is added on every suppressTransitions apply, even when nothing visual changes. Example: another window changes only diffLayout, or edits a custom theme that is not active. That costs two full-document restyles for nothing. The auditor's suggestion to swap the root guard for View Transitions or a scoped transition:none is not real remaining work. caa5f8576 measured the alternatives and kept the guard on purpose, and any global transition suppression needs an 'on' restyle and an 'off' restyle.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useTheme.ts:117-127 startThemeTransitionGuard: adds no-transitions, reads the browser chrome colour in rAF 1, removes the guard in rAF 2. No forced synchronous reflow any more (old code used offsetHeight at f1be4abc7 useTheme.ts:118-120).
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useTheme.ts:129-139 applyTheme starts the guard (line 132) before it knows whether the dark class, the theme CSS or the appearance CSS will change. Every suppressTransitions apply therefore costs a guard-on restyle and a guard-off restyle across the whole document.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useTheme.ts:220-230 handleThemeStorage calls applyThemeChange(getStored(), true) for the theme, active-theme, custom-themes and appearance keys. In another visible tab or window, a change that emits no CSS still toggles the guard: diffLayout via useDiffLayout.ts:9-12 (diffLayout is not part of the CSS text at appearancePreferences.ts:371), or an edit to an inactive custom theme. Result: two full-document recalcs with no visual change. setActiveTheme to the already-active id does the same (useTheme.ts:289-294, e.g. AppearanceSettings.tsx:184).
  • apps/web/src/themes/registry.ts:299-310 applyThemeToDocument still assigns style.textContent unconditionally (line 309) for any non-default theme. The text is ':root{light} :root.dark{dark}' and does not depend on the dark class, so a light/dark/system flip rewrites identical CSS. Unchanged since f1be4abc7 (60633eff3 only added the custom-themes parse cache and registry listeners).
  • apps/web/src/components/settings/ThemeEditor.tsx:197-199 The live-preview effect depends on [draft, resolvedVariant], so every light/dark flip while the editor is open calls applyThemeToDocument again with identical CSS. The registry guard would cover this too.
  • apps/web/src/themes/appearancePreferences.ts:367-380 The appearance CSS is built first and written only when style.textContent differs (lines 374-376). ensureAppearancePreferencesStyleElement (lines 745-759) moves the element only when it is not already the last child of <head>. This proposal part is done.
  • apps/web/src/index.css:10 @custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark, .dark *)): toggling .dark on html re-matches the whole document. This is inherent to the design; the one required restyle per real theme change cannot be avoided.
  • apps/web/src/index.css:495-501 The .no-transitions, .no-transitions * guard is still a root descendant selector, so adding it and removing it each invalidate the whole subtree.
  • scripts/perf/browserProbe.ts:61-130 measureThemeRecalc (caa5f8576, an ancestor of HEAD) toggles no-transitions plus dark over 4,400 cloned elements and reports the median. It is wired at browserProbe.ts:1301 and model.ts:108/407/446/506 with a 20% / 10 ms comparison floor. The commit message records guard+theme at 28 ms plus 17 ms for guard removal. Letting transitions run cost 215 ms, and the theme class alone cost 49 ms because transitions started. That is why the guard was kept on purpose.
  • apps/web/src/themes/themeController.browser.tsx:32-71 Covers one apply per change and the guard lifting without a reflow. It only uses the default theme (no theme style element), so the unconditional theme rewrite and the guard on no-op storage events are not tested.
Remaining

(1) apps/web/src/themes/registry.ts:309 writes the theme style text unconditionally. Compare it with the current text first. (2) apps/web/src/hooks/useTheme.ts:132 starts the transition guard (the guard-on and guard-off full-document restyles) before checking whether anything will change. Same-tab examples: setActiveTheme(sameId). Cross-tab examples via handleThemeStorage, useTheme.ts:220-230: a diffLayout change or an inactive custom-theme edit in another window. These still toggle no-transitions on <html> twice and change nothing. The remaining cost of the guard on a real theme change (about 17 ms synthetic, one frame later) is a deliberate, measured trade-off from caa5f8576, not open work.

Defects in the shipped fix

None that break anything. Minor: the chrome-colour sync and the guard removal run in rAF, so in a hidden tab they wait until the tab is visible again. That is harmless because nothing paints while the tab is hidden. One caveat on wording only: the appearance comment and the auditor say an identical textContent rewrite always forces a full recalc. In Chromium the inline-sheet text cache can make an identical rewrite close to free, so the gain from item (1) is mostly consistency, WebKit/Safari for hosted users, and the no-visual-change paths. On a real light/dark flip the dark-class toggle already forces the full recalc in the same style pass.

Implementation sketch

1) registry.ts: extract buildThemeDocumentCss(theme): string | null (null for DEFAULT_THEME_ID). applyThemeToDocument(theme) returns a boolean 'changed'. It removes the element only if it exists, and writes style.textContent only when it differs from the built text. Optionally cache the built text keyed by theme object identity, since findTheme returns cached objects. 2) appearancePreferences.ts: have applyAppearancePreferencesToDocument() return whether it wrote, or export buildAppearancePreferencesCss() so the caller can compare before writing. Keep dispatching the change event either way. 3) useTheme.ts applyTheme: compute isDark, darkChanged = root.classList.contains('dark') !== isDark, and the pending theme and appearance CSS against the current textContent. Only if suppressTransitions && (darkChanged || themeChanged || appearanceChanged) call startThemeTransitionGuard(root), then do the writes in the same synchronous task (no style reads in between). When nothing changed, skip the guard and the chrome sync. 4) Tests: in themeController.browser.tsx, add (a) with a non-default built-in theme active, a light-to-dark setTheme produces no characterData/childList mutations on the theme style element; (b) a StorageEvent for the appearance key that only changes diffLayout, and setActiveTheme(currentId), produce no class mutations on document.documentElement (MutationObserver on attributes) and leave no no-transitions class behind. In registry.test.ts, add unit coverage of the changed boolean. Run only `bun run test` for the web package's theme tests and the focused browser test file. Do not try View Transitions or a scoped guard: caa5f8576's measurements favour the current guard.

Done#88 Composer drafts persist images as data URLs in localStorage: boot hydration, full re-serialization on every debounced write, and full decode to read one thread's IDs

web-boot-cpu:composer-draft-image-persistence · original impact Low, effort M · Blocking I/O WP10

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. DONE stands: a1e8b31f3 removes all three costs the finding described. The auditor's claim that there was no concrete defect is wrong. The split storage brought in a multi-tab draft-loss regression. Each tab rewrites the shared index only when its own index refs change, so another tab's stale index can drop a draft that this tab is still actively writing. I reproduced this against the real createSplitComposerDraftPersistStorage. The old single-blob model would have kept that draft, because there the last writer's full state won.

Current state

The perf finding is fixed. Drafts now persist as one small localStorage entry each, plus an index. Image bytes are stored as Blobs in IndexedDB, and the entry records only bytes:"local". Hydration builds rows without decoding anything; bytes load lazily at idle time or when a composer shows them. partialize only snapshots references, and the debounced flush stringifies and writes only the drafts whose identity and text changed. readPersistedAttachmentIds reads only the one thread's entry. The lib/utils DraftId import remains, but it is moot because environmentStateSink pulls the store into the boot graph anyway. One fix defect: with two tabs open, the index (draftKeys) is last-writer-wins per index change, while entries are last-writer-wins per draft. Tab B can write an index that omits draft T, which tab A created after B booted. If A then only types in T, A never rewrites the index, so T is dropped on the next reload, and any tab's boot sweep removes T's entry. The old model kept T. Residuals that are not worth fixing: the prompt stash still keeps data URLs in one localStorage blob, capped at 2 MB and written only on stash actions. Hosted mode still encodes a data URL once per image add, and verify then discards it.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/draftSplitStorage.ts:215-251 flush() serializes only drafts whose object identity changed and writes only when the JSON text differs, so a keystroke rewrites one small entry. This confirms the auditor.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/draftStore.ts:2349-2360 The persist config uses the split storage. partialize = snapshotComposerDraftPersistState (references only), so the per-set whole-state JSON.stringify of the old createJSONStorage (f1be4abc7 draftStore.ts:2264-2268) is gone.
  • apps/web/src/composerDraftPersistence.ts:113-135,211-228 Image bytes go to IndexedDB (bytes:"local"). Hydration creates rows with file:null and bytesPending, and decodes nothing. atob now runs only for legacy data URLs during the idle-time restore, which also migrates them into IndexedDB (lines 340-351).
  • apps/web/src/composerDraftPersistence.ts:92-106 readPersistedAttachmentIdsFromStorage parses only composerDraftEntryStorageKey(threadKey), not the whole blob.
  • apps/web/src/composerDraftStore.ts:97-109; apps/web/src/composerFileUpload.ts:142 Bytes restore at requestIdleCallback after hydration. Send is blocked with a 'Loading' message while bytesPending, and stash shows a toast (ChatComposer.tsx:2193).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/draftSplitStorage.ts:253-291 DEFECT: indexChanged compares only this tab's own refs (writtenIndexRefs), and the index is never re-read. Once another tab has overwritten the index, this tab's entry writes for a draft missing from that index never re-list it.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/draftSplitStorage.ts:185,300 DEFECT, compounding: at boot every unindexed ryco:composer-draft:v2:* entry is collected and deleted on the first flush. A newly booted tab therefore deletes the entry of a draft that another live tab is writing but that the current index omits.
  • apps/web/src/composerDraftPersistence.ts:49-73 There is no cross-tab coordination for drafts: no storage-event listener and no rehydrate. Reproduction (bun -e against draftSplitStorage.ts with a shared Map): A creates T, B changes stickyActiveProvider, A types in T. The index stays draftKeys:["X"] while entry T holds the latest text, and reload yields only ["X"].
  • apps/web/src/lib/utils.ts:4; apps/web/src/environments/runtime/environmentStateSink.ts:7-11 The lib/utils DraftId import is still there, but the store is in the boot graph through environmentStateSink regardless, so it is moot.
  • apps/web/src/promptStashStore.ts:105,259-265; packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/promptStash.ts:11 A sibling path with the same pattern, outside this finding: the prompt stash stores data URLs in one localStorage blob, parsed at module eval and capped at 2 MB of attachment chars. Writes happen only on stash, take or finalize, never per keystroke. Boot cost is under 1 ms worst case. Not worth acting on.
Defects in the shipped fix

Multi-tab draft loss from the split storage (a1e8b31f3). packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/draftSplitStorage.ts:253-291 rewrites the shared index only when the tab's own index refs (draft threads, logical mappings, sticky selection, version, draftKeys) change, and never notices a foreign index write. Scenario: tabs A and B are open with draft X. A starts draft T, so the index becomes [X,T]. B changes its sticky model, creates or sends some draft, or promotes a thread, and writes index [X], which omits T. A keeps typing in T, so only entry T is rewritten and the index stays [X]. After a reload, T is gone, and the boot sweep (lines 185 and 300) deletes its entry. A newly booted third tab likewise deletes entries of live drafts that the current index omits. Under the old single blob, A's last write kept T. Reproduced with bun -e against the real module. Minor, mobile-only and outside the web-boot scope: apps/mobile/src/state/composerDraftStore.ts:28-32 passes no scheduleWrite, so every set flushes the changed draft at once, and no keys(), so orphaned entries are never swept. tryWrite only catches synchronous throws, so async KV write failures are treated as written.

Implementation sketch

In packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/draftSplitStorage.ts flush(): (1) Before computing indexChanged, read the stored index when storage.getItem returns synchronously; on web this is a cheap read of a small string. If it differs from writtenIndexJson, another tab wrote it, so force indexChanged. (2) Build draftKeys as the union of (a) this tab's live keys and (b) foreign keys from the stored index that this tab neither tracks in `written` nor removed itself. Track a `removedByThisTab` set, filled where entries are removed. (3) For keys this tab tracks that the foreign index dropped: if this tab's draft is unchanged since it was read or written (written.get(k).draft === draft, or the entry is missing from storage), drop the key and respect the other tab's delete. If this tab edited the draft, keep it, so the user's latest edit wins. (4) Narrow the boot sweep (lines 185 and 300): re-check each candidate against the freshly read stored index at flush time, and skip keys that index now lists. Optionally, also add a window 'storage' listener in apps/web/src/composerDraftPersistence.ts for COMPOSER_DRAFT_INDEX_STORAGE_KEY that marks the split storage stale, so flushes can skip the extra read. Tests in packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/draftStorePersistence.test.ts, using two createSplitComposerDraftPersistStorage instances over one shared Map: - foreign-draft survival: A creates T, B changes sticky provider, A edits T, a fresh instance reads, and T is present. - delete propagation: B clears X, which A never edited, then A flushes an unrelated change, and X is not resurrected. - edit wins: B clears X, A edits X, and X is present. - sweep safety: a new instance does not delete an entry that the current index lists.

Value medium · effort S · risk low

Done#89 React's 300 ms Suspense reveal delay adds ~250-300 ms idle per lazy boundary: twice on every boot and once on every first page open

browser-measure:suspense-fallback-throttle · original impact High, effort M · Rendering WP12B

Current state

The fix removes the measured cost. RootAppShell and HostedHubRoot are preloadableLazy and are awaited in root beforeLoad, so the root match commits the shell directly. Every route body uses lazyRouteComponent, which the router awaits before it commits. defaultPreload is 'intent', the idle preloads warm the thread, draft and settings chunks, and a browser test plus a static test guard the behaviour. I checked react-dom 19.2.8: the 300 ms hold applies only to retry-lane commits (react-dom-client.production.js:10791-10794). TanStack Router 1.170.33 shows route pending UI by throwing router._tx[5] into a Suspense boundary (Match.js:105-108), and the content then commits through a useSyncExternalStore update on SyncLane (forceStoreRerender, :4761-4763), so it is never throttled. Some on-demand React.lazy boundaries the fix did not convert still commit a fallback and pay up to 300 ms on first use; none is on the measured boot or first-page-open paths.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:38-43 RootAppShell and HostedHubRoot are preloadableLazy, so they render synchronously once their module has loaded.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:127-137 withRootSurfaceLoaded awaits surface.preload() before the root context resolves, so the root match commits the shell and not a fallback.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:159-165 The shell chunk and the matched route chunks start loading in parallel with the auth round trips (proposal part 1).
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:199 Hosted path: runHostedBootGate awaits HostedHubRoot.preload(). bootGate.ts:46-55 also awaits the hosted workspace shell when the account is authenticated or a remembered preview applies.
  • apps/web/src/routes/_chat.$environmentId.$threadId.tsx:33-36 Uses lazyRouteComponent. The draft, statistics, projects, pull-requests, _chat, _chat.index, diagnostics and native.authorize routes do too, and settings uses it through settingsRoute.ts:21-24 (proposal part 2).
  • apps/web/src/router.ts:15-16 defaultPreload is 'intent' with a 50 ms delay. Sidebar and inbox rows also preload the route on press (threadNavigationIntent.ts) (proposal part 3).
  • apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:175-187 The idle preloads warm the thread and draft route chunks, the command palette and the settings page. preloadSettingsPage warms the same lazyRouteComponent the route renders.
  • node_modules/@tanstack/react-router@1.170.33 dist/esm/Match.js:105-108 A pending match throws router._tx[5] into the route's Suspense boundary. tx[5] resolves only after the commit (router-core load-client.js:919, :991-997). The reveal itself comes from the store update.
  • apps/web/node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom-client.production.js:4761-4763 forceStoreRerender schedules lane 2 (SyncLane). Router commits are therefore never retry-lane-only and never hit the 300 ms throttle at :10791-10794.
  • apps/web/src/components/perf/RouteRevealThrottle.browser.tsx:107-230 Perf guard (proposal part 4). The root shell and a route-split page must commit within 50 ms of their chunk resolving. A React.lazy control must exceed 150 ms. Every route except /pair and __root__ must be code-split. The test is included by vitest.browser.config.ts:24.
  • apps/web/src/perf/webBundleSplitting.test.ts:27-51 Static guard: the route files use lazyRouteComponent and contain no React.lazy and no <Suspense.
  • apps/web/src/browser/LazyBrowserPanel.tsx:3-17 Not converted. React.lazy with a 'Loading browser…' fallback, mounted by the workspace Browser tab (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:450-458). Its first open is throttled, and so is a reload with workspaceTab=browser in the URL (rightPanelRouteSearch.ts:76-77, :145).
Defects in the shipped fix

The fix itself has no bug, and I found no regression on the measured paths. Some callers outside the measured paths were not converted. These on-demand surfaces still use React.lazy, commit a Suspense fallback, and are held by up to 300 ms on first use: - apps/web/src/browser/LazyBrowserPanel.tsx:3-17: the workspace Browser tab and ProjectBrowserPreview. This one also hits boot when the URL restores workspaceTab=browser. - apps/web/src/components/CommandPaletteDialog.tsx:416-441: CreatePullRequestDialogHost. - apps/web/src/components/onboarding/OnboardingCoordinator.tsx:23-25, :89: the first-run dialog. - apps/web/src/components/chat/AttachmentDocumentPreview.tsx:14, :144: the PDF viewer. - apps/web/src/components/settings/IntegrationsSettingsPanel.tsx:23, :46: ComputerUseSettings. - apps/web/src/components/hostedHub/HubAccountPage.tsx:14-23, :101: the hosted account Security and Appearance panels. - apps/web/src/components/hostedHub/HostedNativeAuthorizationRoute.tsx:19, :81. - The hosted workspace shell after an in-session sign-in (hostedRootAppShell.tsx:33-38 and HostedHubRoot.tsx:221). Two invisible boundaries arm the global fallback clock on every boot: PreviewFileNavigationGuard (__root.tsx:47-51, :80) and, on Electron only, DesktopQuitFeedback (main.tsx:32-36, :77-81). Corrections to the auditor: PreviewFileNavigationGuard is not the only fallback on the common boot path. The root pendingComponent is itself committed as a Suspense fallback, because MatchInner throws router._tx[5]; this is harmless because the reveal is SyncLane. Electron also commits the DesktopQuitFeedback null fallback. The claim that the nested workspace-panel boundaries no longer commit a fallback is wrong for the Browser tab. The auditor's line numbers have drifted slightly: withRootSurfaceLoaded is at :127-137, and the hosted preload await is at :199. The frozen web phone tier still has lazies (PhoneSettingsSurface, PhoneGetAppInterstitial, AppSidebarLayout LazyPhoneSettingsSurface). AGENTS.md says not to extend that tier, so I left them out.

Implementation sketch

For each remaining on-demand site, apply the pattern this fix already established: 1. Replace React.lazy with preloadableLazy. 2. Gate the mount with useLazyComponentReady(component, wanted, { onLoadError }) and render the current fallback as an ordinary element while the hook reports not ready. ChatRightPanel.LazyRightPanel and ChatTerminalShell's drawerReady are the templates. 3. Add an intent or idle preload where one is natural. Per site: - LazyBrowserPanel: make Panel preloadableLazy. Add a loadBrowserPanel to SURFACE_LOADERS['browser'] in workspacePanelPreload.ts so tab hover warms it, then wrap the mount in WorkspaceSurfaceGate or useWorkspacePanelChunkReady. - CommandPaletteDialog: gate CreatePullRequestDialogHost on useLazyComponentReady(host, createPullRequestRequested), and preload it when the palette shows the 'New pull request…' action. - OnboardingCoordinator: gate OnboardingDialog on useLazyComponentReady(dialog, active), and call preload() once `ready` turns true. - AttachmentDocumentPreview: gate the PDF viewer on useLazyComponentReady(viewer, open && kind==='pdf'), and preload it on the preview button's pointerenter. - IntegrationsSettingsPanel: gate ComputerUseSettings the same way. - HubAccountPage: reuse the preloadableLazy AccountSettingsPanel and AppearanceSettingsPanel modules (or SettingsPage's preloadSettingsSection), preload them on rail-item pointerenter or focus, and gate the mount. - HostedNativeAuthorizationRoute: gate the auth surface the same way. - hostedRootAppShell.HostedRootAppShell: call useLazyComponentReady(LazyRootAppShell, true) and render <AppBootLoadingSurface/> as a normal element until it is ready. This drops the fallback commit after an in-session sign-in. Keep the Suspense only as a safety net. The shell download is still deferred until the account is authenticated, so the 'unauthenticated visitors never download it' property holds. - Invisible boundaries: convert PreviewFileNavigationGuard (__root.tsx) and DesktopQuitFeedback (main.tsx) to preloadableLazy + useLazyComponentReady(x, true). Then no fallback commits on boot and the global fallback clock stays unarmed. Tests: - Extend apps/web/src/perf/webBundleSplitting.test.ts with an allowlist scan over apps/web/src for `lazy(` imported from 'react'. It should fail on any new site outside the frozen phone-tier files. - Add one RouteRevealThrottle.browser.tsx case: a gated on-demand surface commits within REVEAL_BUDGET_MS of its chunk resolving even after an unrelated fallback committed just before. Validation: run focused vitest on the touched files, plus the RouteRevealThrottle browser file.

Done#90 Statistics: getUsageSummary takes 2.5-8.2 s on every open (no memoization, sources scanned one after another, everything re-aggregated)

browser-measure:statistics-usage-summary-latency · original impact High, effort M · CPU

Current state

Confirmed DONE (60633eff3 #710, e5e676f95; both are ancestors of 7bc39eec3, so the Hub-vendored web bundle has the client half too). Every cost the finding names is gone. (1) Claude and Codex transcript sources are memoized per source on sourceId + request key, with fingerprint = rates generation + listing (path/size/mtime/dev:ino:ctime per file). Only 'complete' results are stored, LRU 32. (2) The scan cache holds per-file 15-minute slot aggregates, priced once per slot, not per record. The randomized equivalence test covers DST and :45 zones. (3) Sources run with concurrency 2. (4) A client UsageSummaryCache keeps the last usable result per (env, range, tz), peek() repaints it right away, and UsageView shows the skeleton only when nothing is cached. (5) The route loader prefetches on link intent (defaultPreload 'intent', 50 ms). The bare /statistics link defaults to view=usage, range=30d, so hovering it starts the exact request the page makes. The other verifier items are also fixed: scan budgets count only fresh parses, rates are stale-while-revalidate, the cache store is sharded and persists after the response, there is an idle release, and identical and abandoned requests are shared or dropped. Measured here (read-only, real ~/.claude + ~/.codex, about 2.2k files, warm FS): the memo-hit listing plus fingerprint takes 67-94 ms. So a hit sits at the edge of the <100 ms target, and with the client cache a reopen within a session paints instantly. The remaining problems are second-order. One is a rare robustness issue, not a correctness bug.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:792-813 Per-source memo hit: key = sourceId + summaryRequestKey (contract, start, end, tz), fingerprint = ratesGeneration + listingFingerprint (250-262). The hit returns before loadScanCache and before any file read.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:917-928 Only complete results are memoized (LRU SOURCE_MEMO_LIMIT=32 at 112). ratesGeneration bumps only on a new revision (416-420) or a disk load (393).
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:990-992 Effect.forEach(plans, scanSource, { concurrency: SUMMARY_SOURCE_CONCURRENCY = 2 }) replaces the sequential source loop. store.ensureLoaded is serialized by loadLock (usageScanCacheStore.ts:186-187), so concurrent sources load the cache safely.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageFileAggregate.ts:87-145,239-264 Per-file slot aggregates, priced per slot via priceUsageSlot. Keyed responses (dedupeKey) stay as compact typed-array rows and are walked on every summary for cross-file dedup.
  • apps/server/src/usage/claudeTranscript.ts:45-50 Every Claude record gets a dedupeKey, so the Claude fold on a memo miss is still O(records): a Set lookup plus 7 Float64 reads each. The commit reports 42 ms per 97.5k, versus 265 ms per-record.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageTranscriptReader.ts:78-166 The listing (opendir + 32-way batched lstat) runs on every request, including memo hits, because it proves the memo is valid. Measured with a /tmp script importing this module: 67-94 ms for 2,161-2,245 files.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:1162-1196 Identical requests share one forked scan. Abandoned waiters interrupt it. The flight is put in `inflight` (1173) before forkIn runs (1174-1181), so an interrupt at the runtime's auto-yield in between (effect 4.0.2 internal/effect.ts:643-650 wraps the next op in yieldNow) leaves an entry with no fiber and an unresolved Deferred.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCacheStore.ts:32 USAGE_SCAN_CACHE_RECORD_LIMIT = 1,000,000 is still counted in raw records (usageScanCache.ts:509-522), below the per-source SOURCE_CACHED_RECORDS = 2,000,000 (UsageService.ts:101). The cap was sized when entries held raw records.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageTranscriptReader.ts:346-360,234-243 An appended file re-reads and SHA-256s its whole old prefix on each memo miss. Checkpoints are LRU-bounded to 128 files / 100k records / 32 MB, so a file without one is fully reparsed. This machine has 393 Claude transcripts modified within a day (300 MB).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/usage/summaryCache.ts:68-160 UsageSummaryCache: last usable result per (env, range, tz), up to 32. Identical flights are shared and prefetch handoffs go through SharedRequests (sharedRequests.ts:49-182).
  • apps/web/src/components/statistics/useUsageSummary.ts:136-148,158-166 Until the view answers, it uses peek() as the stale-while-revalidate value. refreshing = loading && merged !== null. UsageView.tsx:82 shows StatSkeleton only when nothing is cached.
  • apps/web/src/routes/statistics.tsx:38-45 The loader calls prefetchStatisticsPage (statisticsPrefetch.ts:17-24), which calls prefetchUsageSummary (useUsageSummary.ts:42-50). router.ts:15-16 sets defaultPreload 'intent' with a 50 ms delay. statisticsSearch.ts:50-51 defaults view=usage and range=30d, so the sidebar <Link to="/statistics"> (SidebarChrome.tsx:56, AppSidebarLayout.tsx:211) prefetches the exact request.
Defects in the shipped fix

No defect that defeats the fix. Minor residuals, from most to least relevant: (a) Hit rate while agents run. Any change in a source's listing misses its memo, which in practice means almost always for Claude during active sessions. The miss path is: the listing (~70-90 ms here), one Effect.fn span per listed file from readFileRecords (UsageService.ts:603; LocalFileTracer records every non-SQL span to server.trace.ndjson), an O(records) keyed Claude fold, and a full-prefix SHA-256 re-check of every appended transcript, or a full reparse when its checkpoint was evicted (usageTranscriptReader.ts:236-243, 346-360). For parallel-agent users with dozens of active multi-10MB transcripts I estimate a few hundred ms per miss, not measured. That is still far below 2.5-8 s, and client SWR hides it on reopen, but it is visible on the first open after a reload. (b) Rare robustness race in readSummary. inflight.set (UsageService.ts:1173) runs before Effect.forkIn (1174-1181). If the caller is interrupted at an auto-yield between them, the key is left with no fiber and a Deferred that never completes, and every later identical request hangs until endDate rolls over. (c) USAGE_SCAN_CACHE_RECORD_LIMIT = 1M raw records (usageScanCacheStore.ts:32) is below SOURCE_CACHED_RECORDS = 2M. Histories over 1M responses within the 120-day retention evict the oldest files after each summary. 90d/all views then reparse them under the 100k/5 s budget, return 'partial', and never memoize. (d) I agree with the auditor's notes: OpenCode/Cursor sources are not memoized (OpenCode has its own fingerprinted DB aggregate cache at opencodeUsageReader.ts:224-226, so the impact is small), scanSemaphore is still 1, and there is no whole-summary memo. Corrections to the auditor: the useUsageSummary line refs are 136-148 and 166 (not 132-141 and 163). The hit-path listing measured 67-94 ms, not 'tens of ms'. The Claude fold is still O(records) because every Claude record is keyed.

Current state

Confirmed fixed (56fbe263a). The Statistics view now gets its connections from useSyncExternalStore(subscribeEnvironmentConnections, readConnections) with a cached, reference-stable snapshot. React re-reads the snapshot after subscribing, so a register() emit fired by EnvironmentConnectionManagerBootstrap before the listener attached is no longer lost. Done#92 Each project icon spawns a new Node child process and is resolved twice per load (HTTP fallback before config, then RPC)

browser-measure:project-icon-node-spawn · original impact Medium, effort S · Process spawns WP12A

Current state

Confirmed DONE (60633eff3, #710). The cost in the finding is gone. There was one Node child per lookup with no cache, and each icon was resolved twice (HTTP before config, then RPC). Now every server path, HTTP /api/project-favicon and RPC projects.readIcon (web and mobile), goes through one ProjectFaviconResolver. It has a 10-min TTL cache, per-root single-flight, and 2 reader fibers that batch up to 16 roots per killable child. The web client shows a placeholder until the server config is known and only uses HTTP for servers without the projectIcons capability. The client cache is now keyed by environment+project+revision, so it survives reconnects. Server-side caching also removes the warm-reload RPC spawns the original verifier flagged. No other caller spawns per lookup, and the Hub only relays projects.readIcon. A critical read found only minor fix defects (below), none of which restore the per-project spawn cost.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:10-20 10-min TTL, 60 s stalled-root backoff, 1024-entry cap, 2 reader children, 16 roots per child, 30 s caller deadline. This replaces the old Semaphore(2) with no cache (git show f1be4abc7).
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:96-111 Readers use Queue.takeBetween(queue, 1, 16): one child per batch, not per project.
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:113-129 readIcon returns a cache hit, or joins or registers a pending Deferred and enqueues the root once (single-flight shared by HTTP and RPC).
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:67-94 Per-root results. The first unfinished root gets a 60 s null backoff, and the roots after it get one retry child.
  • apps/server/src/project/readProjectFavicon.ts:73-134 readProjectFavicons(roots) uses one execFile child per batch: deadline 1.5 s + 250 ms per extra root, SIGKILL, partial stdout parsed per line. The isolation the verifier required is kept. argv.slice(1) layout checked under both node and bun --eval.
  • apps/server/src/project/projectFaviconWorker.ts:98-112 The worker resolves every root in order and writes one JSON line per root as it goes.
  • apps/server/src/http.ts:733-766 The HTTP favicon route uses the same resolver.readIcon.
  • apps/server/src/project/readProjectIcon.ts:32 The RPC path uses the same resolver.readIcon(project.workspaceRoot). It is wired from apps/server/src/ws/projectRpc.ts:43-46.
  • apps/web/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:108-128 config == null or deferred gives src null (placeholder). HTTP is used only when the RPC capability is absent and the row is visible. This removes the HTTP-then-RPC double resolve.
  • apps/web/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:80-107 The read is gated on viewport intersection and checks peekProjectIconSource first.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/projectIconSource.ts:25-111 Per-environment LRU keyed by project+revision (no longer by connection generation), 5-min TTL, pending single-flight. Mobile uses the same module (apps/mobile/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:43-59).
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:69 Defect: Effect.tryPromise(() => options.readFavicons(roots)) drops the AbortSignal. The old code passed { signal } (f1be4abc7 resolver line 14), so interrupting a reader no longer SIGKILLs its child.
Defects in the shipped fix

All minor, none restores the per-project spawn cost. (1) The resolver no longer propagates interruption to the child. ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:69 calls Effect.tryPromise(() => options.readFavicons(roots)) and ReadProjectFavicons (lines 22-24) has no signal parameter. The old resolver passed { signal } to readProjectFavicon. When the resolver scope closes (server shutdown), an in-flight child is not SIGKILLed at once. It is bounded only by execFile's own timeout while the parent lives, and is orphaned if the parent exits first. readProjectFavicons still supports signal and the abort tests still pass, but production never uses it. (2) The server cache (lines 37-48) caps entries at 1024 but has no byte budget. Found icons keep up to 512 KB each (readProjectFavicon.ts:15), so the worst case is about 512 MB. The key is the raw cwd string, and the authenticated HTTP route accepts any cwd (http.ts:744-750), so aliases such as '/p', '/p/', '/p/.' each miss and each take an entry. Expired entries stay until capacity eviction. Realistic single-user memory is small. (3) The stalled-root heuristic (lines 84-93) blames the first root of a batch even when the whole child failed: spawn error, or Node/Electron startup slower than the 1.5 s deadline under boot load. That root gets a 60 s null. The RPC result cannot express 'unavailable', so the client caches that null as a known absence for 5 min (projectIconSource.ts:96-104), and that now survives reconnects because the cache is no longer per connection generation. (4) As the auditor noted, there is no mtime/realpath invalidation: a newly added favicon appears after up to 10 min server-side plus 5 min client-side. Each cold miss still pays one Node startup per batch rather than using a long-lived worker. That is acceptable given the kill-ability requirement.

Implementation sketch

Optional hardening, all in apps/server/src/project/Layers/ProjectFaviconResolver.ts (plus a small readProjectFavicon.ts change). (a) Change ReadProjectFavicons to (roots, signal?: AbortSignal). Use Effect.tryPromise((signal) => options.readFavicons(roots, signal)), and pass { signal } in makeProjectFaviconResolver to readProjectFavicons. Test: an injected reader records the signal; close the scope mid-read and assert signal.aborted. (b) Normalize the cache/pending key with path.resolve(cwd), a pure string operation with no FS I/O, so the isolation stays intact. Track retained bytes in remember() and evict oldest entries until under a budget (for example 32 MB) as well as the 1024-entry cap. Optionally sweep expired entries in remember(). Tests: '/p', '/p/' and '/p/.' share one batch entry; a byte budget smaller than 3 icons evicts the oldest. (c) Make readProjectFavicons report whether the child wrote any line or hit its deadline (for example, return { results, childRan: boolean }). In readBatch, apply STALLED_ROOT_BACKOFF_MS only when the child produced output or timed out, not when the spawn itself failed. Optionally, in packages/client-runtime/src/connection/projectIconSource.ts, cache null results with a shorter TTL (for example 60 s) than found artwork, so a transient server-side null does not hide an icon for 5 min. Run the focused vitest files apps/server/src/project/Layers/ProjectFaviconResolver.test.ts and apps/server/src/project/readProjectFavicon.test.ts, plus the client-runtime projectIconSource tests if (c) touches them.

Done#93 Statistics summary blocks on an outbound 2.75 MB LiteLLM pricing fetch inside the scan lock, and retries it on every open after a failure (no negative cache)

browser-measure:usage-rates-blocking-fetch-no-backoff · original impact Medium, effort S · Network / RTT WP06

Current state

Confirmed DONE (60633eff3). The blocking ensureRates (old UsageService.ts:243-283, awaited inside scanSemaphore) was replaced by stale-while-revalidate pricing. startRatesRefresh loads disk rates, then forks one single-flight fetchRates into serviceScope, off the scan permit, when the rates are older than 24 h and no attempt was made in the last hour. fetchRates records ratesLastAttemptAtMs before the request, so failures, timeouts, non-200 responses and captive-portal HTML all back off for 1 h, and old rates stay in place. A summary waits only when no rates exist at all, at most 2 s, and that wait overlaps source discovery. ratesGeneration is bumped only when the document hash changes, and it is part of the transcript-source memo fingerprint. Pricing runs per slot at summary time, never inside the per-file scan cache, so fresh rates re-price memoized and cached data. A 30 s post-boot warm-up refreshes stale rates when a pricing cache exists. A test covers the main behaviour: with a hanging download and stale cache, two summaries come back in under 2 s, priced from the cache, with one fetch; with no cache and failing downloads, three summaries make one fetch. No other network fetch exists in the usage path, and the Hub has no counterpart. The leftover gaps are minor.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:444-465 startRatesRefresh: single-flight through the ratesRefresh Deferred, with no yield between the re-check and the assignment. It skips the fetch within RATES_TTL_MS (24 h) or RATES_RETRY_MS (1 h) of the last attempt, and runs fetchRates via Effect.forkIn(serviceScope), so it is not interrupted when the caller goes away and does not hold the scan permit.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:399-437 fetchRates sets ratesLastAttemptAtMs = now before the request, so every outcome (failure, timeout, empty or HTML body) backs off. The 10 s timeout covers the body read. On failure the old rates stay and state becomes cached/unavailable. On success it bumps the generation only when the revision changes and writes pricing-cache.json atomically.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:965-974 readSummaryUnlocked starts the refresh, plans sources, and awaits the refresh only when rates.size === 0, with timeoutOption(max(0, 2000 - waitedMs)).
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:86-93 Constants: RATES_RETRY_MS 1 h, RATES_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS 10 s, RATES_FIRST_FETCH_WAIT_MS 2 s, RATES_WARM_DELAY_MS 30 s.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:792-795 The memo fingerprint includes pricing.generation, so new rates invalidate memoized transcript sources.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageFileAggregate.ts:268-322 UsageSlotAggregator prices slots with the request's rates when a summary runs (priceUsageSlot), so the scan cache holds no frozen prices and a generation bump fully re-prices the data.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:467-473 Boot warm-up: after 30 s, if pricing-cache.json exists, it calls startRatesRefresh in the background.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:1125-1133 scanSemaphore.withPermits(1) wraps readSummaryUnlocked. The only network work inside it is a bounded 2 s wait, and only when there are no rates at all.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.test.ts:461-525 Test: with a stale cache and a hanging download, summaries return in under 2 s with cached pricing and one fetch. With no cache and failing downloads, three summaries make one fetch.
Defects in the shipped fix

None that bring back the reported cost. Minor gaps: (1) The 10 s RATES_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS (UsageService.ts:89, applied at 402-409) still covers the 2.75 MB body read even though the fetch now runs in the background. On links slower than about 2.2 Mbit/s it always times out: rates never refresh, a fresh install stays 'unavailable', and a partial download is retried each hour a summary is opened. (2) No test covers the generation-bump path, where a background refresh with a new revision re-prices an already memoized source. Only the stale-cache and back-off paths are tested. (3) The back-off is a fixed 1 h kept in memory, and the warm-up is a fixed 30 s delay rather than an idle check. Both are acceptable. (4) A legacy or corrupt pricing-cache.json, while offline, is re-read and JSON-parsed on every summary inside the permit, because loadRatesFromDisk only short-circuits once ratesFetchedAtMs is set. This is cheap and rare.

Done#94 Static assets are served uncompressed, and Vite's preload helper makes main.js wait for the 601 KB CSS

browser-measure:uncompressed-assets-css-serialized · original impact Medium, effort M · Network / RTT

Current state

Confirmed DONE. The standard (node-served) web build writes a .gz sibling for every hashed compressible asset of at least 1 KiB. The Ryco server negotiates Accept-Encoding with per-variant weak ETags, Vary, 304s without Content-Encoding and an identity fallback. The siblings reach the npm package and the desktop stage: dist/client is a plain recursive copy, files=[dist], and no filter strips .gz. index.html now preloads the whole boot chain and the main CSS at document start, so the CSS-then-main.js request chain is gone. Hosted shells use the Hub's own br+gzip precompression (origin/main scripts/build-static-manifest.ts, src/http/staticAssets.ts), so skipping the plugin for hosted-hub builds leaves no gap. Leftovers are cosmetic: brotli is off by default, the extension list is duplicated between build and server, and unhashed vscode-icons SVGs are uncompressed and served no-cache. None of these is a meaningful cost.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/precompressAssets.ts:91 createPrecompressedAssetsPlugin (writeBundle, enforce post) gzips hashed compressible assets of at least 1 KiB at level 9 and skips siblings that save less than 10%. .br is opt-in (:48-54).
  • apps/web/vite.config.ts:131 The plugin runs only for clientMode 'standard'. Hosted builds rely on the Hub, which precompresses br+gzip itself (ryco-hub origin/main scripts/build-static-manifest.ts:119-131, src/http/staticAssets.ts:119-141,271).
  • apps/server/src/http.ts:257 staticFileResponse sets Vary for precompressible extensions, stats the accepted siblings concurrently (br preferred, then gzip), sets Content-Encoding and a per-variant ETag (:134-145), and strips Content-Encoding on 304 (:307). Content-Type comes from the original path.
  • apps/server/src/http.ts:153 acceptedStaticContentEncodings handles q=0, *, x-gzip and an empty header (identity) correctly.

No functional defects. Optional nits: (1) Brotli is off by default (apps/web/vite.config.ts:135 createPrecompressedAssetsPlugin()). Partial#95 The full ~113-130 KB ServerConfig is fetched 3-6 times per session even though it is already subscribed, and it blocks the shell snapshot on slow links

browser-measure:server-config-overfetch · original impact Medium, effort M · Network / RTT decision

Current state

PARTIAL is confirmed. The auditor's evidence holds at ec250e386. The boot duplicate getConfig, the usage preflight, the automation-centre read and the non-hosted new-thread read are gone. Provider pushes are now deltas, and a config snapshot omits catalogs the client names by digest. Saved environments now reuse the subscription snapshot for their metadata refresh; at f1be4abc7 they ran a parallel getConfig. The auditor did not mention that improvement or the following gaps. (a) Catalog persistence is enabled only on desktop and loopback pages. Hosted Hub web, LAN/Tailscale browsers and mobile therefore start every page load or cold start with an empty catalog cache. Their first config snapshot still carries the full ~117 KB of catalogs, on exactly the slow remote links where the finding measured head-of-line blocking. (b) The unary server.getConfig is not catalog-aware. Every remaining caller pays the full ~125 KB. That includes hosted Hub new-thread (every draft) and hosted first worktree send, where it sits on the critical path only to read settings and one capability bit. (c) Mobile opens two subscribeConfig streams on the active connection: the connection-level onConfigUpdated plus startServerStateSync. On a cold start these can carry two full snapshots.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/serverState.ts:156-178 Proposal 1 done: startServerStateSync only subscribes lifecycle and config. The parallel getConfig is gone.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsRpcClient.ts:900-915 getUsageSummary asserts the contract version locally. There is no getConfig preflight.
  • apps/web/src/components/automations/useAutomationCentre.ts:71-74 Providers come from the live useEnvironmentServerConfig, not from a getConfig per bind.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1236-1249 Not noted by the auditor. Saved-environment metadata refresh awaits the subscription's config snapshot (awaitSavedEnvironmentConfig). It falls back to getConfig only on timeout. At f1be4abc7 (service.ts:1143) it ran getConfig in parallel.
  • apps/server/src/ws/providerRpc.ts:718-746 With providerStatuses:'delta' the stream sends providerStatusesDelta, and nothing when nothing changed.
  • apps/server/src/ws/providerRpc.ts:768-777 The snapshot omits catalogs named in knownProviderCatalogs. The client restores them in wsRpcClient.ts:979-1018 and resubscribes without claims on a miss.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderRegistry.ts:583-640 revalidateStale is a single-flight pass owned by the registry. Fresh sources cost nothing (proposal 4).
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:195-201,228-238 Hosted Hub mode returns before the catalog store is attached. Elsewhere persistence runs only when keepsLocalCaches is true.
  • apps/web/src/persistence/primaryShellCacheEligibility.ts:12-17 keepsLocalCaches = desktop || loopback hostname. Any remote browser, including hosted Hub, keeps catalogs in memory only, so each page load's first snapshot carries all catalogs.
  • packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:810-814 WsServerGetConfigRpc payload is Schema.Struct({}) and success is the full ServerConfig. The unary read has no catalog digests or omission.
  • apps/server/src/ws/providerRpc.ts:201-204 serverGetConfig returns the full loadServerConfig, catalogs included (~125 KB per the d1ffcef9f measurement).
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts:146-161 requireFreshConfig is hosted || isHostedHubMode(), so every hosted draft issues a full getConfig. A lease check runs before and after (146-170).
Remaining

1. Hosted Hub new-thread and first send still read the full ~125 KB getConfig on the critical path. - New thread: apps/web/src/hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts:160 into apps/web/src/hooks/newDraftDefaults.ts:125-136. It uses only settings defaults and capabilities.projectPreferences. - First send with a worktree: apps/web/src/hooks/executeChatSendTurn.ts:617-619. It uses only the capability bit. 2. The unary serverGetConfig (packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:810-814, apps/server/src/ws/providerRpc.ts:201-204) has no catalog omission, so every remaining caller pays for all catalogs. 3. Catalog persistence is limited to desktop and loopback (apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:195-201,228-238; apps/web/src/persistence/primaryShellCacheEligibility.ts:12-17). Hosted Hub, remote browsers and mobile receive the full catalogs in the first config snapshot of every page load or cold start. This is the slow-link case the finding measured, though now as one copy instead of two. 4. Small user-action leftovers: apps/web/src/editorPreferences.ts:61 (open in editor) and apps/web/src/components/pullRequests/agentHandoff.ts:185 (PR handoff) do full getConfig reads. 5. Adjacent, mobile: apps/mobile/src/state/serverStateSync.ts:29 opens a second subscribeConfig stream beside the connection-level one. That doubles the snapshot and deltas, and both can carry full catalogs on a cold start.

Defects in the shipped fix

No verified bugs in the implemented parts. Usage, automation centre, the non-hosted draft path, deltas, catalog omission with claim-free resubscribe on a miss, and single-flight revalidation are all correct as read. The mobile double config subscription predates the fix (at f1be4abc7 it also issued a getConfig) and is not a regression. Residual design gap: the per-page catalog cache helps only reconnects and node switches on non-persisting surfaces, never the first load.

Implementation sketch

A. Per-connection live config for hosted targets (removes hosted new-thread and first-send getConfig). - packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts: make every connection kind observe config (drop the kind/onConfigUpdated gate at :179). Expose `config: { read(): ServerConfig | null; subscribe(listener) }`. read() returns observedConfig only if the connection is not disposed, the WS status is connected, and the snapshot arrived on the current attempt. Track the attempt like shellSnapshot does, and reset it in onResubscribe and reconnect(). - Change startServerStateSync (packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/serverState.ts:162) to take that connection-level observer instead of opening its own subscribeConfig. Update apps/web/src/components/ServerStateBootstrap.tsx and apps/mobile/src/state/serverStateSync.ts. This removes mobile's duplicate stream and keeps exactly one config stream per connection everywhere. - apps/web/src/hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts:155-161: for hosted targets pass cachedConfig = readEnvironmentConnection(id)?.config.read() and set requireFreshConfig only when that is null. Keep the existing before/after mutation-lease check. - apps/web/src/hooks/executeChatSendTurn.ts:617-620: same rule. - Tests: connection.test.ts (read() is null after resubscribe until the new snapshot, null after dispose, not double-subscribed); newDraftDefaults/useHandleNewThread tests (hosted with current-attempt config → getConfig not called; stale or absent → getConfig); executeChatSendTurn.test.ts hosted worktree path; mobile serverStateSync test asserting one subscribeConfig per connection. B. Alternative or complement, without touching lifecycle: make the unary read catalog-aware. Add optional knownProviderCatalogs to the WsServerGetConfigRpc payload and an optional providerCatalogs bookkeeping key to the response (a wrapper or optionalKey; older servers ignore the field). Reuse omitKnownProviderCatalogs (apps/server/src/ws/providerCatalogs.ts:33) in providerRpc.ts:201, and pin/restore with providerCatalogCache in wsRpcClient.ts:891. This cuts every remaining getConfig from ~125 KB to ~8 KB. Add contract tests for both shapes, like the subscribe ones. C. Leftovers: - editorPreferences.ts:61: use getServerConfig()?.availableEditors and fall back to getConfig only when it is null. - agentHandoff.ts:176-196: replace readDraftDefaults with readNewDraftDefaults({ cachedConfig: readEnvironmentServerConfig(env), requireFreshConfig: same rule as useHandleNewThread }), removing the duplicated logic. - Tests: the existing agentHandoff and editorPreferences unit tests, with getConfig mocks asserting it is not called when a live config exists. D. Optional, needs decision: persist the catalog cache on hosted and remote browsers and on mobile (ProviderCatalogStore over IndexedDB, or an MMKV/SQLite store on mobile). It would be opt-in or tied to the existing hosted cache opt-in, cleared on sign-out and account change.

Needs a decision

Part A changes how hosted Hub targets decide that config is current. It replaces a fresh scoped read with a generation- and attempt-gated per-connection value, which touches AGENTS.md hosted lifecycle ownership (stale generations must not publish state). Part D persists node-owned catalogs on non-loopback, hosted and mobile clients. The codebase deliberately keeps no copy there without asking (primaryShellCacheEligibility.ts), so that is a privacy and product decision. Parts B and C are plain contract-additive or local changes and need no decision.

Done#96 Every page load opens a second WebSocket and runs device.list (xcrun simctl) even if the simulator panel is never used

browser-measure:eager-device-socket-simctl · original impact Medium, effort M · Process spawns WP15

Current state

Confirmed DONE. A page load no longer opens /ws/device, requests a second ws-token or runs device.list/simctl. Commit 65af92766 made the client side lazy: connections only register the device client, thread views and the pane start a cheap device.subscribeEvents stream on the main /ws, and the pane lists on mount. /ws/device opens only for screenshots or for older servers. Commit 60633eff3 made the server side cheaper: a 2 s shared simctl listing, a 60 s xcode-select cache and a 5 min xcodebuild -version cache, so availability() plus discover() run simctl once. Both commits are in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3. Mobile does not create a device client. The only gap is a narrow behaviour regression: an agent's open-pane request is lost when no thread view has been mounted for more than 60 s.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:323-326 Connect only calls registerDeviceConnection, which starts nothing. The old unconditional bindDeviceConnection (f1be4abc7 connection.ts:281-283) is gone. reconnect (line 363) only bumps the generation and has no inventory wait.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/device/runtime.ts:22-62 bindDeviceConnection only subscribes to events. The f1be4abc7 version called refreshInventory() on bind and on every resubscribe.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/device/runtime.ts:112-183 registerDeviceConnection and ensureDeviceRuntime bind the stream only while something retains it, and unbind after DEVICE_RUNTIME_IDLE_MS = 60 s.
  • apps/web/src/components/routeViews/ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:127-131 Thread views retain the device runtime so they can consume device.open-pane-requested. DraftChatThreadRouteView.tsx:95 does the same.
  • apps/server/src/ws/deviceRpc.ts:122-135 subscribeEvents only registers a manager.onEvent listener. It spawns no simctl/xcode process, so retaining it from thread views is cheap.
  • apps/web/src/components/device/SimulatorPanel.tsx:209-224 Inventory (list plus getThreadState) is read only when the pane mounts or the generation changes. The pane is lazily gated in ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:1537.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/deviceRpcClient.ts:150-276 createDirectDeviceRpcTransport sends control RPCs and the event stream on the main socket. The dedicated /ws/device socket is opened lazily (dedicated ??= openDedicated()) only for requestBulk screenshots or after an 'Unknown request tag' fallback, and closes after 60 s idle.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:988-1011 The primary direct client opens /ws/device lazily. Saved environments do the same at service.ts:1159-1182, and hosted shares the main transport at service.ts:959. Mobile's createWsRpcClient calls pass no device client (apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:333, hostedHub/primaryConnection.ts:218).
  • apps/server/src/ws.ts:62-96 The main /ws route serves WsHostedRpcGroup with makeDeviceWsRpcLayer merged in. /ws/device (ws.ts:98-130) stays for older clients only.
  • apps/server/src/device/IosSimulatorBackend.ts:77-90,1055-1066,1119-1180 DEVICE_LISTING_REUSE_MS = 2 s shares the in-flight simctl listing promise, XCODE_SELECT_CACHE_MS = 60 s and XCODE_VERSION_CACHE_MS = 5 min. Boot refreshes the listing (518, fresh:true) and shutdown drops it (537). IosSimulatorBackend.probeCache.test.ts:50-87 asserts a single xcode-select/simctl.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/device/runtime.test.ts:30-123 Tests cover: no list on connect, nothing started before retain, idle unbind, and handover. deviceRpcClient.test.ts:75-159 covers no device socket for control, the older-server fallback and the screenshot-only dedicated socket.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/device/store.ts:159-181 Residual: clearEnvironment (run on idle unbind) drops pendingOpenByThreadKey. DeviceManager.requestOpenPane (apps/server/src/device/DeviceManager.ts:938-946) emits only to live listeners, so open-pane requests are lost while unbound.
Defects in the shipped fix

Low severity, a narrow behaviour regression and not a perf defect. Before the fix, the event stream was bound for the whole connection, so an agent's device.open-pane-requested for any thread was buffered in pendingOpenByThreadKey and the pane auto-opened when the user later navigated to that thread. Now the stream is bound only while a thread view or the pane retains the environment, and it unbinds 60 s after the last release. The unbind runs store.clearEnvironment (store.ts:159-181), which drops pending open requests. The server emits requestOpenPane to live listeners only (DeviceManager.ts:938-946). So a user who loads the app on, or stays more than 60 s on, a non-thread route (overview, settings) misses the auto-open for an agent's device action. The attachment itself is kept server-side and the pane shows it when opened manually. Out-of-scope notes, also on demand only: (a) on pane mount, list and getThreadState run Android discovery (emulator -list-avds, adb devices -l) twice concurrently with no dedup (AndroidEmulatorBackend.ts:327-329, availability is cached 5 s at 217-222). (b) DeviceManager.publish (1249-1255) runs a full availability plus listing snapshot on every agent activity start and end even with no subscribers, though the 2 s iOS listing reuse bounds it.

Implementation sketch

Optional, for the open-pane regression. Simplest option: since subscribeEvents now rides the main socket and spawns nothing (deviceRpc.ts:122-135), bind the event stream for the connection lifetime again. In registerDeviceConnection (runtime.ts:112-147), call bindRegistration immediately, and keep ensureDeviceRuntime only as a no-op or a ref for the pane. This restores buffering at the cost of one idle stream per connection. Alternative that keeps it lazy: in ensureDeviceRuntime's idle timer (runtime.ts:174-179), carry pendingOpenByThreadKey across clearEnvironment (have clearEnvironment take a keepPendingOpen flag). That still loses requests that arrive while unbound. Fully robust variant: on bind, have the server replay the latest unconsumed paneSurfacedUdid per thread through subscribeEvents (DeviceManager already stores paneSurfacedUdid in threadState at line 939). Emit device.open-pane-requested for threads whose surfaced udid has not been acknowledged; this needs a small ack or consume RPC. Tests: extend runtime.test.ts so an open-pane event delivered while no surface retains the environment is still consumable after a thread view retains it. For Android dedup (optional): cache AndroidEmulatorBackend.listDevices with a short shared-promise TTL, as in IosSimulatorBackend.listDevicesUnchecked, invalidated in boot and shutdown. Add a test that one pane-mount refresh (list plus getThreadState) spawns emulator -list-avds once.

Done#97 Lazy chunk graphs load as 3-4 sequential import levels, and the thread route chunk only starts after the shell snapshot

browser-measure:chunk-waterfalls-no-modulepreload · original impact Medium, effort M · Waterfall WP13

Current state

The fix removes the measured cost. The current web dist (built at HEAD, untracked) has 531 relative import() sites. 530 of them are wrapped by Vite's preload helper, and each one preloads its target's full static closure beyond what the host already loaded (0 uncovered, checked independently). The thread route import preloads 146 files, including ChatRightPanel. The statistics route import preloads useStatistics. index.html modulepreloads the boot chain. Deep-linked routes start their chunks in root beforeLoad alongside auth. The thread chunk starts at the WS welcome, before the shell-snapshot wait, or at idle after the shell paints. Proposals 1 and 3 are fully done, and 2 is done except for the '/' landing. One real defect is in the guard (proposal 4): the coverage regex only reads import() calls that are directly followed by the map. So it silently skips the .then()/async-wrapped forms, which are 147 of the 530 wrapped sites (129 distinct targets), including RootAppShell, SettingsPage, CommandPaletteDialog and every preloadableLazy dialog and settings panel.

Evidence
  • apps/web/vite.config.ts:211-217 build.modulePreload = { polyfill: false, resolveDependencies: resolveWebModulePreloadDependencies }. At f1be4abc7 it was modulePreload: false. createBootPreloadPlugin() is wired at :127. The Hub Dockerfile builds with this same config (VITE_RYCO_CLIENT_MODE=hosted-hub), and the vendored 7bc39eec3 contains 60633eff3, 3ce80cee6 and 451f35925.
  • apps/web/src/viteBuild/modulePreload.ts:22-28 For hostType 'js' the resolver returns all deps, so each dynamic import preloads its whole static closure in one round. HTML gets [], and the boot chain comes from bootPreloadTags (:38-83).
  • apps/web/dist/index.html:28-33 The built document has modulepreload for boot, rolldown-runtime, boot-vendor and main, plus a style preload for main CSS. The boot graph is flattened.
  • apps/web/dist/assets/boot-*.js (__vite__mapDeps table) Independent read-only analysis of every chunk: 531 relative import() sites, 530 helper-wrapped, 0 with closure files missing from the preload map. The only unwrapped site is worker -> wasm, inside a self-contained worker. ChatThreadRouteView preloads 146 files including ChatRightPanel. StatisticsRouteView preloads useStatistics. RootAppShell preloads 102 files. Worker chunks have no static imports, so no waterfall exists there.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:160-165 Outside /pair and native-authorize, beforeLoad starts RootAppShell/HostedHubRoot.preload() and preloadMatchedRouteChunks(pathname) (apps/web/src/lib/routeChunkPreload.ts:53-63) in parallel with auth. Deep links to a thread, draft, statistics or settings URL fetch the body chunk early.
  • apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:283-288 handleWelcome calls preloadRouteChunk(THREAD_ROUTE_ID) when the welcome names a bootstrap thread, before the awaited ensureEnvironmentConnectionBootstrapped at :290. The chunk now overlaps the snapshot instead of following the redirect.
  • apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:175-186 ShellIdlePreloads warms the thread and draft routes first. apps/web/src/lib/shellIdlePreload.ts:36-75 gates this on the primary-shell-painted phase (the cached shell from 45f7a9be6 can paint before the welcome) and skips it on save-data or <4g links.
  • scripts/perf/preloadCoverage.ts:51-52 Guard defect. PRELOADED_IMPORT requires `import("./x.js")` to be immediately followed by `,__vite__mapDeps([..])` or `,[]`. Vite emits `t(()=>import(`./RootAppShell-x.js`).then(e=>e.RootAppShell),__vite__mapDeps([..]))` and the async-destructuring form for named-export lazies, and the regex skips both. Against the current dist it reads 383 of 530 wrapped sites. The 'no readable import' fallback (bundleBudget.ts:131-137) does not fire because other imports parse.
  • scripts/perf/preloadCoverage.test.ts:33-46 The parser test covers only the bare `t(()=>import(x),map)` and `[]` shapes. It has no `.then(...)` or `async()=>{await import(x)}` case, so the gap is untested.
  • .github/workflows/_validation.yml:207-213 perf:bundle-budget, which includes the preload-depth check (scripts/perf/bundleBudget.ts:130-145), runs in CI on the standard build only. The hosted-hub build's preload maps are not checked.
Remaining

This does not block DONE. For the '/' landing the thread route chunk starts at the WS welcome (apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:286) or at idle after the shell paints (:180), not in root beforeLoad alongside auth (apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:160-165). The residual is about auth + ws-token + WS upgrade. During that window the link is already downloading the RootAppShell closure (~409 KB gzip), and modulePreload.ts:15-20 records that preloading later phases at document start delayed beforeLoad through contention. So this was a measured choice, not an omission.

Defects in the shipped fix

The preload-depth guard (proposal 4) has a coverage hole. scripts/perf/preloadCoverage.ts:51-52 only parses import() calls that are directly followed by the preload map. It skips Vite's `.then(...)` and async-destructuring wrappers: 147 of 530 helper-wrapped import sites (129 distinct targets) in the current build. These include RootAppShell, SettingsPage, PhoneHome, HostedHubRoot, CommandPaletteDialog, ForkThreadDialog, AutomationsDialog, OnboardingDialog, all settings sub-panels and the ChatRightPanel lazies. Today all of them are fully covered, so users see no regression. But if one of those closures loses coverage, for example from a different resolveDependencies filter or a rolldown chunking change, the measured 3-5 level waterfall comes back on the shell and settings graphs and CI stays green. The test file has no case for these shapes.

Implementation sketch

Guard fix only (scripts/perf/preloadCoverage.ts plus its test). (1) Replace the single PRELOADED_IMPORT regex with a two-step parse. Match each relative `import(`./X.js`)`. Then scan forward, bounded by the next `import(` or a balanced-paren walk from the preload helper call, for the first `__vite__mapDeps([..])` or `,[])` that closes the same wrapper call. Attribute that map to the import. This covers `t(()=>import(x),map)`, `t(()=>import(x).then(e=>e.Y),map)` and `t(async()=>{const{a}=await import(x);return{a}},map)`. (2) Make format drift fail loudly. Count every relative import() in chunks that carry an `m.f=` table, and add a violation if any of them is neither parsed as preload-managed nor on an explicit allowlist (worker chunks, imports Vite leaves alone), instead of only failing when zero imports parse. (3) In preloadCoverage.test.ts, add parser cases for the `.then(e=>e.X)` and async-destructuring shapes copied from real dist output (for example the RootAppShell and SettingsPage call sites in boot-*.js), and a coverage case where a `.then`-form import misses a level and is reported. (4) Optionally run perf:bundle-budget against a hosted-hub build too, or document that only standard is guarded. Validate with `bun run test scripts/perf/preloadCoverage.test.ts`, then run `bun run perf:bundle-budget` on a RYCO_WEB_SOURCEMAP=hidden standard build: it should report 530 checked imports and 0 uncovered. Optional and separate: preloadRouteChunk('/_chat/$environmentId/$threadId') in resolveRootBeforeLoadContext for pathname '/' on non-phone tiers. Gate it on allowsSpeculativePreload() and measure contention against root-before-load-ready first. No thread id is needed because the chunk is the same for every thread.
