Partial#98 The idle SettingsPage prefetch has no measurable benefit and competes with the critical path on slow links

browser-measure:settings-idle-prefetch-competes · original impact Low, effort S · Bundle size WP12B

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor says the lazy section bodies shrank the old 4-level, about 200 KB graph. They did not. At f1be4abc7 the section bodies were already React.lazy (SettingsPage.tsx:237-285), and the old idle preload never pulled them. preloadSettingsPage still pulls the same static graph: SettingsRouteView -> SettingsPage -> SettingsPanels -> ProjectDefaultsSection -> ProjectPreferenceSettings -> TraitsPicker, plus LifecycleSettings -> lifecycleSuggestionPolicy. Only the timing, the gating and the value of the preload changed. The auditor also takes at face value the doc claim that the per-task idle periods mean none of the preloads competes with the first thread render. requestIdleCallback tracks main-thread idleness, not network idleness, and every task returns before its download finishes. So the thread, palette and settings downloads all start within a few frames of each other. The proposal's 'plus the first thread render' deferral is not implemented.

Current state

PR #710 (60633eff3) removed the boot-time requestIdleCallback(preloadSettingsPage) from SettingsRouteBridge. It added a hover/focus intent preload on the Settings button and moved the speculative preload into ShellIdlePreloads. That scheduler gates on saveData and effectiveType, starts at primary-shell-painted or a 5 s cap, and runs settings last. The route loader now awaits the lazyRouteComponent, so a warmed chunk is no longer wasted by the Suspense reveal throttle. In the common case the preload no longer overlaps the WS shell snapshot. Three gaps remain. (1) The payload is unchanged: about 210 KB raw / 69 KB gz beyond the shell, thread and palette chunks in today's dist. (2) The idle tasks are fire-and-forget, so the downloads are not serialized and the settings graph still downloads alongside the thread route chunk and the thread detail. (3) The 5 s start cap is unconditional, so on a slow link whose shell snapshot lands after 5 s, every preload starts before the snapshot. The NetInfo gate does not cover these cases: Safari and Firefox lack navigator.connection, and Chromium most likely reports '4g' for the report's 150 ms / 1.6 Mbps profile. All of this is low impact.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/SettingsRouteBridge.tsx:27-80 The boot-time requestIdleCallback(preloadSettingsPage, {timeout:4000}) effect (f1be4abc7 lines 33-43) is gone. Removed in 60633eff3.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarChrome.tsx:86-89 Intent preload as proposed: the Settings button calls preloadSettingsPage on onPointerEnter and onFocus.
  • apps/web/src/settingsRoute.ts:21-30 SettingsRouteComponent is a lazyRouteComponent shared with the route, and preloadSettingsPage warms that same component. routes/settings.tsx:29-30 awaits the loader and the component, so no Suspense reveal throttle applies and an earlier preload is not wasted.
  • apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:175-185 ShellIdlePreloads skips the phone tier and orders the tasks: thread and draft route chunks, then the palette, then settings. Every task is fire-and-forget ('void preloadRouteChunk', and preloadCommandPaletteDialog / preloadSettingsPage return void), so nothing waits for the previous download.
  • apps/web/src/lib/shellIdlePreload.ts:49-58 runFrom calls the task synchronously and then immediately schedules the next idle callback. The downloads overlap on the network, which contradicts the doc claim at lines 29-34 that none competes 'with the first thread render'.
  • apps/web/src/lib/shellIdlePreload.ts:25-26,68-69 The comment says the 5 s cap is for sessions without a primary shell (hosted-static), but the cap timer is armed for every session. If the live shell snapshot arrives more than 5 s after RootAppShell mounts, which is plausible at 1.6 Mbps, all preloads start before it.
  • apps/web/src/lib/shellIdlePreload.ts:15-23 The gate checks only saveData and effectiveType === '4g', and returns true when navigator.connection is missing (Safari, Firefox). Chromium's DevTools/CDP emulation most likely derives effectiveType from RTT alone (>= ~272 ms is 3g), so the report's 150 ms RTT / 1.6 Mbps profile reads as '4g' and is not gated.
  • apps/web/src/components/settings/SettingsPage.tsx:73 SettingsPanels (72 KB raw in dist) is still statically imported, and through it ProjectDefaultsSection -> ProjectPreferenceSettings -> TraitsPicker and LifecycleSettings -> lifecycleSuggestionPolicy.

Largest: SettingsPanels 72 KB, api 66 KB, SettingsPage 42 KB, lifecycleSuggestionPolicy 12 KB. That matches the finding's ~200 KB raw, so the payload is unchanged. The server now serves precompressed assets (apps/server/src/http.ts:270-299), so it costs about 0.35 s of link time at 1.6 Mbps.
  • apps/web/src/lib/shellIdlePreload.test.ts:38-62 The tests cover phase gating, ordering of synchronous calls and the cap firing when the shell never paints. They do not test download serialization or a late-painting shell.
Remaining

(a) Download serialization: apps/web/src/lib/shellIdlePreload.ts:49-58 and RootAppShell.tsx:178-185 fire each preload without awaiting it. The settings graph (about 69 KB gz) still overlaps the thread/draft route chunk download and the thread detail stream on bootstrap-redirect and thread-URL boots. (b) The proposal's 'first thread render' deferral is not implemented. Start is gated only on primary-shell-painted (the sidebar). (c) The unconditional 5 s cap (shellIdlePreload.ts:68) lets preloads start before the shell snapshot on slow links where the NetInfo gate (lines 15-23) does not apply: Safari, Firefox, or Chromium reporting '4g' at about 150 ms RTT with low bandwidth.

Defects in the shipped fix

The doc comment at shellIdlePreload.ts:29-34 claims the per-task idle periods keep the preloads from competing with the first thread render. The code does not enforce that, because the tasks return before their downloads finish. The cap comment at line 25 scopes the cap to hosted-static sessions, but line 68 arms it for every session. Neither is a correctness bug. Both are performance gaps against the stated intent.

Implementation sketch

1) apps/web/src/lib/shellIdlePreload.ts: change the task type to () => void | Promise<unknown>. In runFrom, await the task's promise, capped by a per-task timeout (e.g. 8 s via Promise.race, catch-all), before calling scheduleIdleTask for the next index. Check the cancelled flag after the await. Make preloadSettingsPage (settingsRoute.ts) and preloadCommandPaletteDialog (CommandPalette.tsx) return their preload promise; the void callers in SidebarChrome are unaffected. In RootAppShell.tsx ShellIdlePreloads, have task 1 return Promise.all([preloadRouteChunk(THREAD_ROUTE_ID), preloadRouteChunk(DRAFT_ROUTE_ID)]). 2) Add an option like scheduleShellIdlePreloads(tasks, { startCapMs }). From ShellIdlePreloads, pass 5_000 only when no primary shell is expected (authGateState hosted-static, or getPrimaryKnownEnvironment() null). Otherwise pass a long safety cap (e.g. 30_000). 3) Optional: also wait for a 'first-thread-painted' phase when the initial route is a thread route. Add a StartupPhase marked from ChatThreadRouteView's first committed thread detail (layout effect plus markStartupPhaseAfterPaint), and start on that phase or on primary-shell-painted when no thread is routed. 4) Optional: tighten allowsSpeculativePreload to also return false when connection.downlink < ~2 (Mbps) or connection.rtt > ~250. Serialization (1) remains the main protection for browsers without NetInfo. Tests: extend shellIdlePreload.test.ts so that a task returning a pending promise blocks the next task until it resolves or the per-task timeout passes; with startCapMs 30_000 nothing runs at 5 s before primary-shell-painted; allowsSpeculativePreload({effectiveType:'4g', downlink:1.5}) is false. Manual check: scripts/perf/browserProbe at 150 ms / 1.6 Mbps should show the SettingsPage chunk request starting only after the ChatThreadRouteView chunk response ends.

Done#99 vcs.listRefs is sent twice with an identical payload on every thread open (prefetch and watcher race)

browser-measure:duplicate-listrefs · original impact Low, effort S · Caching

Current state

Fixed in 60633eff3 (#710). The prefetch and the watcher's first-page load now go through fetchFirstBranchesPage, which joins any in-flight first-page promise for the same environmentId/cwd/query key. A thread open (the prefetch effect runs, then the useGitBranches watcher effect in the same commit) now sends one vcs.listRefs. The poller runs input.run in a microtask after creation, so the watcher always joins the pending prefetch RPC. A recreated watcher also adopts a list fetched within the 15 s stale time (runImmediately: !adoptCached), so ChatView remounts no longer refetch. Nothing in the web client duplicates this on thread open: every other listRefs caller is a dialog or a one-off search with a different payload. The 'same pattern for status prefetches' part of the proposal does not apply. Git status is a refcounted stream keyed per cwd/view/interval, there is no status prefetch, and refreshStatus already has a keyed in-flight map. I looked for regressions in the fix and found none.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/rpc/gitAtoms.ts:232 branchesFirstPageInFlight replaces the removed prefetch-only branchesPrefetchInFlight Set (deleted in 60633eff3).
  • apps/web/src/rpc/gitAtoms.ts:265-286 fetchFirstBranchesPage returns the pending promise or registers a new one. A read detached by invalidation or reset reports fetchedAt null.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/gitAtoms.ts:329-345 loadInitialBranchesNow (watcher first load via pollBranches) goes through the shared fetch.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/gitAtoms.ts:604-641 prefetchBranchesByKey bails if a first page is in flight or a controller exists. Otherwise it uses the shared fetch and discards its own publish when a controller appeared meanwhile (the controller publishes the same result).
  • apps/web/src/lib/visibilityPolling.ts:44-58,74 refresh() calls run via Promise.resolve().then(run): a microtask after watchBranches. The prefetch RPC is still pending then, so the watcher joins it.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/gitAtoms.ts:531-580 A recreated watcher adopts a fresh cached list and skips the immediate run.
  • apps/web/src/components/BranchToolbarBranchSelector.tsx:242-258 This is the only prefetchBranches caller. The prefetch effect is declared before useGitBranches (useGit.ts:60 useEffect), and both use the same key: query '' with the initial deferred query ''.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/gitAtoms.test.ts:200-218 The test asserts one listRefs for prefetch plus watcher of the same key. It runs in the node environment without window, so it covers the no-poller path, but the poller path only adds a microtask.
  • apps/web/src/lib/gitStatusState.ts:80,137-167,262-265 Status is a refcounted stream subscription and refreshStatus has a keyed in-flight map. There is no status prefetch, so the proposal's status remark does not apply.
Defects in the shipped fix

None that regress or reintroduce the duplicate. Minor notes, not defects: (1) Joiners now share a failure: if the shared first-page read fails, the watcher shows the error until the next 60 s poll or a lifecycle/focus refresh. Before, it made its own attempt, which would normally have failed the same way. (2) An invalidation during the initial load drops the shared in-flight entry, but the poller's own inFlight dedupe (visibilityPolling.ts:47) still swallows the controller's refresh, so the pre-change list can stay up to 60 s. This predates the fix (the old code behaved the same way) and only matters if a branch mutation runs during the first load. (3) The dedupe unit test does not exercise the browser poller path.

Done#100 Layout effects with no dependencies force synchronous style/layout after every commit (getAnimations, getBoundingClientRect, getClientRects)

browser-measure:layout-effect-forced-layout · original impact Low, effort S · Rendering

Current state

Confirmed DONE. The fix landed in 60633eff3 (#710) for useFlipLayout and useInboxListMotion, and in 46b9772ee for ContextWindowMeter. useFlipLayout's trigger effect now has [ref, trigger] deps. A per-commit effect only compares the container element, and resting rects come from one ResizeObserver and one MutationObserver per element, so the old per-commit getAnimations/getBoundingClientRect and observer recreation are gone. A browser test spies on both APIs across five no-op rerenders and asserts neither is called. useInboxListMotion reads row offsets only when the order signature changed or a list ResizeObserver marked positions dirty. ContextWindowMeter's tick now lives in the popup body, which mounts only while the popup is open, and it fires at relative-label granularity. I found no regression in the fix. Remaining issues are cosmetic or edge cases. (1) useFlipLayout's ResizeObserver never unobserves FlipItem spans that were removed, so detached spans stay retained until the row changes or unmounts. (2) Resting rects are viewport-relative and refresh only on row resize or DOM mutation. If the row moves without either (the hero's mount slide-in, or the hero re-centering when the composer grows), the next location change glides from a few px off. The old code had the same weakness, because NewThreadWorkLocation rarely commits in those situations. (3) A display:none inbox still calls getClientRects on each commit. (4) useInboxListMotion has no test for the new skip path. (5) A sibling per-commit getBoundingClientRect exists in ModelTuningDial's useAnimatedHeight, scoped to the open model picker.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/useFlipLayout.ts:26-69 The trigger effect has deps [ref, trigger] and returns early when Object.is(triggerRef.current, trigger). getAnimations and getBoundingClientRect run only on a real trigger change. Previously (f1be4abc7:23-70) it ran with no deps and called recordResting after every commit.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/useFlipLayout.ts:74-88 The only per-commit effect is an identity compare, observedRef.current?.container === container. Observers are disposed on a container change and on unmount. The verifier's point about the old no-deps useEffect recreating the ResizeObserver on every commit is fixed.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/useFlipLayout.ts:91-116 observeResting records once, then on ResizeObserver callbacks (container and items) and MutationObserver callbacks (childList, subtree, characterData; attributes excluded). observeSizes re-observes on every mutation, which is a no-op for targets already observed in Chromium and Gecko, but it never unobserves removed items. Detached FlipItem spans, for example the 'branch' and 'preposition' slots that toggle with location.kind, are kept by the observer until the container changes or unmounts. The leak is small and bounded.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/useFlipLayout.ts:122-136 recordResting still calls getAnimations() per item (the WeakSet idea from the proposal was not done), but only from observer callbacks or a trigger change, where layout is usually fresh. Negligible.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/useFlipLayout.browser.tsx:33-62 The test 'reads no layout on commits that leave the row untouched' spies on Element.prototype.getBoundingClientRect and getAnimations across five rerenders that change only a data-* attribute, and asserts zero calls. A second test checks that a trigger change still glides moved and new items.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:5883-5889 The hero wrapper mounts with 'animate-in fade-in slide-in-from-bottom-1', a 4px translateY over about 150ms, and is laid out as a vertically centred block with the composer. observeResting's first record() and the ResizeObserver's first callback both run during this ancestor transform. Re-centring when the composer grows changes neither the row's size nor its DOM. Resting rects are viewport-relative (getBoundingClientRect), so they can be a few px stale until the row mutates or resizes. The pre-fix code had the same exposure, because NewThreadWorkLocation (prompt not in DraftSessionState) seldom commits in these cases. This is cosmetic, not a regression.
  • apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/useInboxListMotion.ts:131-161 The list ResizeObserver refreshes row tops inside its callback, where layout is already computed. If the list is hidden it marks positions dirty instead. The list is a content-sized relative div (InboxSidebar.tsx:276-281), so a row height change resizes it and fires the observer.
  • apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/useInboxListMotion.ts:178-203 The per-commit effect returns before any layout read when enabled, the signature is unchanged and positions are not dirty. With motion disabled, !input.enabled short-circuits before getClientRects, so there is no read either. Remaining edge case: when the effects run while the list is display:none, signatureRef stays null, so line 197 calls list.getClientRects() on every commit. Hidden panes torn down by Activity do not reach this.
  • apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/InboxSidebar.browser.tsx No test asserts that useInboxListMotion skips offsetTop reads on non-reordering commits, or that a reorder after a row resize glides from the refreshed positions.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ContextWindowMeter.tsx:288-310 ContextWindowDetails mounts only inside PopoverPopup (lines 481-496) and uses useRelativeLabelTick over contextWindowLabelInstants. Before the fix (f1be4abc7:91), the always-mounted meter called useRelativeTimeTick() with a 1 s tick.
  • apps/web/src/components/settings/settingsLayout.tsx:59-83 useRelativeLabelTick is visibility-aware and schedules through relativeLabelRefreshDelayMs (timestampFormat.ts:192-207). It ticks at 1 s only while a future instant is under a minute away, otherwise at the next minute boundary plus 25 ms.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ModelTuningDial.tsx:547-565 A sibling of the same pattern. useAnimatedHeight calls getBoundingClientRect() in a no-deps useLayoutEffect after every commit of ModelTuningDial. It is mounted only in the open model picker footer, so its impact is low and it is outside this finding's scope.
Defects in the shipped fix

None in the core fix. Minor follow-ups only: (a) useFlipLayout.ts:97-103, the ResizeObserver never unobserves removed [data-flip-id] items, so detached FlipItem spans stay retained until the row changes or unmounts. (b) useFlipLayout.ts resting rects are viewport-relative and refresh only on row resize or mutation. When the row moves without either (the hero slide-in at ChatView.tsx:5888, or the hero re-centring as the composer grows), the next location change adds a small spurious vertical glide. This weakness predates the fix and is not a regression. (c) useInboxListMotion.ts:197, a display:none-but-effect-live inbox still forces getClientRects on each commit. (d) No unit or browser test covers the useInboxListMotion skip path.

Partial#101 agentControl.subscribeProposals and automationCentre are requested on every load even when Agent Control is disabled (failing RPC plus console warning)

browser-measure:disabled-agent-control-subscription · original impact Low, effort S · Other WP12A

Current state

PARTIAL is correct. #710 (60633eff3) added a per-environment config gate (agentControlSyncGate.ts) and applied it to MissedAutomationRunsNotice, AgentControlApprovals and useAutomationCentre. The sidebar Automations badge (useWaitingAutomationRuns) is still ungated. It mounts on every desktop-tier load and on every route, /settings included, so a default node (agentControl.enabled defaults to false) still gets the refused agentControl.subscribeProposals and the 'WebSocket RPC subscription failed' warning on every load. The auditor missed three things. (1) The Automations dialog also sends an ungated agentControl.listProposals per checkout device, through useLapsedScheduleProposals and retainScheduleProposalHistory. (2) The gate admits environments whose config is unknown, and at cold boot the primary config is always unknown when the boot-mounted gated caller first subscribes. So even with every caller gated, the refused subscribeProposals still goes out once per cold boot. Only later mounts are saved. (3) Read from the code, not reproduced: the shared retain registry keeps a refused, dead subscription entry alive while the ungated sidebar holds it. When the user then turns Agent Control on, the gated callers re-retain that dead entry and no new stream opens. Approval cards, the waiting badge and missed-run notices stay empty until reload. That breaks the gate's documented 're-admits on enable' behaviour.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/agent-control/agentControlSyncGate.ts:31-58 The gate from 60633eff3. It excludes only environments whose config says enabled === false (lines 55-56). Unknown (null) config is admitted. The primary's flag comes from useServerConfigSelector (line 35), which also honours SettingsTargetProvider. That is latent only: no gated caller renders inside a settings target today.
  • apps/web/src/components/automations/useWaitingAutomationRuns.ts:17-23 Still ungated: useAutomationProposalSync(environmentIds) runs over every connected environment. The file is byte-identical to f1be4abc7 and to the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarPrimaryActions.tsx:67,130,196 showAutomations = automationsCapability.allowed && !phone. The capability is always allowed outside hosted mode (client-runtime authorization/capabilities.ts:43). AutomationsEntry calls useWaitingAutomationRuns() unconditionally.
  • apps/web/src/components/AppSidebarLayout.tsx:297-310 ThreadSidebar (Sidebar.tsx:1484 mounts SidebarPrimaryActions) is rendered on every desktop-tier route, including the /settings page where Agent Control is enabled. The ungated retainer is therefore held throughout.
  • apps/web/src/components/automations/data/useAutomationProposalSync.ts:35-37,88-99 retainAgentControlProposalSync reuses an existing entry and only increments count (line 98). bindEnvironmentProposalSync rebinds only when the connection's client object changes (line 37). A subscription refused by the server, which wsTransport.ts:381-394 does not retry, stays dead for the life of the entry. Later retainers (the gated callers after the feature is turned on) get no stream.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/agentControl/sync.ts:50-62 On a terminal refusal, onError clears the environment's queue, and nothing triggers a resubscribe. A settings change does not replace the client.
  • apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:90,100 + apps/web/src/components/ServerStateBootstrap.tsx:22-25 + packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/serverState.ts:63,162-171 serverConfigAtom starts as null with no hydration. It is filled only by startServerStateSync, which starts in an effect in the same commit in which the primary connection first appears. MissedAutomationRunsNotices sees the primary with a null config, the gate admits it, and subscribeProposals is sent next to subscribeConfig. The refusal goes out on every cold boot whatever the gating.
  • apps/web/src/components/automations/data/useLapsedScheduleProposals.ts:156-165 + apps/web/src/components/automations/data/scheduleProposalHistory.ts:131-150 Missed by the auditor. The Automations dialog (AutomationsDialog.tsx:283) retains schedule history for every checkout environment, and that calls agentControl.listProposals ungated. A disabled server refuses it (AgentControlProposalService getQueue requires enabled). The failure is swallowed and retried on the next hold.
  • apps/web/src/components/automations/data/useProjectAutomations.tsx:67 Ungated useAutomationProposalSync([environmentId]) runs when the dialog opens. It cannot simply be removed: useProjectAutomations.browser.tsx:266-272 mocks useAutomationCentre and asserts this retain. Gate it instead.
  • apps/web/src/components/automations/data/useAutomationProjectCounts.ts:15-25 Ungated automationCentre.snapshot for every checkout, only when the project switcher asks. Minor.
  • apps/web/src/components/automations/useAutomationCentre.ts:78,89,140 Gated correctly. When off it reads nothing and holds no retain. The useAutomationCentre.browser.tsx:114-128 test covers re-admission only with no other retainer mounted.
  • packages/contracts/src/settings.ts:509 AgentControlSettings.enabled defaults to false, so the default install is the affected configuration.
Remaining

1. apps/web/src/components/automations/useWaitingAutomationRuns.ts:19. The sidebar badge subscribes ungated on every desktop load, so the refused subscribeProposals and its console.warn persist. It also holds a dead entry that stops the gated callers from reopening the stream when Agent Control is turned on, until the page is reloaded. 2. apps/web/src/components/automations/data/useProjectAutomations.tsx:67: ungated retain on dialog open. 3. apps/web/src/components/automations/data/useLapsedScheduleProposals.ts:161, which calls scheduleProposalHistory.ts:131-150: ungated agentControl.listProposals per checkout device on dialog open. 4. apps/web/src/components/automations/data/useAutomationProjectCounts.ts:19: ungated automationCentre.snapshot from the switcher (minor). 5. The gate admits unknown config (agentControlSyncGate.ts:55), and the primary config is always null at cold boot. MissedAutomationRunsNotice therefore still sends one refused subscribeProposals per cold boot even after items 1-4 are fixed. The finding's '-1 failing stream RPC per load' needs either deferral while config is pending, or acceptance of the boot-time attempt. 6. Robustness: useAutomationProposalSync.ts:88-99 never rebinds a refused entry, so any retainer held across a refusal blocks re-admission.

Defects in the shipped fix

The gate code is correct for what it checks. Its documented promise, 'turning the feature on re-admits the environment', fails in the real app. The shared retain registry (useAutomationProposalSync.ts:88-99) keeps the refused subscription's entry alive while the ungated sidebar retainer holds it, and bindEnvironmentProposalSync rebinds only on a client change (line 37). After the user turns Agent Control on in Settings (the sidebar stays mounted on /settings), MissedAutomationRunsNotice, AgentControlApprovals and useAutomationCentre re-retain the dead entry and no stream opens. Chat approval cards, the waiting badge and missed-run notices stay empty until reload, and proposals can expire unseen. This is derived from the code and was not reproduced. It is pre-existing from f1be4abc7 and was not fixed by #710. Separately, the boot-time attempt is not prevented because the primary config is null when the boot-mounted gated caller subscribes. Latent: the gate reads the primary flag through useServerConfigSelector, which follows SettingsTargetProvider, so inside a ProjectNodeSettingsScope it would read the targeted node's flag as the primary's. No gated caller renders there today.

Implementation sketch

1. useWaitingAutomationRuns.ts: `const syncIds = useAgentControlSyncEnvironmentIds(environmentIds); useAutomationProposalSync(syncIds);`. Keep the waiting-count selector on environmentIds. 2. useProjectAutomations.tsx:67: `const ids = useMemo(() => [environmentId], [environmentId]); useAutomationProposalSync(useAgentControlSyncEnvironmentIds(ids));`. Unknown config in the browser fixtures still retains, so useProjectAutomations.browser.tsx:266-272 keeps passing. 3. useLapsedScheduleProposals.ts:157-165: build environmentsKey from useAgentControlSyncEnvironmentIds(checkout environment ids) so retainScheduleProposalHistory (listProposals) skips disabled devices. 4. useAutomationProjectCounts.ts: use the gate hook over the checkouts' environment ids and drop disabled checkouts in `request` before loader.request. 5. Make re-admission robust whatever the callers do. In bindEnvironmentProposalSync, pass onError to startAgentControlProposalSync and mark the binding refused (reset currentClient and stopSync). In retainAgentControlProposalSync, when a new retainer finds a refused entry, stop it and bind again, for example with an entry.rebind(). Alternatively, give the entry a refused flag that retain checks. 6. Small and optional: in agentControlSyncGate.ts, read the primary flag with useEnvironmentServerConfigSelector(primaryEnvironmentId, selector) or the serverConfigAtom directly, not the settings-target-aware useServerConfigSelector. 7. Optional, needs owner sign-off (see decisionReason). Treat 'connected but config not yet known' as pending, not admitted. Every connection kind supplies a config: the primary through ServerStateBootstrap, saved and Hub connections through onConfigUpdated into the runtime store (environments/runtime/service.ts:1350-1360,1552-1590). The gate can then exclude environments whose config is null while a connection exists, which removes the per-cold-boot refusal at the cost of one config round trip of approval latency. Tests: (a) a browser test that mounts AutomationsEntry or useWaitingAutomationRuns with primary config enabled:false and expects zero subscribeProposals, then flips to true and expects exactly one; (b) in useAutomationProposalSync.test.ts, retain, fire onError (refused), retain again, and expect a second subscribeProposals; (c) a lapsed-history test expecting no listProposals for a disabled device. Run focused vitest on those files plus the touched *.browser.tsx files with bun run --cwd apps/web test:browser.

Done#102 The WS connection and thread-window subscription only start after React commits RootAppShell / ChatView

browser-measure:connection-and-thread-data-start-late · original impact Low, effort M · Waterfall WP11

Current state

Both late starts are fixed at HEAD. The root beforeLoad now prefetches the ws-token alongside the session check. Once the session is authenticated, it opens the primary connection, and with it the shell subscription, while the RootAppShell chunk is still loading. This happens only in standard mode, so hosted Hub ownership is respected. The RootAppShell effect stays the idempotent owner: createPrimaryEnvironmentConnection returns the registered connection, so no duplicate is built. The thread route loader retains the thread detail subscription synchronously at navigation time. A retain taken before the connection exists is deferred via watch/attach and starts on register. Sidebar and inbox press/hover intents and the welcome bootstrap-thread redirect retain early as well. On a cold deep link the window request now overlaps the shell snapshot instead of waiting for it, which is better than the finding asked for. One minor defect is in the press/hover intent extension. An intent retain is released with {immediately:true} after 10 s. Its doc comment assumes the route's navigation retain is still held then, but ChatThreadRouteView releases that retain as soon as ChatView mounts. So a never-loaded thread that the user opens and leaves within about 10 s is disposed at the intent deadline instead of entering the 5-minute idle cache. The store keeps the detail, so a revisit still renders immediately. The cost is a fresh window snapshot (not a resume) and no live detail events in the meantime. Impact is low.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:163 RootAppShell.preload() and the matched route chunks start at the top of beforeLoad, so the early connect below overlaps the shell chunk download.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:249-256 The ws-token prefetch overlaps ensurePrimaryEnvironmentReady and the session check. If authenticated and not a native-authorize path, startPrimaryConnectionEarly() runs; otherwise the prefetched token is discarded. Hosted-hub and hosted-static return earlier (lines 197-226), so hosted lifecycle ownership is not touched.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:342-348 startPrimaryConnectionEarly dynamically imports the runtime and calls connectPrimaryEnvironment().
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1282-1285 createPrimaryEnvironmentConnection returns the already registered connection, so start() -> connectPrimary() (supervision.ts:1235, 894-905) re-uses the early connection and builds no candidate to dispose.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:258 subscribeShell is issued at connection creation, so the shell snapshot request also moves into beforeLoad.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.ts:179-210,303-311 The prefetched ws-token is consumed by the first socket attempt within a max age; a failure or stale result falls back to a normal request.
  • apps/web/src/routes/_chat.$environmentId.$threadId.tsx:17-30 The non-preload loader calls prewarmThreadDetailSubscription. onEnter, onStay and onLeave release superseded retains. preloadStaleTime is 0 so hover preloads do not replace the navigation's loader run.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:540-551,695-701,805-808 attach() subscribes as soon as the connection exists, even before the shell snapshot (isMissingFromShell is false while the shell set is undefined). Without a connection, watch() defers until register(). On a cold deep link the window request therefore no longer waits for bootstrapComplete, which gated ChatView before.
  • apps/web/src/components/routeViews/ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:149-156 The navigation retain is released (non-immediately) once canRenderRouteThread is true and ChatView holds its view retain (ChatView.tsx:2750).
  • apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:283-288 On a / boot, the welcome bootstrap-thread redirect also prewarms the thread subscription (non-hosted only).
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/threadNavigationIntent.ts:15-35 Press/hover intents (SidebarThreadRow.tsx:459/471, InboxThreadRow.tsx:379/386) retain the detail subscription before navigation, which extends proposal 2.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/threadNavigationIntent.logic.ts:62-70,85-91 Defect: the intent retain is released with {immediately:true} at its 10 s deadline. The comment says the route's navigation retain is 'held as long', but that retain is dropped when ChatView mounts (ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:155) or when the route settles elsewhere.
Defects in the shipped fix

Minor: the sidebar/inbox navigation intent (apps/web/src/components/sidebar/threadNavigationIntent.logic.ts:85-91) releases its retain with {immediately:true} 10 s after a press or hover dwell. It assumes the route's navigation retain still holds the subscription (comment at lines 62-70). That retain is actually released once ChatView mounts (ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:155) or when the route settles elsewhere. Scenario: the user presses a never-loaded thread A, reads it for 3 s, then opens B. A's ChatView releases normally, so refCount drops to 1 (intent only). At t+10 s the intent releases immediately, and supervision.ts:880 calls disposeByKey(A) instead of scheduling the 5-minute idle eviction. A revisit within 5 minutes still renders from the store (selectThreadDetailLoaded stays true), but it re-requests a full window snapshot rather than resuming, and A gets no live detail events in between. History pagination state is also invalidated. Users mostly won't see it; the cost is extra network and server work when flipping quickly through new threads. Separately, start() calls resetProviderInvalidation() (supervision.ts:1229) after the early connection may already have flagged an invalidation, so that flag is dropped. At boot there are no checkpoint-diff or project-search caches to invalidate, so this is a latent ordering quirk with no user-visible effect.

Implementation sketch

Only the minor intent defect needs work. Option A, preferred because it stays in the supervisor: in packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts retain(), record viewedSinceRetain per retain handle. Either set a local flag when entry.viewCount rises while this handle is outstanding, or store entry.lastViewedAt (updated on each view retain and view release) and capture retainedAt = input.now() at retain time. In the returned release, change the immediate path to `if (options?.immediately === true && shouldEvict(entry) && !(entry.lastViewedAt >= retainedAt)) { disposeByKey(key); return; }`; otherwise fall through to reconcileEntry plus evictToCapacity. Then an intent or prewarm that actually led to a view hands the stream to the normal idle cache, while a dwell, scroll or drag without navigation is still disposed immediately. useSidebarThreadPrewarm's immediate releases get the same semantics. Option B, web-only: extend ThreadNavigationIntentDeps with wasViewedSince(ref, sinceMs), backed by a supervisor read, and release with { immediately: !wasViewed }. Also fix the comment in threadNavigationIntent.logic.ts:62-70. Tests: add a supervision unit test (retain -> retain {view:true} -> release view -> release {immediately:true} must leave the entry with an eviction timer; retain -> release {immediately:true} with no view must dispose). Optionally add an apps/web service.threadSubscriptions test that drives noteThreadPressIntent, a view retain and release, and fake timers past THREAD_NAVIGATION_INTENT_RETAIN_MS, asserting the window subscription is not unsubscribed. Validation: focused vitest runs for client-runtime supervision and the web sidebar intent/prewarm tests only.

Done#103 Every orchestration stream sends one RPC Chunk per event and waits for an Ack round trip (Stream.tap/mapEffect de-chunk)

client-runtime-sync:rpc-streams-one-chunk-per-event · original impact High, effort M · Network / RTT WP09

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The DONE status holds for the orchestration streams, and I checked every combinator on them. The auditor's 'no fix defects that matter' is too strong, though. The same one-Chunk-plus-Ack-per-event mechanism is still live in a sibling relayed stream, subscribeTerminalEvents (Stream.tap at apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.ts:280 and :285). No other finding in the report covers it. Separately, mobile still commits thread-detail events to the store one at a time. Neither changes the status of this orchestration-scoped finding.

Current state

Fixed in 60633eff3 (#710), which also ships in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3. The shell, thread and thread-window pipelines are now chunk-preserving end to end, checked against effect 4.0.2. Replay pages leave as one array per page (fromIterable on an Array is fromArray). Live batches drain through fromQueue, which uses Queue.takeAll. The shell mapping is batch-level mapArrayEffect and also collapses repeated per-thread upserts. Ledger and metrics run through tapArray, dedupe uses Stream.filter (filterArray), and rechunkByBudget uses chunks+flatMap, so arrays are never merged. History recovery is mapArrayEffect (with a test asserting array sizes [1,3,1,1]). The perf taps are observeArrays and the RPC instrumentation is onExit only. Thread chunks are capped at 256 KiB and 1000 items; shell chunks at 128 items. The tests show that 1000 replayed events take at most ceil(bytes/256KiB)+1 chunks, that 500 shell events take 2 chunks, and that 200 live events queued during one held ack take at most 2 chunks. On the client, wsTransport.subscribe and requestStream use runForEachArray, and web batches shell and thread-detail items into one store commit per frame. Residual items are outside this finding's scope. The terminal event stream still de-chunks per event (same mechanism). Mobile applies thread-detail events one commit per event. Shell chunks are capped by count, not bytes. Thread priorities still use per-element mapEffect, but they emit one item per ranking. The shell merge with priorityItems pre-fetches one array, which can add up to one RTT of latency but costs no throughput.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreamBatching.ts:78-99 rechunkByBudget (Stream.chunks + flatMap to fromArray/fromArrays, which only splits), tapArray (mapArrayEffect), observeArrays.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:583 Each replay page is Stream.fromIterable(Array). In effect 4.0.2 that becomes fromArray, so one page is one array.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:593-599 shellEventsFromDomainEvents uses mapArrayEffect(toShellStreamEvents) followed by Stream.filter (Channel.filterArray, which preserves arrays). This replaces the old per-element mapEffect+flatMap at f1be4abc7:427-428.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:661-674 drainLiveQueue is Stream.fromQueue (Channel.fromQueueArray, which uses Queue.takeAll) plus one tapArray. This replaces fromQueue->tap->tap at f1be4abc7:549-551/641-643.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:849-859 Shell: per-array replay metric, dedupe by Stream.filter, rechunk to 128 items. The live side passes through Stream.merge with priorityItems; Channel.merge passes whole arrays, so batching is unaffected.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:960-980 Thread: per-array replay metric, filter/map, then rechunk to 1000 items and ORCHESTRATION_STREAM_CHUNK_MAX_BYTES=256 KiB (constants.ts:41). The thread stream is pull-only (concat), with no merge prefetch.
  • apps/server/src/ws/orchestrationRpc.ts:545-547 The subscribeShell perf tap is observeArrays. subscribeThread (611-613) and subscribeThreadWindow (644-646) use the same. Both thread handlers wrap the stream in withHistoryRecovery.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/historyRecoveryPolicy.ts:171-176 mapArrayEffect passes arrays through. historyRecoveryPolicy.test.ts:100-107 asserts that array sizes [1,3,1,1] are preserved.
  • apps/server/src/observability/RpcInstrumentation.ts:72-90 observeRpcStream and observeRpcStreamEffect add only Stream.onExit, which does not de-chunk.
  • node_modules/.bun/effect@4.0.2/node_modules/effect/src/Stream.ts:2127-2140 Confirms the mechanism: mapEffect (and tap, which is built on it) does flattenArray then map(Arr.of), emitting single-element arrays. RpcServer.ts:448-457 writes one Chunk per array and waits on latch.await (the Ack).
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreamBatching.test.ts:197-303 Regression tests: 1000-event replay takes at most ceil(bytes/cap)+1 chunks with every chunk within the cap; 500-event shell replay takes 2 chunks with one row re-read; 200 live events during one held ack take at most 2 chunks.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts:567-578 subscribe uses runForEachArray and delivers a chunk in one synchronous pass. requestStream (line 234) does the same.
Defects in the shipped fix

No defects in the orchestration fix itself. I checked every combinator from source to RpcServer and the client consumer. The uncovered sibling and minor gaps are: (1) apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.ts:280 and :285 still use per-element Stream.tap on subscribeTerminalEvents, a relayed hosted sync subscription. Every terminal output event is therefore a separate Chunk with an Ack round trip. With capacity 256 (terminalRpc.ts:19) at 50-150 ms RTT, the server sends about 7-20 events/s. Sustained output above that fills the queue and fails with TerminalSubscriptionResyncError, so the client resubscribes every 250 ms. No report finding covers this. (2) Mobile commits thread-detail events one at a time (apps/mobile/src/connection/threadDetailEvents.ts:62); web frame-batches them. (3) Shell chunks are bounded by count only (128). A rare project row with a large customSystemPrompt is unmeasured, but 128 such rows still fit under the 4 MiB relay cap. (4) The shell's Stream.merge with priorityItems prefetches one array, which adds up to one RTT of latency but costs no throughput.

Done#104 Every thread subscription polls Codex history every 30 s, spawning a codex app-server and loading the full unbounded thread detail before checking whether anything changed

client-runtime-sync:history-recovery-poll-per-thread-subscription · original impact High, effort M · Process spawns WP02

Current state

Confirmed DONE. The 30 s Effect.forever poll per subscription is gone (60633eff3). Recovery now reads when an active subscription opens (at most once per 5 min per thread) and when the watched session settles (at most once per 30 s), with exponential backoff on failure. Prewarm, retained-idle, tab-prefetch and outbox-drain subscriptions are passive and never read. Stored reads share one pooled read-only codex app-server with a 60 s idle timeout (cd0b163e9). processHistory checks the thread shell and binding preconditions before reading, then runs a payload-free repair query (10fe5af78). That query is 'bounded' only in the sense that it skips payload decode and unrelated rows: for a full includeTurns read it still covers every turn of the thread. Measured read-only on the user's DB, it takes about 19 ms for the largest live Codex thread (4,940 activities, 14.9 MB payload_json), down from the reported 105 ms+. No defect undoes the fix. Two leftovers are design choices, not part of the described cost: a full-history thread/read still runs on each turn end of a viewed Codex thread, and success never backs off.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/ws/orchestrationRpc.ts:85 withHistoryRecovery delegates to withThreadHistoryRecovery with the request's mode (absent means active, for older clients) and a per-connection registry. setThreadHistoryRecovery (line 454) flips running subscriptions. Both subscribeThread (610) and subscribeThreadWindow (643) use it. The old Effect.forever(reconcile, sleep 30 s) at f1be4abc7 orchestrationRpc.ts:68-81 is gone.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/historyRecoveryPolicy.ts:142 There is no timer. The fix reads once on open, only when active (readOnOpen). It reads again only when a mapped stream array contains a thread.session-set that settlesThreadSession accepts (line 46: ready, stopped or error with no active turn). Passive subscriptions never read until setMode turns them active.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/historyRecoveryPolicy.ts:16 Spacing is 5 min after a subscribe, 30 s after a settle, and on failure 30 s doubling up to 15 min. There is no backoff when a successful read restores nothing (proposal 2 asked for one).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:522 Mode is active only while viewCount > 0 (incremented at 862 only for {view: true}). Only apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:2750 and apps/mobile/src/features/threads/ThreadDetailScreen.tsx:434 pass view:true. Sidebar prewarm, threadDetailPrewarm, useChatSessionTabsPrefetch, threadNavigationIntent, messageQueueDrain and the mobile outbox drain are passive. The mode is re-evaluated on every (re)subscribe (wsRpcClient.ts:87-92, 1102-1116). setThreadHistoryRecovery is in RPC_ACCESS_POLICY as viewer/read (packages/shared/src/rpcAccessPolicy.ts:106,364).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:3517 reconcileThread is called only from orchestrationRpc subscriptions. It dedupes in-flight reads (historyReads), checks per-thread spacing and backoff state (an LRU of 1,000 threads), and runs under Semaphore(2) with a 25 s timeout. Failures log once per streak.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:3331 processHistory reads the shell (resolveThreadShell) and checks updatedAt and the runtime/instance ids before loadHistoryRepairContext (3298). getThreadDetailById is used only as a fallback for query doubles without getThreadHistoryRepairContext.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:1937 The repair activity-key query extracts providerItemId in SQL (json_valid/json_extract) for every activity in the transcript's turns. A Codex includeTurns read lists all completed turns, so this is effectively the whole thread, without payload transfer or JS decode. Measured with sqlite3 immutable read-only on the largest live Codex thread (93afaaf4…, 4,940 activities, 14.9 MB payload_json): 19 ms.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexStoredThreadReader.ts:61 One lazily started, shared read-only app-server per adapter instance, closed after 60 s idle (line 59), and retired on exit or transport failure. CodexAdapter.ts:1938 creates it and CodexAdapter.ts:2610 uses it. The old spawn-per-read helper readStoredCodexThread (CodexSessionRuntime.ts:1192) is now used only by CodexCollabRuntime.integration.test.ts.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.ts:2594 A ready or running live runtime serves the read through runtime.readThread with a 2 s timeout. It falls back to the shared stored reader, so a very large thread can be read twice. This behavior predates the fix (same at f1be4abc7).
  • packages/effect-codex-app-server/src/client.ts:228 Every thread/read response (includeTurns:true, CodexSessionRuntime.ts:1228) is JSON-parsed and fully Effect-Schema-decoded (decodeOptionalPayload with getClientRequestResponseSchema), then mapped item by item. That per-read cost is unchanged; only its frequency dropped. Ryco Codex threads on this install have rollouts up to 63 MB zst.
  • apps/server/src/cliRemote/threads.ts:132 The CLI remote follow-turn subscription sends no mode, so it is active. That is at most one read per CLI send (5 min spacing) plus a settle read, which is usually interrupted when the stream ends. Negligible.
Defects in the shipped fix

No verified defects. Minor nits: (1) In reconcileThread, an interrupted read (subscription closed mid-read, e.g. relay reconnect churn) records no attempt (the onFailure interrupt path skips recordHistoryRecovery). The next subscription therefore re-reads at once instead of honoring the 5 min spacing. This is bounded by in-flight dedupe and only matters for large threads on flapping connections. (2) The readStoredCodexThread spawn-per-read helper (CodexSessionRuntime.ts:1192) survives as test-only dead code. Not a defect, but noted for the follow-up: for an actively viewed Codex thread, every turn end (at most once per 30 s) still triggers a full includeTurns thread/read, with JSON.parse, a full Effect Schema decode and O(history) mapping, even when the live runtime streamed the turn cleanly. Proposal part (2), reading only when a gap is possible, once per runtime-session generation, with backoff on no-op reads, was replaced by this settle trigger.

Implementation sketch

Optional follow-up, not required for this finding. (a) In ProviderRuntimeIngestion, track per thread and runtimeSessionId whether a gap is possible: the runtime was retired or failed, a turn ended without turn.completed, the session went stopped or error, or the session was resumed from the stored binding rather than started live. In withThreadHistoryRecovery (historyRecoveryPolicy.ts), or at the top of reconcileThread for trigger 'session-settled', skip the read when the settled session is 'ready' and the live runtime streamed the turn with no anomaly. Keep the 'subscribe' read. (b) Record a no-op outcome: when processHistory dispatches nothing, have recordHistoryRecovery double the success spacing (capped, e.g. at 30 min), and reset it on any restore. (c) Record attemptedAt on interruption too (without counting a failure) in reconcileThread's onFailure interrupt branch. Tests: extend historyRecoveryPolicy.test.ts and ProviderRuntimeIngestion.test.ts with fake providerService.readThreadHistory counters. Assert that a clean live turn end performs no read, that a stopped/error settle or a retired runtime does read, that repeated no-op reads back off, and that an interrupted read still enforces spacing. Gating (a) trades turn-end recovery coverage for CPU, so confirm that the live mapping never relies on the settle read to fill items (e.g. reasoning via historyReasoningActivities) before adopting it.

Partial#105 WebSocket connect, shell subscription and config sync start only after the lazy RootAppShell graph (533 KiB gzip) loads and mounts

client-runtime-sync:connect-gated-on-rootappshell-chunk · original impact Medium, effort S · Waterfall WP12B

Current state

PARTIAL is confirmed. Since 60633eff3 (#710) and 65af92766, the root beforeLoad prefetches the ws-token in parallel with the session check. Once the session is authenticated, it opens the primary connection, which issues the shell subscription at creation, without waiting for the lazy RootAppShell. This is standard mode only; hosted-hub and hosted-static return earlier. The supervisor's start() adopts the early connection without tearing it down. The server-state half is still missing. startServerStateSync, which opens the lifecycle/welcome subscription and the config subscription, has one web caller, ServerStateBootstrap, inside the lazy shell. The primary connection itself observes neither stream. I found no other implementation: no Hub-side change, no renamed module, and no onWelcome/onConfigUpdated handlers on the primary connection. Separately, the finding's premise that startServerStateSync is 'ref-counted or idempotent today' is wrong. Each call opens new lifecycle and config subscriptions, so an early start needs an explicit adopt/take handoff.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:245-265 connectsEarly = !isNativeAuthorizationPath(pathname). prefetchPrimaryWebSocketToken() runs before Promise.all([ensurePrimaryEnvironmentReady(), resolveInitialServerAuthGateState()]). On 'authenticated' it calls startPrimaryConnectionEarly(); otherwise it calls discardPrefetchedPrimaryWebSocketToken(). This part of the proposal is implemented.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:334-349 startPrimaryConnectionEarly() only does import('../environments/runtime').then(connectPrimaryEnvironment). It does not call startServerStateSync, so config and welcome are not started early.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:195-201 The hosted-hub branch returns before any early-connect or prefetch code. Hosted-static (about :213-222) also returns early, so the AGENTS.md single-owner rule for hosted lifecycle is respected.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:236-238 attachProviderCatalogPersistence() (IndexedDB load into providerCatalogCache) is started but not awaited. The comment says it must land 'ahead of the first config subscription'. An early config start has to respect this ordering.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsRpcClient.ts:979-993 subscribeConfig calls providerCatalogCache.pin() when the subscription is sent, to name knownProviderCatalogs. If config sync starts before the catalog store attaches, the snapshot includes the full catalogs (a larger payload).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:178-179 shouldObserveLifecycle and shouldObserveConfig are true only for kind 'saved' or when onWelcome/onConfigUpdated are passed. The primary connection passes neither.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1276-1299 createPrimaryEnvironmentConnection builds a kind 'primary' connection with only createEnvironmentConnectionHandlers (shell, resubscribe and priority handlers, :856-900) and no welcome or config hooks. Compare the desktop-workspace saved connection at :1353-1366.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/serverState.ts:162-180 startServerStateSync opens a new subscribeLifecycle and subscribeConfig on every call, with no adoption or ref-counting. Two callers would mean two ~100 KB config snapshots.
  • apps/web/src/components/ServerStateBootstrap.tsx:15-26 This is the only web caller: startServerStateSync(connection.client.server) runs in the effect, keyed on connection identity. The browser test at ServerStateBootstrap.browser.tsx:50-78 asserts that it restarts when the connection is replaced.
  • apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:90 ServerStateBootstrap is rendered inside the lazy RootAppShell, so the welcome and config requests leave only after the shell chunk loads and commits.
  • apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:262-289 EventRouter.handleWelcome waits for the welcome payload before it calls setActiveEnvironmentId, preloadRouteChunk(THREAD_ROUTE_ID), prewarmThreadDetailSubscription and the '/' to last-thread redirect. On a cold '/' load this whole chain therefore starts at mount plus the lifecycle-subscribe RTT. The welcome atom is subscribed with immediate:true (rpc/serverState.ts useLatestAtomSubscription), so a welcome received before mount would be handled on first mount.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:894-905 connectPrimary() returns the already-registered connection. createPrimaryEnvironmentConnection (service.ts:1282-1285) also short-circuits on an existing one, so the shell adopts the early connection.
Remaining

The primary server-state sync (subscribeLifecycle for welcome, plus subscribeConfig) is still started only from ServerStateBootstrap's effect (apps/web/src/components/ServerStateBootstrap.tsx:21-24), which is rendered inside the lazy RootAppShell (RootAppShell.tsx:90). apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:342-349 starts the connection and shell subscription early but not startServerStateSync. Consequences: the welcome-driven work in EventRouter (RootAppShell.tsx:262-289: setActiveEnvironmentId, thread-route chunk preload, thread-detail prewarm, '/' to last-thread redirect) and config-dependent UI (providers/models, tracing) start at RootAppShell mount plus one subscribe RTT and server compute, instead of being ready at mount. The gain is small on loopback desktop (a few to tens of ms) and about one RTT on remote web links. There is also no test covering the early-connect path in __root.tsx.

Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defects in the implemented half. Minor points: (1) For an unauthenticated /pair load, connectsEarly is true (__root.tsx:245), so it always fires one ws-token POST that returns 401 and is discarded at :258. This is harmless but nearly always wasted on /pair; excluding pathname === '/pair' would cost only the rare authenticated /pair-to-'/' redirect. (2) startPrimaryConnectionEarly swallows errors (.catch at :348). If it fails, the fallback is the shell's own start(), and the ServerStateBootstrap extra commit returns, which is acceptable. (3) No unit or browser test asserts that the root beforeLoad connects early in standard mode and never in hosted-hub or hosted-static mode, so a regression there would go unnoticed. (4) The finding's own premise that startServerStateSync is 'ref-counted or idempotent today' is false (serverState.ts:162-180). Any follow-up must add an explicit handoff rather than calling it twice.

Implementation sketch

1) In apps/web/src/rpc/serverState.ts, or in client-runtime rpc/serverState.ts so mobile can reuse it, add a take/adopt handle that mirrors the ws-token prefetch pattern. prestartServerStateSync(server) stores {server, stop} in a module slot, ignoring repeat calls. startOrAdoptServerStateSync(server) checks the slot: if slot.server === server it clears the slot and returns slot.stop; if it holds a different server, it calls slot.stop() and starts fresh; if the slot is empty it calls startServerStateSync(server). Add discardPrestartedServerStateSync() for the unauthenticated or never-mounted case, with an optional safety timeout of about 60 s like PREFETCHED_WS_TOKEN_MAX_AGE_MS. 2) In apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx startPrimaryConnectionEarly(), take the connection returned by connectPrimaryEnvironment(). If it is non-null, start the lifecycle subscription immediately; it is tiny and lets EventRouter's immediate:true atom subscription see the welcome on first mount. Start the config subscription only after the providerCatalogs promise from attachProviderCatalogPersistence (:238) resolves, so pin() names the persisted catalogs. Optionally also wait for connection.ensureBootstrapped(), so the ~100 KB config snapshot does not compete with the shell snapshot on slow links (the reason getConfig was removed in #710). The simplest version calls prestartServerStateSync(connection.client.server) after `await providerCatalogs`, without blocking beforeLoad. Pass providerCatalogs into startPrimaryConnectionEarly. Keep this standard-mode only; hosted-hub and hosted-static already return earlier. 3) Change ServerStateBootstrap.tsx:24 to `return startOrAdoptServerStateSync(connection.client.server)`, so hosted-hub keeps its current path (nothing is prestarted there) and connection replacement still restarts. 4) Optional, larger gain on slow links: when the early welcome arrives on '/', call preloadRouteChunk(THREAD_ROUTE_ID) and prewarmThreadDetailSubscription from a shared helper extracted from EventRouter.handleWelcome (RootAppShell.tsx:276-288), guarded by shouldApplyBootstrapThreadRedirect from RootAppShell.logic. The thread chunk and thread window would then overlap the RootAppShell download. Keep EventRouter as the owner of the actual navigation. 5) Tests: unit tests for the take/adopt handle (adopt with the same server gives no second subscribeConfig or subscribeLifecycle call; a different server stops the old sync; discard stops it). Extend ServerStateBootstrap.browser.tsx so a prestarted sync is adopted, not duplicated. Add a __root beforeLoad test asserting early connect plus prestart in standard authenticated mode and none in hosted-hub, hosted-static or unauthenticated mode. Measure with the existing markStartupPhase marks plus new 'server-welcome-received' and 'server-config-received' marks, on loopback and on the throttled profile (4x CPU, 150 ms RTT).

Done#106 First shell subscription forks worktree reconciliation that loads the full shell snapshot 1+2P times and spawns git per project

client-runtime-sync:worktree-reconcile-full-snapshots · original impact Medium, effort S · Database WP05

Current state

Confirmed DONE. At HEAD the sweep that subscribeShell forks loads no whole shell snapshot, where the report measured 1+2P. It waits 15 s, lists projects from projection_projects only, and reads each project's worktree and thread rows with two indexed WHERE project_id queries. It runs git in the background process lane and skips `git worktree list` when a stat-based registration fingerprint is unchanged. An architecture test stops worktreeOperations.ts from calling getShellSnapshot again. Two smaller costs are also gone: the old snapshot path resolved repository identity through git, and the project/row reads now decode the persisted identity instead. The thread/worktree row semantics are unchanged: the old snapshot also kept archived threads (deleted_at IS NULL) and all worktrees of live projects. The main-workspace row is now created after the rows are read, but it has a null path, so the planner ignores it and the plan cannot change. One minor robustness defect: an empty git listing is cached against the fingerprint.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/ws/orchestrationRpc.ts:523 subscribeShell still forkDetaches reconcileAllWorktrees. The shell snapshot load is the only remaining getShellSnapshot call on this path.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/worktreeOperations.ts:910-964 The throttle is checked and stamped, then Effect.sleep(RECONCILIATION_START_DELAY_MS = 15_000, :74), then readProjectShells (:919). In production that is listProjectShells, a projects-only SELECT. Then per-project forEach with concurrency 4 inside inBackgroundProcessLane. That helper only sets a FiberRef (processGovernor.ts:33-35), so the sleep holds no process permit.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/worktreeOperations.ts:258-271 loadProjectWorkspaceRows uses getProjectWorkspaceRows. The readWorkspacePlacement fallback applies only when the optional method is missing. The production layer always provides it (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:4538), and ws/context.ts:1288-1290 passes the service unwrapped.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:1001-1027,3592-3626 listProjectWorktreeRows (WHERE project_id = ?) and listProjectThreadWorkspaceRows (WHERE project_id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL), five columns, in one transaction. The indexes are idx_projection_worktrees_project_archived (migration 030) and idx_projection_threads_project_deleted_created (migration 019).
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/worktreeOperations.ts:733-771 The listing is reused when fingerprint, root and known entry all match (:742-748). Rows are read once after git (:767) and passed to ensureProjectMainWorktree (:771). That function fetches only when the rows are absent (:295-296).

Any doubt returns null, which means git runs.

Meanwhile .git exists, so the fingerprint is non-null.
Defects in the shipped fix

Minor robustness regression: reconcileProjectWorktrees (worktreeOperations.ts:749-760) caches an empty `git worktree list` result against a non-null fingerprint. Example: a repository whose rev-parse detection fails while .git exists (git 'dubious ownership'/safe.directory, GitVcsDriver.ts:493-511), or `git worktree list` exiting non-zero, so GitWorkflowService.listWorktreePaths returns []. Every later sweep reuses [] until the server restarts or a worktree registration changes. planWorktreeReconciliation treats [] as 'git could not answer' and returns an empty plan (worktreeReconciliation.ts:155-160). So once the user fixes the cause, reconciliation of phantom worktree nodes stays off for that project until restart. Before the change, every sweep retried git. No issue with the performance fix itself. Residual per-project cost is one getProjectShellById row read (:736), which repeats a project the sweep already has, plus a cached getSettings and a few stat calls. All trivial.

Implementation sketch

In apps/server/src/ws/context/worktreeOperations.ts reconcileProjectWorktrees, store in knownWorktreeListings only when fingerprint !== null && paths.length > 0, and delete the entry otherwise. A git repository always lists at least its root, so an empty listing is never a valid cache entry. Optionally pass the OrchestrationProjectShell from reconcileAllWorktrees into a private reconcileProjectWorktreesFor(project) to drop the redundant getProjectShellById read; keep the exported reconcileProjectWorktrees(projectId) signature. Test in worktreeOperations.test.ts with a git-init'd temp repo (as in the existing 'skips git worktree list' test). Make the listWorktreePaths stub return [] on the first call and [root] on the second, call reconcileProjectWorktrees twice, and assert git was called both times.
