Partial#107 ServerConfig is loaded and sent twice on every connect, the usage page adds a getConfig preflight per request, and each load runs a ~6 ms synchronous PATH probe

client-runtime-sync:duplicate-server-config-loads · original impact Medium, effort S · Caching WP12BWP14A

First-pass audit said PARTIAL; the verifier corrected it. PARTIAL is the right status, but the auditor got the scope of the remaining work wrong. They called the 'primary/mobile connect path' DONE, and it is not for mobile. On mobile the active environment's EnvironmentConnection already runs its own subscribeServerConfig stream: kind 'saved' always observes config, and the hosted primary passes onConfigUpdated. ServerStateBootstrap (useServerStateSync) then calls startServerStateSync(connection.client.server) on the same client, which opens a SECOND subscribeServerConfig stream (and a second lifecycle stream for saved environments). wsRpcClient.subscribeConfig does not multiplex, and mobile has no persisted provider-catalog cache. So a cold mobile connect still gets two full config snapshots, the server runs loadServerConfig twice, and every later delta arrives twice. Before the fix it was three loads; now it is two. The auditor also missed that the saved-environment fallback getConfig is always the full payload: its contract has no knownProviderCatalogs. On web the snapshot it races against may have its catalogs elided through the IndexedDB-persisted catalog cache, so the fallback is usually the bigger and slower of the two and almost never wins.

Current state

Fixed: the startServerStateSync getConfig is gone, the usage getConfig preflight is gone, and the server editor scan is cached for 5 minutes. Two duplicate loads remain. (1) Mobile: the active connection's own config stream plus ServerStateBootstrap's startServerStateSync give two subscribeServerConfig streams per connection. That means two full snapshots on a cold connect (mobile has no catalog persistence), two server config builds and doubled deltas. The auditor missed this. (2) Web saved environments: awaitSavedEnvironmentConfig waits 1 s (was 150 ms), then sends a full getConfig over the same socket beside the snapshot and never cancels the loser. On slow links (the report measured about 1.3 s for the first snapshot) this still doubles the load on connect and on every reconnect, and the getConfig nearly always loses the race because it queues behind the snapshot on the same socket.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/serverState.ts:156-179 startServerStateSync only subscribes to lifecycle and config. The getConfig call is gone. On the web primary this is the only config stream, because the web primary connection has no onConfigUpdated (apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1276-1299).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsRpcClient.ts:900-914 getUsageSummary has no serverGetConfig preflight. A contract mismatch is mapped by isUsageContractRejection. Mobile useStatisticsData has no getConfig either.
  • apps/server/src/open.ts:273-311 resolveAvailableEditors caches the scan for 5 minutes, keyed on platform and PATH. loadServerConfig (apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:1173-1210) no longer runs the synchronous stat sweep on every build.
  • apps/mobile/src/state/serverStateSync.ts:27-34 Mobile ServerStateBootstrap (mounted at apps/mobile/src/features/access/AppAccessGate.tsx:163) calls startServerStateSync(connection.client.server) on the active environment's connection. That opens another subscribeConfig (and subscribeLifecycle) on a client that already has one.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:179,223-249 shouldObserveConfig = kind === 'saved' || onConfigUpdated !== undefined. The connection opens its own subscribeConfig stream.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/primaryConnection.ts:244-251 The mobile hosted primary passes onConfigUpdated, so it observes config itself. The mobile direct saved connection (apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:491-503) is kind 'saved' and also observes config. Combined with ServerStateBootstrap this gives two concurrent config streams.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsRpcClient.ts:979-1020 subscribeConfig opens an independent transport.subscribe for each caller. There is no fan-out. The catalog pin comes from providerCatalogCache, which is persisted only on web (apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:279-286) and not on mobile, so both cold mobile snapshots carry full catalogs.
  • apps/server/src/ws/providerRpc.ts:692-718 Each subscribeServerConfig runs loadServerConfig and its own provider delta tracker. Duplicate subscriptions double the server build and every later update.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/savedEnvironmentSession.ts:25,70-96 SAVED_ENVIRONMENT_CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_WAIT_MS is 1_000. After it expires, Promise.race([snapshot, readConfig()]) runs both loads, and the loser is not cancelled.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1239-1249,1558-1567,1629-1639 The fallback readConfig is client.server.getConfig() over the same socket. It is used on the initial saved connect and on every reconnect through refreshMetadata.
  • packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:810-814 The serverGetConfig payload is an empty Struct with no knownProviderCatalogs. The fallback read always returns full catalogs, while the snapshot it races against can be catalog-elided on web.
Remaining

1) Mobile double config stream. apps/mobile/src/state/serverStateSync.ts:29 opens a second subscribeServerConfig (plus lifecycle) on the active connection, which already observes config (packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:179,223; apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/primaryConnection.ts:248; apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:499). Every cold mobile connect gets two full snapshots (about 100 KiB each with no persisted catalogs), the server runs loadServerConfig twice (providerRpc.ts:718), and every delta arrives twice. 2) Web saved-environment fallback. packages/client-runtime/src/connection/savedEnvironmentSession.ts:91-95 still sends a full getConfig beside the snapshot when the snapshot takes longer than 1 s. That covers ws-token, upgrade, subscribe and transfer, and the report measured about 1.3 s throttled. It applies on connect and on every reconnect (apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1558-1567,1629-1639), and the losing load is never cancelled. Optional: there is no 'refresh editors' invalidation for the 5-minute editor cache (open.ts:279). Adjacent and outside this finding, not counted here: per-action full getConfig reads remain in apps/web/src/editorPreferences.ts:61 (on each open-in-editor), apps/web/src/hooks/newDraftDefaults.ts:125-131 (hosted new drafts), apps/web/src/hooks/executeChatSendTurn.ts:617-621 (hosted worktree sends) and apps/web/src/components/pullRequests/agentHandoff.ts:183-185.

Defects in the shipped fix

Nothing is broken in the shipped parts. The one gap is in the saved-environment fallback. It now fires only after 1 s instead of 150 ms, so it happens less often, but it still runs beside the snapshot. Both requests go over the same socket and the getConfig is queued behind the snapshot, so on exactly the slow links that trigger it, it almost never wins. It adds a full-catalog payload and a main-thread decode, and its result is thrown away. The usage-mismatch detection works by matching substrings in the error message (usage/compatibility.ts), so it can break if that wording changes.

Implementation sketch

A. Mobile double stream (preferred, generic fix): in packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsRpcClient.ts, change server.subscribeConfig (around line 979) so all listeners on one client share one transport subscription. Keep a Set of listeners with a refcount. Keep the projected config, using projectServerConfigEvent, the same projection as connection.ts:238. A listener that joins after the first item gets a synthetic {type:'snapshot', config} so its projection starts from a full config. Pass onResubscribe to every listener. Close the underlying stream when the last listener unsubscribes. Do the same for subscribeLifecycle and replay the last welcome to late joiners. Narrower alternative: add EnvironmentConnection.observeConfig(listener), which replays observedConfig and then forwards later events, and have mobile useServerStateSync feed serverConfigAtom from it (for example a client-runtime startServerStateSyncFromConnection) instead of calling startServerStateSync(client.server). Tests: a wsRpcClient unit test that two subscribeConfig listeners cause exactly one subscribeServerConfig request, a late listener receives a snapshot, and unsubscribing one listener keeps the stream alive. A mobile test that mounting ServerStateBootstrap on an active saved or hosted connection sends one subscribeServerConfig request. B. Saved-environment fallback: in savedEnvironmentSession.ts awaitSavedEnvironmentConfig, stop running readConfig beside the snapshot. Await only input.snapshot, bounded by SAVED_ENVIRONMENT_INITIAL_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MS. Keep configSnapshotUnlessRejected (service.ts:1514) so a credential rejection still fails fast. If a read fallback is still wanted for robustness, start it only when the config stream reports an error or a resubscribe without a snapshot (expose this through the connection's subscribeConfig onError), or after a much longer grace period (5-8 s), and never while the snapshot is still in flight. Update the tests in savedEnvironmentSession.test.ts (lines 90-130) and add a service-level test: with a snapshot delayed by 1.5 s, client.server.getConfig is never called on connect or on reconnect. C (optional): pre-warm resolveAvailableEditors at server start, and let an explicit refreshProviders or settings action invalidate availableEditorsCache.

Value medium · effort S · risk low

Done#108 Every shell snapshot can wait on 2 git processes per project (1-minute TTL, 1 s budget)

client-runtime-sync:repo-identity-git-on-snapshot-path · original impact Medium, effort S · Process spawns WP05

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The DONE status stands: the snapshot no longer runs git. The auditor was wrong to report no fix defects. #710 changed Agent Control project plans so the approved 'before' identity comes from the persisted column, but revalidation still checks it against a live git resolve. The two sources now disagree in reachable cases. The worst is a project whose root is missing: its last persisted identity is kept on purpose, while the live resolve returns null. Agent Control can then never update or remove that project, including re-rooting it after the folder moved. Before #710 both sides came from the same resolver cache.

Current state

The finding is fixed. Shell snapshots, placement and project lookups read repository_identity_json from projection_projects (migration 086) with no git and no timeout. resolveRepositoryIdentitiesForProjects and timeoutOption(1000) are gone. A background sync with concurrency 4 runs at startup, every 30 min, and on project.created or a root move. It revalidates with stat-only fingerprints of the enclosing repo's commondir/config, forces a re-resolve after 24 h, runs git in the background process lane, and announces changes with an empty project.meta.update that keeps updatedAt. The 1-minute resolver TTLs now back only the stream-enrichment fallback, the sync's refresh, and Agent Control. One regression came in with the fix: AgentControlProjectPlans compares the persisted identity key (stateFor via readWorkspacePlacement) with a live resolver key in revalidate. Agent Control project update/remove fails as 'project-stale: The approved repository identity changed' whenever the persisted identity lags or the root is missing. A lag lasts up to 30 min after a remote change, or seconds for a new or moved project. A missing root never recovers.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3007 buildShell is pure SQL, and the comment says identities are persisted so a snapshot never waits on git. The file only imports decodePersistedRepositoryIdentity (line 73), not the resolver.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3267 getWorkspacePlacement maps project rows with the persisted identity. Agent Control reads this through readWorkspacePlacement.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3384 getProjectShellById uses the persisted identity. The pre-fix code called repositoryIdentityResolver.resolve here (f1be4abc7 lines 2806 and 2837).
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations/086_ProjectionProjectRepositoryIdentity.ts:4 Adds the repository_identity_json, _fingerprint and _checked_at columns. There is no backfill: a NULL checked_at means the first sweep resolves the project.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/ProjectionProjects.ts:79 The projector upsert keeps the identity columns unless workspace_root changed. recordRepositoryIdentity only writes when the root still matches, so a race with a move cannot store an identity for the old root.
  • apps/server/src/project/repositoryIdentityPersistence.ts:71 The stat-only fingerprint walks up to the enclosing .git and follows gitdir/commondir to config size and mtime. It returns null for a missing root.
  • apps/server/src/project/repositoryIdentitySync.ts:104 A null fingerprint (missing root) is skipped, so the last known identity is kept indefinitely. Lines 108-113 skip git when the fingerprint is unchanged and the identity is under 24 h old. Line 117 runs git in the background lane.
  • apps/server/src/project/repositoryIdentitySync.ts:133 A changed identity is announced with an empty project.meta.update. decider.ts:655 keeps updatedAt for an update that changes nothing.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1070 runRepositoryIdentitySync is started after the gate, with the domain-event subscription. It sweeps once immediately, then every 30 min.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:429 project.created and project.meta-updated enrichment reads the persisted identity and calls resolver.resolve only when it is null. This is on the event path, not the snapshot path.
  • apps/server/src/agentControl/Layers/AgentControlProjectPlans.ts:69 stateFor uses project.repositoryIdentity, the persisted value from readWorkspacePlacement, as the plan's before/expected repositoryIdentityKey (lines 194 and 219).
  • apps/server/src/agentControl/Layers/AgentControlProjectPlans.ts:266 Regression: revalidate compares the live resolver key (identityKey, git with a 1-min cache) with expected.repositoryIdentityKey, which is persisted. For a missing root, live is null (an unspawnable probe reads as no identity, RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:111) while persisted keeps the old key, so this always fails. After a remote change, persisted lags for up to 30 min. Before #710 both sides came from the resolver (f1be4abc7 used getShellSnapshot with resolver-backed identities).
Defects in the shipped fix

AgentControlProjectPlans mixes identity sources since #710. The before/expected repositoryIdentityKey comes from the persisted column (stateFor via readWorkspacePlacement, AgentControlProjectPlans.ts:69/194/219), but revalidate checks it against a live git resolve (AgentControlProjectPlans.ts:266). Three cases follow. (1) The project root is missing, for example an agent ran `mv` and then proposed a project update to the new root, or it wants to unlink a project whose folder was deleted. The sync keeps the last persisted identity (repositoryIdentitySync.ts:104) while the live probe returns null, so update and remove always fail with 'project-stale: The approved repository identity changed', and retrying does not help. (2) After `git remote add/set-url`, persisted lags the live identity for up to 30 min (the sweep interval), so update/remove fails for that long, depending on whether the 1-min resolver cache already holds the new value. (3) Briefly after a project is created or moved, persisted is NULL until the event-triggered sync records it. This sync can sit behind a running sweep's lock. Agent Control project update/remove is the only consumer that compares identities; the snapshot fix itself is sound.

Implementation sketch

In apps/server/src/agentControl/Layers/AgentControlProjectPlans.ts, compare like with like by binding approvals to the live identity, as before #710. Change stateFor to take the identity key as an argument. In prepareUpdate and prepareRemove, compute `const currentKey = yield* identityKey(project.workspaceRoot)` and build before/expected with it. In revalidate, compute the live key of current.workspaceRoot once. Compare title, workspaceRoot and updatedAt from the projection, compare the live key against expected.repositoryIdentityKey, and drop the persisted-identity equality at line 261. This keeps the TOCTOU guarantee: the repository identity the user approved is re-checked live at execution. Two alternatives: resolve both sides through resolver.refresh to bypass the 1-min cache, or have prepare trigger the identity sync for that project so persisted and live converge. The live-vs-live comparison is simpler. Tests in AgentControlProjectPlans.test.ts: (a) the persisted identity is null or stale while the resolver returns key K; prepareUpdate/prepareRemove followed by revalidate succeeds. (b) The persisted identity is K, the root is missing, and the resolver returns null; prepareRemove followed by revalidate succeeds. (c) The resolver returns K at prepare and K2 at revalidate; revalidate fails with project-stale. No contract or schema change is needed, because AgentControlProjectState.repositoryIdentityKey only changes provenance.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Partial#109 Each thread event re-reads and re-sends a full thread shell to every subscriber, and the client pays O(N threads) per upsert

client-runtime-sync:shell-upsert-per-thread-event · original impact Medium, effort M · CPU WP11

Current state

PARTIAL is correct. I found no implementation the auditor missed. The server half is fixed: shell upserts are coalesced latest-wins per thread over a 250 ms window, collapsed once per drained batch, and the row read is shared across subscribers by (threadId, sequence). These came in 60633eff3 and 8fb94df00, and both are in the Hub vendor pin 7bc39eec3. Still open: there is no WHERE thread_id IN batch read. Unchanged upserts are not skipped, because updated_at is still bumped on every message, activity and plan event. On the client, every changed upsert still spreads up to four dictionaries keyed by every thread; the only change is that ensureThreadRegistered no longer does the threadIds.includes scan. The auditor missed one more case of the same O(N) spread: the detail-stream path still copies all of threadShellById on every 32 ms streaming delta for subscribed threads, and that path has no 250 ms coalescing. I reproduced the auditor's fix defect with a node one-off against effect 4.0.2: if the owner of a shared read is interrupted, a subscriber that joined the read gets an interrupt-only failure, and toShellStreamEvent's Effect.catch does not absorb it.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationEventCoalescing.ts:62 orchestrationShellFrameKey keys thread.activity-appended, thread.message-sent and thread.proposed-plan-upserted by thread. Every other event returns null and flushes held frames first, so ordering holds.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/constants.ts:35 ORCHESTRATION_SHELL_THREAD_COALESCE_WINDOW_MS = 250. It is wired into the shell live feed at orchestrationStreams.ts:831-838. Each subscription runs its own flush tick, at orchestrationStreams.ts:636-640.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:381 toShellStreamEvents keeps only the last upsert-class event per thread in each drained batch. Replay and live both use it, at line 597.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/sharedThreadShellReads.ts:54 Shared reads are keyed by thread and sequence, with a 2 s TTL and 512 entries. Lines 66-72 complete the shared Deferred with the owner's exit, including an interrupt. In my one-off (owner forked, joiner forked, owner interrupted), the joiner exited Failure with an interrupt-only cause, even with Effect.catch applied as toShellStreamEvent does at orchestrationStreams.ts:360.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionPipeline.ts:1160 message-sent (updatedAt at 1178), proposed-plan-upserted (1200) and activity-appended or approval-response (1218) all still write updatedAt: event.occurredAt. ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:177 still flushes assistant deltas every 32 ms.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3481 getThreadShellById still reads one thread per call, with four reads (thread, latest turn, session, priority). There is no batch variant; the grep found no getThreadShellsByIds or similar.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:1113 writeThreadShellState matches f1be4abc7 byte for byte. It spreads threadShellById (1141), threadSessionById (1153), threadTurnStateById (1165) and sidebarThreadSummaryById (1180) whenever the equality checks fail, and both shell and summary compare updatedAt (722, 643).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:877 ensureThreadRegistered skips threadIds.includes when the thread already has a shell (8fb94df00). This is the only client-side change for this finding.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:4310 applyShellEvents commits a frame of updates once, but folds each update through writeThreadShellState and commitEnvironmentState with no batch-local owned copy. supervision.ts:1026 applyShellBatch feeds it. applyThreadPriorities (store.ts:3690) already uses copy-on-first-write (??=), which is the pattern to reuse.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:1589 Missed by the auditor. updateThreadShellTimestamp spreads all of threadShellById. It is called on every detail-stream message-sent (1871) and activity append (1958), next to the messageByThreadId spread at 1808. The thread stream uses orchestrationProgressFrameKey (orchestrationStreams.ts:932), which never coalesces thread.message-sent, so subscribed streaming threads pay an O(N threads) copy about 30 times a second. ownedMessageMaps only avoids re-copying the per-thread message map.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/environmentStateSink.ts:79 The per-upsert after-hook is now cheap: a full UI sync only runs for new threads, seedThreadVisitedAt is a no-op once seeded, and eviction is O(at most 32 subscriptions).
Remaining

At the user's ~282 threads this costs microseconds. It matters only for clients with 2k to 5k threads. (a) Client O(N threads) work per changed upsert. writeThreadShellState (packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:1113-1188) spreads four records at 1141, 1153, 1165 and 1180. Because updatedAt changes on every server event, each coalesced upsert re-copies at least threadShellById and sidebarThreadSummaryById. That is at most about 4 per second per streaming thread per client. (b) The same O(N) pattern on the detail stream, which is not coalesced. updateThreadShellTimestamp (store.ts:1589-1608, called at 1871 and 1958) plus the messageByThreadId spread (1808) and the threadTurnStateById spread (1857) run on every 32 ms assistant delta for subscribed threads. (c) The server does no batch read (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3481) and never skips unchanged upserts. Skipping would first require changing the updatedAt bumps at ProjectionPipeline.ts:1178, 1200 and 1218. This is marginal: the SQL measured 0.017 ms per call. (d) Shared-read hits are below the ideal because each subscription has its own flush phase (orchestrationStreams.ts:636). Concurrent subscribers mostly share only the immediately passed-through structural thread events.

Defects in the shipped fix

sharedThreadShellReads.ts:66-72. The owner's read runs on the owning subscriber's fiber, and Effect.onExit completes the shared Deferred with whatever exit it gets, including an interrupt. If the owning shell subscription is torn down mid-read (a tab closes, or it resubscribes after a reconnect) while another subscriber has joined the same (threadId, sequence) entry, the joiner's Deferred.await fails with an interrupt-only cause. I confirmed this with a node one-off against the installed effect 4.0.2. toShellStreamEvent's Effect.catch (orchestrationStreams.ts:360) only handles typed failures, so the interrupt propagates into the joiner's shell stream and fails or ends it. The client then has to resubscribe or resync. The failed entry is deleted, so later readers re-read; only concurrent joiners are hit. It is unlikely, because joiners mostly arise on non-coalesced structural thread events, and it heals itself, but it is a real correctness gap. sharedThreadShellReads.test.ts does not cover it.

Implementation sketch

1) Fix the shared-read interrupt defect (S, low risk). In sharedThreadShellReads.ts, start the owner's getThreadShellById with Effect.forkDetach, which exists in effect 4.0.2; a uninterruptible wrapper would also work but delays teardown if the SQLite semaphore is busy. The detached fiber completes the Deferred, and the owner and joiners all await it, so interrupting any one subscriber interrupts only its own await. Keep the delete-on-failure. Test in sharedThreadShellReads.test.ts: fork an owner on a query that sleeps, fork a joiner, interrupt the owner, and assert the joiner resolves to Some(shell) after one read. 2) Client batch-local owned records (M, low-medium risk). - Add an owned-records WeakSet next to ownedMessageMaps. Add a helper setRecordEntry(owned, record, key, value) that copies the record on its first write in a batch, adds the copy to the set, and mutates in place after that. This generalizes the ??= pattern in applyThreadPriorities (store.ts:3690). - Thread the set through writeThreadShellState (store.ts:1113), ensureThreadRegistered's threadIdsByProjectId update, updateThreadShellTimestamp (1589), applyThreadMessageSentEvent (messageByThreadId at 1808, threadTurnStateById at 1857) and the activity path (1958). - Create one set per batch in applyShellEvents (store.ts:4310), the ShellEventCoalescer flush (4093) and applyOrchestrationEvents (3192, alongside ownedMessageMaps). Single-event entry points pass undefined, which keeps today's copy-on-write. - Also stop commitEnvironmentState (2001) from re-spreading environmentStateById per event inside a batch: fold per environment, then commit once. - The input state's records must never be mutated. Only copies created in the current batch may be. The prepare callbacks in the web and mobile sinks read values synchronously before each apply, so they stay correct. - Tests in packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.test.ts: a batch of upserts across many threads must equal a sequential fold, the input AppState must stay deeply unchanged (frozen fixture), untouched records must keep their identity, and a detail-stream batch of message-sent events must update threadShellById once. Re-run the investigator's 2k/5k-thread bench, expecting under 0.05 ms per upsert. - Alternative: replace the per-thread records with a persistent map. That is a much larger API change for selectors, so it is not recommended now. 3) Optional, low value. - Batch row reads in toShellStreamEvents with a getThreadShellsByIds(threadIds) built on json_each, like the scoped queries at ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:851. - Widen read sharing: record the engine's latest committed sequence when a read starts, and let a request for (threadId, seq) join any live entry whose start sequence is at least seq. - Changing updatedAt semantics so unchanged upserts can be skipped needs a product decision; see decisionReason.

Done#110 Every environment connect opens a second /ws/device socket and runs device.list, spawning 4–10 simulator/emulator processes (uncached for iOS)

client-runtime-sync:device-socket-and-probes-on-every-connect · original impact Medium, effort M · Process spawns WP15

Current state

Confirmed DONE (65af92766 and 60633eff3). Direct clients no longer open /ws/device or request a second ws-token on connect. Device RPCs and the event stream use the main /ws socket, and the dedicated socket opens only for screenshots, as a fallback for older servers, or closes after 60 s idle. Nothing lists devices on connect or reconnect. The event stream binds only while a thread view or the simulator pane retains the environment. reconnect() no longer awaits a device probe. On the server, the iOS probes are cached and share in-flight promises: xcode-select for 60 s, xcodebuild -version for 5 min keyed on the developer dir, and one simctl list reused for 2 s. Mobile builds no device client at all. Only minor issues remain, and only while the pane is open.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:988-1011 The primary direct client uses createDirectDeviceRpcTransport. DeviceWsTransport is built only inside the openDedicated callback.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1159-1183 The saved environment is the same: the dedicated socket is lazy, so no ws-token POST happens at connect.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:938-960 Hosted reuses the main HostedWsTransport (manageTransport:false). This was already true before.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/deviceRpcClient.ts:150-273 request and subscribe go to main. requestBulk (screenshots) and the 'unsupported' fallback acquire the dedicated socket, which closes after DEDICATED_DEVICE_SOCKET_IDLE_MS=60s (line 132).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts:378-393 A non-retryable 'unknown tag' subscription error calls onError('unsupported') and stops, so an old server causes no retry loop on main.
  • apps/server/src/ws.ts:62-96 Main /ws merges makeDeviceWsRpcLayer into WsHostedRpcGroup. /ws/device is kept for old clients.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:323-326 registerDeviceConnection only registers the client and starts nothing.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:360-375 reconnect is client.reconnect, then refreshMetadata, then bootstrapGate. No inventory read. The old version awaited deviceBinding.refreshInventory (f1be4abc7 connection.ts:317-329).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/device/runtime.ts:22-62,112-182 bindDeviceConnection subscribes only, with no list. Binding is retained by ensureDeviceRuntime and unbinds 60 s after the last release.
  • apps/web/src/components/device/useDeviceRuntime.ts:11-16 Callers are ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:128, DraftChatThreadRouteView.tsx:95 and SimulatorPanel.tsx:166. Thread views retain only the event stream, which is cheap: deviceRpc.ts:122-135 is a plain manager.onEvent.
  • apps/web/src/components/device/SimulatorPanel.tsx:208-225 list and getThreadState run only while the pane is mounted (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:1536 renders it only when activeMode==='simulator'), on a generation change, or on the 5 s setup poll.
  • apps/server/src/device/IosSimulatorBackend.ts:78-90,1055-1066,1119-1180 The listing, xcode-select and xcodebuild -version caches store the pending promise, so concurrent list and getThreadState share one simctl. A failed or non-Xcode answer is not kept. Boot passes fresh:true and shutdown clears deviceListing (line 537).
Defects in the shipped fix

No blocking defects; the connect and reconnect cost is gone. Minor items, all verified by reading: (1) Behaviour change from the lazy stream: an agent's 'device.open-pane-requested' event fires only once per thread and device (DeviceManager.surfaceDeviceForAgent, DeviceManager.ts:963-971, keyed on paneSurfacedUdid). It is now lost if no thread view of that environment was mounted in the last 60 s, for example when the user is on another environment, settings or home. Before, the always-bound stream stored it in pendingOpenByThreadKey until the user opened that thread. Now the pane does not auto-open later. Low impact. (2) While the pane is open, SimulatorPanel.refresh (SimulatorPanel.tsx:210-214) calls list and getThreadState in parallel, and each runs availability() plus discover() on the server. iOS shares one simctl through the 2 s promise cache. Android listDevices runs twice per refresh (about 2+2N processes each) and repeats every 5 s during setup polling. getThreadState already returns devices and availability, so the list call is redundant. (3) Cosmetic: the ws.ts:99-101 comment says /ws/device is used only for older servers, but current clients also open it for screenshots (requestBulk).

Done#111 Resume checks read and decode up to 1,001 global events twice per subscription, and idle thread subscriptions cannot resume once 1,000 global events pass

client-runtime-sync:resume-global-sequence-and-double-read · original impact Medium, effort M · Database

Current state

Confirmed DONE (commit 60633eff3, #710). canResumeAfter no longer reads or decodes event pages in production. It calls eventStore.probeResume, which does a rowid EXISTS anchor check plus count(*) over an inner `SELECT 1 ... LIMIT n+1`. The per-thread count is served by the covering idx_orch_events_stream_sequence index. A thread is judged only on its own backlog (anchored, and at most 1000 thread events after it; the global limit is 0). Its replay pages through readStreamEventsPage on (aggregate_kind, stream_id, sequence) instead of scanning global pages, so an idle retained thread now resumes however many global events have happened. The shell gets the same payload-free probe, and its single replay read is the one it needs anyway. Part (3), the periodic watermark, was not built and is no longer needed. No other caller has the old pattern, and I found no correctness regression.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:688-730 canResumeAfter with probeResume. For the shell, the global limit is 1000. For a thread with readStreamEventsPage, the global limit is 0 (anchor only) and the decision is streamEventsAfter <= 1000. The old two-readEventsPage path (723-729) runs only when probeResume is missing.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/OrchestrationEventStore.ts:510-544 probeResume SQL. It never selects payload_json. The stream count filters aggregate_kind, stream_id and sequence, so the index covers it.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:944-960 Thread replay uses readStreamEventsPage({aggregateKind:'thread', streamId: threadId}) instead of global readEventsPage plus a filter.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/OrchestrationEventStore.ts:251-276,497-508 readStreamEventRows and readStreamEventsPage. OrchestrationEventStore.test.ts:325-349 asserts the plan uses idx_orch_events_stream_sequence with no temp B-tree, and test :245-261 shows the probe works when payload_json is invalid JSON, so it never reads payloads.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:207,1262-1279 Production wiring: OrchestrationEventStore comes from OrchestrationLayerLive (server.ts:505, runtimeLayer.ts:11-33). Its probeResume and readStreamEventsPage are passed to makeOrchestrationStreamHelpers. OrchestrationEventStoreLive is the only implementation.
  • apps/server/src/ws/orchestrationRpc.ts:553-650 subscribeThread and subscribeThreadWindow both call makeReplayableThreadStream(..., threadId, {resumeFromSequence}). They are the only callers. ProviderCommandReactor.ts:3463 is an unrelated single-row anchor read.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreamBatching.test.ts:306-385 Tests cover an idle-thread resume with a large global backlog, a snapshot when the thread's own backlog exceeds 1000, per-stream replay with zero global page reads at eventsAfter=100000, and the shell staying on the global bound.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:556-572 No client change was needed. appliedSequence still advances only on the thread's own events or snapshots, and the server now judges it against the thread's own stream. Transport reconnects resubscribe in place (wsTransport.ts:293-330) and re-read resumeFromSequence, so the closure's appliedSequence survives.
Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defects. Four cosmetic or peripheral notes. (a) The ORCHESTRATION_THREAD_RESUME_MAX_SCAN_EVENTS doc (apps/server/src/ws/context/constants.ts:5-10) still says a thread's 'replay still scans global pages'. That is now true only for the test-only fallback without readStreamEventsPage, so the comment is stale. (b) The readEventPage comment (OrchestrationEventStore.ts:119-123) says the extra +1 row is 'never decoded'. SqlSchema.findAll's Result schema still JSON-parses its payload (UnknownFromJsonString). That costs one row per page and is negligible. (c) The old double decoded read survives only in the fallback branch (orchestrationStreams.ts:723-729), which production never reaches. (d) Out of scope here and already in the report under its own items: resume stays disabled for hosted and hub-hosted connections (supervision.ts:562). attach() also re-creates appliedSequence=null, so an explicit supervisor.remove plus re-register (credential rejection, SSH re-issue, disconnect) always re-snapshots. Ordinary transport reconnects are unaffected.

Partial#112 Saved/remote environment connect is a ≥4-RTT waterfall, and thread subscriptions wait for registration after metadata

client-runtime-sync:saved-env-connect-waterfall · original impact Medium, effort M · Waterfall decision

Current state

PARTIAL is right for web and desktop. 65af92766 registers the saved connection right after the session check and renewal, so thread subscriptions attach before the ws-token, upgrade and config. It also removed the second device socket and ws-token from connect. The web and desktop connect still does GET /api/auth/session and then POST /api/auth/ws-token, two sequential round trips. The auditor missed that mobile already removed that round trip in #710 (60633eff3) without a server change: a cached session hint (apps/mobile/src/connection/savedSessionHints.ts) lets a connect whose session is not due skip the pre-socket session GET, and the check runs in the background after register. Web and desktop never adopted it, so the remaining work is to move that mechanism into client-runtime and wire it into apps/web, not a new prefetch or server endpoint. A smaller leftover the auditor also missed: an SSH saved environment's first connect runs the SSH ensure (ssh -G subprocess plus a tunnel HTTP readiness probe) twice in a row.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1625 registerConnection(connection) runs after the session check (1463) and renewal (1487), before refreshSavedEnvironmentMetadata (1629). Added in 65af92766 with a test in service.addSavedEnvironment.test.ts ('registers a connect before its config arrives...').
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:805 register() attaches every pending thread-detail subscription for the environment (812-814), so attach() (540) no longer waits for config or metadata.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1164 The saved client's dedicated /ws/device socket (with its own ws-token) opens only on demand through openDedicated (65af92766). The finding's 'plus the device socket's own ws-token and socket' cost is gone from connect.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1463 Web still awaits GET /api/auth/session (readSavedEnvironmentSession at 1190) on every connect and reconnect attempt, before any socket. No hint or skip path.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1091 The WsTransport URL provider then reads the bearer and POSTs /api/auth/ws-token (resolveSavedEnvironmentSocketUrl 1012, resolveRemoteWebSocketConnectionUrl at 1033 -> packages/client-runtime/src/connection/remoteApi.ts:151-168). Second sequential RTT before the upgrade.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/savedSessionHints.ts:44 Missed by the auditor. usableSavedSessionHint plus createSavedSessionHints (added in 60633eff3 / #710) persist non-secret session metadata. A connect whose session is bearer-method, more than 1 h from expiry and not due for renewal skips GET /api/auth/session and goes straight to ws-token, which answers an expired or revoked bearer with a terminal 401.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:434 Mobile connect uses hintedSession instead of the session check, registers, then runs the skipped check in the background (about 535-570). A rejection calls rejectCredential and removes the connection by identity. Mobile registers without waiting for config. Web has nothing like this; git grep for sessionHint outside apps/mobile finds nothing.
  • apps/server/src/auth/http.ts:181 The ws-token route still returns only {token, expiresAt} (contracts auth.ts:131). There is no combined session+ws-token endpoint. Mobile shows one is not needed.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/primaryAuth.ts:170 The ws-token prefetch alongside the session check (65af92766) applies only to the primary environment.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1025 For desktop SSH environments, the URL provider calls prepareSavedEnvironmentRecordForConnection again right after connectSavedEnvironment did at 1455. Each call is an IPC ensureEnvironment that runs ssh -G (packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:1525) and a readiness probe through the tunnel (tunnel.ts:1456). The first connect pays it twice. This was the same at f1be4abc7.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/savedEnvironmentSession.ts:25 SAVED_ENVIRONMENT_CONFIG_SNAPSHOT_WAIT_MS is now 1000 ms. The snapshot-then-getConfig race no longer gates thread attach but still gates the connect promise.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:1128 waitForPrimaryShellSnapshotApplied(2500) is unchanged and deliberate. The saved connect queue runs at concurrency 2 (supervision.ts:61; savedEnvironmentConnectionScheduler.ts:44 awaits each connect), so a slot is held until config arrives.
Remaining

Web and desktop direct pairings still pay two sequential HTTP round trips before the WS upgrade on every connect and reconnect: GET /api/auth/session (apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1463 via readSavedEnvironmentSession at 1190), then POST /api/auth/ws-token from the URL provider (service.ts:1091 -> 1012-1043 -> packages/client-runtime/src/connection/remoteApi.ts:151-168). Mobile already skips the first one with cached session hints (apps/mobile/src/connection/savedSessionHints.ts, environmentDriver.ts:434-570), but that code lives only in apps/mobile. The shared runtime and web never got it, which also splits saved-session auth policy between mobile and web, against the AGENTS.md rule that auth and lifecycle policy stays shared. Minor leftovers: (1) a desktop SSH environment's first connect runs ensureEnvironment twice back to back (service.ts:1455, then the URL provider at service.ts:1025), each an ssh -G subprocess plus a tunnel readiness probe (packages/ssh/src/tunnel.ts:1525, 1456); (2) the connect promise, and so one of the two queue slots (supervision.ts:61), is held until the config snapshot or a getConfig fallback after 1000 ms (savedEnvironmentSession.ts:25), which delays the third and later saved environments slightly.

Defects in the shipped fix

None found in the early-registration fix. After registration, an auth failure (credentialRejection or ws-token 401) goes through markSavedEnvironmentCredentialRejected or setRuntimeRequiresAuth. Any other failure (config timeout, network) reaches discardConnection (service.ts:1599-1613), which removes by identity and detaches the subscriptions it attached early. The desktop SSH reissue path discards before continuing. This is covered by the new test in service.addSavedEnvironment.test.ts.

Implementation sketch

Port the mobile session-hint skip to the shared runtime and use it on web and desktop for non-SSH direct pairings. 1. Move apps/mobile/src/connection/savedSessionHints.ts and its .test.ts into packages/client-runtime/src/connection/ (it depends only on @ryco/contracts, shouldRenewSavedSession and KVService) and export it from the connection subpath. Mobile imports it from there with no behaviour change. 2. In apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts, create one hints instance with createWebKV() (apps/web/src/platform/kv.ts). In connectSavedEnvironment, for records without desktopSsh, read the hint alongside the bearer read. If usableSavedSessionHint(hint, Date.now()) returns a session, use it as `session`, skip readSavedEnvironmentSession, and let savedSessionRenewal.renew no-op (a usable hint is never due). Otherwise keep today's check and record renewal.session afterwards, unless the attempt was cancelled. Pass that session to refreshSavedEnvironmentMetadata so it does not re-read. 3. After registerConnection on a hinted connect, run the skipped check in the background with the currently stored bearer (savedSessionRenewal.readBearerToken), the same way environmentDriver.ts does at about 535-570. If it answers null or 401 while the connection is still current, call markSavedEnvironmentCredentialRejected(environmentId, connection) and forget the hint. On success, record the hint, patch role, and restart keepSavedEnvironmentSessionRenewed with the fresh session. 4. Forget the hint wherever web marks requires-auth (setRuntimeRequiresAuth, markSavedEnvironmentCredentialRejected, the onCredentialRejected callback), when the environment is paired again (addSavedEnvironment), and when it is removed. The ws-token 401 path already ends terminally through isTerminalUrlError -> onCredentialRejected -> credentialRejection -> SavedEnvironmentCredentialError in refreshSavedEnvironmentMetadata. 5. Optionally, for SSH: skip the URL provider's ensure on the first socket attempt right after connectSavedEnvironment prepared the record. For example, pass the prepared record or a prepared-at timestamp into createSavedEnvironmentClient and bypass the ensure when it is under a few seconds old. Reconnects keep ensuring. Optionally, release the connect-queue slot once registered instead of after config. Tests: service.savedEnvironments.test.ts and service.addSavedEnvironment.test.ts cases for (a) a hinted connect issues no /api/auth/session before /api/auth/ws-token; (b) a renewal-due or near-expiry hint keeps the check; (c) a ws-token 401 on a hinted connect marks requires-auth, forgets the hint and removes the connection by identity; (d) a background check answering unauthenticated removes the registered connection; (e) SSH records ignore hints; (f) a cancelled attempt does not record a hint. The moved client-runtime unit test covers the hint store. Run focused vitest for apps/web runtime, packages/client-runtime connection and apps/mobile connection.

Needs a decision

This changes the web and desktop saved-pairing auth flow: the credential would be validated by the ws-token request instead of a pre-socket session check, and non-secret session metadata (role, expiry, auth descriptor) would persist in browser localStorage. Mobile already shipped this pattern in #710, so it is a small, precedented decision, but it is still an auth-semantics change and should be approved explicitly. Moving it into client-runtime also fixes the mobile-only fork of saved-session auth policy that AGENTS.md says to avoid.

Value low · effort M · risk medium

Done#113 Thread window snapshots carry full activity payloads (up to 5 MiB for 150 activities on the user's DB), exceed the 4 MiB hosted relay cap, and any non-retryable window error falls back permanently to the unbounded legacy subscribeThread

client-runtime-sync:thread-window-full-activity-payloads · original impact Medium, effort M · Reliability

Current state

Confirmed DONE. The finding said windows could go past the 4 MiB relay cap and then fall back for good to the unbounded legacy subscribeThread. Both are fixed in current code, and all four proposal parts landed: (1) a 1 MiB payload budget on window and history-page activities, counted by SQLite length() without parsing, with hasMoreBefore set correctly; (2) previews that keep payload structure (8 KiB for tool rows, 64 KiB for the rest), getActivityPayload wired on server, client and hosted access policy (viewer/read), and expand-to-fetch in the web timeline; (3) legacy fallback only for 'Unknown request tag' or 'Bounded thread history is unavailable', shrink-and-retry on the relay too-large error, and backoff retry for every other failure; (4) a walking size estimate instead of stringify plus TextEncoder. Migration 088, in the same commit 36760bffd, also rewrote legacy oversized tool rows, so stored payloads behind the 3-5 MiB measurements are smaller too. The Hub vendors Ryco at 7bc39eec3, which includes all four commits, so hosted web clients get the fix. The remaining issues are rare edge cases that do not reopen the finding.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:189-210 THREAD_WINDOW_ACTIVITY_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 1 MiB. takeNewestRowsWithinByteBudget always keeps the newest row, and hasMoreBefore = rows.length > kept.length, which is correct with limit+1 input.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:2140-2163 listNewestThreadActivityRows selects length(CAST(payload_json AS BLOB)) AS payloadBytes, so the budget uses stored byte size.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3881-3886 getThreadWindow applies toSentActivityRows(preview) and then the byte budget. history.activities.hasMoreBefore comes from the budget, so pagination continues from the window's edge.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:4276-4290 getThreadHistoryPage applies the same budget and preview to activity pages.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/activityPayloadPreview.ts:26-37,131-173 Previews cut strings and arrays but keep scalars and keys, so command, exit code, changed files and the numeric additions/deletions in collapsed rows survive. getActivityPayload is capped at 2 MiB.
  • apps/server/src/ws/orchestrationRpc.ts:173-199,442-446,618-650 loadThreadWindow forwards activityPayloads. getActivityPayload is wired. subscribeThreadWindow uses loadThreadWindow.
  • packages/shared/src/rpcAccessPolicy.ts:103,361 getActivityPayload is allowed for hosted viewer/read roles, so expanding a previewed row works over the relay.
  • apps/server/src/ws/RpcByteSession.ts:301-321 An over-cap Chunk or Exit is replaced with an Exit die carrying 'The response exceeded the largest message this connection can carry.' This is the message the client classifies as response-too-large.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts:112-118,145-154,381-396 The too-large message is not a retryable transport error, so it reaches classifyFailure and becomes 'response-too-large'. isUnsupportedRpcError matches only 'Unknown request tag'.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:175-204,612-654 Legacy is used only for 'unsupported'. response-too-large halves messages and activities down to a floor of 10. Any other failure retries the bounded window with backoff (1 s to 30 s).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.test.ts:561-583 Tests cover legacy only for unsupported servers, shrinking on too-large, and backoff retry instead of legacy on load failure.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.test.ts:2531-2627 Test: a 5 MiB activity is previewed in preview mode, and the full payload is returned on request. A client that does not ask for previews gets a byte-bounded window instead.
Defects in the shipped fix

No defect reopens the finding. The residuals are rare edge cases. (a) Mobile (apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:582) does not request previews. If the newest activity alone is over the relay cap, the thread cannot open. That needs a file_change diff or image_view row, which ingestion exempts from the 16k string cap (apps/server/src/orchestration/activityDataCap.ts:24). The same applies to a history page whose first row is that large, since the budget always keeps one row. The window shrinks to 10/10 and then stops (supervision.ts:627-634). (b) Live thread.activity-appended events are never previewed, on any client. One such exempt row over 4 MiB on the relay hits too_large, and the client then shrinks the window, which is unnecessary because the window was not the problem. Hosted resubscribes take a fresh snapshot, so web recovers, but repeated events walk the limits down to the give-up state. (c) The give-up state is silent: only a console.warn, no thread error state and no retry until reconnect or re-retain. Shrunk windowLimits also stay for the lifetime of the entry. (d) threadExport (packages/client-runtime/src/connection/threadExport.ts:90) and inbox context handoff (apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/inboxContextHandoff.ts:67) call getThreadWindow and getThreadHistoryPage without activityPayloads: 'preview'. They fit under the cap thanks to the budget but download full payloads they never use. Export keeps only id, kind, summary, boundary and forkOrigin. (e) The server still JSON-parses limit+1 full payloads and previews all of them before the budget cuts. That is CPU only, and smaller since migration 088.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Partial#114 Shell snapshot is one unbounded JSON message (includes archived threads), decoded 3× on the server, and breaks over the hosted relay above ~4 MiB

client-runtime-sync:monolithic-unbounded-shell-snapshot · original impact Medium, effort L · Reliability WP05

Current state

PARTIAL is right. The two parts that mattered are fixed and shipped to the Hub. First, the shell snapshot is paged: every client in the shared client-runtime asks for 'paged' delivery, so the server sends messages of at most 1 MiB, under the 4 MiB relay cap, and the client reassembles them into one snapshot it applies at once. Second, the extra whole-snapshot decodeShellSnapshot is gone, and a test checks that per-row decoding already normalizes. The Hub vendors 7bc39eec3, which contains both commits, so hosted web pages too. Not done: archived threads are still in every boot snapshot, no wire fields were trimmed, and there is no Worker decode. The paging fix also has a defect the auditor missed. pageShellSnapshot always starts a new message for archived threads. Every RPC chunk waits for a client ack, and the client gains nothing from the split because the assembler holds everything until snapshot-end. So any user with at least one archived thread gets 2 messages instead of 1, which adds a full round trip before the shell can be applied. On hosted web that round trip goes through the relay and happens on every connect, because hosted never resumes. The user's real DB has 27 archived of 323 live threads.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/shellSnapshotPages.ts:74 `if (archived.length > 0 && (page.length > 0 || message.length > 0)) closeMessage();` The message always holds at least snapshot-begin, so any archived thread forces a second message even when the whole shell fits in one 1 MiB page.
  • apps/server/node_modules/effect/src/rpc/RpcServer.ts:457 With supportsAck, streamEffect writes each emitted array as one Chunk and then waits on latch.await before pulling the next one. RpcByteSession (relay) sets supportsAck: true (apps/server/src/ws/RpcByteSession.ts:328). The client sends Ack only after offering the chunk (effect RpcClient.ts:600-610). So each page message costs one round trip.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/shellSnapshotAssembly.ts:41 The assembler buffers snapshot-threads and emits only at snapshot-end. Nothing uses the unarchived-first split to apply early, so the split is pure latency. archivedThreadCount is read nowhere except tests.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:857 resumeShell is false when hostedGeneration !== null. Hosted web takes a full shell snapshot on every connect and reconnect, so it pays the extra relay round trip every time.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/shellSnapshotPages.test.ts:65 The test 'sends unarchived threads first and starts the archive in a new message' asserts messages.length === 2 for a tiny shell. The extra message is deliberate, not accidental.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:747 shellSnapshotItems pages when snapshotDelivery === 'paged'. It is used for the initial snapshot (:876) and for non-delta priority re-ranks (:779). Web and mobile both pass applyThreadPriorities and so subscribe with threadPriorities 'delta' (packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:294), so shipped clients never get full re-rank snapshots.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsRpcClient.ts:1090 The shared client always sends snapshotDelivery: 'paged'.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/constants.ts:54 ORCHESTRATION_SHELL_SNAPSHOT_PAGE_MAX_BYTES = 1 MiB. The relay cap is min(RELAY_MAX_RPC_MESSAGE_BYTES = 4 MiB, maxQueuedBytes 8 MiB - control 256 KiB) (RelayChannelRegistry.ts:726).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:111 decodeShellSnapshot was removed (git grep finds no occurrence). Row schemas apply the wire normalizations, guarded by ProjectionSnapshotQuery.shell.test.ts:81.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:878 listActiveThreadShellRows filters only on deleted_at IS NULL, so archived threads stay in the boot shell (proposal part 3 not done).
  • packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:874 OrchestrationSession still carries threadId, runtimeSessionId and lastError. It is unchanged since f1be4abc7 (part 4 not done).
  • apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/inboxSidebarModel.ts:712 The sidebar reads thread.session.lastError for errorDetail. Part 4 as proposed (move lastError to thread detail) would break this shell consumer. Only session.threadId is truly redundant.
Remaining

(a) Defect in the fix. shellSnapshotPages.ts:74 forces archived threads into a separate message, which adds one ack round trip before a paged snapshot can be applied whenever any archived thread exists. No client gets anything back for it: shellSnapshotAssembly.ts applies only at snapshot-end, and archivedThreadCount is unused. Hosted web is hit on every connect because it never resumes (service.ts:857). (b) Archived threads are still loaded and sent in every boot snapshot (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:878 listActiveThreadShellRows filters only deleted_at, and buildShell is at :3010). Real data: 27 of 323 live threads are archived (8%), so excluding them saves about 8% of a roughly 420 KiB payload. (c) Wire trimming not done (contracts orchestration.ts:874). Only session.threadId is truly redundant. lastError is used by the sidebar (inboxSidebarModel.ts:712), so it cannot move to thread detail as proposed. (d) No Worker decode on web (part 5). (e) snapshot-begin (projects plus worktrees) is still one unpaged message. That is a theoretical bound only.

Defects in the shipped fix

1) Extra round trip (missed by the auditor). pageShellSnapshot always closes the message before the archived threads (shellSnapshotPages.ts:74). Each message is one RPC Chunk, and with supportsAck the server waits for the client's Ack before sending the next one (effect RpcServer.ts:438/457, RpcByteSession.ts:328). The assembler withholds the snapshot until snapshot-end. So a shell that fits in one page now needs 2 messages and 1 more round trip than the old single 'snapshot' item whenever at least one thread is archived. Over the hosted relay that is a browser-Hub-node round trip on every connect, since hosted does not resume shells. The 'show unarchived before the archive arrives' benefit named in the code comments and the contract doc (orchestration.ts OrchestrationShellSnapshotDelivery) is not implemented by any client. 2) Minor: an extra per-thread JSON.stringify to size pages (shellSnapshotPages.ts:10/64). This is under 1 ms at 323 threads, and only the initial snapshot pays it for shipped clients, which take priority deltas. 3) Correction to the auditor: re-rank full snapshots do not reach the shipped web or mobile clients, because both use threadPriorities 'delta'. 4) A thread-count mismatch only console.warns and still applies (shellSnapshotAssembly.ts:56). This is acceptable because the server builds counts from the same array.

Implementation sketch

Recommended (S, low risk): remove the forced archive split. In apps/server/src/ws/context/shellSnapshotPages.ts, drop line 74 (`if (archived.length > 0 && ...) closeMessage();`) so archived threads fill the same page budget. The unarchived-first order can stay because it does no harm, or the original snapshot order can be restored. Then a shell under 1 MiB is again exactly one message ([begin, threads, end]) and one ack. Update the doc comment at shellSnapshotPages.ts:20-25 and the OrchestrationShellSnapshotDelivery/BeginItem comments in packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts (~1266-1280) so they no longer promise an early unarchived view. Keep archivedThreadCount for wire compatibility or mark it informational. Tests: change shellSnapshotPages.test.ts 'sends unarchived threads first and starts the archive in a new message' to expect one message when under budget, and add a case where the archive spills over only once the budget is exceeded. The server.test.ts paged test (~6158) still passes because its order assertion holds. Run `bun run test` scoped to apps/server (shellSnapshotPages.test.ts, server.test.ts -t 'pages the shell') and packages/client-runtime (shellSnapshotAssembly.test.ts). Optional, same file: size pages more cheaply by stringifying the whole snapshot once and returning a single message when it fits (the common case). Fall back to per-thread sizing only above the budget, so the extra O(n) stringify is skipped for most homes. The alternative, keeping the split and having the assembler emit a provisional unarchived snapshot, needs a partial-snapshot concept in the threads store (syncShellSnapshot replaces the thread set, which would briefly drop archived threads). Not worth it at current sizes. Not recommended now: (3) excluding archived threads from the boot shell, with a paged archived-threads RPC used by the archive views, mobile and cliRemote --include-archived. That is L effort, changes archive and search behaviour, and saves about 8% for this user. (4) Making session.threadId optional saves about 40 B per thread with a session and requires a mixed-version window, since old clients decode it as required. lastError must stay. (5) A Worker decode is not justified at about 420 KiB.

client-runtime-sync:shell-sql-reads-deleted-rows · original impact Low, effort S · Database

Current state

Confirmed DONE. Every shell build goes through buildShell (WS subscriptions, Hub mirror, Agent Control, storage, workspace lifecycle). It uses live-only SQL: threads WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, sessions restricted to live threads, latest turns joined to live threads, and worktrees of live projects. latestCompletedTurnAt is a trigger-maintained column (migration 087, registered and also run as a post-migrator repair), so the per-row correlated subquery is gone. The JS deletedAt filter is gone, and concurrent builds are coalesced. A read-only run on the user's real DB (791 threads, 323 live) took 0.68 ms for the live thread query (323 rows), 0.32 ms for live sessions (313 of 732), 0.39 ms for live latest turns and 0.04 ms for updatedAt. The report had 5.47 ms for threads alone. Only the optional partial index is missing, and it is worth well under 0.5 ms.

  • apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations/087_ProjectionThreadAnchorsAndStatisticsPartials.ts:32-221 Adds the column, plus triggers on thread insert and on turns/sessions insert, update and delete, plus a backfill. Registered at apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations.ts:231 and repaired post-migration at :536-546/:746. ProjectionThreads.ts:45/115 upserts with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE without touching the column, and the column has no other writers, so the trigger value survives.

Only the optional partial index from the proposal is missing. There is no index ON projection_threads(created_at, thread_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL in apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations, so listActiveThreadShellRows (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:878-889) still does a full table scan plus a temp B-tree sort. None material. Done#116 Per-event JSON.stringify for byte accounting (server and client) and O(subscriptions) replay-metric publication per event

client-runtime-sync:per-event-size-accounting-and-metrics · original impact Low, effort S · CPU

Current state

Confirmed DONE, all landed in 60633eff3 (#710), with 79b492cd6 and 8fb94df00 on top. Server: each live orchestration event is measured once. orchestrationEventBytes memoizes the size per event object in a WeakMap. The engine's PubSub hands the same object to every subscriber, so the offer, the coalescer (push, supersede, emit), the batch release and the chunk splitter of every subscription share one measurement, and the byte ledger stays balanced by construction. Release and recordLiveDequeued run once per drained array, and replay metrics once per replay page. Replay metrics: every record() is O(1) via incremental sums and RunningMax. Gauges are written only when the aggregate value changes. A stale maximum settles synchronously for up to 8 subscriptions, otherwise through one delayed rescan per stream per second. I traced RunningMax update/add/remove/settle and found no correctness bug. Client: supervision.ts has no JSON.stringify or TextEncoder left. Live events size only the changed row (text.length for messages, an O(nodes) walk for activities and plans). Snapshots and pages use the same walk, which treats string length as O(1). Eviction planning and the per-environment timer reconcile are coalesced to once per delivered chunk (microtask), and on web the reconcile runs once per animation-frame batch. Remaining per-event costs are constant per event or per subscription, not O(S) per event or O(text) per subscription.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreamBatching.ts:18-32 WeakMap<OrchestrationEvent, number> cache. approximateJsonBytes runs at most once per event object.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationEngine.ts:217 PubSub.publish passes the same persisted event object to every subscriber (subscribeDomainEvents at :679-680), so the cache is shared across subscriptions.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationEventCoalescing.ts:132,153,159,165 All coalescer measurements go through orchestrationEventBytes and hit the cache. The offer receives the precomputed size.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:116-153 offerOrchestrationLiveEventOrFail uses input.eventBytes. It measures only when no precomputed size is passed and a ledger exists.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:197-204 releaseQueuedEventsBytes sums cached sizes for a drained batch and does one Ref.update.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:661-674 drainLiveQueue releases bytes and calls recordLiveDequeued once per drained array.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:850,960,971 Replay metrics are recorded per replay page via tapArray. The chunk splitter's sizeOf uses the cached size.
  • apps/server/src/wsReplayMetrics.ts:108-148 RunningMax keeps the maximum in O(1) with a holder count and a stale flag. I traced the update, add and remove branches and they are correct.
  • apps/server/src/wsReplayMetrics.ts:163-233 StreamReplayAggregate keeps the buffer-depth sum and maxima incrementally. It rescans only stale maxima.
  • apps/server/src/wsReplayMetrics.ts:258-299 publishAggregateFor writes only the gauges whose aggregate changed, and returns Effect.void otherwise.
  • apps/server/src/wsReplayMetrics.ts:339-349 record() is O(1). It settles synchronously only for up to 8 subscriptions, otherwise once per WS_REPLAY_METRICS_SETTLE_MS (1 s) per stream.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/approximateJsonSize.ts:12-43 The walk estimate counts strings as length+2 (O(1) per string), so its cost is O(nodes), not O(text bytes).
Defects in the shipped fix

No defect in the implemented fix. Minor residuals that do not reopen the finding: (1) The first measurement of each live event is still a full JSON.stringify plus TextEncoder.encode (packages/shared/src/perf.ts:54-66, called from orchestrationStreamBatching.ts:29). I measured about 14 us for a 20 KB streaming subagent activity and about 68 us for 100 KB, once per event, including frames the coalescer later drops. A walk would be about 0.4 us. Keeping exact UTF-8 bytes is defensible, though: they feed the 256 KiB chunk splitter and the 4 MiB queue budget, and a length walk undercounts non-ASCII by up to 3x and escaped control characters by up to 6x. (2) updateGauge (wsReplayMetrics.ts:252-256) builds a new Metric.withAttributes transform on every write. In effect@4.0.2 that creates a fresh merged attribute set, so the base gauge's hook recomputes makeKey (Object.entries, sort, JSON.stringify) on each write. liveBufferDepth and replayLag change on almost every enqueue and dequeue, so this is about 2-3 small key builds per event per subscription: constant, microseconds each. (3) An adjacent path outside this finding has the same pattern: the terminal subscriber ledger measures each terminal event twice per subscriber with approximateJsonBytes, at offer (apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.ts:100) and again at release (:73). Terminal events are shared objects from Manager.publishEvent (apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:1056-1067).
