Partial#117 WebSocket compression is off; large snapshots to remote and saved environments travel uncompressed (8× compressible)

client-runtime-sync:no-permessage-deflate-remote · original impact Low, effort S · Network / RTT WP03decision

First-pass audit said PARTIAL; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

PARTIAL is confirmed. Since 60633eff3 the Node server enables permessage-deflate with exactly the proposed parameters, and desktop-mode backends skip it for direct loopback peers. Three gaps remain. (1) The fix applies one WebSocketServer config to every route, so the H.264 /ws/device-frames socket now negotiates deflate too. deviceFrame.ts says that path is 'deliberately excluded from per-message deflate', and that is no longer true, which is a small regression. (2) The iOS app gets no compression on direct connections because RN iOS uses SocketRocket, which has no permessage-deflate, so the cellular benefit the finding cites is not realized. (3) The hosted relay still has no compress-before-encrypt. The Bun branch also has no compression option, but it only runs the desktop dev backend over loopback, so that gap does not matter.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:265 The NodeHttpServer layer now gets websocket: { perMessageDeflate: WEBSOCKET_PER_MESSAGE_DEFLATE }. This one ws WebSocketServer (platform-node NodeHttpServer.ts:143, noServer) handles upgrades on every route: /ws, /ws/device and /ws/device-frames.
  • apps/server/src/webSocketCompression.ts:19 Threshold 16 KiB, level 1, server and client no context takeover, as proposed. ws applies the threshold per message (ws/lib/sender.js:382), and Effect's writer calls send with the default compress: true, so RPC frames of 16 KiB or more are deflated.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:257 In desktop mode, skipWebSocketCompressionForLoopbackPeers deletes sec-websocket-extensions for direct loopback upgrades. It is registered before installHttpStartupGate (httpStartupGate.ts:101-104 ignores earlier listeners), and held upgrades replay the same mutated request, so the order is correct. Covered by webSocketCompression.test.ts:76-82.
  • packages/shared/src/deviceFrame.ts:15 This comment says the device-frame socket is 'deliberately excluded from per-message deflate (H.264 is already compressed)'. It was written when deflate was globally off (ec9571c2f). Nothing in webSocketCompression.ts or deviceFrameRoute.ts:97 strips the offer for DEVICE_FRAME_WS_PATH, so browsers watching the simulator remotely (or via loopback on a web-mode node) now have every frame of 16 KiB or more (keyframes, many P-frames) deflated at level 1 for no size gain.
  • node_modules/.bun/ws@8.21.3/node_modules/ws/lib/permessage-deflate.js:70 ws uses one process-wide zlib Limiter (default concurrency 10) for all sockets. A 30-60 fps video stream deflating incompressible frames competes with RPC snapshot compression and adds latency to both.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:240 BunHttpServer.layer still has no websocket option, although platform-bun supports websocket.perMessageDeflate (BunHttpServer.ts:84). The only Bun runtime is the desktop development backend (apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3189 resolveDevelopmentBunExecutable). Packaged desktop runs Electron as Node (backendLauncher.ts:111), and the CLI runs under node (apps/server/package.json:20,23). So this gap is loopback/dev-only and negligible.
  • apps/mobile/src/platform/socket.ts:9 The mobile app uses the RN global WebSocket. In RN 0.86.3, iOS backs it with SocketRocket (react-native/scripts/cocoapods/rndependencies.rb:30, React/CoreModules/RCTWebSocketModule.mm:16), which does not implement permessage-deflate. iOS direct saved-environment connections over LAN, Tailscale or cellular therefore stay uncompressed. Android's OkHttp 4.9.2 does negotiate it.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayEngine.ts:538 The relay send entry dispatches straight to the negotiating buffer, the E2EE seal or the plaintext chunker, with no compression step. Receive delivery at :1230 has no inflate step either. Node side: apps/server/src/hubConnector/RelayChannelRegistry.ts:748 chunks raw RPC bytes. A grep for deflate, gzip, CompressionStream, fflate or pako across client-runtime, shared relay, hubConnector and apps/mobile finds no compression.
  • packages/contracts/src/relay.ts:49 RELAY_MAX_RPC_MESSAGE_BYTES = 4 MiB applies to uncompressed relay messages. A 2k-thread shell snapshot (3.2 MiB) is close to this hard ceiling, so compression would also add headroom, not just save bytes.
  • ryco-hub:src/relay/websocketRuntime.ts:1066 On Hub origin/main, relay sockets use perMessageDeflate: false (also hubSession.ts:453). That is correct for ciphertext, so any relay compression has to be end-to-end inside the opaque payload.
Remaining

(a) Regression: /ws/device-frames negotiates permessage-deflate (deviceFrame.ts:15 says it must not; deviceFrameRoute.ts:97 upgrades through the same deflate-enabled server configured at server.ts:265). (b) iOS app: SocketRocket (RN 0.86.3) never offers permessage-deflate, so direct saved-environment traffic to iOS stays uncompressed. (c) Hosted relay: no compress-before-encrypt at relayEngine.ts:538/1230 or RelayChannelRegistry.ts:748, and the Hub correctly cannot help. Large shell snapshots, ServerConfig and thread windows cross the relay at full size, pay full ChaCha cost, and count against the 4 MiB RELAY_MAX_RPC_MESSAGE_BYTES ceiling. Negligible: the Bun branch (server.ts:240) has no websocket compression option, but only the loopback desktop dev backend uses it.

Defects in the shipped fix

The fix enables deflate for every upgrade route through the single shared ws WebSocketServer. That silently drops the documented exclusion of the H.264 device-frame socket (packages/shared/src/deviceFrame.ts:13-16). For remote browser viewers, and loopback viewers of web-mode nodes, simulator frames of 16 KiB or more are now deflated at level 1 for no gain. This costs threadpool CPU and per-frame latency, and the frames compete with RPC compression in ws's process-wide zlib limiter (concurrency 10). No test covers the exclusion. The stale comment is now misleading. Nothing else is wrong: loopback detection, header-based proxy detection, listener ordering against the startup gate, and the parameters all look correct.

Implementation sketch

1. Device-frame exclusion (S, low risk). In apps/server/src/webSocketCompression.ts, replace skipWebSocketCompressionForLoopbackPeers with a general installWebSocketCompressionPolicy(server, { skipDirectLoopback: boolean }). Register it in all modes at server.ts:257 (skipDirectLoopback = config.mode === 'desktop'). It deletes request.headers['sec-websocket-extensions'] when the upgrade path (new URL(request.url, 'http://x').pathname) equals DEVICE_FRAME_WS_PATH from @ryco/shared/deviceFrame, or when skipDirectLoopback && isDirectLoopbackUpgrade(request). Extend webSocketCompression.test.ts negotiatedExtensions to accept a path, and assert that '/ws/device-frames' from a non-loopback-skipped peer negotiates '' while '/ws' still negotiates permessage-deflate. Keep the deviceFrame.ts comment accurate. 2. Optional, trivial: add websocket: { perMessageDeflate: true } to BunHttpServer.layer at server.ts:240 for parity. Low value because only the dev desktop backend runs there. 3. Application-level compression for relay and iOS direct (M, needs a decision). Compress at the RPC-message seam, above both E2EE and chunking. Client: packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayEngine.ts send() before the mode dispatch at :543, and #deliver at :1230 after reassembly. Node: apps/server/src/hubConnector/RelayChannelRegistry.ts before prepareRelayMessage at :748, and in its inbound reassembly path. Use a framing marker inside the opaque payload, following the RELAY_CHUNK_CAPABILITY_PRELUDE pattern in packages/shared/src/relayMessageChunks.ts: a leading NUL-prefixed header (JSON never starts with 0x00) with magic, version and a deflate-raw flag, plus a whitespace-prelude capability advertisement so mixed-version peers stay compatible. This needs no Hub or wire change. Compress only messages of 16 KiB or more, at level 1, and keep the result only if it shrinks the message. Cap the inflated size at RELAY_MAX_RPC_MESSAGE_BYTES and fail the channel with transfer_limit beyond it (zip-bomb guard). Put the codec in packages/shared (new relayMessageCompression.ts) so client and node share it. Use node:zlib deflateRawSync on the node side, and on clients either DecompressionStream('deflate-raw') (web) or a small pure-JS inflater such as fflate (Hermes has no CompressionStream). That one codec also covers iOS direct if a later step applies it to WsTransport, or the iOS socket could be swapped for a native module whose WebSocket supports compression. Tests: shared codec round-trip and bomb-cap tests, relayEngine and RelayChannelRegistry tests that legacy peers without the prelude get uncompressed payloads, and E2EE-mode tests confirming compression happens before submit/seal and sizes are checked post-compression in planRelayMessage.

Needs a decision

The device-frame exclusion (item 1) needs no decision. Relay compression (item 3) does. It is compress-before-encrypt inside the E2EE channel, so ciphertext lengths would depend on content. When attacker-influenced text (agent output, repo content) and secrets share one RPC message, that gives a CRIME/BREACH-style length side channel to the Hub, which is the party E2EE protects against. This needs a security review and possibly per-RPC opt-out. It also changes the opaque relay payload format (client-runtime and the node's hubConnector, and the Hub vendors Ryco), even though the Hub itself never parses it.

Value medium · effort M · risk medium

Done#118 Each thread-priority ranking re-sends the full shell snapshot to every subscriber (and priority handling is inconsistent)

client-runtime-sync:priority-change-full-snapshot-fanout · original impact Low, effort M · Network / RTT

Current state

Confirmed DONE. The cost and both bugs from the finding are gone. Every current client (web, desktop through web, mobile) asks for threadPriorities:"delta". A ranking now sends those clients one small thread-priorities item, read once per server and shared by all subscribers. The client patches only the summaries whose priority changed. Older clients still get a full snapshot, but the read is shared (single-flight plus coalesceConcurrentRuns). getThreadShellById includes the projected priority, so an upsert no longer erases it. The snapshot updatedAt includes rankedAt, so a re-rank at an unchanged sequence counts as 'newer'. I found no other caller that turns a ranking into a full snapshot. The CLI remote takes only the first snapshot. ensureCurrent callers do not refetch the shell. Expired rankings are filtered on the client by isUsableThreadPriorityRanking. Only a minor ordering race remains, and I traced its actual mechanism (see fixDefects).

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:761-782 priorityStream: a delta client gets {kind:'thread-priorities', priorities} from listThreadPriorities. Any other client gets a fallback snapshot. Both reads go through joinPriorityLoad.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:50-101 joinPriorityLoad single-flight. It lives in a module-level WeakMap keyed by the shared projectionSnapshotQuery, so subscribers on different connections join the same load.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:788-801,866-877 A resumed delta client gets the current rankings right after the resumed marker. Priority items are merged in only after the head snapshot or resumed items.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:1262-1271 coordinator.changes is wired once into makeOrchestrationStreamHelpers. subscribeShell (orchestrationRpc.ts:518-548) is the only production user of makeReplayableShellStream, and it is unscoped, so the unscoped listThreadPriorities leaks nothing.
  • apps/server/src/threadPriority/ThreadPriorityRepository.ts:135-176 replace() deletes every ranking and the single batch slot before inserting. So 'every currently usable ranking' is exactly the latest batch, as the proposal asked.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3481-3560 getThreadShellById reads listThreadPriorityRows(threadId), a PK lookup on thread_priority_rankings.thread_id (migration 053), and attaches priority. The upsert-erases-priority bug is fixed.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3104-3109 The snapshot updatedAt takes maxIso over ranking rankedAt. Because classifyProjectionSnapshot compares sequence first and then updatedAt (projectionTracker.ts:8-29), a re-rank snapshot is now classified 'newer'.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3205-3216 getShellSnapshot outside transactions goes through coalesceConcurrentRuns, so the fallback snapshot path is shared too.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:286-294 Routes thread-priorities to applyThreadPriorities and asks for delta whenever the host supplies the callback. Web wires it at apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:888, mobile at apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:514.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:1022-1077 Priority items share the shell batcher (FIFO with upserts, one store commit) and skip the sequence check.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:3677-3702 applyThreadPriorities replaces priority only on changed summaries. Unchanged rows keep their identity, and it is a no-op when nothing changed. Priority lives only on SidebarThreadSummary (types.ts:275), and the only reader is threadInbox.ts:572.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/sharedThreadShellReads.ts:27-75 The shared (threadId, sequence) read cache with a 2 s TTL is how a pre-ranking upsert can reach a second subscriber after its thread-priorities item (see fixDefects).
Defects in the shipped fix

Minor, low impact: a thread upsert can still briefly revert a fresh ranking on the client. The delta item has no sequence, so the auditor flagged this ordering issue in general terms. I traced the actual mechanism. For a single subscriber the race is effectively closed. getThreadShellById's queries run sequentially on the one connection, so the priority read lands either before or after the ranking transaction. A pre-commit upsert is also offered to the merge before the post-commit priorities load finishes. The real window is readSharedThreadShell (apps/server/src/ws/context/sharedThreadShellReads.ts:42-75). Its (threadId, sequence) entries live for 2 s. Suppose subscriber A read a thread's shell just before a ranking committed. A slower or backpressured subscriber B (hosted relay, mobile) that maps the same event up to 2 s later gets the pre-ranking priority from the cache, possibly after B already received the thread-priorities item. That thread then shows its old or no priority until its next upsert or the next actual ranking. A cache-hit ensureCurrent publishes nothing. The impact is small: AI Focus is opt-in, a ranking takes seconds of LLM time, and active threads re-upsert quickly. A small correction to the auditor: the remark that the item carries 'every usable ranking rather than only the latest batch' is moot. replace() wipes all rankings, so the two sets are the same.

Implementation sketch

Optional hardening for the race, effort S. (1) In apps/server/src/ws/context/sharedThreadShellReads.ts export invalidateSharedThreadShellReads(query: object), which clears tables.get(query). Alternatively, add a priority generation to the cache key. (2) Call it as soon as a ranking commits. The cleanest place is a single fiber in apps/server/src/ws/context.ts (next to makeOrchestrationStreamHelpers at ~1262) that runs coordinator.changes and invalidates for projectionSnapshotQuery. Another option is a Stream.tap in priorityStream (orchestrationStreams.ts:761) ahead of the joinPriorityLoad mapEffect. For a fully closed window, have ThreadPriorityCoordinator expose a generation counter bumped right after repository.replace and inside the lock, and include it in the readSharedThreadShell key. In orchestrationStreamBatching.test.ts, two shell subscribers where the first caches a pre-ranking upsert, a ranking is then published, and the second subscriber's upsert of the same event carries the new priority.

Partial#119 Shell re-syncs replace every thread object, and thread-detail events commit one zustand set per event

client-runtime-sync:client-store-identity-churn-and-unbatched-detail-events · original impact Low, effort M · Rendering WP11WP14A

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor marked this DONE and saw no defect in the web fix. However, #710's web batching made coalesceOrchestrationUiEvents active on multi-event detail batches. A streaming delta followed by the empty-text completion of the same message now coalesces into a non-streaming replacement, which drops earlier message text. That always affects legacy token streaming and affects default-mode messages over 24k chars. The auditor also listed mobile's unbatched detail path only as a side note, but it is the same problem in the intended phone app, so the status is PARTIAL rather than DONE. The structural-sharing half of the finding is done as the auditor described.

Current state

The structural sharing part is done: syncEnvironmentShellSnapshot reuses unchanged projects, worktrees, shells, sessions, turn states, summaries, id lists and record containers, and the equality helpers cover every field. Web thread-detail events are frame-batched through createEnvironmentEventBatcher (#710). The batching turned on a latent bug, though. coalesceOrchestrationUiEvents in web applyRecoveredEventBatch used to be an identity function because every call had one event. It now merges a streaming delta and the following empty-text completion of the same message into one non-streaming event that carries only the delta text. The reducer treats non-streaming text as a replacement, so the assistant message loses all earlier text in the live view. Mobile, the intended phone app, still commits once per detail event.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:2064-2213 syncEnvironmentShellSnapshot reuses each previous object through plainDataEqual, sidebarWorktreesEqual, threadShellsEqual, threadSessionsEqual, threadTurnStatesEqual and sidebarThreadSummariesEqual. reuseUnchangedRecord, reuseUnchangedIds and reuseUnchangedIdsByKey keep the containers. Checked against types.ts:196-334 and the contract schemas: no compared field is missing. environmentId is not compared on summaries, but it is constant per environment. The snapshot-identity part of the finding is done.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/eventBatching.ts:42-143 createEnvironmentEventBatcher batches per frame with a 100 ms fallback and a 512-event bound. It is registered as a store mutation barrier. Added by 60633eff3 (#710) and tested in storeStructuralSharing.test.ts:287-442.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:804-814 threadDetailEventBatcher sends N detail events into one applyRecoveredEventBatch call. The web per-event commit is gone.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:679-713 REGRESSION. When two consecutive message-sent events share a messageId, coalesceOrchestrationUiEvents builds {...event, text: (!event.streaming && event.text.length>0) ? event.text : previous.text + event.text}. For [delta 'tail' streaming:true, complete '' streaming:false] it emits {text:'tail', streaming:false}. Before #710 the function only ever saw one event (f1be4abc7 service.ts:768), so it did nothing.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:736 The coalesced uiEvents, not the raw events, go to environmentStateSink.applyOrchestrationEvents.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:1663-1682 mergeMessageUpdate: if message.streaming is false and its text is non-empty, that text replaces existing.text. The coalesced event {text:'tail', streaming:false} therefore wipes the text already stored for the message. A node simulation of both functions (/tmp/verify119/sim.mjs) gives 'Earlier streamed text. tail chunk' when applied event by event and 'tail chunk' when frame-batched.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/decider.ts:2907-2932 thread.message.assistant.complete emits message-sent with text `command.text ?? ""` and streaming:false. Without an attachment delivery the text is empty.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:2461-2464 Legacy token streaming mode (user toggle, settings.ts:618): every non-delta runtime event, including item.completed, first flushes the live tail delta. finalizeAssistantMessage (1813-1901) then dispatches the empty complete right after it. The two events arrive back to back and land in one client frame, so the message is cut down to its last chunk.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:1685-1702 Default buffered mode: past MAX_BUFFERED_ASSISTANT_CHARS (24,000, line 176) the buffer spills as a streaming delta in an earlier frame. At completion, finalize sends delta(remainder) followed by complete(''). The coalescer merges these two, so any assistant message over 24k chars is cut to the remainder until a resubscribe or reload.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/threadDetailEvents.ts:16-19 The mobile comment says coalesceOrchestrationUiEvents 'is identity for the single-event detail path'. That assumption broke on web when #710 batched the detail path.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/threadDetailEvents.ts:62 Mobile still applies one event per batch: `(environmentId, event) => applyRecoveredEventBatch([event], environmentId)`, wired at environmentDriver.ts:259 and :646. Each detail event costs one zustand set plus projectionChanged/markEnvironmentSnapshotDirty. Mobile's shell events, by contrast, are batched by the shared supervisor (supervision.ts:1067).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/orchestration/orchestrationRecovery.ts:88 createOrchestrationRecoveryCoordinator is still exported and used only by its test. The optional cleanup was not done.
Remaining

(1) Fix defect, see fixDefects: apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:679-713 coalesceOrchestrationUiEvents now runs on multi-event detail batches and cuts assistant message text when a streaming delta and an empty-text completion of the same message share a frame. (2) Mobile thread-detail events still commit once per event: apps/mobile/src/connection/threadDetailEvents.ts:62, wired at apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:259/:646. (3) Optional: delete the dead createOrchestrationRecoveryCoordinator (packages/client-runtime/src/state/orchestration/orchestrationRecovery.ts:88) and its test.

Defects in the shipped fix

Correctness regression from #710 (60633eff3). The web threadDetailEventBatcher (service.ts:804) now passes multi-event batches into applyRecoveredEventBatch, which runs coalesceOrchestrationUiEvents (service.ts:679-713, used at :736). For consecutive thread.message-sent events with the same messageId, where the earlier one is a streaming delta and the later one is the non-streaming completion with empty text (decider.ts:2907-2932), the coalescer produces one event with streaming:false and text set to just the delta. mergeMessageUpdate (store.ts:1663-1682) reads non-streaming non-empty text as a full replacement, so all text applied in earlier frames is dropped. With legacy token streaming on (a user toggle), almost every assistant message is cut to its last chunk at completion, because the server flushes the live tail and dispatches the complete back to back (ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:2461-2464, 1813-1901). In the default buffered mode, any message over 24,000 chars is cut to the post-spill remainder (ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:176, 1685-1702). Server snapshots stay correct, so a reload or resubscribe repairs the view. No test covers coalesceOrchestrationUiEvents, and the batcher tests do not exercise message coalescing. Confirmed by a node simulation that copies both functions (/tmp/verify119/sim.mjs).

Implementation sketch

A. Fix the regression (do this first). In apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:679-713, either (preferred) remove coalesceOrchestrationUiEvents and pass the raw events to environmentStateSink.applyOrchestrationEvents, or restrict it. Removal is safe because applyOrchestrationEvents in store.ts:3192 already shares one owned message map across consecutive message-sent events via ownedMessageMaps, so a batch costs one commit anyway. To restrict it instead: merge only streaming+streaming pairs (concatenate text, keep previous createdAt, attachments = event ?? previous). Let a non-streaming event with empty text pass through unmerged. A non-streaming event with non-empty text may replace the previous delta, as it does today. Add tests to apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.test.ts, exporting the helper or going through applyEnvironmentThreadDetailEvent + flushEnvironmentThreadDetailEvents with a seeded store: (a) existing assistant text 'Earlier ' plus batch [delta 'tail' streaming, complete '' non-streaming] gives 'Earlier tail' with streaming false; (b) [delta, complete with full text] gives the full text; (c) [delta 'a', delta 'b'] appends 'ab'; (d) a message with no existing text plus [delta 'x', complete ''] gives 'x'. B. Mobile batching, which also removes duplication: move the shared part of applyRecoveredEventBatch (batch effects, applyOrchestrationEvents, draft promotion, draft/terminal cleanup, eviction reconcile) into client-runtime, e.g. packages/client-runtime/src/state/orchestration/applyThreadDetailEventBatch.ts, with web-only hooks (projectSearchInvalidations, syncProjects/syncThreads) as optional sink calls. Both apps then build createEnvironmentEventBatcher({ apply }) around it. In apps/mobile/src/connection/threadDetailEvents.ts, return batcher.enqueue in place of the per-event closure, use the default runtime frameScheduler (mobileFrameScheduler is already configured in apps/mobile/src/state/threadsRuntime.ts:17), and call batcher.dispose when the driver is torn down. Extend apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.test.ts to check that N detail events within one frame produce one applyOrchestrationEvents call and keep their order relative to a following snapshot (the barrier flush). C. Optional: delete createOrchestrationRecoveryCoordinator and orchestrationRecovery.test.ts if nothing else in that module needs them. Checks: focused vitest for apps/web service tests, client-runtime state/threads tests and apps/mobile connection tests, plus typecheck of the touched packages.

Partial#120 wsTransport chunk is ~half contracts schemas for all 199 RPCs, and some server layers are rebuilt per WS connection

client-runtime-sync:wsTransport-chunk-and-per-connection-layers · original impact Low, effort M · Bundle size WP13

First-pass audit said PARTIAL; the verifier corrected it. The auditor's PARTIAL classification and server-side analysis are correct. Their remaining-work plan is wrong in two ways. First, it treats the agent-control RPCs as cold and proposes a lazy agent-control group plus making agentControl.ts unreachable from boot, estimating 30-35 KiB. In fact subscribeProposals is started at shell mount for every connected environment (SidebarPrimaryActions.tsx:196 → useWaitingAutomationRuns → useAutomationProposalSync, and RootAppShell.tsx:100 → MissedAutomationRunsNotice), and its schema needs agentControl.ts:1-1065, which imports device.ts. So neither the agent-control nor the device group split saves much, and agentControl.ts cannot leave the startup path. Second, they missed the real cheap win: about 38 KB of raw source of server-only MCP tool schemas (agentControl.ts:1362-2164, 2390-end) that ship in the client boot chunk only because they share a module with client-used schemas. Minor: wsTransport.ts the file still exists (packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts); only the separate chunk is gone.

Current state

PARTIAL stands. The server half is fixed by #710 (60633eff3). SourceControlDiscovery, ProviderMaintenanceRunner and ContextHandoffInspection are now process-wide in RuntimeServicesLive. Per-connection builds on direct /ws and relay reuse them through the forked CurrentMemoMap; I traced this through effect 4.0.2's MemoMapImpl parent fallthrough, HttpRouter.serve and HubConnectorDeferred. Every leaf of the leftover provisions in ws.ts is also in the server graph. discoverSourceControl serves the 2-minute TTL cache when cached:true is sent. The client half is not done. WsRpcGroup is still monolithic, the main WsTransport uses the merged app+device group, and agentControl.ts, device.ts, changeRequestReview.ts and relay.ts are still in the 895 KB boot chunk, while hostedIdentity, nativeE2ee, nativeHandoff and computer have left it. The auditor's remaining-work plan is wrong, though. The agent-control RPC surface is not cold: subscribeProposals starts at shell mount for every connected environment, and its stream schema needs the whole action-plan part of agentControl.ts, which imports device.ts. So splitting the agent-control or device RPC groups would save almost nothing. The cheap, real remaining win is different: about 38 KB of raw source of server-only MCP tool schemas inside agentControl.ts ship in the client boot chunk, because top-level Schema calls are not tree-shaken within a module.

  • apps/server/src/server.ts:608-612 SourceControlDiscovery.layer, ProviderMaintenanceRunner.layer and ContextHandoffInspectionLive are in RuntimeServicesLive (process-wide). ChatAttachmentUploadsLive is in the runtime base at server.ts:575. All leaves of the ws.ts provisions (VcsDriverRegistry, VcsProjectConfig, GitVcsDriver, ForgejoApi, SourceControlProviderRegistry, ServerSecretStoreLive, AtlassianConnectionRepositoryLive, SqlitePersistenceLayerLive, ContextHandoffRepositoryLive, VcsProcess) are the same objects in server.ts:330-511 and :838, so they hit the memo too.

  • node_modules/.bun/effect@4.0.2/node_modules/effect/src/http/HttpRouter.ts:1382-1395 HttpRouter.serve builds routes with a fork of the launch memo map, so the /ws handler's Effect.provide (ws.ts:87-89) forks again and falls through to the runtime memo map.

Background callers send cached:true (packages/client-runtime/src/sourceControlDiscoveryState.ts:181, apps/web/src/lib/sourceControlDiscoveryState.ts). Only explicit refreshes (SourceControlSettings, CommandPalette) re-probe.

RootAppShell.tsx:100 also mounts MissedAutomationRunsNotice (useAutomationProposalSync at :243). agentControl.subscribeProposals is therefore attempted at shell mount for every connected environment (useAutomationProposalSync.ts:26-60), so the agent-control RPC group is hot, not cold.

Server consumers (~20 files under apps/server/src/agentControl, provider/ProviderDriver.ts, server.ts) import via the @ryco/contracts barrel. The Hub does not import them.
Remaining

Client side only; the server half is done. (1) Main concrete remaining cost: packages/contracts/src/agentControl.ts:1362-2164 (internal provider-session MCP surface, tool inputs, tool results) and :2390-end (external stdio MCP tool catalog) are server-only, about 38 KB of raw source and roughly 15-25 KB minified, yet they are evaluated in the web boot chunk. agentControl.ts is a hot module, imported by the RPC group, by wsRpcClient.ts:13 and by state/agentControl, and Schema declarations are not tree-shaken within a module. (2) Cold RPC payloads are still evaluated at boot because WsRpcGroup and WsDeviceRpcGroup share rpc.ts (rpc.ts:2247,2392,2826) and the main transport uses the merged group (wsTransport.ts:617). Truly cold parts: agent-control integration/MCP-installation admin schemas (agentControl.ts:2164-2390, ~10 KB source), device control-plane payloads (device.ts:311-end, ~23 KB source; device.ts:1-311 stays hot via agentControl.ts:60-71), and changeRequestReview.ts (~18 KB source). relay.ts is pulled in by non-RPC importers. The auditor's main proposal, splitting the agent-control RPCs into a lazy group, would gain almost nothing: subscribeProposals runs at shell mount (SidebarPrimaryActions.tsx:196, RootAppShell.tsx:100) and needs agentControl.ts:1-1065 plus device.ts:1-311.

Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defect in the server fix. Minor: no test asserts that per-connection and relay RPC layers resolve to the process-wide SourceControlDiscovery, ProviderMaintenanceRunner and ContextHandoffInspection instances. The reuse depends on the request or relay fiber still carrying CurrentMemoMap. If that were lost, the fallback provisions in ws.ts:34-60 would silently rebuild those services, and their caches, per connection. The cached flag is opt-in, so older clients still re-probe on every call. That is acceptable, because explicit refresh must bypass the cache.

Implementation sketch

Step A (worth doing, effort S): move the server-only Agent Control MCP schemas out of agentControl.ts. Create packages/contracts/src/agentControlMcp.ts and move agentControl.ts:1362-2164 and :2390-end into it, importing the base identifiers and schemas it needs from ./agentControl.ts (the dependency goes one way only, since nothing client-reachable references the moved code). Add `export * from "./agentControlMcp.ts"` to packages/contracts/src/index.ts. Server code imports these names via the @ryco/contracts barrel, so almost no server import changes are needed; check apps/server/src/agentControl/** and provider/ProviderDriver.ts with typecheck. Optionally add an `./agent-control-mcp` subpath to packages/contracts/package.json. Fix packages/contracts/src/agentControl.test.ts and projectChats.test.ts imports if they reference the moved names via ./agentControl.ts. Verify: run `bun run build --filter=@ryco/web`, then probe apps/web/dist/assets/boot-*.js for distinctive moved literals (e.g. ryco_create_task, the stdio catalog tool descriptions, and the internal-MCP description strings). They should be absent, and the boot chunk should shrink by about 15-25 KB minified. Run focused vitest for packages/contracts and apps/server/src/agentControl, plus bun typecheck. Optional guard: a small vitest that bundles or imports the client entry graph and asserts agentControlMcp.ts is unreachable. Step B (optional, low value, effort M): to also defer the cold RPC payloads, split rpc.ts into feature group modules: WsDeviceRpcGroup in its own module, plus the agent-control integration/MCP-installation admin RPCs and the changeRequestReview RPC. Split device.ts at ~line 311 into hot identifiers/descriptor/availability and cold control-plane payloads. Make the main WsTransport (wsTransport.ts:617) use WsRpcGroup without device. Create secondary RpcClients lazily (dynamic import of the group module) over the same socket protocol; Effect 4's socket protocol already multiplexes clientIds (effect/src/rpc/RpcClient.ts:1249-1254). This needs RpcTransport to expose its protocol and scope for extra clients and to keep admission, latency tracking and reconnect semantics per request. The server keeps serving the merged group on /ws (ws.ts:79), so the wire protocol does not change. Test with the browser suite for device and integrations settings plus wsTransport unit tests. Do not split the agent-control proposal RPCs: they are hot.

Partial#121 The primary local/desktop environment has no persisted shell cache: the sidebar stays empty until the whole network critical path completes

client-runtime-sync:no-local-shell-cache-for-primary · original impact Low, effort L · Caching decision

Current state

Phase 1 is implemented in 45f7a9be6 (plus e664e643f, which keeps last-activity data so cached rows settle). The direct primary environment on loopback pages and the desktop app persists a bounded WorkspaceMetadataSnapshot to IndexedDB. It reads the snapshot in parallel with the auth and descriptor requests in the root beforeLoad, then hydrates it through hydrateEnvironmentStateFromCache as last-known, not-live state. Measured cached sidebar commit: 73-94 ms, against 217-303 ms for the live sidebar on the 2,000-thread fixture. Phase 2 is not implemented anywhere: web, desktop or mobile. That means persisting the projection sequence and resuming the first subscription from the cached baseline. I found no renamed module or alternative mechanism (conditional snapshot, epoch, persisted sequence). A cold boot still takes a full, paged shell snapshot, and mobile likewise resumes only from an in-memory baseline. The auditor's single fix defect (no persistence after pairing post-boot) is refuted, because navigating to '/' after pairing re-runs the root beforeLoad. There is a different minor persistence gap: the write debounce has no maximum wait and no flush on pagehide.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/persistence/primaryShellCache.ts:112 hydratePrimaryShellFromCache hydrates via useStore.hydrateEnvironmentStateFromCache. It is a no-op over existing state (:124) and drops records for other environments (:119-122).
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:228 beforeLoad starts the IndexedDB read in parallel with ensurePrimaryEnvironmentReady and resolveInitialServerAuthGateState (:232-253). It restores after startPrimaryConnectionEarly, bounded at 150 ms (:96, :311-332), and clears the cache when the session is unauthenticated (:258-262). The paint still waits for the descriptor and auth round trips (:316-317).
  • apps/web/src/routes/pair.tsx:49 After pairing, the page navigates to '/'. That re-runs the root beforeLoad (router-core load-client.js:146-155 runs beforeLoad for every match on each navigation). cachedReadyRootContext was never set for requires-auth (__root.tsx:170-175), so the restore and persistence path runs. The auditor's fix defect is refuted.
  • apps/web/src/persistence/primaryShellCacheEligibility.ts:15 Persistence is limited to desktop or loopback, by design (privacy). LAN/WAN browsers, where the finding expected the largest gain, never cache.
  • apps/web/src/persistence/primaryShellCache.ts:199 scheduleWrite resets a 2 s timer on every identity change of the environment state. EnvironmentState also holds messageByThreadId and activityByThreadId (packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts ~:150-160), so continuous streaming postpones the write indefinitely. There is no maximum wait and no pagehide or visibilitychange flush in the module.
  • apps/web/src/persistence/primaryShellCache.ts:38 PrimaryShellCacheRecord holds only origin, environmentId, savedAt and snapshot. There is no sequence or epoch, and WorkspaceMetadataSnapshot (packages/client-runtime/src/state/workspace/types.ts:141) has none either. The snapshot is bounded to 400 threads (metadataSnapshot.ts:11) with session null (apps/web/src/workspaceMetadataProjection.ts:214), so it is lossy as a resume baseline.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:252 hasShellBaseline=false is set only by a live 'resumed' or 'snapshot' item (:262, :277). resumeFromSequence returns null until then (:298-299), so the first subscription always takes a snapshot.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:1295 readShellProjectionSequence reads the in-memory projectionTracker, which only syncShellSnapshot (:1102) and shell events (:1041) seed. The web reader is apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:861 and the mobile reader is apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:510. Neither is persisted.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:2144 Only syncServerShellSnapshot sets bootstrapComplete=true and clears hydratedFromCacheAt. A resume from a cache-hydrated baseline would need a new promotion action.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/OrchestrationEventStore.ts:516 The resume anchor is EXISTS(sequence = N) only (also orchestrationStreams.ts:724). The environment id is a separate file from state.sqlite (apps/server/src/config.ts:328, :350), so a persisted sequence could resume against a reset database. The shell snapshot contract has no epoch or anchor id (packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:1194).
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:813 makeReplayableShellStream resumes only when canResumeAfter accepts, with at most 1,000 events (ORCHESTRATION_REPLAY_PAGE_MAX_LIMIT, constants.ts:3). Otherwise it sends a full or paged snapshot.
Remaining

Phase 2 (resume from the cached baseline) is not implemented on web, desktop or mobile. (1) The persisted record has no sequence or epoch (apps/web/src/persistence/primaryShellCache.ts:38; mobile apps/mobile/src/persistence/environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts). The cached view is also lossy: 400-thread cap, session null (workspaceMetadataProjection.ts:214). (2) connection.ts:252-299 sends resumeFromSequence only after a live baseline. (3) No store or supervisor path promotes a cache-hydrated environment to live on a 'resumed' item (store.ts:2144-2147 is the only place bootstrapComplete becomes true; projectionTracker and shellThreadIdsByEnvironment are seeded only in syncShellSnapshot, supervision.ts:1090-1106). (4) The server resume anchor checks only that a sequence exists (OrchestrationEventStore.ts:516-518), which is unsafe across a database reset that keeps the environment-id file. Smaller Phase 1 gaps: the paint still waits for the descriptor, auth and RootAppShell chunk (__root.tsx:250-257, :316-317, withRootSurfaceLoaded :127-137). Non-loopback browsers never cache (by design). The persistence debounce has no maximum wait or pagehide flush (primaryShellCache.ts:199-206).

Defects in the shipped fix

Minor: startPrimaryShellCachePersistence (apps/web/src/persistence/primaryShellCache.ts:199-206) restarts a 2 s debounce on every change to the environment state object, which includes message and activity maps. Continuous streaming therefore starves writes, and there is no flush on pagehide or hidden visibility. If a session closes during a long agent run, the cache can be stale or never written on a first session. The impact is low, because live data replaces it on the next boot. The auditor's claimed defect (no persistence after pairing post-boot) is not real: pair.tsx:49 navigates to '/', which re-runs the root beforeLoad and starts persistence.

Implementation sketch

Minor fix (S): in startPrimaryShellCachePersistence, add a maximum wait so a write happens at least every ~30 s under continuous change (track firstPendingAt; skip clearing the timer once the maximum wait has elapsed). Add a window 'pagehide' / document 'visibilitychange'→hidden listener that runs write() synchronously-scheduled, removed in stop(). Test with fake timers in apps/web/src/persistence/primaryShellCache.test.ts: continuous store changes every 500 ms still produce a write within the maximum wait, and pagehide triggers a write. Phase 2 (L), if pursued: (a) Contracts and server: add a projection epoch, a random id created with the database in a meta table, to OrchestrationShellSnapshot (packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:1194). Add an optional resumeEpoch next to resumeFromSequence on the shell subscribe input (:1352). In canResumeAfter (apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:688) return false when the epoch differs. Alternatively, anchor on the anchor event's event_id in probeResume (OrchestrationEventStore.ts:510). (b) Client persistence: store a separate full-fidelity baseline record next to the bounded paint snapshot: {sequence, epoch, updatedAt, complete}. Capture it in the same tick as the store snapshot after supervisor.flushShellEvents(), using readShellProjectionSequence. Mark it complete only when the snapshot was not truncated and includes thread sessions and latestTurn; otherwise persist no sequence. (c) connection.ts: add an input readPersistedShellBaseline(environmentId). When !hasShellBaseline and that returns a baseline that matches the cache-hydrated store, have resumeFromSequence return it and send the epoch. On a 'resumed' item that came from a persisted baseline, call a new supervisor method, seedShellBaselineFromCache(environmentId, {sequence, updatedAt, threadIds}). It should markSnapshot the projectionTracker, set shellThreadIdsByEnvironment, run reconcileSubscriptionsForEnvironment, attachListedThreads and reconcileSnapshotDerivedState, and call a new store action promoteCachedEnvironmentToLive (bootstrapComplete=true, hydratedFromCacheAt=undefined) before notifyShellReadiness. If the server sends a snapshot instead, the existing syncServerShellSnapshot path already replaces the cache. (d) Wire the same baseline into mobile (apps/mobile/src/persistence/environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts, environmentDriver.ts:510). Hosted stays snapshot-only. Tests: connection.test.ts (first subscription sends the cached sequence; a resumed item promotes to live; a snapshot fallback replaces the cache), a server orchestrationStreams test (epoch mismatch or reset database gives a snapshot), and a browser test extending apps/web/src/browser/primaryShellCache.browser.tsx for a cold boot that resumes.

Needs a decision

Phase 2 needs three decisions. (1) A contract and server protocol addition (a projection epoch or anchor identity on the shell subscribe and snapshot) to make cross-boot resume safe against a database reset. (2) A reversal of the deliberate Phase 1 design that the cache holds no sessions or liveness and is capped at 400 threads, because a resume baseline must be complete. (3) Extending caching to non-loopback browsers, where the gain is largest, which is a privacy and product decision; the module comments say paired devices should not keep a copy without asking. The measured loopback gain is small, because the cached sidebar already paints at ~73-94 ms. The minor debounce fix needs no decision.

Done#122 React 19's 300 ms Suspense reveal delay adds ~300 ms to the first thread/draft open in every document

thread-and-draft:suspense-300ms-throttle-route-lazy · original impact High, effort S · Rendering WP12B

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor's evidence says WorkspaceSurfaceGate removes the 300 ms hazard for the inner panel surfaces, and fixDefects says 'None seen'. The Browser workspace surface (LazyBrowserPanel) is still React.lazy plus Suspense with no preloader. #710 also added a new Suspense-wrapped hosted workspace shell lazy that reintroduces the throttle on the in-page hosted sign-in -> workspace transition. The core thread/draft/route finding is DONE as claimed.

Current state

The core finding is fixed. The thread and draft routes, along with statistics, projects, pull-requests, diagnostics, native-authorize, _chat, _chat.index and settings, use lazyRouteComponent. The router awaits the chunk before it commits (router-core load-client.js loadRouteChunk -> component.preload()), so no Suspense fallback commits and the 300 ms reveal throttle never starts. The root shell is a preloadableLazy that is resolved in the root beforeLoad. The workspace panel shell is gated by useLazyComponentReady. Settings preload warms the exact lazyRouteComponent wrapper. Thread and draft chunks are preloaded on hover, press, new-thread, bootstrap redirect and idle. The bundle-splitting and RouteRevealThrottle browser tests guard all of this. I keep the DONE status. I correct the auditor's 'fixDefects: None seen' and the claim that WorkspaceSurfaceGate covers every inner panel surface. Two instances of the same hazard remain. (1) The workspace Browser tab still renders a React.lazy inside its own Suspense. It has no preloader and no intent preload, so its first open in each document still waits on the 300 ms throttle. (2) #710 introduced a new Suspense lazy, hostedRootAppShell, for the hosted workspace shell. Nothing preloads it before an in-page sign-in flips accountStatus to authenticated. Before #710 this transition rendered RootAppShell synchronously because it was statically imported into HostedHubRoot. Now it commits AppBootLoadingSurface as a fallback and can wait up to ~300 ms after the chunk lands. Both are minor, one-time-per-document or per-sign-in costs. I verified them statically and did not measure them.

Evidence

  • apps/web/src/routes/_chat.draft.$draftId.tsx:10 Uses lazyRouteComponent for DraftChatThreadRoute, exported at DraftChatThreadRouteView.tsx:311.

The installed react-router lazyRouteComponent.js sets comp before the promise resolves, so the committed render does not suspend.

It is preloaded only by bootGate.ts:46-53, when the account is already authenticated at boot or a read preview applies, and by the HostedHubRoot.tsx:218-222 effect, which runs after the commit that already renders the shell.

The chunk is not loaded yet, so the fallback commits and the reveal throttle applies. At f1be4abc7, HostedHubRoot imported RootAppShell statically, so this path never suspended.
Defects in the shipped fix

The auditor's 'None seen' is not accurate. (1) Uncovered caller: the workspace Browser tab (apps/web/src/browser/LazyBrowserPanel.tsx:3-17, rendered via ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:450-458/:1509) still uses React.lazy plus Suspense. It has no SURFACE_LOADERS entry (workspacePanelPreload.ts:78-84) and no launcher intent preload (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:798-805). Its first open in each document commits 'Loading browser…' and waits on the 300 ms reveal throttle. This is the same hazard WorkspaceSurfaceGate removes for the other surfaces. (2) Regression introduced by #710: hostedRootAppShell.tsx:33-39 wraps the now code-split hosted workspace shell in a Suspense fallback. bootGate.ts:46-53 preloads it only when the account is authenticated at boot. After an in-page sign-in (signIn / redeemInvitation / bootstrapOwner), HostedHubRoot.tsx:318/320 renders it immediately, so AppBootLoadingSurface commits and the shell reveal can be held until ~300 ms after the fallback even when the chunk is HTTP- or SW-cached. Before #710 that transition was synchronous. Both are once per document or per sign-in, not per thread navigation.

Implementation sketch

(1) Browser tab: move the browser chunk into workspacePanelPreload.ts as `export const LazyBrowserPanelSurface = preloadableLazy(() => import('./browser/BrowserPanel').then(m => m.BrowserPanel))` plus `loadBrowserPanel = preloadOf(...)`, and add `browser: loadBrowserPanel` to SURFACE_LOADERS. Set LOADING_LABELS.browser to 'Loading browser...'. In ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx, render `<WorkspaceSurfaceGate key="browser" chunk={LazyBrowserPanelSurface} mode="browser"><LazyBrowserPanelSurface .../></WorkspaceSurfaceGate>` and add `onIntent={() => preloadWorkspacePanel('browser', { intent: true })}` to the Browser LauncherCard. Rewrite browser/LazyBrowserPanel.tsx, which ProjectBrowserPreview uses, to gate on useLazyComponentReady(LazyBrowserPanelSurface, true) and render the 'Loading browser…' status as an ordinary render, keeping Suspense only as a safety net. Test: add a ThreadWorkspacePanel.browser.tsx case modelled on the simulator case (around line 241) that asserts the browser surface mounts with no committed fallback once preloaded and that preloadWorkspacePanel('browser') warms it. (2) Hosted shell: in hostedRootAppShell.tsx, make HostedRootAppShell call `useLazyComponentReady(LazyRootAppShell, true)` and return <AppBootLoadingSurface/> as an ordinary render until ready. This is the same pattern as ChatRightPanel and removes the throttle with no product change. Optionally also call preloadHostedRootAppShell() as a code-only prefetch on sign-in intent (passkey or submit press in HostedAuthenticationSurface), consistent with bootGate's code-only prefetch rule. It starts no session, relay or store work. Test: a HostedHubRoot.browser.tsx case that signs in without the preloadHostedRootAppShell() setup and asserts, using the RouteRevealThrottle observeCommit pattern, that the shell commits within ~50 ms of the chunk resolving. Validate with focused vitest and browser runs for these files only.

Done#123 Chat route code is never prefetched; at boot it waits for the shell snapshot and then loads as a 5-level waterfall

thread-and-draft:chat-route-not-prefetched-waterfall · original impact Medium, effort S · Waterfall

Current state

I tried to refute DONE and could not. All three parts of the proposal are in the code and in the current build output. (1) The thread and draft route chunks preload at idle after the shell paints, first in the queue, ahead of the palette and settings. handleWelcome starts the thread chunk, and outside hosted mode prewarms the thread detail, before it awaits the shell snapshot. (2) Sidebar rows, inbox rows and every New-thread control preload on intent; the router uses defaultPreload 'intent'. (3) modulePreload is back on, with a resolver that only handles JS hosts. The built boot chunk now preloads all 146 deps of ChatThreadRouteView (145 for the draft route, lexical included) in one round, and index.html has only the 4 boot-chain modulepreloads. The thread and draft routes now use lazyRouteComponent, which the router awaits before it commits the route. That removes the 300 ms Suspense-throttle caveat the earlier verifier raised. The fix commits (60633eff3, 3ce80cee6) are ancestors of 7bc39eec3, so the Hub's vendored build has them too. I found one minor inefficiency and one gap in test coverage; neither changes the DONE status.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:175-188 ShellIdlePreloads: the thread and draft route chunks are the first idle task, then the command palette, then settings. Mounted at :111. Skipped on the phone tier.
  • apps/web/src/lib/shellIdlePreload.ts:37-76 Starts after primary-shell-painted (capped at 5 s), runs one task per idle period, and skips on saveData or networks slower than 4g. The phase-already-reached path is safe: it starts synchronously before cancelPhaseWait is assigned, and the default is a no-op.
  • apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:276-290 When the bootstrap redirect applies, preloadRouteChunk(THREAD_ROUTE_ID) (:286) and, outside hosted mode, prewarmThreadDetailSubscription (:287) run before `await ensureEnvironmentConnectionBootstrapped` (:290).
  • apps/web/src/lib/routeChunkPreload.ts:26-47 Calls router.loadRouteChunk, which goes to route.options.component.preload(), the same lazyRouteComponent load the navigation awaits (router-core load-client.js:21-37).
  • apps/web/src/routes/_chat.$environmentId.$threadId.tsx:19-36 lazyRouteComponent. The loader returns early on preload, so hovering opens no streams. preloadStaleTime is 0.
  • apps/web/src/routes/_chat.draft.$draftId.tsx:10-13 The draft route is also a lazyRouteComponent.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/threadNavigationIntent.ts:15-39 Hover and press warm the thread chunk, plus a detail retain after a 120 ms dwell. preloadDraftRoute warms the draft chunk.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarThreadRow.tsx:452-472 Thread and draft rows preload on pointerenter and pointerdown.
  • apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/InboxThreadRow.tsx:375-388 Inbox rows use the same hover and press intents. The auditor did not list this, but it covers the second sidebar surface.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarPrimaryActions.tsx:112-113 The New thread button preloads the draft route on pointerenter and focus. SidebarChatList.tsx:150-151 and SidebarProjectHeader.tsx:179-180 do the same.

Defects in the shipped fix

Minor nit, no correctness impact. handleWelcome checks only shouldApplyBootstrapThreadRedirect (pathname '/', not phone, not hosted home) before it prewarms (RootAppShell.tsx:276-287). It does not check handledBootstrapThreadIdRef, which is read only at :321 after the snapshot. Each new connection re-emits the welcome (client-runtime rpc/serverState.ts:165-166 into welcomeAtom). So a desktop user who sits on '/' after the bootstrap redirect was handled (for example after the active thread was deleted or archived and the view fell back to '/') gets a thread-detail subscription to the bootstrap thread on every reconnect. Nothing consumes it, and threadDetailPrewarm.ts releases it after 10 s. The chunk preload on that path is a free no-op. Coverage gap: no component or browser test asserts the welcome-time preload/prewarm ordering or the ShellIdlePreloads task order. Only the helper modules are unit-tested (shellIdlePreload.test.ts, routeChunkPreload.test.ts, threadDetailPrewarm.test.ts). The hosted skip of the prewarm (:287) looks deliberate and matches the AGENTS.md hosted lifecycle ownership rule. The route loader still prewarms in hosted mode at navigation time.

Implementation sketch

Optional nit fix in apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx EventRouter.handleWelcome. Gate the early prewarm (and optionally the chunk preload) on `handledBootstrapThreadIdRef.current !== payload.bootstrapThreadId`, the same check the redirect uses at :321. Better, extract a small pure predicate into RootAppShell.logic.ts (e.g. shouldPrewarmBootstrapThread({pathname, tier, hostedHome, handledThreadId, bootstrapThreadId})) and use it at both sites so the two cannot drift. Add a RootAppShell.logic.test.ts case: a handled bootstrap thread on '/' does not prewarm. Optionally add a browser test that mounts EventRouter with a mocked welcome and checks that preloadRouteChunk and prewarm run before ensureEnvironmentConnectionBootstrapped resolves, then don't run again on a second welcome.

Partial#124 'New thread' waits for a full getConfig (85–131 KB) and then getProjectPreferences before it navigates

thread-and-draft:new-thread-rpc-waterfall · original impact Medium, effort S · Network / RTT WP10decision

First-pass audit said PARTIAL; the verifier corrected it. The auditor reported no blocking defect, but the remembered-preferences fast path has a real correctness gap. Its background correction is defeated by ChatComposer's mount-time clearPersistedAttachments rewrite (whole-object identity guard, no no-op guard in the store), and the remembered cache is never invalidated when defaults are saved. The auditor also over-scoped the remainder to 'hosted nodes': in the standard build nodeIdForHostedEnvironment is always null, and desktop Hub-relay nodes already use a per-environment config from their own subscribeConfig stream, so only the hosted-hub web build still pays getConfig. They also missed the duplicate sequential read in agentHandoff.ts.

Current state

PARTIAL is the right status, but the auditor's details need two corrections. (1) 'No blocking defect' is wrong. The new remembered-preferences fast path (65af92766) applies the node's background answer only if the composer draft object is identical to the one it seeded. ChatComposer replaces that object on mount (its image-persist effect calls clearPersistedAttachments, which has no no-op guard). So whenever the preferences RPC returns after the draft view mounts (typical on remote saved environments), the correction is silently dropped and the draft keeps stale defaults. Nothing invalidates the remembered cache when the user saves project defaults, so the next New thread after a settings change opens with the old model/env mode. The browser test mocks navigate, so it never mounts ChatView and misses this. (2) The remaining waterfall is narrower than 'hosted nodes and hosted-hub web'. nodeIdForHostedEnvironment is stubbed to null in the standard build, so only the hosted-hub web build still pays the fresh ~100 KB getConfig on every fresh draft (in parallel with preferences when the cached primary config shows the capability). Desktop Hub-relay workspace nodes use their own per-environment saved-runtime config with no getConfig. Everything else the auditor credited is verified: the route-chunk preload at click time, cached config for non-hosted targets, the boot-time duplicate getConfig removed, and the resolveAvailableEditors cache. A smaller duplicate of the same sequential getConfig-then-preferences read remains in the PR agent handoff (agentHandoff.ts readDraftDefaults), mostly hidden behind the change-request fetch.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts:146 preloadRouteChunk('/_chat/draft/$draftId') at click time: done.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts:156-162 cachedConfig: readEnvironmentServerConfig(env), requireFreshConfig: hosted || isHostedHubMode().
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/hostedConnectionCoordinator.standard.ts:50 nodeIdForHostedEnvironment returns null in the standard build, so `hosted` is true only in the hosted-hub web build. Desktop Hub workspace nodes take the cached path.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:1349-1359 Desktop workspace (Hub relay) connections feed a per-environment, identity-normalised serverConfig from their own subscribeConfig stream into the saved runtime store. readEnvironmentServerConfig reads that store, so no getConfig runs on desktop.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/newDraftDefaults.ts:113-123 Non-hosted fast path: a cached config plus a remembered answer opens the draft with no RPC, and the preferences read runs in the background as `fresh`. Without a remembered answer, only the small preferences RPC is awaited (1 RTT on the first draft per project per session).
  • apps/web/src/hooks/newDraftDefaults.ts:125-135 Hosted-web path still awaits the full getConfig. Preferences run in parallel only when the cached primary config shows the capability; otherwise the two reads are sequential.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts:198-209 The background answer applies only if getComposerDraft(draftId) === seeded.composer and the session object is unchanged (whole-object identity).
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx:1444-1449 The image-persist effect runs on mount and calls clearComposerDraftPersistedAttachments(composerDraftTarget) whenever composerImages is empty.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/draftStore.ts:2235-2257 clearPersistedAttachments always writes {...current, persistedAttachments: [], nonPersistedImageIds: []}, a new object even when nothing changes. The identity guard therefore fails after the composer mounts.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:622-623 On a draft route the composer target is the draftId, the same key the seed captured. ChatComposer renders unconditionally (ChatView.tsx:6070).
  • apps/web/src/browser/NewThreadSettings.browser.tsx:222-272 The test that 'applies the node's newer answer' mocks navigate, so ChatView/ChatComposer never mount and the mount-time rewrite race is not covered.
  • apps/web/src/components/settings/ProjectPreferenceSettings.tsx:119-152 Saving project defaults updates server settings but never refreshes or forgets the effectivePreferencesCache in newDraftDefaults.ts:27. The next New thread opens with the pre-change answer.
Remaining

(a) Hosted-hub web build only: every fresh draft still awaits a fresh full getConfig (~85-130 KB plus 1 relay RTT, about 100-400 ms, and a long decode frame at 4x CPU). See useHandleNewThread.ts:160 and newDraftDefaults.ts:125-135. The remembered-preferences fast path is disabled there (newDraftDefaults.ts:113), and when the cached primary config lacks the capability the reads stay sequential. (b) Non-hosted: the first fresh draft per project per session still waits 1 preferences RTT before navigating (newDraftDefaults.ts:122). The proposal's full 'navigate first, fill defaults later' is only applied to repeat drafts. (c) agentHandoff.ts:176-199 duplicates the sequential getConfig and preferences read for every target, mostly hidden behind the change-request fetch.

Defects in the shipped fix

1) The background correction is dropped in the real app. useHandleNewThread.ts:202-206 compares whole composer and session object identity. ChatComposer's mount effect (ChatComposer.tsx:1444-1449) calls clearPersistedAttachments, which always replaces the composer draft object (draftStore.ts:2245-2255, no no-op guard). If the background getProjectPreferences returns after the draft route mounts (typical on remote saved environments, possible locally under load), the node's current answer is ignored. The draft keeps the remembered model and env mode even though the user never touched it. The browser test mocks navigate and does not catch this (NewThreadSettings.browser.tsx:222-272). 2) The remembered cache (newDraftDefaults.ts:27) is never invalidated when project or node defaults are saved (ProjectPreferenceSettings.tsx:119-152) or when a settingsUpdated config event arrives. Combined with defect 1, the first New thread after a user changes the project default model or env mode on a remote node opens with the old values; later drafts are correct. 3) Minor: the cache is not cleared on hosted account teardown (hostedHub/environment.ts:58). Low risk because keys are environment-scoped.

Implementation sketch

Defect fix (S, no decision): (1) In packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/draftStore.ts clearPersistedAttachments, return `state` unchanged when current.persistedAttachments.length === 0 && current.nonPersistedImageIds.length === 0. This also removes a pointless store write and re-render on every composer mount. Audit syncPersistedAttachments for the same pattern. (2) In apps/web/src/hooks/useHandleNewThread.ts createAndOpenDraft, replace the whole-object identity guard with a field-level 'untouched' check. Capture the seeded values the seed writes: composer.modelSelectionByProvider, composer.activeProvider, session.envMode/branch/worktreePath/tokenMode/runtimeMode. Compare those references or values in the background `.then`, so unrelated writes such as attachments, upload tokens or prompt typing no longer block the correction. Decide whether prompt typing should still block it; it probably should not, since it is not a defaults field. (3) Add `forgetRememberedProjectPreferences(environmentId, projectId?)` in apps/web/src/hooks/newDraftDefaults.ts (or refresh through readAndRememberProjectPreferences). Call it from ProjectPreferenceSettings.save on success. Clear an environment's entries when a settingsUpdated config event arrives: hook applySettingsUpdated/applyServerConfigEvent for the primary and onConfigUpdated with type settingsUpdated in environments/runtime/service.ts for saved environments. Clear the whole map in clearWebHostedAccountScopedState. Tests: extend NewThreadSettings.browser.tsx so the second draft calls useComposerDraftStore.getState().clearPersistedAttachments(draftId) (simulating the composer mount) before resolveAnswer and still expects envMode 'local' / 'newer-model'. Add a unit test that saving project defaults makes the next readNewDraftDefaults await a fresh read. Add a draftStore unit test that clearPersistedAttachments on an already-empty draft keeps object identity. Hosted remainder (M, needs decision): in hosted-hub web, record the primary config together with the hosted mutation lease's selectionGeneration when the current primary connection's subscribeConfig snapshot is applied (ServerStateBootstrap/startServerStateSync, or a hosted-only wrapper keyed by environmentId). In readNewDraftDefaults, accept that cached config when its stamp equals readHostedNodeMutationLease(env)?.selectionGeneration, and use requireFreshConfig only when it is absent or mismatched. Then let hosted use the remembered-preferences-plus-background-refresh route; the lease check before/after at useHandleNewThread.ts:163-170 stays. Alternative: a light `server.getNewDraftDefaults` RPC returning defaultThreadEnvMode, defaultAgentTokenMode, chats availability, projectPreferences capability and effective preferences, with an 'Unknown request tag' fallback to getConfig. That is a contracts, server and rpcAccessPolicy change and may need a Hub pin bump for relay policy. Optionally switch agentHandoff.ts readDraftDefaults to readNewDraftDefaults to remove the duplicated logic.

Needs a decision

The defect fixes (draftStore no-op guard, field-level untouched check, cache invalidation) need no decision. Removing the fresh getConfig on hosted-hub web does: it means trusting a cached config snapshot under the hosted lifecycle rules in AGENTS.md ('stale generations cannot publish ... snapshots'), which the code comments deliberately avoid today. The light-RPC alternative is a protocol/contracts change that may need a Hub pin bump and deploy.

Done#125 Composer mount triggers source-control discovery, and the server's 'discover' RPC discards its cache and re-runs gh/glab auth checks (network)

thread-and-draft:source-control-discovery-refresh-bypasses-cache · original impact Medium, effort S · Process spawns

Current state

Confirmed DONE (fix in #710, 60633eff3, which is also in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3). The composer no longer runs discovery on mount. ChatComposer has no discovery hook, and ContextPickerButton enables it only on hover, focus or open. Client staleTime went from 30 s to 5 min, with revalidation on foreground, resume and online (Atom.swr focus respects staleTime). Background reads send {cached:true}, which the RPC routes to the cached discover. The server cache TTL went from 5 s to 2 min, is process-wide (built once in server.ts, and per-connection layers fork the runtime memo map) and is bypassed only by explicit refreshes. The finding's per-chat-entry probes (gh, glab, az auth) are gone. The only other mount-time reader at chat entry would be GitActionsControl, which the crown does not mount until the card opens or a branch flyout is hovered. The leftovers are small: PublishRepositoryDialog reads with the default enabled=true, the proposal's server background refresh was not done (and the 5-min client staleTime exceeds the 2-min server TTL, so a single client's revalidation almost always misses the server cache), the palette add-project view runs an uncached probe, and the discovery target ignores the thread's environmentId (true before the fix as well).

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ContextPickerButton.tsx:21-34 Discovery runs only when `open || wanted`; wanted is set by onPointerEnter/onFocus (lines 49-50). It shows the lists optimistically while discovery is pending. It is called with `undefined` target although props.environmentId is available.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ContextPickerButton.browser.tsx:30-48 Test asserts that mounting does not call manager.refresh and that clicking does.

Defects in the shipped fix

None of these brings back the per-chat-entry cost. (1) apps/web/src/components/GitActionsControl.tsx:556: PublishRepositoryDialog reads discovery with enabled=true while closed. Also, the 5-min client staleTime is longer than the 2-min server TTL, so a single client's revalidation (hover or foreground after 5 min) nearly always misses the server cache and runs the full gh/glab/az probe (~0.8-1.5 s). That happens off the paint path, at most once per 5 min. The `cached` path mainly helps multiple tabs or documents within 2 min. (3) CommandPaletteDialog.tsx:1265: the add-project source view always runs the uncached probe. (4) ContextPickerButton.tsx:25 and GitActionsControl.tsx:556 ignore the thread/dialog environmentId and target the primary node. Partial#126 Sibling-tab prefetch starts up to 6 thread windows the moment ChatView mounts, competing with the active thread

thread-and-draft:prefetch-competition · original impact Medium, effort S · Network / RTT WP11

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

PR #710 fixed the local/desktop path: sibling-tab retains wait on activeDetailLoaded, run in an idle slot and are staggered 100 ms apart, and the active thread is retained earlier (route loader). The gate is the weak part. It uses selectThreadDetailLoaded, which is also true for messages hydrated from a cache. The hosted browser persists the routed thread's messages locally (and the Hub thread read cache supplies them too), so on a hosted cold open of a previously opened thread the gate passes at mount, before any live window. The relay usually takes seconds to come up while the 6 staggered retains take about 600 ms. So all sibling retains are made before the relay can carry them, and their subscribeThreadWindow requests go out in one burst right behind the active thread's request: either via the watch()/register() loop or the transport flush on socket open. On the hosted path, the slowest one (E2EE relay), sibling windows therefore still compete with the active window, which is the cost the finding describes. Sidebar prewarm (3 windows, one idle callback, no gate, no stagger) has the same problem on a smaller scale. The optional smaller prewarm window was not done.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/useChatSessionTabsPrefetch.ts:129-135 Effect gates on activeDetailLoaded, then startStaggeredThreadPrefetch (idle slot + 100 ms stagger, lines 70-106). This is correct when the gate means 'live window applied'.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:1000-1002 activeThreadDetailLoaded = selectThreadDetailLoaded(store, activeThreadRef) for server threads; passed as activeDetailLoaded at 1226-1230.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/storeSelectors.ts:178-185 selectThreadDetailLoaded is true when threadHistoryByThreadId OR messageIdsByThreadId has the thread. It does not exclude cachedMessageThreadIds.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:3895-3912 hydrateEnvironmentStateFromCache writes messageIdsByThreadId[id] (and marks cachedMessageThreadIds) for every cached thread with content, before any live window (3846-3850 does the same on the retainedLiveSnapshot path).
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/readCache.ts:286-297 On hosted boot the local persisted read cache hydrates threads with record.content. The routed thread is kept with priority (527-539), so a reopened thread has cached messages at mount.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/threadReadCache.ts:107-124 The Hub thread read cache also hydrates the routed thread's content before the node is live.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:4051-4058 Elsewhere ChatView already treats detailLoaded as insufficient: the Claude review state requires activeThreadShellLive && activeThreadDetailLoaded, because cache-hydrated detail is not live.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:836-868 retain(): attach() or, without a connection, watch(). Retains made before the hosted connection is up park here.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:805-817 register() attaches every parked entry for the environment in one synchronous loop, so the stagger collapses into a burst (active first by insertion order, then all siblings).
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useSidebarThreadPrewarm.ts:39-43 Sidebar prewarm retains up to SIDEBAR_THREAD_PREWARM_LIMIT=3 (Sidebar.logic.ts:22) in one idle callback, with no active-window gate and no stagger. Same competition on a smaller scale.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/useChatSessionTabsPrefetch.test.ts:57-127 Only the pure helpers are tested (stagger, cancel). No test covers the activeDetailLoaded gate or a cache-hydrated active thread.
Remaining

(1) The gate useChatSessionTabsPrefetch.ts:130 relies on selectThreadDetailLoaded (storeSelectors.ts:178-185), which is satisfied by cache-hydrated messages (store.ts:3895-3912 via hostedHub/readCache.ts:286-297 and hostedHub/threadReadCache.ts:107-124). On a hosted cold open of a previously opened thread, sibling retains therefore start at mount, not after the live window. Because the relay is not up yet, they flush as one burst with the active request (supervision.ts:805-817 register loop, or the transport flush on open). Up to 6 sibling windows of 80-500 KB still compete with the active window over the E2EE relay. (2) useSidebarThreadPrewarm.ts:39-43 retains 3 windows in one idle callback, ungated and unstaggered, so it competes the same way at cold open. (3) Optional: no reduced prewarm window for speculative retains (MAX_SPECULATIVE_SIBLING_TAB_PREFETCH is still 6 full windows).

Defects in the shipped fix

The gate in the implemented fix uses the wrong signal. selectThreadDetailLoaded counts cache-hydrated messages (cachedMessageThreadIds) as loaded, so in hosted mode the gate passes before the live window. The idle+stagger scheduling only spaces the retain() calls, not the wire requests: retains made before the connection registers or opens attach and flush together (supervision.ts:805-817). Minor: no hook-level test for the gate. The test's manual scheduleIdle cancel uses splice(indexOf(cb),1), which removes the wrong item if the callback already ran (test-only).

Implementation sketch

S fix: (a) Add selectThreadLiveDetailLoaded(state, ref) in packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/storeSelectors.ts: threadHistoryByThreadId?.[id] !== undefined || (messageIdsByThreadId[id] !== undefined && !cachedMessageThreadIds?.[id]). syncServerThreadWindow writes the history entry, and writeThreadState clears the cached mark via markThreadMessagesLive, so both live paths flip it. Export it from @ryco/client-runtime/state/threads. (b) In ChatView.tsx (~1000), derive activeThreadLiveDetailLoaded from it (true for drafts) and pass it as activeDetailLoaded to useChatSessionTabsPrefetch. Optionally also use it in the Claude review check at ~4058 instead of shellLive && detailLoaded. (c) Move startStaggeredThreadPrefetch to a shared module (e.g. apps/web/src/lib/staggeredThreadPrefetch.ts). Make useSidebarThreadPrewarm take the same foreground-ready gate (e.g. the routed thread's live-detail state, or true when no thread route is active) and retain its additions through the staggered helper, not in one idle callback. Tests: selector unit tests (cache-hydrated content -> false; window snapshot applied -> true; legacy syncServerThreadDetail over cached content -> true). A hook test (vitest with fake timers, or a browser test) that a cache-hydrated active thread does not trigger sibling retains until syncServerThreadWindow is applied. A sidebar-prewarm browser test for gating and stagger. More robust M alternative, which also covers mobile and the register()/transport-flush burst: add a { speculative: true } retain option in packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts. Speculative entries in an environment are not attached while a view-retained entry there is still awaiting its first live snapshot, then drain from a per-environment queue one attach per ~100 ms. Route sibling, sidebar and intent retains through it.
