Partial#127 The thread-detail cache's byte estimate adds up every live event forever, so one busy thread fills the 12 MiB budget and evicts every idle cached thread on each event

thread-and-draft:thread-cache-byte-estimate-never-decays · original impact Medium, effort S · Caching WP11

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor marked this DONE and called the remaining overestimate minor ('bounded', 'slightly early'). The cap is the same 12 MiB as the whole budget, and real data shows 4 recent threads would pass it within about 6 hours. Activity ids come from event ids, so 'only row-creating events' still counts about a third of the raw traffic bytes for b2714955 (10.8 of 30.5 MB) and stays about 15 times the retained state. At the clamp, releasing the idle hot thread evicts every older idle entry, the same symptom the finding described, now once per session instead of on every event. So the status is PARTIAL, not DONE.

Current state

PR #710 (60633eff3) fixed the main symptom. Deltas and repeated updates of the same row no longer add bytes. Pinned threads no longer count against the idle byte budget. Eviction runs once per chunk instead of once per event. The unit test the finding asked for exists. But the estimate still never decays. Every new row id adds its full size, and the store trims to 500 activities and 2000 messages without the estimate following. Most activity kinds use the event id as the row id, so nearly every tool and subagent update is a new row. Read-only data from the user's state.sqlite: thread b2714955 (the one the finding cites) has 8,312 unique activity rows. The fixed estimate grows to about 10.8 MB while the store keeps only the last 500 rows, about 0.6 MB. Four recent threads would pass the 12 MiB per-entry clamp: 1f88d2e9 (43 MB of unique-row bytes), c3110312 (15.8 MB), 08be3c64 (15.7 MB) and 58db77a7 (12.6 MB). 1f88d2e9 and 58db77a7 each reach the clamp after about 6 hours. A thread at the clamp fills the whole idle budget once it goes idle. Releasing it then evicts every older idle cached thread, or the hot thread is evicted at the next release. The original problem happened on every event. This one happens about once per long session, and the next snapshot resets it.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:215-248 retainedRowWrite counts message-sent, activity-appended and proposed-plan-upserted, keyed by row id. Other events add nothing. This part of the proposal is done.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:438-451 recordRetainedEvent counts a repeated row id only by its growth, but every new row id adds bytes plus 256. Nothing is ever subtracted, so rows the store has trimmed stay counted until the next snapshot (434-437).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:452-455 recordRetainedHistoryPage adds each page's size with no dedup and no decay.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:431-433 The per-entry clamp equals the whole 12 MiB budget, so one inflated entry can take the entire idle budget by itself.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:173-176 The store caps a thread at 2000 messages, 200 plans and 500 activities. Trimming happens at 1770-1779 for messages and 1930-1941 for activities. The estimate ignores this cap.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:988-1003 subagent.updated activities use id: event.eventId, as do many other kinds (lines 565-770). Each runtime update is a new row on the client, so for tool and subagent traffic creating a row is the same as traffic.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:724-740 evictToCapacity uses byteBudget "evictable", which fixes the problem while the hot thread is pinned. Once the hot thread is idle and unviewed, its inflated estimate does count.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:869-887 Release sets lastAccessedAt to now (878) and runs evictToCapacity (885). Switching away from an idle hot thread at the clamp makes it the newest idle entry. LRU then evicts every older idle entry until the total fits.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/evictionPolicy.ts:25-41 The byteBudget option is implemented correctly.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.test.ts:665-720 Tests cover a pinned hot thread and a single row re-sent many times. None covers many unique rows beyond the store cap, or a hot thread being released.
  • ~/.ryco/userdata/state.sqlite (read-only, immutable=1) b2714955: 25,779 activity events (30.5 MB), 8,312 unique ids. Sum of max row size plus overhead is 10.77 MB. The last 500 rows hold 0.60 MB. Hourly growth of the new estimate: 1.7, 5.9, 8.2, 9.9 and 10.6 MB. 1f88d2e9 reaches 12 MiB at 22:08 after starting at 16:08, and 58db77a7 at 21:11 after starting at 15:08.
Remaining

The estimate still only grows for row-creating events and history pages (supervision.ts:438-455). It ignores the store's trim to MAX_THREAD_ACTIVITIES 500 and MAX_THREAD_MESSAGES 2000 (state/threads/store.ts:173-176). Activity rows use the event id as row id (ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:988-1003 and others), so a busy tool or subagent thread reaches 10-12 MiB in about 4-6 hours on real data, while the store holds about 0.6 MB. Once that thread is idle and released, it takes the whole idle budget (per-entry clamp = budget, supervision.ts:431-433). The release at supervision.ts:878-885 then evicts all older idle cached threads (idle less than 5 minutes), or the hot thread itself at the next release. That causes cold window re-opens. It happens once per long session and resets on the next snapshot.

Defects in the shipped fix

This is a defect in the implemented fix, not just the minor residual the auditor described. The auditor called the overestimate 'bounded' and said it evicts entries 'slightly early'. On the user's real data it reaches the 12 MiB clamp on 4 recent threads, and at the clamp releasing that thread evicts every older idle entry. Smaller items: (1) A row already in the snapshot that is later updated live is counted again as a new row (the full size plus 256 B, once per row). (2) History pages add without dedup. (3) No test covers unique rows beyond the store cap, or releasing a hot thread.

Implementation sketch

1) Move the store caps (MAX_THREAD_MESSAGES, MAX_THREAD_ACTIVITIES, MAX_THREAD_PROPOSED_PLANS in state/threads/store.ts:173-176) into a small shared module, e.g. state/threads/limits.ts, and import them in both store.ts and connection/supervision.ts. 2) In supervision.ts, replace the single rowRetainedBytes map with one insertion-ordered Map per collection (message, activity, plan). In recordRetainedEvent, when a new key makes a collection exceed its cap, delete the oldest key and subtract its bytes, mirroring the store's FIFO trim. Optionally, at recordRetainedSnapshot, record each collection's row count and average row bytes from the snapshot. Then, once live rows plus snapshot rows exceed the cap, also subtract one average snapshot row per new row, so the estimate tracks the retained window. 3) In recordRetainedHistoryPage, key page items by id into the same per-collection maps, which dedups them and subjects them to the same cap, instead of adding the raw page size. 4) Optional hardening: clamp a single entry to MAX_CACHED_THREAD_DETAIL_ESTIMATED_BYTES / 2, so one entry cannot flush every other idle entry. Alternative to 2-3: add an input callback estimateThreadRetainedBytes(environmentId, threadId) that walks the stored rows with approximateJsonSize. Call it only in evictToCapacity, and only for evictable entries when the cheap estimate is over budget, to re-baseline. Tests in supervision.test.ts: (a) a thread receives 2,000 unique 10 KB activity rows (about 20 MB), goes idle and is released. An older idle 200 KB thread must not be evicted, because the estimate stays at about 500 rows (about 5 MB). (b) A history page re-applied twice is counted once. (c) The existing two tests still pass. Run with bun run test --filter client-runtime, i.e. Vitest scoped to packages/client-runtime. Separately, consider upserting subagent.updated activities by subagent id on the server, which would also cut store churn. That is a data-model change outside this finding.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Done#128 Every thread switch remounts the whole ChatView (split-pane keys), which also undid the deferred-timeline optimisation

thread-and-draft:chatview-remount-on-switch · original impact Medium, effort M · Rendering WP10

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. DONE holds for the performance cost. A lone pane now passes its React key on, so desktop thread switches reuse ChatView, the composer and the Lexical editor, and useDeferredValue has an initial value again. The auditor's 'fixDefects: None seen' is wrong. Reusing the ChatView brings back cross-thread state leaks that the per-thread remount used to hide. (1) The Lexical undo history is shared across threads, so Cmd+Z after a switch writes the previous thread's prompt into the new thread's draft. I reproduced this with lexical@0.50 registerHistory: a controlled swap from 'draft for thread A' to '' followed by UNDO_COMMAND gives back 'draft for thread A' with the 'historic' tag, and OnChangePlugin does not filter that tag. (2) The send pipeline runs async continuations that write to instance-wide state (sendInFlightRef, promptRef, the local dispatch snapshot, the composer handle). When the user switches threads while a send is in flight, those writes now land on the new thread. The ChatPanes browser test the auditor cites mounts a stub textarea, not ChatView, so it cannot catch any of this.

Current state

The performance fix is in. In ChatPanes, nextPaneReactKeys hands a lone pane's React key to the next lone thread, so ChatView, ChatComposer and the Lexical editor survive a desktop thread switch. useDeferredValue(activeThreadIdRaw, null), plus the worktree-launch exception, paints chrome and composer first and mounts the timeline in a transition. The proposal said reusing the instance would require resetting thread-scoped state, and that is only partly done. ChatView and ChatComposer reset their useState on a thread switch. Two kinds of thread-scoped state are still shared. First, the composer's Lexical HistoryPlugin stack: undo after a switch puts thread A's prompt into thread B's draft. Second, the send pipeline's instance-wide refs and callbacks: a send from A that is still in flight when the user switches can leave B stuck as busy, drop B's sends without feedback, or, if A's send fails, lose A's prompt or load A's text into B's prompt ref.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/paneReactKeys.logic.ts:23-47 If reuseLonePane is set and both the previous and next root are a lone thread, the next thread inherits the previous React key.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ChatPanes.tsx:158-168, 353-362, 623 nextLayoutMotion passes reuseLonePane = enabled, and the <section> is keyed by layoutMotion.reactKeys. The discarded render with stale keys is replaced by React's setState-during-render re-render, so it never commits.
  • apps/web/src/components/routeViews/ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:249, 296-315, 336-352 Both desktop branches use <ChatPanes threadRef> with the default enabled=true. The frozen phone tier passes enabled={false} and still remounts. The route loader is synchronous, so a thread switch never shows the pendingComponent.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:922-934 useDeferredValue(activeThreadIdRaw, continuesWorktreeLaunch ? activeThreadIdRaw : null). continuesWorktreeLaunch is computed once per instance and only feeds the initial value, which React ignores after mount, so it does no harm.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:2625-2633, 3286-3306, 3382-3392, 3543-3545 Thread-scoped resets for the header popovers, provider-status dismissal, the PR dialog, scroll and live-follow, the overview, optimistic messages, resetLocalDispatch and the pending branch. ChatComposer.tsx:1362-1368 resets the cursor and trigger on a draftId/activeThreadId change.
  • apps/web/src/components/ComposerPromptEditor.tsx:1454-1497, 1695, 1745 DEFECT: the controlled value sync calls editor.update with no history tag, so every thread switch pushes the previous thread's editor state onto the shared HistoryPlugin undo stack. Nothing dispatches CLEAR_HISTORY_COMMAND, and the editor is keyed only by an HMR constant. Undo after a switch restores thread A's text. OnChangePlugin, which ignores only history-merge, then calls onChange, and ChatComposer writes that text into thread B's draft. Reproduced with lexical@0.50 registerHistory: [["draft for thread A",""],["",""],["","historic"],["draft for thread A","historic"]].
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/sendEngine.ts:402 + apps/web/src/components/chat/useLocalDispatchState.ts:43-53, 93 DEFECT (race): just before thread.turn.start, which comes after the uploads, the Claude resume review and the settings round trip, the pipeline calls beginLocalDispatch again. That snapshot is taken from activeThreadRef.current. After a switch, this is thread B. B's turn and session state do not change, so the server never acknowledges the snapshot. On success, executeChatSendTurn.ts:781-783 does not reset it. B stays isSendBusy (runSend returns at ChatView.tsx:4423-4430) and shows a working timer until the user switches threads again.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:715, 829, 4423-4430 + apps/web/src/hooks/executeChatSendTurn.ts:437, 782 DEFECT (race): sendInFlightRef is shared by all threads the instance shows, while thread A's send pipeline is in flight. Enter in thread B returns silently during that window. The composerSubmitGuard at ChatView.tsx:4720 is already keyed by thread, which shows the intended design.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/executeChatSendTurn.ts:340-354, 288-317 + apps/web/src/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx:1275-1278 DEFECT (failure after a switch): rollbackSendTurn checks the live instance refs, which now hold thread B's content. If B's composer has text, thread A's failed prompt is never restored to A's draft, so it is lost: A's draft was cleared at send and the optimistic message is removed. If B is empty, refs.promptRef.current is set to A's prompt and resetCursorState runs on B's composer. B's prompt state does not change, so ChatComposer's promptRef sync effect does not re-run, and the next runSend in B reads promptForSend = promptRef.current (ChatView.tsx:4446). The plan follow-up continuation (ChatView.tsx:4888-4906) also calls setPlanSidebarOpen/resetLocalDispatch on whatever thread is showing.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ChatPanes.browser.tsx:360-376 The reuse test renders a stub <textarea>, not ChatView, so it does not exercise composer, editor or send-pipeline state across a switch.
Defects in the shipped fix

1) Cross-thread undo: the reused Lexical editor (ComposerPromptEditor.tsx:1454-1497 controlled sync, HistoryPlugin at :1695) keeps one undo stack for every thread. After switching A->B, Cmd+Z in B's composer, which the switch effect at ChatView.tsx:3309-3317 auto-focuses, restores A's prompt, and OnChangePlugin writes it into B's persisted draft. That can send A's text to B's agent, possibly on a different machine or project. This is deterministic and needs only an undo. 2) Send continuations hit the newly shown thread. beginLocalDispatch at sendEngine.ts:402 runs after the awaits and can snapshot thread B, which leaves B busy and blocks its sends (useLocalDispatchState.ts:43-53, 93). sendInFlightRef (ChatView.tsx:829) silently drops B's sends while A's send is in flight. On a failed A send, rollbackSendTurn (executeChatSendTurn.ts:340-354) either loses A's prompt, when B has content, or loads A's prompt into the shared promptRef behind B's empty composer. These need a switch while a send is in flight: likely with image uploads, settings changes, a Claude resume review or a slow hosted relay, rare for plain text sends. Before 141d441c7, when ChatView was also unkeyed, these hazards existed too; the per-thread remount that the fix removed is what had been hiding them. Minor, cosmetic: ChatComposer's isStashPickerOpen and isComposerModelPickerOpen (ChatComposer.tsx:919, 923) are not reset on a switch.

Implementation sketch

A) Undo history: give ComposerPromptEditor a `historyScope` prop. ChatComposer passes scopedThreadKey(composerDraftTarget) or the draftId. In ComposerPromptEditorInner's controlled-sync useLayoutEffect, when historyScope changes, run the rewrite with editor.update(fn, { tag: HISTORIC_TAG }) and then editor.dispatchCommand(CLEAR_HISTORY_COMMAND, undefined). Optional: keep a small LRU Map<scope, HistoryState> and pass <HistoryPlugin externalHistoryState={...}> so each thread keeps its own undo stack. Test: a ComposerPromptEditor browser test that renders value 'A' with scope a, rerenders value '' with scope b, presses Mod+Z, and asserts that onChange never receives 'A' and the editor stays empty. B) Thread-bound send continuations, as one shared helper rather than per-call patches: (1) useLocalDispatchState: store the thread key in LocalDispatchSnapshot; make beginLocalDispatch take the send's thread key and ignore it when that key is not the active one, and treat a snapshot whose key differs from the active thread as null. (2) Replace sendInFlightRef with a per-thread-key Set, the same shape as createThreadSubmitGuard (ChatView.logic.ts:462), and check the active key in runSend, onSubmitPlanFollowUp, onImplementPlanInNewThread and startGoalTurnRef. (3) executeChatSendTurn: capture the send's draft target, and before rollback or restore compare it with a getActiveDraftTarget() dep. When they differ, decide whether to restore from the target's draft in the composer draft store, not from the live refs; write only to that target; skip refs and composerHandle. (4) Guard the setPlanSidebarOpen and resetLocalDispatch calls in the plan follow-up continuation the same way. Tests: extend executeChatSendTurn.test.ts with a switch before failure (B's refs have content, then B's refs are empty) and assert A's draft is restored and B's refs are untouched. Add a useLocalDispatchState unit test for a begin after the key changes. Add a ChatView browser test: hold dispatchCommand pending, navigate A->B, resolve, assert B is not busy and B can send.

Value medium · effort M · risk medium

Partial#129 A thread's history is requested only after ChatView mounts and paints; until it arrives the 'new thread' screen (hero) shows for existing threads

thread-and-draft:detail-subscription-after-mount-hero-flash · original impact Medium, effort M · Waterfall WP10

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

#710 (60633eff3) shipped the main parts: retain at navigation time (route loader, sidebar and inbox intent, welcome prewarm) and a hero gate with ThreadHistorySkeleton. But the gate decides 'never started' from latestTurn and latestUserMessageAt only. A fresh fork has inherited history yet neither field, because the server leaves inherited prompts out of latestUserMessageAt and the fork has no turn of its own. So every fork opened on web still flashes NewThreadHero, with NewThreadWorkLocation and its git and listRefs reads, until the window arrives. The web fork dialog navigates into the fork right away, so this is the normal fork path. The browser test hides the gap: its fixture gives the fork a latestUserMessageAt the server would never send. Separately, the sidebar intent retain ends with release({immediately:true}). If the user left the thread within 10 s, that disposes the subscription and skips the 5-minute idle cache. Part 3 (a non-hosted message read cache) is still absent, but it matters less than the auditor said. Idle eviction keeps messages in the store, so a revisit in the same session paints at once. Only the first open after a reload or restart waits.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.logic.ts:441 isServerThreadHistoryPending counts a thread as started only if hasLatestTurn or latestUserMessageAt is set. It ignores lineage.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/forkInheritance.ts:88 countsTowardUserRecency leaves inherited prompts out. Used by ProjectionPipeline.ts:789 and :1170, so a fork's shell latestUserMessageAt stays null until it sends its own message.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/decider.ts:1020 thread.fork.create emits thread.created (latestTurnId null) plus the inherited message-sent events. Nothing sets latestTurnId, so the fork's shell has latestTurn === null.
  • packages/shared/src/threadFork.ts:97 threadHasConversation already exists for this case ('a fork that has not sent anything yet still counts through its lineage'), but the hero gate does not use it.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ForkThreadDialog.tsx:193 The fork dialog navigates into the new fork right away, with its detail not loaded. Result: hero plus NewThreadWorkLocation (git status, listRefs) until the window arrives.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.Fork.browser.tsx:271 The test fixture sets latestUserMessageAt to the first inherited message's time. The real server sends null, so the test passes and hides the hero flash.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/threadNavigationIntent.logic.ts:90 Intent retains release with {immediately:true} after 10 s. Scenario: press opens thread A (intent retain, then view retain), and the user leaves A within 10 s. ChatView's release only drops refCount to 1. The intent release then reaches refCount 0 and disposes at once (supervision.ts:880), skipping the 5-minute idle cache. The comment at lines 63-69 claims the subscription 'stays and later reaches the idle cache as usual', which is false here.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.threadSubscriptions.test.ts:328 The immediate-release test covers only 'speculative released first, view later'. The reverse order (view released first) is untested.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:1224 Thread messages leave the store only on thread removal (removeThreadState) or when the thread drops out of the shell (store.ts:2114). Disposing a subscription (supervision.ts:709) does not clear them, so selectThreadDetailLoaded stays true and in-session revisits paint at once. Part 3 only helps after a reload or restart.
  • apps/web/src/routes/_chat.$environmentId.$threadId.tsx:19 Confirmed: the route loader retains synchronously (not on preloads), lifecycle hooks drop superseded retains, and ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:155 releases the bridge once ChatView holds its own retain. Releasing too early is harmless: a normal release only starts the idle timer.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:5777 Confirmed: the skeleton replaces the hero and timeline while history is pending, and showNewThreadComposerSpacer (line 1785) is gated as well.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:628 Minor: if a 'response-too-large' window cannot shrink further, the code returns without retrying. The detail never loads and the skeleton stays indefinitely with no error state. It is rare, and the old behaviour (hero) was also wrong.
Remaining

1) Fork gap: isServerThreadHistoryPending (apps/web/src/components/ChatView.logic.ts:441) treats a fresh fork (lineage.relationship === 'forked', latestTurn null, latestUserMessageAt null) as never started. Each first open of such a fork, including the one the fork dialog does automatically (ForkThreadDialog.tsx:193), renders NewThreadHero and NewThreadWorkLocation (git status, listRefs) for one window round trip before the inherited transcript appears. 2) Optional proposal part 3: there is no non-hosted message read cache (persistence/primaryShellCache.ts holds metadata only). It affects only the first open of a thread after a reload or restart. In-session revisits after idle eviction already paint from the store.

Defects in the shipped fix

a) The hero gate misses forks. The browser fixture at ChatView.Fork.browser.tsx:271 sets latestUserMessageAt from an inherited message, which the server never does (forkInheritance.ts:88), so the gap is untested. b) Sidebar and inbox intent retains end with release({immediately:true}) (threadNavigationIntent.logic.ts:90; supervision.ts:880). When the user opens a thread whose detail was not loaded and leaves within 10 s, the view's release runs first, and the intent's immediate release then disposes the subscription at once instead of letting it idle for 5 minutes. A revisit shows stale store data and pays a fresh window request. Only the reverse order is tested (service.threadSubscriptions.test.ts:328).

Implementation sketch

Fork gap (S): change isServerThreadHistoryPending in apps/web/src/components/ChatView.logic.ts to take `lineage` (or a precomputed hasConversation) and use the shared rule: pending = isServerThread && !detailLoaded && messageCount === 0 && (hasLatestTurn || threadHasConversation({ latestUserMessageAt, lineage })), importing threadHasConversation from @ryco/shared/threadFork. In ChatView.tsx around line 1773, pass activeThread.lineage (or selectSidebarThreadSummaryByRef(...).lineage). Add a unit case in ChatView.logic.test.ts ('fork with lineage, no latestTurn and no latestUserMessageAt is pending'). Change the ChatView.Fork.browser.tsx fixture (line 271) to latestUserMessageAt: null so it matches the server, and assert that the fork view never shows the hero or the 'Work in' surface before the window arrives. Intent idle-cache bypass (S): in packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts retain(), add a per-entry viewEpoch counter that increments on each view retain. Capture it in the returned release closure, and dispose on `immediately` only if no view retain happened since this retain was taken (entry.viewEpoch === epochAtRetain); otherwise fall through to reconcileEntry (idle eviction). This also fixes useSidebarThreadPrewarm's immediate releases. Add a test to service.threadSubscriptions.test.ts: speculative retain, view retain, view release, then immediate release of the speculative one → not disposed until the 5-minute idle timer. Optionally fix the comment in threadNavigationIntent.logic.ts. Part 3 (optional, M): persist the last ~20 messages per recently opened thread for loopback or desktop primary environments, alongside primaryShellCache, and seed them through hydrateEnvironmentStateFromCache. This only improves the first open after a reload, and it changes what the persistence boundary stores, so treat it as a product decision.

Value medium · effort S · risk low

Current state

Partial#131 Thread windows are 80–95 % full tool output and diffs, and pre-#481 rows still carry raw outputs up to 1 MB

thread-and-draft:thread-window-activity-overfetch · original impact Medium, effort L · Network / RTT WP14A

First-pass audit said PARTIAL; the verifier corrected it. PARTIAL holds and the mobile gap is real. I found no mobile or Hub-side implementation the auditor missed. Their fixDefects line ('None seen') is wrong, though: the fix has two small fidelity regressions on web/desktop. (a) Multi-file file_change previews collapse to 4 changes. (b) Long commands stay truncated in the expanded panel after the full payload loads. The auditor also left out that live and replayed thread.activity-appended events still carry full payloads. That is outside the finding's window scope and low worth.

Current state

The server side shipped in 36760bffd: bounded per-kind previews (8 KiB for tool rows, 64 KiB for other kinds) with payloadPreview {fullBytes}, orchestration.getActivityPayload (2 MiB cap, viewer/read policy) and migration 088, which re-projects legacy rows. The web/desktop client opts in and fetches on expand (a01ef8557). Both commits are in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3, and the Hub has no method allowlist that needs a change. The native mobile client never opts in, so the intended phone surface still gets full payloads, bounded only by the 1 MiB window budget. Within the fix, the preview levels cut arrays to 16 and then 4 items at the same step that strings shrink. A file_change touching 14 or more files with ordinary diffs therefore keeps only 4 changes, and the collapsed row shows 'Edited 4 files' with +/- totals for those 4. The expanded panel also re-derives only output and exitCode from the fetched payload, so commands longer than 2 KiB stay cut with an ellipsis.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/activityPayloadPreview.ts:26-31,129-153 Per-kind preview budgets and boundPayload/previewActivityPayload are implemented as the auditor described.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:225-241,3880-3885,4277-4282 toSentActivityRows is applied before the 1 MiB byte budget, both for windows and for history pages.
  • apps/server/src/ws/orchestrationRpc.ts:185,442-445 activityPayloads is forwarded for get/subscribeThreadWindow, and getActivityPayload is registered.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations/088_LegacyActivityPayloads.ts:32-94 Legacy re-projection: tool rows over 16,000 B go through capActivityData and projectActivityPayload. It is idempotent, recorded in ryco_compatibility_repairs and also re-run as a boot repair (Migrations.ts:547,749).
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:199 Web/desktop sets threadWindowActivityPayloads: 'preview'. The supervisor applies it to windows, activity history pages and stale recovery (packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:478-507,656).
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:629-636 The mobile supervisor config has no threadWindowActivityPayloads. rg finds no payloadPreview, getActivityPayload or outputPreviewActivityId anywhere in apps/mobile.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/threads/threadActivityFold.ts:96 and ThreadActivityFoldRow.tsx:29,89-94 Mobile renders entry.output whole from the window payload when a row is opened. There is no on-demand fetch.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/activityPayloadPreview.ts:55-62,137-141 Fix defect (a). Level 2 is {512 chars, 16 items} and level 3 is {128 chars, 4 items}, so arrays shrink as strings shrink. I re-ran the same algorithm in node: a file_change with 12 changes and ~3 KB diffs lands at level 2 and keeps 12; with 14 or more changes it lands at level 3 and keeps 4.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/session/session-logic.ts:2008-2017,2108-2119 and apps/web/src/components/chat/MessagesTimeline.tsx:2892-2908 changedFiles and changedFileStats come from the (preview) payload, capped at 12. The collapsed row's 'Edited N files' count and +/- summary therefore drop to 4 files' worth for large multi-file edits. Tests cover only a 2-change payload (activityPayloadPreview.test.ts:27-53).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/session/session-logic.ts:1829-1834 and apps/web/src/components/chat/MessagesTimeline.tsx:3075-3082 Fix defect (b). deriveActivityPayloadOutput returns only output and exitCode. The panel's inputLine comes from workEntryRawCommand(workEntry), which is derived from the preview, so a command over 2048 chars stays cut with an ellipsis after the full payload loads. Before the fix it showed up to 16,000 chars.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:937,965 and apps/server/src/orchestration/activityDataCap.ts:24 Live and replayed thread events (thread.activity-appended) still carry full activity payloads. file_change diffs are exempt from the 16K cap. This is out of the finding's window scope; it is incremental cost only.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:2140-2164 The window SQL still selects and JSON-decodes full payload_json for limit+1 rows, and all of them are previewed before the budget cut. This affects server CPU only, not wire size.
Remaining

1) Mobile, the main gap. apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:629-636 does not set threadWindowActivityPayloads: 'preview', and mobile has no getActivityPayload fetch (threadActivityFold.ts:88-101 drops outputPreviewActivityId; ThreadActivityFoldRow.tsx:89-94 renders row.output directly). Mobile windows and history pages therefore still carry full tool output and diffs, up to the 1 MiB activity budget per window, over hosted relays and cellular links. 2) The fix defects listed in fixDefects. 3) Optional, low worth: live and replayed thread.activity-appended events still carry full payloads, including uncapped file_change diffs (orchestrationStreams.ts:937,965). 4) Optional, low worth: the server still reads and parses full payload_json for up to 201 rows per window or page and previews all of them before the budget cut (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:2140-2164, 3881-3885, 4278-4282).

Defects in the shipped fix

(a) Preview levels cut arrays in the same step that strings shrink (activityPayloadPreview.ts:55-62). A file_change whose changes do not fit at level 2 (512 chars, 16 items) drops to level 3 (128 chars, 4 items). In practice that means about 14 or more changed files with diffs of roughly 600 B or more, which I verified by simulating the exact algorithm. The web collapsed row then reads 'Edited 4 files' with +/- totals for only those 4 (MessagesTimeline.tsx:2892-2908; derivation at session-logic.ts:2008-2017,2108-2119). Before the fix it showed up to 12 files. The expanded panel never re-derives changedFiles or changedFileStats from the fetched payload. (b) WorkEntryExpandedPanel (MessagesTimeline.tsx:3075-3082) takes inputLine from the preview-derived work entry, and deriveActivityPayloadOutput (session-logic.ts:1829-1834) returns only output and exitCode. Commands over 2048 chars (heredocs, python -c scripts) therefore stay cut with an ellipsis even after the full payload loads; before the fix they showed up to the 16,000-char ingestion cap. Both are small display regressions, not correctness or security issues.

Implementation sketch

Mobile: (1) Move the keyed query from apps/web/src/rpc/activityPayloadAtoms.ts into packages/client-runtime/src/rpc as makeActivityPayloadQuery({ resolveGetActivityPayload(environmentId) }), keeping stale Infinity, gc 2 min and max 16 entries. Web and mobile each pass their own ensureEnvironmentApi(...).orchestration.getActivityPayload. Mobile already uses defineKeyedQueryByKey in apps/mobile/src/rpc/projectFilesAtoms.ts. Keep deriveActivityPayloadOutput shared. (2) Add threadWindowActivityPayloads: 'preview' to the supervisor input in apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts (next to syncThreadWindowSnapshot, about line 633). (3) Carry outputPreviewActivityId on ActivityRow in threadActivityFold.ts toRow. (4) In ThreadActivityFoldRow.tsx, when the row is open and the id is set, watch the query: show the preview text with a small spinner, then the full output, with retry on error and a 'truncated' note when result.truncated. Tests: a threadActivityFold unit test for the id passthrough, and a row test with a mocked getActivityPayload. Fix (a): in activityPayloadPreview.ts previewLevels, shrink strings before arrays, for example [{s:base,a:64},{s:base/4,a:64},{s:base/16,a:64},{s:base/16,a:16},{s:base/16,a:4}], or never cut arrays below 12 items before the scalar shell. Optionally also re-derive changedFiles and changedFileStats from the fetched payload in the expanded panel. Add an activityPayloadPreview.test.ts case: a 20-file file_change with 2 KB diffs stays under 8 KiB and keeps at least 12 changes with path, additions and deletions. Fix (b): extend deriveActivityPayloadOutput to also return rawCommand/command (reuse session-logic's existing command-preview extractor) and the changed-file lists. Use them in WorkEntryExpandedPanel once loaded, and cover it with a long-command case in MessagesTimeline.browser.tsx (near the existing getActivityPayload test, about line 1206). Optional: preview live thread.activity-appended activities for preview-mode thread subscriptions. That means threading the mode into makeReplayableThreadStream and mapping event.payload.activity through previewActivityPayload with payloadPreview. It is low value because live rows are what the user is watching.

Value medium · effort M · risk low

Done#132 Branch list is fetched twice on first mount and again on every thread switch (~7 git processes each)

thread-and-draft:branch-listrefs-duplicate-and-teardown · original impact Low, effort S · Process spawns

Current state

Confirmed DONE (commit 60633eff3, #710). On first mount, the prefetch and the controller now share one in-flight first-page read per key. This holds whichever effect runs first: the prefetch registers its request synchronously, and the poller's run happens a microtask later and joins it. A remount within the 15 s stale time adopts the cached pages and the ledger timestamp, and its poller does not run immediately. Past 15 s it refetches, which is exactly the rule the proposal gave, so dropping the idle-TTL keep-alive changes nothing visible. On the server, listRefs is now one for-each-ref plus a cached config snapshot, behind a 5 s per-cwd listing cache. That cache is dropped by driver writes and by GitManager invalidateLocalStatus/invalidateStatus after git actions and agent turns. Only two small issues remain in how invalidations interact with the new freshness ledger. Neither brings back the duplicate or teardown cost.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/rpc/gitAtoms.ts:232 branchesFirstPageInFlight plus the branchesFetchedAt ledger. fetchFirstBranchesPage (265-286) joins a pending first-page read per key and marks detached reads with fetchedAt=null.
  • apps/web/src/components/BranchToolbarBranchSelector.tsx:242 The prefetch effect (242-245) still runs before useGitBranches (254 -> useGit.ts:60 watchBranches). prefetchBranchesByKey (gitAtoms.ts:604-641) puts its request in the shared map synchronously. The controller's poller runs pollBranches a microtask later (visibilityPolling.ts:46-49), and loadInitialBranchesNow (gitAtoms.ts:340) joins that request, so first mount issues exactly one listRefs. If the order were reversed, prefetch returns early because a controller exists (608-612).
  • apps/web/src/rpc/gitAtoms.ts:531 watchBranches adopts the cached pages when the ledger is within GIT_BRANCHES_STALE_TIME_MS (105). It sets hasLoadedOnce, and runImmediately is !adoptCached (575), so a thread or draft remount within 15 s makes no listRefs. unwatchBranches (585-602) still deletes the controller, but the proposal also refetches past 15 s, so behavior is equivalent.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/gitAtoms.ts:302 markBranchesStaleForScopes (called from invalidateScopes:53) drops ledger entries and in-flight joins for the cwd, so the menu-open invalidation (BranchToolbarBranchSelector.tsx:515) and branch actions (396) are not hidden by adoption.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/gitAtoms.ts:410 Defect (minor): refetchBranchesNow writes the ledger whenever generation === branchesFetchGeneration. That generation only changes in clearGitAtomState (859), not on invalidation. An invalidation that lands during an in-flight 60 s poll is swallowed by the poller's inFlight dedupe (visibilityPolling.ts:47), and the ledger is then re-stamped fresh for a pre-invalidation read. A remount within 15 s adopts it. The first-page path has explicit protection against this through detach (fetchedAt=null); the refetch path does not.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/gitAtoms.ts:350 Defect (minor, the auditor's): controller.lastFetchedAt = Date.now() even for a detached read (fetchedAt === null). This suppresses the focus stale refetch (maybeRefetchStaleBranches:506) for 15 s after an invalidation was swallowed.

Done#133 The client re-serialises every snapshot and live event just to estimate memory

Current state

Confirmed DONE. Commit 8fb94df00 swapped the per-snapshot, per-event and per-history-page TextEncoder.encode(JSON.stringify(value)) for approximateJsonSize, a walker that adds up string lengths. Live events are now sized per written row: an O(1) text.length for streaming deltas, a walk of the single activity or plan for upserts, and nothing for other events. evictToCapacity runs once per delivered chunk through a microtask. All 3 old estimator call sites and every per-event evictToCapacity call were converted. I benchmarked real 150-activity plus 150-message windows from the user's state.sqlite (161-319 KB, full payloads, so heavier than the web's preview payloads). The walk took 0.057-0.070 ms against 0.46-0.98 ms for the old stringify plus encode, 7-17x cheaper and below the windows' JSON.parse time (~0.26-0.33 ms). wsTransport hands each chunk to the listener synchronously, so the microtask coalescing really does run eviction once per chunk. Tests cover a pinned thread streaming past the budget and an activity updated in place being counted once. I found no other code path that re-serializes thread snapshots or events just to measure them. recordWebPerfPayload is behind the perf-profile flag. The remaining stringify sizers (sourceControlAtoms estimatePayloadBytes, workspaceMetadataPayloadBytes, hosted read vault encryption) sit outside this path or need the bytes anyway.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/approximateJsonSize.ts:12-43 Walker: string.length+2, small constants for number, boolean and null, key length plus 4 per key. It builds no serialized string or Uint8Array, caps depth at 64 and keeps a cycle-guard Set.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:206-207 estimateJsonLength = approximateJsonSize. git grep finds no TextEncoder or JSON.stringify left in the supervisor.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:215-247 retainedRowWrite: streaming message-sent costs text.length only (matches mergeMessageUpdate's append at state/threads/store.ts:1663-1670). Activity and plan upserts walk the one row. Every other event type returns null.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:434-455 recordRetainedSnapshot walks the snapshot once. recordRetainedEvent applies a per-row delta through rowRetainedBytes. recordRetainedHistoryPage walks page.items.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:567-572 applyEvent calls scheduleEvictToCapacity, not evictToCapacity, for each event.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:724-751 evictToCapacity (at most 32 entries) is coalesced by scheduleEvictToCapacity into one microtask after the chunk. It runs synchronously only after snapshots (586, 665) and stale recovery (517). The history-page apply at 496 also uses the scheduled path.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:770-781,1304 The companion per-event reconcileForEnvironment timer re-arm is coalesced the same way, once per chunk.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts:545-577 Stream.runForEachArray hands each server chunk to the listener in one synchronous loop, so the microtask really fires once per chunk.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/evictionPolicy.ts:33-42 planEvictionsToCapacity returns early when under both caps.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.test.ts:665-718 Tests cover a pinned thread streaming past the byte budget without evicting idle ones, and an in-place activity update counted once.

Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness defects. Two caveats, neither worth reopening. (1) The walker's cost scales with object count, not bytes, and its per-object cost (closure recursion, for...in plus hasOwn, Set.add) is higher than stringify's. A synthetic payload of about 100k tiny objects (3.5 MB) took 7.3 ms against 6.0 ms for the old stringify plus encode. Real windows hold about 700-800 objects, the web requests 'preview' payloads (capped strings and arrays), and the most object-dense real activity has about 1.4k braces, so this does not happen in practice. (2) The 'seen' Set dedupes shared (non-cyclic) references as well as cycles, so a shared subtree is counted once. Decoded wire data is a fresh tree, so this changes nothing.

The auditor's suggested fallback (getFixedItemSize instead of writing getState().sizes) is not a defect in the code, but it is a flawed recommendation: getFixedItemSize writes into the same sizesKnown map (react.mjs:1155-1162) and short-circuits checkAllSizesKnown in the same way. It does not avoid the suspected readiness problem.

Step 0 (gate): use the describeBlankTimeline warning (MessagesTimeline.tsx:696-722) in dev or dogfood to collect `hidden`, listRange and listBufferedRange, and whether didFinishInitialScroll was reached, on the current 56 px build. If blank reports still appear with no seeding at all, the cache was not the cause. Step 1 (low risk, S): raise only the estimate. Change MessagesTimeline.tsx:909 to a named constant around 100-120 px. It touches no list internals. Verify with a real-list browser test: restore the deleted MessagesTimeline.rowHeights.browser.tsx from 5ebb23825^ minus the cache assertions. Mount a ~150-message fixture, count [data-timeline-root] elements after settle (expect about 11 instead of 23), and assert that the end anchor is reached and the content wrapper's opacity is not 0 (reuse describeBlankTimeline logic) with both initialScrollAtEnd and a readHostedThreadScroll offset. Step 2 (M, only after step 0 clears it): reuse heights without feeding the readiness path. One option is to keep a module LRU (thread key + row id + rounded width) written from onItemSizeChanged. Instead of seeding sizesKnown, use it to compute a per-thread mean or median height, pass that as estimatedItemSize on remount, and pass estimatedListSize from the last viewport. The list then still measures every mounted row before it reports readiness. Another option is to seed only rows outside the initial buffered range, so that above-the-fold rows are still measured before checkAllSizesKnown passes. Do not use getFixedItemSize for this: it has the same sizesKnown effect. A third option is to stop keying MessagesTimeline by thread, which keeps LegendList's own caches; that is a larger change with scroll and expansion state reset implications. Tests: a browser test that opens thread A, switches to B, returns to A, and asserts no blank (opacity 1, rowsInView > 0), at most N onItemSizeChanged corrections, and the end anchor held. Also cover a width change between visits.

Current state

PARTIAL is right. #710 (60633eff3) removed the headline cost. Settled code blocks now render as plain text, and DeferredShikiCodeBlock queues a job in codeHighlightQueue, which runs codeToHtml in requestIdleCallback slots, on-screen blocks first, and swaps the HTML in. The cost has moved off the commit, but it still runs on the main thread. The first block of each grammar costs 50-80 ms, large blocks cost 44 ms warm and 165 ms cold for 400 TSX lines, and both still land as long tasks in idle time. (2) codeHighlightQueue.ts:119 and :126 pass no tokenizeMaxLineLength. Keep the queue, LRU and visibility ordering on the main thread. Replace highlight() with a promise-based post to a single lazily created worker, and fall back to the current main-thread path when Worker is unavailable or the worker fails. Optionally terminate the worker after an idle grace, like diffWorkerPoolOwner. Stage 3 (S, optional): once the worker exists, prewarm it with ts/tsx/json/bash/diff as a last task in ShellIdlePreloads (RootAppShell.tsx:178), gated by allowsSpeculativePreload. Validate with the focused tests (codeHighlightQueue.test.ts, ChatMarkdown.browser.tsx, chatViewBundleSplitting.test.ts), and keep the parity HTML class .chat-markdown-shiki pre.shiki so styling stays the same.

If that hits the quota, onWriteError only logs and verifyPersistedAttachments drops the attachment so the prompt still saves. In hosted mode verify drops it right away, because readPersistedAttachmentIds returns [] there. (2) The first flush after hydration re-stringifies every hydrated draft once, because hydrated entries have draft:null. This is a one-off and skips the writes because the JSON is identical. Done#139 Seed the checkpoint temp index from the real index instead of read-tree HEAD (7x faster capture)

gap-first-turn-latency:checkpoint-seeded-index · original impact High, effort S · Process spawns

Current state

DONE holds. Commit 60633eff3 (#710) removes both costs in the finding. (1) captureCheckpoint seeds its temp GIT_INDEX_FILE from a copy of the checkout's real index, so `add -A` only rehashes files whose stat data changed. It no longer rehashes every tracked file after `read-tree HEAD`. The spawn count stays at 6. (2) Positive VCS detections are cached for 2 minutes instead of 2 s, and each read checks the dev:ino:kind identity of <root>/.git again. Negative detections stay at 2 s. The seeding code handles these cases: linked worktrees (`--git-path index`); racy git (the copy keeps the original mtime, truncated to ms, which only makes more entries racy; update-index later writes the temp index from that timestamp, so racy entries are still smudged); assume-unchanged entries (cleared on the copy); skip-worktree/sparse and split index (fall back to read-tree HEAD); listings over 64 MiB, no index yet and old git (non-absolute output) also fall back. It never fails: catchCause returns false. Both the turn-start baseline (:784) and the completion capture (:532) use it. No other code path rebuilds an index from HEAD and rehashes it. GitIndexReview already copied index bytes, and prepareCommitContext's `add -A` uses the real index. Two optional leftovers, neither a regression: sparse-checkout repos always fall back (no speedup, by design), and one detect spawn (about 45 ms) still runs once per 2-minute cache expiry.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/checkpointing/Layers/CheckpointStore.ts:138-213 seedIndexFromCheckout: rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index; sharedindex.* check on the index's directory; stat, copyFile, utimes(orig mtime); ls-files -v -z with a 64 MiB cap; S/s tag -> false; lowercase tag -> update-index --no-assume-unchanged -z --stdin on the copy (env carries GIT_INDEX_FILE); catchCause -> false.
  • apps/server/src/checkpointing/Layers/CheckpointStore.ts:233-258 Seeds first. Only when seeding fails does it remove the partial copy, then run hasHeadCommit and read-tree HEAD. add -A / write-tree / commit-tree / update-ref are unchanged. The old version always ran rev-parse plus read-tree HEAD into an empty index (git show f1be4abc7:...CheckpointStore.ts).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/CheckpointReactor.ts:432-466 resolveCheckpointCwd returns a cwd only when isGitWorkspace(cwd), which is existsSync(<cwd>/.git) (apps/server/src/git/Utils.ts:4-5). So capture cwds are always checkout roots and the auditor's subdirectory defect cannot happen.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/CheckpointReactor.ts:532 The completion capture (captureAndDispatchCheckpoint) uses the seeded captureCheckpoint.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/CheckpointReactor.ts:784 The first-turn and pre-turn baseline capture uses the same path. The knownCheckpointRefs memo skips git entirely after the first baseline.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsDriverRegistry.ts:12-20,138-190 NEGATIVE TTL 2 s, POSITIVE TTL 2 min. detect() checks the <root>/.git identity (and a nested <cwd>/.git) again on every read and invalidates when it changes. Old code: one DETECTION_CACHE_TTL = 2 s for both. Covered by VcsDriverRegistry.test.ts ('keeps a detected checkout until its .git identity changes').
  • apps/server/src/checkpointing/Layers/CheckpointStore.test.ts:179-297 Tests: seeded tree equals referenceCaptureTree with staged, unstaged, untracked and deleted changes at once; real index untouched; racy same-size edit; assume-unchanged; skip-worktree fallback; linked worktree; repo with no commits. Untested: split-index fallback, and ignored paths whose tracked state differs between index and HEAD.
  • apps/server/src/checkpointing/Layers/CheckpointStore.ts:131-133 The doc comment says the seeded tree equals read-tree HEAD + add -A. That is not exact for ignored paths that are tracked in only one of HEAD or the index, or for modes staged under core.fileMode=false (see fixDefects).
Defects in the shipped fix

Low severity, semantic only, no perf impact: the seeded tree is NOT always identical to read-tree HEAD + add -A, contrary to the doc comment at CheckpointStore.ts:131-133. `add -A` updates tracked entries even when ignored, but never adds untracked ignored files. So the result now follows the real index, not HEAD, for ignored paths whose tracked state differs between the two. (a) A file force-added with `git add -f` but not committed is now recorded; before, it was omitted. (b) A file untracked with `git rm --cached` while HEAD still has it and .gitignore matches it (for example .env) is now omitted; before, it was recorded with its worktree content. The same applies to modes staged with `update-index --chmod` under core.fileMode=false or core.symlinks=false. Effects: turn diffs show these index-only changes before they are committed. restoreCheckpoint (`git restore --source C --worktree --staged -- .`) removes tracked paths that are missing from C. Case (b) can therefore delete an ignored local file such as .env if that path is tracked in the index again by restore time, for example after a previous revert's `git reset -- .` put it back. Case (a) used to have the mirror-image risk, and seeding removes it. Both chains are narrow.

Implementation sketch

Optional polish, all in apps/server/src/checkpointing/Layers/CheckpointStore.ts (seedIndexFromCheckout). (1) Exact equivalence with the old algorithm: before copying, run `git diff-index --cached --no-renames --name-only -z --diff-filter=AD HEAD` against the real index (cheap, uses cache-tree; skip when there is no HEAD). Pipe those paths to `git check-ignore -z --stdin --no-index`. If any is ignored, return false (fall back to read-tree HEAD). Optionally do the same for mode-only staged changes (`diff-index --cached --raw` with old mode != new mode) when core.fileMode is false. Otherwise just correct the doc comment to describe the index-following semantics. (2) Sparse-checkout speedup (low value): when S entries exist, return false only if one of them differs between index and HEAD. Check this by intersecting the S paths with `git diff-index --cached --name-only -z HEAD`. Otherwise keep the seeded copy, because add -A leaves skip-worktree entries alone and they equal HEAD. (3) VcsDriverRegistry.ts:20: since every read checks .git again, POSITIVE_DETECTION_CACHE_TTL could be raised to 10-30 min to remove the remaining detect spawn after idle, but that saves only about 45 ms per expiry. Tests in CheckpointStore.test.ts, compared against referenceCaptureTree: a force-added ignored file, a `git rm --cached` ignored file, a sparse-checkout cone with an unmodified out-of-cone path, and a split index (`git update-index --split-index`) falling back.

Partial#140 Per-turn attachment-instructions prefix turns '/compact' and every Claude slash command into a plain prompt

gap-first-turn-latency:attachment-prefix-breaks-claude-slash-commands · original impact High, effort S · Reliability WP01

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor marked this DONE with no defect in the fix. That is wrong. The new 'session' channel for Claude (top-level appendSystemPrompt) is ignored by the pinned Claude Agent SDK 0.3.296, so the instructions never reach Claude: this is a regression from the old per-turn prefix. The auditor's ClaudeAdapter.test.ts:623,634 evidence only checks the options object, not what the SDK sends to the CLI. The adjacent gaps the auditor named (Ultrathink prefix, source-control contexts ahead of slash commands) cannot be reached today: the bundled manifest has no promptInjectedValues, and turn-start sourceControlContexts are never forwarded to ProviderSendTurnInput, which is itself a separate bug.

Current state

The bug the finding describes is fixed. ProviderService.sendTurn no longer prefixes attachment instructions per turn. Slash commands and '/compact' reach the Claude adapter verbatim, the Claude host-context and goal prefixes skip slash input, and buildPromptText still returns a bare '/compact'. The other half of the proposal, moving the instructions to Claude's session-level system prompt, does not actually work. ClaudeAdapter passes them as a top-level `appendSystemPrompt` query option, and the pinned @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.296 ignores that option: query() reads appended text only from `systemPrompt: {type:'preset', append}`. I confirmed this with a fake spawnClaudeCodeProcess. A top-level appendSystemPrompt marker never appears in the initialize request or the CLI args. The same marker passed as systemPrompt.append arrives as initialize.appendSystemPrompt. Since 60633eff3, Claude therefore receives no attachment instructions at all, which is a regression: before, they reached Claude through the prompt prefix. The same dead channel also drops the token-mode reduction instructions and the project custom system prompt for Claude, a pre-existing bug since 6fceb686c and ba08d1f55. The auditor's adjacent gaps (Ultrathink prefix, source-control contexts ahead of slash commands) cannot be reached today. The bundled model-manifest declares no promptInjectedValues, and thread.turn.start never forwards sourceControlContexts to the provider: the event payload has no such field.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:1747-1760 Per-turn prefix removed. Adapters with the 'session' capability get no prefix, slash input is never prefixed, and other adapters get it once per runtime through the tracker.
  • apps/server/src/provider/attachmentInstructionDelivery.ts:17-60 isSlashCommandInput guard plus the once-per-runtime tracker; ProviderService.ts:2399 forgets the thread on rollback.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.test.ts:3778-3860 /compact and hello pass through verbatim with a Claude double that declares 'session'. First-turn adapters get the prefix once, /init goes out verbatim, and the prefix is re-sent after rollback. The Claude double never exercises the real system-prompt channel.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:5572-5580 appendSystemPrompt combines ASSISTANT_ATTACHMENT_INSTRUCTIONS, the token reduction instructions and the project custom system prompt.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:5612-5613 DEFECT: the options set `systemPrompt: { type: "preset", preset: "claude_code" }` with no `append`, and `appendSystemPrompt` sits at the top level behind `as Partial<ClaudeQueryOptions>`. The cast is needed because the SDK Options type has no such field.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:1917-1927 createQuery calls the SDK query() directly with these options, and no wrapper translates appendSystemPrompt.
  • apps/server/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:1526-2464 SDK 0.3.296 `Options` has no appendSystemPrompt. The documented way to append is systemPrompt {type:'preset', preset:'claude_code', append} (around :2330-2371). appendSystemPrompt exists only on ClaimOptions (:364) and the internal initialize request (:4534).
  • apps/server/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs (function yT) `{systemPrompt:s,...,...d}=e; ... else if(s.type==="preset")f=s.append ...; WZ={systemPrompt:p,appendSystemPrompt:f,...}`. The append text comes only from systemPrompt.append, and options.appendSystemPrompt is never read. Probe with a fake spawnClaudeCodeProcess: the top-level marker gave initialize appendSystemPrompt undefined; systemPrompt.append gave the marker.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.test.ts:619-639 The test only checks the options object handed to the fake createQuery (cast to {appendSystemPrompt}), so it cannot catch the SDK ignoring the field.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:1351-1371 buildPromptText returns a bare '/compact'. For other slash commands it can still prepend source-control contexts or 'Ultrathink:', but neither input reaches this code today (see the next two entries).
  • apps/server/src/provider/model-manifest.json No profile declares promptInjectedValues, so resolvePromptInjectedEffort never returns 'ultrathink' with the bundled catalog. A remotely refreshed manifest could change that.
  • packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:2826-2845 ThreadTurnStartRequestedPayload has no sourceControlContexts, and no server orchestration code forwards them. ProviderSendTurnInput.sourceControlContexts is never set on the turn-start path. This is a separate bug: context chips are dropped on normal sends and only inlined on queued steers (ChatView.tsx:3992-3995).
Remaining

Session-level delivery of the attachment instructions to Claude has no effect. apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:5612-5613 passes appendSystemPrompt as a top-level SDK option, and @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.296 ignores it; only systemPrompt.append is read. Claude therefore gets ASSISTANT_ATTACHMENT_INSTRUCTIONS neither per turn nor in the system prompt. The same applies to the token-mode reduction instructions and the project custom system prompt.

Defects in the shipped fix

Regression from 60633eff3. Claude now declares attachmentInstructions: "session" (ClaudeAdapter.ts:6661), so ProviderService stopped prefixing the instructions. The replacement channel, appendSystemPrompt at ClaudeAdapter.ts:5613, is silently dropped by the SDK, as confirmed against sdk.mjs and a spawn probe. As a result Claude is no longer told about the ryco-attachments fence fallback or the attachment rules. File delivery from Claude threads now depends on the ryco_attach_file tool being installed. The unit test at ClaudeAdapter.test.ts:619-639 asserts the ignored field, which hides the problem. Pre-existing on the same line: since 6fceb686c and ba08d1f55, the project custom system prompt and the token-reduction instructions have never reached Claude either. Minor, not regressions: isSlashCommandInput also matches prompts that start with an absolute path ('/Users/...'), which only defers the first-turn prefix, host context and goal by one turn and keeps such a message from being steered into a running Claude turn. A context handoff still puts its context document ahead of a slash command, which is expected for a handoff.

Implementation sketch

1) In ClaudeAdapter.ts startSession (around :5608-5613), replace the top-level cast with `systemPrompt: { type: "preset", preset: "claude_code", ...(appendSystemPrompt ? { append: appendSystemPrompt } : {}) }` and delete the `appendSystemPrompt` spread. The removal of the `as Partial<ClaudeQueryOptions>` cast then lets the type checker enforce the shape. Add a span attribute such as claude.query.system_prompt_append_bytes for observability. 2) Update ClaudeAdapter.test.ts:619-639 to assert `options.systemPrompt` deep-equals {type:'preset', preset:'claude_code', append: <string containing ASSISTANT_ATTACHMENT_INSTRUCTIONS>}. Add cases for a project customSystemPrompt and a token-reduction mode landing in systemPrompt.append, and assert there is no top-level appendSystemPrompt key. 3) Optionally add a small SDK-contract test that calls the real SDK query() with a fake spawnClaudeCodeProcess (PassThrough stdin/stdout) and checks that the initialize control request's appendSystemPrompt contains the marker. That guards against future SDK option renames; the probe that confirmed this bug took about 30 lines. 4) Note on rollout: by default the SDK and CLI record the system prompt on the first request and reuse it on resume until compaction (systemPromptSnapshot). Resumed existing Claude sessions may therefore pick up the appended text only after their next compaction, while new sessions get it at once. That is acceptable; setting `snapshot: false` would trade prompt-cache stability and is not recommended. 5) Optional hardening, not needed today: make ClaudeAdapter.buildPromptText return `input.input.trim()` unchanged when isSlashCommandInput(input.input) and there are no attachments. That generalizes the /compact bypass so a future source-control-context or Ultrathink prefix cannot break /init, /review or custom commands. Validate with focused vitest runs only: `bun run test` filtered to ClaudeAdapter.test.ts and ProviderService.test.ts, plus `bun typecheck` for apps/server.

gap-first-turn-latency:speculative-session-prewarm · original impact High, effort L · Process spawns WP02WP10WP14A

First-pass audit said PARTIAL; the verifier corrected it. The auditor's PARTIAL status and the three remaining gaps hold (worktree and chat-folder first sends, native mobile, no eviction or latency measurement). Their fixDefects claim, "No correctness bug seen in the adopt/stop/expire paths", is wrong. The claim path in ensureSessionForThread ignores options.computerCatalogChanged. Prewarm fires on composer focus, before the user can type /computer-use. So a computer-use first turn on a new, stopped or reaped thread adopts a session whose Agent Control tool catalog was fixed at boot without the computer tools. A minor inaccuracy: makeRoom evicts the oldest ready entry, so browsing does not just hit the caps; each visit retires a warm process and spawns a new one. The concurrency race I suspected between two prewarms of one thread is harmless, because ProviderService.startSession stops the previous runtime of the same thread.

Current state

Prewarm is implemented. 440c42224, 65c7e6f2d, a8a683529 and 3cbe9a677 added an owner-gated provider.prewarmSession RPC, a server pool (2 per instance, 4 overall, 2-minute TTL), adopt-or-stop at the turn start through a shared start key, and web triggers on composer focus and the first keystroke. A send adopts the warm session. Claude's query() spawns the CLI and sends initialize eagerly, so the CLI boot overlaps with typing. Codex startSession awaits initialize and thread/start. Still not covered: sends that first create a worktree or chat folder (the default env mode is local, so this is opt-in worktree users only), and the native mobile app, which never calls the RPC. There is also a regression the auditor missed. The claim path skips the computer-catalog restart check, so a /computer-use first turn adopts a prewarmed session whose MCP tools were listed before the computer plan was staged.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderSessionPrewarm.ts:251 prewarm(): resolveStart and then providerService.startSession unbound from orchestration. Pool limits are at lines 74-76. makeRoom (158-180) retires the oldest ready entry, so each new prewarm past the cap kills a warm process and spawns another.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderSessionPrewarm.ts:203 Requires an existing cwd. A draft that first creates a worktree or chat folder can never be prewarmed server-side.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderSessionPrewarm.ts:315 claim() compares threadProviderStartKey only. The key (threadProviderStart.ts:78-87) has no computer-use or catalog dimension.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:1119 With no live session the claim path adopts the prewarm unconditionally. options.computerCatalogChanged is honoured only for existing sessions (line 1007), not here.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:1303 computerCatalogChanged is computed, and stageComputerTurn runs (1305), right before ensureSessionForThread (1317). A fresh start would boot with the plan staged; an adopted prewarm booted without it.
  • apps/server/src/agentControl/Mcp/computerBetaTools.ts:215 descriptorsFor adds the computer tools only when computerTurnPlan(threadId) is staged at tools/list time.
  • apps/server/src/agentControl/Mcp/listener.ts:254 The Agent Control MCP advertises listChanged:false, and tools/list (265) is evaluated when the CLI connects at boot. A prewarmed Claude or Codex session keeps the catalog without computer tools for the claimed turn.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/OpenCodeAdapter.ts:2134 OpenCode installs the computer lease (2178-2184) only when the plan is staged at startSession. A prewarmed OpenCode session therefore has no computer lease. This fails closed (no authority leak) but breaks the computer-use turn.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.test.ts:7576 The prewarm tests cover adopt, mid-start wait, mismatch, idle expiry, cursor discard, pool limit and drafts. None covers a computer-use turn adopting a prewarm.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:5667 createQuery is called at startSession. In SDK 0.3.296, ProcessTransport spawns in its constructor (or right after async prep when deferSpawn is set), and Query sends initialize eagerly. awaitCliInitialized (5929) then resolves at once on the first turn of a warm session.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:1426 startSession stops the thread's previous runtime before starting a new one. Orphans from racing prewarms or from handoff starts are cleaned up.
  • apps/server/src/ws/providerSessionPrewarmRpc.ts:12 The RPC is ownerEffect-gated. The capability is advertised at apps/server/src/environment/Layers/ServerEnvironment.ts:102.
Remaining

1. Worktree and chat-folder first sends are never prewarmed. The web client skips them at apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:5228 and 5243, and the server needs an existing cwd at ProviderSessionPrewarm.ts:203. Users who opt into worktree mode still pay the full Claude or Codex start on the first turn. 2. The native mobile app (apps/mobile), the intended phone surface, never calls requestProviderSessionPrewarm (packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/sessionPrewarm.ts:35). 3. Minor gaps: - No eviction on memory pressure or settings change. - No dwell delay on focus-triggered prewarm, so browsing threads churns full-config CLI processes (ChatView.tsx:3345 plus makeRoom at ProviderSessionPrewarm.ts:158). - No real latency measurement; only a mocked one at ProviderCommandReactor.test.ts:7625.

Defects in the shipped fix

Regression: a computer-use first turn adopts a prewarmed session that lacks the computer tools. The path: 1. Opening or focusing a thread whose session is stopped or absent prewarms it (ChatView.tsx:3345, then onFocusCapture, then provider.prewarmSession). 2. The prewarmed CLI connects to the Agent Control MCP at boot and lists tools while no computer plan is staged, so computerBetaTools.ts:215 omits the computer descriptors. listChanged is false (agentControl/Mcp/listener.ts:254), so the list never refreshes. 3. When the user sends /computer-use, runTurnStart stages the plan and computes computerCatalogChanged=true (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:1303-1316). ensureSessionForThread honours that flag only for an existing live session (line 1007). The no-session branch claims and binds the prewarm unconditionally (1119-1128). Result: Claude and Codex run the turn without the computer tools. OpenCode never installed the computer lease (OpenCodeAdapter.ts:2134, 2178), and its host context says Agent Control without computer. This fails closed, with no authority leak, but the desktop beta computer-use feature breaks on the first turn of every new, stopped or reaped thread. No test covers it (ProviderCommandReactor.test.ts:7576-7790).

Implementation sketch

A. Computer-use defect (do first; S effort, low risk). - Add a `computerTurn: boolean` field to ThreadProviderStart. - Include it in threadProviderStartKey (apps/server/src/orchestration/threadProviderStart.ts:78). - In ProviderCommandReactor's desiredStart (around line 879), set it to `computerTurnPlan(threadId) !== undefined`. The plan is already staged before ensureSessionForThread. - In ProviderSessionPrewarm.resolveStart (around line 221), set it the same way. In practice that is false at focus time. - A computer turn then mismatches. claim() stops the warm runtime (and discards a never-run native conversation), and the turn starts fresh with the plan staged. - Simpler alternative: in ensureSessionForThread, skip the claim when options.computerCatalogChanged or computerTurnPlan(threadId) is set. This needs an explicit retire of the entry, e.g. a new `discard(threadId)` on ProviderSessionPrewarmShape, so the warm process is not left until its TTL. - Test in the "session prewarm" describe block (ProviderCommandReactor.test.ts:7576): prewarm, then dispatch a turn start with computerUse set. Assert two startSession calls, a stopSessionBinding on the prewarmed runtimeSessionId, and that the second start ran with the plan staged. B. Native mobile prewarm (S-M effort, low risk). - Extract the web gating policy (ChatView.tsx:5224-5255: no pending chat, dispatch allowed, no pending hosted target, session stopped or null, no worktree create or materialize, model, runtime and token mode) into a pure client-runtime helper next to requestProviderSessionPrewarm, e.g. `resolveProviderSessionPrewarmRequest(...)` in packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/sessionPrewarm.ts. Have ChatView use it. - Call it from the mobile thread composer on editor focus and on the first non-empty change (apps/mobile/src/native/ComposerEditor.* as wired by the thread detail screen), gated on server config capabilities.providerSessionPrewarm. - Unit-test the helper in sessionPrewarm.test.ts and add a mobile screen test asserting one RPC per focus. C. Browse churn (S effort). - Keep the first-keystroke trigger immediate, but delay the focus-triggered prewarm until the composer has held focus on the same thread for about 500-800 ms. Cancel on thread change or blur. - Extend apps/web/src/components/ChatView.Prewarm.browser.tsx: rapid thread switching sends no RPC; dwelling sends exactly one. D. Worktree-mode first turns (L effort). - Either create the worktree speculatively at draft time, or prewarm only providers whose cwd can be rebound before the first turn. - This is a product decision and is not recommended now.

Value medium · effort M · risk low

Done#142 ProviderService.listSessions scans every historical binding (1 + N queries) and runs ≥6 times per turn start

gap-first-turn-latency:listsessions-n-plus-one · original impact Medium, effort S · Database

Current state

Confirmed DONE (60633eff3, #710; also in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3). listSessions no longer calls listThreadIds plus getBinding per persisted row. It reads bindings only for the distinct threadIds that adapters report live. The new getSessionForThread does one getBinding and lists one adapter's in-memory sessions. Every per-turn and per-completion caller named in the finding goes through findThreadSession: PCR x3, ingestion turn.started and the ready reconcile, CheckpointReactor resolveSessionRuntimeForThread and revert relocation, and the newer ProviderSessionPrewarm. resolveCheckpointCwd skips the lookup when preferSessionRuntime is false and the thread workspace resolves. The old listSessions call sites at f1be4abc7 match the current ones one for one, and no new per-turn listSessions or full-binding scan was added since. The semantics hold or improve: the same reportedSession override logic is applied. A broken binding on another thread can no longer fail a single-thread lookup. Only the bound instance is consulted, where the old code could relabel a same-thread session from another instance. A test asserts that only the live thread's binding is read when 20 stopped history rows exist. The optional pruning was not done, but no per-turn cost remains that grows with history.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:2268-2295 listSessions now reads adapter sessions first, then readBindingOrUndefined for each distinct live threadId: k reads, no listThreadIds. At f1be4abc7:2160-2228 it ran listThreadIds plus getBinding per row with unbounded concurrency.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:2297-2323 getSessionForThread: one getBinding, then the bound instance's adapter.listSessions (in-memory Effect.sync in the Claude, Cursor, ACP and OpenCode adapters). It filters through the shared reportedSession (2239-2266). An instance-less legacy binding falls back to listSessions, which is now O(live).
  • apps/server/src/provider/threadSessionLookup.ts:16-25 findThreadSession prefers getSessionForThread and falls back to listSessions only for test doubles. The production layer exports getSessionForThread (ProviderService.ts:2572), and no production wrapper rebuilds the shape without it.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:792 Turn-start lookup (old 723-728) uses findThreadSession. Also :1339 (old 1226-1230) and :2489 (goal resume, old 2208).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:2100-2105 getExpectedProviderTurnIdForThread uses findThreadSession. It is used on turn.started (:2538 to :2114) and on the session ready reconcile (:2434).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/CheckpointReactor.ts:356-363 resolveSessionRuntimeForThread uses findThreadSession. resolveCheckpointCwd at 435-447 only looks up the session when preferSessionRuntime is true or the thread workspace does not resolve, so the proposal's last bullet is in. Revert relocation at :492 also uses it.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/CheckpointReactor.ts:875 The only remaining reactor listSessions call is the checkpoint restore neighbours. It is off the per-turn path and now O(live sessions).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.test.ts:3852-3916 Test with 20 stopped history bindings and one live thread. It asserts that listSessions and getSessionForThread each read only the live thread's binding, return the same session, and return none for a stopped history thread.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderSessionReaper.ts:55 Remaining full-table reads are background only: the reaper's single listBindings SELECT every 2 min (DEFAULT_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS, :14), plus the user-action paths in WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:1083, managedWorktreeMigration.ts:141 and StorageService. Each is one query, not N+1, and none is per turn.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:2460-2506 Out of scope and pre-existing (f1be4abc7:2362): on shutdown, runStopAll upserts every historical binding (~701 x getByThreadId+upsert). Each upsert resets lastSeenAt to now (ProviderSessionDirectory.ts:142), which would defeat any age-based pruning. listThreadIds is read only for the analytics sessionCount (:2505), which counts history rather than live sessions.
Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defects. Two trivial nits. (1) The module doc in apps/server/src/provider/threadSessionLookup.ts:4-6 still says listSessions 'reads every adapter and every persisted binding'. That stopped being true in the same commit. (2) getSessionForThread sits next to the pre-existing getSession (ProviderService.ts:1231-1242, via findExactAdapterSession at :910). That is a near-duplicate targeted lookup that differs only in applying the binding overrides and in the error channel, a small maintainability smell and not a perf issue.
