Partial#143 ~230-token ASSISTANT_ATTACHMENT_INSTRUCTIONS is prepended to every user message

gap-first-turn-latency:attachment-instructions-per-turn · original impact Medium, effort S · Other WP01

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

The per-turn cost is gone. Since #710 (60633eff3), ProviderService.sendTurn no longer prefixes ~230 tokens to every message. Claude /compact and other slash commands now reach the provider verbatim, Codex carries the text in collaboration-mode developer_instructions, and first-turn adapters get it once per runtime session. The Claude replacement channel does not work, though. ClaudeAdapter passes the text as a top-level `appendSystemPrompt` query option, cast past the type. The pinned Claude Agent SDK (0.3.296, also 0.3.263) ignores that option and reads only `systemPrompt: {type:'preset', preset:'claude_code', append}`. The result is that real Claude sessions now get no attachment-delivery instructions at all, where before they got them on every turn. The same dropped field also carries the project custom system prompt and token-reduction instructions, which were already silently lost before #710. The unit test passes only because it checks the mocked createQuery input instead of what the SDK uses.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:1747-1760 The per-turn prefix is removed. It applies only when capability !== 'session', the input is not a slash command, and the tracker needs it. markDelivered runs after submitTurn. The per-turn cost removal is really done.
  • apps/server/src/provider/attachmentInstructionDelivery.ts:17-58 isSlashCommandInput, withAttachmentInstructions and a bounded per-thread tracker keyed by runtimeSessionId. runtimeSessionId is always set, because ProviderService generates it at start and requires adapters to echo it back (ProviderService.ts:1392-1394, 1533-1538).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:5572-5579 appendSystemPrompt = [ASSISTANT_ATTACHMENT_INSTRUCTIONS, tokenReductionInstructions, customSystemPrompt].join.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:5612-5613 DEFECT: the options pass `systemPrompt: { type: "preset", preset: "claude_code" }` with no `append`. The text goes in as a top-level `appendSystemPrompt`, forced in with `as Partial<ClaudeQueryOptions>` because Options has no such field.
  • node_modules/.bun/@anthropic-ai+claude-agent-sdk@0.3.296+0d0f8d729a8f3b25/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs (query option builder yT) The builder destructures `{systemPrompt:s,settings:i,managedSettings:a,settingSources:l,sandbox:c,...d}` and sets `f` only from `s.type==="preset" -> f=s.append`. The initialize config uses `appendSystemPrompt:f`. Nothing reads `d.appendSystemPrompt`. The only other `.appendSystemPrompt` read is in claimSession (ClaimOptions), which Ryco does not use (no prewarm/claim calls). 0.3.263 behaves the same.
  • node_modules/.bun/@anthropic-ai+claude-agent-sdk@0.3.296+0d0f8d729a8f3b25/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:2422-2433 Options.systemPrompt preset is `{ type: 'preset'; preset: 'claude_code'; append?: string; ... }`. The `appendSystemPrompt?: string` entries at :364 and :4534 belong to ClaimOptions and the internal initialize request, not to query Options.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.test.ts:619-639 The test asserts `options.appendSystemPrompt` on the mocked createQuery input. That top-level field is the one the real SDK drops, so the test passes while the feature does not work.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:6660-6661 Claude declares attachmentInstructions: 'session', so ProviderService never adds the first-turn fallback either. Claude ends up with no attachment instructions unless the Agent Control ryco_attach_file tool description happens to be installed (AgentControlMcpServer.ts:136; Agent Control is optional, ClaudeDriver.ts:162).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexSessionRuntime.ts:513-555 Codex works. The attachment text is appended to collaborationMode.settings.developer_instructions on every turn/start (line 2320). Codex adds a developer message only when the collaboration mode changes. The per-turn prompt fallback (lines 597-603) needs interactionMode === undefined, which the orchestration paths never produce: the reactor uses event.payload.interactionMode with a decoding default, and the handoff uses thread.interactionMode.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:2397-2399 The tracker is forgotten on rollback. Nothing forgets it after provider-side compaction ('compacted' thread state, packages/contracts/src/providerRuntime.ts:74), so first-turn adapters can lose the instructions in long threads that auto-compact.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CopilotAdapter.ts:279-292 Copilot has an unused session-level systemMessage append channel. OpenCode promptAsync also accepts `system?: string` (@opencode-ai/sdk v2 types.gen.d.ts:8676) and does not use it. Both stay on the first-turn fallback.
  • apps/server/src/assistantAttachments.ts:27 The fence is parsed provider-agnostically in ProviderRuntimeIngestion. Every adapter supports the fence, so the proposal's 'gate on fence support' part is moot.
Remaining

Claude: ClaudeAdapter.ts:5612-5613 sends the composed instructions as a top-level `appendSystemPrompt`. The Claude Agent SDK 0.3.296 drops that option; it honours only `systemPrompt.append`. Since #710, real Claude sessions therefore get no attachment-delivery instructions. The project customSystemPrompt and token-reduction instructions joined into the same string are also never applied (a pre-existing bug since 6fceb686c and ba08d1f55). ClaudeAdapter.test.ts:619-639 asserts the wrong field and hides this. Minor: first-turn adapters (Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok, ACP) can lose the one-time instructions after provider-side auto-compaction, because the tracker is only forgotten on rollback (ProviderService.ts:2399). Copilot (systemMessage append) and OpenCode (promptAsync `system`) have session/system channels that would avoid this.

Defects in the shipped fix

(1) Main defect: the Claude 'session' channel is a no-op. ClaudeAdapter.ts:5612-5613 passes `{ appendSystemPrompt }` through a type cast, and the SDK reads only `systemPrompt: {type:'preset', preset:'claude_code', append}`. Because Claude declares attachmentInstructions:'session' (ClaudeAdapter.ts:6661), ProviderService also skips the fallback. Claude went from per-turn instructions to none. Fenced ryco-attachments delivery works for Claude only if the model guesses it, or partly through the ryco_attach_file tool description when Agent Control is enabled. The ClaudeAdapter test checks the mock input field the real SDK ignores. (2) Minor: the first-turn tracker is never reset on provider compaction, so long Copilot/OpenCode/Cursor threads can lose the instructions once the provider summarizes the first message. (3) Minor and outside this finding: OpenCodeAdapter.ts:2516-2519 prefixes <ryco_host_context> on the first turn even for slash-command input. This is the same pattern the fix avoided in ClaudeAdapter.

Implementation sketch

1) ClaudeAdapter.ts around 5608-5613: build `systemPrompt: appendSystemPrompt ? { type: "preset", preset: "claude_code", append: appendSystemPrompt } : { type: "preset", preset: "claude_code" }` and delete the `({ appendSystemPrompt } as Partial<ClaudeQueryOptions>)` spread. Without the cast, tsgo will reject any future top-level misuse. Update the comment at 6660 and the module doc in attachmentInstructionDelivery.ts:6 to say `systemPrompt.append`. 2) ClaudeAdapter.test.ts:619-639: assert `(options.systemPrompt as { append?: string }).append` includes ASSISTANT_ATTACHMENT_INSTRUCTIONS and that `'appendSystemPrompt' in options` is false. Add cases showing that a project customSystemPrompt and token-mode instructions also land in `systemPrompt.append`. Run only `bun run test` focused on apps/server ClaudeAdapter.test.ts and ProviderService.test.ts, plus the server typecheck. 3) Be aware of the SDK's default system-prompt snapshot: sessions created since #710 may keep their recorded prompt (without the append) on resume until the next compaction. Either accept that, or set `systemPrompt.snapshot`/`systemPromptSnapshot` deliberately; do not prefix again. 4) Optional hardening: give Copilot the attachment text in its systemMessage.content and declare attachmentInstructions:'session'. Do the same for OpenCode by passing `system: ASSISTANT_ATTACHMENT_INSTRUCTIONS` in session.promptAsync, after checking that OpenCode does not store `system` as conversation text. Add adapter tests. For the remaining ACP adapters, call attachmentInstructionTracker.forget(threadId) in ProviderService when a thread.state.changed 'compacted' runtime event arrives, with a ProviderService.test.ts case.

Done#144 sendTurn does not wait for the pre-turn baseline (correctness), and the CheckpointReactor is one global serial queue

gap-first-turn-latency:checkpoint-baseline-race · original impact Medium, effort M · Reliability WP02

Current state

DONE is correct. Commit 60633eff3 implements the core of the proposal. The turn start forks a baseline wait before session preparation, so the wait overlaps the session start. It joins that wait, bounded at 5 s, before markDispatched and sendTurn. The CheckpointReactor now runs one keyed-serial lane per thread, and the turn-start baseline is a queued lane item, so it also waits for the previous turn's queued completion capture. That closes the follow-up-send variant the earlier verifier raised. sendTurn has only two callers: the turn-start path and the context-handoff path, and both join the baseline first. Layer wiring provides CheckpointReactor to the ProviderCommandReactor (PCR). The auditor missed two problems in the fix. (1) The Stop check (laneControl.failIfCancelled) runs before the new baseline join and nothing re-checks afterwards. A user Stop that arrives during the join (0-5 s, and usually the whole capture on a prewarmed or warm session) therefore no longer cancels the start. The turn is still sent, and the queued interrupt reaches the provider before the turn exists, so the Stop is lost. (2) On timeout the fix records a 'checkpoint.baseline.unconfirmed' activity with turnId null. The client work log hides turnId-null activities once a latest turn exists, and the turn's checkpoint status is never set to 'missing', so the timeout is effectively silent in the UI. Two minor uncovered paths remain. If the thread's recorded worktree is missing, the forked baseline sees a non-git cwd and reports success without capturing, before ensureSessionForThread recreates the worktree. The setup script also still writes into the worktree alongside the first-turn baseline, but the proposal did not cover that.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:2073 The baseline fork (`forkScoped(awaitPreTurnBaseline(threadId))`) starts before buildSendTurnRequestForThread (2086). That function reaches ensureSessionForThread (758), so the capture overlaps the session start as proposed.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:2158 DEFECT: `laneControl.failIfCancelled(turnFence)` runs at 2158, BEFORE `joinPreTurnBaseline` at 2159. Nothing re-checks cancellation before `retain`, `markDispatched` (2189) and the forked `providerService.sendTurn` (2166). Before 60633eff3 the check sat immediately before the send. `git show 60633eff3` shows the join was inserted after it.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/threadLaneControl.ts:314 Only `guardStart` registers a `currentStart` cancel Deferred (322). PCR uses guardStart only for session starts (896, 1121) and the handoff path (1852), so the baseline join is not cancellable by a noted Stop.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:2364 The interrupt lane item runs after the turn-start item has forked the send. cancelledAStart is false, so it calls providerService.interruptTurn (2433). That can run before the forked markDispatched and sendTurn reach the adapter. For example, ClaudeAdapter.ts:6194 has no turnState yet and just calls query.interrupt(). The turn then runs despite the Stop.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:1944 awaitPreTurnBaseline wraps `ensurePreTurnBaseline` in `timeoutOption(preTurnBaselineWait)`. The default is 5 s (252).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:1979 The timeout activity `checkpoint.baseline.unconfirmed` is appended with turnId null. No checkpoint status is set to 'missing'.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/session/session-logic.ts:940 shouldIncludeActivityInWorkLog drops activities whose turnId is not the latest turn, so the turnId-null unconfirmed notice is hidden once the turn starts. No UI code references this activity kind.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/CheckpointReactor.ts:1618 makeKeyedSerialWorker keyed by inputThreadId (100) replaces the global drainable worker. Capacity is global (1024) but lanes do not block each other (packages/shared/src/KeyedSerialWorker.ts).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/CheckpointReactor.ts:1627 ensurePreTurnBaselineForTurnStart always enqueues a `baseline` item and awaits its Deferred. processInputSafely (1596-1613) always completes the Deferred, so the wait is ordered behind the thread's queued completion capture.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/CheckpointReactor.ts:759 ensurePreTurnBaseline checks the knownCheckpointRefs memo, then hasCheckpointRef, then captureCheckpoint. If the thread's cwd is not a git repo yet (462), it returns as if it had succeeded. That happens when a missing recorded worktree is only recreated later in ensureSessionForThread (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:786).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:2594 streamEvents creates a fresh PubSub subscription per consumer. The reactor's runtime consumer (CheckpointReactor.ts:1657) only filters and enqueues, so in practice turn.completed is in the lane before a follow-up send can pass ingestion, the projection, PCR and a client round trip.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:331 CheckpointReactorLive is provideMerge'd below ProviderCommandReactorLive, so PCR's serviceOption(CheckpointReactor) (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:449) resolves to Some.
Defects in the shipped fix

1. Stop regression (verified by reading the code). In prepareAndSubmitTurnStart, `laneControl.failIfCancelled(turnFence)` (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:2158) runs before `joinPreTurnBaseline(baseline, event)` (2159), and nothing re-checks before markDispatched (2189) and sendTurn (2166). A user Stop (session stop or turnId-less interrupt) noted during the join therefore does not cancel the start. The join can take up to 5 s. On a prewarmed first turn or a quick follow-up it is the whole capture, roughly 0.1-1.7 s. The interrupt's lane item then runs before the forked send reaches the provider, interrupts nothing (no turnState yet), and the turn runs anyway. Before the fix this window was essentially zero. 2. The timeout is not visibly recorded. The `checkpoint.baseline.unconfirmed` activity has turnId null (1979), and the client work log filters it out once a latest turn exists (session-logic.ts:940). Nothing marks the turn's checkpoint as 'missing'. The proposal's 'record checkpoint status missing' is therefore only a server log plus a hidden activity. 3. Missing-worktree path (minor). The baseline is forked before ensureSessionForThread recreates a missing recorded worktree (786). resolveCheckpointCwd then sees a non-git cwd (CheckpointReactor.ts:462), and the join reports success without a capture. On that thread's first turn the baseline still races the agent through the runtime turn.started fallback. Out of scope, noted for completeness: the setup script runs alongside the first baseline (ws/context.ts:1016). Separately, a pre-existing and unrelated Codex issue: turn.diff.updated fires mid-turn, and ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:3119 creates a placeholder for it that CheckpointReactor.captureCheckpointFromPlaceholder (CheckpointReactor.ts:705) captures at once. The turn.completed capture is then skipped because a real checkpoint exists, so a Codex turn's ref N can be a mid-turn snapshot. This needs its own finding.

Implementation sketch

1. Stop fix, in apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts prepareAndSubmitTurnStart. Make the join cancellable by wrapping it: `yield* laneControl.guardStart(turnFence, joinPreTurnBaseline(baseline, event))`. Interrupting a Fiber.join does not interrupt the baseline fiber, and the queued lane item still completes. The minimal alternative is to call `laneControl.failIfCancelled(turnFence)` again right after the join. Either way the cancellation surfaces as ProviderSessionStartCancelledError, and processTurnStartRequested -> reportTurnStartFailure -> settleCancelledTurnStart handles it. Skip appending the unconfirmed activity when the start was cancelled. Test in ProviderCommandReactor.test.ts, cloned from 'holds the provider turn until the pre-turn checkpoint baseline lands': hold the baseline, wait for startSession, dispatch a user thread.session.stop or a turnId-less thread.turn.interrupt, release the baseline. Assert sendTurn is never called, markDispatched is not recorded, no provider.turn.start.failed activity exists, and the session is settled as after a cancelled start. 2. Visible timeout (optional, low value). After sendTurn returns the turnId, attach the notice to that turn: dispatch the activity with the turn's id, or have CheckpointReactor mark the turn's checkpoint payload with a `baselineUnconfirmed` flag that the diff panel can show. Test that the activity survives deriveWorkLogEntries with the new latest turn. 3. Missing worktree (optional). Have CheckpointReactorShape.ensurePreTurnBaseline return a status ('ensured' | 'no-git-cwd'). When PCR gets 'no-git-cwd' and buildSendTurnRequestForThread then recreated the worktree, run awaitPreTurnBaseline again after preparation and before the join. Add a PCR test with a missing recorded worktree. Setup-script gating and the Codex mid-turn placeholder capture belong in separate findings.

Done#145 CheckpointReactor loads the full thread detail 3x per turn start (plus a fully redundant turn.started path) and enqueues streaming deltas into its global queue

gap-first-turn-latency:checkpointreactor-redundant-detail-loads · original impact Medium, effort M · CPU WP02

Current state

Confirmed DONE. All four parts landed in 60633eff3 (#710). (1) Baseline, completion and placeholder paths read getThreadCheckpointContext, a thread-and-project join plus checkpoint rows, instead of getThreadDetailById. Messages, activities and plans are no longer decoded. (2) The runtime turn.started handler is kept but goes through ensurePreTurnBaseline, which skips git through a per-thread known-ref memo. Only the first trigger of a turn start can reach the VCS detect and rev-parse, and only on a memo miss. (3) start() drops assistant, streaming, turn-bound and inherited thread.message-sent events before enqueue. (4) The worker is a KeyedSerialWorker with one lane per thread. The rare revert path is now the only CheckpointReactor caller of full thread detail. There are 4 triggers per turn start, not 3: message-sent, turn-start-requested, the baseline that ProviderCommandReactor awaits, and runtime turn.started. Triggers 2 to 4 cost two indexed SQLite reads plus an existsSync. One small residual, not worth reopening: getThreadCheckpointContext decodes every checkpoint's checkpoint_files_json, and no caller reads it. That costs about 9 ms per call on the user's largest checkpoint and is negligible for typical threads.

  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/CheckpointReactor.ts:759-797 ensurePreTurnBaseline uses the narrow context and checks the knownCheckpointRefs memo before checkpointStore.hasCheckpointRef, which runs vcsRegistry.resolve (the 'detect') plus rev-parse. The memo is filled at 796 and also at 536 after a completion capture, so turn N's capture covers turn N+1's baseline. It is cleared on revert at 1010.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/CheckpointReactor.ts:432-466 When the thread's own workspace resolves and preferSessionRuntime is false, no session lookup runs. The git check is isGitRepository, an existsSync of .git (apps/server/src/git/Utils.ts:4).

Defects in the shipped fix

No real defects. Minor residuals: (1) getThreadCheckpointContext (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:1808-1827, 3433-3441) decodes the full checkpoint_files_json of every checkpoint row, but no caller reads .files. Callers checked: CheckpointReactor, CheckpointDiffQuery.ts:71, ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:1855 and :3123 (on every Codex turn.diff.updated), attachmentTools.ts:95, htmlRenderTools.ts:364, computerBetaTools.ts:178. A read-only query of the user's DB found one checkpoint with 23,376 files (3.6 MB JSON) and 7 rows over 100 KB. A warm Schema decode of that row takes about 9 ms (JSON.parse alone about 3 ms). It runs synchronously 4 times per turn start, plus completion and Codex diff updates, so about 40-60 ms of event-loop time per turn start on that one thread. Typical threads stay under 1 ms. (2) Memo trust: knownCheckpointRefs assumes a remembered ref still exists. If refs are removed outside Ryco (repo re-initialised at the same path, or a manual update-ref -d), the next baseline is skipped. (3) captureAndDispatchCheckpoint still runs hasCheckpointRef(fromRef) (VCS resolve plus rev-parse) on every completion, even when the memo already holds that ref. Partial#146 Worktree-mode first send: full-remote fetch, worktree add, client RPCs and dispatches run serially before the turn exists

gap-first-turn-latency:worktree-first-send-serial-chain · original impact Medium, effort M · Waterfall decision

Current state

PARTIAL is right. Fixed: base-only fetch, origin/HEAD resolved locally, a node-side prefetch when worktree mode is entered, no client RPCs on the common non-hosted path, one dispatch removed (thread.create carries branch and path), the rename moved to idle, and the storage lock made read-write. Still open, as the auditor said: hosted sends await getConfig, 4 serial bootstrap dispatches, no provider warm-up for worktree sends, and the branch name is not generated in parallel. The auditor missed three things. (a) The prefetch runs once, when the hero mounts or the mode is entered, and is reused for only 60 s after it settles. Nothing refreshes it, so anyone who takes longer than about a minute to write the first prompt gets the base fetch back on the critical path. (b) With a setup script, the PTY open (exclusive storage admission, history read, spawn), the terminal write and 2 sequential activity dispatches still run inline before turn.start. Other worktree paths already launch setup in the background. (c) The idle-deferred rename has no 'already pushed' guard and now runs after the whole first turn, so it can rename a branch the agent already pushed or opened a PR from.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2261-2267 fetchOriginBranch fetches only +refs/heads/<base>. The all-heads fetchOrigin (2247) remains only for listRefs (2609-2610). Its doc comment still says 'Always fetches (creation must see origin as it is now)', which contradicts the 60 s prefetch reuse (2258).
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2318-2334 fetchOriginDefaultBranch uses the locally recorded refs/remotes/origin/HEAD and calls ls-remote --symref only when nothing is recorded or the fetch fails.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:936, 2349-2359, 2724-2745 WORKTREE_BASE_PREFETCH_REUSE_MS = 60_000. createWorktree joins an in-flight prefetch or reuses one settled within 60 s. Otherwise it runs fetchWorktreeBase serially inside the send.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/NewThreadWorkLocation.tsx:155-162 MISSED BY AUDITOR: prefetchWorktreeSend is called from one useEffect keyed on [canEdit, cwd, environmentId, prefetchRefName, projectId]. It fires once on hero mount or mode entry and never again while the user types. Combined with the 60 s server reuse, a prompt written over more than ~60 s gets no prefetch benefit.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:5258; apps/web/src/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx:1579, 2756 onComposerIntent fires on focus and first keystroke but only drives the provider-session prewarm, which returns early for worktree plans (ChatView.tsx:5243). It never refreshes the base prefetch.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/executeChatSendTurn.ts:598-640 Non-hosted sends with a cached config and remembered preferences make no RPC before dispatch. runSetupScript is left undefined for nodes with preferences.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/executeChatSendTurn.ts:617-621 REMAINING: hosted mode always awaits api.server.getConfig() (one relay round trip) before dispatch. The result is used only for capabilities.projectPreferences, a compatibility check that decides whether runSetupScript is sent as undefined or true.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:870-893, 972-1011, 1052-1054 REMAINING: thread.create + drainThrough, worktree.create, thread.attach-to-worktree, then turn.start. That is 4 serial dispatches (thread.meta.update is gone).
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:721-760, 768-830, 1016 MISSED BY AUDITOR: runSetupProgram() runs inline before turn.start. runForThread does a project read, terminalManager.open (flushPersist, readHistory, exclusive storageLifecycleLock admission via admitPtyStart, PTY spawn) and terminalManager.write. recordSetupScriptStarted then runs Effect.all of 2 thread.activity.append dispatches, which is sequential by default. Only the output watcher is detached (worktreeSetupProgress.ts forkDetach).
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/managedCheckout.ts:294-330; apps/server/src/ws/context/worktreeOperations.ts:711; apps/server/src/threadFork/Layers/ThreadFork.ts:1925 Precedent: other worktree paths already launch setup detached through launchSetupScriptForWorktreeInBackground. Only the first-send bootstrap still runs it inline.
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:2156-2225, 1503-1510 Terminal open still waits for exclusive admission, which must drain every in-flight shared holder (orchestration commands, path leases) before spawning. That wait sits on the worktree first-send critical path when a setup script exists.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:5212-5243; apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderSessionPrewarm.ts:59-66 No provider prewarm for worktree sends. The server prewarm needs an existing directory. Codex sessions spawn a per-session runtime (CodexAdapter.ts:2049), so nothing shared is warm either.
Remaining

1) The prefetch expires. It fires once (NewThreadWorkLocation.tsx:159-162) and is reused for only 60 s after it settles (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:936, 2726-2736), so a first prompt written over more than ~60 s pays a full base-only fetch (~0.3-0.5 s on the network) inside the send. 2) Hosted sends still await a serial getConfig before dispatch (executeChatSendTurn.ts:617-621). 3) The setup script runs inline before turn.start when the project has one (ws/context.ts:1016 -> 768-830): exclusive storage admission, history read, PTY spawn, terminal write and 2 sequential activity dispatches. 4) 4 serial orchestration dispatches plus drainThrough remain (ws/context.ts:870-893, 991-1011, 1052-1054). This is cheap (ms each) but still serial. 5) No provider warm-up overlaps fetch and worktree add (ChatView.tsx:5243; ProviderSessionPrewarm.ts:59-66). 6) The branch name is not generated in parallel. This is a deliberate design choice (PCR.ts:1528-1541), and the remaining cost is mostly cosmetic now that the rename is idle-deferred.

Defects in the shipped fix

1) Idle-deferred rename has no 'already published' guard (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:1465-1511, GitVcsDriverCore.ts:3137-3155). Because the rename now runs after the whole first turn rather than seconds into it, a temp branch the agent pushed or opened a PR from gets renamed locally. Upstream stays origin/<temp>, the thread shows a name that differs from the remote and PR head, and a plain git push from the agent fails under push.default=simple. 2) The prefetch is effectively a one-shot with a 60 s life, so it does not cover slower composers (see remaining 1). 3) The fetchOriginBranch doc comment (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2258) still claims creation always fetches, which contradicts the reuse window. 4) Minor: the auditor's caveat names mobile as a surface missing the prefetch, but mobile never makes worktree first sends.

Implementation sketch

A) Keep the prefetch warm (biggest remaining win, small change). In apps/web/src/components/chat/NewThreadWorkLocation.tsx, while prefetchRefName && canEdit, also call prefetchWorktreeSend on composer intent. One way: export a small 'refreshWorktreeSendPrefetch' that ChatView's onComposerIntent calls when the plan is a worktree plan, instead of returning at ChatView.tsx:5243 with nothing. Another way: a setInterval of about 45 s while the draft is in newWorktree mode and the window is focused. The client throttle (30 s) and the server's reuse-or-start logic in prefetchWorktreeBase already dedupe, so this costs at most one base-only fetch per minute per open worktree draft. Alternatively, call prefetchWorktreeSend at the very top of executeChatSendTurn (before attachment encoding and scroll) so the fetch overlaps client-side preparation. Tests: extend worktreeSendPrefetch tests for the refresh; add a GitVcsDriverCore test that a prefetch settled 61 s ago is not reused but a refreshed one is. B) Move the setup script off the critical path. In apps/server/src/ws/context.ts dispatchBootstrapTurnStart, keep the requireWorktree liveThread check, then dispatch turn.start first. Run runSetupProgram forked (Effect.forkDetach), or reuse launchSetupScriptForWorktreeInBackground plus the setupProgress stage hooks, so the setup PTY admission, spawn and activity dispatches overlap the provider session start. At minimum, run the two recordSetupScriptStarted dispatches with { concurrency: 'unbounded' } or fold them into one dispatch. Update the setup-progress tests in ws/context and WorktreeSetupTracker to cover the new order (agent stage running while the setup-script stage is still starting). C) Hosted getConfig. Either derive capabilities.projectPreferences from the config the hosted lifecycle owner already accepted for the current relay generation (readEnvironmentServerConfig, made generation-safe), or start the getConfig read at worktree-mode entry inside prefetchWorktreeSend and reuse the promise if the connection generation is unchanged. Test in executeChatSendTurn tests with isHostedHubMode mocked. D) Fold the bootstrap dispatches. Add a server-only decider command (for example thread.bootstrap-worktree) that emits thread.created (with branch, path and worktreeId), worktree.created and thread.attached in one transaction, then drainThrough on its sequence. This removes 2 dispatches. Cover it in OrchestrationEngine decider tests and the projection tests. E) Rename guard. In renameWorktreeBranchWhenIdle, before gitWorkflow.renameBranch, skip the rename (keep the temp name and log it) when the old branch has an upstream (git rev-parse --abbrev-ref <old>@{upstream}) or refs/remotes/origin/<old> exists. Reuse or extract GitManager's probeBranchPublished. Add a PCR test where the branch is published and renameBranch is not called. Fix the fetchOriginBranch doc comment. F) Optional, Codex only: a cwd-less warm-up of the codex app-server binary (spawn + initialize) at send time, adopted by startSession after the worktree exists. This needs adapter work in CodexAdapter/CodexSessionRuntime and is not possible for Claude, whose CLI is spawned with its cwd.

Needs a decision

Several of these are behaviour trade-offs. Keeping the prefetch warm adds periodic background git fetches. Starting turn.start before the setup script has spawned changes the order the user sees (agent before setup). Skipping the rename for published branches leaves temp names on pushed branches. The hosted getConfig removal touches config freshness per relay generation, which falls under the AGENTS.md rule that hosted lifecycle recovery has one owner and that stale generations must not publish state.

Value medium · effort M · risk medium

Done#148 Turn-start lane repeats thread/project reads, takes the node-wide storage lock 2-3 times, and runs a provider goal RPC every turn

gap-first-turn-latency:turnstart-redundant-reads-and-global-lock · original impact Low, effort S · Database decision

Current state

The perf finding is fixed. Per turn start, thread reads fell from 4 to 2 and project reads from 3-4 to 1. Path leases fell from 3 (each a realpath plus about 6 SQL queries) to 1, plus a retain with no I/O in startSession. The goal RPC now runs once per runtime instead of every turn. storageLifecycleLock is a fair read/write lock: leases and command processing take it shared, and terminals take it exclusively only for a short admission section. One defect in the fix: the retained lease skips the project-relocation fence re-check that startSession used to do, so in a narrow race a session start can be admitted into a chat folder being promoted. Small leftovers: the reconcileThreadGoal re-read, a double lease on the context-handoff path, sqlite_master probes on every lease, and WorkspaceFileSystem writes holding the exclusive lock for the whole write.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:2005 prepareAndSubmitTurnStart reads the thread once (:2005) and the project once (:2085), then passes both to buildSendTurnRequestForThread, which passes them to ensureSessionForThread as prefetched (:1318-1324).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:776 ensureSessionForThread uses prefetched.thread and prefetched.project (:776-783), takes one lease (:785) and calls ensureRecordedWorktreeAvailable with pathLeased: true (:786, skip at :622). It passes the held lease to startSession (:901).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:1139 reconcileThreadGoal still re-reads the thread shell, the second shell read per turn. It needs the runtimeSessionId that ensureSessionForThread may just have rebound. The goalless cache returns early at :1149-1152 and is filled at :1220-1226. Test: ProviderCommandReactor.test.ts:1112.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:1469 startSession retains heldPathLease when its path equals effectiveCwd (:1471-1472). The reactor's lease candidate (worktreePath ?? workspaceRoot) and resolveThreadWorkspaceCwd (checkpointing/Utils.ts:33) produce the same string, so the fast path really fires.
  • apps/server/src/storage/lifecycle.ts:165 retainStoragePathUseLease: when creations.get(canonical) > 0 it only increments the count. It does not call storagePathBlocker, so it never checks project_relocations (isProjectRelocationBlocked, :334-352).
  • apps/server/src/project/chatPromotion.ts:979 Chat promotion writes the 'pending' relocation fence under withPermit and never calls hasWorktreeCreationLease. Only checkoutFence.ts:49, managedWorktreeMigration.ts:105/411 and StorageService.ts:734 do. The comment at :976-978 says nothing new starts in the folder from this point. vacateChatFolder (:934-945) catches queued turns (busy 'queued-turn') and live sessions, but not an in-flight start on a thread without a session.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:2449 Exposed path: processGoalUpdated calls ensureSessionForThread(kind 'restart'), which starts a new session on an idle thread with no session. Between the reactor lease (:785) and the retain, it can wait seconds: the prewarm claim awaits an in-flight prewarm start (ProviderSessionPrewarm.ts:315-330), and startSession waits on its per-thread lock. A fence written in that window is no longer re-checked.
  • apps/server/src/storage/lifecycle.test.ts:175 This test, and ProviderService.test.ts:2645, assert that a lease-holding start is admitted after a 'pending' project relocation was journaled. The behaviour is deliberate and covered by tests.
  • apps/server/src/storage/readWriteLock.ts:36 Fair FIFO read/write lock; interruption handling is correct. I found no nested shared acquisition under processEnvelope: OrchestrationEngine.ts:339, chatPromotion and managedWorktreeMigration call storagePathBlocker without the lock. A nested acquisition would deadlock only under contention.
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:1509 Terminal open, restart and guarded write hold the exclusive lock only for assertValidCwd plus commit. Spawn and history I/O run outside it.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:1843 The context-handoff turn path still takes two leases (ensureRecordedWorktreeAvailable without pathLeased at :1844, then leaseThreadPath at :1849). The coordinator's own startSession does a full acquire. Rare path.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceFileSystem.ts:656 writeFile and stageFileReference hold the exclusive lock for the whole write, so a large staged attachment delays every shared lease and command. This was not part of the proposal, and relaxing it has fence semantics of its own.
Defects in the shipped fix

1) Fence regression from the lease handoff (d97dac1d9). retainStoragePathUseLease (storage/lifecycle.ts:165-171) skips the admission check whenever the path has any counted use. Only cleanup and worktree-relocation claims consult those counts. Chat promotion's project_relocations fence (chatPromotion.ts:979-984) does not, and relies on every later start being refused at admission. A provider start whose reactor lease (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:785) was admitted before the fence is therefore admitted into the moving folder. Concrete case: processGoalUpdated on an idle chat thread with no session (:2449), with promotion fencing while the start waits on the prewarm claim or startSession's per-thread lock. The old code refused it with PROJECT_RELOCATION_PENDING_MESSAGE. busyThreads does not see such a start, and stopChatSessions only sees it if the adapter has already registered it. The window is narrow, but the result is a provider session spawned in a folder being renamed or copied. 2) Minor and contrived: goallessRuntimes (:467-475) is never invalidated when goal state changes. If a native goal notification is dropped while a client goal sync is pending (ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:2386-2387) and the goal later returns to null, later turns on that runtime skip the getThreadGoal that used to repair it. Cheap hardening: delete the threadId:runtimeSessionId entry whenever reconcileThreadGoal or ingestion dispatches a goal sync or clear.

Implementation sketch

Fence fix, preferred because it adds no I/O. In storage/lifecycle.ts add a module counter, fenceEpoch, and export noteStorageFenceRaised() to increment it. Capture the counter in HeldStoragePathUseLease (new field 'epoch') inside acquireStoragePathUseLeaseHandle's withShared section. retainStoragePathUseLease takes the fast path only when count > 0 && held.epoch === fenceEpoch; otherwise it does a full acquireStoragePathUseLease. Call noteStorageFenceRaised() inside every exclusive section that raises a fence: chatPromotion.ts:979 after relocations.create, checkoutFence.claim, managedWorktreeMigration's moving-state writes (:251/:405) and the StorageService claims (:728/:919). Simpler alternative: in retain, always run isProjectRelocationBlocked(sql, held.canonical). That is 2 SQL queries and no realpath; the other fence kinds already honour use counts. Tests: invert the relocation part of lifecycle.test.ts:175 and ProviderService.test.ts:2645 so that retaining after a 'pending' relocation is refused. Add a lifecycle test showing that retain still needs no lock and no SQL when no fence was raised, e.g. it completes while an exclusive holder is parked. Optional leftovers, all low value: (a) have ensureSessionForThread return the bound runtimeSessionId and pass it, with the prefetched thread's goal, into reconcileThreadGoal, which drops the :1139 re-read, or use a narrow goal-plus-session query. (b) Cache the sqlite_master existence probes in isWorktreeRelocationBlocked and isProjectRelocationBlocked (lifecycle.ts:309-311, :340-342) once they return true; this cuts the per-turn lease from about 6 to about 4 queries. (c) In runContextHandoffTurnStart (:1843-1860), take leaseThreadPath once in one scope, call ensureRecordedWorktreeAvailable with pathLeased: true, and thread heldPathLease through the coordinator's startSession. (d) Pass prefetched shells from processModeChange (:2931) and processGoalUpdated (:2445). Do not make the per-turn lease lazy: it is the turn-start admission gate that checkoutFence.ts:13-16 documents.

Needs a decision

The defect is in storage-admission and lifecycle fence semantics, and the current behaviour is deliberate: both lifecycle.test.ts:175 ('retains a held use lease without the admission check') and ProviderService.test.ts:2645 assert that a start holding a lease is admitted into a path with a pending project relocation. Restoring the refusal reverses a choice the author tested for, so the owner should confirm that 'nothing new starts in a moving chat folder' (chatPromotion.ts:976-978) is the invariant to keep. The fix itself costs nothing in performance.

Partial#149 Session-start hangs surface only after 120-300 s; Cursor's default binary name collides with another CLI

gap-first-turn-latency:phase-deadlines-and-hangs · original impact Low, effort M · Reliability WP01

First-pass audit said PARTIAL; the verifier corrected it. The auditor said Cursor binary identity is not verified and suggested adding a probe-time `--version`/`about` identity check. #710 already added one: isCursorAgentAboutOutput (CursorProvider.ts:740), used at :1055 and tested. With pickers limited to 'ready' instances, a foreign `agent` cannot be picked for new sessions. The auditor also missed the uncovered `agent update` maintenance caller (CursorDriver.ts:48), which runs the Grok binary on this machine. The auditor called the registry 300 s default 'effectively unreachable' but missed that the same 30 s registry cap also cuts off the new 60 s session/load budget and replaces the actionable phase messages with a generic one.

Current state

PARTIAL is right: #710 (60633eff3) added per-phase startup deadlines with actionable messages for ACP (Cursor, Grok, registry), Codex and Claude, plus a PATH-based cursor-agent preference. The auditor got the Cursor part wrong in two ways. First, #710 already verifies the binary's identity at probe time (isCursorAgentAboutOutput on `about` output), and model pickers only offer 'ready' instances, so a foreign `agent` is kept out of new sessions. Second, the auditor missed callers the fix does not cover: the Cursor maintenance update still runs a bare `agent update`, which on this machine resolves to ~/.grok/bin/agent first. Also missed: the registry ACP runtime's older 30 s whole-start cap hides the new phase budgets and messages. Still open: no client-visible phase reporting, 180 s text generation on commit/PR paths (tracked by the textgen finding), and Copilot start has no phase deadline.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/acp/AcpSessionRuntime.ts:41 DEFAULT_ACP_STARTUP_PHASE_TIMEOUTS: initialize 20 s, authenticate 20 s, session/new 30 s, session/load 60 s. withStartupPhaseDeadline (:485) wraps initialize (:520), authenticate (:560), session/new (:588) and session/load|resume (:621). Timed-out phases are not retried (:597, :633).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexSessionRuntime.ts:165 Codex phases: initialize 15 s, thread/start 30 s, thread/resume 60 s, applied at :2224/:2233. CodexAdapter.ts:2157 maps them to ProviderAdapterRequestError with the actionable detail. Covered by CodexStartupDeadline.integration.test.ts.

  • apps/server/src/provider/acp/AcpAdapterSupport.ts:39 mapAcpToAdapterError passes AcpTransportError.detail through, so the phase message reaches the user for Cursor/ACP/Grok session starts.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CursorProvider.ts:740 MISSED BY AUDITOR: isCursorAgentAboutOutput, added in #710, checks who answered `about` and is used at :1055 to mark a foreign `agent` as not installed/error ('did not identify as the Cursor Agent CLI'). Tested at CursorProvider.test.ts:441. packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/providerInstances.ts:161 offers only status==='ready' instances in pickers.
  • apps/server/src/provider/acp/CursorAgentCommand.ts:39 resolveCursorAgentCommand prefers cursor-agent when binaryPath is the default 'agent'. Used for sessions/textgen (CursorAcpSupport.ts:56) and probes (CursorProvider.ts:1001).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/CursorDriver.ts:48 UNCOVERED CALLER: the maintenance update is hardcoded as `agent update` and run as a bare command by providerMaintenanceRunner.ts:354. Locally `which -a agent` gives ~/.grok/bin/agent (-> grok-1.0.44 binary) before ~/.local/bin/agent, so 'Update Cursor' runs the Grok binary.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CursorProvider.ts:790 The lab-channel hint hardcodes `agent set-channel lab && agent update`. The :1033 not-installed message and cliSetup/machine.ts:23 (labels any `agent` on PATH as Cursor) also ignore the resolver.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CursorProvider.ts:745 isCursorAgentAboutOutput accepts 'unknown command'/'unexpected argument' output as an old Cursor build, so a foreign CLI that rejects `about` that way passes as Cursor (with only a warning status).
  • apps/server/src/provider/acp/AcpRegistrySupport.ts:66 Older code (17bcd353b): registry runtime.start() is capped at 30 s overall with the generic 'ACP agent startup timed out after 30 seconds.'. The new 60 s session/load budget can never apply to registry agents (strictResume). A session/new hang (30 s phase deadline, starting after initialize+auth) always surfaces with the generic text.
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerOperationPolicy.ts:26 DEFAULT_REGISTRY_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT_MS = 300 s with 'may download its agent on first run', but resolveAcpRegistryInstallation (AcpRegistrySupport.ts:9-23) only resolves an explicitly installed agent, so both the value and the comment are stale.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:1403 progress.phase (lock/admission/adapter) is still used only for the timeout text (:1598). Admission stays at 4 concurrent starts per instance (:135).
Remaining

1) Client-visible startup phase reporting is absent. Phase deadlines (AcpSessionRuntime.ts:485, CodexSessionRuntime.ts:205, ClaudeAdapter.ts:5925) emit nothing. ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:556 drops 'starting' reasons, and there is no contracts field to carry one. The user sees a plain working state for up to 15-30 s before the actionable error. 2) Cursor wrong-binary is fixed for session, probe and textgen spawns, and the probe already does an identity check, which the auditor said was missing. Still uncovered: the maintenance update `agent update` (CursorDriver.ts:48 -> providerMaintenanceRunner.ts:354), which runs ~/.grok/bin/agent on this machine; the hardcoded `agent` in user-facing hints (CursorProvider.ts:790, :1033); setup detection (cliSetup/machine.ts:23); and the permissive 'unknown command' identity heuristic (CursorProvider.ts:745). The schema default stays 'agent' (packages/contracts/src/settings.ts:323). With the resolver that is acceptable, so do not change it. 3) Text generation keeps 180 s full-length timeouts (CodexTextGeneration.ts:47, ClaudeTextGeneration.ts:58, CursorTextGeneration.ts:35, GrokTextGeneration.ts:41). This is deferred to the textgen finding, and lowering them needs a slow-model decision there. 4) Copilot start (CopilotAdapter.session.ts:272-302) has no phase deadline. That provider is outside the proposal's list but has the same failure mode. 5) Admission of 4 starts per instance (ProviderService.ts:135) is unchanged. It is now bounded by the phase deadlines, so this is low priority.

Defects in the shipped fix

(a) Uncovered caller of the Cursor collision fix: CursorDriver.ts:45-51 builds static maintenance capabilities with updateExecutable 'agent'. Update runs a bare `agent update` (providerMaintenanceRunner.ts:354) and bypasses resolveCursorAgentCommand. On this machine `which -a agent` resolves ~/.grok/bin/agent first, so Update Cursor executes the Grok binary. The hint at CursorProvider.ts:790 tells users to run `agent set-channel lab && agent update`, with the same problem. (b) Registry ACP: the older 30 s whole-start cap (AcpRegistrySupport.ts:66-78) masks the new phase deadlines. session/load|resume can never get its intended 60 s, and session/new or late authenticate hangs surface with the generic 'ACP agent startup timed out after 30 seconds.' instead of the actionable phase message. DEFAULT_REGISTRY_SESSION_START_TIMEOUT_MS = 300 s (providerOperationPolicy.ts:26) and its 'may download on first run' comment are stale. (c) Phase deadlines are fixed constants with no env knob, unlike RYCO_PROVIDER_*_TIMEOUT_MS, so very slow machines cannot raise them.

Implementation sketch

A) Cursor update/hints (S, do first). In CursorDriver.ts, replace the static MAINTENANCE_CAPABILITIES (:45) with an Effect that runs resolveCursorAgentCommand(effectiveConfig.binaryPath, processEnv, { fresh: true }) and builds makeProviderMaintenanceCapabilities with updateExecutable = resolved.resolvedPath ?? resolved.command. Keep lockKey 'cursor-agent'. Pass it at :130 and :143. Thread the resolved command into getCursorParameterizedModelPickerUnsupportedMessage (CursorProvider.ts:762-790) and the not-installed message (:1033). In cliSetup/machine.ts:23, detect Cursor by `cursor-agent`. Tests: a CursorDriver/maintenance test with a temp PATH holding fake `agent` and `cursor-agent` executables asserts the update executable is cursor-agent, plus a CursorProvider message test. B) Registry deadlines (S). In AcpRegistrySupport.ts:66-78, remove the outer 30 s timeout and rely on the per-phase deadlines, or raise it above the phase sum (about 90 s) and keep it only as a backstop. Set the registry session-start default to the standard 120 s and fix the comment at providerOperationPolicy.ts:25-26. Test: a fake registry agent answering session/load after 40 s succeeds, and a hung session/new yields the phase message. C) Phase reporting (M). Add an optional `onStartupPhase: (phase) => Effect<void>` to AcpSessionRuntimeOptions and CodexSessionRuntimeOptions, invoked inside withStartupPhaseDeadline / withCodexStartupPhaseDeadline before the request. Adapters (CursorAdapter, AcpAdapter, GrokAdapter, CodexAdapter) emit session.state.changed { state: 'starting', reason: 'Authenticating with Cursor…' | 'Opening session…' | 'Resuming session…' }. ClaudeAdapter emits 'Loading Claude Code (plugins, MCP servers)…' before awaitCliInitialized when not initialized. In packages/contracts, add an optional session `statusDetail` (schema-only). In ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts, set it on starting and clear it on ready/running/error/stopped in the session.state.changed lifecycle branch (around :2540-2600). Render it where client-runtime treats status 'starting' (threadWorkspaceViewModel.ts:470) in the working indicator. The Codex path already proves that pre-ready runtime events are ingested. Tests: an AcpSessionRuntime test for callback order initialize→authenticate→session/new, an ingestion projection/clear test and a view-model test. D) Optional: a Copilot start deadline (30 s create / 60 s resume) via providerStartupPhaseTimeoutDetail in CopilotAdapter.session.ts:272. Also an env multiplier (e.g. RYCO_PROVIDER_STARTUP_PHASE_TIMEOUT_SCALE) resolved in providerOperationPolicy and passed as phaseTimeouts/startupPhaseTimeouts. E) Textgen 180 s caps: handle in the textgen finding.

Not done#150 One codex app-server process per thread session; share one per provider instance (as OpenCode already does)

gap-first-turn-latency:codex-shared-app-server · original impact Low, effort L · Process spawns decision

Current state

Confirmed NOT_DONE. Each live Codex session still spawns its own `codex app-server` in a per-session scope, runs `initialize`, then thread/start or thread/resume. Nothing owns a shared app-server per instance, and #710 even widened stopAll to unbounded with the comment 'Sessions own independent app-server processes'. The only sharing is CodexStoredThreadReader (cd0b163e9, extended by bb8d23c7c for skills/list): one read-only process for thread/read and skills/list, no thread start. Two things the auditor missed. (1) Session prewarm (440c42224, 65c7e6f2d, a8a683529, 3cbe9a677) now starts the session on composer focus or first keystroke. That hides most of the ~140 ms spawn+initialize, so the latency value is lower than the finding claims. Prewarm still spawns a full app-server per prewarmed thread, up to 2 per instance and 4 overall, idling for 2 min. (2) Sharing is harder than the sketch suggests. The runtime treats every non-root conversation on its process as a collab child. The client keeps one request handler per method (last wins) and has no way to remove notification handlers. The remaining value is mainly about 125 MiB RSS per concurrently live Codex thread. The ProviderSessionReaper stops sessions after 5 min idle, which bounds how many are live. Per-thread MCP children (about 730 MiB per thread) are unaffected.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexSessionRuntime.ts:1276 makeCodexSessionRuntime still calls spawner.spawn(ChildProcess.make(binaryPath, ["app-server"], { cwd: options.cwd, env })) once per runtime, in the per-session runtimeScope. The client is built on that child (1294-1301). Each runtime has its own queues: events 2048 (1252), serverNotifications 512 (1302).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexSessionRuntime.ts:2222 start() sends initialize under a startup deadline and the initialized notify (2224-2228), then openCodexThread (thread/start or thread/resume) on every session.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.ts:2036 startSession creates a per-session Scope.make and calls createRuntime = options.makeRuntime ?? makeCodexSessionRuntime (2049-2050). No shared owner on this path.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.ts:2813 Comment added in #710 (60633eff3): 'Sessions own independent app-server processes; stop them all at once.' stopAll concurrency changed to unbounded. This confirms per-session processes are the intended model.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/OpenCodeDriver.ts:135 OpenCode builds makeOpenCodeServerOwner per instance and passes it to the adapter and to text generation. CodexDriver.ts has no counterpart; its only 'shared' hits are the header comment (line 14) and sharedHomePath (153).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.ts:1938 makeCodexStoredThreadReader (cd0b163e9): one lazy read-only app-server per adapter in process.cwd(), closed after 60 s idle. It serves readThreadHistory (2610-2611) and, since bb8d23c7c, readProjectCommands skills/list (2564). It starts no thread and is not used for session start.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexSessionRuntime.ts:1192 readStoredCodexThread (spawn per read) has no production callers left. Its only use is CodexCollabRuntime.integration.test.ts:99, so the auditor's 'partly rerouted' understates this: history reads are fully rerouted.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderSessionPrewarm.ts:74 Prewarm (440c42224 and later) starts the exact session the next send would start, through providerService.startSession (line 277). For Codex that is a full app-server spawn+initialize+thread/start per prewarmed thread. Limits: 2 min idle, perInstanceLimit 2, totalLimit 4. The web composer triggers it on focus or first keystroke (65c7e6f2d). This hides first-turn spawn latency in the common path, but each prewarm is a full process.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexSessionRuntime.ts:1763 handleRawNotification treats any notification whose threadId is not this runtime's root as a foreign or child conversation. It suppresses it and records its live turns in collabChildLiveTurnsRef (1775-1800), and interruptTurn (2373-2436) interrupts those child turns. On a shared process, another Ryco thread's turns would be classified as this thread's children and interrupted on Stop. Routing must therefore happen above the runtime.
  • packages/effect-codex-app-server/src/client.ts:94 requestHandlers is a Map with one handler per method, last registration wins (251-254). notificationHandlers are append-only arrays with no removal (255-260). Several runtimes calling handleServerRequest or handleServerNotification on one shared client (CodexSessionRuntime.ts:1898-2130) would overwrite each other's approval handlers and leak closures. A shared owner needs one demultiplexing router.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderSessionReaper.ts:13 Sessions are reaped after 5 min of inactivity (sweep every 2 min). This bounds how many idle Codex processes coexist, and with it the RSS saving.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexProvider.ts:325 Other one-off app-server spawns remain, each with its own initialize: the status probe (CodexProvider.ts:325), CodexResetCredits.ts:140, CodexMcpService.ts:680 and codexIsolatedAppServer.ts:75. None of them is on the first-turn path.
Remaining

Live sessions are not shared. makeCodexSessionRuntime spawns its own process (CodexSessionRuntime.ts:1276-1301) and runs initialize (2224-2228) for every session. CodexAdapter.startSession (CodexAdapter.ts:2036-2062) creates one runtime per thread, and CodexDriver has no per-instance app-server owner. Prewarm (ProviderSessionPrewarm.ts) now hides most of the spawn+initialize latency for composer-driven sends. Session starts that are not prewarmed still pay it: Agent Control or automation-created threads, sends with no composer focus window, and prewarm misses. What remains is mainly memory: one ~125 MiB app-server per live Codex thread within the 5-min reaper window, plus up to 2 per instance for unclaimed prewarms.

Implementation sketch

Two options; take the lower-risk one first. Option A, recommended first step: a warm standby process with no multiplexing. Add apps/server/src/provider/CodexAppServerStandby.ts, built in CodexDriver.create next to the adapter and passed through makeCodexAdapter options. - It keeps 0 or 1 spare `codex app-server` per instance: spawned with the instance env and CODEX_HOME, already sent initialize/initialized, closed after idle (e.g. 2 min) and with the instance scope. - Split makeCodexSessionRuntime so it accepts an already-initialized { child, client, transportFailure } handle instead of always spawning at 1276. start() skips initialize when the handle is pre-initialized. - startSession takes the spare if there is one, otherwise spawns as today, then refills in the background. - This keeps one process per thread, so failure isolation, collab-child classification and handler registration are unchanged. It removes about 140 ms from every non-prewarmed start and turns prewarm into thread/start only. - Open question: the spare's process cwd is neutral rather than the thread's. Verify against a real codex-cli that project config (.codex/config.toml), AGENTS.md discovery and sandbox roots all follow the thread/start `cwd` param, not the process cwd. If they do not, keep a spare only for the most recent project cwd. - Tests in CodexAdapter.test.ts with makeRuntime or a fake spawner: a spare is adopted, a dead spare is discarded, refill happens, and close happens on adapter teardown. Option B, the full finding: a shared multiplexed owner (CodexAppServerOwner, modelled on OpenCodeServerOwner.ts). (1) The owner spawns lazily, initializes once and refcounts sessions. It registers exactly one handler per server-request method and one notification fan-out on the client. It routes by params.threadId to registered per-thread views. It registers collab children through thread/started source.subAgent.thread_spawn.parentThreadId and the collabAgentToolCall receiverThreadIds. It must buffer or resolve notifications for unknown thread ids, because CodexSessionRuntime.ts:1763 notes that child thread/status/changed arrives before registration. (2) Refactor CodexSessionRuntime into a view. It takes notifications and requests from the owner's per-thread queue instead of client.handleServer*, and drops the 'any non-root conversation is my child' rule (1763-1800) in favour of explicit child ownership. (3) On process exit or transport failure the owner fans session/exited out to every view and settles their pending approvals. The next acquire restarts it. (4) Each view still gets its own queue capacity, so one busy thread cannot fill another thread's queue. (5) Fold CodexStoredThreadReader into the owner, or keep it separate so reads do not contend with live turns. (6) Tests: two threads on one fake app-server (codexCollabMockPeer) with interleaved notifications. Stop on thread A must not interrupt thread B. Approvals route to the right thread. A process crash ends both sessions with session.exited. Collab children still group under the right parent. For either option, measure RSS and the time from send to first token, with and without prewarm.

Needs a decision

Option B trades per-thread failure isolation for memory. With a shared process, one crashed or wedged codex app-server ends or blocks every Codex thread on the instance. AGENTS.md lists reliability first and says correctness and robustness win tradeoffs. Since prewarm already hides most of the latency, the remaining gain is mostly about 125 MiB RSS per concurrent thread. Someone needs to decide whether that memory justifies a shared failure domain, or whether the isolation-preserving standby (Option A) is enough.

Value low · effort L · risk high

Terminal, diff, files panels (16)

Done#151 Initial terminal snapshots share the 4 MiB subscriber byte budget, so large combined histories cause a deterministic resync loop every 250 ms

gap-right-panel-first-open:terminal-bootstrap-byte-budget-resync-loop · original impact High, effort S · Reliability

Current state

Confirmed DONE. In 60633eff3 (#710, also in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3), bootstrap 'started' events stopped going through a charged initialQueue. They are now emitted with Stream.fromIterable(initial), concatenated ahead of the live queue, and only live events count against the 256-event / 4 MiB ledger. The only production subscriber (wsRpcClient terminal.onEvent) asks for replay:'metadata', so bootstrap events carry an empty history plus the cursor. The web drawer re-hydrates missed output through terminal.open(sinceCursor) when a replay cursor is ahead (TerminalReplay.browser.tsx:133). All transports (web, mobile, hosted, device) share RpcTransport.subscribe, which detects TerminalSubscriptionResyncError by _tag. Cause.squash preserves _tag, and the test decodes through the real wire codec. Detection triggers exponential backoff from 250 ms to an 8 s cap, reset after 30 s of quiet, with one warning per transport session. Both proposed tests exist. I found no other subscriber, and no Hub-side subscriber. listSessions hands out the retained history string by reference and listDiagnostics is an in-memory map, so a metadata bootstrap is cheap. Legacy no-replay subscribers against the new server get uncharged full snapshots, and no loop is possible from the bootstrap. Old servers against new clients still loop, but at the backed-off rate. Adjacent, pre-existing and out of scope: the terminal stream is not rechunked like the orchestration streams are (ORCHESTRATION_STREAM_CHUNK_MAX_BYTES = 256 KiB via rechunkByBudget). Stream.fromQueue drains with Queue.takeAll, so one live RPC chunk can approach the 4 MiB ledger, which equals RELAY_MAX_RPC_MESSAGE_BYTES (4 MiB). Over the relay, a chunk whose framing pushes it just past 4 MiB gets the non-retryable 'response exceeded the largest message' die. That would stop the terminal subscription for the life of the connection object, since connection.ts passes no onError. Large chunks also block other RPCs queued behind them on the shared socket. This window is narrow and needs saturating terminal output over the relay. It is not a defect of this fix.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.ts:20-31 Budget doc now says bootstrap snapshots are not charged, and that charging them caused the deterministic resync loop.
  • apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.ts:42-61 terminalBootstrapEvent: replay 'metadata' sets history to "" and adds replay:true and hasRunningSubprocess, keeping the cursor. A legacy request without replay keeps the full snapshot.
  • apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.ts:234-298 Only the live queue goes through makeTerminalSubscriberOffer and the ledger. Bootstrap uses Stream.fromIterable(initial) with a perf-only tap, concatenated before Stream.fromQueue(queue). The old initialQueue that shared the ledger (f1be4abc7 terminalRpc.ts:231-244) is gone.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsRpcClient.ts:574-580 The single production caller of subscribeTerminalEvents sends { replay: "metadata" }. git grep finds no other caller in apps/ or packages/, and none in the Hub.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts:72-80,120-139 RESYNC_SUBSCRIPTION_MAX_DELAY_MS 8 s, 30 s backoff reset, _tag-based detection, and resyncSubscriptionRetryDelayMs doubling.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts:359-380 Resync branch: consecutive count is reset only after a quiet period. One console.warn per transport session. Backed-off waitForRetry.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts:593 rejectCompleted(Cause.squash(exit.cause)) preserves the decoded TaggedError, so _tag detection works on real wire failures.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/terminal/reconciliation.ts:58-85 Replay events are accepted only when the cursor proves missed output. apps/web/src/components/ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:872-877 then re-hydrates through openTerminal({ resync: true }), so slow-consumer recovery still works without history in the bootstrap.
  • apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.test.ts:234-264 Test 'completes the bootstrap when retained histories exceed the live byte budget'. It uses three escape-heavy full-history snapshots of about 2.6 MB each on the wire, about 7.9 MB total, and expects 3 started events then live output. The auditor cited 211-250.
  • apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.test.ts:417 Live-event byte-budget resync test retained.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.test.ts:185-232 Backoff and single-warning test, with the failure delivered as a raw wire Exit.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/constants.ts:36-41 Adjacent, out of scope: orchestration streams cap each RPC chunk at 256 KiB to stay far below the 4 MiB relay cap. The terminal stream has no such rechunking, and Stream.fromQueue uses Queue.takeAll (effect 4.0.2 Channel.ts:1294-1296).
Defects in the shipped fix

None in the fix. Minor correction: the new terminalRpc test is at :234-264, not :211-250. Not a defect, but adjacent and pre-existing: terminal live chunks are not byte-rechunked, so over the hosted relay a drained queue near the 4 MiB ledger can exceed RELAY_MAX_RPC_MESSAGE_BYTES (4 MiB) once RPC framing is added. That turns into a non-retryable 'response exceeded the largest message' failure, and the terminal subscription stops for good, because packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:320 passes no onError and the error is not retryable. The window is narrow (framing is about 50 bytes plus 1 per event) and needs saturating output over the relay.

Done#152 Every connect and reconnect streams the full scrollback of every running terminal, then terminal.open sends it again

gap-right-panel-first-open:terminal-history-in-subscription-snapshot · original impact High, effort M · Network / RTT

Current state

Fixed in #710 (60633eff3), which is also in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3. The shared rpc client (web, desktop, mobile, hosted relay) subscribes with replay:"metadata". The server answers with history-free started events marked replay:true, and bootstrap events no longer count against the 4 MiB budget. A mounted drawer that receives a replay showing missed output now re-hydrates through terminal.open({sinceCursor}), which returns only the delta from the history cursor index. It no longer blanks the view. A cached or detached view refuses buffer catch-up when a replay is pending and opens with its own cursor. The store only registers replayed terminals and never opens them, and persist writes are skipped when the persisted slice is unchanged. Old and new clients and servers stay compatible in both directions: the old payload was Schema.Struct({}), excess fields are ignored, and replay is opt-in. I tried to break the reconnect, first-mount race, cached-view and failure paths and found no defect. Two residual history/bandwidth paths remain. Both are outside this finding's connect-time scope.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsRpcClient.ts:574-580 This is the only caller of subscribeTerminalEvents (git grep). It always passes { replay: "metadata" }, so it covers web, desktop, mobile and hosted relay (relay/transport.ts:45 passes through).
  • apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.ts:42-61 terminalBootstrapEvent sets history to "", replay:true and hasRunningSubprocess for metadata subscribers. Legacy callers keep the full snapshot.
  • apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.ts:249-298 Bootstrap is built from running sessions and concatenated without being queued, so it is not charged against the budget. The live cursor filter is unchanged from f1be4abc7. Generation is per manager lifetime (contracts terminal.ts:42), so the filter does not drop events after a restart.
  • packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:2209-2214 The payload is TerminalSubscribeEventsInput. At f1be4abc7 it was Schema.Struct({}), so an old server ignores replay and old clients still get full snapshots.
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:241-262 openSnapshot returns the history after sinceCursor through TerminalHistoryCursorIndex.since (historyCursorIndex.ts:74-92). It falls back to full history on a generation mismatch, trimming or reset.
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:833-879 appliedCursor is not advanced for replays. An accepted replay sets terminalHydratedRef=false and calls openTerminal({resync:true}) without writing the empty snapshot.
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:930-946,983-1079 applyPendingTerminalEvents stops at a replay. openTerminal sends sinceCursor=appliedCursor, appends the delta, replays buffered entries after the answer's cursor, and on failure resumes live events.
  • apps/web/src/components/terminalViewCache.ts:105-126 resolveTerminalViewCatchUp returns null when the pending buffer has a replay, so a reattached view goes through the sinceCursor open and never applies output on top of a gap.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/terminal/reconciliation.ts:74-85 A replay is accepted only for a later cursor or a new generation. Otherwise the store and drawer drop it and keep the scrollback.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/terminal/store.ts:813-836,483-496 For replays, registerThreadTerminal never opens or focuses and is reference-preserving, so terminalStateByThreadKey is unchanged and no persist write happens.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/terminal/store.ts:84-109,986 skipUnchangedPersistedState wraps createJSONStorage, so the JSON.stringify and setItem are skipped when the partialized reference is unchanged.
  • apps/web/src/components/TerminalReplay.browser.tsx:133,222 Browser tests cover a caught-up replay that keeps the scrollback and a missed replay that re-hydrates from the view's cursor. ThreadTerminalDrawer.browser.tsx:477 covers the detached-view replay.
Defects in the shipped fix

None found. I checked reconnect with missed output, reconnect without missed output, a first mount racing the subscription, a cached view with a buffered replay, a failed resync open, cross-generation replays and wire compatibility in both directions. Each one is handled correctly. Non-defect residuals: (1) useChatProjectScripts.ts:162 downloads and discards up to 2 MiB of history per script run on a non-busy base terminal, and the opened drawer may then fetch it again. (2) mobile subscribes to terminal events it discards (environmentDriver.ts:519, hostedHub/primaryConnection.ts:288 with connection.ts:320), so live terminal output of all threads still crosses the relay to phones. Both are outside this finding's connect/reconnect-history scope.
