Partial#153 Diff worker ships a 608 KiB inlined Oniguruma WASM it never uses, while running the 3.5-5x slower JS regex engine

gap-right-panel-first-open:worker-inlined-unused-wasm · original impact Medium, effort S · Build config WP13

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor marked this DONE after checking only the local and no-CSP path. They missed that the hosted Hub serves this client under a CSP without 'wasm-unsafe-eval'. There, shiki-wasm makes every diff worker fail to initialize, and highlighting moves to the main thread, a regression against the pre-fix off-thread JS engine. They also counted the missing webBundleSplitting guard as cosmetic. It is an unimplemented proposal item, though minor.

Current state

Both proposal parts landed in #710 (60633eff3). (a) worker.format "es" means the diff worker no longer inlines the Oniguruma WASM: the built worker is 213 KB and loads ./wasm-*.js on demand. (b) The pool prefers shiki-wasm and claims the main-thread singleton for shiki-js. On local and desktop (no CSP) this works as the auditor described. But (b) regresses the hosted Hub. The Hub builds the pinned client (vendor/ryco = 7bc39eec3, which contains #710) and sends `script-src 'self' 'sha256-…'` on every response, with no 'wasm-unsafe-eval'. supportsWasmHighlighter() only checks that the WebAssembly global exists. Under that CSP every diff worker fails to initialize with a CompileError after fetching the 622 KB wasm chunk. The pool sets workersFailed, and all hosted diff and file highlighting falls back to JS tokenization on the main thread. That is worse than before the fix, when the JS engine ran off-thread. I reproduced it in Playwright Chromium with the Hub's CSP: both `new WebAssembly.Module` on the main thread and `WebAssembly.instantiate` in a module worker throw CompileError ("violates the following Content Security Policy"). The proposed bundle guard in webBundleSplitting.test.ts is also missing. Side note: the Playwright MCP wrote one snapshot file into the gitignored /Users/laurinfrank/Code/ryco/.playwright-mcp/ (page-2026-10-14T22-10-58-583Z.yml, 250 B). git status is still clean, and I left the file in place per the no-delete rule.

Evidence
  • apps/web/vite.config.ts:231-235 worker: { format: "es" } is set (part a, 60633eff3). The built dist/assets/worker-DLI31svb.js is 213,046 B, starts with ES module code, not an IIFE, and calls import(`./wasm-S0UXjx1m.js`) only on the shiki-wasm path.
  • apps/web/src/lib/diffWorkerPool.ts:25-27 supportsWasmHighlighter() returns true whenever the WebAssembly global and instantiate exist. It does not detect a CSP that blocks WebAssembly compilation.
  • apps/web/src/lib/diffWorkerPool.ts:34-58 The pool is created with preferredHighlighter "shiki-wasm" whenever that probe passes. The main-thread singleton is claimed for shiki-js first (:35-45). That claim is what lets the main-thread fallback still work under CSP.
  • ryco-hub:src/http/securityHeaders.ts:30 On origin/main the hosted CSP is `script-src 'self' 'sha256-<inline>'[ turnstile]` with no 'wasm-unsafe-eval' or 'unsafe-eval', so browsers refuse WebAssembly compilation.
  • ryco-hub:src/http/app.ts:428 withSecurityHeaders(response, csp) applies to every response, static assets included. The worker-*.js response therefore carries the CSP, and the dedicated worker inherits it from that response.
  • ryco-hub:Dockerfile:10 The Hub builds vendor/ryco (pinned at 7bc39eec3; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 60633eff3 7bc39eec3` is true) with VITE_RYCO_CLIENT_MODE=hosted-hub, so the hosted client ships the shiki-wasm workers.
  • apps/web/node_modules/@pierre/diffs/dist/worker/WorkerPoolManager.js:258-286 If any worker's initialize rejects (the engine import, then the WASM CompileError), the pool sets workersFailed=true, terminates the workers and rejects queued render tasks.
  • apps/web/node_modules/@pierre/diffs/dist/renderers/DiffHunksRenderer.js:382-409 When isWorkingPool() is false, renderers tokenize on the main thread through getSharedHighlighter. That singleton was claimed as shiki-js, so it works, but all tokenization is then main-thread JS (the report measured 337-460 ms per 1,600 lines).
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffWorkerPoolProvider.browser.tsx:10-24 The browser test asserts shiki-wasm and workersFailed=false, but runs without a CSP, so it cannot catch the hosted failure.
  • apps/web/src/perf/webBundleSplitting.test.ts There are no worker or wasm assertions. The proposed guard that the worker chunk contains no wasm-inlined source was never added. viteConfig.test.ts:122 only checks the format flag.
  • (empirical) Playwright Chromium, in-memory node server on 127.0.0.1 with the Hub CSP Main thread: `new WebAssembly.Module(<8-byte empty module>)` gave "CompileError: WebAssembly.Module(): Compiling or instantiating WebAssembly module violates the…". Module worker: `WebAssembly.instantiate` gave the same CompileError. This also shows that the synchronous probe detects the block.
Remaining

Hosted regression from part (b): apps/web/src/lib/diffWorkerPool.ts:25-27 selects shiki-wasm in CSP environments that forbid WebAssembly, such as the hosted Hub (ryco-hub src/http/securityHeaders.ts:30). Diff workers then fail to initialize and hosted highlighting runs on the main thread. Missing guard: apps/web/src/perf/webBundleSplitting.test.ts has no assertion that the built worker chunk is free of inlined WASM.

Defects in the shipped fix

The shiki-wasm switch (60633eff3, diffWorkerPool.ts:25-34) has no CSP awareness. Under the Hub's production CSP (no 'wasm-unsafe-eval'), each diff worker downloads the 622 KB wasm chunk (230 KB gz), fails Oniguruma instantiation with a CompileError, and the pool goes to workersFailed. Queued renders reject with console.error, and every later diff or file highlight runs as JS tokenization on the main thread. Before the fix, the JS engine ran inside the workers. The failure repeats every time the owner recreates the pool after its idle grace, and each attempt logs CSP violations. The browser test cannot catch this because it runs without a CSP. The code comment's measured warm gain is only 25-30% (36 -> 27 ms per 200 lines), so falling back to shiki-js in CSP-restricted contexts costs little.

Implementation sketch

1) apps/web/src/lib/diffWorkerPool.ts: make supportsWasmHighlighter() a memoized real probe: `try { new WebAssembly.Module(Uint8Array.of(0x00,0x61,0x73,0x6d,0x01,0x00,0x00,0x00)); return true } catch { return false }`. Under a CSP without 'wasm-unsafe-eval' this throws synchronously; verified in Chromium. A worker gets its CSP from its own script response, and on the Hub that is the same header as the document, so the main-thread probe is a valid proxy. Keep the existing main-thread shiki-js claim. 2) Optional extra safety: when a pool created with shiki-wasm reports workersFailed (subscribeToStatChanges, or a .catch on pool.initialize()), record a module-level downgrade flag. Then terminate the pool and recreate it with shiki-js, through createDiffWorkerPoolOwner so DiffWorkerPoolProvider's pool state is refreshed, for example via a pool-replaced listener. This covers proxies that add CSP only to JS responses. 3) Tests: a unit test (vitest, stubbed globalThis.WebAssembly.Module that throws) asserting the pool is built with shiki-js. Keep DiffWorkerPoolProvider.browser.tsx for the no-CSP path. If feasible, add a Hub browser-qualification or Playwright check that opens a diff under the production CSP and asserts getStats().workersFailed === false. 4) apps/web/src/perf/webBundleSplitting.test.ts: add the missing guard. The built worker-*.js must stay under about 400 KB and must not contain the base64 WASM magic 'AGFzbQ' or reference wasm-inlined, while a separate wasm-*.js chunk exists. 5) Hub, optional and needing a decision: add 'wasm-unsafe-eval' to script-src in src/http/securityHeaders.ts (and update the spec doc and CSP tests) if hosted users should get the WASM engine. In any case, bump the vendored Ryco pin and deploy so hosted users get the client fix.

Needs a decision

The client-side probe and fallback is a plain Ryco bug fix that needs no decision. Getting it to hosted users requires a Hub vendored-pin bump and deploy. Giving hosted users the faster WASM engine instead would mean adding 'wasm-unsafe-eval' to the Hub CSP, a security-policy change: the Hub spec says CSP failures stop deployment rather than broadening script-src.

Value high · effort S · risk low

Partial#154 Client checkpoint-diff store keeps every viewed patch forever (keepAlive atoms, no eviction at refCount 0)

gap-right-panel-first-open:checkpoint-diff-client-cache-unbounded · original impact Medium, effort S · Memory WP11WP14A

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor's check of the web raw store holds: no functional bug. The auditor treated the mobile twin as an out-of-scope side note and did not look at DiffPanel's parsed-payload cache. Both still show the retention pattern the finding describes (a new entry per completed turn under the conversation key), so the expected bound of about 16 MB is not reached. DONE overstates the outcome; PARTIAL is accurate.

Current state

The web raw checkpoint-diff store fix (60633eff3, #710) is correct and covers every part of the proposal: an inactive LRU capped at 8 entries and 16M chars, conversation-slot supersession, and eviction on archive and removal, all with tests. The finding's goal of keeping client patch memory near 16 MB is still not met, for two reasons. (1) The mobile client store apps/mobile/src/rpc/checkpointDiffAtoms.ts describes itself as a verbatim mirror of the web store and already existed at f1be4abc7. It is unchanged and still keeps every viewed full-thread patch forever. ReviewSheet keys diffs by toTurnCount, so every turn that completes while the sheet is open adds another retained patch, and every thread reviewed keeps its own. (2) On web, DiffPanel's module-level renderablePatchCache is a DiffParseCache with 50 entries and its memory budget explicitly turned off. It keys parsed payloads by the conversation:<all turn ids> scope, which changes on every turn. Since 65af92766, patches of 1M chars or more parse in a worker and come back as independent structured clones. Context lines are stored in both line arrays, so each clone is at least the size of the raw patch. The finding's own example (50 turns with a 1 MB diff) therefore still retains about 50 MB or more, now in parsed form. A minor residue remains as well: evicted keys leave keepAlive atom nodes whose key strings contain every turn id.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/rpc/providerAtoms.ts:212-213 MAX_INACTIVE_CHECKPOINT_DIFF_ENTRIES = 8 and MAX_INACTIVE_CHECKPOINT_DIFF_CHARS = 16 MiB. The web raw store is now bounded as proposed.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/providerAtoms.ts:313-398 evictCheckpointDiffEntry, enforceInactiveCheckpointDiffBudget, releaseCheckpointDiffEntry and supersedeCheckpointDiffSlot are correct. React runs the old cleanup before the new watch: the old key joins the inactive set and the new watch evicts it. Watched entries are never evicted.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/providerAtoms.ts:450-466 evictCheckpointDiffsForThread is called on archive and on thread-removed (apps/web/src/environments/runtime/environmentStateSink.ts:100,113).
  • apps/web/src/rpc/providerAtoms.test.ts:356-480 Tests cover the count and char budgets, protection of watched entries, conversation-slot supersession and archive eviction.
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffPanel.tsx:138 renderablePatchCache = new DiffParseCache<ParsedDiffContent>() is module-level and is never cleared: not by evictCheckpointDiffsForThread and not by clearCheckpointDiffState on hosted teardown.
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffPanel.tsx:616 The parse cache key uses turnId = conversationCacheScope ('conversation:' plus every turn id, built at :523-528), so every completed turn with the panel open creates a new parse-cache entry. The superseded entry stays until 50 newer parses push it out.
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffPanel.tsx:633-665 Patches of OFF_THREAD_DIFF_PARSE_MIN_CHARS (1,000,000, diffParseOffThread.ts:8) or more are parsed in the worker with no previous payload. Each result is a fresh structured clone, stored by renderablePatchCache.set at :665, with no file objects shared between successive conversation parses.
  • apps/web/src/lib/diffParseCache.ts:35-64 DEFAULT_DIFF_PARSE_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES = 50 and UNBOUNDED_MEMORY_BYTES = Infinity. The shared LRUCache byte budget is deliberately disabled, so there is no byte bound on parsed payloads.
  • apps/web/src/lib/diffParsing.ts:14-23 RenderablePatch holds FileDiffMetadata[]. In @pierre/diffs 1.4.1, deletionLines and additionLines both include context lines, so each parsed payload takes at least as much memory as the raw patch.
  • apps/mobile/src/rpc/checkpointDiffAtoms.ts:185-191 The mobile twin (its header says it mirrors the web store verbatim) still uses an Atom.family with keepAlive and has no inactive budget, slot or eviction. Since f1be4abc7 it has changed only in import paths.
  • apps/mobile/src/rpc/checkpointDiffAtoms.ts:304-310 Release only decrements refCount. Patch data stays until the user clears the device cache in settings (deviceCache.ts:55) or a hosted reset runs (hostedHub/nodeStateCleanup.ts:9).
  • apps/mobile/src/features/review/useReviewDiffData.ts:19-37 buildFullThreadDiffInput keys by toTurnCount, the latest turn count. ReviewSheet.tsx:44-46 uses it, so each completed turn while the sheet is open creates a new key, and the old patch is never released.
Remaining

(1) Mobile: apps/mobile/src/rpc/checkpointDiffAtoms.ts:185-311 has no automatic count or byte bound, no slot supersession and no archive or removal eviction. ReviewSheet (apps/mobile/src/features/review/ReviewSheet.tsx:44-46 via useReviewDiffData.ts:19-37) creates a new full-thread key for every completed turn and for every thread reviewed, and none is ever released. On a phone that is memory the OS can kill the app over. (2) Web: DiffPanel's renderablePatchCache (DiffPanel.tsx:138, set at :642 and :665, keyed at :616 by the per-turn conversation scope) keeps parsed copies of superseded conversation patches, up to 50 entries with no byte budget (diffParseCache.ts:41,64). Patches of 1M chars or more are independent worker clones, so 50 turns with a 1 MB conversation diff still retain 50 MB or more. The cache also survives thread archive and hosted node or account teardown.

Defects in the shipped fix

The web raw-store fix has no functional bug. One minor residue: evictCheckpointDiffEntry (providerAtoms.ts:313-331) resets the atom value, but keepAlive atoms are never removed from appAtomRegistry and Atom.family keeps its entry. Each distinct key therefore keeps an atom, a node, a label and its key string. Conversation keys contain every turn id (about 37 chars per turn), so a thread whose diff panel stays open across N turns keeps roughly 18·N² bytes of key strings: about 185 KB at 100 turns and about 1.7 MB at 300. Separately, evictCheckpointDiffsForThread and clearCheckpointDiffState do not touch renderablePatchCache. Parsed node-owned diff content therefore outlives the raw store's archive and hosted-teardown eviction (in memory only, never persisted).

Implementation sketch

1) Shared store and mobile port. Move the bounded checkpoint-diff store out of apps/web/src/rpc/providerAtoms.ts (entries, inactive LRU, slot supersession, evictCheckpointDiffsForThread, invalidate and clear functions) into packages/client-runtime, for example src/state/checkpointDiff/store.ts. It must stay free of DOM and React Native code, use appAtomRegistry from @ryco/client-runtime/rpc, and take the API through a resolveApi(environmentId) parameter, or through a small factory makeCheckpointDiffStore({ ensureEnvironmentApi }). The web providerAtoms.ts and mobile checkpointDiffAtoms.ts then become thin wrappers, which removes the verbatim duplicate as AGENTS.md asks. Reimplement mobile's checkpointDiffCacheBytes and clearCheckpointDiffCacheForEnvironment on top of the shared evict function so they also update the inactive set and slot map. In the mobile useReviewDiffData.ts, have buildFullThreadDiffInput set cacheSlot: 'conversation' and have useCheckpointDiff forward it. Call evictCheckpointDiffsForThread on the archive transition and on thread-removed in apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentStateSink.ts:80-98. Move the cache-bound tests (providerAtoms.test.ts:356-480) to client-runtime, and add a mobile test showing that toTurnCount churn under the slot leaves a single entry. 2) Web parse cache. Give DiffParseCache an optional maxMemoryBytes and a per-entry weight, and pass normalizedPatch.length at DiffPanel.tsx:642 and :665 (for example a 32M-char budget). Also make conversation parses supersede each other: use a stable turnId of 'conversation:' + environmentId + ':' + threadId (blobSha already identifies the content), and add a slot-replace operation so a new hash for the same slot evicts the previous entry. Export a clearDiffPanelParseCache and call it beside clearCheckpointDiffState in apps/web/src/hostedHub/environment.ts and in account teardown. Optionally drop a thread's entries on archive. Tests: weight-based eviction in diffParseCache.test.ts, and a check that two successive conversation scopes for one thread leave one parse entry. 3) Optional: stop embedding every turn id in the cache key. Hash the joined ids, or use the latest turn id plus the count, to remove the O(N²) key residue. Alternatively hold atoms with registry.mount instead of keepAlive and unmount on eviction so the registry can drop the node.

Value medium · effort M · risk low

Done#155 Connect-time snapshot replay is treated as a fresh terminal start: it reopens closed drawers and switches the active terminal on every connect or reconnect

gap-right-panel-first-open:terminal-replay-started-forces-drawer-open · original impact Medium, effort S · Reliability

Current state

Confirmed DONE (60633eff3, #710; also in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3). The shared client subscribes with replay:"metadata". The server marks connect-time catch-up `started` events with replay:true, history "" and hasRunningSubprocess. In applyTerminalEvent, a replay takes the registerThreadTerminal path, which never sets terminalOpen or changes the active terminal or group. Force-open now only happens on live started/restarted. Reconciliation drops replays that prove nothing was missed. A mounted drawer that accepts a replay re-hydrates with terminal.open(sinceCursor) instead of wiping its scrollback. Because ChatTerminalShell mounts the drawer only when terminalOpen is true, a closed drawer no longer loads the xterm chunk or issues terminal.open on reload or reconnect. The server only replays at subscribe, Manager.open reattach emits no event, and mobile ignores terminal events, so no other replay path remains. Two side notes, neither a reason to reopen this finding: (1) A live `started` from another device's terminal.open is broadcast to every subscriber and still force-opens the drawer on all other web clients. That is intended semantics for server-initiated starts, so changing it is a separate product decision. (2) On a device with no stored state for the thread, the fix leaves the placeholder `default` terminal focused (see fixDefects).

Evidence
  • packages/contracts/src/terminal.ts:142-155 `started` gains an optional `replay: true` plus `hasRunningSubprocess`, both documented as catch-up-only.
  • packages/contracts/src/terminal.ts:203-210 TerminalSubscribeEventsInput { replay?: "metadata" }. The old server payload was Schema.Struct({}), so old servers ignore the field.
  • apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.ts:42-61 terminalBootstrapEvent emits replay:true with history "" for metadata subscribers. Legacy subscribers keep the full snapshot.
  • apps/server/src/ws/terminalRpc.ts:227-293 Only running sessions are replayed, once per subscription. Live events behind the snapshot cursor are filtered out.
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:2230-2245 A reattach in Manager.open returns openSnapshot and publishes no `started`, so a reopen is not a second replay path.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsRpcClient.ts:577 The single shared subscription site always passes { replay: "metadata" }.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/terminal/store.ts:813-837 `replay || quiet` goes through registerThreadTerminal. setThreadActiveTerminal and setThreadTerminalOpen(true) now run only for live starts. Old code at f1be4abc7 called both unconditionally.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/terminal/store.ts:483-496 registerThreadTerminal adds an unknown id and restores terminalOpen, activeTerminalId and activeTerminalGroupId.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/terminal/reconciliation.ts:76-84 A replay is accepted only when its cursor is past the highest output or activity sequence already accounted for, or the generation is new.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/terminal/activity.ts:7-10 A replay carries running-subprocess state through, and unknown leaves the state unchanged.
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:833-878 A drawer that accepts a replay keeps appliedCursor and calls openTerminal({resync:true}), which asks for sinceCursor=appliedCursor (lines 1001-1018). Repeated replays are rejected, so it cannot loop.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ChatTerminalShell.tsx:81 drawerOpen still requires terminalState.terminalOpen, so a closed drawer stays unmounted at boot.
Defects in the shipped fix

One minor edge case, not a correctness bug. On a device with no stored terminal state for the thread (new browser or device, or cleared storage), the store starts from the default state: terminalIds ["default"], active "default". registerThreadTerminal adds a replayed non-default terminal (for example terminal-<uuid>, or one running after the user closed `default` elsewhere) as an unfocused group. When the user later opens the drawer, the placeholder `default` is active, so terminal.open spawns a brand-new shell and the user lands on it instead of the running one. The old code focused the replayed terminal. store.test.ts:90-98 asserts this exact outcome (terminalIds [default, background], active default). The proposal itself asked for no focus change, so this is an accepted trade-off rather than a regression of the finding. It affects only first use on a new device, and its value is low. Separately and out of scope: a live `started` from another client's terminal.open is published to every subscriber (Manager.startSession publishEvent) and still force-opens and refocuses the drawer on all other web clients.

Implementation sketch

Optional polish for the fresh-device edge case. In packages/client-runtime/src/state/terminal/store.ts applyTerminalEvent, when a replay registers a terminal for a threadKey with no entry in state.terminalStateByThreadKey (no state stored on this device) and the current active terminal is the untouched default placeholder, make the replayed terminal active without opening. Do this only for the first replay that creates the entry: listSessions sorts by updatedAt descending, so that is the most recently used session, and later replays find the entry present and keep focus. Leave terminalOpen false. Add a store.test.ts case: with no prior state, replaying `background` then `default` keeps terminalOpen=false and makes `background` active only when `default` was not itself replayed first. Keep the existing 'keeps a closed drawer closed' test unchanged. Not needed to close this finding.

Done#156 Diff worker pool (3 workers) is created for every right-panel mode and torn down on every close

gap-right-panel-first-open:diff-worker-pool-every-mode · original impact Medium, effort M · CPU

Current state

Fixed in #710 (60633eff3), which is also in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3. LazyRightPanel no longer wraps every mode in a pool provider. Only DiffPanel (review), the PR FilesTab and the read-only DiffsFile branch of PreviewPanel lease the pool. On desktop, text files go straight to the edit-mode editor, because the edit session snapshot is created synchronously in the constructor. That editor gates the pool off anyway (FileRenderer checks !editSessionActive), so files, terminal, launcher, agents, simulator and render modes start no workers. A module-level, lease-counted owner keeps the pool after close, with a 3 min idle grace (30 s while hidden), so grammars and AST caches survive close, reopen and thread switches. Pool size is now clamp(floor(cores/4), 1, 2) instead of min(3, floor(cores/3)). Review intent (hover, focus, shortcut or open) prewarms the workers. Non-intent idle preloads only fetch code. Unit and browser tests cover the owner lifecycle, provider reuse across remounts, and intent-only prewarm. I found no other @pierre/diffs pool consumer outside a provider. The remaining gaps are minor polish.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatRightPanel.tsx:86-88 LazyRightPanel has no DiffWorkerPoolProvider. The old f1be4abc7 code wrapped every mode. It is mounted only while open or during the delayed unmount (ChatRightPanel.tsx:146-149, 252).
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffPanel.tsx:362-368 DiffPanel wraps itself, so the lease lives only while review is mounted. It is rendered only in the review gate (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:1499-1501).
  • apps/web/src/components/pullRequests/files/FilesTab.tsx:152-154 The PR files surface wraps itself. PullRequestReader.tsx:41 renders FilesTab, and DiffFileSection is only reached through PullRequestDiffStream inside FilesTab.
  • apps/web/src/components/PreviewPanel.tsx:904-925 Editable text uses PreviewFileEditor (no provider). Only the read-only DiffsFile fallback (phone tier, mixed line endings, no session) is wrapped. PreviewFileEditSession.ts:61 creates the session snapshot synchronously, so desktop never flashes through the DiffsFile branch.
  • node_modules/@pierre/diffs (1.4.1) dist/renderers/FileRenderer.js:166,398 The pool is skipped while editSessionActive. Taking the pool context away from the editor path does not move work onto the main thread.
  • apps/web/src/lib/diffWorkerPoolOwner.ts:9-21,46-123 Lease-counted owner with a 3 min / 30 s hidden idle grace. Pool size is clamp(floor(cores/4), 1, 2).
  • apps/web/src/lib/diffWorkerPool.ts:62-99 Single app-lifetime owner bound to WorkerPoolManager, with a visibilitychange listener and get/acquire/prewarm exports.
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffWorkerPoolProvider.tsx:39-66 Renders WorkerPoolContext.Provider directly. Resolves the pool in the useState initializer, leases it in an effect and re-syncs if the pool was retired.
  • apps/web/src/workspacePanelPreload.ts:115-138,183-190 Only intent (hover, focus, shortcut, open) on review calls prewarmDiffWorkerPool(). Idle preload only imports the module.
  • apps/web/src/lib/diffWorkerPoolOwner.test.ts Tests cover shared lease, reopen within grace, termination after grace, the hidden grace, retiring an unleased pool, double release and pool sizing.
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffWorkerPoolProvider.browser.tsx:26-52 Browser test: the same pool is reused across a provider unmount and remount.
  • apps/web/src/workspacePanelPreload.test.ts:88-102 Only an intent warms the workers.
Defects in the shipped fix

Minor, low impact. (1) Theme drift while the pool idles: owner.get(themeName) at diffWorkerPoolOwner.ts:79-87 ignores themeName when a pool already exists. Suppose the app theme flips (manual or OS-driven) while no provider is mounted, and review reopens within the 3 min grace. The FileDiff instances are then created in the commit's ref callbacks with the stale pool theme. DiffWorkerThemeSync's passive useEffect (DiffWorkerPoolProvider.tsx:10-26) only calls setRenderOptions afterwards. That call clears diffCache and fileCache and invalidates tasks (WorkerPoolManager.js:102-140), so the reopen briefly shows the old theme colours, wastes one round of worker highlighting and loses the warm cache for that open. The old per-open provider always created the pool with the current theme. (2) Proposal item 4 is only partly done. Prewarm starts the workers and the theme, but it does not call primeFileHighlightCache with a snippet in the thread's dominant language, and there is no requestIdleCallback prewarm when a thread with turnDiffSummaries renders. The first diff in a fresh pool still compiles its grammar on demand. (3) Proposal item 3 is only partly followed: hosts with 8 or more cores get 2 workers, not a default of 1. That is a deliberate trade-off for large patches.

Implementation sketch

Optional polish. (1) Theme drift: in DiffWorkerPoolProvider's useState initializer, or in diffWorkerPool.getDiffWorkerPool, compare pool.getDiffRenderOptions().theme with the requested themeName when the owner returns an existing pool. If they differ, fire pool.setRenderOptions({...current, theme}) before the children commit. Alternatively, subscribe the owner to the theme store (useTheme's root class toggle) so an idle pool re-themes eagerly. Test: in DiffWorkerPoolProvider.browser.tsx, mount with dark, unmount, switch to light, remount, and assert getDiffRenderOptions().theme === light before the first highlight result. A unit test in diffWorkerPoolOwner.test.ts can cover a get() theme-mismatch hook. (2) Grammar prime: in prewarmDiffWorkerPool, accept an optional language hint (dominant extension from the active thread's latest turnDiffSummaries files) and call pool.primeFileHighlightCache({name: `prewarm.${ext}`, contents: '\n', cacheKey: `prewarm:${ext}`}). Optionally schedule it from scheduleIdleTask once a thread with turn diffs renders, honouring saveData. Extend workspacePanelPreload.test.ts to assert the hint is passed. (3) Pool size: if memory matters more than large-patch throughput, change MAX or the divisor in resolveDiffWorkerPoolSize to default to 1, or size it from the first lease's file count. Update the sizing test.

Done#157 PTY spawn waits for chunk load, reveal and xterm fit, so shell rc startup is serialized after all client work

gap-right-panel-first-open:terminal-pty-spawn-after-mount · original impact Medium, effort M · Waterfall

Current state

Confirmed DONE (landed in #710, 60633eff3). The finding's measured waterfall was on the cold drawer path: the PTY spawn waited for the chunk, the Suspense reveal and xterm fit, and each mount sent 2 resizes. That waterfall is gone. ChatTerminalShell calls prepareThreadTerminal as soon as the drawer is open and visible while the xterm chunk is still loading. The drawer's openTerminal then takes that in-flight promise instead of opening again. Prepare and drawer share one cwd/env resolver (terminalLaunchKey checks they match), and hosted capability is checked first. The drawer now mounts through useLazyComponentReady, so the Suspense throttle no longer applies. Resizes are 0 or 1 per mount: the 30 ms timer and the rAF effect are both skipped until hydration and only fire when the fitted size changed. When the chunk is already loaded (hover or idle preload, later opens), no prepare runs, but the mount happens in the same commit and the open is sent from a layout effect right after xterm construction, so only a few tens of ms stay serialized. The hover/pointerenter PTY prewarm was not implemented, on purpose: a fresh start still force-opens the drawer (store.ts:813-831). I found no functional bugs or regressions. The residuals below are small.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/terminalPrepare.ts:158 prepareThreadTerminal: one in-flight terminal.open per (env, thread, terminal), deduped by launchKey, 10 s TTL (:134). Uses the last fitted size per layout (:99). Skips when hosted terminalOpen capability is not granted (:171). No xterm imports.
  • apps/web/src/terminalPrepare.ts:36 resolveThreadTerminalLaunch is the shared cwd/worktree/env resolver used by the chat drawer, the workspace terminal tab and prepare. This addresses the verifier's concern that a cwd/env mismatch makes the server relaunch the PTY and wipe its history (Manager.ts:2236-2241 relaunch rule).
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ChatTerminalShell.tsx:91 Prepare effect fires when visible && drawerOpen && launch && the chunk is not loaded, so it runs on toggle, shortcut, server start and persisted-open reload. `visible` includes terminalCapability.allowed (ChatView.tsx:6359-6364), so on hosted the effect re-runs once access is granted. useLazyComponentReady (:85) replaces the old React.lazy + Suspense (f1be4abc7 ChatTerminalShell.tsx:14,155).
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:504 The terminal tab prepares with the same resolver, but this code lives inside the lazy ThreadWorkspacePanel chunk and WorkspaceTerminalPanel only renders when the terminal tab is active (:1506-1507). With a cold panel shell, the spawn still waits for the shell chunk. That chunk is preloaded on hover/idle (ChatRightPanel.tsx:141-145).
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:994 openTerminal takes takePreparedTerminalOpen and awaits prepared.promise instead of calling api.terminal.open. lastSentDimensionsRef is seeded with the prepared size (:1004-1008). Snippet and resync opens bypass it.
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1062 After hydration there is at most one resize (sendResizeIfChanged :973). The fitTimer resize is skipped until hydrated (:1127). The rAF effect skips before hydration or when the size is unchanged (:1286-1291). The open runs from a layout effect (usePaneEffect, PaneFocus.tsx:46), so on a loaded chunk it starts right after xterm construction.
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadTerminalDrawer.browser.tsx:598 The test checks that a prepared open is taken (open called once) and that there is no resize when the sizes match. Despite its title ('resizes once if the fit differs'), it never exercises the size-differs branch. No test covers the prepare wiring in ChatTerminalShell or WorkspaceTerminalPanel (prepare fires before the chunk resolves and the total open count stays at 1).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/terminal/store.ts:813 A non-replay, non-quiet started event still forces terminalOpen=true and switches the active terminal. That is why hover prewarm is unsafe (terminalPrepare.ts:14-21). A quiet-start mechanism now exists, but only by terminal-id prefix for setup scripts (:815-816, added in #728).
  • apps/web/src/components/BranchToolbar.tsx:198 Hover/focus on the terminal toggle only preloads the drawer chunk. When that chunk is already loaded at click time, prepare is skipped by design (it would race the same-commit mount and leave an unconsumed entry), and the mount opens at once.
Defects in the shipped fix

No functional bugs or regressions found. Minor non-blocking items: (1) Coverage: the browser test at ThreadTerminalDrawer.browser.tsx:598 is named for the 'fit differs -> exactly one resize' case but only asserts the equal-size branch. ChatTerminalShell.tsx:91 and ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:504 have no wiring tests. (2) Some prepared entries are never consumed: a snippet-insertion mount skips takePreparedTerminalOpen (ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:995), and a prepare can target a terminal whose viewport never mounts. Such entries stay up to 10 s, and a later mount adopts their older snapshot plus the buffered events. That is intended per the TTL comment, but it depends on event-buffer retention. (3) The window in which a fresh PTY's started event re-opens a drawer the user just closed now starts at the click, not after chunk load and reveal. It is only about spawn time plus one round trip, and only for a new PTY, which is the same order as before. (4) rememberTerminalDimensions is shared by all viewports of a layout (split panes, hidden drawers), so the stored size can be off and cost one resize later.

Done#158 Closing the drawer or switching panel tabs disposes xterm; every reopen re-downloads and re-parses the whole scrollback

gap-right-panel-first-open:terminal-remount-replays-history · original impact Medium, effort M · Rendering WP09

Current state

Confirmed DONE. Commit 60633eff3 (#710) removed the described cost. Unmounting a hydrated, still-open terminal (drawer close, workspace tab switch, terminal tab switch, pane focus loss) now stashes the live xterm element in a module LRU instead of calling dispose(). Remounting re-appends that element, fits, catches up from the client event buffer, and calls terminal.open with sinceCursor. The server answers with only the history after the cursor (historySince), and the client appends it with no reset. Event handler disposables are disposed and re-registered on every mount, so a reattached view does not get duplicate onData or link handlers. The prepared-open shortcut (full answer) only runs while the xterm chunk is not yet loaded, so it never coincides with a cached view. The history sanitizer strips only query and response sequences, so the delta reproduces the live stream (including alt-screen switches). The Hub does not inspect terminal.open. Remaining defect, minor: the LRU bound of 3 with immediate eviction is too small for a 4-way split group or for a pane-focus swap between panes with split terminals. Those transitions still do one full rehydrate each. Adjacent, outside this finding: running a project script on an idle existing terminal calls terminal.open without sinceCursor, downloads the full history, and discards it.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/terminalViewCache.ts:15 MAX_CACHED_TERMINAL_VIEWS = 3. stash() evicts synchronously in the while loop at line 56, so the bound is enforced before any same-commit take().
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:499 On mount, take() the cached view keyed by (environmentId, threadId, terminalId) plus launchKey. Line 515 re-appends the kept element instead of constructing a new Terminal.
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1001 sinceCursor = appliedCursor, unless the open was prepared or this is a snippet. The historySince answer is appended without \u001bc at line 1039. An older server's full answer is skipped through isTerminalViewCurrent.
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1213 Cleanup keeps the view when it is hydrated or awaiting a delta, has not exited, and the terminalId is still in the store. onData, selection and link-provider disposables are disposed before the stash at line 1242, so a reattach registers them once.
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadTerminalDrawer.tsx:1853 A split view mounts up to MAX_TERMINALS_PER_GROUP (4) TerminalViewports at once. Closing the drawer stashes all 4, which evicts the first, and that one fully rehydrates on reopen.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/types.ts:43 MAX_TERMINALS_PER_GROUP = 4, which is above the cache bound of 3.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/PaneFocus.tsx:46 usePaneEffect is a useLayoutEffect keyed on focus. A pane-focus swap stashes the outgoing pane's views in the same commit, before the incoming pane takes its views. ChatPanes.tsx:267 scopes each pane to its own thread, so outgoing plus incoming views can exceed 3.
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:241 openSnapshot returns only the history after sinceCursor through TerminalHistoryCursorIndex.since (apps/server/src/terminal/historyCursorIndex.ts). It falls back to the full history after a generation change, a reset, or trimming. Tested in Manager.test.ts around line 1990.
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadTerminalDrawer.browser.tsx:352 Browser tests cover reattach without rebuild or rewrite, delta-only append, a failed delta open, and re-hydration after a reconnect replay. No test covers the cache bound against a 4-way split or a pane-focus swap.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/useChatProjectScripts.ts:162 Adjacent, not this finding: a project script run on an idle existing terminal calls terminal.open without sinceCursor. The full history (up to about 2 MiB) is downloaded, decoded and thrown away.
Defects in the shipped fix

Minor. MAX_CACHED_TERMINAL_VIEWS=3 (apps/web/src/components/terminalViewCache.ts:15) is below MAX_TERMINALS_PER_GROUP=4, and stash() evicts synchronously (line 56). React runs all layout-effect cleanups of a commit before its mounts. Two cases follow. (a) Closing or reopening a 4-way split drawer, or switching a workspace tab away from and back to a 4-way split, evicts the first terminal every time. (b) A focus swap between split chat panes that hold 2+2 or more terminals stashes the outgoing views before the incoming views are taken, which evicts an incoming one. In both cases that terminal is rebuilt, its full history is downloaded, and it is parsed with \u001bc on every transition. That is the exact cost the finding describes, limited to these uncommon layouts.

Implementation sketch

1) apps/web/src/components/terminalViewCache.ts: make stash() trim lazily. Keep the insertion-ordered Map, and on stash schedule one queueMicrotask (deduplicated with a flag) that evicts the oldest entries beyond maxEntries. Takes that happen in the same React commit (the incoming mounts) are then served before the trim, and the steady-state bound still applies. Also raise MAX_CACHED_TERMINAL_VIEWS to at least MAX_TERMINALS_PER_GROUP (import from @ryco/client-runtime state/threads types, or the apps/web/src/types re-export), so a full split group survives a drawer close. 4 is enough; memory is about 4 detached xterms of up to 5,000 lines. Keep clear() and discard() synchronous. 2) Tests: in terminalViewCache.test.ts, assert that stashing 4 views into a bound-3 cache and taking one in the same tick returns a hit, and that after `await Promise.resolve()` size() is at most the bound and the oldest is disposed. In ThreadTerminalDrawer.browser.tsx, mount a 4-way split group, unmount, remount, and assert that terminalConstructorSpy was called 4 times (not 5) and that no \u001bc or full-history write happened. 3) Optional adjacent fix: in useChatProjectScripts.ts:142-162, pass sinceCursor from useTerminalStateStore.getState().terminalEventReconciliationByKey[key]?.cursor when reusing an existing terminal, so the discarded open answer is a delta and not the full scrollback.

Done#159 Local-changes review runs 9 sequential git spawns plus one per untracked file (up to 200)

gap-right-panel-first-open:local-changes-git-n-plus-1 · original impact Medium, effort M · Process spawns WP07A

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

The perf finding is fixed. In 60633eff3 (#710), GitIndexReview.read() replaced the per-file `diff --no-index` loop with one `git add --intent-to-add --pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul` in the disposable GIT_INDEX_FILE, followed by one working-tree diff. Branch is now read from the HEAD file by fs, so `symbolic-ref` is skipped, and the index and HEAD git-paths come from one rev-parse. A local review now costs 7 spawns, or 8 with untracked files, down from 10+N. The auditor's 'no fix defects' is wrong, though. `git add` always uses ADD_CACHE_OK_TO_REPLACE, so an intent-to-add path that clashes file-vs-directory with a tracked entry silently removes that entry from the temp index, and the unstaged review then hides the tracked deletion. Also, the stdoutTruncated checks are dead code (`run` never sets truncateOutputAtMaxBytes). Untracked content over 2 MB, which used to get the friendly 'Local changes exceed the 2 MB review limit', now surfaces as a raw GitCommandError.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitIndexReview.ts:214-238 One `add --intent-to-add --pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul` spawn (GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1, core.hooksPath=/dev/null, core.splitIndex=false) runs on the temp index, then a single `diff --`. The per-file loop at :269-279 runs only when Git refuses the batch. The 200-file cap is still enforced at :205.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitIndexReview.ts:83-97,115-146 One rev-parse returns both `--git-path index` and `--git-path HEAD`. readHeadFileBranch reads the HEAD file by fs and falls back to `symbolic-ref` for a symlinked HEAD, an unparseable file or the reftable `.invalid` stub. identity() is now one `rev-parse --verify HEAD` per call. The before/after comparison is kept at :282-287.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitIndexReview.ts:171-282 Spawn count: show-toplevel, rev-parse git-paths, rev-parse HEAD, ls-files --unmerged, diff --cached, ls-files --others, [add -N], diff, rev-parse HEAD. That is 7, or 8 with untracked files, down from 10+N at f1be4abc7.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitIndexReview.ts:217-233 DEFECT. Git's read-cache.c add_to_index always passes `ADD_CACHE_OK_TO_ADD|ADD_CACHE_OK_TO_REPLACE` (plus NEW_ONLY for -N). With OK_TO_REPLACE, check_file_directory_conflict, has_file_name and has_dir_name remove conflicting entries instead of failing; I checked this against upstream git master read-cache.c. Case 1: tracked file `foo` is replaced in the worktree by a directory `foo/` holding untracked `foo/bar`, and `add -N foo/bar` drops `foo` from the temp index. Case 2: tracked `dir/x` is replaced by an untracked file `dir`, and `add -N dir` drops `dir/x`. Either way, the single `diff --` at :238 never reports the tracked deletion, so the unstaged review silently omits it. The old code ran `diff --` on the unmodified temp index and showed it. The vanish lstat check at :248-265 does not catch this.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitIndexReview.ts:191-193,238-245 MINOR DEFECT. `run` (:61-77) never sets truncateOutputAtMaxBytes. In GitVcsDriverCore.ts:757-768 collectOutput then fails with a raw `git diff ... output exceeded 2000000 bytes and was truncated.` GitCommandError, and stdoutTruncated is always false, so these checks are dead. The old per-file loop gave the friendly 'Local changes exceed the 2 MB review limit.' when cumulative untracked output passed 2 MB. The batched diff now gives the raw error.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitIndexReview.test.ts:247-384 Tests cover a constant command count, no --no-index or symbolic-ref, new-file mode headers (100644, 100755, empty, glob names), an untouched live index, applying a batched untracked file, the refused-batch fallback, the partially refused sparse batch, hooks, a vanished path and reftable HEAD. No test covers a file/directory conflict between an untracked path and a tracked entry.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitReadWorkspace.ts:33-40 The authorization `rev-parse --show-toplevel` spawn is unchanged, as the proposal intended. A test (GitIndexReview.test.ts:385-402) expects it to be the only command before authorization fails.
Defects in the shipped fix

1) File/directory regression from the intent-to-add batch (GitIndexReview.ts:217-238). `git add` always uses ADD_CACHE_OK_TO_REPLACE, so marking an untracked path intent-to-add removes any tracked temp-index entry it clashes with as file vs directory. Examples: tracked file `foo` replaced by directory `foo/` with untracked `foo/bar`, or tracked `dir/x` replaced by an untracked file `dir`. The single working-tree diff then never shows the tracked deletion, so the unstaged review silently omits a real change and the user cannot stage it from review. The pre-#710 code showed it. This is an edge case and untested. I verified it against Git's read-cache.c source, not with a live repo, because writing scratch repos was not allowed. 2) Minor: the stdoutTruncated checks at :192 and :244 are dead because `run` does not pass truncateOutputAtMaxBytes, and GitVcsDriverCore fails the command instead. Untracked content over 2 MB in the batched diff now surfaces as a raw `git diff ... output exceeded 2000000 bytes` GitCommandError instead of 'Local changes exceed the 2 MB review limit.'

Implementation sketch

In apps/server/src/vcs/GitIndexReview.ts read(): (a) Restore a tracked-only view so intent-to-add can never hide tracked changes. Run `readRun([...diffArgs, "--"])` on the unmodified temp index before the add step, as the old code did. Then, only when untracked.length > 0 and the add succeeded, run a second `readRun([...diffArgs, "--diff-filter=A", "--"], true)`. In diff-files only intent-to-add entries can be status A, so it emits only the untracked files. Set unstaged = tracked + untrackedPatch. This restores the old tracked-then-untracked order and costs +1 spawn only when untracked files exist (9 instead of 8, still constant). Keep the refused-batch fallback and the vanish lstat check unchanged. A vanished intent-to-add path is filtered out by A, so the lstat check still catches it. (b) Map the output-limit failure to the friendly message. Wrap the diff runs with Effect.catchIf/mapError on a GitCommandError whose detail contains `output exceeded`, and return error(root, "Local changes exceed the 2 MB review limit."). Better: make GitVcsDriverCore emit a typed output-limit error to match on. Drop the dead stdoutTruncated checks, or pass truncateOutputAtMaxBytes, which is worse because git would keep producing output to the end. Tests in GitIndexReview.test.ts: (1) commit file `foo`, `rm foo`, `mkdir foo`, write `foo/bar`, read(). Expect unstaged.patch to contain `diff --git a/foo b/foo\ndeleted file mode 100644` and `diff --git a/foo/bar b/foo/bar\nnew file mode`. (2) The reverse: commit `dir/x`, remove dir, write file `dir`. Expect the deletion of dir/x and the new file dir. (3) Keep the constant-command-count test and update its expected count. (4) Untracked files totalling more than 2 MB give the friendly limit message.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Partial#160 No intent or idle preload for panel chunks or data; with modulePreload off, the chunk graph is a 3-level waterfall

gap-right-panel-first-open:panel-intent-preload · original impact Medium, effort M · Waterfall WP12B

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor called the RightPanelSheet gap minor and kept DONE. It is a whole desktop-tier layout (768-980 px, including touch tablets with no hover) where the proposal's idle preload and the mode-aware hover preload are missing, so the hidden-download benefit does not reach it. The auditor also missed that the idle preload goes around the same PR's speculative-preload gate (shellIdlePreload.ts: start after primary-shell-painted or the 5 s cap, and only on 4g), and that the default mod+D diff.toggle shortcut has no pre-navigate preload. The waterfall part of the finding is fully fixed.

Current state

The core proposal is in place and works on the main wide desktop layout. workspacePanelPreload.ts holds shared memoized preloadableLazy surfaces and load thunks. The header toggle, terminal drawer toggle, launcher cards, tab bar and workspace.* shortcuts all preload on intent. A closed inline sidebar runs a 4 s idle preload of the last mode. Vite modulePreload is on for dynamic imports, so each panel chunk brings its static closure in one round, and the shell and surface start in parallel on mount. The 3-level waterfall is gone everywhere. Three things are still missing. (1) Only RightPanelInlineSidebar sets the mode hint and schedules the idle preload. The desktop-tier sheet layout (768-980 px: iPad portrait, narrow windows) gets neither, so a header hover preloads only the shell, and touch tablets have no early start at all. (2) The idle preload goes around the speculative-preload policy that the same PR (#710) added in shellIdlePreload.ts: wait for primary-shell-painted or a 5 s cap, and skip unless effectiveType is 4g. It can therefore pull about 200 KiB gz of review code while a hosted cached-shell boot is still connecting. (3) The default mod+D diff.toggle shortcut does not preload before navigating. Data prefetch, which the proposal marked optional, is also not done.

Evidence

  • apps/web/src/workspacePanelPreload.ts:115-140 preloadWorkspacePanel starts the shell and the mode surface in parallel. For review it also fetches diffWorkerPool, and starts the workers only on intent. For files it preloads the icon resolver.

The panel idle preload ignores both.
  • apps/web/src/components/routeViews/ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:115-117 The route renders from a cached thread before bootstrapComplete. hostedHub/readCache.ts and threadReadCache.ts hydrate it on hosted. So RightPanelInlineSidebar mounts, and its idle preload can fire while the hosted relay and shell snapshot are still loading.

DraftChatThreadRouteView.tsx:290 is the same. The phone tier is <768 px (presentationTier.ts:12-13), so 768-980 px desktop-tier viewports miss the idle preload the proposal asked for.

Remaining

1) The desktop-tier sheet layout (viewport 768-980 px) has no idle preload and no mode hint. ChatThreadRouteView.tsx:359 and DraftChatThreadRouteView.tsx:290 render RightPanelSheet + LazyRightPanel, but the hint and idle scheduling live only in RightPanelInlineSidebar (ChatRightPanel.tsx:138-145). A header hover there loads only the shell, and touch tablets (no hover) get no early start: the first open waits for one round plus about 200 KiB gz for review. 2) The diff.toggle shortcut branch (useChatGlobalShortcuts.ts:116-121, default mod+d) does not preload review before navigate(). 3) Optional, not implemented: intent data prefetch for files (listEntries, staleTime 0 at projectPreviewAtoms.ts:15) and the simulator device list.

Defects in the shipped fix

scheduleIdleWorkspacePanelPreload (workspacePanelPreload.ts:154-172) uses a bare rIC with a 4 s timeout and checks only saveData. It does not use allowsSpeculativePreload (effectiveType must be 4g) or the primary-shell-painted / 5 s gate that the same PR set up in lib/shellIdlePreload.ts for every speculative chunk download. ChatThreadRouteView renders from a cached thread before bootstrapComplete (:115-117, hosted read cache), so on a slow hosted link the ~200 KiB gz review closure can download alongside the relay connect and the shell snapshot, and ahead of the shell's own ordered idle preloads. The module-global hint (workspacePanelPreload.ts:142-147) is never reset when the inline sidebar unmounts. This is harmless but stale. There is no test that a closed RightPanelInlineSidebar schedules the idle preload, or that the ChatHeader toggle preloads on hover.

Implementation sketch

1) In workspacePanelPreload.ts, add a hook useWorkspacePanelPreloadScheduling({ open, panelMode, enabled }). It sets the hint, clears it on unmount if the value is unchanged, and schedules the idle preload while the panel is closed. Call it once per route view for every non-phone tier: in ChatThreadRouteView and DraftChatThreadRouteView, next to the existing presentationTier branch, with enabled = presentationTier !== 'phone'. Remove the two effects from RightPanelInlineSidebar so the inline and sheet layouts share one path. 2) Gate the idle preload with the shell policy. In lib/shellIdlePreload.ts, export a single-task helper such as scheduleAfterShellIdle(task) that reuses the primary-shell-painted / SHELL_IDLE_PRELOAD_START_CAP_MS start and allowsSpeculativePreload(). Make scheduleIdleWorkspacePanelPreload use it and drop the local prefersReducedData. 3) In useChatGlobalShortcuts' diff.toggle branch, call preloadWorkspacePanel('review', { intent: true }) when the diff is not open: pass diffOpen in, or add an onBeforeOpenDiff hook. 4) Tests. workspacePanelPreload.test.ts: the idle preload waits for the startup phase or cap and is skipped for effectiveType '3g'. ChatRightPanel.browser.tsx or a route-view browser test: a closed panel in both inline and sheet layouts schedules the idle preload of the last mode (stub requestIdleCallback and mark primary-shell-painted). useChatGlobalShortcuts.browser.tsx: diff.toggle preloads review before navigate. 5) Optional: prefetch listEntries on files intent only after giving projectListEntriesQuery a short staleTime (around 2 s), so the mount watch does not refetch. Measure first.

Done#161 File-tree icons load a 285 KB manifest chunk after the tree data, then fetch each SVG from cdn.jsdelivr.net

gap-right-panel-first-open:vscode-icons-third-party-cdn · original impact Medium, effort M · Network / RTT

Current state

Confirmed DONE (60633eff3, #710). The jsdelivr CDN is gone. Icons now come from the app's own origin at /vscode-icons/v12.17.0/*.svg, and a slim generated lookup replaces the full manifest plus language-associations JSON: 128 KB on disk, a 90 KB raw / 24 KB gzip chunk, down from 285 KB. Opening, hovering or focusing the Files panel, its keyboard shortcut, and the idle preload (when Files is the hinted mode) all preload the resolver. I tried to refute this. I compared the new resolver with the old one over 6,026 inputs: every fileNames, fileExtensions and folderNames key and every language association, in both themes. There were 0 differences, so behaviour did not regress. All 1,121 icons the lookup can return are shipped, and a test enforces that. All six VscodeEntryIcon callers (file tree via ChangedFilesTree, composer menu, composer editor, timeline, markdown) go through the same hook. No other third-party CDN reference exists in apps/, packages/ or scripts/. The web build and server bundle copy the icons into dist/client, and the desktop app is served from the same static root. The Hub (vendors 7bc39eec3, which contains the fix) serves /vscode-icons/v*/ as explicitly immutable and brotli/gzip precompressed, under CSP img-src 'self'. That CSP would have blocked the old jsdelivr URLs on hosted. Only low-value hardening remains.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/vscode-icons.ts:32 Base URL is `${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}vscode-icons/v${lookup.version}`, a same-origin, version-pinned path. Vite base defaults to '/', so the path is absolute on nested routes.
  • apps/web/src/vscode-icons.ts:1 Imports only the slim vscode-icons-lookup.json. The old vscode-icons-manifest.json and language-associations JSON are deleted, and no source imports them.
  • apps/web/src/vscode-icons-lookup.json Old and new resolvers were run side by side on the f1be4abc7 manifest/associations against the current lookup: 6,026 file and folder inputs, dark and light, 0 differences. The light-theme default `_file_light`/`_folder_light` have an empty iconPath upstream, so dropping them from the lookup matches the old fallback to default_file/default_folder.
  • apps/web/src/vscode-icons.test.ts:65 Test asserts every lookup icon exists under public/vscode-icons/v<version>. :59 asserts the URL is same-origin (no '://'). I reproduced it: 1,121 icons, 0 missing, 0 extra.
  • scripts/sync-vscode-icons.mjs:20 Dev-time sync (root script `sync:vscode-icons`) generates the slim lookup and copies only the referenced SVGs and the MIT LICENSE into apps/web/public/vscode-icons/v<version> (:24). It needs no network at build or run time.
  • apps/web/src/workspacePanelPreload.ts:128 preloadWorkspacePanel('files') calls preloadVscodeIconResolver(). Callers: ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:787/1315 (intent), useChatGlobalShortcuts.ts:126 (shortcut), ChatRightPanel.tsx:88/144 (open and idle with the hinted mode). The lookup chunk now loads alongside the surface chunk, not after listEntries.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/useVscodeIconUrl.ts:27 preloadVscodeIconResolver shares the single in-flight import. The hook seeds state synchronously from loadedResolver, so tree rows paint icons on first render once the chunk is in.
  • apps/server/src/http.ts:120 Ryco server: the broad basename regex marks all 1,121 icon names `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (verified 0 misses). This is incidental: the regex predates f1be4abc7 (4864e68b7), is not path-based, and http.test.ts has no vscode-icons case.
  • ryco-hub:scripts/build-static-manifest.ts:33 Hub origin/main: `immutablePath = /^(?:assets\/|vscode-icons\/v[^/]+\/)/`. Icons are precompressed (br q11 + gzip 9) and covered by tests/http/static-assets.integration.test.ts:116-128. securityHeaders.ts:32 sets img-src 'self' data: blob:.
  • apps/server/scripts/cli.ts:195 The server build copies apps/web/dist, which includes vscode-icons/v12.17.0 (1,122 files present in the current dist), into dist/client. Both the npm package and the desktop app therefore ship the icons.
Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defect or regression. The resolver output matches the old one exactly, every icon is shipped, and all callers are covered. Non-blocking hardening gaps: (1) Immutable caching of the icons on the Ryco server rests on the pre-existing heuristic regex at apps/server/src/http.ts:120, not on the version-pinned path, and no test covers it. If someone tightens that regex to Vite's real `-<8 chars>.` hash pattern, which it should be (it currently also marks non-hashed public files such as apple-touch-icon.png, favicon-96x96.png, web-app-manifest-*.png and mockServiceWorker.js immutable for a year), the icons would silently drop to no-cache. (2) The Ryco server only serves build-time .gz siblings for content-hashed Vite outputs (apps/web/src/viteBuild/precompressAssets.ts:31-43), so it serves icon SVGs uncompressed. Common icons are under 1 KB and unaffected, but a few rare ones are large (file_type_shellcheck.svg 249 KB, about 178 KB gz; file_type_lerna.svg 220 KB, about 65 KB gz). The Hub precompresses them. (3) apps/web/vercel.json sets no headers for /vscode-icons, but the hosted SPA is served by the Hub, so this looks legacy.

Partial#162 Terminal server spawns ps over the whole system every second and rewrites the full history file every 40 ms under output

gap-right-panel-first-open:terminal-server-background-poll-and-persist · original impact Medium, effort M · Process spawns WP09

Current state

PARTIAL holds. PR #710 (60633eff3) fixed persistence. The 40 ms full rewrite is now a 1 s trailing window per session, with write-through on clear, restart, close and exit, a flush on shutdown, and readHistory doing a single read with no rewrite. It also added an I/O-gated back-off to the subprocess poll: 1 s for 5 ticks after any I/O, then 5 s. No spawn-free detection exists, and no implementation was found elsewhere: PtyAdapter has no foreground API and no other module replaces the snapshot. Every server with a live shell still spawns `/bin/ps -eo pid=,ppid=` (powershell Get-CimInstance on Windows) every 5 s when idle and every 1 s while any terminal has output. A live shell can exist even if the drawer was never opened, because ProjectSetupScriptRunner opens one for worktree setup scripts. The auditor's subscriber-gating option is weaker than it implies. Every connected client subscribes to all terminal events at connect time (connection.ts:320, wsRpcClient.ts:577), and worktreeSetupProgress subscribes on the server, so gating would only save spawns on headless nodes with no attached client.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:90 DEFAULT_PERSIST_DEBOUNCE_MS = 1_000. In f1be4abc7 it was 40 (per the git show 60633eff3 diff).
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:1281 queuePersist keeps one pending window per session and reads the latest historyState.history when the window ends. Superseded windows are dropped at 1292. The output path calls it at 1704 only for visible text.
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:1336 A finalizer flushes and drains pending windows on shutdown, with a 5 s cap. Tests at Manager.test.ts:1355-1429 cover window coalescing, exit write-through and shutdown flush.
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:1344 readHistory does a single readFileString (NotFound maps to none) and caps in memory only. The old exists check and rewrite-on-cap are gone.
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:1644 appendTerminalHistoryChunk appends incrementally (string concat at historyBuffer.ts:183). Only the 1 s window does the full-file writeFileString (1264).
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:98 DEFAULT_SUBPROCESS_IDLE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000, the back-off the proposal suggested.
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:2105 subprocessPollTick skips a spawn only when there was no I/O for 5 ticks. I/O is bumped by output (1651), PTY start (1915), input (2353) and activity change (2117). Continuous output (dev server log, top, a TUI) still means 1 spawn/s, the same as before. Tested by Manager.test.ts:1431.
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:2120 Effect.forever(waitForRunningSession -> tick -> sleep 1 s) runs for as long as any session is 'running'. The loop is not gated on subscribers.
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Layers/Manager.ts:637 snapshotPosixProcessTable is still a ps -eo pid=,ppid= spawn. snapshotWindowsProcessTable (668) spawns powershell.exe Get-CimInstance Win32_Process at the same cadence, which costs far more per spawn. Windows (nsis) is a desktop build target.
  • apps/server/src/terminal/Services/PTY.ts:25 PtyProcess exposes only pid, write, resize, kill, onData and onExit. It has no foreground-process or tcgetpgrp API, so spawn-free detection was not implemented anywhere.
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/ProjectSetupScriptRunner.ts:53 The server opens a shell terminal for worktree setup scripts and the shell stays alive afterwards. The poll can therefore run for the server's lifetime even if the user never opened the drawer.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts:320 Every connection subscribes to all terminal events (subscribeTerminalEvents replay 'metadata', wsRpcClient.ts:577). Subscriber-count gating would only help when no client is attached.
Remaining

Polling still spawns a process. Every server with at least one running shell runs subprocessPollTick (Manager.ts:2105-2125), which spawns `/bin/ps -eo pid=,ppid=` (Manager.ts:637-666), or powershell Get-CimInstance on Windows (Manager.ts:668-700). The rate is about 0.2/s when idle and 1/s for as long as any terminal produces output, plus 5 s after that. Long-running noisy processes (dev servers, watchers, top, TUIs) keep the 1/s rate indefinitely, so the proposal's '-1 spawn/s' is only reached when terminals are idle (-0.8/s). Persistence still rewrites the full file (up to 2 MiB) at most once per second per terminal under sustained output, not O(chunk). That matches the proposal's explicitly offered alternative and is acceptable.

Defects in the shipped fix

No defects found in the implemented fixes. The shutdown finalizer ordering is correct: the session-kill finalizer runs first, then the persist flush, before workerScope and the persist worker are torn down, and this is covered by a test. Back-off interaction checked: a foreground command ending prints a prompt, which bumps I/O, so the next 1 s tick polls. Foreground end detection, including the worktree setup-script watcher, stays at about 1 s. Only silent background-job exits are delayed by up to 5 s, which is a documented trade-off (Manager.ts:92-97). One nit: worktreeSetupProgress.ts:37 says '~1s process-table poll'. That is accurate for the cases it handles but does not mention the idle cadence.

Implementation sketch

Preferred, with no semantic change: make the poll edge-triggered instead of periodic during output. In Manager.ts, replace the ticksSinceIo scheme in subprocessPollTick (2099-2125) with explicit triggers: (1) on input or PTY start (noteTerminalIo at 1915 and 2353), poll on the next tick plus one or two follow-ups (catches false->true when a command starts); (2) on output, do not poll every tick but arm a trailing quiet timer of about 300-500 ms per manager, and poll once when output goes quiet (catches true->false because the shell prints a prompt and then goes quiet); (3) keep a slow sweep (raise DEFAULT_SUBPROCESS_IDLE_POLL_INTERVAL_MS to 10-15 s) only for silent background-job changes. Optionally skip the sweep when terminalEventListeners.size === 0, and run a fresh pollSubprocessActivity when a subscription starts or listDiagnostics is called, so headless nodes with no attached client stop spawning entirely and reattaching clients still get fresh hasRunningSubprocess. Optional spawn-free source: add an optional `snapshotFromNativeMonitor` processTableSnapshotter that maps nativeResourceMonitor.sample() (NativeResourceMonitor.ts:406) to childrenByParent when health is 'healthy' and the shell pids are in the retained set, falling back to ps or powershell. This matters most on Windows. A foreground-only variant (Linux: read /proc/<shellPid>/stat tpgid; macOS: sysctl KERN_PROC_PID e_tpgid or node-pty IPty.process behind a new optional PtyProcess.foregroundProcessGroup()) removes spawns entirely but stops detecting background jobs. Tests: extend Manager.test.ts:1431 (TestClock plus a counting processTableSnapshotter) with (a) continuous emitData for 10 ticks, asserting at most 1-2 snapshots, then quiet, asserting exactly one trailing snapshot; (b) write() followed by an activity event within 1 tick; (c) the idle sweep count at the new interval; (d) no listeners means no sweep snapshots, and subscribing triggers one. Keep watchSetupScriptTerminal behaviour covered: script starts, then ends with a prompt, and the stage settles within about 1 s. Update the comment at worktreeSetupProgress.ts:37.

Done#163 Each turn or conversation diff runs 5 git spawns (4 sequential) with no cache for immutable checkpoint pairs

gap-right-panel-first-open:checkpoint-diff-git-spawns · original impact Low, effort S · Process spawns

Current state

The fix in 60633eff3 (#710, also inside the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3) does what the proposal asked. getTurnDiff and getFullThreadDiff no longer run the 2 parallel hasCheckpointRef rev-parse calls followed by 2 sequential re-resolves. One `git cat-file --batch-check=%(objectname)` process resolves both refs (`<ref>^{commit}` on stdin), and the OIDs go straight into `git diff`. A cache miss now costs 2 spawns with a critical path of 2, down from 5 spawns with a critical path of 4. A cache hit costs 1 spawn and no `git diff`. The 32-entry / 32 MB LRU is keyed by [cwd, fromOid, toOid, ignoreWhitespace], so a ref rewritten by a revert misses instead of serving a stale patch. A scratch repo on git 2.55 confirmed the batch semantics: a missing ref or a failed peel prints one `<name> missing` line, keeping output aligned with input, and exits 0. Every server consumer goes through the cache: WS getTurnDiff/getFullThreadDiff (ws/orchestrationRpc.ts:388-405) and Agent Control threadReads.ts:522. The only remaining users of hasCheckpointRef and diffCheckpoints are in CheckpointReactor, on the turn-completion path rather than the panel-open path. No regressions found. Error semantics match the old code: a non-zero cat-file exit maps to CheckpointUnavailableError, as a failed rev-parse did. Two small leftovers, both outside the finding's scope. First, concurrent identical cache misses each run `git diff` because there is no in-flight dedup. Second, CheckpointReactor.captureAndDispatchCheckpoint (CheckpointReactor.ts:520-548) still runs a warning-only hasCheckpointRef rev-parse and then re-resolves the same from-ref inside diffCheckpoints, which is one redundant spawn per turn completion.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/checkpointing/Layers/CheckpointDiffQuery.ts:126-146 One resolveCheckpointCommits call replaces the old Effect.all of two hasCheckpointRef calls (f1be4abc7 :100-112). A null OID maps to CheckpointUnavailableError with the same detail text as before.
  • apps/server/src/checkpointing/Layers/CheckpointStore.ts:317-341 Runs one process, `cat-file --batch-check=%(objectname)`, with refs on stdin. CR/LF refs are filtered out and only FULL_COMMIT_OID lines are accepted. A scratch-repo probe confirmed that missing refs and failed peels each answer one 'missing' line and exit 0.
  • apps/server/src/checkpointing/Layers/CheckpointStore.ts:386-407 diffCheckpointCommits takes resolved OIDs and runs only `git diff --patch --minimal --no-color [--ignore-all-space]`.
  • apps/server/src/checkpointing/Layers/CheckpointDiffQuery.ts:32-48 LRUCache of 32 entries and 32 MB, keyed by JSON [cwd, fromCommitOid, toCommitOid, ignoreWhitespace].
  • apps/server/src/checkpointing/Layers/CheckpointDiffQuery.ts:154-161 Uses get-or-compute with a null-sentinel miss. packages/shared/src/lruCache.ts:18-26 returns null only for a missing key, so an empty "" diff is a valid hit. The maximum entry is 10 MB of output, about 20 MB counted at UTF-16 x2, so it fits under the byte bound.
  • apps/server/src/checkpointing/Layers/CheckpointDiffQuery.ts:180-188 getFullThreadDiff delegates to getTurnDiff, so the conversation view and Agent Control (agentControl/Mcp/threadReads.ts:522) use the same batch resolve and cache.
  • apps/server/src/checkpointing/Layers/CheckpointDiffQuery.test.ts:188-238 Tests a cache hit, a separate whitespace-flag entry, and a miss after the ref moves (diffRuns == 3). The mock store makes hasCheckpointRef and diffCheckpoints die, which proves the query path no longer uses them.
  • apps/server/src/checkpointing/Layers/CheckpointStore.test.ts:372-404 A real-git test checks that resolveCheckpointCommits returns results in input order with a missing ref in the middle, then diffs the resolved OIDs.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/CheckpointReactor.ts:520-548 Out of scope: the turn-completion path still runs a warning-only hasCheckpointRef rev-parse and then diffCheckpoints, which re-resolves the same from-ref (one redundant spawn per turn completion, ignoreWhitespace:false, so it cannot seed the default query cache).
Defects in the shipped fix

None that matter. 1) There is no in-flight dedup, so concurrent identical cache misses (two clients, or invalidation refetches racing) each run `git diff`. 2) resolveCheckpointCommits filters only CR and LF, while the old resolveCommitOid also rejected leading '-' and all control characters. A leading '-' is harmless on stdin. Other control characters could only arrive through server-generated checkpoint refs (Base64Url thread ids), so the gap is theoretical. 3) The documented trade-off stands: .gitattributes and diff config are not part of the cache key.

Done#164 Files tree fetches the whole index (≤25k entries) and re-sorts it with per-call locale options

gap-right-panel-first-open:files-tree-listentries-sort-payload · original impact Low, effort S · CPU

Current state

Confirmed DONE (landed in 60633eff3, #710). The client no longer re-sorts the listEntries result on load or refetch. The server listing sends only {path, kind}, is not sorted, and is built once per index and cached. Both tree builders (web turnDiffTree, mobile/client-runtime fileTree) sort each directory's children with a hoisted Intl.Collator, so unsorted server order is safe. The full-list client sort was redundant even before the fix, because the tree builders already sorted per directory. No consumer of listEntries depends on order or on parentPath: PreviewPanel's filter and .some() calls, the mobile ThreadFiles model, and search rows that derive parentPath from the path. Older clients are safe under version skew: at f1be4abc7 the old web client sorted itself, the old mobile tree builder sorted per directory, and no client read parentPath from listEntries. The Hub has no listEntries handling, and its vendored Ryco (7bc39eec3) contains #710.
