Done#165 Correctness: file-preview image branch can never render, and the size guard reads fields that never exist

gap-right-panel-first-open:preview-image-branch-dead · original impact Low, effort S · Reliability

Current state

Confirmed DONE. Perf PR #710 (60633eff3) fixes both parts of the finding. Raster images (png/jpg/jpeg/gif/webp) skip the text read and render from projects.readFileBinary through a revoked-on-replace blob URL. SVG uses the text read and a data: URL. The dead RichPreviewFileData casts and the sizeBytes/mimeType size guard are removed, and the server's stat-before-read cap now does the guard's job. The disabled text query cannot be revived by refetch: keyOf returns null when disabled, so refreshAsync is a no-op. That means no failing text RPC fires for raster images, including agent-touch refreshes. Browser tests cover raster, scriptable-type refusal and SVG. Some web-only gaps remain next to the fix, and the fix itself duplicates logic. Details are in fixDefects. None of them makes the image preview broken again.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/PreviewPanel.tsx:407-420 selectedImageSource = resolvePreviewImageSource(path). The text useProjectReadFile query is enabled only when selectedImageSource !== 'raster'.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/keyedQuery.ts:692-697 keyOf returns null for a disabled input, and refreshAsync(null) at :770-773 returns the initial state without fetching. The agent-touch refetch at PreviewPanel.tsx:447 therefore cannot fire a doomed text read for raster images.
  • apps/web/src/components/PreviewPanel.tsx:895-903 The image kind renders <PreviewImage> with source and refreshKey=latestSelectedFileRefreshKey. The base64-gated <img> branch is gone.
  • apps/web/src/components/PreviewImage.tsx:37-88 readFileBinary, then the isInertRasterImageMimeType check, then a Blob object URL. The previous URL is revoked after the replacement is ready and the last one on unmount. An active flag guards path-switch races.
  • apps/web/src/components/PreviewImage.tsx:95-104 SVG renders from a data: URL (opaque origin), never a blob: URL.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceFileSystem.ts:121,485-517 readStableFileBytes stats before reading and refuses files over 4 MiB cheaply. readFileBinary sniffs magic bytes (png/jpeg/gif/webp/bmp/ico/avif/heic). The client-side guard was rightly removed rather than revived.
  • apps/web/src/components/PreviewPanel.browser.tsx:350-410 Tests: a raster image renders from a blob: URL with no text read, an image/svg+xml binary result is refused, and SVG renders from a data: URL with no binary read.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/files/previewClassification.ts:42-155 The shared classifier (used by mobile, and older than both the report and the fix) has a wider raster set (avif/bmp/heic/ico/tiff), a BINARY_EXTENSIONS list, and workspaceFileReadTransport returning 'none' for known binaries. The web fix added its own parallel resolvePreviewImageSource/IMAGE_EXTENSIONS in PreviewPanel.logic.ts:3,116-122 instead of using it.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/projectPreviewAtoms.ts:76-84,147-157 runWithRetry retries every readFile failure once, including deterministic node refusals ('Binary files cannot be previewed.', 'too large'). A known-binary or oversized selection costs 2 RPCs.
  • apps/server/src/ws/RpcByteSession.ts:302-317 Over the hosted relay a response above RELAY_MAX_RPC_MESSAGE_BYTES (4 MiB, packages/contracts/src/relay.ts:49) fails only its own request with 'The response exceeded the largest message this connection can carry.' A base64 readFileBinary result passes 4 MiB at about 3 MiB raw, below the node's 4 MiB raw cap.
Defects in the shipped fix

No regressions, and the core bug is fixed. Adjacent gaps, all low impact. (1) Duplicated, diverging classification. The fix added a web-only IMAGE_EXTENSIONS/resolvePreviewImageSource (apps/web/src/components/PreviewPanel.logic.ts:3,116-122) even though @ryco/client-runtime/state/files previewClassification.ts already owns this decision for mobile. AGENTS.md calls this kind of duplication a code smell. As a result, web shows .bmp/.ico/.avif as kind 'binary': it issues a doomed text read and shows 'Binary files cannot be previewed.', although the node's readFileBinary supports these formats and mobile renders them. (2) Known binaries (zip, pdf, woff, wasm, sqlite, mp4...) still issue the text read on web (PreviewPanel.tsx:409-420). The shared workspaceFileReadTransport would return 'none' for them. The original finding mentioned 'binary kinds' as always failing. That holds only for genuinely binary files, because web's 'binary' kind also covers unknown extensions such as LICENSE, which must still be read. (3) runWithRetry (projectPreviewAtoms.ts:76-84) retries deterministic node refusals, so each doomed read is 2 RPCs, worse over the relay. (4) Over the hosted relay, raster images of roughly 3-4 MiB exceed the 4 MiB reassembled-message ceiling after base64. Their request fails with 'The response exceeded the largest message this connection can carry.' This was already true for ChatMarkdown, DiffImagePreview and mobile, and is now reachable from the preview panel. (5) Nit: a failed raster read keeps the previous blob URL (up to 4 MiB) alive until the next successful load or unmount (PreviewImage.tsx:57-64,79-85).

Partial#166 DiffPanel hashes, parses and indexes the whole patch for search synchronously in render, even when search is never opened

gap-right-panel-first-open:diff-parse-render-eager-index · original impact Low, effort S · CPU WP11

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

Three of the four proposal parts are implemented (60633eff3, 65af92766). The search index is built only while a query is active. The parse scope is the constant "diff-panel", so a theme toggle no longer re-parses. Patches of 1,000,000 chars or more parse in a worker with a main-thread fallback. The fourth part is only partly done: using a server revision as the cache key instead of hashing multi-MB strings works for local changes only. Comparison patches still hash the whole text, even though comparison.data.source.revision (a server sha256 that covers the patch and ignoreWhitespace) is already in turnScope. Checkpoint diffs carry no revision in the contract, so they hash too. The memo that is supposed to avoid re-hashing lives on the per-instance ActiveDiffParser (DiffPanel.tsx:399 useState), and DiffPanel unmounts whenever the review tab is left. So every open of the review tab, including the first open this finding is named after, still runs two full FNV passes over a checkpoint or comparison patch. That happens even when the parsed result is already in the module-level renderablePatchCache and the atom cache hands back the same string. The diffParsing.ts docstring wrongly says a remount costs only one string comparison. The residual is small: measured in Node about 1.9 ms for 800 KiB and 4.7 ms for 1.9 MiB at 1x, about 4 times that at 4x CPU.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffPanel.tsx:694-699 Search index is built only when diffSearchActive (non-empty normalized query); otherwise EMPTY_DIFF_SEARCH_INDEX. Done.
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffPanel.tsx:603-605 parseScope = DIFF_PANEL_PARSE_SCOPE (constant). resolvedTheme is not in the memo deps (645-655). Done.
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffPanel.tsx:633-638,657-677 Patches of OFF_THREAD_DIFF_PARSE_MIN_CHARS (1_000_000, diffParseOffThread.ts:8) or more parse in diffParse.worker.ts. Any failure or the 5 s watchdog falls back to an inline parse. Done.
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffPanel.tsx:623-626 blobSha is `revision:${localScope}` only for local changes. Comparisons and checkpoint diffs call activeDiffParser.identify(normalizedPatch) synchronously in render, even for patches of 1 MB or more that then go to the worker.
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffPanel.tsx:580-585,611-613 comparisonRevision already includes comparison.data.source.revision and is in turnScope, so the extra content hash is redundant for comparisons.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitComparison.ts:95-108 The comparison revision is sha256 over [mode, ref/base/head OIDs, ignoreWhitespace, patch], so it fully identifies the patch text.
  • packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:3369-3375 ThreadTurnDiff has only threadId, the turn-count range and diff. Checkpoint diffs have no server revision or OIDs, so the client must hash.
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffPanel.tsx:399 const [activeDiffParser] = useState(() => new ActiveDiffParser()). The identify memo is per mounted DiffPanelContent instance.
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:1498-1501 DiffPanel mounts only while activeMode === "review". Switching tabs or closing and reopening the panel remounts it with a new ActiveDiffParser, which loses the identify memo.
  • apps/web/src/lib/diffParsing.ts:103-113 The docstring says 'a refetch, a remount, or any re-render ... costs one string comparison'. The remount case is false because #identified is an instance field.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/providerAtoms.ts:212-213,363-375 Released checkpoint diffs are kept (8 entries / 16M chars), so a re-open gets the same data object and string, and renderablePatchCache (module-level) hits. Only the full-patch double-FNV hash is redone on every re-open.
  • apps/web/src/components/DiffPanel.identity.browser.tsx:385-420 The test covers the worker parse and the no-rehash-on-rerender case only. There is no unmount-and-remount case and no comparison case.
Remaining

The full patch text is still hashed with buildPatchCacheKey (two FNV passes plus a regex trim) synchronously in render for comparison and checkpoint patches, at DiffPanel.tsx:626 via ActiveDiffParser.identify (diffParsing.ts:109-114). (a) Comparisons: the server revision is already available (DiffPanel.tsx:584, GitComparison.ts:95) but is not used as blobSha. (b) Checkpoint diffs: the identify memo is per component instance (DiffPanel.tsx:399), so every open of the review tab re-hashes, even with a warm renderablePatchCache and an unchanged string from the atom cache. The ThreadTurnDiff contract (orchestration.ts:3369) has no revision that would let the very first open skip the hash. Cost is about 2-5 ms at 1x for 0.8-1.9 MiB patches, roughly 4 times that at 4x CPU, per open.

Defects in the shipped fix

The ActiveDiffParser.identify docstring (diffParsing.ts:103-108) says a remount re-delivering an unchanged patch costs one string comparison. The memo is an instance field of a parser created per DiffPanelContent mount (DiffPanel.tsx:399), and DiffPanel unmounts on every review-tab switch or panel close (ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:1498). So a remount re-hashes the whole patch. The browser test only checks rerender, so this gap is untested. No functional or correctness defect: the off-thread path has a full inline fallback, the local revision is a server sha256 over root and both patches (GitIndexReview.ts:288), and the cache keys stay content-correct.

Implementation sketch

1) Comparisons (client only, trivial): in DiffPanel.tsx blobSha (line 623), add a `comparing && comparison.data ? "revision:comparison"` branch. turnScope already holds JSON [environmentId, source.revision], and that revision is a server sha256 over the patch and ignoreWhitespace, so it identifies the content. 2) Remount: move the identity memo out of the per-instance ActiveDiffParser into a module-level helper in apps/web/src/lib/diffParsing.ts, either (a) a WeakMap<object, string> keyed by the checkpoint-diff result object (activeCheckpointDiffQuery.data, which lives exactly as long as its providerAtoms cache entry), or (b) a small bounded list (about 8 entries, matching MAX_INACTIVE_CHECKPOINT_DIFF_ENTRIES) of {source, key} compared with === (an O(1) pointer compare for the same atom-cached string). Keep the per-instance #previous for segment reuse. Fix the docstring. 3) Optional, to remove the first-open hash too: add an optional `revision` field to ThreadTurnDiff (packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:3369), computed on the server where the checkpoint diff is produced (sha256 over [threadId, fromTurnCount, toTurnCount, ignoreWhitespace, diff], or the from/to checkpoint commit OIDs plus ignoreWhitespace). Use `revision:${revision}` as blobSha when present and fall back to identify() for older servers. Tests: in DiffPanel.identity.browser.tsx, extend 'never re-hashes unchanged text' with unmount and a fresh render of the same patch, asserting wholePatchHashes stays 1 (0 with option 3). Add a comparison fixture asserting no whole-patch hash. Add a unit test for the module-level memo bound.

Partial#167 @-mention index: a 15 s TTL plus a 4-key cache force blocking full rebuilds (no stale-while-revalidate), and every agent turn invalidates it

gap-composer-pickers:workspace-index-swr · original impact High, effort M · Caching WP08

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

PR #710 (60633eff3) replaced the Cache.makeWith index with a per-root stale-while-revalidate store. It has single-flight builds, a global build semaphore of 2, debounced background rebuilds for hot roots, in-place patching of new files and a 300k-entry / 32-root budget. The idle (>15 s) case is fully fixed. The 'after every agent turn' case is fixed only when the root was read in the last 10 minutes. markRootChanged deletes the index of any colder root that is not refreshing, and the client re-queries only while a path menu is open, so nothing warms it again. A turn that ends more than 10 minutes after the last '@' in that checkout (common for long agent runs, and for users who rarely type '@') still makes the next '@' wait for a full cold build: 210 ms on this repo, ~0.7-0.9 s on a 60k-file repo, capped at 4 s before a tracked-files stand-in.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:1001 markRootChanged: if isHot (read within WORKSPACE_INDEX_HOT_WINDOW_MS, 10 min, :56) it calls scheduleRebuild. Otherwise, if the root is not refreshing, it runs slots.delete(slot.cwd) at :1013 and drops the index entirely.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:938 With no index, readIndex takes the cold path: startRefresh plus awaitColdIndex, which blocks the reader on the full build for up to WORKSPACE_INDEX_COLD_BUILD_DEADLINE_MS (4 s, :64). This is the cost the finding wanted removed after agent turns.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/CheckpointReactor.ts:540 invalidate runs once per turn completion, inside captureAndDispatchCheckpoint (called from :686 and :743). The hot window counts from the last '@' read, not from turn start, so turns longer than 10 minutes always hit the drop branch.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/projectAtoms.ts:485 invalidateProjectSearchEntries only re-requests a scope when observerCount > 0 (:501-503), and useProject.ts:33-36 says only an open path menu observes. Nothing re-warms a dropped server index after a turn.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:1012 The policy is inconsistent. A cold root that happens to be refreshing keeps its dirty index, and later reads serve it immediately with superseded=true. A root idle for hours without an invalidation is also served instantly (:928-936). Only a cold root invalidated while idle is dropped.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:918 Confirms the auditor: readIndex returns slot.index without waiting. It starts a background startRefresh when the index is dirty or older than 15 s (:51) and reports superseded for dirty or degraded indexes.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:813 Confirms the auditor: startRefresh is single-flight per root and runRefresh holds buildPermits (Semaphore of 2, :696, :774). runRefresh re-schedules when an invalidation raced the build (:785). Note: startDegradedBuild (:864) runs outside the permits, apparently on purpose.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:1025 recordFileWrite patches new files and their missing ancestors in place, then calls markRootChanged. For a cold root that same call drops the patched index right away.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:728 enforceBudget (300k entries at :70, 32 roots at :71, evicts by lastReadAt) already bounds memory. Dropping cold roots on invalidate is not needed for memory.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.index.test.ts:236 The tests cover burst collapse (:236), non-blocking age revalidation (:267), write patching (:293), single-flight cold reads (:347) and the budget (:516). No test covers invalidating a root outside the hot window.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:557 The cold build is cheaper now (3 concurrent ls-files, no check-ignore chunks), but it still blocks in the residual case.
Remaining

apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:1010-1014: markRootChanged deletes the index of a root that is not hot (no read in 10 min, :56) and not refreshing. CheckpointReactor.ts:540 invalidates at every turn completion, and the web client re-requests only for open path menus (projectAtoms.ts:501-503). So the first '@' after any turn that ended more than 10 minutes after that checkout's last '@' read goes through the cold path (readIndex :938-946) and blocks on a full rebuild (210 ms here, ~0.7-0.9 s on 60k files, up to the 4 s deadline). That is the 'after every agent turn' cost the finding targeted, now limited to long turns and occasional '@' users. Lower-value leftovers from the proposal: (a) no fs.watch or .git/index+HEAD mtime revalidation, so external changes such as a terminal git checkout are seen only by the first read past 15 s; (b) answers from an index that is only age-stale are not flagged refreshing, so the client caches them for 15 s (DEFAULT_PROJECT_SEARCH_ENTRIES_STALE_TIME_MS) while the server is already replacing the index.

Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness bugs found in the SWR store. The generation, refreshing and refreshDone handshakes, slot-identity checks in scheduleRebuild and startDegradedBuild, and budget eviction (skips refreshing slots) hold up. Minor: (1) the cold-root drop described in 'remaining' makes the in-place patch in recordFileWrite useless for cold roots. (2) A write that races a running refresh can briefly lose the patched file when the refresh publishes a listing taken before the write. The generation bump keeps the slot dirty and a hot root rebuilds 250 ms later, so it is only a short flicker while reads are flagged refreshing. (3) recordFileWrite scans index.entries linearly (up to 200k) per user write. That is negligible at the rate users write. (4) startDegradedBuild runs outside buildPermits, so more than 2 git listings can run at once during a slow cold build. This looks intentional.

Implementation sketch

1) apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts markRootChanged (:1001): remove the `else if (!slot.refreshing) slots.delete(slot.cwd)` branch. A cold root keeps its index with dirty=true and generation bumped, and no rebuild is scheduled, so it costs no git work. readIndex (:928-936) already returns that index immediately with superseded=true and calls startRefresh with no debounce. The client already shows the answer without caching it and re-asks every 400 ms up to 5 times (projectAtoms.ts scheduleRefreshingRefetch :302), so the menu settles on the rebuilt index in about a second. listEntries already waits through awaitPendingChanges for dirty roots (:1288), so the files tree stays fresh. Memory stays bounded by enforceBudget. If very old cold indexes are a concern, drop only when `now - index.builtAt` exceeds a generous cap such as 1 h. 2) Optional: in readIndex, also report superseded when this read started an age-based revalidation, so the client does not cache an answer the server is already replacing. This costs at most 5 extra small requests per 15 s of typing. 3) Optional freshness work: stat the repository metadataPath (`.git/index`, `HEAD`, available from VcsDriverRegistry.detect) on read and mark the slot dirty when an mtime changes. Keep the 15 s age revalidation, because untracked files do not touch .git/index. 4) Tests in apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.index.test.ts: search a root, TestClock.adjust(10 * 60_000 + 1), change the fake listing, invalidate, then expect search to return the old entries immediately with refreshing: true, the build count to rise by exactly 1 (started by the read), and after settle the new entries without refreshing. Also add a recordFileWrite-on-cold-root case where the patched file is visible immediately.

Value medium · effort S · risk low

Done#168 The '#' issue/PR picker loads the heaviest PR list (comments, statusCheckRollup, stack GraphQL), and per-surface limits split the cache

gap-composer-pickers:composer-hash-pr-list-heavy · original impact High, effort M · Network / RTT WP08

Current state

I confirmed DONE for the composer '#' path. Commit 0c0d9eafc added view "picker". The composer asks for it (ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:158-165), and the server answers from the lean change-request index or a lean gh call, with no checks, comment bodies, mergeable or stacks (sourceControlRpc.ts:275-302). Commit 60633eff3 added the 100-row client superset, so the cache key no longer includes the limit (sourceControlAtoms.ts:262-381). Both full PR and issue lists are now one GraphQL request each, with comments{totalCount} and stacks in the same request (gitHubRepositoryLists.ts:49-58, 153-167). The chip is attached at once from the summary (ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:382-441). All four parts of the proposal landed. The leftovers are small: (1) ContextPickerPopup still reads full rows, and its comment wrongly says it shares rows with the '#' picker. (2) Sending before the background detail arrives triggers a second, non-joined detail RPC, because the send path uses a different client cache. (3) The picker's index rows can show stale titles after an edit. (4) Search fallbacks still use the heavy gh --json comments field sets plus a stack GraphQL.

Evidence
  • packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:1200-1218 listChangeRequests payload has view: optional Literals(["picker"]). Older servers ignore it.
  • apps/server/src/ws/sourceControlRpc.ts:275-302 listPickerChangeRequests: open and all scopes come from gitWorkflow.indexedChangeRequests. Otherwise provider.listChangeRequests runs with fields "summary" and includeStackSummary:false.

  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/gitHubRepositoryLists.ts:49-58 PULL_REQUEST_ROW_FIELDS uses comments { totalCount }. GITHUB_ISSUE_LIST_QUERY (153-167) does the same for issues, used by GitHubCli.listIssues (1432-1439).

  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ContextPickerPopup.tsx:17-47 Leftover: the paperclip 'Add context' picker requests the open PR list without view "picker", so it gets full rows. The comment on line 17 ('Same rows as the composer # picker') has been false since 0c0d9eafc split the keys. Proposal (a) explicitly named this component.
  • apps/web/src/hooks/chatSendShared.ts:102-135 New defect: the send-time refresh of a stale context uses queryClient.fetchQuery with issueDetailQueryOptions/changeRequestDetailQueryOptions (lib/sourceControlContextRpc.ts:201-234, 370-403). That is a separate client cache from the detailCache (sourceControlAtoms.ts:1136, 1176-1240) used by the background fetch. A send during the roughly 1 s detail window therefore starts a second, non-joined getChangeRequestDetail. The server does not dedupe it (sourceControlRpc.ts:585-604), and the send waits for it.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.logic.ts:317-336 On fetch failure the original context is kept. If both the background and send-time fetches fail, the stub (body "", comments []) is sent.
  • apps/server/src/ws/sourceControlRpc.ts:43-56,240-247,859-868 Title-only edits (action edit without baseRefName) only call invalidateRepositoryLists (list cache), not the change-request index (60 s TTL, pullRequestIndex.ts:22). The '#' picker re-reads the stale index and can show the old title for up to about 60 s, while full lists show the new one.
Defects in the shipped fix

Minor, low-impact leftovers and defects. (1) ContextPickerPopup.tsx:42-47 still requests full open-PR rows (checks contexts first:100 per PR, labels, assignees, stacks in the GraphQL request) for a list that shows only number and title. Its comment on line 17 says it shares rows with the composer '#' picker, which has been false since 0c0d9eafc. It does share the full superset with the overview, PR page, branch selector and create dialog, so the extra cost appears only on a cold open. (2) chatSendShared.ts:102-135 refreshes stale contexts through the ~/rpc/queryClient cache. The chip's background fetch uses sourceControlAtoms' detailCache instead. A send within the detail window after picking therefore makes a duplicate, non-joined gh pr view or issue view (about 1 s), and the send waits for it. This race was introduced by the chip-first change. (3) If both fetches fail, the empty-body summary stub is sent silently (ChatView.logic.ts:326-333). This is the same pattern as proposal (c), on paths outside the core '#' flow.

Implementation sketch

(1) In apps/web/src/components/chat/ContextPickerPopup.tsx, pass view: "picker" to useSourceControlChangeRequestList and fix the comment on line 17. That makes the popup share the composer's picker key, served from the warm index or a lean gh call. Update ContextPickerPopup.browser.tsx expectations. (2) In apps/web/src/hooks/chatSendShared.ts createSourceControlContextFetcher, call fetchSourceControlIssueDetail / fetchSourceControlChangeRequestDetail from ~/rpc/useSourceControl (the detailCache, which joins in-flight reads) instead of queryClient.fetchQuery(issueDetailQueryOptions / changeRequestDetailQueryOptions). This joins the chip's in-flight background read and removes one of two caches for the same data. Then check whether issueDetailQueryOptions/changeRequestDetailQueryOptions in lib/sourceControlContextRpc.ts still have other users, and fold them onto detailCache if not. Add a unit test: pick, then send immediately, and assert exactly one getChangeRequestDetail call. Done#169 The 25,000-entry cap is applied after an alphabetical sort, so most files in large repos can never be found (correctness)

gap-composer-pickers:index-truncation-hides-files · original impact High, effort M · Reliability

Current state

Confirmed DONE. #710 (60633eff3, also in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3) removed the alphabetical dirs-then-files slice(0, 25_000). The search corpus is now every listed path, capped at 200k per VCS root; past that cap, shallower paths are kept. The 25k cap now applies only to the listEntries payload (shallowest entries). The ls-files byte cap went from 16 to 32 MiB, and truncation flows into index.partial. search() returns partial, the web client stops narrowing partial results from its cache, and the @ menu shows 'Showing results from part of the workspace.' both under results and under an empty result. A regression test with 30k files finds the last file. I found no correctness hole in the composer picker path. What is left are small follow-ups and policy nits, listed under fixDefects.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:76 WORKSPACE_INDEX_MAX_ENTRIES = 200_000 is the search corpus cap, separate from WORKSPACE_LIST_ENTRIES_MAX = 25_000 (line 80). The global budget is 300k entries across 32 roots (lines 70-71); the old code allowed 4 roots of 25k each.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:484 indexListedFiles does not sort. It builds every file plus its ancestor directories and calls selectShallowestFiles only when the total exceeds 200k (lines 504-511), setting partial in that case.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:177 selectShallowestFiles: buckets by depth, keeps listing order within a depth (tracked before untracked), and stops at the budget. Depth takes priority over tracked status.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:226 buildWorkspaceListing caps only the listEntries payload, using selectShallowestEntries. The kept set is a consistent tree, because parents are always shallower than their children.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:1264 search() ranks all index.entries and returns truncated = partial || matchedCount > limit, plus partial: true when the index is partial.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:546 The listing's truncated flag (or tracked-only mode) is passed in as index partial.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:318 WORKSPACE_FILES_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES = 32 MiB, applied to each of the three concurrent ls-files runs. listWorkspaceFiles (line 557) emits tracked paths before untracked ones and ORs the truncated flags.
  • packages/contracts/src/project.ts:63 ProjectSearchEntriesResult.partial is an optional boolean.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/projectAtoms.ts:272 narrowFromCache refuses to narrow a cached prefix result that is truncated or partial, so local narrowing cannot hide files.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:313 pathResults.partial is passed to resolveComposerPathMenuEmptyState (composerPathMenu.ts:73). ComposerCommandMenu.tsx:236-249 renders the footnote under an empty result and under the result list.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.index.test.ts:106 Regression test: 30k files, the last file is found, partial is undefined, and the listEntries payload is capped at 25k with shallow-first ordering. Lines 399-460 cover partial for the tracked-files fallback and stand-in. No test covers the 200k selectShallowestFiles path or listing.truncated -> partial.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:643 The non-VCS filesystem fallback still stops at 25k entries in BFS order. It is now shallow-first like the VCS path and flagged partial, but its search corpus is still limited to 25k.
Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness defect in the composer picker fix. Minor points: (1) Policy nit: past 200k entries, selectShallowestFiles (WorkspaceEntries.ts:177-199) lets depth beat tracked status. A repo with a huge untracked, non-ignored, shallow directory (data dumps, un-ignored venv or vendored SDK) can fill the cap with untracked files and drop deep tracked sources. The proposal asked for tracked before untracked. (2) Perf cost of the fix: search() ranks the whole corpus in one synchronous loop with no yield (WorkspaceEntries.ts:1268). On 200k synthetic paths (average 57 chars) rankWorkspaceEntries took about 18-42 ms per query on this machine, roughly 8x the old 25k cost. Short queries come back truncated, so the client cannot narrow them and every keystroke reaches the server. The build path is also only partly chunked: selectShallowestFiles plus entry construction took about 60 ms unyielded for a 450k listing (lines 504-519). The heap cost is about 33 MB per 200k-entry root, bounded by the 300k global budget. (3) The non-VCS fallback corpus is still 25k (line 78), flagged partial. (4) No test covers the 200k cap or the listing.truncated -> partial path. (5) Adjacent, outside the composer: the PreviewPanel filter is limited to the listEntries payload, and the mobile files search footer ignores partial.

Current state

Fixed in 60633eff3 (#710), which is in HEAD and in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3. GitVcsDriver.listWorkspaceFiles now runs `ls-files --cached`, `ls-files --cached --ignored --exclude-standard` and `ls-files --others --exclude-standard` concurrently and subtracts the tracked-but-ignored set. WorkspaceEntries no longer calls filterIgnoredPaths/check-ignore anywhere, and the K-chunk retry is gone. The old readdir-walk fallback inside a work tree, which also ran check-ignore (old line 479), was removed too. A failed full listing now falls back to one cheap tracked-only listing. listWorkspaceFiles has a single production caller (WorkspaceEntries), and git is the only registered VcsDriver, so no other path still pays for check-ignore. I ran a read-only equivalence check on this repo: old pipeline (ls-files -co then check-ignore) and new pipeline (-c minus -ci, plus -o) both gave 7678 paths, as identical sets.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:552-588 listWorkspaceFiles: three concurrent ls-files runs (Effect.all, concurrency unbounded, fail-fast). Tracked paths in the --cached --ignored set are dropped and adjacent unmerged-stage duplicates are deduped. trackedOnly skips the untracked walk.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:528-547 listVcsIndex passes driver.listWorkspaceFiles output straight to indexListedFiles. No check-ignore step.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:668-688 buildWorkspaceIndex: if the full listing fails, it retries once with the tracked-only listing (2 cheap ls-files runs), replacing the old filterVcsIgnoredPaths K-chunk retry (old 359-362).
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:59-64,859-885,889-903 Two-phase build exists, but only as a deadline fallback. Readers wait up to WORKSPACE_INDEX_COLD_BUILD_DEADLINE_MS = 4000 for the full build, and only then is a tracked-only stand-in listed and published. It is not the proposal's 'answer first from ls-files -c (~30 ms), then merge -o'.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:318 WORKSPACE_FILES_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES is 32 MiB per ls-files run (raised from 16 MiB in the same commit), not 16 MiB as the auditor said.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:348,631-676; apps/server/src/vcs/VcsDriver.ts:34 filterIgnoredPaths and chunkPathsForGitCheckIgnore remain as dead API. Their only callers are tests and VcsDriverContractHarness.ts:141,158.

  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.test.ts:220-237 This contract test uses `.convex/`, which IGNORED_DIRECTORY_NAMES (WorkspaceEntries.ts:84-94) already strips by first segment. It would pass even without the -ci subtraction, so only the driver-level test exercises git-ignore subtraction.

Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defects found. Minor notes, none blocking: (1) The auditor's 'matches the optional proposal part' overstates it. The tracked-only stand-in only starts after the 4 s cold-build deadline (WorkspaceEntries.ts:64,889-903), so the report's 'first results in about 30 ms' is not realized for normal repos. The first cold '@' still waits for the untracked walk (~45-50 ms here, ~165-210 ms at 60k files). It is still well below the old check-ignore cost, and the proposal marked this part optional. (2) Past the deadline, startDegradedBuild re-spawns `ls-files --cached` and `--cached --ignored` (WorkspaceEntries.ts:878 -> GitVcsDriver.ts:562-563), although the still-running full build has usually already finished those two runs. That is two redundant processes, only on >4 s cold builds. (3) The output cap is 32 MiB, not 16 MiB. A truncated `--cached --ignored` run could leak a few ignored tracked paths, which is negligible. (4) The WorkspaceEntries-level test 'excludes tracked paths that match ignore rules' is weak: `.convex` is already in IGNORED_DIRECTORY_NAMES. (5) filterIgnoredPaths and chunkPathsForGitCheckIgnore are dead outside tests.

Done#171 Bare '@' sends nothing and says 'No matching files'; the cold build starts only after the first character plus 120 ms, and errors show as 'no matches'

gap-composer-pickers:prewarm-on-at · original impact Medium, effort S · Waterfall WP08

Current state

Independently confirmed DONE (commit 60633eff3, #710). The contract now accepts an empty query (TrimmedString, max 256). The server ranks an empty query by depth, directories first, and marks the result truncated when more than the limit matched, so the client never wrongly narrows from a partial bare listing. The client sends the bare-'@' request at once, without the debounce, when the server advertises capabilities.projectSearchEmptyQuery. That request warms the single-flight server index while the user types. The menu shows 'Indexing workspace…' or 'Searching workspace files…' while loading, 'Couldn't search workspace files.' with a Retry button on failure, and a footnote for partial results. A typed query's results never stand in for the bare listing. Unit tests and browser tests cover both the capable-server and legacy-server paths. Not done: the optional prewarm on composer focus (onComposerIntent only prewarms the provider session). That part was optional, and adding it carries a server-load cost: any read of an index older than 15 s starts a background rebuild. Minor fix defect: during the debounce window after a bare '@', the bare listing still stands in for the typed character (see fixDefects).

Evidence
  • packages/contracts/src/project.ts:38 ProjectSearchEntriesInput.query is TrimmedString with max length 256. Its comment says an empty query lists the shallowest entries and warms the index.
  • packages/contracts/src/environment.ts:72 Declares projectSearchEmptyQuery as an optional capability. The server sets it to true at apps/server/src/environment/Layers/ServerEnvironment.ts:104, and the hosted descriptor field-set test is updated (apps/server/src/agentControl/Mcp/hostedBoundaries.test.ts:54).
  • packages/shared/src/workspaceEntrySearch.ts:62 scoreWorkspaceEntry scores an empty query by depth*2 plus 1 for files. The server search at apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:1264-1279 sets truncated = index.partial || matchedCount > limit, so a bare listing of a workspace with more than 80 entries is never used by narrowFromCache (apps/web/src/rpc/projectAtoms.ts:262-289).
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:917 readIndex is single-flight: only the first read of a root waits, for at most the cold-build deadline. Later typed queries reuse the build the bare-'@' request started.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/projectAtoms.ts:150 resolveInput no longer requires query.length > 0. commitError (lines 227-236) records the error, and the state exposes dataQuery and error.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:124 effectivePathQuery uses the raw query for a bare '@' (no debounce) and for queries answerable from the cache. Otherwise it uses the trailing-only debounced value. @tanstack/pacer 0.22.0 defaults to leading:false, trailing:true.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:141 The check that keeps a stale bare listing out (isRelatedPathQuery) compares against normalizedEffectivePathQuery, the debounced value, not the typed pathTriggerQuery. That is the source of the minor defect.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/composerPathMenu.ts:39 The design intent is in the comment: 'nothing stands in between the bare trigger's listing and a typed search'. The code breaks this for about 120 ms after the first typed character.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:302 isComposerMenuLoading covers a debounce in progress and any bare or typed request while it is loading or fetching. The empty state comes from resolveComposerPathMenuEmptyState (composerPathMenu.ts:54-77) and is rendered by ComposerCommandMenu.tsx:208-256: error row with Retry, loading text, and footnote.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx:1925 Enter or Tab with the menu open selects activeComposerMenuItem, or else items[0]. During the debounce window that is the first entry of the unfiltered bare listing, which may not match the typed character.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:5258 onComposerIntent only prewarms the provider session. The optional workspace-index prewarm on composer focus was not implemented.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.Composer.browser.tsx:1482 Browser tests check both paths: a legacy server sends no empty query and shows 'Type to search files and folders.', and a capable server lists the workspace for a bare '@'. Unit tests are in apps/web/src/components/chat/composerPathMenu.test.ts.
Defects in the shipped fix

Minor, low severity. In apps/web/src/components/chat/ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:141-146, the check that keeps the bare listing from standing in for a typed search compares against normalizedEffectivePathQuery, the trailing debounced value. Take a workspace with more than 80 entries, so the bare listing is truncated and cannot be narrowed locally. After a bare '@' has shown its listing, typing the first character (e.g. '@s') leaves effectivePathQuery at '' for 120 ms. During that window: (1) the menu keeps showing the unfiltered top-level listing for a query it does not answer; (2) Enter or Tab (ChatComposer.tsx:1925-1935) inserts the first listing entry (e.g. '.github/') instead of a match for 's'; (3) when the debounce fires, the listing turns into an empty 'Searching workspace files…' row for one round trip, then the results appear. So the menu flickers listing → blank → results, which typed-to-typed transitions do not. Not a perf regression. The optional composer-focus prewarm (ChatView.tsx:5258) was also not implemented. It was optional, so it is not a defect.

Implementation sketch

Defect fix in useComposerAttachmentMenus (apps/web/src/components/chat/ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx). Base the empty-versus-typed decision on what the user typed. Option A (minimal, matches the stated design): when pathTriggerQuery is non-empty and workspaceEntriesQuery.dataQuery === '', treat the data as unrelated, i.e. pathResults = isRelatedPathQuery(dataQuery, normalizedEffectivePathQuery) && !(dataQuery === '' && normalizeWorkspaceEntryQuery(pathTriggerQuery).length > 0) ? data : null. Simpler: pass normalizeWorkspaceEntryQuery(pathTriggerQuery) as the second argument when one side is empty. The menu then shows the 'Searching workspace files…' loading row during the debounce, and Enter/Tab have no stale item to select. Option B (smoother, no flicker): when dataQuery === '' and the typed query is non-empty, rank the cached bare listing locally with rankWorkspaceEntries(listing, typedQuery, limit) from @ryco/shared/workspaceEntrySearch and show that subset as an interim stand-in until the real result commits. Every shown item then matches the typed query, and the menu goes straight from listing to matching subset to full results. If B is chosen, update the composerPathMenu.ts:39 comment. Tests: add a browser case in apps/web/src/components/ChatView.Composer.browser.tsx under 'bare @ workspace listing'. Use a capable server whose resolveSearch returns more than 80 entries or truncated:true for '' and a distinct entry for 's'. Fill '@', wait for the listing, then fill '@s' and assert at once that the listing's first item id is not rendered (A) or that only matching items are (B). Optional, separate, product trade-off: workspace-index prewarm on composer focus. In ChatView.tsx's prewarmProviderSessionRef or a sibling ref, call requestProjectSearchEntries({environmentId, cwd: gitCwd, query: '', limit: 80}) when gitCwd is non-null, the capability is advertised and dispatch is allowed. The 15 s client staleTime dedupes repeat focuses. Caveat: on the server, any read of an index older than WORKSPACE_INDEX_REVALIDATE_AFTER_MS (15 s, WorkspaceEntries.ts:51) starts a background rebuild. A focus prewarm would therefore add rebuild churn for users who never type '@'. Measure that before shipping.

Done#172 A cold index build runs about 100-130 ms of synchronous JS on the server event loop (60k files), and about 80% of it is avoidable

gap-composer-pickers:index-build-event-loop-block · original impact Medium, effort S · CPU WP08

Current state

Confirmed DONE (60633eff3, #710; the addDirectoryAncestors, WORKSPACE_INDEX_BUILD_CHUNK and selectShallowestFiles symbols all landed there). Every cost the finding names is gone. (1) isPathInIgnoredDirectory uses indexOf+slice. (2) directoryAncestorsOf is replaced by a lastIndexOf walk that stops at the first known parent. (3) The redundant per-ancestor ignore check is dropped. (4) Both localeCompare sorts are removed; the index and the listing are unsorted and the cap uses depth buckets. The build is also chunked: Effect.yieldNow runs every 20k paths. In effect 4.0.2 that goes through MixedScheduler.setImmediate (a macrotask, not a microtask), so pending WebSocket I/O really does run between chunks. I replayed the new code path on 61k synthetic paths (this repo's tracked list x8, node 24). The longest chunk took 3-5 ms, the whole loop 10-13 ms, entry construction 2-6 ms, and the first cached listEntries payload 4-5 ms. The finding measured 104-127 ms of one block, so it no longer applies. I checked the code-unit/no-sort risk: every listEntries consumer is order-independent. The web side (ChangedFilesTree via buildTurnDiffTree) and mobile (client-runtime buildWorkspaceFileTree) each sort per directory with a cached Intl.Collator, and search tie-breaks on path. I found no correctness defect in the fix. The one leftover is minor and only hits repos past the new 200k-entry cap: after the chunked loop, selectShallowestFiles and entry construction run as one unchunked block.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:151 isPathInIgnoredDirectory: first segment via indexOf/slice, no split.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:161 addDirectoryAncestors: lastIndexOf walk, deepest first, returns at the first directory already in the set. Every caller passes a set built only by this function (indexListedFiles, selectShallowestFiles, recordFileWrite's fresh missingDirectories), so the early-exit invariant holds.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:484 indexListedFiles: one filter + ancestor pass with no ancestor ignore check and no sort. The loop at 490-502 yields with Effect.yieldNow between WORKSPACE_INDEX_BUILD_CHUNK (line 82, 20_000) slices.
  • apps/server/node_modules/effect/src/Scheduler.ts:176 effect 4.0.2: the default MixedScheduler in async mode dispatches yieldNow via setImmediate. The yield is a real event-loop turn, so I/O callbacks run between chunks.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:505 Only past WORKSPACE_INDEX_MAX_ENTRIES (line 76, 200_000; the auditor cited line 69): selectShallowestFiles (177-199) depth-bucket selection. It is unchunked, then entries are built in an unchunked loop (513-519).
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:226 buildWorkspaceListing: unsorted shallowest-first payload, cached on index.listing (line 1293). About 5 ms at 65k entries and 13-16 ms at 212k in my replay.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/useProjectPreview.ts:20 Documents order-independence. Confirmed: apps/web/src/lib/turnDiffTree.ts:92/105 and packages/client-runtime/src/state/files/fileTree.ts:61-64 sort each directory with a cached Intl.Collator.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:557 listWorkspaceFiles now uses three ls-files calls and no check-ignore. The listing side adds no new per-path sync hot spot: adjacent-dedupe plus push.
Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness defects or regressions. One minor gap: the chunking covers only the per-path loop. When a repo exceeds WORKSPACE_INDEX_MAX_ENTRIES (200k), WorkspaceEntries.ts:505-519 runs selectShallowestFiles over every listed path and then builds all 200k entries (toLowerCase each) in one synchronous block. On 537k synthetic paths I measured 48-75 ms for the selection plus 7-23 ms for entries, about 60-90 ms in one block. That case only applies to giant monorepos, which the old code took about 1 s to index, so it is a small leftover, not a failure of this fix. A related but separate point: raising the cap from 25k to 200k (the fix for finding 169) means rankWorkspaceEntries scans up to 200k entries per server search. I measured about 10-12 ms at 61k and 35-48 ms at 200k per keystroke, which is a different code path. There is no test of the over-cap path (selectShallowestFiles); the largest index test uses 30k paths.

Done#173 A slow or failing git ls-files waits 20 s, then silently falls back to a whole-tree filesystem walk that runs check-ignore at every level

gap-composer-pickers:ls-files-timeout-fallback · original impact Low, effort S · Reliability WP08

Current state

The bug as described is gone in 60633eff3 (#710). A slow or failing `git ls-files` no longer leads to a readdir walk with check-ignore at every level. Cold '@' reads wait at most 4 s and then get a tracked-only stand-in flagged partial/refreshing, which the full build replaces in the background. Inside a detected work tree there is no readdir walk and no check-ignore. A failed full listing falls back to tracked files. Total failures back off for 5 s, warnings are logged, and the web menu shows partial and error states with a retry and re-asks refreshing answers. All the auditor's evidence and line numbers check out. One correction to the residual: the stand-in is not the index-only `ls-files -c` the finding measured at 28-32 ms. trackedOnly mode also waits on `ls-files --cached --ignored --exclude-standard`, which opens `<dir>/.gitignore` in every tracked directory. That listing is fast on local disks but scales with directory count on slow or network volumes, one of the finding's named triggers. So the 4 s bound holds for huge untracked trees on fast disks, but on very slow volumes the stand-in can arrive late, or time out and leave readers parked for about 40 s before an error.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:64 WORKSPACE_INDEX_COLD_BUILD_DEADLINE_MS = 4_000. awaitColdIndex (887-906) waits for the full build with Effect.timeoutOption, then starts the degraded build.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:864 startDegradedBuild runs listVcsIndex(..., 'tracked') in the background with no build permit and logs a warning with cwd and deadlineMs. Its failure is swallowed by Effect.option (878), so readers are not told.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:905 After the deadline the reader does an unbounded `Deferred.await(waiters)`. With no stand-in it waits for the full build's outcome, including the tracked retry in buildWorkspaceIndex (675-687): up to 20 s + 20 s.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:668 buildWorkspaceIndex: a VCS root never walks the tree, and a failed full listing falls back to tracked files with a log. The walk (583) runs only when detectVcsDriver returns null and has no check-ignore.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:560 trackedOnly still runs `--cached` and `--cached --ignored --exclude-standard` together, and Effect.all waits for both. The second loads per-directory .gitignore from the work tree (git prep_exclude/add_patterns open() per directory), so the stand-in is not index-only. Locally on ryco (7.7k files, 475 dirs): -c 0.01 s, -c -i 0.03 s, --others 0.02 s.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:529 Every ls-files, the stand-in's included, uses the shared WORKSPACE_FILES_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000 (319).
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:631 filterIgnoredPaths (chunked check-ignore) has no production callers left. Only VcsDriverContractHarness uses it.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsDriverRegistry.ts:146 Pre-existing, unchanged: a failed detection (rev-parse over its 5 s timeout, GitVcsDriver.ts:503) is cached with TTL 0 and mapped to null by detectVcsDriver (WorkspaceEntries.ts:549). That still sends a git work tree on a hung volume to the readdir walk, which has no deadline. Narrow.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:704 isBackingOff with WORKSPACE_INDEX_FAILURE_RETRY_MS = 5_000 (66). readIndex (938) returns the cached failure. Covered by the test at WorkspaceEntries.index.test.ts:481.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:1274 search() returns partial and refreshing (contracts project.ts:63,70).
  • apps/web/src/rpc/projectAtoms.ts:354 The web client does not cache refreshing answers and re-asks them up to 5 times at 400 ms (constants at 27-28), so the full index replaces the stand-in in the menu.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/composerPathMenu.ts:68 'Couldn't search workspace files.' with a retry (70), the partial footnote (73), and 'Indexing workspace…' while the first build runs.
Defects in the shipped fix

Narrow, slow-volume only. (1) The stand-in and fallback 'tracked' listing (GitVcsDriver.ts:560-569) also waits on `ls-files --cached --ignored --exclude-standard`. That opens .gitignore in every tracked directory, so it is not the index-only `ls-files -c` that WorkspaceEntries.ts:60-62 documents and the finding measured. On network or cloud volumes it scales with directory round-trips. If it passes 20 s, the stand-in fails silently (WorkspaceEntries.ts:878) and the tracked fallback fails too, so a cold '@' waits about 40 s (WorkspaceEntries.ts:905) and then errors, retried every 5 s. An index-only listing would have answered in milliseconds. (2) The same unbounded second wait applies when git hangs outright (auditor's residual). (3) Minor background cost: if the full listing keeps timing out, every revalidation (on read, at least 15 s after the last build) runs another doomed 20 s `--others` scan, then a second tracked listing, although the stand-in already holds that data. (4) Pre-existing, unchanged: a detection timeout (rev-parse over 5 s) still sends a git work tree to the deadline-free readdir walk. On huge untracked trees on fast disks, the finding's other trigger, the fix fully bounds latency.

Implementation sketch

Optional hardening, small: (a) GitVcsDriver.listWorkspaceFiles: in trackedOnly mode, give `--cached` a short timeout (e.g. 5 s), and run `--cached --ignored --exclude-standard` with a short timeout (about 1.5 s) or skip it, treating a timeout as no ignored-tracked paths. The result is already flagged partial, so a rare force-added ignored file showing briefly is harmless. With a short timeout, the existing test 'lists only tracked files when asked' (GitVcsDriver.listWorkspaceFiles.test.ts:66) stays valid. Fix the WorkspaceEntries.ts:60-62 comment either way. (b) WorkspaceEntries.awaitColdIndex: bound the second `Deferred.await(waiters)` (e.g. another 4-6 s). Past that, fail this reader with a WorkspaceEntriesError such as 'still indexing' without writing slot.failure, so the menu shows 'Couldn't search workspace files' with a retry that joins the in-flight single-flight build. Or have startDegradedBuild complete a per-refresh 'degradedFailed' deferred that the reader races. (c) buildWorkspaceIndex: when the full listing fails and a stand-in for the same generation is already in slot.index, reuse it instead of re-listing. Optionally remember a full-listing timeout per slot for a few minutes and skip repeat `--others` scans on revalidation. Tests in WorkspaceEntries.index.test.ts using the existing fake driver and TestClock: full listing Effect.never plus trackedOnly Effect.never makes the cold search settle by about 10 s; trackedOnly ignored-listing slow still yields a stand-in at about 4 s; full listing fails after the stand-in is published means no second tracked call.

Partial#174 The client @-search cache never evicts and never reuses earlier results; every keystroke is a 9-12 KB round trip after a fixed 120 ms debounce

gap-composer-pickers:client-search-cache-unbounded · original impact Low, effort S · Memory decision

Current state

Confirmed PARTIAL. 60633eff3 (#710) replaced the per-scope Map with an LRUCache (64 queries, 2 MiB). It also added exact local narrowing: when a fresh, complete (not truncated, not partial) result exists for a prefix, the query is reranked on the client with the same shared rankWorkspaceEntries the server uses, and the composer skips its 120 ms debounce for it. I checked that narrowing is exact. Every match tier implies a subsequence match, the server indexes with normalizedPath = path.toLowerCase(), the tie-break is the path, and the limit is the scope's limit. Pre-fix servers used the same predicate and scoring for non-empty queries, so they stay compatible. Results flagged refreshing are never cached. No Hub-side or alternative implementation exists; the Hub vendors Ryco 7bc39eec3, which already contains 60633eff3. Still missing: proposal 3 (the listEntries or relay-local search, a shorter debounce, and a server-pushed index-change invalidation). Also missing is a small part of proposal 1: entries older than staleTime are never dropped. They are only evicted under LRU pressure within the same scope. Scope runtimes are never pruned outside hosted teardown, so total memory is bounded per scope but not across scopes.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/rpc/projectAtoms.ts:20 PROJECT_SEARCH_ENTRIES_CACHE_MAX_QUERIES = 64 and MAX_BYTES = 2 MiB (line 21). LRUCache is built at 180-183, and writes at 355 and 404 pass estimateResultBytes (238).
  • apps/web/src/rpc/projectAtoms.ts:246 readFreshCacheEntry treats entries older than staleTime (15 s) as misses but never deletes them. Only LRU pressure from a new insert into the same scope evicts them.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/projectAtoms.ts:262 narrowFromCache walks prefixes from longest to shortest, including the empty query. It stops if the nearest fresh prefix is truncated or partial, reranks with the shared ranker otherwise, and keeps the prefix's fetchedAt, so freshness is not extended.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/projectAtoms.ts:399 requestProjectSearchEntries tries the exact cache, then narrowing, then the server. A local answer bumps the token so older in-flight responses cannot overwrite it.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/projectAtoms.ts:354 As before the fix, cache.set runs before the token check and there is no invalidation-generation fence. A response computed before an invalidation can repopulate the cache after it, and narrowing would serve its extensions for up to 15 s. The window is tiny: CheckpointReactor.ts:540 invalidates the server index before the turn-diff event, and dirty indexes answer with refreshing=true, which is never cached.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/projectAtoms.ts:113 scopeRuntimes (and the keepAlive state atoms at 115) are only cleared by clearProjectAtomState. Its only non-test caller is the hosted Hub environment teardown (apps/web/src/hostedHub/environment.ts:47). Desktop and local web keep a scope for every env+cwd (including worktrees) where the @ menu was opened, together with its up to 64 stale entries.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:115 canResolveProjectSearchEntriesLocally bypasses the debounce for locally answerable queries. Anything else still waits the fixed COMPOSER_PATH_QUERY_DEBOUNCE_MS = 120 (line 48, used at 107-111), with no relay-aware value.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:1275 truncated = index.partial || matchedCount > limit (80). Narrowing therefore applies only once a prefix has 80 or fewer matches, so short prefixes in large repos still pay debounce plus RTT (a relay round trip when hosted).
  • packages/shared/src/workspaceEntrySearch.ts:60 scoreWorkspaceEntry is shared by the server and the client narrowing. The empty query ranks by depth*2+kind, so a complete '' result (an index of 80 entries or fewer) is the whole index and narrowing from it is exact.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/projectPreviewAtoms.ts:112 projectListEntriesQuery is used only by the files tree (useProjectPreview.ts). Its staleTime is 0 (line 15), it is not invalidated on turn diffs, and the server caps it at WORKSPACE_LIST_ENTRIES_MAX = 25_000 shallowest entries (WorkspaceEntries.ts:80), marking it truncated beyond that. The composer never searches it.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/projectSearchInvalidation.ts:54 Client invalidation is still inferred from thread.turn-diff-completed and thread.reverted, scoped per checkout cwd. There is no server-pushed index-changed signal.
  • apps/mobile/src/rpc/projectFilesAtoms.ts:368 Out of scope but related: the mobile searchEntries query is already bounded (retainedKeyLimit 30), but it has no narrowing.
Remaining

1) Proposal 3 (M, optional) is not done. (a) No local search over cached listEntries data or on hosted relay connections: requestProjectSearchEntries (projectAtoms.ts:385) consults only its own search cache, and projectListEntriesQuery (projectPreviewAtoms.ts:112) is used only by the files tree. (b) Queries that cannot be answered locally still use a fixed 120 ms debounce (ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:48, 107-111), on relay connections too. (c) No server push of index changes. Invalidation is client-inferred (projectSearchInvalidation.ts:54), and listEntries has staleTime 0 with no turn-diff invalidation, so a local index copy needs its own freshness policy. 2) Part of proposal 1 is missing (S): entries older than staleTime are never dropped (projectAtoms.ts:246 only skips them), and scope runtimes and state atoms are never pruned outside hosted teardown (projectAtoms.ts:113, 795). Each scope is capped at 64 entries (about 1 MB at roughly 16 KB per 80-entry result), but an idle worktree scope keeps unservable stale entries for the whole session and the number of scopes has no limit. Both items are low impact.

Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness defects. Narrowing is exact: it uses the shared ranker, server normalizedPath equals path.toLowerCase(), the tie-break is the path, fetchedAt is preserved, refreshing results are never cached, and pre-fix servers used the same predicate for non-empty queries. Two minor hardening points. (1) startFetch writes into the cache before its token check, with no invalidation generation (projectAtoms.ts:354-356), which was already the case before the fix. Narrowing widens the effect: a response computed before invalidateProjectSearchEntries can be re-cached afterwards and then answer every extension of its query for up to 15 s. The server makes this nearly impossible by invalidating before emitting the turn-diff event and flagging dirty answers as refreshing. (2) canResolveProjectSearchEntriesLocally runs narrowFromCache during render (reranking at most 80 entries and promoting LRU entries), and requestProjectSearchEntries repeats the work in the effect. The cost is negligible.

Implementation sketch

A) Pruning (S, no decision needed). In apps/web/src/rpc/projectAtoms.ts, when releaseProjectSearchEntriesScope drops observerCount to 0, start one timer per runtime for staleTime (15 s); if observerCount is still 0 when it fires, call runtime.cache.clear(), because nothing older than staleTime can ever be served. Optionally cap scopeRuntimes to about 16 idle scopes in LRU order: delete idle runtimes beyond the cap and reset their state atoms the way clearProjectAtomState does. Add a per-runtime `generation` that invalidateProjectSearchEntries increments; startFetch captures it and skips cache.set when it has changed. Tests in projectAtoms.test.ts: a release followed by vi.advanceTimersByTime(15_000) leaves the cache empty (the next request hits the server); a response that resolves after an invalidation is not cached and is not used for narrowing. B) Local listing source (M, needs a decision). Add resolveListingSearch(environmentId, cwd, query, limit) to projectAtoms.ts or a new apps/web/src/rpc/projectLocalSearch.ts. It reads the projectListEntriesQuery state for env+cwd from the atom registry and uses it only when data exists and truncated === false. It memoizes the search keys per listing object in a WeakMap, as {path, kind, normalizedPath: path.toLowerCase(), entry: {path, kind, parentPath: workspaceEntryParentPath(path)}}, and ranks them with rankWorkspaceEntries, returning truncated = matchedCount > limit. Call it from requestProjectSearchEntries after the cache and narrowing misses, and from canResolveProjectSearchEntriesLocally. No worker is needed, because listEntries is capped at 25k entries and ranking that many measured 2.3-8.6 ms. Freshness: invalidate or refresh projectListEntriesQuery from the same ProjectSearchInvalidationQueue flush (per env+cwd), and treat the listing as a local source only within the search staleTime of its fetch. Optionally, on relay connections (the transport kind comes from the client-runtime connection catalog), prefetch listEntries when the @ menu opens. The proper fix for out-of-band edits is a server push of index generation changes (a new orchestration or workspace push in packages/contracts plus ws.ts), but the client-side invalidation reuse is enough for a first step. Tests: unit-test that listing-based results equal server-ranked results for the same entries (reuse the WorkspaceEntries fixtures), that a truncated listing is ignored, and that invalidation drops the listing source; extend ComposerAttachmentMenus coverage so a locally resolvable query skips the debounce.

Needs a decision

Only part B (proposal 3) needs a decision. Answering @-search from a client copy of the full index trades bandwidth and memory for latency. On hosted relays that means prefetching up to 25k entries through the E2EE relay, which is capped at 4 MiB per RPC message. It also changes freshness semantics: listEntries has staleTime 0, no turn-diff invalidation, and no server push. Robust invalidation needs a new server-pushed index-change signal in contracts/ws, a protocol addition, not a Hub change. Part A (pruning and the generation fence) is local and needs no decision.

Value low · effort M · risk low

Done#176 Path-picker alias probing stats and opens every small file in the browsed directory, which can trigger cloud-file downloads

gap-composer-pickers:alias-probe-hydration · original impact Low, effort S · Blocking I/O

Current state

Confirmed DONE. PR #710 (60633eff3) replaced the per-entry isMacOSBookmarkAlias call in filesystem.browse with probeBrowseAliasCandidate. That function skips content extensions before any syscall, stats once, refuses to open dataless placeholders (blocks===0), and caches results by path, size and mtime (FIFO, 2048 entries). Browse also skips probing when a directory has more than 500 regular-file candidates. I checked the blocks guard on this user's real Dropbox File Provider tree: csconfig.txt (593 B, flags 'compressed,dataless') stats as blocks=0, a materialized file stats as blocks=8, and stat() left the file dataless. So the hydration path described in the finding is closed. No other code path probes aliases: isMacOSBookmarkAlias is only used for the single typed-path check, and no other readdir path opens files to detect aliases. The leftovers are minor: the 500-file cap also counts content-extension files that are never opened, the typed-path check has no dataless guard, and the new tests are darwin-only, so Linux-only CI never runs them.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:1188-1191 Browse calls probeBrowseAliasCandidate(fullPath, dirent.name), not isMacOSBookmarkAlias, only for regular files and only when probeAliases is true.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:1159-1166 fileCandidateCount counts every regular-file candidate, and probeAliases = isDarwin && count <= MACOS_ALIAS_PROBE_MAX_CANDIDATES (500, line 353). Content-extension files are included in the count even though they are never opened.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:357-373 MACOS_ALIAS_CONTENT_EXTENSIONS plus hasContentExtension. Returns false before any stat or open (line 381).
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:380-400 One stat per probed file, a 4 B to 64 KiB size gate, and `if (stats.blocks === 0) return false` before readsMacOSBookmarkMagic. The cache key is `${filePath}\0${size}\0${mtimeMs}` with FIFO eviction at 2048 (line 354).
  • /Users/laurinfrank/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/csconfig.txt (live check, read-only stat) node fs.statSync: size=593 blocks=0 on a 'compressed,dataless' Dropbox File Provider file. The materialized rules.dropboxignore reports blocks=8. After the stat, ls -lO still shows 'dataless', so the guard detects online-only files correctly and stat does not download them.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts:324-334, 1095-1104 isMacOSBookmarkAlias (stat, then open, with no blocks guard) is now only called for the single typed path, when it ends with a separator and lstat says it is a regular file.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.test.ts:460-514 New tests 'only opens small files without a content extension' (476) and 'skips alias probing in directories with many files' (496) are both it.effect.skipIf(process.platform !== 'darwin'). The size-cap test at 569 predates the fix and tests isMacOSBookmarkAlias, not the browse probe. No test covers the cache or the blocks===0 guard.
  • scripts/ci/test-matrix.ts:28-46 All unit-test CI runners are ubuntu, so the darwin-gated browse alias-probe tests never run in CI.
  • apps/web/src/lib/projectPaths.ts:201-212; apps/web/src/components/CommandPaletteDialog.tsx:767-818 The palette always browses the directory path with a trailing separator and filters on the client, so prefix is '' and every regular file in the directory becomes a candidate. The 500 cap and the cache matter here, and both are in place.
Defects in the shipped fix

Minor, low-impact items only. (1) The candidate cap counts content-extension files that are never opened (WorkspaceEntries.ts:1159-1166). A directory with more than 500 media or source files plus one Finder alias (for example ~/Downloads or ~/Desktop) therefore stops showing that alias, even though probing it would cost one stat. The cap only needs to bound probe-eligible files. (2) The typed-path check isMacOSBookmarkAlias (WorkspaceEntries.ts:324-334, called at 1102) has no blocks===0 guard. If a user types a dataless, extension-less regular file with a trailing slash, the open() can still download that one file. (3) readsMacOSBookmarkMagic returns false on any open or read error (WorkspaceEntries.ts:336-348), and probeBrowseAliasCandidate caches that false (line 399), so a transient EMFILE or EIO hides an alias until the file's size or mtime changes. (4) The new browse-probe tests are darwin-only and CI is Linux-only. There are also no tests for the cache hit or the dataless guard, so a regression in this logic would only show up on a developer Mac. Out of scope but adjacent: resolveMacOSAliasTargets still spawns osascript and Finder on every browse or prefetch of a directory that contains aliases, because only the probe result is cached, not the resolved target.

Implementation sketch

Optional polish in apps/server/src/workspace/Layers/WorkspaceEntries.ts. (a) In browse, count only dirent.isFile() && !hasContentExtension(dirent.name) toward MACOS_ALIAS_PROBE_MAX_CANDIDATES. (b) Move the size and blocks gate into a shared helper, for example statAliasProbeCandidate(filePath), returning the stats or null. Use it from both isMacOSBookmarkAlias and probeBrowseAliasCandidate so the typed-path check also refuses dataless files. (c) Make readsMacOSBookmarkMagic return `boolean | undefined`, with undefined on an error other than ENOENT, EACCES or EPERM, and skip caching undefined. (d) Tests in WorkspaceEntries.test.ts: export probeBrowseAliasCandidate, or an internal test hook plus a cache reset, and drop the darwin gate for the helper-level tests so they run on Linux CI. Add one test that browses twice and expects a single open per alias candidate, using the existing countOpensDuring spy. Add one test that mocks fsPromises.stat to return blocks: 0 and expects no open. Add one test where 600 .png files plus a 'Projects' bookmark file still yields probing after (a). Optionally cache resolveMacOSAliasTargets results per (aliasPath, mtime) so repeat browses and prefetches skip osascript. Validation: focused `bun run test` on apps/server WorkspaceEntries tests only.

Done#177 Every turn completion force-refetches the last '@' query of each mounted composer (all environments), so the server rebuilds the file index even when the menu is closed

Current state

Confirmed DONE in 60633eff3, which is also inside the Hub's vendored Ryco (7bc39eec3). All three proposal parts are in place. (1) Turn-diff and revert events invalidate only the changed thread's checkout (worktree, else project root). They fall back to the whole environment only when the thread's cwd is unknown. The old unfiltered global call is gone, and the queue is the only caller of invalidateProjectSearchEntries. (2) The composer retains a search scope only while enabled, meaning an '@' path trigger is active. composerMenuOpen is Boolean(composerTrigger), so a closed menu has observerCount 0. Invalidation then only clears its client cache, and the next open refetches. (3) The server owns rebuild timing. An invalidated root rebuilds in the background (debounced, single-flight) only if it was read in the last 10 minutes, and otherwise drops its index. Live thread-detail events are the only web route into the provider invalidation (service.ts:744-746). React <Activity> hiding runs effect cleanups, so a hidden composer cannot keep a scope retained either. One residual by design: if '@' was used in a root within 10 minutes, each turn completion there still triggers one server-side background rebuild, even when the turn changed no files. This is the SWR warm-index trade-off the proposal asked for. Separately, the mobile Files screen has its own unscoped invalidateProjectFilesState. That is a different surface and only refetches observed queries.

Partial#178 Every issue/PR list or search read starts a project-wide linked-worktree sweep with unbounded detached gh calls

gap-composer-pickers:linked-worktree-sweep-on-read · original impact Low, effort M · Process spawns WP07B

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

The core list/search problem is fixed. Reads no longer launch an unbounded sweep on the response path: sweeps run detached in the background process lane with concurrency 2, links are re-read at most once per 5 min per worktree (60633eff3), and a project-wide sweep reads PR states in one aliased GraphQL call (9a601cbd1). The stated gain ('1 GraphQL call per sweep') is only partly met, for three reasons. (1) The batch is computed before any per-worktree due check, so every read that passes the 5 s debounce spends a `gh api graphql` that is thrown away unless a link refresh is due. After 60633eff3 those sweeps cost zero forge calls, so 9a601cbd1 added this cost back. (2) Linked-issue states are not batched. Each due worktree with an issue still runs getIssueState, which on GitHub is a full `gh issue view --json ...body,comments` plus a second `gh api graphql` for comment reactions, just to read `state`. Each due worktree also still resolves its provider. (3) The same read-triggered refresh exists on another path, refreshStateForLinkedReference. getChangeRequestDetail, getIssue and the issue-comment RPCs call it, and clients poll detail every 30-60 s. It has no debounce, a link-refresh interval of 0 and no known states, so every detail poll re-reads each open link of the linked worktrees with `gh pr view` (including the PR the detail call just returned) and re-reads the linked issue.

Nothing tests the context-level batch selection or gating. GitManager.test.ts:574 only stubs the method.
Remaining

(a) context.ts:495-498 runs batchedPullRequestStates on every debounced sweep, even when no swept worktree is due for a link refresh (due state lives in refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:86/:155). That is one wasted `gh api graphql` per 5 s of read activity. (b) Linked-issue states are not batched or reused from list rows. refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:341-350 calls getIssueState per due worktree, which on GitHub is a full `gh issue view` with body and comments plus a reactions GraphQL call (GitHubSourceControlProvider.ts:1199, GitHubCli.ts:2899-2925, :1710-1731). (c) refreshStateForLinkedReference (context.ts:531-555), tapped by getChangeRequestDetail (sourceControlRpc.ts:598), getIssue (:391) and issue comment RPCs (:413, :435), still makes forge calls on every read. It has no debounce, no link-refresh interval and no reuse of the state the detail read just returned, so a 30-60 s detail poll on a PR with a linked workspace re-reads that PR with `gh pr view` and the linked issue on each poll.

Defects in the shipped fix

The batch added in 9a601cbd1 ignores the 5-min link-refresh gate from 60633eff3. Every sweep past the 5 s debounce with 2 or more open/current link numbers makes a `gh api graphql` call, and the per-worktree refreshes discard the result unless a link refresh is due (refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:209-212). Sweeps between due windows went from zero forge calls to one. That includes picker list reads that are now served from cachedRepositoryList with no gh call at all. The process runs in the background lane and is cheap, but it is mostly wasted. No context-level test covers when the batch fires.

Implementation sketch

1) Make the batch lazy in apps/server/src/ws/context.ts. In refreshLinkedWorktreeSourceControlStates, wrap batchedPullRequestStates(input.cwd, refreshed) with `Effect.cached` (or a Deferred/Ref memo) and call it from inside `knownStates`. refreshWorktreeSourceControlState only invokes knownPullRequestStates when linkRefreshDue (refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:209-212), so the GraphQL call happens only on the first due worktree and at most once per sweep. Optionally also export a non-claiming `isWorktreeLinkRefreshDue(worktreeId, intervalMs, nowMs)` from refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts and pass only due worktrees' numbers to the batch. Test: a context.ts sweep test or a small extracted helper test. Two debounced sweeps inside 5 min give one getPullRequestStates call; after the interval, one more. 2) Batch and reuse issue states. Extend the GitHub batch document (gitHubRepositoryLists.ts buildGitHubPullRequestStatesQuery) to also take issue numbers (`i<n>: issue(number: n) { number state }`). Add an optional `getIssueStates` (or make the method `getLinkStates({ pullRequests, issues })`) on SourceControlProvider.ts / GitHubSourceControlProvider.ts, collect worktree.issueNumber in context.ts, and add `knownIssueStates` to RefreshWorktreeSourceControlStateInput so line 341 skips provider.getIssueState when the state is known. Also pass the listIssues/searchIssues rows from sourceControlRpc.ts:367/:458 as known issue states, the same way knownPullRequests is passed. Separately, make GitHub getIssueState cheap: `gh issue view N --json state`, or a GraphQL issue(number){state}, instead of github.getIssue with body, comments and reaction hydration. Tests: refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.test.ts, where a known issue state means no getIssueState call. gitHubRepositoryLists.test.ts, for the mixed query builder and decoder. 3) De-piggyback refreshStateForLinkedReference (context.ts:531). Split read callers (getChangeRequestDetail :598, getIssue :391) from mutation callers (refreshLinkedChangeRequest, comment/reaction RPCs). For read callers, add a per (projectId, kind, number) debounce like SOURCE_CONTROL_LINKED_REFRESH_DEBOUNCE_MS, pass linkRefreshIntervalMs = WORKTREE_PULL_REQUEST_DISCOVERY_INTERVAL_MS, and pass the detail just read as a known state. For a PR: state, isDraft, reported.terminalAt from mergedAt/closedAt. For an issue: its state, via the new knownIssueStates. A detail poll then never re-reads the same PR or issue. Mutation callers keep interval 0. Test in apps/server/src/ws (the authRpcRegression-style context stub or a new sourceControlRpc test): two getChangeRequestDetail calls within the interval produce zero getPullRequestState calls for the linked worktree.
