Done#179 Skills and provider slash commands come from a global probe at the server's cwd, so project-level skills and commands for the active thread are missing (correctness)

gap-composer-pickers:skills-project-scope · original impact Low, effort M · Other WP01

Current state

Confirmed DONE. bb8d23c7c, on main and in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3, adds lazy discovery per (instance, cwd) on the first / or $. Codex calls skills/list for the thread cwd over the shared read-only app-server. Claude runs the capabilities probe with cwd. The server caches results stale-while-revalidate for 5 min, the client keeps its own cache, and the results merge into the snapshot lists. Nothing runs on thread open, so the finding's correctness gap (missing project skills and commands) is closed. The auditor's 'no defects in the core fix' is wrong, though. Failures are cached as successful empty lists, which can wipe a good list. The global probes still run in the server's own cwd, so that directory's project-scoped items still show up in every project. All residuals are low severity.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:1344-1366 SWR cache (fresh 5 min, capacity 128). The load includes timeout(20 s) and catchCause→EMPTY_PROJECT_COMMANDS, so a failure is stored as a successful value. A failed background revalidation overwrites a previously good list with empty for another 5 min.
  • apps/server/src/provider/staleWhileRevalidateCache.ts:1-6,30-45 By design, the load 'returns a fallback itself'. The fallback is written into entry.value and readAtMs, so errors are indistinguishable from real empty results. Tests cover only the success paths.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:6677-6681 readProjectCommands maps probe?.slashCommands ?? [] to a success. probeClaudeCapabilities returns undefined on failure or on its 8 s timeout (ClaudeProvider.ts:215, 382-386), so a cold or slow Claude CLI start yields a cached empty list.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/composer/projectProviderCommands.ts:12,86-100 The client's 30 s RETRY_AFTER_FAILURE_MS only fires on a transport rejection. A server-side failure arrives as a successful empty result, which replaces `data` and is treated as fresh for 5 min. Worst case after one transient failure: about 5-10 min without project commands.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexProvider.ts:516-520 The global snapshot probe still uses cwd: process.cwd(), and parseCodexSkillsListResponse keeps repo-scoped skills.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/ClaudeDriver.ts:174 The global Claude probe still runs without a cwd and with settingSources user/project/local (ClaudeProvider.ts:349-355). A CLI node started inside a repo leaks that repo's project commands into every project. mergeProjectProviderCommands makes the snapshot entry win on name collisions (projectProviderCommands.ts:104-131).
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ChatComposer.tsx:748-766,901-912 The fix is wired correctly. Discovery is lazy (only on a slash-command or skill trigger), keyed on gitCwd (worktree path or project cwd), and the merged status feeds the menus and the editor skills prop (line 2926). Covered by ChatView.ProjectCommands.browser.tsx.
  • apps/server/src/ws/providerProjectCommandsRpc.ts:13-37 Reads only active project roots or active worktree paths. The RPC is operator-gated via rpcAccessPolicy.ts:232. Tested in providerSessionRpcs.test.ts.
  • apps/web/src/components/ChatView.tsx:5831 Timeline skill chips (SkillInlineText) still use the snapshot-only activeProviderStatus.skills. A project-only $skill renders as plain text in sent messages.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:252 The skill item id is `skill:${provider}:${skill.name}`. The merge dedupes by path, so a same-named skill at a different path (e.g. the server-cwd repo and a worktree of it, or a project skill shadowing a user skill) yields duplicate ids and keys.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.ts:2563-2580 skills/list is sent without forceReload. If the stored-thread reader app-server stays alive (60 s idle timeout, CodexStoredThreadReader.ts:59), a refresh may return Codex's cached list. Very minor.
Defects in the shipped fix

(1) Failure masking, the main defect. ProviderService.ts:1349-1366 caches the EMPTY fallback as a real value. ClaudeAdapter.ts:6677-6681 turns a probe timeout (8 s) or failure into a successful empty list. So a transient failure during revalidation replaces a good project list with empty. The client then caches that empty success for 5 min, and its 30 s failure retry (projectProviderCommands.ts:12) never engages for server-side failures. Result: project commands can disappear for about 5-10 min after a single slow Claude CLI start. (2) The global snapshot probes still run in the server's start directory (CodexProvider.ts:519 process.cwd(); ClaudeDriver.ts:174 has no cwd but uses project/local setting sources). Project-scoped skills and commands from that directory still appear in every project, and the snapshot entry wins name collisions in the merge. This doesn't affect desktop; it does affect a CLI node started inside a repo. (3) Timeline skill chips use snapshot-only skills (ChatView.tsx:5831). (4) Duplicate skill item ids when names collide across paths (ComposerAttachmentMenus.tsx:252). (5) Codex skills/list is sent without forceReload (CodexAdapter.ts:2565). None of these is a performance issue. All are low-severity correctness/UX issues.

Implementation sketch

1) Stop caching fallbacks. Generalize makeStaleWhileRevalidateCache to Effect<A, E>. On a failed refresh, keep the previous value (the tap is already skipped, so entry.value survives once the fallback is no longer in the load); on a failed first read, the entry is already deleted. Add an optional short negative TTL (about 30 s) so a broken CLI isn't re-probed on every keystroke. In ProviderService.readProjectCommands, move timeout plus catchCause→EMPTY outside projectCommands.get(...) so only real results are cached. In ClaudeAdapter.readProjectCommands, fail with ProviderAdapterRequestError when probeClaudeCapabilities returns undefined. Either let the RPC fail, so the client keeps stale `data` and sets failedAtMs (the 30 s retry now applies), or keep returning EMPTY and have the server hold the stale value. Tests: SWR cache test for 'failed revalidation keeps old value' and 'failed first read is not cached'; ProviderService.test with an adapter that fails once and then succeeds; projectProviderCommands.test checking that a rejected call keeps previous data. 2) Optional scope fix: run the global snapshot probes in a neutral directory (os.homedir() or the server state dir) instead of process.cwd() at CodexProvider.ts:519, and give the Claude global probe at ClaudeDriver.ts:174 that same neutral cwd or settingSources ['user']. Snapshots then carry only user/system items, and project items come solely from readProjectCommands. 3) Extract a shared hook (e.g. useProjectMergedProviderStatus(environmentId, instanceId, cwd, snapshot)) from ChatComposer.tsx:748-766 and use it in ChatView for the timeline skills prop at line 5831. 4) Make the skill menu id path-based: `skill:${provider}:${skill.path || skill.name}`. 5) Pass forceReload: true on the stale refresh path of the Codex skills/list call. Focused validation: vitest for apps/server/src/provider (SWR, ProviderService), packages/client-runtime composer tests, and the ChatView.ProjectCommands browser test.

Done#180 Activity statistics: NOT EXISTS can't use its expression index (affinity) and the tool-use count scans all 560k activity rows

dedicated-pages:statistics-sql-affinity-and-tooluse-scan · original impact High, effort S · Database

Current state

Confirmed DONE. All three parts of the proposal shipped in #710 (60633eff3). (1) The NOT EXISTS lookup compares against `+a.activity_id` and `+a.created_at`. (2) Migration 085 adds a full kind-led index `(kind, thread_id, sequence, created_at, activity_id)` and drops the redundant 008 prefix index. It serves both the tool-use count and the fallback's outer `kind='context-window.updated'` scan, scoped and unscoped. (3) Each payload is parsed once and shared by every aggregation pass. I re-ran EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN read-only on the user's live 9.8 GB DB (migration 90) with the exact current SQL. The NOT EXISTS uses `idx_orch_events_statistics_usage (stream_id=? AND <expr>=? AND <expr>=?)` both unscoped and scoped. The tool-use query is `SEARCH ... COVERING INDEX idx_projection_thread_activities_kind_order (kind=?)` (plus `AND thread_id=?` when scoped). The fallback outer is `SEARCH a USING INDEX ..._kind_order`. Timed (warm): fallback branch 0.11 s, was 1.67 s. Tool-use count 0.05 s over 121k tool.completed rows, was 0.70 s. The whole unscoped token query is 0.3-0.5 s. Reads now run on the read-only worker connection and are mostly thread-scoped incremental reads, so the event-loop cost the finding described is gone. I found no regressions. The new fork-inheritance residual filters only read columns the kind index already covers. The kind index also turns the `provider.turn.start.cancelled` lookup in delegatedRunStatus.ts into an index SEARCH. No other statistics or recap query has the affinity-blocked expression-index pattern.

COVERING INDEX ..._kind_order (kind=?)` (+thread_id when scoped) and a temp b-tree for GROUP BY.

It improves the cancelled lookup to `SEARCH ... kind_order (kind=? AND thread_id=?)`.
Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defects. One small test gap: StatisticsQuery.test.ts:917-927 checks only that the scoped token query's outer event branch uses `(stream_id=?)`. Done#181 Usage limits count cached records as scan work: codex 90d/all is already truncated, and a decode-cap cliff is ~3 days away

dedicated-pages:usage-scan-limits-truncate-cached-data · original impact High, effort S · Reliability

Current state

Confirmed DONE (60633eff3, #710; e5e676f95 moved the cache to per-file aggregates). All three proposal items are in. (1) Only fresh parses are charged to SOURCE_SCAN_BYTES/RECORDS/DURATION. Cached files are bounded only by a separate 2M SOURCE_CACHED_RECORDS cap, and a record-cap hit now uses `continue` instead of the old `break`. (2) The 250k decodedRecordCount cliff is gone. The cache is 64 v6 shards with only structural per-shard limits. A 1M-record in-memory cap evicts oldest-mtime files first, and the 120-day retention prune runs on load as well as after requests. (3) Budget-limited files are tallied separately and get diagnosticCode transcript-scan-budget plus a 'Refresh to continue' message, which web and mobile both render. Checked against the live cache at ~/.ryco/userdata/usage/scan-cache: 262k records (claude 128.7k, codex 133.2k). That is already over the old 250k decode cap, and both the codex 90d window (~123k) and the claude 30d window (~126k) are over the old 100k cap. All of it now decodes and aggregates without truncation. I found only minor leftovers, none user-visible at today's volumes.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:96-101 SOURCE_SCAN_* is documented as fresh-parse-only. SOURCE_CACHED_RECORDS = 2_000_000 is a separate cap for cached records.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:819-853 On a cache hit, only cachedRecords grows. The byte/record/duration checks, parsedBytes (840) and parsedRecords (845) apply only to non-cached files. Every limit uses `continue`, so later cached or small files are still included.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:866-888 budgetLimitedFileCount feeds status partial and diagnosticCode transcript-scan-budget, separate from failedFileCount/transcript-read-partial.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:276-281 Budget-specific coverage message. Rendered at apps/web/src/components/statistics/usage/UsageView.tsx:566 and apps/mobile/src/features/settings/statistics/UsageStatistics.tsx:152.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCache.ts:254-311 decodeUsageScanCache has no running record-total cap any more. Only per-shard structural limits remain: 10k files, 250k sessions, and 100k records per file (MAX_RECORDS_PER_FILE, line 31). Compare git show f1be4abc7:apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCache.ts, which had `decodedRecordCount + entry.r.length > 250_000`.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCache.ts:509-522 capUsageScanCache sorts by mtime and evicts the oldest files first.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCacheStore.ts:32,173-181 USAGE_SCAN_CACHE_RECORD_LIMIT = 1_000_000. On load, the retention prune runs, then the cap.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:1077-1087 Prune and cap run again after each request, before the coalesced persist.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.test.ts:265-330 The byte-budget test asserts partial status with transcript-scan-budget, then a complete second pass with reusedCacheFileCount 2, so cached files are not charged again. No test seeds more than 100k cached records, but the code path is simple.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageTranscriptReader.ts:362 Minor residual: a read resumed from a checkpoint returns the retained records plus the new ones. UsageService.ts:845 charges the file's full recordCount to SOURCE_SCAN_RECORDS even though only the tail was parsed. The byte charge is fair, because the old prefix is re-read for hashing.
Defects in the shipped fix

None material. Minor residuals, all low impact today: (a) Checkpoint-resumed reads of active transcripts charge the whole file's records to SOURCE_SCAN_RECORDS (UsageService.ts:845 with usageTranscriptReader.ts:362). The cap is only reached if more than about 100k records of concurrently changing files exist; the biggest live codex file has 9.7k. Files are processed in path order, so the same last file would then be budget-limited on every refresh. (b) The 1M in-memory cap is re-applied after every request (UsageService.ts:1085). Once a user's 120-day history exceeds 1M records, all-time and other long windows would re-parse the evicted oldest files and evict them again on every request. If that evicted set is over 100k records, those views stay partial permanently. The cap has about 4x headroom over today's 262k. (c) When failed reads and budget limits happen together, the diagnostic is transcript-read-partial and the budget hint is hidden. If every file is budget-limited and nothing is accepted, the status is failed rather than partial. Both are cosmetic or edge cases.

Done#182 Projects map runs git status --ignored=traditional per worktree on every open (13x slower than --ignored=matching)

dedicated-pages:projects-git-status-ignored-traditional · original impact High, effort M · Process spawns

Current state

Fixed in #710 (60633eff3). inspectCheckout now runs `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=normal --ignored=matching`. It then drops protected `!! dir/` entries that hold only nested empty directories, using a bounded readdir walk that keeps the entry protected when the budget runs out. Listing reads go through a fingerprinted 30 s TTL cache with in-flight sharing, which list() and suggestions() share. I ran a read-only comparison on 22 live ryco worktrees, using GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 and a JS copy of parse, classify and drop. Matching plus drop gave the same blocking decision as traditional in all 22. Git time fell from 30.2 s to 0.64 s total (about 1.4-1.7 s down to about 30 ms per worktree). The only !! differences were per-file listings of directories no pattern names, for example apps/web/output/*.png against apps/web/output/, and they did not change blocking. The other inspectCheckout callers (Agent Control preflight, WorkspaceChangeSummary, preview and apply) also use matching mode and pass no cache, so they read fresh and still get the speed-up. The finding's verifier asked for a correction for empty-only directories; it is implemented and covered by an integration test. The remaining `--ignored` (traditional) call is storage/filesystem.ts assertCleanWorktree, which an on-demand storage cleanup apply path runs once per checkout as a deliberately strict check, so the Projects listing does not hit it.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/workspace/checkoutInspection.ts:511 Status args are `-c core.fsmonitor=false status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=normal --ignored=matching`, with a 10 s timeout, maxOutputBytes 256 KiB, truncateOutputAtMaxBytes and readOnly. Only the storage cleanup path still uses traditional `--ignored` (apps/server/src/storage/filesystem.ts:279).
  • apps/server/src/workspace/checkoutInspection.ts:78 directoryHoldsContent and dropEmptyIgnoredDirectories (lines 78-124) only drop a protected `dir/` entry when the walk proves it has no files or symlinks. Unreadable directories count as content, and an exhausted 4096-entry budget keeps the entry. Every failure case keeps the entry protected.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/checkoutInspection.ts:531 The drop runs after parseWorktreeStatus, before `truncated` is attached. A truncated partial path fails readdir, so the entry stays protected, and `truncated` blocks anyway.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/checkoutInspection.ts:157 makeCheckoutReadCache keys each slot by kind and directory, versioned by checkoutReadFingerprint (line 217): the directory ino and mtime, the .git link, HEAD, index and branch head. Concurrent callers join one in-flight run, failures are not kept, capacity is 1024 slots, and checkoutInspection.test.ts covers it.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:457 listingCaches is shared by list() (line 1384, concurrency 4, with one projectFactsFor per listing) and suggestions() (line 1436). loadState (line 912), which preview, apply and applyCurrent use, calls inspectWorkspace without caches, so every destructive path reads fresh.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/WorkspaceLifecycle.test.ts:519 Integration test: an empty scratch-cache/a/b/ does not block, while userdata/profiles/state.json blocks in both preview and list().
  • packages/shared/src/workspaceLifecycle.test.ts:77 parseWorktreeStatus tests for both the traditional (line 77) and matching (line 88) output shapes, as the finding asked.
  • /tmp (read-only live check) On 22 live ryco worktrees, traditional mode took 30,181 ms in total and matching mode 641 ms. blockT equalled blockM in every worktree. The only differing entries were per-file listings, in the agent-control worktree's apps/web/output and output/taskNN, which blocked either way.
Defects in the shipped fix

None that blocks. Three low-severity caveats. (1) checkoutReadFingerprint covers the top-level directory mtime, the .git link, HEAD, index and branch head, but not changes deeper in the working tree. A tracked file edited in a subdirectory, or a new untracked file below the top level, can therefore leave a cached 'clean' status in list() and suggestions() for up to CHECKOUT_READ_TTL (30 s). That holds even after an explicit reinspect, because the client nonce does not bypass the server cache. Preview, apply and applyCurrent re-inspect without the cache, so this can never cause data loss; the worst case is a briefly stale summary or suggestion that preview then blocks. (2) Matching mode lists a wholly-ignored directory per file when no pattern names it. A directory with thousands of such files could reach the 256 KiB bound, and truncated is treated as blocking. That fails safe but could block a removal that traditional mode allowed. I saw no such case in live worktrees. (3) dropEmptyIgnoredDirectories has no direct unit test for the budget-exhaustion, symlink and unreadable-directory branches; only the WorkspaceLifecycle integration test covers it.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Partial#183 Every PR list RPC fans out an unbounded background refresh of all project worktrees (gh pr list --state all per worktree + gh pr view per link) during first open

dedicated-pages:pr-list-triggers-unbounded-worktree-sweep · original impact High, effort M · Process spawns WP07B

Current state

PARTIAL is correct. The first-open burst the finding describes is gone. The old code (f1be4abc7 context.ts:366) ran one forkDetach per worktree. Now there is one Effect.forEach at concurrency 2, detached in the background process lane. Discovery answers from a shared repo-wide index (limit 100, TTL 60 s) through a cached refSummary (30 s). Open links are skipped when the list rows or the index already report them. All other link states come from one batched GraphQL call (GitHub only). getPullRequestState now asks for the lean summary field set. Per-link re-reads wait for the 5-minute sweep interval. What remains: every project-wide sweep that passes the 5 s debounce still makes the batched GraphQL call, before the per-worktree link-refresh gate. While the PR page is open, its lists poll every 30 s, so that is about one gh api graphql every 30 s. Roughly 9 of every 10 of those calls are discarded, because no worktree is due for a link refresh. I checked the live DB (16 live non-main ryco worktrees, 14 linked, every current link a merged PR in the range #678-#728, inside the index window). Today the steady-state sweep costs exactly that one batch call per poll plus the shared index list. The auditor's evidence and line numbers hold. One fixDefects note was wrong (see correction), and the auditor missed three minor residuals, listed under remaining.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:495-498 batched = yield* batchedPullRequestStates(input.cwd, refreshed) runs on every project-wide sweep (not lifecycle, no checkout scope, at least one worktree) that passes the 5 s debounce at :458-462. It does not consult lastLinkRefreshAtByWorktree.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:403-416 The batch's number set: every non-dismissed link of every swept worktree, plus the current link even when it is merged. One forge call whenever there are 2 or more such numbers. It does not drop open links the list rows or the index already cover.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:155-160,213-216 The batched states are consumed only when linkRefreshDue (5 min per worktree for sweeps). When no worktree is due, the batch result is thrown away.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/sourceControlRefreshPolicy.ts:6 AUTOMATIC_ACTIVE_REFRESH_MS = 30_000. The PR page polls 3 change-request lists for the project root (prefetchPullRequestLists.ts) with ±8% jitter. One sweep per poll round passes the shared 5 s debounce, so about 2 batch calls per minute against 1 useful batch per 5 min.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:517-528 Proposal 1 is implemented. The sweep is Effect.forEach(refreshIds, refresh, {concurrency: LINKED_SOURCE_CONTROL_SWEEP_CONCURRENCY=2}). Non-lifecycle sweeps run as sweep.pipe(inBackgroundProcessLane, Effect.forkDetach). The background lane queues behind interactive work in the forge pool (processGovernor.ts:33-38, FORGE_PROCESS_LIMIT 4). The sweep is not explicitly deferred until the list group settles.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.ts:1221-1284 Proposal 3 is implemented. findLatestPr asks findLatestPrInIndex first and falls back to one gh pr list --head <sel> --state all --limit 20 per head selector only when lookupIndexedChangeRequest (pullRequestIndex.ts:166-195) is unresolved. Unresolved means the branch's PR is older than the 100 most recent, or the branch is published but has no PR and the repo has 100 or more PRs. Nothing caches 'no match' beyond the 30 s refSummary TTL, so such a worktree costs one gh pr list per 5-minute sweep. Today none of the live ryco worktrees is in that state.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:285-333 When a discovered PR is rejected (finished before the workspace's createdAt, or no forge close time), it is never linked or remembered. Every discovery pass (5 min in sweeps, 1 min for the on-screen checkout) repeats readPullRequestStateFromForge (gh pr view) for it. The batch covers link numbers only. Test 'ignores a reused branch's pull request that finished before the workspace' (refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.test.ts:527) checks the rejection but not the repeated reads.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/GitHubSourceControlProvider.ts:1153-1198 Proposal 4 is implemented: fields 'summary' maps to GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_SUMMARY_LIST_JSON_FIELDS (GitHubCli.ts:134-150, 2812-2820). getPullRequestStates is implemented only for GitHub (grep: GitHubCli.ts and GitHubSourceControlProvider.ts only). GitLab, Azure DevOps and Bitbucket still read each link separately, once per 5 min.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:381-391 Proposal 2, first half: knownPullRequestStatesFor merges the list rows the RPC just returned (sourceControlRpc.ts:542-548 passes knownPullRequests: items) with gitWorkflow.indexedPullRequestStates (GitManager.ts:1830-1844, peek only, never asks the forge).
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:531-555 Related sibling path, not this finding's: on every change-request or issue detail read, refreshStateForLinkedReference calls refreshWorktreeSourceControlState without linkRefreshIntervalMs (default 0) and without knownPullRequestStates. Each detail poll (30-60 s while active or watching) re-runs gh pr view for that worktree's links, even though the detail RPC just read that PR's state.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.test.ts:672-760 Unit tests cover the known-open skip, batched 'reported' adoption and the per-interval link re-read gate. No test covers the sweep in context.ts: the concurrency bound, the background lane, or how often batchedPullRequestStates runs.
Remaining

1) apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:495-498 (with :398-438) runs the batched GraphQL state read on every project-wide sweep that passes the 5 s debounce. That is about one `gh api graphql` per 30 s PR-page poll round, but the per-worktree link refresh it feeds is gated to 5 min (refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:155-160). About 90% of these calls are discarded, and the number set at :403-413 also includes open links the list rows already cover. 2) A rejected discovered PR (refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:285-333) gets gh pr view on every discovery pass, not once. This is rare: it needs a reused branch name, or a host with no close time. 3) The index fallback (GitManager.ts:1253-1275): a published branch the index cannot answer for still costs one gh pr list per head selector per 5-minute sweep, with no negative caching. It is bounded (concurrency 2, background lane) and none of the current live ryco worktrees hits it. 4) Batching exists only for GitHub; other forges read each link separately, gated to 5 min. Everything above is polish. The burst and the 12+ gh pr view calls per poll that the finding measured are gone.

Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness defect. One efficiency defect: the batch runs before the interval gate it serves (context.ts:495-498 vs refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:155-160), so most batch results are computed and thrown away. The batching, concurrency bound and lane placement in context.ts have no test.

Implementation sketch

Gate the batch (S, ryco only): (a) In apps/server/src/sourceControl/refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts, export `isWorktreeLinkRefreshDue(worktreeId, intervalMs, nowMs = Date.now())`, a read-only wrapper over intervalDue(lastLinkRefreshAtByWorktree, ...). Also extract the per-link decision now inline at :241-261 (skip dismissed, skip finished non-current links, skip an open link whose known state is open with the same isDraft) into an exported `linkNeedsForgeRead(link, current, known)`. The per-worktree loop and the batch number collection then share one rule. (b) In apps/server/src/ws/context.ts refreshLinkedWorktreeSourceControlStates, compute the batch only over `refreshed.filter(w => isWorktreeLinkRefreshDue(w.worktreeId, intervalMs))`. Build its number set with linkNeedsForgeRead against the known map (list rows plus the index peek, i.e. knownPullRequestStatesFor(input.knownPullRequests)(input.cwd)). If you want an even smaller change, wrap the batch in `Effect.cached` and call it lazily from `knownStates`. knownStates only runs for worktrees whose link refresh is due, so with no worktree due there is no forge call. (c) Optional: in refreshWorktreeSourceControlState, remember rejected discovered PRs in a module Map keyed by worktreeId to {number, state}. Skip the forge re-read while discovery still reports the same finished number and state, and clear the entry on reopen or in resetWorktreePullRequestDiscoveryForTests. Tests: in refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.test.ts, cover isWorktreeLinkRefreshDue and the rejected-discovery memo (two runs with discoveryIntervalMs 0 give one getPullRequestState call). In apps/server/src/ws/sourceControlRpc.test.ts or a context-level test, use a stub provider that counts getPullRequestStates. Call listChangeRequests on the project root twice, more than 5 s apart (TestClock), and assert one batch call. Advance past 5 min and assert a second. Validate with focused vitest runs of those two files and `bun typecheck` scoped to apps/server.

Done#184 getStatistics recomputes the whole history synchronously on the single SQLite connection, inside a transaction, on almost every open

dedicated-pages:statistics-blocks-event-loop-and-connection · original impact High, effort L · Blocking I/O WP06

Current state

DONE is correct. The multi-second stall on the whole server is gone. Statistics rows are read in one WAL read transaction on a read-only worker_thread connection, which has its own semaphore. Only threads with new events or changed meta are re-read, using json_each scopes. Per-thread partials are persisted, so the first open after a restart is incremental too. The RPC serves the previous snapshot after 250 ms and lets the refresh finish. The web hook keeps a module-level snapshot. Aggregation chunks yield through setImmediate (Effect 4.0.2 MixedScheduler), so I/O runs between chunks. Production servers run on Node (CLI and Electron-as-node), so the worker is actually used; the main-connection fallback is only for Bun, :memory: or a crashed worker. I checked the invariant behind incremental refresh: thread-scoped rows are written only by the projection pipeline, ThreadFork and ProviderRuntimeIngestion only read them, and every event advances every projector cursor. It holds. The auditor missed one real defect in the client cache (proposal 4) and some smaller server edge cases; they are listed in fixDefects.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:263 reader = SqliteReadClient or the main client. readRows runs inside reader.withTransaction (603-605), so the writer semaphore is not held.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/SqliteReadClient.ts:365 The worker transactionAcquirer uses its own Semaphore(1). Its only users are StatisticsQuery and DailyRecapQuery, so a full statistics read cannot hold up hot paths.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/Sqlite.ts:74 SqliteReadClientLayer.layer(dbPath) is in the runtime layer. apps/server/package.json runs the server with node; the desktop uses ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE (apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts:111).
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:366-386 Dirty set = threads with events after coveredSequence, plus threads whose metaKey changed. Rebuilds fully on an external commit, a sequence regression, or more than max(256, threads/4) dirty threads.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionPipeline.ts:2551-2558 Every projector cursor is advanced on every event, so projectedSequence (MIN over thread-scoped projectors) cannot get stuck and force rebuilds.
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:432 Effect.yieldNow every 256 threads. MixedScheduler uses setImmediate (effect 4.0.2 dist/Scheduler.js:112), so the event loop gets control back.
  • apps/web/src/components/settings/statistics/useStatistics.ts:21-29 DEFECT: lastSnapshot is one module-level value, not keyed by environment. The SharedRequests key is the constant "statistics".
  • apps/web/src/components/statistics/activity/ActivityView.tsx:70,87,114 The error panel shows only when snapshot is null. The data is labelled with getPrimaryKnownEnvironment()?.label, so a carried-over snapshot appears under the current node's name.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/environment.ts:29-55,58-98 clearWebHostedNodeScopedState and clearWebHostedAccountScopedState do not clear the statistics snapshot. usageSummaryCache, by contrast, is keyed per environment (packages/client-runtime/src/usage/summaryCache.ts:68-92).
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:599-602,638 restored=true is set before the first refresh succeeds. With no stale snapshot, the first refresh runs in the RPC fiber, so a WS disconnect throws away the restored partials and the next open does a full rebuild.
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:639-643 If the joined background refresh fails inside the wait window, the error is returned (orDie in statisticsRpc.ts:24) even though a stale snapshot exists.
  • apps/server/src/statistics/StatisticsQuery.ts:282,480 Persisted partials are keyed on MAX(migration_id). Migrations 087-090 landed on 2026-10-12..14, so the first open after most upgrades does a full rebuild: reads off-thread, but structured-clone and Schema decode of all rows (409-415) happen in one main-thread step.
Defects in the shipped fix

1) Client cache is not scoped to an environment (introduced in 60633eff3). useStatistics.ts:21 keeps one module-level lastSnapshot and uses the constant SharedRequests key "statistics". The hosted node-switch and account teardown catalogs (hostedHub/environment.ts:29,58) never clear it. A hosted user who opens Activity on node A, switches to node B in the Hub directory and reopens Activity sees A's projects, token usage and PR titles under B's label (ActivityView.tsx:87,114) until B answers. If B's request fails, A's data stays on screen with no error, because the error panel only renders when snapshot is null (ActivityView.tsx:70, StatisticsPanel.tsx:91). After an in-page account switch (passkey sign-in, handled at hostedConnectionCoordinator.ts:737-750 without a reload), the previous account's owner-only statistics are painted the same way. 2) StatisticsQuery.ts:599-602 sets restored=true before the refresh that uses the loaded state succeeds. The first open after a restart runs refresh in the RPC fiber (line 638), so an interruption (WS drop) or failure discards the valid persisted partials, and the next open in this process does a full rebuild. persistState also deletes the on-disk header first (line 534), so an interrupted persist drops the disk cache too. 3) StatisticsQuery.ts:640-643: a background refresh that fails within maxWaitMs surfaces as an RPC defect (orDie) instead of returning the available stale snapshot. 4) Manual Refresh goes through the same 250 ms stale-while-revalidate path (the client's fresh:true only bypasses the client handoff), so the button can return the same stale snapshot. There is no push or poll for the finished background refresh (auditor's point 3). 5) Residuals the auditor noted, which I agree with: rebuilds after any migration, an external commit, or more than max(256, n/4) dirty threads still structured-clone and Schema-decode every row in one main-thread step (StatisticsQuery.ts:409-415), which is likely hundreds of ms rather than seconds. Nothing ties STATISTICS_PARTIAL_FORMAT_VERSION to edits of processedTokenUsage.ts, statisticsAggregation.ts or forkInheritanceSql.ts, so a semantic change shipped without a migration would leave stale partials for idle threads.

Implementation sketch

A) Client (main defect): turn useStatistics.ts into a per-environment cache. Better still, move it into packages/client-runtime/src/usage next to summaryCache.ts as a statisticsSnapshotCache keyed by EnvironmentId, so mobile (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/statistics/useStatisticsData.ts:41) can share it. In useStatistics, read usePrimaryEnvironmentId() and seed useState from cache.get(environmentId), not a global. Include environmentId in the SharedRequests key (`statistics:${environmentId}`) and in the useEffect deps. Export clearStatisticsSnapshots() and call it from clearWebHostedAccountScopedState (apps/web/src/hostedHub/environment.ts:58), next to defaultQueryClient.clear(). Optionally delete the environment's entry in clearWebHostedNodeScopedState. In ActivityView.tsx and StatisticsPanel.tsx, when error && snapshot, render a small inline notice ('Showing data from <generatedAt>; refresh failed') instead of hiding the error. Tests in useStatistics.browser.tsx: env A's snapshot is never painted for env B, and the snapshot is gone after the account teardown helper runs. B) Server: in StatisticsQuery.ts replace the `restored` boolean with a `restoredState` variable that is cleared only once a refresh has stored `cached`. Route every non-transaction call through sharedRefresh (forked into the layer scope) and Fiber.join it, with the timeout only when a stale snapshot exists. That way a caller interruption never cancels a rebuild. When stale !== undefined, map a failed join to stale (log a warning). Tests: interrupt the first getStatistics after a restart and assert that the next call re-reads only dirty threads (check the json_each scope size or worker statement count); a failing refresh with a stale snapshot returns the stale one. C) Optional: add an optional `fresh` flag to WsServerGetStatisticsRpc (packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts:1044) so a manual Refresh waits without maxWaitMs. Or have the client re-request once after ~1 s when generatedAt did not advance. D) Optional: decode token rows in slices with Effect.yieldNow, or compute partials in a statistics-specific worker so only partials cross the thread boundary. Fold a hash of the statistics SQL text and the aggregation source into the persisted header in place of the manual format version.

Value medium · effort S · risk low

Done#185 ensureRates blocks every usage summary on a 2.75 MB GitHub download once the pricing cache is >24 h old

dedicated-pages:usage-pricing-fetch-blocks-summary · original impact Medium, effort S · Network / RTT

Current state

Confirmed DONE by 60633eff3 (#710). The summary no longer awaits the LiteLLM download whenever any rates exist. startRatesRefresh starts at most one background fetch: a Deferred in ratesRefresh guards it, it is forked into serviceScope, and the check-then-set has no yield between check and assignment. ratesLastAttemptAtMs is stamped before the request, which gives a 1 h backoff for timeouts, errors and 200 responses that are not JSON (captive portals). With no rates at all, the summary waits at most 2 s instead of 10 s. A warm-up 30 s after boot refreshes stale rates, and it does run at boot because UsageServiceLive is built eagerly in server.ts. The revision is a sha256 of the raw text. Rates change only through ratesGeneration, which is part of the per-source memo fingerprint, and pricing is snapshotted once per summary, so a refresh that finishes mid-scan cannot mix rates or leave stale memos behind. e5e676f95, the only later commit to the file, did not touch this logic. I found no other network fetch on the usage-summary path. The trimmed rate table is not refetched on the summary path.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:86-93 RATES_TTL_MS 24 h, RATES_RETRY_MS 1 h, RATES_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS 10 s, RATES_FIRST_FETCH_WAIT_MS 2 s, RATES_WARM_DELAY_MS 30 s.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:399-437 fetchRates sets ratesLastAttemptAtMs before the GET. A null text or an empty parsed table keeps the cached rates. The generation is bumped only when the revision changes. The new fetchedAtMs is persisted.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:444-465 startRatesRefresh: ratesRefresh is re-checked after the disk-load yield, and the TTL and backoff checks are done synchronously before ratesRefresh = done. fetchRates is forked into serviceScope, so the caller never runs or awaits it.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:468-473 Boot warm-up, forked: after 30 s, if pricing-cache.json exists, call startRatesRefresh.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:556-560 UsageServiceLive is in RuntimeCoreBaseWithSettingsLive, so it is constructed at boot and the warm-up actually fires.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:965-990 readSummaryUnlocked (inside scanSemaphore, computeSummary at 1125) starts the refresh, runs discovery, and waits only when rates.size === 0, for at most 2 s minus the time already spent. It snapshots rates, generation, state and revision once.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:793 The memo fingerprint includes pricing.generation, so rates that a background refresh changes invalidate memoized source results on the next summary.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:241-243 The revision is a sha256 of the raw response text. The document is no longer re-stringified.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.test.ts:461-520 Tests: stale cache with a fetch that hangs forever, where two summaries take under 2 s, are priced from the cache, and make exactly 1 fetch. No cache and a failing fetch, where three summaries are unpriced and make exactly 1 fetch.
Defects in the shipped fix

No real defects. Minor deviations, all bounded: (1) With no rates at all (first-ever open or an unusable cache), the download overlaps only resolveTranscriptSources and planSources, not the directory walk or parse (UsageService.ts:967-973). The rates snapshot is taken before scanSource, so the first-ever summary waits for the download for up to 2 s, then returns unpriced if it is slower, even when the scan takes longer than the download. Pricing is applied after collection in UsageSlotAggregator (usageFileAggregate.ts:268-297), so a later snapshot is possible, but the Cursor record aggregator prices at add time. (2) When no rates exist and the first attempt fails, pricing stays 'unavailable' for the full RATES_RETRY_MS (1 h), even if the network comes back a minute later. The old code retried on every summary, which was the bug, so this is a deliberate trade-off. (3) While ratesFetchedAtMs is null, loadRatesFromDisk re-reads pricing-cache.json on every summary. That costs an ENOENT, or a re-parse of an invalid file, until a fetch succeeds. This is negligible.

Value low · effort none · risk none

Done#186 Pull Requests page statically imports FilesTab, pulling @pierre/diffs + shiki into first open (~50% of the page's JS)

dedicated-pages:pr-files-tab-eager-diff-highlighter · original impact Medium, effort S · Bundle size WP12B

Current state

Fixed in #710 (60633eff3). PullRequestReader now loads FilesTab through preloadableLazy(() => import("./files/FilesTab")). It shows the diff-free PullRequestDiffSkeleton until useLazyComponentReady reports the chunk ready, and preloads it when a reader mounts. A reader only mounts when ?pr=N is set, since there is no auto-selection. I confirmed this on the real build as well as in source. apps/web/dist was built at 21:45 on Oct 14, after HEAD ec250e386 (21:40). The static chunk closure of PullRequestsRouteView-*.js (73 chunks) has no @pierre/diffs, shiki or oniguruma code. The only shiki strings in it are __vite__mapDeps preload-list filenames for the dynamic FilesTab import. FilesTab adds about 621 KB raw / 174 KiB gzip that load only behind that import: shiki-engine, useDiffFileNavigation, DiffWorkerPoolProvider, diffWorkerPool, FilesTab and a few small chunks. This is more than the finding's 518 KiB / 148 KiB estimate. The ThreadLinkList chunk that used to carry shiki is now 1.5 KB. Three guards protect the fix, the third of which runs in CI: (1) a source-text test, (2) a transitive source-graph test, and (3) a dist-level bundle-budget rule that forbids @pierre/diffs, shiki and @shikijs from the PullRequestsRouteView closure. The proposal's optional parts are only partly done: ChecksTab and CommitsTab stay eager, which is low value. The preload runs on PR selection rather than on pointer intent, and the code documents this as a deliberate trade-off.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/pullRequests/PullRequestReader.tsx:29 const FilesTab = preloadableLazy(() => import("./files/FilesTab").then(m => m.FilesTab)). No static FilesTab import remains.
  • apps/web/src/components/pullRequests/PullRequestReader.tsx:37 FilesTabBody renders PullRequestDiffSkeleton until useLazyComponentReady(FilesTab, true). It never commits a Suspense fallback, and a deep link to tab=files works because the hook starts the load.
  • apps/web/src/components/pullRequests/PullRequestReader.tsx:73 FilesTab.preload() runs on reader mount. The reader mounts only when model.selection && readerKey (PullRequestsPageBody.tsx:150), and selection comes only from search.pr (usePullRequestsModel.ts:162). The inbox first open therefore downloads no diff code.
  • apps/web/src/components/pullRequests/files/PullRequestDiffSkeleton.tsx:1 The skeleton imports only cn and Skeleton, so it is diff-free.
  • apps/web/src/perf/standardBootGraph.test.ts:203 Transitive source-graph guard. From PullRequestsPage.tsx it forbids pkg:@pierre/diffs, pkg:shiki, files/FilesTab.tsx and the hosted runtime.
  • scripts/perf/model.ts:292 Dist-level bundle budget rule for the PullRequestsRouteView closure. It forbids DIFF_RENDERER_SOURCES (@pierre/diffs, shiki, @shikijs/*). It runs in CI at .github/workflows/_validation.yml:213.
  • apps/web/src/perf/webBundleSplitting.test.ts:190 Source-text test. The reader must use import("./files/FilesTab") and preloadableLazy, with no static import, React.lazy or Suspense.
  • apps/web/dist/assets/PullRequestsRouteView-Dbp7z5yw.js Read-only analysis of the built static-import closure. No chunk in it contains @pierre/diffs or shiki code. Beyond RootAppShell the page is now 817 KB raw / 267 KB gzip, and about 340 KB raw of that is markdown-stack, which #710 moved out of RootAppShell. The FilesTab dynamic import adds about 621 KB raw / 178 KB gzip only when the tab chunk loads.
  • apps/web/src/components/pullRequests/PullRequestReader.tsx:6 ChecksTab and CommitsTab are still static imports. The finding listed these as optional ('probably'), and they are small and diff-free.
Defects in the shipped fix

No material defects. There is one minor reliability nuance. FilesTabBody calls useLazyComponentReady without onLoadError. If the reader-mount preload fails and the retry on Files tab open also fails (a transient network error), the hook reports ready, FilesTab throws, and the error propagates. /pull-requests has no route errorComponent (routes/pull-requests.tsx), so the error reaches RootRouteErrorView (routes/__root.tsx:435), a full-screen 'Something went wrong'. Chat surfaces handle the same case with notifyChatSurfaceLoadFailure and an in-place retry. RootAppShell dialogs use the same default as FilesTab, so this matches existing practice. For a stale chunk hash after a server update, a full reload is the right recovery anyway. Low impact.

Done#187 MCP settings fetches workspaces and servers twice on open (hook dependency bug); each Codex listServers spawns a fresh codex app-server

Current state

The double fetch on open is fixed. loadWorkspaces no longer depends on selectedWorkspaceId: the selection lives in a ref, the effect runs once per mcpApi, and mcpApi stays stable because the WeakMap API lookup and the panel key remount it only on a node change. Selector changes trigger exactly one loadServers, and a generation token drops responses that arrive late. A browser test asserts 1x listWorkspaces and 1x listServers on open. On the server, a 5 s per-workspace listing cache in CodexMcpService skips the codex app-server spawn on a quick reopen, and mutations do mutate+reload+list in one app-server session. That is the proposal's 'and/or cache' option; no pooled app-server was built. The described cost (2x loads and 2x app-server spawns per open, plus the selection race) is gone. Several fix defects remain, all edge cases. (a) If a mutation result lands while a non-quiet loadServers is in flight, applyServersResult bumps the generation and refreshing stays true, leaving Refresh and Reload disabled. (b) The server cache is per instance (one per WebSocket connection plus one for Agent Control), not process-wide. (c) A listing that started before a mutation can overwrite the fresh post-mutation cache entry. (d) Agent Control's install/remove fingerprint guards now read through the cache. (e) Cache hits still pay full all-adapter discovery in ProviderMcpRegistry.findAdapter, including an `opencode --version` spawn per enabled OpenCode instance.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/settings/McpServersSettings.tsx:864-868 selectedWorkspaceIdRef and a stable selectWorkspace (deps []) replace the selectedWorkspaceId dependency.
  • apps/web/src/components/settings/McpServersSettings.tsx:902-929 loadWorkspaces deps are [loadServers, mcpApi, selectWorkspace]. The effect runs once per mcpApi, so the self-retrigger is gone.
  • apps/web/src/components/settings/McpServersSettings.tsx:837-841 mcpApi is memoized on settingsTarget, which is a new object every SettingsPage render. It stays referentially stable because createEnvironmentApiLookup caches the api per WsRpcClient (packages/client-runtime/src/connection/environmentApi.ts:213-231). SettingsPage panelKey (SettingsPage.tsx:795, 1057) remounts the panel on a node change.
  • apps/web/src/components/settings/McpServersSettings.tsx:870-875 DEFECT: applyServersResult bumps serversGenerationRef for mutation results. Any non-quiet loadServers still in flight then fails isCurrent() and its finally (line 896) skips setRefreshing(false). No mutation resets refreshing, so Refresh (disabled at 1072) and Reload (disabled at 1085) stay disabled until a workspace switch or a remount. Server toggles are not disabled while refreshing, so a user can reach this state.
  • apps/web/src/components/settings/McpServersSettings.tsx:1059-1062 The workspace switch now does a single loadServers. The previous workspace's snapshot is not cleared (this predates the fix), so its server cards briefly render under the new workspace's header and capabilities, and a click there mutates the newly selected workspace.
  • apps/web/src/components/settings/McpServersSettings.browser.tsx:136-146 Regression test for single load on open. Nothing tests the selection race, the refreshing reset, or the server cache.
  • apps/server/src/mcp/CodexMcpService.ts:756-792 5 s recentServerLists cache, checked at 784 before findWorkspace/withClient. rememberServerList (767-779) overwrites unconditionally, so a listing that started before a mutation and finishes after it replaces the fresh entry with pre-mutation data for 5 s.
  • apps/server/src/mcp/CodexMcpService.ts:795-816 reloadAndList invalidates, then does mutate + reload + list in one app-server session. startOauthLogin invalidates at 891.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:263 makeCodexMcpService runs inside makeWsRpcContext, which is built per WebSocket connection (apps/server/src/ws.ts:27; ws/index.ts:36). The cache and its invalidation are therefore per connection.
  • apps/server/src/agentControl/Layers/AgentControlExternalInstallation.ts:537 A second, process-wide CodexMcpService with its own cache. Edits made through the Settings page connection never invalidate it, and the reverse is also true.
  • apps/server/src/mcp/adapters/CodexMcpAdapter.ts:14-15 inspect, used for install's before/after fingerprint checks and for verify, plus remove's preservedUserChanges check (line 75), read through the cached service.listServers. The compare-and-set guards can act on a listing up to 5 s old.
  • apps/server/src/mcp/ProviderMcpRegistry.ts:154-170 findAdapter calls adapter.listWorkspaces for every adapter, one after another, on every routed listServers or mutation. This happens before the Codex cache is consulted, so cache hits still pay all-adapter discovery.
Defects in the shipped fix

1) Client, refreshing can stick (McpServersSettings.tsx:870-875, 895-897). Mutation results bump the same generation that gates the in-flight load's setRefreshing(false). If a mutation lands while a Refresh or workspace-switch load is pending, refreshing stays true and the Refresh/Reload buttons stay disabled until a workspace switch or a remount. 2) Server cache scope (CodexMcpService.ts:756; ws/context.ts:263; AgentControlExternalInstallation.ts:537): the cache is per CodexMcpService instance, which means one per WebSocket connection plus one Agent Control instance, so invalidation is not shared. After an edit made elsewhere (another tab or device, Agent Control install/disconnect, or an external config edit), a listing can be stale for up to 5 s. 3) Stale overwrite (CodexMcpService.ts:767-792): rememberServerList stores whatever finishes last, so a listing that started before a mutation can replace the post-mutation entry. 4) Guard reads (CodexMcpAdapter.ts:14-15, 75): Agent Control's install 'before' check and remove's preservedUserChanges check read through the cache. Within the 5 s window they can miss a user edit, then overwrite or delete a user-modified entry. The window is narrow, but these are data-preservation guards. 5) Cache placement: ProviderMcpRegistry.findAdapter (154-170) runs every adapter's discovery serially before the cache, including an `opencode --version` spawn per enabled OpenCode instance (OpenCodeMcpAdapter.ts:347). A miss also runs Codex discovery twice (findAdapter, then findWorkspace at CodexMcpService.ts:785). 6) Minor: loadWorkspaces (902-925) has no generation or unmount guard, so a pending listWorkspaces from an old mcpApi (client replaced on reconnect) can toast errors or clear loading after the new load starts. Server-side calls are not coalesced (concurrent misses each spawn an app-server). No test covers the cache.

Implementation sketch

Client (apps/web/src/components/settings/McpServersSettings.tsx): keep two refs. loadGenerationRef is bumped only by loadServers and gates setRefreshing(false). applyGenerationRef is bumped by both loadServers and applyServersResult and gates setSnapshot. Alternatively, clear refreshing in applyServersResult when it supersedes a pending load. On a workspace switch, set the snapshot to null (or hold a snapshotWorkspaceId and render cards only when it equals the selection) so stale cards cannot mutate the new workspace. Give loadWorkspaces a generation or AbortController and cancel it in the effect cleanup. Browser tests: (a) Refresh pending + toggle resolving first -> Refresh button becomes enabled again; (b) switch A->B with A resolving last -> B's servers shown; (c) unmount during load -> no toast. Server: move recentServerLists out of makeCodexMcpService into a process-wide Layer (e.g. CodexMcpListCache, keyed by workspaceId) that ws/context and AgentControlExternalInstallation share, so invalidation is global. Add a per-workspace epoch that every forget increments. listServersForWorkspace captures the epoch before spawning and only remembers when it is unchanged. Coalesce concurrent misses with a per-key Deferred or Effect.cached. Add a `fresh` path (internal readServersFresh, not on the RPC) that CodexMcpAdapter's inspect/install/remove use, so fingerprint guards never read cached data. In ProviderMcpRegistry, memoize adapter discovery with a short TTL (or keep a workspaceId->adapter index from the last listWorkspaces, revalidated on miss). Cache OpenCode probeVersion by binaryPath plus binary mtime/size. Pass the resolved runtime from the registry into the Codex service so a miss does not rediscover. Tests in apps/server/src/mcp: a stubbed withClient/spawner counting spawns verifies a hit skips the spawn, a mutation invalidates across two service handles, a list started before a mutation does not overwrite the post-mutation entry, and guard reads bypass the cache.

Value low · effort M · risk low

Partial#188 Workspace inspection repeats project-level git commands per worktree and never caches results

dedicated-pages:projects-inspection-root-git-dedupe-cache · original impact Medium, effort M · Process spawns WP07B

Current state

PR #710 (60633eff3), with follow-ups 502adfd1e and 46f0f6cd0, implemented proposal parts 1 and 3 for the Projects page. inspectProjectGitFacts reads common-dir, root HEAD, worktree list and every branch head once per list() or suggestions() call. A 30 s stat-fingerprint read cache (single-flight via Effect.cachedWithTTL) and a 10 min ancestry cache are shared by list() and suggestions(). Preview and apply deliberately inspect from scratch. Removed rows skip worktree-level git implicitly (the directory is missing), and list's loadContext is project-scoped. Still open: (a) a cold listing runs 4 spawns per live worktree (rev-parse HEAD, status, symbolic-ref, common-dir) plus one rev-list per diverged branch (ahead/behind is not batched); (b) nothing is delivered progressively, and the settings-view workspace list waits for the slower suggestions call; (c) Agent Control's ryco_list_workspaces still repeats the 4 project-level spawns per workspace with no hoisting; (d) the status cache can show a dirty checkout as clean (or the reverse) for up to 30 s, because edits to file contents do not change the fingerprint. This affects display only, since preview and apply re-inspect.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/workspace/checkoutInspection.ts:335-386 inspectProjectGitFacts runs common-dir, rev-parse HEAD, worktree list --porcelain -z and for-each-ref refs/heads once. No ahead-behind or --no-merged batching.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/checkoutInspection.ts:458-461 Uses the precomputed facts when projectId matches. Without them (Agent Control, WorkspaceChangeSummary, preview) it recomputes all 4 project-level spawns.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/checkoutInspection.ts:133-202 CheckoutReadCache: 30 s TTL, single-flight via Effect.cachedWithTTL (semantics checked in node_modules/effect Effect.ts:14377), failures not kept, LRU capacity 1024. The ancestry cache has a 10 min TTL.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/checkoutInspection.ts:217-271 Fingerprint covers dir ino/mtime, .git link, gitdir HEAD and index stats, and branchHead. Reproduced in /tmp: in-place edits to root.txt and src/a.txt plus a new src/new/ untracked dir left all components unchanged while git status showed M, M, ??. Status can be stale for up to 30 s in listings.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/checkoutInspection.ts:492-570 Cold per-live-worktree spawns: rev-parse HEAD (:494), status (:498), symbolic-ref (:560), common-dir (:564-567). rev-list --count per diverged branch (:542-555), cached 10 min.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:1372-1388 list(): project facts once, then inspectWorkspace with listingCaches at concurrency 4. Returns the whole array at once.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:1395-1451 suggestions(): loadContext('all') (full shell snapshot plus listTrashed 10000 at :423-426), per-project facts via Effect.cached, shared listingCaches, concurrency 2.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:513-516 Only main or null-path rows skip inspectCheckout. checkoutRemovedAt rows still go through overlap loops, policy checks and lstat, and through the rev-list when the branch survives.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:900-913,952,1136 loadState (preview, execute, applyCurrent) inspects without caches, so the stale listing status cannot cause unsafe removal.
  • apps/server/src/agentControl/workspaceLifecycle.ts:269-279,309-320 Missed by the auditor. Agent Control list calls inspectCheckout per workspace (up to 50, concurrency 2) with no projectFacts, so it repeats the 4 project-level spawns per workspace, including removed rows.
  • apps/web/src/components/projects/sections/useProjectWorkspaceInspection.ts:57-82 Missed by the auditor. Promise.allSettled([listWorkspaces, suggestions]) means the settings-view list renders only after suggestions finishes. Component-local state, so a remount starts from 'loading'.
  • apps/web/src/components/projects/map/useProjectMapCheckouts.tsx:158-164 The map view passes suggestionsEnabled: false, so the map is gated only on list().
Remaining

1. Cold Projects listing: about 4 git spawns per live worktree (checkoutInspection.ts:494, 498, 560, 564-567) plus one rev-list --count per branch that differs from baseHead (:542-555). The proposed batched ahead-behind in inspectProjectGitFacts (:366-370) was not done. 2. No progressive delivery (rpc.ts:1824-1828; lifecycleRpc.ts:21-25). In the settings view, useProjectWorkspaceInspection.ts:60-63 also gates the list on lifecycle.suggestions, which does loadContext('all') plus up to 20 cross-project inspections (WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:1400-1451). 3. Agent Control ryco_list_workspaces (agentControl/workspaceLifecycle.ts:309-320) still re-runs inspectProjectGitFacts for each workspace, which is the finding's original per-worktree project-level pattern. 4. checkoutRemovedAt rows are not short-circuited explicitly (WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:513-516). 5. Project facts (4 spawns) are recomputed on every list() and suggestions() call, not single-flighted across concurrent calls (WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:575-583). This is small.

Defects in the shipped fix

The status read cache's fingerprint (checkoutInspection.ts:259-270) does not capture worktree content. With GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, status never refreshes the index, and in-place edits to tracked files anywhere, or new files or directories below the checkout root, change none of: dir ino/mtime, .git link, gitdir HEAD, index. Reproduced with a real worktree. list() and suggestions() can therefore show a dirty checkout as clean, with 'remove checkout' and suggestions enabled (or the reverse), for up to CHECKOUT_READ_TTL (30 s) after a previous listing. Safety is intact because preview, execute and applyCurrent re-inspect without caches (WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:900-913, 952, 1136). The 'previews always inspect from scratch' test writes at the checkout root and the cache test uses git add, so no test covers nested or in-place edits. The original proposal's key had the same blind spot.

Implementation sketch

A. Web, smallest change with the most visible effect: in apps/web/src/components/projects/sections/useProjectWorkspaceInspection.ts, settle listWorkspaces as soon as it resolves and fill suggestions in when they arrive (two promises, or keep suggestions: null plus a suggestionsLoading flag), so the settings-view list no longer waits for loadContext('all') and the cross-project inspections. Optionally keep the last settled value in a module-level Map keyed by scopeKey, so a remount shows previous results with refreshing: true instead of 'loading'. Test: a browser or unit test where suggestions never resolves and summaries still render. B. Batch unmerged: in inspectProjectGitFacts (checkoutInspection.ts:366-376), after baseHead, run `git for-each-ref --no-merged=<baseHead> --format=%(refname) refs/heads` (git 2.7+, so no version fallback is needed; %(ahead-behind:) would need 2.41+) and store unmergedBranches: ReadonlySet<string> in ProjectGitFacts. In inspectCheckout (:542-555), when projectFacts came from the precomputed path, use unmerged = branchHead !== null && branchHead !== baseHead && unmergedBranches.has(branch). Keep the rev-list fallback when facts are read fresh. Test with WorkspaceLifecycle.test.ts gitCalls: a list() with N diverged branches issues no rev-list. C. Agent Control: in apps/server/src/agentControl/workspaceLifecycle.ts list (:309-320), compute inspectProjectGitFacts once (Effect.option, fall back to per-workspace reads on failure) and pass projectFacts into inspect/inspectCheckout. Do not pass the TTL caches, because revalidate compares a fresh read() with plan.expected via isDeepStrictEqual. read() and revalidate stay unchanged. Test: count git calls for a 3-workspace list and assert one worktree list. D. Removed rows: in WorkspaceLifecycle.inspectWorkspace (:513), when worktree.checkoutRemovedAt != null, skip inspectCheckout, or pass a flag so inspectCheckout only computes unmerged from projectFacts. Check that summarize/workspaceActionBlockers do not need facts for removed rows (the delete action may use unmerged; keep that field). E. Staleness (optional): fold a cheap content signal into the status fingerprint, for example the max mtime of the root's direct child directories plus root files (one readdir with stat, bounded), or cut the status TTL to about 5-10 s while keeping the HEAD, symbolic-ref and common-dir TTL at 30 s. Add a test that edits a nested tracked file in place and expects the next list() within the TTL to report modified > 0, or document the lag explicitly. F. Needs a decision, not recommended now: for listings only, derive HEAD and branch from the worktree list entry and validate common-dir via the already-read .git link, gitdir/commondir file reads, instead of running symbolic-ref, rev-parse HEAD and common-dir in the checkout. That leaves status as the only per-checkout spawn.

Done#189 Usage summary loads, re-serialises and rewrites a 22 MB JSON scan cache synchronously, and keeps 63 MiB resident forever

dedicated-pages:usage-scan-cache-monolithic-persist · original impact Medium, effort M · Blocking I/O

Current state

The fix holds up under independent checking. The 22 MB scan-cache.json is gone. In its place are 64 hash shards (version 6, 8,099,126 B on this machine, largest 209 KB) holding per-file aggregates. Persist rewrites only dirty shards, debounced by 1 s and forked after the response under persistLock. The cache plus parser checkpoints are released after 10 idle minutes. I measured the real shards with a one-off node probe that imports the repo's decoder. Full load is 19.9 ms JSON.parse plus 19.1 ms decode, at most 2.0 ms per shard, spread over 64 async reads (before: one 80-115 ms sync block). Encoding one dirty shard takes at most 1.2 ms and writes about 130-210 KB (before: 50-55 ms sync and a 22 MB write on every active-session open). The decoded cache retains about 16.5 MiB while loaded (before: 62.9 MiB for the process lifetime) and nothing after the idle release. The Statistics UI has no polling, so the idle release really fires. Two races I looked for are not reachable. persist vs unload is serialised by persistLock. persist vs a concurrent summary is safe: the snapshot is synchronous and versions are captured per shard, so a shard that changes mid-persist stays dirty and a new persist is scheduled.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCacheStore.ts:27 64 shards. usageScanCacheShardOf (:38) takes the first hex byte of the SHA-256 file key mod 64 (an exactly even spread). OpenCode file keys are hashed too (opencodeUsageReader.ts:215,222,361), so nothing piles up on shard 0.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCacheStore.ts:190-228 persist captures dirty versions, then snapshots entries per dirty shard synchronously and writes each shard atomically with Effect.yieldNow between shards. markPersisted uses the captured version, so a shard mutated mid-persist stays dirty. A failed write stays dirty. The legacy file is removed only after a clean pass.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCacheStore.ts:134-183 load reads and decodes shards with concurrency 8 (one small parse per shard). The legacy v4/v5 single document is migrated once (cache.set marks every shard dirty), then retention prune and cap run.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:325-337 schedulePersist: 1 s debounce, coalesced, forked into serviceScope under persistLock. Called at :1086 only when store.isLoaded(). A shutdown flush finalizer is at :319.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:342-366 watchIdle takes scanSemaphore and persistLock, then store.unload() and readTranscript.clear() after SCAN_CACHE_IDLE_MS = 10 min (:110). unload (usageScanCacheStore.ts:231-242) persists first and keeps the cache resident only if a write failed.
  • apps/web/src/components/statistics/useUsageSummary.ts:100-131 No polling or interval refetch. Summaries come only from Statistics navigation, prefetch on route intent (routes/statistics.tsx:42) or a manual refresh, so the 10-minute idle release fires in practice.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCache.ts:181-243 v6 encoding stores 15-minute slots plus keyed rows (16-hex dedupe key, slot index, 7 numbers) with interned models/sessions. On this machine: 2,598 files, 261,986 records become 7,792 slots plus 128,738 keyed rows. The keyed rows are 86% of the bytes, the cross-file dedupe keys that proposal item 4 explicitly keeps.
  • /Users/laurinfrank/.ryco/userdata/usage/scan-cache Measured with a read-only node probe that decodes the real shards using the repo's decodeUsageScanCache/encodeUsageScanCache. Parse 19.9 ms + decode 19.1 ms total, at most 2.03 ms per shard; encode of all shards 26.1 ms, at most 1.18 ms per shard; retained heap plus ArrayBuffers 16.5 MiB. The legacy scan-cache.json is gone.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageScanCacheStore.test.ts:60 Tests cover legacy migration, dirty-only rewrite, unload/reload, empty-shard removal, retention on load, shared concurrent load and partial-migration cleanup. UsageService.test.ts:629 covers the idle release.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:739-740 Small correction to the auditor's 'memo hit never loads the cache'. That holds for transcript sources only. OpenCode database sources have no source memo and call loadScanCache() on every summary. For users with an OpenCode instance, the first summary after boot or an idle release always loads all shards (about 40 ms, sliced). That is a cost of memoization, not of monolithic persistence.
Defects in the shipped fix

No defect that needs action. Minor, non-blocking observations. (1) readText (usageScanCacheStore.ts:106-111) maps any read error (EMFILE, EACCES, oversize, or the file changing mid-read) to null, the same as a missing shard. A shard that fails to read transiently is then rewritten later with only its in-memory entries. Its other files are just rescanned, so the only cost is extra rescans, not wrong totals. (2) The OpenCode database is one cache entry whose aggregate keeps every response as a keyed row. With an active OpenCode session, that whole entry and its shard are re-encoded on each summary. This is proportional to the full DB rescan opencodeUsageReader already does, which belongs to a separate finding. (3) The SQLite table, lazy per-root loading and worker encoding from the proposal were not built. The measured cost no longer justifies them, and the finding itself named dirty-shard JSON as the alternative.

Value none · effort none · risk none

Partial#190 Usage client: extra getConfig round trip per request, all-or-nothing Promise.all, no cross-mount cache, no cancellation

dedicated-pages:usage-client-waterfall-no-cache · original impact Medium, effort M · Waterfall WP06

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor called this DONE and dismissed the mobile hook's missing signal as harmless for a single-shot load. The mobile Statistics screen has a range control, and its hook re-runs on every range change. Without a signal every superseded flight is pinned, so each node still queues one scan per switch, which is the exact cost proposal 4 targets. The mobile hook also still uses the all-or-nothing Promise.all across nodes (proposal 2). The web page and the shared client and server pieces are done. Mobile, the intended phone client per AGENTS.md, is not, so the status is PARTIAL rather than DONE.

Current state

On the web Statistics page all four proposals are in place and tested. There is no serverGetConfig round trip, environments merge as each one settles, a module-level SWR cache with in-flight sharing exists, and superseded requests are aborted on the client and interrupted on the server (a queued scan nobody waits for never runs). The other client of the same shared usage stack, the native mobile Statistics hook (apps/mobile, the intended phone surface per AGENTS.md), still has two of the four described problems. It waits on Promise.all across nodes, so one slow or hung node hides every other node, and it passes no AbortSignal, so its flights are pinned and every range switch queues another full scan on each node. Proposals 1 and 3 reach mobile through the shared wsRpcClient and usageSummaryCache. The web fix has only minor edge cases.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsRpcClient.ts:900-914 Proposal 1 done for all clients. getUsageSummary checks the version locally, sends the request directly and maps a version rejection to UsageContractMismatchError. The serverGetConfig call is gone.
  • apps/web/src/components/statistics/useUsageSummary.ts:106-134 Web proposals 2 and 4. There is one usageSummaryCache.load per connection with its own setAnswers. The previous run's controller is aborted only after the new run has joined, so only superseded flights are withdrawn. Unmount does not abort.
  • apps/web/src/components/statistics/useUsageSummary.ts:136-158 Per-environment pendingEnvironmentIds. Until an environment answers, the view shows usageSummaryCache.peek (stale while revalidating).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/usage/summaryCache.ts:73-160 Proposal 3. Module-level UsageSummaryCache, keyed by environment, range and time zone, with a 32-entry LRU, peek and prefetch.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/usage/sharedRequests.ts:153-175 #hold and #abortIfAbandoned. A flight whose waiting count drops to 0 is aborted. A caller without a signal sets pinned=true, so the flight is never aborted.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsTransport.ts:195-221 The signal is passed to runtime.runPromise({signal}). Aborting interrupts the RPC fiber, which sends an Interrupt to the node.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:1125-1196 Server side of proposal 4. Identical requests share one forked scan. When the last waiter is interrupted, the scan fiber is interrupted, and computeSummary rethrows interrupts. File reads use Effect.promise(signal), so a running scan can be interrupted as well.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.test.ts:583-626 Test: 'drops a queued scan once every caller has gone away'.
  • apps/web/src/components/statistics/useUsageSummary.browser.tsx:128-228 Browser tests cover progressive merge (fast node vs slow node), repaint on remount, joining a prefetch, and withdrawing a superseded range while an unmounted view still finishes.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/settings/statistics/useStatisticsData.ts:127-138 REMAINING. The mobile hook still awaits Promise.all(selected.map(loadNodeStatistics)) and calls setResult once at the end. A slow node (up to the 30 s SUMMARY_SCAN_DURATION_MS budget) or a hung node hides every other node's fresh result. Only cached peek data is shown meanwhile, and nothing is shown on a first visit to a range.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/settings/statistics/useStatisticsData.ts:48-56 REMAINING. usageSummaryCache.load is called without a signal, and getUsageSummary drops the options argument. Every flight is pinned, so switching 7d, 30d, 90d keeps all three requests alive and queues three scans on each node's scanSemaphore. The effect cleanup only sets cancelled=true.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/settings/SettingsStatisticsRouteScreen.tsx:24-80 Mobile has a range segmented control (setRange), so rapid range switching is a real interaction there.
Remaining

The native mobile usage client still has the all-or-nothing wait and the missing cancellation that the finding describes. apps/mobile/src/features/settings/statistics/useStatisticsData.ts:127-138 waits for Promise.all across every node before it shows any fresh result. apps/mobile/src/features/settings/statistics/useStatisticsData.ts:48-56 loads without an AbortSignal (getUsageSummary: (request) => api.server.getUsageSummary(request)), so SharedRequests pins each flight (sharedRequests.ts:154-156). A superseded range is never withdrawn, and the node queues one full scan per range switch. The web Statistics page and the shared client and server pieces are done.

Defects in the shipped fix

No significant defect in the web fix. Two minor, timing-dependent edge cases. (1) useUsageSummary.ts:113 treats a failed answer as answered for the view, and flightKey (summaryCache.ts:155-157) ignores connection identity. When a connection is replaced, the failed result can stay until a manual refresh, or the new connection can join a flight bound to the disposed client. Before the fix, every registry change triggered a refetch. (2) A loader prefetch for a range the view has already answered (7d, then 30d, then 7d before 30d answers) is never joined or aborted, which costs one wasted, memoised server scan. isUsageContractRejection's substring match on 'contractVersion' is fragile, but wsRpcClient.usage.test.ts covers it, and a misclassification only produces an 'update Ryco' message.

Implementation sketch

Mobile (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/statistics/useStatisticsData.ts). (a) Add an optional signal parameter to loadNodeStatistics(environment, tab, range, signal?). Pass it as usageSummaryCache.load(target, range, tz, { signal }) and forward it as getUsageSummary: (request, options) => api.server.getUsageSummary(request, options). (b) Replace the single Promise.all and setResult with per-node state, e.g. a Map<environmentId, { requestKey, node }> updated by setState as each loadNodeStatistics settles, guarded by a generation or requestKey check. Derive pendingEnvironmentIds, loading = pending.length > 0, and refreshing = loading && any usable result. Merge fresh answers with cachedNodeUsage/peek for nodes that are still pending, as the web hook does. (c) Copy the web supersede rule: keep the previous run's AbortController in a ref, start the new run's loads first so identical flights are joined, then abort the previous controller. Do not abort on unmount, so a closed screen still fills the cache. Optionally on web, stop recording 'failed' answers in answeredViews, or key them by connection object, so a re-registered connection is re-asked. First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor reported no fix defects. In fact the Statistics route prefetch does not handle the "limits" view added by #709 after #710: it fires an unused getStatistics on every Limits entry or tab switch and leaves the Limits data in the chunk-then-data waterfall. The DONE status still holds for the pages and views in the finding's original scope.

Current state

The core fix from #710 (60633eff3) is in place and the Hub's vendored Ryco (7bc39eec3) includes it. Statistics, Pull requests and Projects use lazyRouteComponent. The router sets defaultPreload "intent" with a 50 ms delay. Statistics and PRs have loaders that start their data in parallel with the chunk. The boot-logo fallback is now a blank RoutePagePending shell that appears only after 300 ms. I checked the PR loader's cause/preloadStaleTime handling against router-core 1.171.28: with preloadStaleTime 0, a hovered match reloads on navigation with cause "enter", so the prefetch runs. The auditor's "no fix defects" is wrong in one small way. #709 (56fbe263a, merged after #710) added a third Statistics view, "limits", and prefetchStatisticsPage still sends every non-usage view to the else branch. So entering /statistics?view=limits, or switching to the Limits tab, starts a getStatistics activity snapshot that the Limits view never uses. The Limits view's own data (readCliProxyHubs) is not prefetched, so that view still loads its chunk first and its data after mount. Two common entry points reach it: the composer's ContextWindowMeter "All accounts" button and the CLIProxyAPI settings link. The optional proposal 5 (idle chunk preload for these pages) is also not done.

Evidence
