  • apps/web/src/routes/pull-requests.tsx:28-55 Loader prefetches lists only when cause === "enter". preloadStaleTime: 0 makes navigation after a hover reload the match (router-core load-client.ts:789-802 uses preloadStaleTime for match.preload and reloads when match.cause === 'enter'), so the prefetch does run on click.
  • apps/web/src/routes/projects.tsx:22-30 lazyRouteComponent plus RoutePagePending; no loader (proposal 3 did not ask for one for Projects).

Remaining

Core finding resolved. Leftovers: (1) Defect: statisticsPrefetch.ts:17-25 starts an unused getStatistics for view=limits, and the Limits view's readCliProxyHubs is not prefetched (useCliProxyHubs.ts:94-110). (2) Optional proposal 5: no idle preload of the /statistics, /projects and /pull-requests chunks in ShellIdlePreloads (RootAppShell.tsx:177-185). (3) Minor: imperative entry points (CommandPaletteDialog.tsx:1598/1612/1693, ContextWindowMeter, ProjectBar menus, inbox rows) get no hover chunk warm-up. Their navigations still run the chunk and loader in parallel with no logo flash.

Defects in the shipped fix

prefetchStatisticsPage (apps/web/src/components/statistics/statisticsPrefetch.ts:17-25) was written when StatisticsView was only "usage" | "activity". After #709 added "limits", the else branch fires prefetchStatistics() (a server getStatistics snapshot, sent over the relay in hosted mode) every time someone enters or switches to the Limits view (loaderDeps { view } at routes/statistics.tsx:36). No component joins it unless the user then opens Activity within 30 s. Meanwhile the Limits view's real request (readCliProxyHubs) still starts only after the chunk mounts. Impact is low: the server query is incremental and the request is deduped per 30 s. But it is wasted work, and the statisticsPrefetch tests do not cover the third view.

Implementation sketch

1) apps/web/src/components/statistics/statisticsPrefetch.ts: replace the if/else with an exhaustive switch on search.view: case "usage" keeps the current capability check and prefetchUsageSummary; case "activity" keeps the getStatistics check and prefetchStatistics(); case "limits" returns, or prefetches hubs as in step 2. Add a `const unreachable: never = search.view` default so a future view breaks typecheck. Add a test to statisticsPrefetch.test.ts: with both capabilities allowed, prefetchStatisticsPage({view:"limits",...}) calls neither prefetchStatistics nor prefetchUsageSummary. 2) Optional, to remove the Limits waterfall: in apps/web/src/components/statistics/limits/useCliProxyHubs.ts, move the per-environment non-refresh readCliProxyHubs call into a module-level SharedRequests<CliProxyEnvironmentResult> (from @ryco/client-runtime/usage) keyed by environmentId. Export prefetchCliProxyHubs(environmentIds) that uses selectConnections(listEnvironmentConnections(), ids) and skips nodes whose serverConfig lacks capabilities.cliProxyHubs. In load(), call requests.request(key, ...) with fresh: forceNextRef.current. Call it from the "limits" branch after readHostedRpcCapability(WS_METHODS.serverReadCliProxyHubs).allowed. Extend LimitsView.browser.tsx so a prefetched read is joined and not repeated. 3) Optional proposal 5: in RootAppShell.tsx ShellIdlePreloads, add a final idle task that calls void preloadRouteChunk("/statistics") and void preloadRouteChunk("/projects"). Optionally add "/pull-requests" last (about 311 KiB gzip) and gate it on !isHostedHubMode() to keep hosted bandwidth down. scheduleShellIdlePreloads already skips constrained networks and the phone tier. Validate with the focused vitest for statisticsPrefetch and the statistics/limits browser tests only.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Done#192 PR page lists: involvement lists wait for git status, each list makes 2 sequential gh calls, and full comment bodies are fetched only to count them

dedicated-pages:pr-list-overfetch-and-waterfall · original impact Medium, effort M · Network / RTT WP07B

Current state

The costs the finding describes are gone. The authored and review-requested lists no longer wait for git status: shouldReadInvolvementLists reads them while the provider is still unknown, and the route loader starts all three in parallel. Each list is a single GraphQL request with comments { totalCount } and stack info inline, so there are no comment bodies and no second stack call. A 30 s per-repository server cache dedupes concurrent identical reads. The worktree sweep that runs after a list read is now detached in the background process lane. One residual came with the fix: on a cold per-cwd repository cache, a `gh repo view` network round trip (~0.45-0.5 s) runs before the list queries. The cold first open is still two sequential gh waves, and this repeats every time the 10-minute TTL lapses.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/pullRequests/pullRequestsModel.logic.ts:111 shouldReadInvolvementLists returns true while provider === null, so the involvement reads start with the state list (proposal 1).
  • apps/web/src/components/pullRequests/usePullRequestsModel.ts:98 involvementEnabled uses the new gate. involvementSupported (:118) hides those rows until the host is known to support them. useGitStatus uses view 'summary', so there is no fetch.
  • apps/web/src/routes/pull-requests.tsx:41 The route loader runs prefetchPullRequestLists on enter. prefetchPullRequestLists.ts:84-98 watches all three list keys in parallel with the page chunk.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/gitHubRepositoryLists.ts:55 Rows select comments { totalCount } instead of bodies. Stack fields (:61) and checks are in the same document (proposal 2).
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/GitHubSourceControlProvider.ts:544 A plain or involvement list with no free-text query goes to github.listPullRequests (GraphQL with inline stack). enrichChangeRequestsWithStacks is not on this path.
  • apps/server/src/ws/sourceControlRpc.ts:528 The list RPC is wrapped in cachedRepositoryList, keyed by state, involvement, query, limit and picker. The repository key comes from the remote URL (GitManager.ts:1151-1216).
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/repositoryListCache.ts:14 30 s TTL, concurrent reads join one in-flight call, failures are not cached, invalidated on remote refresh and mutations (proposal 3).
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:528 The linked-worktree sweep after a list read is forked detached in the background lane, so it is not on the response path (9a601cbd1).
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/GitHubCli.ts:1370 RESIDUAL: listPullRequests first runs Cache.get(listRepositories, cwd). listRepositories (:1239) runs `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url`, a network GraphQL call measured at 0.43-0.52 s. It must finish before the list GraphQL can be built.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/GitHubCli.ts:76 LIST_REPOSITORY_TTL = 10 min from lookup, keyed by cwd, with no stale-while-revalidate and no prewarm. Nothing else warms it: the PR index and branch lookups use the gh pr list paths.
Defects in the shipped fix

Cold-path waterfall added by the fix. GitHubCli.listPullRequests (apps/server/src/sourceControl/GitHubCli.ts:1370), and also listIssues (:1434) and getPullRequestStates (:1342), awaits Cache.get(listRepositories, cwd) before the GraphQL list. On a miss that runs `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url` (:1239-1272), which makes a GraphQL network request: 0.43-0.52 s measured, confirmed with GH_DEBUG=api. The entry is keyed by cwd (each worktree pays separately) and expires 10 min after lookup (LIST_REPOSITORY_TTL, :76), with no background refresh. The 30 s list cache has also expired by then, so the first page open after boot, and any open more than 10 min after the last resolution for that checkout, is still two sequential gh waves with 4 gh processes. The finding's 'first open after boot ... in two waves' therefore still holds on the cold path, only with a cheaper first wave. Old gh pr list resolved the base repo inside its own process (no extra API call with a single remote). Minor residuals the auditor already noted: free-text and involvement+query search still use gh pr list with full comment bodies plus a sequential enrichChangeRequestsWithStacks call (GitHubSourceControlProvider.ts:588-621). That is not the page's first open. Proposal 4 (persistent or SWR seeding across restarts) is not implemented, and that part was optional.

Implementation sketch

Remove the repository-resolution round trip from the list critical path in apps/server/src/sourceControl/GitHubCli.ts. (1) Resolve locally first. In the listRepositories lookup, before falling back to `gh repo view`, apply gh's own rules: if GH_REPO is set, use it. If a remote has `remote.<name>.gh-resolved` (`git config --get-regexp '^remote\..*\.gh-resolved$'`, where the value is 'base' or owner/repo), use that remote or value. If exactly one remote points at a GitHub host, use it. Parse with parseGitHubRepositoryIdentityFromUrl. Only an ambiguous setup (several GitHub remotes and no gh-resolved) calls `gh repo view`. The git reads are local and go through the git pool. Alternatively, pass the remote URL the registry already resolved (sourceControlProviders.resolveHandle -> handle.context.remoteUrl) into listPullRequests/listIssues as a hint. (2) Make the cached identity stale-while-revalidate. After 10 min, keep serving it and refresh it with a background-lane fork, keeping the failure TTL. Optionally key it by the repository common dir so worktrees share one entry. (3) If a list GraphQL call fails with 'Could not resolve to a Repository' (rename or transfer), invalidate the entry and retry once through `gh repo view`. Tests in GitHubCli.test.ts: a single GitHub remote means listPullRequests makes no `repo view` call and issues the graphql call first. gh-resolved and GH_REPO are honoured. Ambiguous remotes fall back to one `repo view`. After the TTL (TestClock) a read is served from the stale identity while exactly one background `repo view` runs. A NOT_FOUND from the list triggers one re-resolution. Validate with focused vitest runs for GitHubCli and GitHubSourceControlProvider, and with GH_DEBUG=api timing of a cold PR page open (expect a single wave of 3 graphql requests).

Value medium · effort S · risk low

Optional hardening, no further work is needed for the finding itself. Partial#196 Transcript parser decodes and copies every line and lists files with serial lstat; 3.5x below the I/O floor

dedicated-pages:usage-transcript-reader-throughput · original impact Low, effort M · CPU WP06

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor called per-directory batching 'still a large cut from fully serial'. Measured on the real layout it is about 10% (63 to 57 ms), because serial per-directory lstat and opendir (~39 ms) dominates and directories hold about 4 files each. The listing target in the finding (~25 ms) is not met. The parse throughput part is done and verified.

Current state

The parse half is done and measured. PR #710 (60633eff3) moved readTranscript to 1 MiB reads, a sha256 update per chunk, byte-level marker tests and array-pending long lines. On real files the current module beats the f1be4abc7 code: a 125 MB codex rollout drops from 197 to 62 ms and a 63 MB Claude transcript from 81 to 37 ms. Records, skipped counts and malformed counts are identical, and checkpoint resume reuses all 2,332 lines. The listing half falls short of the finding's target. lstat now runs in per-directory Promise.all batches, but directories are still walked one at a time (await lstat, then opendir, then flush). Real layouts hold about 4 .jsonl files per directory (Claude: 2,274 files in 528 dirs, median 4), so the batches are tiny. Listing ~/.claude/projects went from 63 to 57 ms median, about 10%, against the finding's ~25 ms target. Serial directory traversal alone costs about 39 ms. Listing runs on every usage summary, memo hits included, so it is now the main cost of a warm Usage refresh.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageTranscriptReader.ts:28 TRANSCRIPT_CHUNK_BYTES = 1 MiB. The read buffer at :338 is min(1 MiB, size), replacing the old 64 KiB buffer.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageTranscriptReader.ts:403-411 One hash update per chunk, through the chunk's last newline, after the pending pieces. This matches per-line hashing whenever a checkpoint is kept (discarded lines and the record cap set limited). Checkpoints are memory-only, so no old digest has to stay compatible.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageTranscriptReader.ts:287-315 Markers are tested on Buffers. toString('utf8') runs only for lines that carry a marker. usageLineMarker (usageRecord.ts:69-71) returns the same strings as the old mightCarryUsage.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageTranscriptReader.ts:380-389,424-429 pending is a Buffer[]. Each unfinished piece is copied once, and the line is concatenated once in takeLine. A line inside one chunk is a zero-copy subarray, consumed synchronously before the next read reuses the buffer.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageTranscriptReader.ts:44-59 Extra: lines of at least 1 KiB whose codex envelope is inert are skipped. This is safe for records because parseCodexTranscriptLine (codexTranscript.ts:60-95) acts only on session_meta, turn_context, thread_settings_applied and token_count. The only difference is diagnostic: a large inert line that carries only a context marker now increments skippedLineCount.
  • apps/server/src/usage/usageTranscriptReader.ts:117-162 Remaining gap. The directory loop is still serial: await lstat at :125, opendir at :130, and the stat batch flushed per directory at :161. Batches therefore hold only a directory's few files, about 4 at the median.
  • apps/server/src/usage/UsageService.ts:767-793 listUsageTranscriptFiles runs for every root on every summary, before the sourceMemos fingerprint check, so even a memo hit pays the full listing.
  • measurement (read-only node one-offs, warm cache, this machine) Parse, old vs current, medians of 5: codex 125 MB 197 -> 62 ms, Claude 63 MB 81 -> 37 ms, outputs identical. Listing ~/.claude/projects, medians of 12: old serial 63 ms, current 57 ms, traversal only (lstat+opendir, no file stats) 39 ms, 16-worker directory pool keeping lstat+opendir 28-31 ms with an identical sorted file list, readdir BFS 18 ms. opendir bufferSize made no difference.
Remaining

In listUsageTranscriptFiles (apps/server/src/usage/usageTranscriptReader.ts:117-162), directories are still visited one at a time: lstat :125, opendir :130, then the stat flush at :161. Concurrency only exists inside a directory, and real directories are small (Claude ~/.claude/projects: 528 dirs, median 4 .jsonl each). Listing therefore went only from ~63 to ~57 ms for 2,274 files, not to the ~25 ms the finding projected. It runs on every usage summary, memo hits included (UsageService.ts:767-793).

Implementation sketch

In apps/server/src/usage/usageTranscriptReader.ts, change listUsageTranscriptFiles from a serial pop loop to a bounded directory worker pool, about 8-16 directory visits in flight over a shared queue. Each visit keeps the current checks: lstat for directory and symlink, then opendir, pushing subdirectories with the depth check and collecting .jsonl candidates. Candidates are stat'ed with Promise.all per directory, or through a shared limiter capped at about 32-64 lstats in flight. Keep the shared count and files limits, checked before each push; overshoot is bounded by the number of workers. Keep the errorCount accounting identical, because UsageService only adds walkedRootKeys when errorCount === 0 and stale cache pruning depends on that. Keep signal.throwIfAborted: on abort, stop scheduling, let in-flight visits settle so their opendir handles close, then reject once. Keep the final localeCompare sort so output stays deterministic. Tests in usageTranscriptReader.test.ts: (1) about 200 nested dirs with 3 files each; assert the full sorted list, the window skips and errorCount 0. (2) Entries and files limits still set errorCount > 0 when wide directories are walked concurrently. (3) Abort during a walk rejects without unhandled rejections. (4) The existing symlink and depth tests stay unchanged. A local read-only prototype gave ~28-31 ms against the current ~57 ms on 2,274 files in 528 dirs.

Partial#197 Sidebar thread rows run the full local+remote VCS status pipeline (≈44 child processes, a git fetch and a gh call per feature-branch folder) just to show a branch name and PR badge

projects-loading:sidebar-pr-badge-runs-full-vcs-pipeline · original impact High, effort L · Process spawns WP07B

Current state

PARTIAL is right. Commit 60633eff3 (#710, which the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3 also contains) replaced the per-row full status with a `view: "summary"` stream. HEAD is read from disk with no status, diff or fetch. The PR comes from a shared per-repository index (gh pr list, limit 100, 60 s, single-flight). The broadcaster cache is LRU-bounded to 256 folders, and the shared sliding(64) PubSub is now one channel per folder. Background git and gh spawns are also capped by the process governor. So the ~40-44 spawns, fetch and status chain per folder are gone. Three gaps remain. (1) GitManager.findLatestPr still makes one or more `gh pr list --head` calls per branch whenever the index cannot answer. This is common in repos with more than 100 PRs, Ryco's own included, for old merged branches or pushed branches without a PR, and it breaks the '<=1 gh per repo' goal. (2) A cold folder still costs about 3-4 git spawns (rev-parse detect, config --list, remote -v, and for-each-ref when there is no upstream). The proposal targeted about 0-1. (3) The batched channel, fs.watch and projection-sourced worktree PRs were not built. The auditor missed two smaller items: the command palette mounts summary streams for every rendered thread with no visibility gating, and project roots below the repository root lose the spawn-free HEAD path.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarThreadRow.tsx:139 Rows call useGitStatus(..., { enabled: shouldEnableSidebarRowGitStatus({isActive, isIntersecting}), view: "summary" }). This view is the only git status a sidebar row reads.
  • apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/InboxThreadRow.tsx:206 Inbox rows also use the summary view. Full status (line 214) is read only while hover or focus intent is active.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:699 streamRefSummary runs workflow.refSummary in inBackgroundProcessLane. It re-reads on a per-folder publication, a 5 s HEAD file poll (line 717) and an optional poll of at least 60 s. Lines 754-755 dispatch on input.view. Test VcsStatusBroadcaster.test.ts:998 asserts no local/remote/fetch calls.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.ts:1718 readRefSummary gets the branch and origin/HEAD from readCheckoutHead (a disk read), uses the cached config snapshot, probeBranchPublished, then findLatestPr. It does no status, diff or fetch. Lines 1821-1828 cache it 30 s per cwd + branch read from disk.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/pullRequestIndex.ts:21 Per-repository index: limit 100, 60 s TTL (10 s on failure), capacity 256, single-flight through Cache.get, keyed by provider and normalized remote URL. lookupIndexedChangeRequest (line 186) returns resolved:false when the recent list is full and has no match.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.ts:1259 Residual: when the index is unresolved, findLatestPr loops over head selectors with listChangeRequests (state all, limit 20), one gh call each, with no cache beyond refSummary's 30 s. GitManager.test.ts:1610-1614 pins the sequence for an old branch: pr list all + pr list open + pr list --head.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:37 STATUS_CACHE_MAX_FOLDERS=256 (LRU through withCachedFolder, line 232). FOLDER_CHANNEL_CAPACITY=16 per-folder PubSub (subscribeFolder/publishFolderEvent, lines 183-229) replaces the shared sliding(64).
  • apps/server/src/processGovernor.ts:33 The background lane caps concurrent git children at 8 and gh/glab/az at 4, so a first-render burst queues instead of spawning hundreds at once.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/SourceControlProviderRegistry.ts:682 Residual spawn: detectProviderContext runs `git remote -v` (GitVcsDriver.ts:592) per folder, cached only 5 s (line 33). The config snapshot (`git config -z --list`, GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1145, TTL 5 s at line 79) already holds remote.*.url. Detect (rev-parse) is cached 2 min (VcsDriverRegistry.ts:20).
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.ts:921 Residual spawn: probeBranchPublished runs `git for-each-ref refs/remotes/<r>/<branch>` when the branch has no upstream config.
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadStatusIndicators.tsx:145 Missed caller: ThreadRowLeadingStatus subscribes the summary view with no `enabled` gating. CommandPaletteDialog.tsx:1045 and 1076 render it for every thread item, and CommandPaletteResults.tsx:43 renders the whole Base UI collection (not virtualized). A broad query therefore opens one summary stream per distinct folder of all matching threads (about 53 for the user). It was full view before, so this is better, but still ungated.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/gitCheckoutHead.ts:47 A project cwd below the repository root returns null. readRefSummary then spawns two `git symbolic-ref` (GitManager.ts:1722-1737 and 1765-1780). The summary stream's HEAD poll (VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:717-723) always yields null for such a folder, so a checkout switch made outside Ryco is not noticed until a publication arrives or the row resubscribes after the 30 s TTL.
Remaining

1. Per-branch gh fallback on the badge path (GitManager.ts:1246-1281, reached from readRefSummary at GitManager.ts:1793-1808). In a repository with more than 100 change requests, the index cannot answer for a published branch whose PR falls outside the recent 100 (old merged worktrees) or that has no PR. Each such folder then costs 1-3 `gh pr list --head` calls on every cold refSummary read (30 s cache; rows resubscribe on visibility changes), queued behind the 4-slot forge pool. Ryco's own repo (more than 700 PRs) is exactly this case. The same fallback also runs when the index listing itself failed (offline, no auth), where the per-branch calls fail the same way. 2. Not spawn-free: a cold folder costs rev-parse detect (2 min cache), `git config -z --list` (5 s), `git remote -v` (5 s) and, without an upstream, `git for-each-ref`. That is about 3-4 per folder, roughly 90-120 for 30 folders, versus the proposed 0-30. Project roots below the repository root add 2 `symbolic-ref` spawns and get no HEAD-change detection (gitCheckoutHead.ts:47, VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:717). 3. The command palette mounts ungated summary streams for every rendered thread row (ThreadStatusIndicators.tsx:145 via CommandPaletteDialog.tsx:1045/1076). 4. Optional, not done: a batched `subscribeSummaries({cwds})` channel (each visible folder is still its own RPC stream plus a 5 s HEAD poll), fs.watch on HEAD, and projection pull_requests for worktree-thread rows. Adjacent but outside this finding's VCS-status scope: in inbox mode, each visible row with a PR also issues an uncached getChangeRequestDetail (InboxThreadRow.tsx:219 to sourceControlRpc.ts:585), polled every 30 s while the PR is open. This should be tracked separately if wanted.

Defects in the shipped fix

No regression found. Minor: (a) the first summary snapshot (VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:708) waits for the whole readSummary, including a cold index gh call or the per-branch fallback, so even the spawn-free refName arrives only after gh. (b) refSummaryKeysByCwd (GitManager.ts:1716) remembers only the latest branch key per cwd, so after a checkout switch the old branch's entry lives until its TTL (harmless). (c) In the HEAD-poll stream, Stream.changes + drop(1) on the first immediate tick can swallow a switch that happens between the initial read and the first tick (a millisecond window). (d) For a non-root project cwd, isDefaultRef falls back to the main/master heuristic when origin/HEAD is missing, which can differ from the full path's base-branch resolution (an edge case).

Implementation sketch

A. Bound the gh fallback (main value). In GitManager.ts add a `branchChangeRequestCache` (Effect Cache, capacity about 2048) keyed by `pullRequestIndexRepositoryKey + headSelector`. Its lookup runs the existing per-selector listChangeRequests. TTL depends on the result: open 60 s, merged/closed 15 min, none 2-5 min, failure 10 s. Use it inside findLatestPr (lines 1259-1275) for both the summary and full paths. invalidatePullRequestIndex (line 1170) should also invalidate that repository's entries, which an explicit refresh or git action already triggers. In lookupIndexedChangeRequest (pullRequestIndex.ts:186) distinguish `unavailable` (listing failed) from `incomplete`, and skip the per-branch loop when it is unavailable (return null; the 10 s failure TTL retries). Tests in GitManager.test.ts: two refSummary reads of an old branch on separate checkouts of the same repo, with the cache invalidated in between, issue at most one `--head` call within the TTL; a failing `pr list --state all` causes no `--head` call; an explicit invalidateRemoteStatus re-asks. B. Fewer spawns per cold folder (optional). (1) In SourceControlProviderRegistry.detectProviderContext (line 682), build remotes from gitCore.readConfigSnapshot (`remote.<name>.url`/`pushurl`), applying `url.<base>.insteadOf`/`pushInsteadOf` from the same snapshot, and fall back to `remote -v` only when the snapshot is unavailable. (2) In probeBranchPublished (GitManager.ts:904), check `<commonDir>/refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` and packed-refs (commonDir from readCheckoutHead) before running for-each-ref; reftable keeps the spawn. (3) Revalidate the config snapshot by stat (mtime/size of <commonDir>/config and <gitDir>/config.worktree) instead of the 5 s TTL. (4) For a cwd below the root, resolve the root once (cached with detect) and run readCheckoutHead on the root, which restores the HEAD poll and drops the symbolic-ref spawns. Test with spawn counters in GitManager.test.ts and VcsStatusBroadcaster.test.ts: a cold summary costs at most 1 git spawn (detect). C. Gate the palette. Give ThreadRowLeadingStatus (ThreadStatusIndicators.tsx:145) an `enabled` option. In CommandPaletteDialog pass enabled only for the first RECENT_THREAD_LIMIT rendered items or the highlighted one, or add a `useGitStatusSnapshot(target, 'summary')` that reads the existing atom without watching, so palette rows reuse badges the sidebar already loaded. Browser test: a palette query with N threads opens at most 12 vcs subscriptions. D. Optional: worktree-thread rows read the projection's pull_requests (already in SidebarWorktreeList) and skip the stream; a batched `vcs.subscribeSummaries({cwds})` RPC with fs.watch on HEAD.

Partial#198 The first remote-status load per repo blocks on a network git fetch (5 s timeout), even with gitStatusPollIntervalMs = 0 (the default)

projects-loading:status-remote-load-fetches-network · original impact Medium, effort S · Network / RTT WP07A

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

Mostly fixed for the default setting, but not on every path. With gitStatusPollIntervalMs=0, a full-view stream with a stale cache now reads remote status from the current tracking refs (statusDetailsLocal plus the indexed PR lookup) with no fetch. It then forks the shared fetch into the background lane, behind a 2-permit semaphore and a 15 s cache per (gitCommonDir, remote), and republishes if the fingerprint changes. Sidebar, inbox and PR-page rows use the summary view, which never fetches. So the 'R fetches at boot' cost and the blocking first load at the default are gone. The auditor missed the poll>0 path. The proposal said that path should also serve immediately and fetch in the background, but it was left unchanged. When the poller is retained, streamFullStatus skips the no-fetch load. The poller's first iteration is refreshRemoteStatus, which runs the git fetch (up to 5 s plus semaphore wait) inside the remote single-flight before computing anything. So users who turned polling on still wait on the network for the first ahead/behind and PR badge. A no-fetch 'load' that arrives while such a fetch-first refresh is in flight also waits for it. The rare turn-start worktree-recovery path still awaits a fetching refreshStatus.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:686 With poll=0 and a stale cache, the stream emits getOrLoadRemoteStatus (no fetch), then taps refreshRemoteStatusAfterFetch (line 689). With retainedRemotePoller=true the remote branch is Stream.empty, so the first remote status comes only from the poller's publication.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:548 makeRemoteRefreshLoop runs refreshRemoteStatus immediately on its first iteration (Effect.repeat at line 571 runs once before any delay). So for poll>0 the first remote status waits for the fetch.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:497 refreshRemoteStatus calls workflow.remoteStatus({cwd},{fetch:true}) inside coalesceRemoteStatus(cwd,'refresh'), so the network fetch holds the per-cwd remote single-flight.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:278 A 'load' arriving while any flight is in progress awaits it, so a no-fetch initial load can wait behind an in-flight fetch-first refresh (poller, window-focus refreshGitStatus, or git-action refresh) for the same cwd.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.ts:942 readRemoteStatus uses takeRecentLocalStatusDetails or statusDetailsLocal, with no refreshStatusUpstream. remoteStatus (line 1693) fetches only when options.fetch is set. This confirms the default path is fixed.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1265 fetchRemoteForStatus is wrapped in a Semaphore(STATUS_UPSTREAM_REFRESH_CONCURRENCY=2). The cache keyed by (gitCommonDir, remote) at line 1320 holds results 15 s; the fetch uses allowNonZeroExit, so a failed fetch with a non-zero exit also counts as 'fetched' and triggers a recompute.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:699 streamRefSummary (view:'summary') does no git status and no fetch. It is used by SidebarThreadRow.tsx:144, InboxThreadRow.tsx:208, ThreadStatusIndicators.tsx:150/211 and usePullRequestsModel.ts:80.
  • apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/InboxThreadRow.tsx:214 The inbox hover card mounts a full-view stream, so hovering a row whose remote cache is stale starts a background fetch at poll=0. It is non-blocking and deduped per repo, but it is not limited to the focused thread's folder.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:734 ensureRecordedWorktreeAvailable, called on turn start at lines 786 and 1844, awaits refreshStatus, which fetches first. A turn that has to recreate a missing worktree therefore waits up to about 5 s on git fetch. ws/context.ts:1257 and ThreadFork.ts:699 fork the same call instead.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.ts:1684 After a fetch, only this cwd's localStatusDetailsByCwd entry and remote cache are invalidated. A readLocalStatus that started before the fetch can re-set stale details at line 861 just before the republish reads them. This is a narrow race.
Remaining

1) When polling is on (gitStatusPollIntervalMs>0, opt-in), the first remote status per stream still blocks on the network fetch. At VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:686 the no-fetch load is skipped when a poller is retained. The poller's first iteration (line 548, then 497) runs the fetch inside the remote single-flight before computing. A second client attaching to an already-retained poller with a stale cache (poll 60 s or 300 s) gets remote:null and waits until the next poll tick, up to about 270 s. That problem predates the fix and is on the same path. 2) Any no-fetch 'load' that arrives while a fetch-first refresh for the same cwd is in flight awaits that fetch (line 278). 3) The rare turn-start recovery path (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:734) awaits refreshStatus, including the fetch, before the provider turn starts.

Defects in the shipped fix

No significant bugs in the poll=0 fix. Minor issues: (a) refreshStatusUpstreamIfStale reports 'fetched' whenever a fetch process completed, including non-zero-exit failures and fetches that moved nothing. Each background fetch therefore re-runs git status and the PR-index lookup for the republish, which only publishes if the fingerprint changed. That costs work but is not wrong. (b) A fetch run for one checkout invalidates only that checkout's GitManager caches (GitManager.ts:1684-1688). An already-open poll=0 stream on another worktree of the same repo keeps its pre-fetch ahead/behind until its own refresh or until it reattaches. (c) There is a narrow race where a concurrent readLocalStatus re-sets pre-fetch details (GitManager.ts:861) right after the fetch invalidation, so the republish can reuse stale ahead/behind.

Implementation sketch

VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts: (1) Move the network fetch out of the remote single-flight. In refreshRemoteStatus (line 487), first run `workflow.refreshRemoteTrackingRefs(cwd)` outside coalesceRemoteStatus. Then do the coalesced 'refresh' with invalidateRemoteStatus + `workflow.remoteStatus({cwd})` (no fetch option) + updateCachedRemoteStatus(publish). Version ordering stays as it is, so a refresh still sees mutations that completed before its caller, and a concurrent 'load' never waits on the network. (2) In streamFullStatus (line 686), drop the `retainedRemotePoller ||` term so a stale cache always gets the no-fetch getOrLoadRemoteStatus. Tap refreshRemoteStatusAfterFetch only when !retainedRemotePoller, because the poller fetches. Together with (1), the poller's first fetch no longer blocks the first remote status, and a second subscriber on a retained poller no longer waits for the next poll tick. (3) ProviderCommandReactor.ts:734: fork the refreshStatus (forkIn the reactor scope or forkDetach, like ws/context.ts:1257 refreshGitStatus) so worktree recovery does not delay turn start on a fetch. Optional: in GitVcsDriverCore refreshStatusRemoteCacheEntry, return true only for exitCode 0, so a failed fetch neither counts as a ref move nor gets a 15 s success TTL; move the generation bump to successful fetches. Tests in VcsStatusBroadcaster.test.ts: (a) with automaticRemoteRefreshInterval=10s and a refreshRemoteTrackingRefs mock blocked on a Deferred, the stream yields remoteUpdated from remoteStatus before the fetch is released, and a second remote update arrives after release; (b) using TestClock, a second stream attaching to a retained 60 s poller with a remote cache older than 30 s receives remote status without advancing to the next tick; (c) a stream attaching while refreshStatus is blocked in its fetch gets its initial remote status without waiting. Update the existing poller tests near lines 817 and 904 that count remoteStatus calls or assume the poller is the first loader. Run focused checks only: `bun run test` filtered to VcsStatusBroadcaster.test.ts, GitManager.test.ts and ProviderCommandReactor tests, plus typecheck for apps/server.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Partial#199 Background git status reads run without GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, so they rewrite .git/index and take index.lock while agents run git in the same worktree

projects-loading:status-takes-optional-index-lock · original impact Medium, effort S · Reliability WP07A

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

Commit 60633eff3 (#710) added the central readOnly flag. It sets GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 and is applied as the auditor described, so `git status` no longer rewrites the index or takes index.lock. The fix still misses the main case. The next command in the same status read is a porcelain `git diff HEAD --numstat`, and porcelain `git diff` ignores GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS. In git's builtin/diff.c, cmd_diff calls refresh_index_quietly() (lock the index, refresh, write it) with no use_optional_locks() check whenever a tracked file has changed stat data but identical content, and diff.autoRefreshIndex defaults to true. The repo knows this already: GitIndexReview.ts:172 says diff paths refresh the index even with optional locks disabled. So after an agent or tool touches files (formatter rewrites, reverts, checkout), the index write and index.lock window that `git status` used to cause now comes from the numstat diff. The fix does remove the status-only writes (fsmonitor token, untracked cache, racy timestamps), but the finding's core claim, no index.lock contention from background reads, only partly holds.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:985 readOnly adds READ_ONLY_GIT_ENV (GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0) to the spawn env before input.env. The central option exists as proposed.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1619-1628 `git status --porcelain=2 --branch` uses readOnly: true. This part is fixed, because cmd_status honours use_optional_locks.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1651-1656 The hot-path `git diff HEAD --numstat` has readOnly: true, but porcelain git diff ignores GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS. It still takes index.lock and rewrites .git/index when any tracked file has changed stat data but identical content.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1675-1677 The fallback `git diff --numstat` (worktree vs index) has the same problem. The `diff --cached` sibling at 1678-1683 never refreshes the worktree, so it is fine.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitIndexReview.ts:172 The repo's own comment says some git diff paths refresh index stat data even with optional locks off. It works around this with a disposable index copy. The status path has no such workaround.
  • git/git master builtin/diff.c refresh_index_quietly + cmd_diff refresh_index_quietly() calls repo_hold_locked_index, refresh_index and repo_update_index_if_able. It runs when `1 < rev.diffopt.skip_stat_unmatch`, where skip_stat_unmatch = !!diff_auto_refresh_index. use_optional_locks does not appear in the file. The local git is 2.55.0.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/WorkspaceChangeSummary.ts:113-123 On-demand summary reads `git diff HEAD --stat` and `git diff HEAD --patch` with readOnly. It has the same porcelain-diff index write, on a less hot path.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1765-1784 Every numstat row becomes a workingTree file, including rows not in the status output. Turning off the diff's auto-refresh would surface stat-only files as 0/0 rows, so a filter against the status path set is needed.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.test.ts:427-428 The only test asserts call.readOnly === true on mocked calls. Nothing checks that the real index is left untouched or that the env reaches git.
Remaining

The two worktree numstat diffs on the status hot path still take .git/index.lock and rewrite the index whenever a tracked file has changed stat data but identical content: `diff HEAD --numstat` at apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1651-1656 and the fallback `diff --numstat` at 1675-1677. readOnly/GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 has no effect on porcelain `git diff`, which calls refresh_index_quietly unconditionally when diff.autoRefreshIndex is true. Agent `git add`/`commit` can therefore still hit 'index.lock: File exists' against Ryco's per-row/per-event status refresh after agents or tools touch files. Same on a cold path at apps/server/src/workspace/WorkspaceChangeSummary.ts:113-123.

Defects in the shipped fix

(1) The readOnly contract in GitVcsDriver.ts:69-74 says 'must never take optional locks'. It is not upheld for porcelain `git diff`, yet it is applied to the status-path diffs and WorkspaceChangeSummary diffs as if it were. The comment and the test give false confidence. (2) The test (GitVcsDriverCore.test.ts:427-428) checks only the flag on mocked calls. It does not cover env propagation (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:985) or real index immutability. (3) Unrelated pre-existing nit seen while reading: parseNumstatEntries (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:156-158) mishandles git's brace rename syntax (`src/{a => b}.ts` becomes `b}.ts`). Not part of this finding.

Implementation sketch

1) apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts readStatusDetailsLocal: prefix both worktree numstat diffs with `-c diff.autoRefreshIndex=false`: ["-c","diff.autoRefreshIndex=false","diff","HEAD","--numstat"] and the same for the `diff --numstat` fallback. This sets skip_stat_unmatch=0 in cmd_diff, so refresh_index_quietly never runs and the live index and index.lock are untouched. The plumbing diff-index/diff-files commands are equivalent. Optionally make it central instead: when input.readOnly is set in executeRaw (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:~985), also inject GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n=diff.autoRefreshIndex/GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n=false (git >= 2.31), merging with any caller GIT_CONFIG_* env. Then every readOnly porcelain diff, including WorkspaceChangeSummary.ts:113-123, honours the documented contract. 2) Side effect to handle: with auto-refresh off, files with only stat changes appear as `0\t0\tpath` rows. In readStatusDetailsLocal, after parseNumstatEntries (~1765), drop entries with insertions===0 && deletions===0 whose path is not in the status-derived set (changedFilesWithoutNumstat, built at ~1723-1727; collect it into a separate statusPaths set before the merge). Keep binary '-\t-' rows that are in status. WorkspaceChangeSummary may show empty 'diff --git' headers for such files; that is acceptable for summary input, or the --stat/--patch output can be filtered the same way. 3) Trade-off to note in a comment: Ryco then never heals stat-only entries, so each poll re-hashes them (status already does that lock-free) until an agent or user git command refreshes the index. This is the robustness-over-convenience choice AGENTS.md asks for. 4) Tests in GitVcsDriverCore.test.ts using a real temp repo (that file already has real-git tests): commit a file, utimes() it forward without changing content, snapshot .git/index bytes and mtime, call statusDetailsLocal, assert the index is byte-identical with the same mtime, workingTree.files is empty and hasWorkingTreeChanges is false. Second case: pre-create .git/index.lock, touch a file, call statusDetailsLocal, assert it succeeds and the lock file still exists unchanged. Add a mocked unit case where diff returns `0\t0\tsrc/touched.ts` with empty status, and assert files is []. Validate with `bun run test` scoped to apps/server/src/vcs and apps/server/src/workspace, plus `bun typecheck` for the server package.

Partial#200 On Windows, the repository identity probe goes through shell: true with unquoted -C <workspaceRoot>, so roots containing spaces never get an identity (and every probe pays an extra cmd.exe)

projects-loading:identity-probe-windows-shell-unquoted-paths · original impact Medium, effort S · Reliability WP07A

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

The reliability half is fixed. Since 60633eff3 the identity probe runs git through VcsProcess with no shell and with the root as cwd, so Windows roots with spaces resolve, and a test covers that case. The auditor's other claim is wrong for Windows: 'no cmd.exe, so the extra process-creation cost is gone'. VcsProcess adds an unconditional child.kill() finalizer (VcsProcess.ts:132). On win32, Effect's Node spawner turns every kill into an awaited `taskkill /pid N /T /F`, even after the process has already exited. So each probe still spawns a second process: taskkill.exe instead of cmd.exe. It now runs after git rather than alongside it, inside the git-pool slot and the 1 s probe timeout. A non-zero exit, such as rev-parse in a folder that is not a repo, costs two more taskkill runs: the spawner's release and its exit listener. Running taskkill /T /F against an exited PID cannot find that process's tree, and if Windows has reused the PID it can kill an unrelated process tree. Identity probes are now rare, because the same commit gated them behind a stat fingerprint and a 30-minute sweep. The identity-specific cost is therefore small, but the same redundant finalizer adds a taskkill to every VcsProcess git command on Windows.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:105-136 makeGitIdentityProbe runs vcsProcess.run({command:'git', args, cwd}) with no `-C <root>`. A failure or timeout maps to null. The comment names the Windows shell/space bug.
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:141-158 `rev-parse --show-toplevel` runs with cwd=root and `remote -v` with cwd=cacheKey, so the path never goes into argv. Reliability bug fixed.
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/RepositoryIdentityResolver.test.ts:260 A test 'resolves roots whose path contains spaces' exists. It runs on POSIX only, but the design change makes the result independent of the platform.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsProcess.ts:111-120 ChildProcess.make(command, args, {cwd, env}) sets no `shell`. buildSpawnOptions (apps/server/node_modules/@effect/platform-node-shared/src/internal/nodeChildProcessSpawner.ts:13) passes `shell: options.shell`, which is undefined, i.e. false. No cmd.exe.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsProcess.ts:132 `Effect.addFinalizer(() => child.kill().pipe(Effect.ignore))` is unconditional and runs on every scope close, including normal completion after exit.
  • apps/server/node_modules/@effect/platform-node-shared/src/NodeChildProcessSpawner.ts:99-108,396-418,478-498 handle.kill is terminateProcessGroup, which always calls signalGroup. On win32, killProcessGroup is an awaited execFile('taskkill', ['/pid', pid, '/T', '/F']). There is no is-running check, so an exited child still costs a taskkill.exe spawn and wait. Effect 4.0.2. The repo patch to this package only touches fd sinks.
  • apps/server/node_modules/@effect/platform-node-shared/src/NodeChildProcessSpawner.ts:548-573 On exit 0 under win32 the spawner's own acquireRelease release deliberately skips the group kill, and VcsProcess's finalizer defeats that. On a non-zero exit the release (awaited) and the 'exit' listener (fire-and-forget) each run taskkill as well, so a failed probe means git plus three taskkill runs. The release already kills a child that is still running, which makes the VcsProcess finalizer redundant.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsProcess.ts:214-217 Scope close, and with it the taskkill finalizer, happens inside governChildProcess and Effect.timeoutOption. taskkill latency holds a git-pool slot and counts toward the 1000 ms identity probe timeout (RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:97).
  • apps/server/src/project/repositoryIdentitySync.ts:1-8,43 Identity is now persisted. Probes run only when a stat-based git-config fingerprint changes, with a 30-minute sweep, so the '2 probes per project per 60 s' cadence no longer applies. Same commit, 60633eff3, so no stale nulls from the old buggy code were persisted.
  • apps/server/src/processRunner.ts:44-48,187-198 quoteWindowsShellArgument quotes only arguments that contain whitespace or are empty. Arguments without whitespace that contain cmd metacharacters (`&|<>^()`, e.g. `C:\R&D\proj`) and the command path itself are not quoted. This does not affect identity any more and only matters for other runProcess callers that keep shell:true.
  • apps/server/src/imports/claudeNativeFork.ts:39-41 Out of scope, but the same bug class. runProcess(process.execPath, ['--input-type=module', '-e', <multi-line script>]) uses the default Windows shell:true. An unquoted `C:\Program Files\...` execPath and a multi-line script both break under cmd.exe. It should pass shell:false.
Remaining

Of the finding's two claims, only the process-cost one is not met. apps/server/src/vcs/VcsProcess.ts:132 kills the child unconditionally when the scope closes. On Windows this spawns and awaits `taskkill /pid N /T /F` after every git command, the identity probes included, even after the process has exited. A probe therefore still costs two processes (git plus taskkill, now serial and inside the governor slot and the 1 s timeout) instead of the old cmd.exe plus git. A non-zero exit costs two more taskkill runs from Effect's own spawner (NodeChildProcessSpawner.ts:553-571). Running taskkill /T /F on an exited PID is pure overhead, and if Windows has reused the PID it kills an unrelated tree. Probes are now fingerprint-gated, so the identity share is small. The finalizer adds the cost to every VcsProcess git call on Windows.

Defects in the shipped fix

The fix routes the probe through VcsProcess. On win32, VcsProcess's redundant unconditional `child.kill()` finalizer (VcsProcess.ts:132) replaces the cmd.exe the fix removed with an awaited taskkill.exe after each command, plus two more taskkill runs on non-zero exits from @effect/platform-node-shared 4.0.2. Smaller caveats outside the identity path: quoteWindowsShellArgument does not quote metacharacter-only arguments (`&`, `^`, `|`, `<`, `>`) or the command itself, and leaves arguments containing `"` as they are. filesystem.ts:238-299 (git) and claudeNativeFork.ts:39 (execPath with a multi-line -e script) still use the default Windows shell:true. claudeNativeFork is likely broken outright on Windows. The optional combined `rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir` / `git config -z` probe was not adopted, and the fingerprint gating makes it largely moot.

Implementation sketch

1) apps/server/src/vcs/VcsProcess.ts:132: delete the `Effect.addFinalizer(() => child.kill()...)` line. The spawner's acquireRelease release (NodeChildProcessSpawner.ts:550-565) already terminates a referenced child that is still running when the scope closes, which covers interruption and Effect.timeoutOption. VcsProcess never unrefs. If an explicit intent is preferred, guard it instead: `Effect.addFinalizer(() => child.isRunning.pipe(Effect.flatMap((running) => running ? child.kill() : Effect.void), Effect.ignore))`. 2) Optional, larger: extend patches/@effect%2Fplatform-node-shared@4.0.2.patch (both src and dist) so that on win32, when the leader has already exited, the release branch (`code !== 0`) and the 'exit' listener's killProcessGroupOnExit skip taskkill. /T cannot walk the tree of a dead PID, and the PID may have been reused. Keep the POSIX behaviour. 3) Optional cleanup: pass `shell: false` for the git calls in apps/server/src/storage/filesystem.ts:238-299 and for process.execPath in apps/server/src/imports/claudeNativeFork.ts:39. Extend quoteWindowsShellArgument to also quote arguments containing `&|<>^()`. Tests: add a VcsProcess unit test with a stub ChildProcessSpawner whose handle counts kill() calls. Assert there is no kill after a normal exit (exit 0 and exit 1) and exactly one terminate on timeout or interrupt. Keep the RepositoryIdentityResolver tests, including 'resolves roots whose path contains spaces', and run the vcs and project tests (`bun run test` filtered to apps/server/src/vcs and apps/server/src/project). A manual Windows smoke check (Process Monitor, or counting taskkill.exe launches while polling git status) would confirm the saving.

Done#201 Repository identity is recomputed with 2 git spawns per project (60 s TTL) inside every shell snapshot and project lookup. A 1 s timeout silently nulls it and flips sidebar grouping

projects-loading:persist-repository-identity · original impact Medium, effort M · Caching WP05

Current state

#710 (60633eff3, also in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3) did what the finding asked. Identity is persisted in projection_projects (migration 086, plus a post-migrator repair). buildShell, listProjectShells, getProjectShellById, getActiveProjectByWorkspaceRoot and the command read model now decode the stored JSON with no resolver and no timeout. A background sync keeps the identity current: a startup sweep, a 30 min sweep, triggers on project.created and on root/kind changes, a spawn-free stat fingerprint of <commonDir>/config, a 24 h max age, and the background git lane. A changed identity is announced with an empty project.meta.update that keeps updatedAt. The resolver now goes through VcsProcess with cwd and no shell. The snapshot/lookup git cost and the snapshot-timeout null flips are gone. I agree with the auditor's main fix defect and found two more smaller ones. First, a failed or timed-out probe is persisted as null for up to 24 h. That was a 60 s negative TTL before. Second, remote changes, including Ryco's own publishRepository, now take up to 30 min to show up. Third, the shell stream sends null identity for new and moved projects until the background sync records one.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:3007 buildShell is labelled and implemented as pure SQL. Identity comes from decodePersistedRepositoryIdentity at :3129, :3227, :3267, :3364, :3384 and :2646. Nothing in this file references the resolver or uses timeoutOption.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts:567 resolveProject only calls getProjectShellById (SQL), so starting a turn no longer spawns git.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Migrations/086_ProjectionProjectRepositoryIdentity.ts:24 Adds the repository_identity_json, _fingerprint and _checked_at columns idempotently. It is registered at Migrations.ts:230 and repaired at :742-743.
  • apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/ProjectionProjects.ts:78 The upsert keeps the identity columns only while workspace_root is unchanged. The projector's meta-updated path (ProjectionPipeline.ts:692-720) rewrites the same root, so the sync's announcements never reset the identity. recordRepositoryIdentity (:161-174) is guarded by project_id and workspace_root.
  • apps/server/src/project/repositoryIdentitySync.ts:101 syncProject skips the probe when the fingerprint matches and the identity is under 24 h old. Otherwise it records whatever resolveFresh returns, null included, with the new fingerprint and checked_at (:115-127). It announces when the stored identity differs (:129-147). There is no failed state.
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:113 makeGitIdentityProbe maps a 1 s run-time timeout, a spawn failure and a non-zero exit all to null (:129, :135). refresh (:195-207) cannot tell 'not a repository' apart from 'probe failed'. VcsProcess.ts:214-217 confirms that queue time is excluded from the timeout.
  • apps/server/src/project/repositoryIdentityPersistence.ts:71 The fingerprint is stat-only: it walks to .git, follows .git files and commondir, and uses the config path, size and mtime. It returns null for a missing root, which keeps the last identity.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/decider.ts:655 An empty project.meta.update keeps updatedAt. toShellStreamEvent (orchestrationStreams.ts:268-279) re-reads the row and sends project-upserted. enrichProjectEvent (:444-469) sends the persisted identity on the full event stream.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:268 On project.created and root moves, the shell stream (used by the sidebar) reads the persisted row, which is still null at that point. The full event stream resolves live (:435, :459). The sidebar therefore shows null until the background sync records the identity and announces it.
  • apps/server/src/ws/sourceControlRpc.ts:338 publishRepository runs git.ensureRemote (SourceControlRepositoryService.ts:521) and only refreshes git status. Nothing triggers an identity sync, so the new remote waits for the 30 min sweep. Before #710, the next snapshot picked it up within the 60 s TTL.
  • apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts:1070 runRepositoryIdentitySync is started after the ready gate.
  • apps/server/src/project/repositoryIdentitySync.test.ts:136 Tests cover the fingerprint, staleness, chat/missing/deleted skips, the moved-root guard, event backpressure and triggers. Nothing tests a probe that fails or times out.
Defects in the shipped fix

1. Main defect, confirming the auditor: a transient probe failure is persisted as 'no repository'. - makeGitIdentityProbe (RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:113-136) turns a timeout (1 s of run time), a spawn error and any non-zero exit into null. refresh returns that null, and syncProject (repositoryIdentitySync.ts:115-127) writes it with the current fingerprint and checked_at. - The identity then stays null until the git config changes or 24 h pass. That holds across restarts, because the startup sweep sees 'fresh'. Before #710, the same failure was cached for only 60 s (negative TTL). - If a good identity existed, the null is announced live (:129-147), so every client regroups the project. - If the failure happens on the very first resolution, for example the first sweep after the upgrade on a slow Dropbox/CloudStorage root or a loaded Windows box, null is stored silently. - The effect goes beyond grouping. Everything keyed on project.repositoryIdentity disappears for that period: the sidebar remote link (apps/web/src/components/sidebar/sidebarProjectRemoteLink.ts:123), the logical project key (packages/client-runtime/src/state/workspace/logicalProjects.ts:57), the project repository section and the project map. - The trigger is now rarer than the old snapshot-wide timeout, but each failure lasts much longer. 2. Freshness regression for remote changes. Only project.created, root/kind changes and the 30 min sweep re-resolve an identity. - Ryco's own sourceControl.publishRepository adds a remote (SourceControlRepositoryService.ts:521; RPC at sourceControlRpc.ts:338-345) and never requests a sync, so a just-published project keeps a null identity for up to 30 min. - The same applies to an external `git remote add` or `set-url`. - Before #710, the next snapshot or priority refresh picked these up after at most the 60 s TTL. 3. Minor: the shell stream sends a null identity for new or moved projects. toShellStreamEvent (orchestrationStreams.ts:268-279) reads the persisted row, which is still null for project.created and is reset by a root move. enrichProjectEvent, on the full stream, resolves live instead. - The sidebar shows the non-repository grouping until the background sync records the identity and announces it. - That sync runs in the background lane behind the sync lock. After an upgrade it can sit behind the whole first git sweep. - Before #710, getProjectShellById resolved live. 4. Optional proposal items not done, and not needed to close the finding: identity still uses two spawns (rev-parse --show-toplevel, then remote -v), and pickPrimaryRemote (RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:32-45) ignores project.preferredRemoteName.

Implementation sketch

1. Persisted failure. - In RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts, make the probe return a three-way result: { kind: 'ok', stdout } | { kind: 'none' } | { kind: 'failed' }. - rev-parse exit 128 with 'not a git repository' in stderr counts as 'none'. - A timeout (VcsProcessTimeoutError), a spawn error or any other non-zero exit counts as 'failed'. - remote -v exit 0 with no remotes counts as 'none'; a non-zero exit counts as 'failed'. - Have `refresh` fail with a typed RepositoryIdentityProbeError, or return a tagged union, on 'failed'. Keep `resolve` returning null for compatibility, but do not cache failures: let the cache lookup fail so the existing onFailure: Duration.zero TTL applies, then catch it into null in `resolve`. - In repositoryIdentitySync.ts:syncProject, when refresh fails, do NOT call recordRepositoryIdentity and do NOT announce. Log at debug or warn and return a new 'failed' outcome. The stored identity, fingerprint and checked_at stay unchanged, so the next sweep retries. - Optionally keep an in-memory Map<projectId, failures> and schedule a retry for failed projects (for example after 1-2 min, with exponential backoff up to the 30 min sweep) through worker.enqueue. - Tests in repositoryIdentitySync.test.ts: (a) a stored identity plus a failing resolver: the identity is kept and no dispatch happens; (b) a never-resolved project plus a failing resolver: checked_at stays null and the next sync retries; (c) the resolver recovers: the identity is recorded and announced. - Resolver test: a timeout produces the failed state rather than null. Inject a VcsProcess double that fails with VcsProcessTimeoutError. 2. Freshness after Ryco-initiated remote changes. - Expose the sync as a small service, for example RepositoryIdentitySync with requestSyncForRoot(cwd). It maps cwd to projects whose workspaceRoot is inside the repository (listRepositoryIdentityStates plus a path-prefix match) and enqueues them on the existing DrainableWorker. - Call it from sourceControlRpc publishRepository (next to refreshGitStatus), and from any other server flow that runs ensureRemote or set-url. - The fingerprint changes because .git/config was rewritten, so the probe runs. - Test: after publishRepository, the project's identity is recorded and a project.meta-updated is dispatched without waiting for the sweep. - Optional: the sweep interval could drop to about 5 min, since a steady-state sweep is only a few stat calls per project. 3. Shell-stream null window. - In toShellStreamEvent, for project.created, and for project.meta-updated with payload.workspaceRoot, when the persisted identity is null, fill it from the cached resolver.resolve the same way enrichProjectEvent does. Pass the resolver in, or share a helper with enrichProjectEvent so the two stream paths agree. - Alternatively, let the sync's per-project path for a project.created trigger run in the interactive lane and skip the lock queue when no sweep is running. - Test: a project.created followed by a shell stream emits project-upserted with a non-null identity for a git root that has a remote. 4. Optional. - Collapse the probe into `git rev-parse --show-toplevel --git-common-dir` plus `git config -z --get-regexp '^remote\..*\.url$'`. - Honour project.preferredRemoteName in pickPrimaryRemote. That needs the sync to pass the project's preferred remote and the stored identity to be invalidated when preferredRemoteName changes.

Done#202 First subscribeShell starts a worktree reconciliation that loads 2 full shell snapshots per project (2P+1 total) plus 4 git spawns per project

projects-loading:reconcile-worktrees-snapshot-amplification · original impact Medium, effort M · Database WP05

Current state

Verified on main at ec250e386. The sweep no longer does 2P+1 whole shell snapshots. reconcileAllWorktrees reads listProjectShells once, then per project does one primary-key project read and one transaction with two indexed, column-narrow reads (getProjectWorkspaceRows). It passes those rows to both ensureProjectMainWorktree and the planner. The sweep starts 15 s after subscribeShell and runs its git in the background process lane. An in-memory registration fingerprint skips detection and `git worktree list` for unchanged repos, so a later sweep costs 0 git spawns. An architecture ratchet test bans new getShellSnapshot callers, and worktreeOperations.ts is not on its allow-list. Semantics match the old code: live non-deleted threads, live project worktrees, and a main row created mid-pass has a null path, which the planner ignores. One minor defect: an empty ("git could not answer") listing is cached and reused while the fingerprint stays the same.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/worktreeOperations.ts:910-964 reconcileAllWorktrees: 5-min throttle, Effect.sleep(RECONCILIATION_START_DELAY_MS=15s, line 74), readProjectShells (listProjectShells, no snapshot), concurrency 4, whole effect wrapped in inBackgroundProcessLane. The lane only affects child-process admission (processGovernor.ts:33-35, 109-124), so no permit is held during the sleep.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/worktreeOperations.ts:733-805 reconcileProjectWorktrees: getProjectShellById, then the fingerprint, then git only on a fingerprint miss, then getProjectWorkspaceRows once. rows.worktrees go to ensureProjectMainWorktree (no extra read) and the same rows feed planWorktreeReconciliation.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/worktreeOperations.ts:749-760 Defect: the tap caches `paths` even when it is [] (listWorktreePaths returns [] when the exit code is non-zero or detection says not-a-repo, GitVcsDriverCore.ts:3289-3305 and GitWorkflowService.ts:445-453). The planner treats [] as 'git could not answer' (worktreeReconciliation.ts:166-171).
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/worktreeListFingerprint.ts:22-69 Fingerprint = realpath(commonDir) + sorted worktrees/<name> + gitdir size and mtime. It returns null when <root>/.git is absent (subfolder projects, non-repos), so those always take the git path. When the worktrees dir is absent the value is `${commonDir}\0-`, so a .git dir that exists while git fails gets a stable non-null fingerprint.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:1001-1027,3592-3626 listProjectWorktreeRows plus listProjectThreadWorkspaceRows (5 columns, project_id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL) in one transaction. Index idx_projection_threads_project_deleted_created (migration 019) and idx_projection_worktrees_project_archived (migration 030). Same thread set as the old snapshot filter deletedAt === null.

  • apps/server/src/ws/context/worktreeOperations.test.ts:149-281 Tests cover: one project's rows instead of snapshots; git skipped while registrations are unchanged and re-run after a new worktrees/<name>/gitdir; 15 s delay via TestClock; background lane; chat and missing roots skipped. There is no test for an empty listing.
  • apps/server/src/ws/orchestrationRpc.ts:518-552 subscribeShell still forkDetaches reconcileAllWorktrees. Because of the delay and the narrow reads, it no longer competes with the shell snapshot that the subscription loads.
Remaining

Nothing required. Optional residuals, all low value: (a) knownWorktreeListings (worktreeOperations.ts:91-94) is in-memory. The first sweep after each restart still spawns up to 2 git processes per repo (combined rev-parse unless detection is cached, plus `git worktree list`), 15 s after the first subscribe and in the background lane. (b) reconcileProjectWorktrees re-reads each project via getProjectShellById (line 736) although the sweep already holds the shells from line 919: P cheap PK reads. (c) Projects whose root has no own .git (monorepo subfolders) never get a fingerprint and run git on every sweep. A non-repo project with no main row also costs 1 detection spawn per sweep via localStatus (line 306). (d) knownWorktreeListings never evicts deleted projects. The memory is trivial. (e) The sweep is still triggered by subscribeShell rather than a startup phase. For load the effect is the same.

Defects in the shipped fix

Minor: worktreeOperations.ts:749-760 caches an empty `git worktree list` answer whenever the fingerprint is non-null. That happens when <root>/.git exists but git exits non-zero or detection returns null. Examples: 'detected dubious ownership' before the user fixes safe.directory, or a .git dir that is partial or corrupt during a clone. The planner treats [] as 'git could not answer' and plans nothing. With no worktree churn, the fingerprint (`${commonDir}\0-`) stays the same after the repo becomes healthy, so reconciliation for that project stays a silent no-op until the server restarts or a worktree is added or removed. Before the fix it was retried every sweep. Timeouts and spawn errors fail the effect and are not cached, so only non-zero-exit and not-a-repo answers are affected. Nothing is corrupted (an empty plan does nothing), but the self-healing is lost.

Implementation sketch

1) Fix the defect (S). In reconcileProjectWorktrees (worktreeOperations.ts:750-759), store the entry only when `fingerprint !== null && paths.length > 0`, otherwise delete it. A real repository always lists at least its own root, so [] is never a trustworthy answer. Add a test in worktreeOperations.test.ts next to 'skips git worktree list while a repository's registrations are unchanged': run `git init` on a temp dir, make the listWorktreePaths stub return [] the first time and [root] the second, and assert git is called on both runs. 2) Optional (S): let reconcileProjectWorktrees take the OrchestrationProjectShell from the sweep's listProjectShells result (keep a projectId overload for other callers) to drop P getProjectShellById reads. 3) Optional (S): remove knownWorktreeListings entries for project ids missing from the current project list in reconcileAllWorktrees, next to the missingProjectRoots cleanup. 4) Optional (M, low value): persist {projectId, root, fingerprint, paths} (a small projection table or a JSON file under the server state dir) so the first post-restart sweep is also spawn-free. Load it lazily in the sweep and keep the same validation (root equality plus fingerprint match, and never persist []).

Done#203 Project icons spawn one node/Electron child per project, per connection, with no server cache and a 5 s budget that includes queue time

projects-loading:project-favicon-child-per-project-uncached · original impact Medium, effort M · Process spawns WP12A

Current state

Confirmed DONE, fixed by #710 (60633eff3; also in the Hub's vendored 7bc39eec3). The server now has one favicon resolver per server (server.ts:552). It keeps an in-memory cache with a 10 min TTL that also caches absent icons, dedupes in-flight reads, and batches up to 16 roots per isolated child with 2 children at once. It has per-child deadlines and a 30 s caller deadline in place of the old 5 s timeout that counted queue time. The client cache is keyed by environment + project + avatar revision, not by connection, and every ProjectFavicon (sidebar, palette, switcher, inbox) waits until it is near the viewport. The old per-connection, per-project spawn cost is gone. What is left is small: (1) a stalled or unfinished read still reaches clients as plain null, which the client caches as 'no icon' for 5 min; (2) when a child writes nothing, the first root of its batch is blamed and backs off; (3) the optional proposal parts (persisted fingerprint cache, iconRevision, ETag GET) were not built, so a new tab still sends cheap readIcon RPCs that hit the server cache.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:11 RESOLVED_ICON_TTL_MS 10 min, STALLED_ROOT_BACKOFF_MS 60 s, ICON_CACHE_CAPACITY 1024, READER_CHILDREN 2, ROOTS_PER_CHILD 16, READ_ICON_DEADLINE 30 s (lines 11-20). At f1be4abc7 this was Semaphore(2) + Effect.timeout('5 seconds') around permit + child, with no cache.
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:113 readIcon: cache hit, else join the pending deferred, else queue. Found and absent icons are remembered (line 80). Unavailable roots are not; the first one gets a 60 s backoff (line 87) and the rest get one retry child (89-93).
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:552 ProjectFaviconResolverLive is provided once at runtime level, so the cache and batching are shared across connections and tabs (ws/context.ts:292 only looks the service up).
  • apps/server/src/project/readProjectFavicon.ts:73 readProjectFavicons spawns one process.execPath --eval child for many roots. Its deadline is 1.5 s + 250 ms per extra root (105-108), and roots it finished survive a kill (114-125). The worker (projectFaviconWorker.ts:98-112) writes one JSON line per root, which keeps the cloud-file isolation.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/projectIconSource.ts:53 entryKey = project + avatar revision inside a per-environment LRU (64 entries / 8 MiB). There is no connectedAt or generation, so reconnects and remounts reuse icons for PROJECT_ICON_TTL_MS = 5 min. Rejected reads are not cached.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/projectIconSource.ts:97 Residual: a null result is cached for 5 min like a real 'no icon'. The server cannot say 'unavailable' because ProjectReadIconResult is Schema.NullOr(...) (packages/contracts/src/project.ts:204) and readProjectIcon.ts:32-33 turns every resolver null into null.
  • apps/web/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:82 Every web ProjectFavicon waits until it is near the viewport (useHasIntersectedViewport, effect at 93-107 needs `visible`). The sidebar also defers by header (SidebarProjectHeader.tsx:85, 129). Proposal part 4 is done for all web callers.
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/ProjectFaviconResolver.test.ts:84 Tests cover shared children (<=2 batches for 20 roots, none on re-read), no negative caching of unfinished reads with a 60 s backoff (116-148), and recovery from a broken batch (152-182). The broken-batch test also shows root '/a' gets null and backs off after a spawn failure.
  • apps/server/src/http.ts:750 The legacy GET /api/project-favicon uses the same cached resolver. It still sends no ETag or validators (proposal part 3 not done) and accepts any cwd, which is pre-existing behaviour behind auth.
Remaining

Nothing that keeps the original cost (per-connection, per-project spawns with no server cache) alive. Optional leftovers: (a) the server cache is memory-only with a fixed 10 min TTL and no stat fingerprint (ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:11, 80). After a restart or TTL expiry the next near-viewport request spawns ceil(P/16) children again, and a newly added or changed repo icon can be stale for up to 10 + 5 min. (b) There is no iconRevision on the project shell, so a new tab, or a remount after the 5 min client TTL, still sends readIcon RPCs for near-viewport rows. These hit the server cache, but over a Hub relay found icons are resent as base64 (up to about 683 KiB). (c) GET /api/project-favicon (http.ts:733-765) has no ETag or immutable caching.

Defects in the shipped fix

Minor, no regression versus f1be4abc7: (1) An unfinished read (stall, child deadline, spawn failure, 30 s caller deadline) is settled as null (ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:70, 88, 92, 128) and goes over the wire as null. The client cannot tell it from 'no icon', caches it for 5 min (projectIconSource.ts:97-104), and a mounted row never refetches until it remounts or reconnects (ProjectFavicon.tsx:93-107). So 'timed-out results must not be negative-cached as no icon' only holds on the server; these cases are now rare. (2) Blame for a stall goes to 'the first unfinished root' (ProjectFaviconResolver.ts:84-88). When a child writes nothing at all (slow Electron start under boot load, spawn error), root 0 is backed off for 60 s and shows the fallback even though it did not stall. (3) Cache memory is bounded by entries, not bytes (1024 x up to 512 KiB in theory). The legacy HTTP route takes any cwd, so an authenticated caller could fill it. This is low risk.

Implementation sketch

Only worth doing as cleanup. (1) Unavailable vs absent: make ProjectFaviconResolverShape.readIcon return a three-way result (found / absent / unavailable), or fail with a tagged ProjectIconUnavailable on unavailable, stalled-backoff and deadline paths in ProjectFaviconResolver.ts. In readProjectIcon.ts map unavailable to the existing ProjectReadIconError so the RPC rejects; projectIconSource already skips caching rejections. In http.ts, serve the fallback SVG with Cache-Control: no-store for unavailable. Optionally have web and mobile ProjectFavicon retry once after about 60 s on rejection. Tests: extend ProjectFaviconResolver.test.ts so a stalled root yields 'unavailable' rather than null; add a projectRpc test that the RPC errors; projectIconSource.test.ts already covers 'retries failed reads'. (2) Stall attribution: have readProjectFavicons report how many lines the child wrote (or whether it exited from the deadline vs a spawn error). In readBatch, when zero lines arrived, retry the whole batch once without backing off root 0. Add a resolver test for 'child emits nothing, then succeeds'. (3) Optional: add a byte budget to the server cache (reuse @ryco/shared/lruCache with a byte cap), and/or the proposal's iconRevision (hash of found bytes, or 'none') on OrchestrationProjectShell so clients can skip readIcon, plus an ETag on /api/project-favicon. The iconRevision part touches contracts and the projection, so it is M effort for little gain.
