Partial#204 Local status resolves the base branch twice and does one spawn per config/ref lookup; remote status recomputes the whole local status

projects-loading:status-pipeline-redundant-git-calls · original impact Medium, effort M · Process spawns WP07A

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor rated the remote half done ('reuses the local details', 0 to 2 git spawns plus gh). That holds only when no fetch completed during the call and the local details are under 5 s old. On upstream-tracked branches a fetch usually completes: the stream-open background republish, refreshStatus after agent or git actions once 15 s have passed since the last fetch, and polling. Then readRemoteStatus re-runs the full 6-8-spawn local pipeline with working-tree scans, not the proposed single `rev-list --left-right --count`, and refreshStatusUpstream adds 3 serial spawns per read. The auditor also missed that a failed fetch counts as completed, the in-flight race where pre-fetch local details get a post-fetch timestamp (GitManager.ts:860-861 vs :1686), and that no test covers the reuse.

Current state

The local half is fixed. A feature-branch local status resolves the base once, reads config from one cached `git config -z --list` snapshot and caches results by commit pair: 8 spawns cold and 6 warm, which the GitVcsDriverCore test pins. The remote half is only partly fixed. GitManager reuses the local details only if they are under 5 s old and no fetch completed in that call. Branches with an upstream usually do complete a fetch: the background fetch after a stream opens, refreshStatus after agent or git actions once 15 s have passed since the last fetch, and opt-in polling. In those cases readRemoteStatus re-runs the full local pipeline (6-8 spawns, including the working-tree scans `git status --porcelain=2` and `git diff HEAD --numstat`) where the proposal asked for a single `rev-list --left-right --count`. Each fetch-enabled remote read also spends 3 serial spawns resolving the upstream and common dir, and the snapshot already holds that data. Totals are still roughly halved: first load about 44 to about 22 spawns, with only about 10 on the critical path. The auditor treated the re-run after a fetch as intended and missed three things: a failed fetch also counts as a completed one, a narrow race in the reuse, and the missing test coverage.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1649-1755 Confirmed fixed. The status wave runs status, diff HEAD, symbolic-ref origin/HEAD and the config snapshot. The base is resolved once (needsBase, statusBaseBranchContext, one for-each-ref, one rev-parse) and shared by the ahead count, the ahead-of-default count and the committed diff.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.test.ts:365-436 This test pins the cold feature-branch local status at 8 spawns, all read-only, and checks that rev-list and the three-dot diff are skipped on a warm commit pair. That matches the proposal's target of about 6.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.ts:942-947 readRemoteStatus uses takeRecentLocalStatusDetails(cwd). If that returns null (older than 5 s, or dropped by a fetch) it calls gitCore.statusDetailsLocal, which is the full local pipeline including the working-tree scans. The remote result only needs hasUpstream, ahead/behind, aheadOfDefault, branch, upstreamRef and isDefault.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.ts:1679-1690 When refreshStatusUpstream returns true, the reused local details are deleted. So every completed fetch makes the next remote read re-run the whole local pipeline, not just recompute the counts that depend on the upstream.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:508-523 On first stream load, refreshRemoteStatusAfterFetch forks a background fetch. If a fetch completed, it republishes through remoteStatus, which re-runs the full local pipeline. This runs on every stream open for an upstream-tracked branch when the last fetch was over 15 s ago, even if the fetch moved nothing.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:487-501 refreshRemoteStatus (used by refreshStatus after agent turns and git actions, the RPC, and polling) always passes fetch:true, so on upstream-tracked branches the local details are usually dropped and the pipeline re-runs.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1268-1318 fetchRemoteForStatus uses allowNonZeroExit, and the generation is bumped in `ensuring`. A fetch that fails with a non-zero exit (offline, auth error) still reports fetched=true, drops the reuse and triggers a full-pipeline republish. It is also cached with the 15 s success TTL instead of the failure cooldown.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1241-1263,1290-1298,1330-1344 Each fetch:true remote read runs `rev-parse --abbrev-ref @{upstream}`, then `git remote`, then `rev-parse --git-common-dir`: 3 serial spawns even when the fetch cache is warm. The config snapshot (branch.<b>.remote, remoteNames) and the already-read `# branch.upstream` line hold the same data, and the common dir never changes for a given cwd.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.ts:854-861 Race: readLocalStatus stores the details with atMs = Date.now() after the read finishes. A read that started before a fetch completed (its `git status --branch` saw the old tracking refs) can finish after the delete at :1686. Its pre-fetch ahead/behind then look fresh for 5 s, and a later remote read that does not complete a fetch itself (for example the next poll with the 15 s fetch cache warm) reuses them and caches them for 30 s. This window is narrow and is new in #710.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1076-1082,2598-2601 Any execute without readOnly runs Cache.invalidateAll on the config snapshot and branch listing for every cwd. That includes status fetches, checkpoint rev-parse and ls-files reads, and many reads that never set readOnly. This is correct but coarse: with many open folders the 5 s snapshot rarely survives, so each status pays its own `config --list`.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/SourceControlProviderRegistry.ts:682-699 Not done from the proposal. Provider detection still spawns `git remote -v` through GitVcsDriver.listRemotes (GitVcsDriver.ts:590-597, 5 s TTL), and RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:149 spawns it again under its own 60 s cache. No RepoFacts per gitCommonDir exists, and the snapshot is cached per cwd.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.test.ts:1425-1461 No test covers remote status reusing local details, dropping them after a fetch, or the in-flight race. The only status-cache test counts gh calls, not git spawns.
Remaining

(1) After a completed fetch, or once the local details are over 5 s old, GitManager.readRemoteStatus (GitManager.ts:942-947) re-runs gitCore.statusDetailsLocal. That is 6-8 spawns including `git status --porcelain=2` and `git diff HEAD --numstat`, where the proposal asked for `rev-list --left-right --count @{upstream}...HEAD` plus a re-resolved ahead-of-default count. This happens on every stream-open background republish (VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:508-523), on refreshStatus after agent or git actions for upstream-tracked branches when the last fetch was over 15 s ago (:487-501, GitManager.ts:1684-1688), and on every opt-in poll. (2) A fetch with a non-zero exit still counts as fetched (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1268-1318), which drops the reuse and causes a republish for nothing. (3) refreshStatusUpstreamIfStale spends 3 serial spawns per fetch:true read (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1241-1263, 1290-1298) on data the snapshot and the status details already hold. (4) `git remote -v` is still spawned separately by SourceControlProviderRegistry.detectProviderContext (:682-699) and RepositoryIdentityResolver (:149). There is no RepoFacts per common dir and no base-branch memo per (commonDir, refName). (5) The snapshot invalidation is global (invalidateAll on any non-readOnly execute, GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1076-1082, 2598-2601).

Defects in the shipped fix

(a) Race in the local-details reuse, new in #710. readLocalStatus (GitManager.ts:860-861) stamps the details when the read completes, not when it starts, and records no fetch generation. A local read in flight when a fetch completes can store pre-fetch ahead/behind after refreshRemoteTrackingRefsForKey (GitManager.ts:1686) deleted the entry. A later remote read within 5 s that does not complete a fetch itself reuses them, and the stale behind count is then cached for 30 s and published. invalidateLocalStatusResultCache (GitManager.ts:885-893) has the same delete-then-repopulate problem. (b) A failed fetch (non-zero exit) is reported as completed (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1306-1318), so offline or unauthenticated repos re-run the full local pipeline on each fetch cycle and skip the failure cooldown. (c) No tests cover the remote reuse path, its invalidation after a fetch, or the race.

Implementation sketch

1) Lean upstream counts. In GitVcsDriverCore add `readTrackingCounts(cwd, { branch, upstreamRef, isDefaultBranch })` and expose it on GitVcsDriverShape. It runs `git rev-list --left-right --count @{upstream}...HEAD` (readOnly) for ahead/behind. For aheadOfDefaultCount it reuses the snapshot-based statusBaseBranchContext, resolveBaseBranchForNoUpstream, resolveBaseCommitPair and the aheadCountCache (1 for-each-ref, 1 rev-parse, rev-list cached by pair). It never runs status or diff HEAD. 2) In GitManager, replace delete-on-fetch with generations. Keep `fetchGenerationByCwd` and `localGenerationByCwd` maps. readLocalStatus captures both generations before calling statusDetailsLocal and stores them with the details. refreshRemoteTrackingRefsForKey bumps the fetch generation instead of deleting, and invalidateLocalStatusResultCache bumps the local generation. In readRemoteStatus: if the entry's local generation is current and it is under 5 s old, reuse the whole entry when the fetch generation also matches. If only the fetch generation differs, and readCheckoutHead(cwd) (spawn-free, vcs/gitCheckoutHead.ts) still shows the same branch, overlay readTrackingCounts on the cached details. Otherwise fall back to statusDetailsLocal. This fixes the race and removes the post-fetch pipeline re-run. 3) Make fetchRemoteForStatus return the exit code, and bump the generation and return true only when exitCode === 0. Optionally compare the upstream oid before and after so a no-op fetch skips the republish. Non-zero exits should get the failure cooldown. 4) refreshStatusUpstreamIfStale: take the upstream remote from readConfigSnapshot (`branch.<b>.remote`, with b from readCheckoutHead) plus snapshot.remoteNames, instead of `rev-parse @{upstream}` and `git remote`. Cache `rev-parse --git-common-dir` per resolved cwd with a long TTL or take it from the VcsDriverRegistry detection. 3 spawns become 0 in steady state. 5) Optional: build listRemotes and RepositoryIdentityResolver remotes from readConfigSnapshot (remote.<n>.url and pushurl). Caveat: `git remote -v` applies `url.<base>.insteadOf` and `pushInsteadOf` rewrites and raw config does not, so apply those rewrites from the snapshot or keep `remote -v` for those two callers. Narrow invalidateReadCaches to the command's cwd or common dir, and mark pure reads readOnly (CheckpointStore rev-parse and ls-files, runGitStdout reads). Tests: GitManager.test.ts with a counting executeOverride or spy. (i) localStatus then remoteStatus runs exactly one `status --porcelain=2`. (ii) After a simulated successful fetch, remoteStatus issues `rev-list --left-right` and no `status` or `diff HEAD`. (iii) A fetch that completes while a local read is in flight is not reused (use a Deferred to hold the read). (iv) A fetch with exit 128 does not invalidate. GitVcsDriverCore.test.ts: refreshStatusUpstream spawns no `git remote` or `rev-parse @{upstream}` when the snapshot is warm. Validate with the existing VcsDriverContractHarness and focused `bun run test` on apps/server's git and vcs test files.

Value low · effort M · risk medium

Partial#205 PR discovery runs one gh pr list per worktree branch with heavy GraphQL fields (mergeable, comments, statusCheckRollup…) but uses only 6 of them

projects-loading:pr-lookup-heavy-fields-per-worktree · original impact Medium, effort M · Network / RTT WP07B

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

The auditor is right about the main GitHub path. #710 (60633eff3) added the lean GITHUB_PULL_REQUEST_SUMMARY_LIST_JSON_FIELDS set and a per-repository PR index (Effect Cache: single-flight, 60 s TTL, 10 s on failure). Status, refSummary (sidebar badges) and worktree discovery all use it, and a lean per-branch query runs only as a fallback. GitLab and Azure are also fine. But proposal item 3 (other providers) is not correctly done, and the auditor missed it. (a) Bitbucket regression: Bitbucket caps pagelen at 50, and the index marks a listing complete when items.length < 100. A 50-row Bitbucket page therefore always counts as complete, the open listing and per-branch fallback never run, and in a repo with 50+ PRs any branch whose PR is not among the 50 most recently updated shows no PR (status, sidebar badge, worktree discovery). Before the change, the per-branch query filtered server-side on source.branch.name and found it. (b) Forgejo: the index's repo-wide listing (empty headSelector) takes the page-list path. That path ignores includeStackSummary:false and fields:'summary' and runs withRowReadiness: up to 50 /commits/{sha}/status reads per index refresh, at concurrency 6, behind a 20 s row cache that has expired by each 60 s refresh. So the Forgejo index listing is heavier than the old per-branch lists. Forgejo also caps at 50, so it has the same complete-flag mislabel. That one is not a regression, because the old per-branch path already filtered only the 20 newest PRs client-side.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/pullRequestIndex.ts:79-92 Index listing: headSelector '', limit PULL_REQUEST_INDEX_LIMIT (100), includeStackSummary false, fields 'summary'. complete = items.length < 100, regardless of the page size the provider actually honours.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/pullRequestIndex.ts:180-185 When the 'all' listing is complete, the lookup resolves at once with recentMatch (possibly null). The open listing and per-branch fallback are skipped.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/BitbucketApi.ts:1127 pagelen = min(limit ?? 20, 50) and no pagination is followed. A 100-limit index read returns at most 50 rows, so complete is always true. The old per-branch path (line 1122) filtered server-side with source.branch.name = "X" and found PRs of any age.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/ForgejoApi.ts:48 DEFAULT_PAGE_LIMIT = 50. clampLimit (576-577) caps every list at 50, which gives the same always-complete mislabel. The old per-branch path filtered the newest 20 client-side (1089-1094), so this part is not a regression.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/ForgejoApi.ts:1069-1096 An empty head selector means pageList=true, which runs page.withRowReadiness(input, list) on the index listing. ForgejoSourceControlProvider.ts:199-209 does not forward includeStackSummary or fields.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/ForgejoPullRequestPageApi.ts:581-617 withRowReadiness reads the head commit status for up to FORGEJO_ROW_STATUS_MAX (50, line 202) open rows at READ_CONCURRENCY 6. The shared read TTL is 20 s (line 198), so every 60 s index refresh re-reads them. Status reads never use this readiness data.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/GitHubSourceControlProvider.ts:588-598 On GitHub, fields==='summary' uses the lean set with no statusCheckRollup retry. The core of the finding is fixed here.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.ts:1221-1281 findLatestPrInIndex resolves from the index first. The per-head-selector fallback runs only when the index is unresolved, and it uses fields:'summary' and limit 20. At line 1232 an index read error becomes null, which leads to a per-branch fallback.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:354-355 discoverPullRequest = refSummary(cwd).pr, which goes through findLatestPr and the index, not a full remoteStatus.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.ts:1861-1873 invalidateRemoteStatus drops the whole repository index. VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:495 calls it on every explicit refresh and on every opt-in remote poll (gitStatusPollIntervalMs, default 0), so the 60 s sharing is defeated while polling is enabled.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.test.ts:1576-1625 Index tests cover only GitHub (gh). No test covers Bitbucket or Forgejo listing caps or Forgejo readiness on the index path, and pullRequestIndex.ts has no unit test file.
Remaining

Forgejo index listing is not lean. ForgejoSourceControlProvider.ts:199-209 and ForgejoApi.ts:1069-1096 run page.withRowReadiness on the index's repo-wide list, ignoring includeStackSummary:false and fields:'summary'. That adds up to 50 commit-status requests per index refresh (ForgejoPullRequestPageApi.ts:581-617).

Defects in the shipped fix

1) Correctness regression (Bitbucket): pullRequestIndex.ts:91 sets complete = items.length < 100, but BitbucketApi.ts:1127 caps pagelen at 50 with no pagination. Every Bitbucket index listing is therefore 'complete', and lookupIndexedChangeRequest (pullRequestIndex.ts:183-185) resolves with match null (or an older finished match) for any branch whose PR is outside the 50 most recently updated. The branch then loses its PR in status, sidebar badge and worktree discovery, whereas the pre-index per-branch query (server-side source.branch.name filter) found it. Forgejo has the same mislabel (ForgejoApi.ts:48/576, cap 50). That is not a regression there, but it means the 'open' listing is never consulted. 2) Minor: when the index read fails (offline, no auth), GitManager.ts:1232 maps the failure to null, so every branch still runs 1-3 failing per-branch calls; the 10 s failure TTL protects only the index call. 3) Minor and opt-in: with gitStatusPollIntervalMs > 0, each full-status poller's invalidateRemoteStatus (GitManager.ts:1861-1873, via VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:495) drops the shared index every tick. In repos with 100+ PRs, a branch without a recent PR then costs an all-list, an open-list and 1-3 per-branch calls per poll, against 1-3 per-branch calls before.

Implementation sketch

A) Provider-aware completeness. Add an optional `listLimitCap?: number` to SourceControlProviderShape: Bitbucket 50, Forgejo 50, GitHub/GitLab/Azure unset or 100. Expose it through bindProviderContext in SourceControlProviderRegistry. In pullRequestIndex.ts listIndex, use `const limit = Math.min(PULL_REQUEST_INDEX_LIMIT, provider.listLimitCap ?? PULL_REQUEST_INDEX_LIMIT)`, pass it as the limit, and set `complete: items.length < limit`. Forgejo servers can cap below 50 (MAX_RESPONSE_ITEMS), so a stricter alternative is to have Bitbucket return `next` and Forgejo return the Link or X-Total-Count header, and mark complete only when there is no next page. With completeness fixed, Bitbucket falls back to the 'open' listing and then to the server-side source.branch.name per-branch query, which restores correctness. Optionally make Forgejo's per-branch fallback useful by querying GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{base}/{head} or by paginating. B) Lean Forgejo index listing. In ForgejoSourceControlProvider.listChangeRequests, forward `readiness: input.includeStackSummary !== false && input.fields !== 'summary'` into forgejo.listPullRequests. In ForgejoApi.listPullRequests, call page.withRowReadiness only when pageList && readiness; it is fine to keep sharedPullRequest.remember. C) Optional: in findLatestPrInIndex, propagate the index read error, or skip the per-branch fallback when the index failed within the failure TTL, instead of mapping it to null. Optional: let poll-driven refreshRemoteStatus invalidate the per-cwd remote status only and let the index's 60 s TTL govern, keeping the full index drop for explicit user refreshes, git actions and agent turns. Tests: pullRequestIndex unit test where a fake provider with listLimitCap 50 returns 50 rows, asserting complete=false and that the open listing is read. GitManager or Bitbucket integration test with 50 unrelated recent PRs plus an older open PR on the branch, asserting the PR is found. Forgejo provider test asserting that listChangeRequests({headSelector:'', includeStackSummary:false, fields:'summary'}) makes no /commits/{sha}/status requests.

Partial#206 No process-wide concurrency limit or priority for git/gh/glab child processes

projects-loading:no-global-child-process-limiter · original impact Medium, effort M · Process spawns WP07B

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The auditor marked this DONE. Three things were missed. (1) The interactive lane is the default and is unbounded, and the inbox sidebar's per-row change-request-detail RPC (sourceControlRpc.ts:585-603, InboxThreadRow.tsx:219) was never tagged as background, so it still launches about 4 gh children per visible PR row with no limit. (2) The in-flight metric was not implemented. (3) Shared Effect Cache single-flights inherit the first caller's lane, so interactive status can still wait behind background queues through configSnapshotCache, the PR index and the status-fetch cache plus statusFetchPermits.

Current state

The core of the proposal landed in #710 (60633eff3), and the projects-sidebar git burst is gone. A process-wide ProcessGovernor has a git pool (min(8, cores)), a forge pool (4) for gh, glab and az, interactive and background lanes, and a queue-wait timer. It is wired into VcsProcess.run, the git driver's executeRaw and processRunner.runProcess. The identity probe now runs through VcsProcess with no shell, and queue time no longer counts toward its 1 s timeout. Sidebar ref summaries, identity sync, worktree reconcile and the linked-worktree sweeps run in the background lane. The auditor's DONE overstates it, for three reasons: 1. The lane is chosen per call site and defaults to interactive, which is unbounded. The inbox sidebar's per-row PR detail query still fires one `gh pr view` plus up to three `gh api` children for every visible row with a linked PR, in the interactive lane. That is the same many-row forge burst, and the forge pool does not bound it. 2. The proposal's in-flight metric was never exported. processGovernorStats() has no production caller. 3. Interactive callers can still wait behind the background queue. Effect's Cache runs a lookup in the first caller's context, so when a background fiber starts a shared single-flight lookup (git config snapshot, PR index, status upstream fetch), an interactive caller that joins it inherits the background queue position.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/processGovernor.ts:29-38,95-137 ProcessLaneRef defaults to interactive. GIT_PROCESS_LIMIT = min(8, max(2, cores)) and FORGE_PROCESS_LIMIT = 4. Interactive requests are always granted at once and only count toward the pool. Background requests queue FIFO when the pool is full or has waiters.
  • apps/server/src/processGovernor.ts:165-207 processGovernorStats() exists, but only tests call it (git grep finds no production caller). The only real metric is the ryco_process_governor_queue_wait_duration timer, and it is recorded only when the wait is above 0. There is no in-flight gauge, although the proposal asked for one.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsProcess.ts:159-160,214-233 run() is governed, with queue time outside the timeout. The public withProcess() is not governed. Today only run() calls it, so this is a latent hole.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1050-1054 Every git child is wrapped in governChildProcess("git").
  • apps/server/src/processRunner.ts:168-176 runProcess is governed through governChildProcessPromise. The new `lane` option is never passed by any caller, so these spawns are always interactive.
  • apps/server/src/project/Layers/RepositoryIdentityResolver.ts:113-136,195-207 The identity probe goes through vcsProcess.run with no shell and READ_ONLY_GIT_ENV. refresh() probes outside the caches on purpose, so an interactive resolve() does not wait behind background git.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:522,706 The background fetch-and-republish and the sidebar `summary` stream run in the background lane. The web sidebar rows use view:"summary" (SidebarThreadRow.tsx:144, InboxThreadRow.tsx:208).
  • apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/InboxThreadRow.tsx:199,219-224 Every visible inbox row whose row.pullRequest is set (the persisted link is available at boot, with no wait for the summary) calls useSourceControlChangeRequestDetail. Nothing limits this on the client side.
  • apps/server/src/ws/sourceControlRpc.ts:585-603 The sourceControlGetChangeRequestDetail handler runs provider.getChangeRequestDetail in the default interactive lane. It is not wrapped in inBackgroundProcessLane.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/GitHubSourceControlProvider.ts:657-701 Each detail is `gh pr view` followed by stack, merge-capabilities and required-checks lookups, run with concurrency 3 and none cached. That is up to 4 or more gh children per row, all interactive, so N visible PR rows launch about 4N concurrent gh processes. This repeats on every poll.
  • apps/server/node_modules/effect/src/Cache.ts:216-218,638,671 A Cache lookup is forked from the first caller's fiber with the caller's context merged over the construction context. ProcessLaneRef is therefore inherited from whichever caller arrives first.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1145-1173,1666 The configSnapshotCache is shared by full status (interactive, line 1666) and the sidebar refSummary (background, GitManager.ts:1739). An interactive status that joins a lookup a background fiber started waits behind the background git queue.
Remaining

1. Lane coverage gap, which matters most. The inbox sidebar's per-row PR detail is still an unbounded forge burst. InboxThreadRow.tsx:219-224 queries detail for every visible row with a linked PR. The server handler at ws/sourceControlRpc.ts:585-603 runs it in the default interactive lane, and GitHubSourceControlProvider.ts:657-701 spawns 1 `gh pr view` plus up to 3 `gh api` calls per row with no cache. The forge pool (FORGE_PROCESS_LIMIT = 4) never bounds this, at boot or on polls. The finding's goal of about 4 concurrent gh/glab children does not hold in inbox mode. 2. The proposal's in-flight metric is missing. processGovernorStats() (processGovernor.ts:165) is not exported to metrics or diagnostics, and only the queue-wait timer exists. 3. 'Interactive never waits behind background' does not fully hold. Shared single-flight caches inherit the lane of the first caller: configSnapshotCache (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1145-1173, used at 1666 and at GitManager.ts:1739), the pullRequestIndex Cache (pullRequestIndex.ts:96-111, used at GitManager.ts:960 and 1799), and statusRemoteRefreshCache plus statusFetchPermits (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1267-1343). An interactive caller that joins a lookup a background fiber started waits behind that fiber's position in the background queue. The delay is bounded by how long the background queue takes to drain, typically under a second at boot.

Defects in the shipped fix

1. Priority inversion through shared Cache single-flights, described in remaining item 3. A background-lane fiber owns the lookup, and interactive joiners inherit its queue position. statusFetchPermits is also held while the governed fetch is queued in the background lane, so an interactive status fetch for another repository can block on that semaphore. 2. VcsProcess.withProcess (VcsProcess.ts:55,159-160) is a public spawn entry point that is not governed. It has no external caller today, so this is latent. 3. processRunner's `lane` option has no callers, and the Promise path cannot be cancelled while queued. That is harmless today because every caller is interactive. 4. No correctness bugs in ProcessPool itself. Release is idempotent, cancel on interrupt both withdraws the request and releases a permit already granted, and the tests cover queuing and cancellation.

Implementation sketch

A. Inbox PR detail in the background lane (S, highest value). - Add an optional schema-only field to the change-request-detail RPC input in packages/contracts, for example `priority: "background"`. - In apps/server/src/ws/sourceControlRpc.ts:585-603, wrap the provider.getChangeRequestDetail(...) effect in inBackgroundProcessLane when the field is set. Apply the same to any other per-row passive read handlers. - In apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/InboxThreadRow.tsx:219, pass the flag for non-active rows (`!props.active`). The selected row and PullRequestDetail stay interactive. - Cheaper alternative with no contract change: have the inbox glyph use the summary stream's pr/state, which already comes from the PR index, and fetch full detail only on hover or for the active row. - Tests: a server test like RepositoryIdentityResolver.test.ts:300-335 that fills the forge pool with interactive holders, issues a background-flagged detail, and asserts processGovernorStats().forge.queued === 1. Add a browser test that a non-active InboxThreadRow sends the flag. B. In-flight metric (S). - In processGovernor.ts, add a Metric.gauge("ryco_process_governor_in_flight") with pool and lane attributes, plus a queued gauge. - Update both from ProcessPool grant, release and enqueue through an onChange hook, or sample processGovernorStats() in LocalDiagnosticsMetrics or Diagnostics. - Unit test: the gauges follow inFlight and queued across request and release. C. Priority inversion (M, optional). - Give ProcessPool waiters a promote() that moves a queued background request to an immediate grant. - Add a small `sharedLookupScope` Context.Reference (a mutable record of pending permit requests plus a promoted flag) that governChildProcess registers queued requests into. - Wrap the lookups of configSnapshotCache, pullRequestIndex and statusRemoteRefreshCache so that a joining caller whose ProcessLaneRef is interactive marks the owner's scope as promoted and promotes its queued requests. Later requests in a promoted scope are then admitted as interactive. - In fetchRemoteForStatus, acquire the governor permit before statusFetchPermits, for example by moving the semaphore inside a governChildProcess call, so a queued background fetch does not hold a fetch slot. - Test: a background fiber starts Cache.get, which queues behind full pool holders, and an interactive joiner then completes without waiting for the holders to be released. D. Govern withProcess (S). - Wrap withProcess's spawn and use in governChildProcess(input.command, ...) and keep an internal ungoverned variant for run(), so nothing is governed twice. - Test: withProcess in the background lane queues when the pool is full.

Value medium · effort S · risk low

Done#207 VCS repository detection runs three sequential git rev-parse processes and caches the result for only 2 s

projects-loading:repo-detection-three-sequential-spawns · original impact Low, effort S · Process spawns WP07A

Current state

Confirmed DONE by 60633eff3 (#710). detectRepository now runs one combined `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree --show-toplevel --git-common-dir` (nonzero exit or a non-'true' first line means not a repository). The VcsDriverRegistry keeps positive detections for 2 minutes and revalidates each read with a stat of <root>/.git (dev:ino:kind); negative results keep the old 2 s TTL. The real-git contract harness and a registry test cover the combined command and .git-identity revalidation. No consumer reads handle.repository.rootPath/metadataPath/freshness (only kind and driver, run against input.cwd), so a stale positive entry can only matter if the folder stops being a repository, and removing the root .git catches that. That makes the auditor's 'intermediate git init' gap functionally moot. Two minor issues remain. (1) The nested-.git check can defeat the cache entirely in a rare layout. (2) The proposal's explicit invalidation after `git init` was not implemented. Negative entries are never revalidated, so a ≤2 s stale 'not a repository' can still be read right after init. This race already existed and is not a regression.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:491-519 detectRepository: a single gitCommand with the combined rev-parse, allowNonZeroExit, READ_ONLY_GIT_ENV (GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0).
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriver.ts:377-389 parseDetectRepositoryOutput returns null on a nonzero exit, a first line other than 'true', or an empty toplevel. This covers bare repositories and cwd inside .git, where --show-toplevel exits 128.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsDriverRegistry.ts:12-20 NEGATIVE_DETECTION_CACHE_TTL is 2 s and POSITIVE_DETECTION_CACHE_TTL is 2 min.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsDriverRegistry.ts:138-185 The cache stores gitPathIdentity, and detect() restats <root>/.git on every read. When cwd differs from rootPath it also stats <cwd>/.git and invalidates if that differs from the root's identity.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsDriverRegistry.test.ts:110-152 Test that a re-initialized .git and a nested git init both cause redetection.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/testing/VcsDriverContractHarness.ts:53-85 The real-driver contract tests detection outside a repo, at the root and in a nested directory.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitWorkflowService.ts:209-309 Every consumer (also WorkspaceEntries.ts:550, CheckpointStore.ts:58, ForgejoApi.ts:902, BitbucketApi.ts:862, SourceControlProviderRegistry.ts:684) uses only handle.kind and handle.driver with input.cwd. The cached rootPath and metadataPath are never read.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsProjectConfig.ts:54-110 resolveKind still walks the ancestors with fs.exists on every detect. These are cheap stats, not spawns.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/worktreeOperations.ts:1085-1107,306-307 initializeGitForProject runs git init and then ensureProjectMainWorktree -> gitWorkflow.localStatus -> registry.detect. A negative entry cached for workspaceRoot in the prior 2 s returns isRepo=false, which leads to 'The initialized repository is unavailable.' No invalidation happens after init (VcsProvisioningService.ts:41-47; gitRpc.ts:496 refreshGitStatus has the same window).
Defects in the shipped fix

Minor, and none is a regression in the targeted cost. (1) Cache-defeating loop: VcsDriverRegistry.ts:172-181 compares <cwd>/.git with the root's .git identity. If cwd is a subdirectory whose .git exists but which git does not treat as its own root, the two always differ. Examples are an empty or invalid .git directory, which git discovery skips before moving to the parent. In that case every detect() invalidates and spawns rev-parse again, so that cwd never gets a cache hit (one spawn per call, worse than the old 2 s TTL). The layout is rare. (2) The proposal's 'invalidate explicitly on project init' was not implemented, and negative entries are never revalidated. After VcsProvisioningService.initRepository, worktreeOperations.ts:306 (ensureProjectMainWorktree via localStatus) and gitRpc.ts:496 (refreshGitStatus) can read a stale negative cached within the prior 2 s. In the chat-promotion flow (chatPromotion.ts:1236 -> initializeGitForProject), a client status subscription on the new root shortly before init could make init report 'The initialized repository is unavailable.' This race already existed with the old uniform 2 s TTL. The code path is verified; how often the timing occurs is not. (3) The auditor's intermediate-directory git-init gap has no functional effect, because no consumer reads the cached rootPath.

Implementation sketch

Optional cleanup, low priority. (a) In VcsDriverRegistry, record a cwdGitIdentity in CachedDetection (stat of <cwd>/.git at load time, null if absent, skipped when cwd resolves to rootPath). In detect(), compare the current <cwd>/.git identity against that stored value instead of against the root identity. This fixes the empty/invalid nested .git loop and still catches a new nested git init. Add a registry test that creates an empty <root>/nested/.git directory with the fake process still reporting the outer root, and assert that repeated detects spawn once. (b) Add `invalidate(cwd)` to VcsDriverRegistryShape: Cache.invalidate for keys `auto\0cwd` and `git\0cwd`, plus realpath(cwd) to match VcsStatusBroadcaster.normalizeCwd. Call it in VcsProvisioningService.initRepository after a successful driver.initRepository, and wherever Ryco creates or removes worktrees if desired. Add a test that detects a non-repo folder (negative), runs initRepository, and checks that detect immediately returns a handle. Also consider replacing GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1290-1298 resolveGitCommonDir (an extra rev-parse spawn per remote-status refresh) with the metadataPath already in the cached detection. That is a separate, small saving.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Current state

Confirmed DONE. Commit 60633eff3 (#710) is the only commit that introduced listActiveThreadShellRows, listActiveThreadSessionShellRows and readShellUpdatedAt. buildShell, which backs both getShellSnapshot and getScopedShellSnapshot, now reads only live projects, threads, worktrees and sessions in SQL. There is no JS deletedAt filter any more. The per-row latestCompletedTurnAt subquery is gone on every path; it is now a trigger-maintained column (migration 087, d6a3f6819). (a) The (created_at, thread_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL partial index was not added; at about 323 live rows the temp B-tree sort costs about 0.2 ms. Done#209 Branch listing (new thread / branch selector) spawns 6 git processes and re-runs all of them for every page

projects-loading:listrefs-six-spawns · original impact Low, effort S · Process spawns

Current state

Confirmed DONE (60633eff3, #710). The six-process listRefs pipeline (branch, branch --remotes, remote, symbolic-ref origin/HEAD, worktree list, for-each-ref recency) is now one read-only `git for-each-ref --format=%(refname)%00%(committerdate:unix)%00%(HEAD)%00%(symref)%00%(worktreepath) refs/heads refs/remotes`. Remote names come from the shared 5 s config-snapshot cache, origin/HEAD comes from the symref field, and worktree paths are de-duplicated and stat'ed at concurrency 8. The parsed listing sits in a per-cwd 5 s cache, so pages, query variants and the several web pickers that call listRefs (BranchToolbar, NewThreadSourcePicker, NewWorktreeDialog, WorkItems, PR remote presence) share one read. Old helpers are gone (readBranchRecency, worktree-list parsing), and `git worktree list` survives only as a fallback for git without %(worktreepath). Repository detection before listRefs is cached in VcsDriverRegistry (2 min positive), so a cache hit costs no spawn. I checked behaviour: symref entries such as origin/HEAD are skipped, %(worktreepath) includes the main worktree (checked on git 2.55: main -> /Users/laurinfrank/Code/ryco), the sort order is unchanged, and hasPrimaryRemote is unchanged. Effect's Cache.invalidate removes the entry and does not re-insert an in-flight lookup, so a write cannot be masked by a read that started before it. Measured read-only on this repo (1,143 refs, 37 worktrees): the single for-each-ref takes 22-29 ms and `git config -z --list` about 9 ms, against the report's 63-85 ms for the old pattern. What is not met: the proposal's 'unchanged polls cost about 0' via packed-refs/refs mtime validation. The cache is a 5 s TTL, so each 60 s client poll per mounted controller still costs one for-each-ref, plus a config spawn if that snapshot expired. That is 1-2 spawns where there were 6. Getting it to 0 is low value and error-prone to do with mtimes.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:190-226 LIST_REFS_FIELDS (refname, committerdate:unix, HEAD, symref, worktreepath), the NUL-separated format, and parseListedRefs.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2402-2413 readListedRefs runs a single for-each-ref over refs/heads and refs/remotes (readOnly, 15 s timeout, 16 MiB output cap).
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2445-2456 readBranchListing makes one call. The worktree list fallback (2416-2438) runs only on an 'unknown field name' error from old git.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2471-2486 Remote names come from readConfigSnapshot (cached, 1145-1173) and the default branch from the origin/HEAD symref, so the `git remote` and `git symbolic-ref` spawns are gone. The config read is sequential after for-each-ref, which costs about 9 ms extra on a cold miss.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2489-2508 Worktree paths are de-duplicated and stat'ed with Effect.forEach at concurrency 8, replacing the old sequential yield* stat inside the parse loop.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2594-2604 branchListingCache (capacity 256, 5 s TTL, failures not cached), keyed by path.resolve(cwd). invalidateReadCaches clears it and the config cache. invalidateRefListing clears one key.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:2606-2643 listRefs serves filtering, dedupe and pagination from the cached listing. fetchOrigin fetches and then invalidates the key.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.ts:1076-1082 Every execute without readOnly runs invalidateAll on the config and branch caches for all repos. This is safe, but more than needed, because invalidation is tied to the GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS readOnly flag. Pure reads such as runGitStdout (1183-1191: readConfigValue 2241, listRemoteNames 1389, originRemoteExists 1384), branchExists (1205) and the status fetch (1268-1286, at most once per 15 s per watched repo) also clear every repo's listing.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.ts:1852-1887 invalidateLocalStatus and invalidateStatus call gitCore.invalidateRefListing(cwd) after git actions and agent turns, which covers ref moves made outside the driver.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitWorkflowService.ts:418-427 registry.detect runs before listRefs. It is cached (VcsDriverRegistry.ts:14-20: 2 min positive, 2 s negative), so no extra spawn per page.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/GitVcsDriverCore.test.ts:461-576 parseListedRefs unit test, plus effect tests that check one forEachRef across limit/cursor/query variants, a re-read after createRef, and a re-read after invalidateRefListing.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/gitAtoms.ts:105-107 The client still uses a 15 s stale time, a 60 s poll and 100-item pages. Each poll per mounted controller is one server call, which is a cache hit within 5 s and otherwise 1 for-each-ref (plus about 1 config spawn).
Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness bug in the fix. Minor gaps, none needing action now: (1) The proposal's mtime-validated cache is not implemented, so the 60 s poll is not free. Each mounted branches controller costs about 23 ms of for-each-ref (plus about 9 ms config if that snapshot expired) per minute, against about 70 ms before. (2) Cache invalidation is tied to the readOnly (GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS) flag, so pure reads that are not flagged readOnly (runGitStdout helpers, branchExists, originRemoteExists) and the periodic status fetch run invalidateAll across every repo's listing and config snapshot. This lowers the hit rate for later pages but never causes staleness. (3) On a cold miss, readConfigSnapshot runs after for-each-ref rather than alongside it, about 9 ms of avoidable latency. (4) The cache key is the cwd, not the gitCommonDir, so a branch an agent creates in worktree W invalidates only W's key. The project-root listing can lag by up to the 5 s TTL. This is bounded and deliberate. Out of scope and pre-existing since f1be4abc7: GitManager.ts:2035 and 2047 call gitCore.listRefs({ cwd }) with no limit, so paginateBranches truncates to 100 refs (GitVcsDriverCore.ts:250). In repos with more than 100 branches, PR worktree prep can miss an existing local PR branch. That belongs in a separate correctness item.

A disabled row returns NOOP, and unsubscribe happens only at refCount 0, which is now reached only after the 60 s exit delay.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:699-748 streamRefSummary only reads workflow.refSummary in the background process lane. It has no remote poller and no git status, diff or fetch. The 5 s HEAD tick is readCheckoutHead, a file read, not a spawn.
  • apps/server/src/git/GitManager.ts:1709-1828 refSummaryCache has a 30 s TTL, keyed by `${cwd}\0${branch from disk}`. On a cache miss the work is a config snapshot, at most one for-each-ref when there is no upstream, and a PR lookup through the per-repository PR index. Re-subscribing within 30 s is a cache hit.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarThreadRow.browser.tsx:188-262 Browser tests with fake timers cover the shared per-cwd demand, an active offscreen row, no subscription on a fling (re-exit before enterDelay), keeping the stream through a scroll-out shorter than exitDelay, and release after the full exit window. They also assert view: 'summary'.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProjectThreadList.tsx:210-219 Lists of more than 20 threads are virtualized with LegendList (recycleItems={false}). Rows that scroll out of LegendList's render window unmount, which drops their subscription immediately and skips the 60 s exit delay. Re-mounting goes through the 150 ms enter delay and then the 30 s server summary cache, so the cost is negligible.
  • apps/web/src/components/ThreadStatusIndicators.tsx:145-151; apps/web/src/components/CommandPaletteDialog.tsx:1045,1076 Adjacent caller: command-palette thread rows subscribe to the summary view with no visibility gating, and subscribe and unsubscribe as search results change. It is the same cheap summary stream, shares the sidebar's watch key, and hits the 30 s server cache. It is not the described sidebar cost.
Defects in the shipped fix

No material defects. Minor observations: (1) Exit hysteresis applies only while a row stays mounted. Rows unmounted by LegendList windowing (SidebarProjectThreadList.tsx:210-219) or by collapsing a project release their stream at once. Because of the 30 s refSummary cache this costs only an RPC stream re-open. (2) The proposal's server-side 'stat HEAD/index mtime instead of a 5 s TTL' was not implemented. It is moot for this finding: sidebar and inbox rows no longer use the full view, and LOCAL_STATUS_CACHE_TTL_MS (VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:57) only affects full-view consumers such as ChatView, DiffPanel and the inbox hover card. (3) The hook's own unit test (useHasIntersectedViewport.browser.tsx) does not cover hysteresis or multiple nodes, but SidebarThreadRow.browser.tsx does.

Done#211 Each visible sidebar project issues an Atlassian project-link RPC only to precompute a context-menu URL

projects-loading:sidebar-jira-link-rpc-per-project · original impact Low, effort S · Network / RTT

Current state

Confirmed DONE for the stated cost. PR #710 (60633eff3) changed the gate on useSidebarProjectJiraLinks from projectHeaderHasIntersected to a sticky projectMenuIntent flag, which is set on pointerenter or focus capture of the project header. On first sidebar render the getProjectLink and listConnections RPCs no longer fire (30 -> 0-1). No other surface issues per-row Atlassian reads: ProjectOverviewTab, WorkItemsTab, the settings forms and ProjectAtlassianSection are single-project, user-opened views; PhoneHome passes an empty map; mobile and client-runtime never call getProjectLink. The auditor missed some small leftovers. (1) Both queries use staleTime 0, so every newly hovered project re-watches the per-environment connections key and sends a fresh listConnections RPC. The boot-time in-flight coalescing is gone, so a first hover costs 2 RPCs, and moving the pointer across collapsed headers sends 2 RPCs per header crossed. (2) That connections read is redundant in the common case: since 332da2298, saveProjectLink always stores a vetted jiraSiteUrl, and resolveJiraProjectOpenUrl prefers it. (3) The native/DOM-fallback context menu snapshots the map synchronously, so a fast right-click over a slow relay can leave out "Open Jira project". (4) No test covers the intent gating.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProjectItem.tsx:189-193 projectMenuIntent useState(false) plus handleProjectMenuIntent; the comment states the goal: resolve the Jira link on menu intent, not for every visible project at boot.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProjectItem.tsx:251-255 useSidebarProjectJiraLinks({ explorerOpen: false, projectVisible: projectMenuIntent }). At f1be4abc7 this was projectHeaderHasIntersected.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/SidebarProjectHeader.tsx:88-93 The header wrapper div has onFocusCapture and onPointerEnter = onMenuIntent. The ProjectSettingsMenu trigger (around line 228) sits inside this wrapper, so the dropdown always sets intent before it opens.
  • apps/web/src/components/Sidebar.logic.ts:479-484 shouldQuerySidebarSourceControlCounts returns explorerOpen || projectVisible, which is false until intent because explorerOpen is hard-coded false.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/atlassianAtoms.ts:22-23,96,113-152 isEnabled requires enabled, so keyOf returns null and watch is a no-op while disabled. Both stale times are 0, so shouldFetchOnWatch is always true and every new watch on an existing key starts a new read unless one is already in flight.
  • apps/web/src/rpc/useAtlassian.ts:118-123,159-168 Each SidebarProjectItem watches the shared connections key for its environment in its own effect. With per-item intent the watches are staggered in time, so each new hover sends a fresh listConnections instead of joining one in-flight read (packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/keyedQuery.ts:343,744).
  • apps/web/src/lib/workItemLocalLinks.ts:96-111 resolveJiraProjectOpenUrl uses link.jiraSiteUrl first and falls back to the connection's baseUrl only when it is null.
  • apps/server/src/atlassian/AtlassianConnectionService.ts:189-222,386-397 saveProjectLink always stores a vetted jiraSiteUrl when jiraConnectionId is set (added in 332da2298), so the sidebar's connections RPC matters only for legacy rows.
  • apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useSidebarProjectContextMenu.ts:145-182 The right-click menu reads jiraProjectOpenUrlByProjectKey synchronously before api.contextMenu.show. If the lazily started reads have not returned (e.g. over a hub relay), "Open Jira project" is left out of that menu. The React dropdown (ProjectSettingsMenu.tsx:40-43,57) is reactive and fills in once the reads return.

Defects in the shipped fix

No regression against the finding's metric; minor inefficiency and UX leftovers in the fix. (1) The connections read has staleTime 0 (apps/web/src/rpc/atlassianAtoms.ts:22) and is watched once per project item (apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useSidebarProjectJiraLinks.ts:28-35). Each first hover therefore sends getProjectLink plus a new listConnections, even when connections were fetched a moment earlier for another project in the same environment. A vertical pointer sweep across N collapsed headers sends about 2N RPCs. Before the fix it was P+E, coalesced at boot. Lazy and amortized, but more total relay frames per session if the user eventually hovers most projects. (2) That listConnections call is usually unnecessary: links saved since 332da2298 always carry jiraSiteUrl. (3) Race in the right-click menu: useSidebarProjectContextMenu.ts:145-182 snapshots the map at contextmenu time. A right-click within one relay RTT of pointerenter, or on a header that scrolled under a still cursor without a pointerenter, omits "Open Jira project" for that open. (4) No unit or browser test asserts that sidebar boot issues zero getProjectLink calls or that hover issues one per member.

Connecting to a Hub (20)

Done#212 Every in-session relay drop establishes the relay twice (probe reconnect, then full client rebuild)

hub-connection:relay-reconnect-double-establishment · original impact High, effort M · Waterfall decision

Current state

Confirmed DONE. a38ecac4b (on main and in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3) removes the second establishment. recoverHostedRelayConnection now only calls HostedHubController.connectionRecovered, which clears the relay gap, sets sessionEstablished:false and re-arms the session-sync deadline. It no longer calls retrySelectedNode, activateHostedNode, reset, disconnect or connect. The ordering checks out. relayEngine #applyModeLock flushes the buffered resubscriptions, emits online (which synchronously calls connectionRecovered), then emits sessionStatus 'synchronizing'. Hosted shell streams resubscribe without a resume cursor (service.ts resumeShell is false when hostedGeneration is set), so the replacement delivers a full snapshot that markHostedSessionReady accepts on the unchanged generation. The only remaining callers of retrySelectedNode are explicit ones: terminal-failure demand, browser resume, the draft retry and the UI retry button. Mobile's selected env is also adopted now. Before the fix it was released and rebuilt through nodeLifecycle.connectPrimaryEnvironment. The tests cover 2 tickets / 2 sockets per initial connect plus one drop, the stale-snapshot gap and the lost mutation. I found one small regression the auditor missed. The old path skipped recovery entirely (no rebuild, no deadline) while directoryStatus was not 'ready'. The new connectionRecovered arms the 30 s deadline unconditionally, so a directory that stays stale for more than 30 s after the relay returns now ends in terminal-failure.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:273 recoverHostedRelayConnection is a one-liner calling hostedHubController.connectionRecovered(generation). The old queueMicrotask -> retrySelectedNode is gone.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:428 On online with #recoveringAfterClose set, calls binding.connectionRecovered once per drop. The flag is set only on an unintentional close (line 521).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayEngine.ts:971 #applyModeLock: flush the buffered resubscriptions, then onTransportStatus('online') (connectionRecovered runs synchronously here), then onSessionStatus('synchronizing'), then onOpen. No inbound snapshot can reach markSessionReady before connectionRecovered has cleared the gap.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:2624 connectionRecovered: generation and gap fence, sessionEstablished:false, then #startSessionSyncTimer(generation) at :2636. It does not check directoryStatus or browserStatus.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:2644 markSessionReady ignores snapshots while #relayGapGeneration equals the current generation.
  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:857 resumeShell is false for hosted. The shell resubscribes with a full snapshot. onResubscribe -> markHostedSessionReplaying (:868) and onCurrent/onReady -> markHostedSessionReady (:895-905) on the same hostedGeneration.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/nodeLifecycle.ts:84 Before the fix, mobile's rebuild ran here: connectPrimaryEnvironment releases a non-ready connection and reconnects it, which created a new per-env record. Mobile now adopts instead (primaryConnection.ts:193 forwards to the shared controller only).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.test.ts:621 Adoption test: exactly 2 issueRelayTicket calls and 2 sockets across the initial connect plus one drop. retrySelectedNode, disconnectPrimaryEnvironment and connectPrimaryEnvironment are never called, and mutations are denied until markHostedSessionReady. :672 covers the gap snapshot and :701 the lost mutation.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:2342 A failed directory refresh sets directoryStatus 'stale' and effectiveRole null, with backoff up to 60 s (:2347). notifyDirectoryInvalidated is suppressed while #directoryRetry > 0 (:2169). Session-sync streams then get 'awaiting-session' (transport.ts:76-98, hostedRoleAllows with roleFresh=false).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:2810 #failSessionSync sets terminal-failure after HOSTED_SESSION_SYNC_DEADLINE_MS (30 s, :499). Before the fix, recoverHostedRelayConnection returned early on directoryStatus !== 'ready' (git show a38ecac4b^:packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:260), and sessionEstablished stayed true, so no deadline applied in that case.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/hostedConnectionCoordinator.ts:516 On web, a terminal-failure is retried only by the coordinator renewal tick or presence edge (comment at :358-361), and that retry is a full rebuild via retrySelectedNode. On mobile it needs a user retry or a lifecycle signal.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:604 #invalidateAttempt (from onSessionStart/onDispose/reset) clears #recoveringAfterClose without clearing the controller's #relayGapGeneration. A WsTransport.reconnect() during a gap would leave the gap stuck (markSessionReady ignored, no deadline). This is latent only: hosted web disables generic reconnects (supervision.ts:1244, WebSocketConnectionSurface recoveryOwner), and on mobile the resume reconnect always follows suspendBrowser's generation bump.
Defects in the shipped fix

1) New terminal-failure path (low frequency, low to medium impact). HostedHubController.connectionRecovered (packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:2624-2637) arms the 30 s session-sync deadline even when directoryStatus is not 'ready'. A stale directory nulls effectiveRole (state.ts:2342-2346), so the shell and the other session-sync streams stay 'awaiting-session' until the directory retry succeeds. That retry backs off up to 60 s, and invalidations are suppressed while it is backing off (state.ts:2169). After a Hub outage of roughly 60 s or more, the relay can recover more than 30 s before the next directory retry. #failSessionSync (state.ts:2810) then publishes terminal-failure with 'Ryco state could not be synchronized'. The pre-fix recoverHostedRelayConnection bailed out on a non-ready directory with no rebuild and no deadline, and sessionEstablished stayed true, so the session recovered by itself once the directory refreshed. Now web waits for the coordinator renewal tick and does a full rebuild; mobile waits for a user retry or a lifecycle event. 2) The auditor's mobile per-env note is accurate but minor. apps/mobile/src/connection/hostedConnectionCoordinator.ts connectionClosed (:503) and markSessionReady (:515) have no gap guard, and sessionEstablished is never reset on adoption, so reportShellSnapshotFailure (:538) is ignored there. The relay engine's 'synchronizing' on online resets the per-env sessionStatus, which neutralises most of the gap risk. Non-selected retained mobile connections always adopted like this, even before the fix. 3) Latent, not reachable today: #invalidateAttempt (transport.ts:604) clears #recoveringAfterClose but not #relayGapGeneration. Any future WsTransport.reconnect() on a hosted client during a gap would leave the session unable to become ready, with no deadline. Behaviour change, not a defect: the HostedReconnectPolicy backoff is no longer reset on every drop (the factory is not recreated), so flapping links back off progressively per the 60 s stable-interval policy.

Implementation sketch

Defect 1: in HostedHubController.connectionRecovered (state.ts:2624), arm #startSessionSyncTimer only when directoryStatus === 'ready' and browserStatus is current or synchronizing. Otherwise record #deferredSessionSyncGeneration = generation. In the #refreshDirectory success branch (around state.ts:2294-2314, where directoryStatus becomes 'ready'), start the timer if the deferred generation equals the current generation and sessionEstablished is false, then clear the field. Also clear it wherever #relayGapGeneration is reset (around :1951) and on generation bumps. A simpler alternative: in #failSessionSync, re-arm instead of failing while directoryStatus !== 'ready'. Test in transport.test.ts: drop, set directoryStatus stale, replacement online, advance 30 s, expect transportStatus not terminal-failure; then set the directory ready and call markHostedSessionReady, expect ready; keep a test that the deadline still fires with a ready directory. Defect 2 (optional): give the mobile coordinator connectionRecovered(environmentId, generation), which clears a per-record gap flag (set in connectionClosed) and sets sessionEstablished:false. Have markSessionReady ignore snapshots while the flag is set, and call it from primaryConnection.ts:193 before forwarding. Cover it in hostedConnectionCoordinator.test.ts. Defect 3 (hardening): add an optional binding hook from #invalidateAttempt (or onSessionStart) that clears the controller gap for the current generation, or clear #relayGapGeneration in transportStatus('online') when no recovery is pending. Add a unit test that a reconnect() during a gap still lets markHostedSessionReady make the session ready.

Done#213 Relay connect waits for the 570 KiB-gzip HostedHubRoot chunk graph, which starts loading only after bootstrap finishes

hub-connection:boot-gate-hostedhubroot-waterfall · original impact High, effort M · Waterfall WP12B

Current state

Confirmed DONE for the finding. Relay connect no longer waits for the HostedHubRoot chunk graph. The boot gate starts the routed-node orchestrator, the workspace coordinator and the browser lifecycle once the small hostedWorkspaceOwners chunk loads, in parallel with the access check. These owners only call controller primitives. The directory read rides with the session restore, and `connectPrimary` registers the relay connection and its shell subscription without RootAppShell mounting, so selectNode, the ticket, the relay and `markSessionReady` all proceed without the hosted root or the workspace shell mounting. HostedHubRoot is preloaded at the start of beforeLoad. RootAppShell is lazy (only a type import remains), and the thread route chunk is prefetched. One defect in the fix: for a signed-in account, the hosted gate preloads and awaits HostedHubRoot and the RootAppShell graph even on /native/authorize/* (the native app's sign-in handoff) and /pair, where neither renders. On a cold cache that delays the consent page by roughly a few hundred ms to about 1 s. Also, the shell graph download is serialized after the access check, despite the gate comment. There is no behavioural test that the gate starts the owners before the root mounts.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:159-165 HostedHubRoot.preload() and preloadMatchedRouteChunks(pathname) fire before the async gate, but only when pathname is not /pair and not a native-authorization path.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:195-201 The hosted branch calls `runHostedBootGate({ pathname, hostedRoot: HostedHubRoot.preload() })` unconditionally, so /native/authorize/* and /pair also preload and await HostedHubRoot. This is the fix defect.
  • apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:405-407 RootRouteView renders only <Outlet/> for /pair and native-authorization paths, so HostedHubRoot and RootAppShell are never rendered there.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/bootGate.ts:28-41 Imports the owners module and the hostedRootAppShell wrapper. Once the owners chunk loads it calls retainHostedWorkspaceOwners() and prefetchHostedRouteCode(), in parallel with bootstrapAccess.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/bootGate.ts:45-55 Awaits bootstrapAccess only, then awaits hostedRoot plus preloadHostedRootAppShell() when authenticated or a read preview is possible. Neither wait depends on pathname. The RootAppShell import starts here, after the access check.
  • apps/web/src/components/hostedHub/hostedRootAppShell.tsx:15-30 preloadableLazy calls import('../RootAppShell') only when preload() is called. The early import in the gate fetches just this wrapper.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/hostedWorkspaceOwners.ts:32-72 Reference-counted single start of the orchestrator, coordinator and lifecycle, in the same order as the old root effects. prefetchHostedRouteCode warms ChatThreadRouteView for thread URLs.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/nodeRouteOrchestrator.ts:203-370 reconcile needs only the installed history (main.tsx:25-29, installed before the router) and the hosted store, with no React tree. It reaches selectNode, or retains the thread scope for the coordinator, once the directory is ready and browserStatus is current or synchronizing.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:894-906 connectPrimary, called by selectNode through the hosted runtime, registers the connection and its shell subscriptions without supervisor.start(). markHostedSessionReady (apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:893-905) therefore fires without RootAppShell's EnvironmentConnectionManagerBootstrap.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:619-662,743-780 bootstrapAccess settles on the account answer. The directory read rides with the session restore and is committed by the controller, independent of any mount.
  • apps/web/src/components/hostedHub/HostedHubRoot.tsx:35-38,210-222 No static RootAppShell import remains (grep finds only a type import in hostedRootAppShell.tsx:5). The root only retains the owners, and preloads the shell once authenticated.
  • apps/web/src/components/hostedHub/HostedNativeAuthorizationRoute.tsx:19-23 The native consent page needs the HostedHubRoot chunk only for the signed-out authentication surface (lazy). Signed-in consent needs neither HostedHubRoot nor RootAppShell, yet the gate awaits both.
Defects in the shipped fix

(1) Regression from the fix: the hosted boot gate preloads and awaits HostedHubRoot (__root.tsx:199). For an authenticated account or a read preview it also awaits the RootAppShell graph (bootGate.ts:46-55). This happens on every pathname, including /native/authorize/$handoffId and /pair, which render only <Outlet/> (__root.tsx:405). For the native app's sign-in handoff with a signed-in browser, the consent page waits for downloading, parsing and evaluating roughly the 570 KiB gzip graph it never renders. On a cold cache that is about 0.3-1 s; on a warm SW cache, about 0.1-0.3 s of phone parse and eval. The native-authorization route chunk itself is also not prefetched (excluded at __root.tsx:159), so it starts only after those waits. The gate also starts the workspace owners on these paths. That is mostly harmless: no discovery, and the lifecycle only suspends and resumes. (2) The bootGate.ts:23-27 comment claims the workspace shell downloads while the access check is on the wire. Only the wrapper module does: `import("../RootAppShell")` starts after bootstrapAccess, so a signed-in cold-cache boot holds the boot surface for the access check plus the shell graph fetch in series. This does not affect relay connect. (3) Cosmetic: an orphaned `bootstrapAccess` docblock sits above `accessCheckPending()` (packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:639-648). (4) Test gap: there is no test that the gate's early owners drive selectNode before the root mounts.

Implementation sketch

Fix (1): compute once in resolveRootBeforeLoadContextAsync whether the hosted root renders for this path. Reuse the check from rootSurfaceFor (pathname !== '/pair' && !isNativeAuthorizationPath(pathname)) by extracting a shared `rendersRootSurface(pathname)` helper, so the preload at :159-165, rootSurfaceFor and the gate cannot drift. Pass `hostedRoot: renders ? HostedHubRoot.preload() : Promise.resolve()` and a `rendersHostedRoot` flag to runHostedBootGate. When the flag is false, skip the shell import/preload and, optionally, the owners retain. HostedHubRoot already retains the owners on mount, and withRootSurfaceLoaded preloads it on a later navigation to '/'. For native-authorization paths in hosted mode, call preloadMatchedRouteChunks(pathname) so the consent chunk downloads during the access check. Add that branch to the :159 guard while keeping the standard-mode exclusion. Fix (2), optional: correct the bootGate comment. If wanted, start preloadHostedRootAppShell() before the access check when a synchronous 'likely signed-in' hint exists, such as canShowHostedReadPreview() with a remembered account or a bearer token present. That is a bandwidth trade-off for signed-out visitors, so only on such a hint. Fix (3): move the orphaned docblock onto bootstrapAccess. Tests: a Vitest unit test for runHostedBootGate with rendersHostedRoot=false, where a never-resolving hostedRoot and a spied preloadHostedRootAppShell must not block or be called. A test that the gate's owners call hostedHubController.selectNode for a routed node once the store reports authenticated, ready and current, with HostedHubRoot never rendered. Extend webBundleSplitting.test to assert that the root does not pass HostedHubRoot.preload() for native-authorization paths. Validate with focused `bun run test` on apps/web for these files and `bun typecheck`.
