Partial#214 Session restore and directory fetch run serially on every cold start and every foreground resume; the Hub-session socket opens only afterwards

hub-connection:session-and-directory-serial · original impact Medium, effort S · Waterfall decision

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The main part is done as the auditor says, and it is done in bearer mode too (9adb0372c, which is also in the Hub pin 7bc39eec3). But the finding lists two separate gains, and the early Hub-session socket is one of them. That part was not implemented. On a cold start in the hosted web app, every node relay stream waits for that socket's `ready`, and the socket still opens only after the restore answers. So the second RTT is still on the cold-start connect path. Under the 'keep DONE only if the described cost is removed' rule this is PARTIAL, not DONE. Smaller point: the auditor's line refs have shifted a little (#resumeBrowser is now 2048-2073 and the hubSession gate is 55-63).

Current state

Checked independently: the directory read now goes out beside the session restore on cold start (#restoreAccess) and on every foreground or online resume (#resumeBrowser), in both cookie and bearer mode. Its answer is held and committed only after the restore validates, under the session fence. A failed, aborted or 401 speculative read is never authoritative and falls back to an ordinary read. The tests cover this, and the Hub never rotates the token on GET /api/auth/session, so the bearer overlap is safe. The fix is also in the Hub's vendored Ryco. Not done: the optional early Hub-session socket. On web cold starts the socket still opens one restore RTT late, and node relay streams wait for it. No functional defect in the fix. There is a stale API doc comment, and a signed-out cookie-mode cold start now sends one speculative GET /api/nodes that 401s.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:449-486 HostedDirectoryPrefetch / prefetchHostedDirectory runs listNodes on its own AbortController, which is aborted with the access operation. The result is held, and failure or abandonment resolves to null. It uses the default deadline.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:749-774 #restoreAccess sends restoreSession, then the prefetch at once. It patches authenticated on the answer and then calls #refreshDirectoryWith(check.directory). The prefetch is abandoned on abort or error. This covers bootstrap, the access-retry backoff and adoptSessionCredential, because all three go through this function.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:2048-2073 #resumeBrowser does the same. The prefetch is abandoned on a generation change, on abort, or when the account id differs from expectedAccountId (which expires the session), and it is committed via #refreshDirectoryWith.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:2147-2160 #refreshDirectoryWith drops the held read if a directory read is already in flight and joins that read instead. A push-triggered read that lands during the restore therefore wins over the older held read.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:2239-2259 #refreshDirectory awaits prefetch.nodes, and null falls back to listNodes. The commit is fenced on abort, accountStatus and session.id.
  • ryco-hub:src/http/authRoutes.ts:706-720 On Hub origin/main, GET /api/auth/session only reads the account and session and never mints or rotates a token or cookie. That makes the bearer-mode overlap (commit 9adb0372c) safe.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.test.ts:3907 Tests: parallel send with the held read not published early (3907), a 401 on the restore discards the held read (~3938), a failed held read is not authoritative (~3960), bearer mode (4056, 4087), and a resume for a different account drops the held read (4209).
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/hubSession.ts:55-63 Still a gap: watchWebHostedHubSession creates the HostedHubSession only once accountStatus is authenticated, which is after the restore RTT. The initial state while the check runs is 'signed-out', and sync() disposes on that.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/hostedHubSession.ts:103-149 createSocket() opens logical node relay streams only after the session's `ready`. On cold start, a new non-H2 WebSocket (TCP+TLS+upgrade, about 3 RTT) that starts at restore+1 RTT is therefore the critical path for the first node connection. The relay ticket only needs about 1 RTT after the directory commits. The web side wires this in apps/web/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:92.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.ts:873-881 Stale doc on credentialMode: it says overlapping a restore with other authenticated reads is allowed only in cookie mode, but state.ts now overlaps in bearer mode too.
Remaining

Only the early Hub-session socket is left. apps/web/src/hostedHub/hubSession.ts:55-63 still starts the account socket only after accountStatus becomes authenticated. On a hosted-web cold start the socket therefore begins one restore RTT after bootstrap starts, and every node relay stream waits for its `ready` (packages/client-runtime/src/relay/hostedHubSession.ts:103-149, 286-297). Without WebSocket-over-H2 that leaves about 1 RTT (50-150 ms) on the cold-start node-connect path. Foreground resume is unaffected, because the socket survives suspension.

Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defect found in the implemented fix. Minor items: (1) The doc comment on HostedHubApi.credentialMode (packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.ts:873-881) is stale. It says overlapping a restore is cookie-only, but state.ts:449-463 now overlaps in bearer mode as well. (2) The web CSRF token is held only in memory (apps/web/src/platform/sessionCredentials.ts:7), so there is no 'probably signed in' hint. Every signed-out cookie-mode cold start now also sends a speculative GET /api/nodes that the Hub answers with 401. It is harmless and non-authoritative, but it is one wasted request per signed-out page load. (3) The doc block at state.ts:455-463 has a run-on line ('...clears nothing. Its answer is held...'). This is cosmetic only.

Implementation sketch

Early socket, web only (web is always cookie mode): (a) In apps/web/src/hostedHub/hubSession.ts, add a 'pending' session with authority === null. Inside sync(), when accountStatus is not authenticated but hostedHubController.accessCheckPending() is true (the hook already exists, state.ts:655), and optionally only when the hosted read cache holds a last account as a 'likely signed in' hint, create the HostedHubSession early. (b) While it is pending: onStatus records the status but does not set the module `status` to online; onInvalidate buffers events, including the directory/threadCache invalidation that `ready` emits (hostedHubSession.ts:296); an onFailure of kind authentication only disposes it and never calls expireSession; and a non-retryable failure disposes it without calling hostedHubController.failure. (c) When the store reaches authenticated, adopt the pending session: set authority to [account.id, session.id, activeSpaceId], then flush the buffered invalidations so notifyDirectoryInvalidated still runs after the held directory read. On signed-out, session-expired or unavailable, dispose the pending session. Keep the existing authority-change path for every other change. (d) Security note: the Hub's `ready` frame carries no account or session id, so the adopted socket is trusted on the same ambient-cookie basis as today's post-restore socket (the same cookie-swap race, a slightly different window). If that is not acceptable, the Hub would add sessionId to `ready` and the client would adopt only on a match (Hub protocol change). (e) Tests in apps/web/src/hostedHub/hubSession.test.ts: a pending socket is reused on authenticated, with no second createSocket; a restore 401 disposes it without calling expireSession; a 4401 before the restore settles does not call expireSession; buffered `ready` invalidations reach notifyDirectoryInvalidated after adoption; nothing is created with no access check pending. Also correct the stale credentialMode doc in api.ts:873-881 (doc-only).

Needs a decision

The remaining early-socket work changes hosted lifecycle ownership (AGENTS.md: one authoritative owner, and nothing may publish readiness or mutation authority before the session revalidates). It also opens an authenticated socket before the session is validated. The Hub's `ready` frame does not carry account or session ids, so an adopted socket cannot prove it matches the restored session without a Hub protocol change. Deciding whether the ambient-cookie race is acceptable, or whether the Hub needs to add ids to `ready`, is a security and lifecycle call.

Value low · effort M · risk medium

Done#215 Boot gate can hold the loading surface for 30-60 s on a stalled network (30 s deadline, directory awaited)

hub-connection:boot-gate-request-deadline · original impact Medium, effort S · Reliability WP15

Current state

The described cost is gone (shipped in 60633eff3 / #710; the Hub pin 7bc39eec3 includes it). On a black-holed network the web boot gate now releases after about 8 s, down from 30-60 s. In cookie mode the session restore runs with an 8 s request deadline (HOSTED_ACCESS_CHECK_DEADLINE_MS), and the gate awaits bootstrapAccess(), which settles on the account answer before the directory read. A timeout publishes 'unavailable' with the access retry armed (1 s base backoff), and HostedHubRoot renders 'Retry Hub'. An authenticated account with a loading directory renders the app shell or the node-restoring surface, not the boot surface. The chunks the gate loads (HostedHubRoot, hostedRootAppShell) are in the PWA precache, so they cannot re-stall the gate. Mobile has its own 8 s launch-decision bound plus the bearer decision deadline. Tests cover the bound, the settle-before-directory behaviour and the bearer decision deadline. One adjacent path is still uncovered: the signed-out branch (see fixDefects). It is low value and does not affect the headline scenario.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.ts:176-186 REQUEST_DEADLINE_MS stays 30 s. HostedHubReadOptions.deadlineMs lets a read give up sooner.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.ts:3039-3048 #request arms its timer with Math.min(REQUEST_DEADLINE_MS, options.deadlineMs ?? REQUEST_DEADLINE_MS) and covers body consumption. restoreSession (api.ts:996-1004) and listNodes (api.ts:2476-2481) forward deadlineMs.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:518 HOSTED_ACCESS_CHECK_DEADLINE_MS = 8_000.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:850-855 #accessCheckOptions returns { deadlineMs: 8000 } in cookie mode until a check has timed out. Used by #restoreAccess (state.ts:750) and #resumeBrowser (state.ts:2054).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:618-662 bootstrap() publishes #bootstrapAccessPromise, and bootstrapAccess() returns it. #restoreAccess calls accessSettled at state.ts:772, before awaiting #refreshDirectoryWith at state.ts:773.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:829-843 In bearer mode, #armAccessDecisionDeadline publishes 'unavailable' at 8 s and releases the gate without abandoning a request that may rotate the token.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:470-486 The directory prefetch rides beside the restore at the full deadline and is abandoned on failure, so no gate waits on it.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/bootGate.ts:42-45 The gate awaits bootstrapWithHostedReadCache(() => hostedHubController.bootstrapAccess()). Called from apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:199.
  • apps/web/src/pwa/buildArtifacts.ts:59-60 HostedHubRoot and hostedRootAppShell, which the gate also awaits, are precached by the service worker, so on a black-holed link they come from cache.
  • apps/web/src/components/hostedHub/HostedHubRoot.tsx:280-330,911-919 With the account unavailable, the auth surface renders 'Retry Hub'. With the account authenticated and the directory not ready, the RootAppShell (hosted-cached) or HostedNodeRestoringSurface renders, not the boot surface.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/access/AppAccessGate.tsx:66-82 The mobile launch gate is bounded by HOSTED_LAUNCH_DECISION_DEADLINE_MS = 8_000 (launchDecision.ts:20), even though ensureMobileHostedSession awaits the full bootstrap().
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.test.ts:3981-4205 Tests cover: the gate settling before the directory read, settling on unavailable without a directory read, the 8 s bound followed by the full deadline after a timeout, and the bearer decision deadline including late success or late 401.
Defects in the shipped fix

Minor uncovered path (the auditor said none). In #restoreAccess's session-failure branch (packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:776-790), a 401 restore chains getBootstrapAvailability(operation.signal), which has the default 30 s REQUEST_DEADLINE_MS (api.ts:904-913). accessSettled is not called on this branch, so bootstrapAccess() and the web boot gate only release after that probe. A signed-out or expired-session visitor without a remembered read cache can therefore sit on AppBootLoadingSurface for up to ~30 s if /api/auth/session answers 401 but /api/auth/bootstrap-status then stalls. This is the same partial-stall pattern the finding counted for /api/nodes. It does not arise on a fully black-holed link, the headline case, because the 401 never arrives there. Cosmetic: the bootstrapAccess JSDoc (state.ts:639-648, introduced alongside 8c42d3334) is orphaned above accessCheckPending()'s own JSDoc, so bootstrapAccess() at state.ts:659 has no doc.

Implementation sketch

1) api.ts: change getBootstrapAvailability(signal?) to getBootstrapAvailability(signal?, options?: HostedHubReadOptions) and forward deadlineMs to #request, as restoreSession does at api.ts:1000-1004. 2) state.ts #restoreAccess session-failure branch (~state.ts:783-789): pass { deadlineMs: HOSTED_ACCESS_CHECK_DEADLINE_MS } to getBootstrapAvailability. It is a public, idempotent probe that already falls back to false on any failure, so a short bound changes nothing but the wait. In bearer mode the DPoP mint signing runs before the timer and is unaffected. 3) Move the orphaned JSDoc block at state.ts:639-648 to directly above bootstrapAccess() at state.ts:659. Tests: in state.test.ts (cookie mode), restoreSession rejects HostedHubApiError('session_invalid', 401); assert getBootstrapAvailability received { deadlineMs: HOSTED_ACCESS_CHECK_DEADLINE_MS }; then with fake timers and a getBootstrapAvailability that rejects with a timeout, assert bootstrapAccess() settles with accountStatus 'signed-out' and bootstrapAvailable false. In api.test.ts, extend the existing deadline test (~api.test.ts:992) to cover getBootstrapAvailability. Validate with focused vitest runs of packages/client-runtime authorization tests only.

Partial#216 A silently dead Hub-session socket takes up to 45 s to detect; foreground and online signals skip 'healthy' states

hub-connection:hub-session-liveness-probe · original impact Medium, effort S · Reliability WP15

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

The trigger list in the proposal is implemented. HostedHubSession has probe() and resume(), with a 5 s bound. The web lifecycle calls them on visibilitychange, resume, online, pageshow and NetworkInformation change. A 5 s stall watch on unary requests also calls probe(). While a probe is armed, new logical streams are held back. One scenario named in the finding still waits up to 45 s: a NAT rebinding or path change with no browser signal while the user only watches streams (an agent running) and sends no unary request. In that case the logical channel's Effect RpcClient ping timeout (16-24 s) tears the channel down, but neither that timeout nor the unintentional close calls probe(). The replacement relay stream therefore opens at once on the still-#ready dead account socket (hostedHubSession.ts:148). This is exactly the gap the original verifier flagged. Recovery waits for the 45 s session heartbeat. The fix also has a plausible regression. The probe's ping goes into the same FIFO queue as data, behind up to about 2 MiB of outbound bytes. A large unary upload on a slow uplink can trip the stall probe at about 10 s, kill the upload and repeat on every retry. Before the fix, the same upload survived until the 16-24 s RpcClient ping timeout.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/hostedHubSession.ts:192-216 probe() is implemented as described: 5 s deadline, reuses a pending heartbeat nonce, and fails at once when silent past the 45 s bound.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/hostedHubSession.ts:148-149 New streams are held back only while #probeDeadline is armed. With no probe armed, a replacement stream opens on the dead socket because #ready is still true.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/browserLifecycle.ts:25-55 probe or resume is called on visibilitychange, resume, online, pageshow and NetworkInformation change. All of these are browser signals that a NAT rebinding may never fire. Safari and Firefox have no navigator.connection.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:531-532 The stall watch is armed only for unary requests (`if (!info.stream)`). Thread and shell streams, the main traffic while an agent runs, are never watched.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:515-530 An unintentional logical-channel close calls connectionClosed and starts a reconnect, but no probe.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:478-562 The hosted lifecycleHandlers set no onHeartbeatTimeout. The RpcClient ping-timeout hook exists (rpc/protocol.ts:48, 502-510) but nothing forwards it to probeHubSubscription.
  • node_modules/.bun/effect@4.0.2/node_modules/effect/src/rpc/RpcClient.ts:1271-1300,1190-1205 The Effect pinger pings every 8 s and fires its timeout after 16 s of silence, so 16-24 s. A ping timeout fails the socket read and the retry policy reconnects. That makes a new BrowserHostedRelaySocket, then session.createSocket(), which opens on the dead account socket.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:2596-2611 controller.connectionClosed only patches reconnecting or stale. It does not probe the account socket.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/hostedHubSession.ts:408-436 #send is FIFO for every frame type. A ping goes behind queued data, up to HUB_SESSION_MAX_QUEUED_BYTES (2 MiB) including physical bufferedAmount. The probe deadline starts at enqueue time, not when the ping leaves.
  • packages/contracts/src/relay.ts:49 RELAY_MAX_RPC_MESSAGE_BYTES is 4 MiB. Image attachments travel inline as dataUrl in unary dispatch (orchestration.ts:599-607), so one unary request can be several MiB.
  • ryco-hub:origin/main:src/relay/websocketRuntime.ts:522-545 The Hub sends flow.pause/resume only on backpressure toward the consumer. A slow client uplink produces no inbound frames that could satisfy the probe during a large upload.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/hostedHubSession.test.ts:282-436 The tests cover probe success and failure, nonce reuse, silent-past-bound, held streams and carried pending streams. Nothing covers a probe behind a congested send queue, and no transport test covers probing on a channel close or ping timeout.
Remaining

(1) A path change with no browser signal while only streams are active, the common case of watching an agent run, still takes up to 45 s. The logical channel's RpcClient ping timeout (16-24 s) and unintentional channel closes (transport.ts:515-530) do not probe. The replacement stream then opens immediately on the dead account socket (hostedHubSession.ts:148), and recovery waits for the session heartbeat (hostedHubSession.ts:468-497). (2) Fix defect: probe() starts its 5 s deadline while the ping may still sit behind up to 2 MiB of queued data (hostedHubSession.ts:202-215, 433-435). A large unary upload on a slow uplink can be misclassified as a dead socket.

Defects in the shipped fix

Plausible false-positive regression. The stall watch (transport.ts:567-590) fires 5 s after a unary request starts, including while that request's own multi-MiB payload is still uploading. probe() then enqueues its ping FIFO behind up to about 2 MiB of session-queued and browser-buffered data (hostedHubSession.ts:408-436) and arms a 5 s deadline at enqueue time. If no inbound frame arrives in that window, #lost('network') closes every logical stream, marks the dispatch delivery-unknown and reconnects. No inbound frame arrives when no other stream is chatty and no Hub heartbeat lands; the Hub sends no flow frames toward a slow producer. Example: a 1.5-4 MiB image dataUrl on a 1-3 Mbps uplink. It used to succeed if the upload finished before the 16-24 s RpcClient ping timeout. Now it fails at about 10 s, and every retry fails the same way. Minor: #unansweredRequests is not cleared on an unintentional close (transport.ts:515-530), and the exit and interrupt hooks are skipped while the lifecycle is inactive. Stale entries can each fire one extra probe after a reconnect. That is harmless apart from one held RTT.

Implementation sketch

A. Probe on logical-channel suspicion (packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts, lifecycleHandlers()). Add `onHeartbeatTimeout: () => { if (!this.#disposed) this.#binding.requestStalled?.(); }`. In onClose, when !context.intentional, call `this.#binding.requestStalled?.()` before connectionClosed. Optionally rename the binding hook to `connectionSuspect`. The protocol's onPingTimeout hook runs before the RpcClient retry builds the replacement socket, so the probe is armed before session.createSocket(). hostedHubSession.ts:148 then holds the new stream until a frame proves the account socket alive, or carries it to the replacement READY (PENDING_STREAM_MAX_WAIT_MS). Optional tighter version: arm a 5 s timer on onHeartbeatPing and clear it on onHeartbeatPong/onRequestChunk, so stream-only sessions are probed within about 8+5 s of path death. Only do this after B. Also clear #unansweredRequests in the unintentional-close branch. B. Make the probe congestion-aware (hostedHubSession.ts). (1) Give ping and pong control frames priority: in #send, when the queue is non-empty, unshift control frames instead of pushing. Hub-session frames are atomic and stream-independent, so a ping may overtake data. (2) Start the probe deadline only when the ping has been handed to the physical socket, i.e. in #scheduleDrain when it leaves the queue. (3) At the deadline, if no frame has arrived but `#queueBytes + socket.bufferedAmount` has shrunk since the previous check, re-arm once more. Stay bounded by HUB_SESSION_DEAD_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS since #lastReceived. Tests: in hostedHubSession.test.ts, give the fake socket bufferedAmount >= 256 KiB and queued data. Assert the ping is sent ahead of queued data, that steady drain progress keeps the session past 5 s, and that no progress loses it at 5 s. In transport.test.ts, assert that onHeartbeatTimeout and an unintentional onClose call probeHubSubscription once, and that an intentional close does not. Add an integration-style test (HostedRelaySessionIntegration or hostedHubSession plus transport): after a ping timeout, the replacement stream is not opened on the suspect socket before a frame arrives.

Value medium · effort S · risk low

Done#217 SW install precaches ~7.3 MiB gzip at boot, refetches everything on every deploy, and the PWA boot document has no boot shell

hub-connection:pwa-precache-and-boot-doc · original impact Medium, effort M · Bundle size

Current state

I re-checked the current code and the auditor's DONE holds. All four parts of the proposal are on main and in the Ryco version the Hub vendors (60633eff3 and 3ce80cee6 are both ancestors of 7bc39eec3). (1) The install-time precache now covers only the static closures of 12 named boot, hosted-root, workspace and thread modules. Fonts and images are left out except the DM Sans boot face. Every other fingerprinted chunk is cached the first time it is fetched, and only if it is on the build's own allowlist; API, relay and E2EE paths stay network-only. (2) Install copies each unchanged URL from older ryco-pwa-shell-* caches and fetches only what is new. Activate also carries runtime-cached chunks forward. (3) Registration waits for the hosted boot gate's root-before-load-ready mark (capped at 15 s), then for idle (capped at 5 s). (4) The boot document is the built index.html (themed boot shell and logo) plus modulepreload links. I also checked the Hub side. Its CSP allows exactly one inline script, by the hash of index.html's inline script, and applies that CSP to every response. The boot document copies that script byte for byte, so it runs. Fingerprinted assets are served with 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'. I found no correctness defects, only minor non-blocking observations.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/pwa/buildArtifacts.ts:52 HOSTED_PWA_PRECACHE_MODULES: main.tsx, hosted state/readCache/e2eeRuntime, PreviewFileNavigationGuard, hostedWorkspaceOwners, HostedHubRoot, hostedRootAppShell, RootAppShell, ChatThreadRouteView, DraftChatThreadRouteView, PhoneHome. All 12 files exist. The lazy ones are real dynamic-import targets (e.g. bootGate.ts:28,31, __root.tsx:39-48), so each has its own chunk. state and readCache are statically imported by bootGate and land in the boot chunk anyway.
  • apps/web/src/pwa/buildArtifacts.ts:162 cacheableUrls covers the full reachable set (followDynamic:true) and is used only as the allowlist. The precache (lines 167-177) follows static imports from the named roots (followDynamic:false) and drops fonts and images (RUNTIME_CACHED_ASSET_PATTERN, line 76) except bootDocumentAssets.
  • apps/web/src/pwa/buildArtifacts.ts:245 install(): copies each fingerprinted precache URL from older shell caches, otherwise fetches it through the HTTP cache. A text/html fallback is rejected (cacheableResponse). offline.html is always refetched with no-cache. A partial cache left by a failed install is reused on retry (cache.match short-circuit at 252) and removed at the next successful activate.
  • apps/web/src/pwa/buildArtifacts.ts:272 activate(): copies runtime-cached allowlisted entries forward, then deletes old caches and claims clients. Carry-over failures cannot keep old caches alive.
  • apps/web/src/pwa/buildArtifacts.ts:336 Fetch handler: only exact allowlisted same-origin fingerprinted URLs are cached on first use, with basic/200/non-HTML checks. Network-only paths are checked first (line 329), before the navigation fallback.
  • apps/web/src/pwa/lifecycle.ts:338 registerWhenSettled: awaits whenAppReady, then requestIdleCallback (5 s timeout, line 80), then register. Both the readyState==='complete' branch (405-406) and the load listener (408) go through it. Covered by lifecycle.test.ts:203 and :237.
  • apps/web/src/pwa/lifecycle.ts:442 whenBrowserAppReady waits for ryco:startup:root-before-load-ready via getEntriesByName or a buffered PerformanceObserver, with a 15 s cap. In hosted mode that mark fires after runHostedBootGate, i.e. after the access check and the HostedHubRoot/workspace-shell preload (routes/__root.tsx:200).
  • apps/web/src/pwa/offlineDocument.ts:20 renderHostedPwaBootDocument injects deduplicated modulepreload links into the built index.html before </head>. It returns null, and the caller falls back to the minimal document, only when the HTML has no root div or module src script.
  • apps/web/src/pwa/buildArtifacts.ts:365 The plugin runs in generateBundle with order:'post', after vite:build-html has applied the transformIndexHtml hints from createBootPreloadPlugin (modulePreload.ts:72). The boot document therefore inherits the boot-chain modulepreload and stylesheet preload, and its own preloads are deduplicated against them.
  • ryco-hub:scripts/build-static-manifest.ts:99 The Hub requires exactly one inline script in index.html and hashes it into the CSP (src/http/securityHeaders.ts:30). The CSP is applied to every response, offline.html included (src/http/app.ts:428). The boot document contains the identical inline script, so it is allowed.
  • ryco-hub:src/http/staticAssets.ts:260 Hashed assets are served with 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'. service-worker.js and offline.html get 'no-cache' plus a strong ETag. Missing dotted paths never get the SPA HTML fallback, so a removed chunk returns 404, not HTML.
  • apps/web/src/pwa/buildArtifacts.test.ts:343 Tests cover carry-over from older caches, rejecting an HTML fallback during install (375), surviving a failed carry-over (393), runtime caching on first use plus the allowlist (407), and deriving the boot document (244).
Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness defects. Minor non-blocking observations: (a) activate() at buildArtifacts.ts:272-297 copies every runtime-cached chunk before clients.claim(). After the user applies an update, the reload navigation's fetch waits for activation, so this copy (proportional to how many lazy chunks the user has loaded) is now on the post-update reload path. Before the fix, activate only deleted caches. The cost is unmeasured and probably tens to a few hundred ms on phones for heavy users. (b) whenBrowserAppReady (lifecycle.ts:442-466) re-implements phase waiting with a PerformanceObserver even though startupInstrumentation.ts:85 already exports onStartupPhase, which also fires when performance.mark is unavailable. (c) No real-build guard checks that each HOSTED_PWA_PRECACHE_MODULES entry still maps to a chunk facade. A rename, or a merge into a manual group, would silently shrink the offline precache. (d) The DM Sans face is precached in hosted builds, but the boot document paints only an SVG logo.

Done#218 Hosted relay/E2EE/noble code is statically reachable from the standard boot graph through the relay barrel and hostedHub/state

hub-connection:hosted-code-in-standard-boot · original impact Medium, effort M · Bundle size WP12A

Current state

Confirmed DONE. In standard and desktop builds, the static boot graph from main.tsx carries no hosted relay, E2EE, noble, cborg or Hub-API code, and neither do the RootAppShell and ChatThreadRouteView closures. The build-time seam plugin swaps hostedHub/state, transport, bootGate, the coordinator, HostedConnectionControls, NoActiveThreadHostedStatus and pwa/lifecycle for inert *.standard siblings. The relay barrel no longer re-exports the E2EE initiator or channel. In hosted builds, the initiator and noble load through import("./e2eeRuntime"), which starts when the account authenticates and is awaited before a ticket is bought. If the code is not loaded yet, the attempt fails closed. I checked this in two ways: (a) an independent source-graph walk with the seams applied (standard main.tsx: 388 modules, none heavy and hosted; hosted main.tsx: no @noble), and (b) the current apps/web/dist, which contains HEAD-only code (worktree-setup-spin), so it was built from HEAD. In that dist the relay engine, the E2EE handshake and cborg appear in no chunk, and the authorization/api code appears only in api-*.js, which the boot and shell chunks do not import statically. The auditor made two mistakes. First, regression guards do exist. Second, it understated one leftover: the settings route is idle-preloaded on every standard launch and pulls in the Hub API chunk.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/clientModeSeams.ts:29-37 Seam list. The plugin at :56-91 is registered first at apps/web/vite.config.ts:104. It applies only to non-test standard builds (shouldApplyClientModeSeams), which is the build desktop ships (apps/desktop/src/main.ts:2123 loads apps/web/dist).

Defects in the shipped fix

The fix itself has no defect. It does miss one shared-code caller: apps/web/src/components/settings/DeviceIdentitySettings.tsx:6 statically imports hostedHubApi from hostedHub/api, which is not a seam. SettingsPanels renders this component in standard builds. As a result, the standard settings route closure contains api-*.js (66.4 KB raw / 17.9 KB gzip of HostedHubApi, hosted schemas and webauthn). RootAppShell idle-preloads that route on every standard/desktop launch (RootAppShell.tsx:184), so the hosted Hub API client is still fetched and evaluated in nearly every standard session, after first paint. It is not on the boot path and contains no relay, E2EE or noble code. The bundle-budget policy does not catch it because it has no SettingsRouteView closure.

Implementation sketch

1. DeviceIdentitySettings.tsx: drop the static `import { hostedHubApi } from "../../hostedHub/api"`. Not done#219 Every connect and reconnect needs a separate HTTP ticket round trip although the Hub-session socket is already authenticated

hub-connection:ticket-rtt-hub-session · original impact Medium, effort L · Network / RTT decision

Current state

I could not refute NOT_DONE. On the web hub-session path every logical relay attempt still awaits POST /api/relay/tickets (CSRF) before the stream is created. The ticket then travels in the stream's first relay auth frame. Neither repo has a v2 hub-session open, a server-minted ticket, a ticket prefetch, or a parallel-with-directory ticket. Hub origin/main (5f656ad) has no ticketless stream auth: openLogicalStream only reserves an unauthenticated connection that waits for the auth frame. Three related changes since f1be4abc7 shrink the problem but do not remove the RTT. (1) 94ec18751 overlaps the ticket with the socket upgrade, but only on mobile's native /v1/relay/client. (2) a38ecac4b adopts the transport's reconnected channel, so a relay drop buys one ticket instead of two. (3) ea96462d1 means that when the account socket itself died, the transport's ticket POST now runs alongside the account-socket reconnect: the pending stream waits for the replacement READY, so the ticket RTT is already hidden in that case. Foregrounding a healthy connection starts no new attempt. The RTT is still exposed on reload or deep-link route restore, on node select or switch, and on relay-level reconnects where the account socket stays healthy.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:343-372 nextUrl: the early socket is mobile-only (#openEarlySocket, :646). It awaits prepareSocketContext (:345), then awaits issueRelayAttempt or issueRelayTicket (:349-358), and only then returns the URL. createSocket (:396) runs after that.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:224-233 The web path actually goes through the default binding's issueRelayAttempt. Web configures no runtime issueRelayAttempt, so it falls through to getHostedHubApi().issueRelayTicket(nodeId) at :228.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.ts:2683-2729 issueRelayTicket still sends POST /api/relay/tickets with csrf:true. It offers protocolMinor 3 and falls back once to 2 (latched per session).
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:66-94 Web sets prepareRelaySocketContext (E2EE chunk load) and createRelaySocket via createWebHubRelaySocket. It sets no openEarlyRelaySocket and no issueRelayAttempt, so nothing overlaps the ticket.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/hubSession.ts:111-116 createWebHubRelaySocket just calls session.createSocket(). The account socket is opened independently, on authentication (watchWebHostedHubSession).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/hostedHubSession.ts:103-151,368-379 createSocket and #openStream send an empty `open` and flip the stream to open without an ack. The open is pipelined, so the only extra serial cost is the HTTP ticket RTT.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayEngine.ts:487-499 The client relay engine still builds the auth frame with relayTicket from options.ticket. There is no server-authenticated mode.
  • packages/contracts/src/hubSession.ts:5,19 HUB_SESSION_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1. The `open` frame is {type, streamId} only.
  • packages/shared/src/hubSessionCodec.ts:28-30 The codec encodes `open` as an empty payload. The auditor cited :34; the case is at :28.
  • docs/hub-session-protocol.md:9-11,23 The doc says each logical stream consumes a fresh single-use node ticket and that `open` is empty.
  • docs/hosted-hub-client.md:200-203,242-245 The documented restore order is directory refresh, then node validation, then ticket. Ticket custody: the ticket is requested over authenticated Hub HTTP for every logical attempt.
  • ryco-hub:src/relay/hubSession.ts:361-420,515-516 On origin/main, `case "open"` calls openStream(socket, streamId). That re-authorizes the cookie session per open and calls relay.openLogicalStream. No node or ticket minting happens there.
Remaining

Web hosted connects still serialise the HTTP ticket RTT, then the hub-session stream open plus the relay auth frame, then the node READY. This covers reload/deep-link restore, node select and switch, and relay-level reconnects over a healthy account socket. The sequence is transport.ts:349-358 (via :228), api.ts:2683, then relayEngine.ts:487-499. The Hub has no ticketless or server-minted stream open: ryco-hub src/relay/hubSession.ts:515, websocketRuntime.ts:1367. The hub-session protocol is still v1 (contracts/src/hubSession.ts:5,19; shared/src/hubSessionCodec.ts:28). The one case already hidden is resume over a dead account socket, where the ticket overlaps the account-socket reconnect.

Implementation sketch

Preferred: hub-session protocol v2 with a server-minted ticket (both repos, coordinated release, then a Hub deploy). The steps are below. (1) Contracts and codec. In packages/contracts/src/hubSession.ts, accept ready protocolVersion 1|2. Add a new frame kind 8 `openNode` {streamId, nodeId: RelayNodeId, capability: "ryco.rpc", protocolMajor: 1, protocolMinor: 2|3}. Use a new kind rather than overloading `open`: a v1 Hub then fails closed on an unknown kind, and the v1 `open` stays byte-identical. In packages/shared/src/hubSessionCodec.ts, encode the payload as [minor u8][capability u8][nodeId len u8][nodeId UTF-8]. Validate the nodeId with the RelayNodeId schema. Add round-trip and fail-closed tests: bad length, unknown capability, minor out of range, and kind 8 under v1. (2) Client session. In packages/client-runtime/src/relay/hostedHubSession.ts, record the negotiated version from READY. Expose serverTicketAvailable() (ready && version >= 2 && no armed probe). createSocket takes an optional {nodeId, protocolMinor}. #openStream sends `openNode` when that option is set and negotiated v2; it otherwise sends `open`. A pending stream that ends up on a v1 replacement after a reconnect must close with a retryable code, so the transport retries via the HTTP ticket. (3) Transport. In packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts nextUrl, add a binding hook serverMintedAttempt?(nodeId). Web wires it to the hub session's serverTicketAvailable(). When it is true, skip issueRelayAttempt and store a PendingTicket with ticket:null and serverMinted:true. createSocket passes {serverMinted:true, nodeId, protocolMinor} through createRelaySocket into BrowserHostedRelaySocket and createWebHubRelaySocket. Keep the existing HTTP path unchanged for v1, mobile and desktop. Keep the 400 invalid_request minor-3 to minor-2 fallback semantics: the Hub answers an unsupported minor with a typed close reason, and the client latches minor 2. (4) Relay engine. In relayEngine.ts, add a serverAuthenticated mode that sends no auth frame. It keeps the same 5 s authentication deadline and requires the Hub/node READY plus channel.accept as today. E2EE capability validation, the shell snapshot gate and the generation fencing do not change. (5) Hub (ryco-hub). In src/relay/hubSession.ts, add `case "openNode"`. It runs the same per-open cookie re-authorization already in openStream. It then calls a new ticketService.issueAndConsumeForSession(session, {nodeId, capability, protocolMajor, protocolMinor}). That function must apply exactly the /api/relay/tickets checks: browser session kind, space scoping, node authorization and revocation, node presence and live protocol binding (d21f9c8), rate limits and audits. Minting and consumption happen in one transaction, so no ticket row outlives the call. Then call openLogicalStream with a pre-authenticated RelayWebSocketData, and let the node handshake answer READY on the stream. Advertise ready version 2 only behind a config flag for rollout. (6) Docs. Update docs/hub-session-protocol.md (v2 table, negotiation, fail-closed rules) and docs/hosted-hub-client.md §Relay transport and ticket custody (a server-minted ticket for v2 sessions, with HTTP tickets kept for v1, native and desktop). Tests: transport.test.ts must assert that issueRelayTicket is not called when the session is v2-ready and is called for v1, not-ready or probe-armed sessions. hostedHubSession.test.ts covers version negotiation and a v2 pending stream crossing to a v1 replacement. relayEngine.test.ts covers no auth frame in server mode and the timeout. Hub tests prove authorization parity with /api/relay/tickets for every refusal reason, rate limiting, audit events, and v1 clients unaffected. A browser-suite hosted connect should show one fewer POST /api/relay/tickets. Cheap client-only interim (also a decision, because it changes the documented restore order at hosted-hub-client.md:200-203). In HostedHubController restore (packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts, around refreshDirectory/selectNode :2358), start issueRelayTicket(routedNodeId) in parallel with refreshDirectory when the routed id is in the last known directory. Hand the result to the attempt factory as a one-shot pre-issued ticket bound to {nodeId, generation}. Discard it if validation fails or the generation moves. This saves the RTT only on reload/deep-link restore, and a failed validation wastes a persisted ticket row.

Needs a decision

The full fix is a Hub protocol change: a new hub-session version and frame kind, plus server-side ticket minting and consumption over the WebSocket instead of a CSRF-protected HTTP POST. That changes the ticket-custody and authorization surface the docs define, needs a security review for parity with /api/relay/tickets, and needs a coordinated Hub release and deploy. The client-only interim reorders the documented fail-closed restore pipeline (a ticket before directory validation) and can waste single-use tickets, which is a product and security trade-off.

hub-connection:hosted-reconnect-no-shell-resume · original impact Medium, effort L · Caching decision

Current state

Hosted shell resume is still not implemented. Web hosted connections are excluded at service.ts:857 and :1296, and the mobile hosted primary (primaryConnection.ts:243) does not wire readShellResumeSequence. Hosted thread windows are excluded at supervision.ts:562. Each drop still downloads, decrypts and hydrates the full shell plus retained thread windows. No Hub-side or renamed implementation exists.

  • apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:857 `resumeShell = options.resumeShell === true && hostedGeneration === null` still excludes hosted. The doc comment at 825-831 states the policy. onShellResumed (863-866) only completes the query refresh and never calls markHostedSessionReady (snapshot path does so at 895-906).

  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:2001-2033 suspendBrowser bumps the generation and calls suspendHostedNode, which disconnects the primary (environment.ts:57-65). resumeBrowser -> #retrySelectedNode (2477-2523) -> activateHostedNode (environment.ts:67-92) builds a fresh connection.   • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:818-830 remove() (used by disconnectPrimary at 907-913) calls projectionTracker.clearEnvironment and unsubscribes thread subscriptions. After any suspend or reactivation, readShellProjectionSequence (1295-1298) returns null, so a cross-connection resume also needs the sequence captured or preserved, not just a hoisted hasShellBaseline.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/environment.ts:45-53 A node switch (deactivateCurrentHostedNode) resets the E2EE session and demotes the environment to a cached snapshot. The finding's 'node revisit' case therefore has no live projection to resume onto.

Remaining

Every hosted reconnect still transfers, decrypts, decodes and hydrates the full OrchestrationShellSnapshot (estimated ~363 KiB for the user's DB) plus every retained thread window. This happens in two cases. (1) In-session relay drops: the connection is kept since a38ecac4b, but the gate at apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:857 and :1296, the missing wiring at apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/primaryConnection.ts:243, and the thread exclusion at packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:562 force fresh snapshots. (2) Foreground resume (mobile background/foreground every time, web freeze/pagehide/offline), retrySelectedNode and session-sync retries: the connection is rebuilt (packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/environment.ts:57-92), and supervision.ts:818-830 remove() clears the projection sequence and thread subscriptions. Readiness on resume also needs a definition of 'current', because the `resumed` item precedes up to 1000 replayed events (orchestrationStreams.ts:865-876). The policy docs (AGENTS.md:63-65, docs/hosted-hub-client.md:381) need sign-off and updating.

Implementation sketch

Phase A, same connection (in-session relay drop, connection already kept since a38ecac4b). (1) Node protocol: in apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts makeReplayableShellStream (and makeReplayableThreadStream), when `resumed`, emit a trailing `{kind:'current', sequence}` item after the bounded replay stream ends and before live events. Alternatively carry `throughSequence` from captureReplayUpperBound. Add the item to OrchestrationShellStreamItem / thread window items in packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts and advertise a capability (e.g. `shellResumeCurrentMarker`) in the server config/welcome descriptor. (2) packages/client-runtime/src/connection/connection.ts: add `onShellResumeCurrent(environmentId)`, fired when that marker arrives after the preceding events are applied. Keep awaitingResubscribeBaseline semantics. (3) apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts: drop `&& hostedGeneration === null` at 857 and pass resumeShell: true at 1296. For hosted, offer resume only when the node advertises the capability and hostedHubStore.sessionStatus !== 'delivery-unknown' and no relay requests are pending (otherwise return null -> full snapshot). Call markHostedSessionReady(environmentId, hostedGeneration) + completeQueryRefresh only from onShellResumeCurrent, guarded by acceptsEvent(). Keep the #relayGapGeneration guard in state.ts:2641-2645. (4) apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/primaryConnection.ts:243: add the same readShellResumeSequence/onShellResumeCurrent wiring, calling coordinator.markSessionReady + markHostedSessionReady like syncShellSnapshot.onCurrent at 272-286. (5) supervision.ts:561-565: allow resumable for hosted thread windows on the same connection under the same capability, and update supervision.test.ts:424-441. Phase B, cross-connection (foreground resume/retrySelectedNode). (6) Add an in-memory hosted shell baseline registry in packages/client-runtime/src/authorization (e.g. shellBaseline.ts) storing {environmentId, sequence, accountSessionId, nodeId, effectiveRole, e2ee session class}. Capture it in suspendHostedNode / the same-node branch of activateHostedNode via readShellProjectionSequence before disconnectPrimary, because supervision.ts:823 clears the tracker. Invalidate it in deactivateCurrentHostedNode (node switch demotes the store), clearAccount/sign-out, effectiveRole or directory change, and delivery-unknown. (7) connection.ts:255: accept a seeded baseline (hasShellBaseline = true, awaitingResubscribeBaseline = true for the first subscription) so a first-subscription snapshot still resets the projection and a `resumed` keeps it. Restore the projectionTracker sequence on register. (8) Move thread appliedSequence from the attach closure into ThreadDetailSubscriptionEntry so it survives remove()/attach. (9) After sign-off, update AGENTS.md:63-65 and docs/hosted-hub-client.md:381. Tests: server stream tests for the current marker after replay and absence on the snapshot path; connection.test.ts for hosted resume with no readiness until the marker, snapshot fallback resetting the projection, and the seeded baseline; update apps/web/src/hostedHub/lifecycle.integration.test.ts:234 and apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/nodeLifecycle.test.ts:86 to cover stale-generation resumed items being ignored, the relay-gap guard, and role/account change forcing a snapshot; browser suite (bun run --cwd apps/web test:browser) since this touches hosted reconnect.

Needs a decision

Hosted resume relaxes the AGENTS.md:63-65 hosted lifecycle rule (accept a current shell snapshot before mutation capability) and docs/hosted-hub-client.md:381 ('Nothing is resumed'). It changes when hosted mutation authority is published, so it needs product/security sign-off. Doing it safely most likely also needs a node protocol addition (a caught-up/current marker after the resume replay, gated by a capability). That marker is a node/contracts change, not a Hub protocol change. The relay and E2EE semantics do not change. To reach hosted users the change ships through a Hub vendored-Ryco pin bump and deploy.

Not done#221 No payload compression on the relay; E2EE makes transport-level deflate useless

hub-connection:relay-payload-compression · original impact Medium, effort L · Network / RTT decision

Current state

Confirmed NOT_DONE. I searched for any relay compression path, including Hub-side ones, and found none. Since f1be4abc7, no commit adds CompressionStream, deflate-raw, a compressed inner type or an RPC-level compression flag; `git log -S` and `--grep=compress` only turn up the report HTML. Relay RPC is still JSON (RpcSerialization.json in apps/server/src/ws/RpcByteSession.ts), and both directions seal raw bytes under E2EE_INNER_TYPE_RPC. The permessage-deflate policy from #710 covers only the server's direct WebSocket. The Hub keeps perMessageDeflate: false, which would not help anyway because the ciphertext does not compress. Screenshots still travel as base64 JSON. I have four corrections or additions to the auditor's result. (1) The auditor's send-side evidence (relayE2eeChannel.ts:811, relayEngine.ts:561) is the client-to-node path, which the proposal deliberately leaves out. The node-to-client seal that matters is NodeE2eeChannelSession.ts:1610. The client receive point where inflation would go is relayEngine.ts:1230-1238. (2) Mobile runs on Hermes, which has no CompressionStream, and apps/mobile has no compression library. Mobile therefore needs fflate (or a native module), or it must simply not advertise the capability. (3) The Hub's 50 MiB transfer budget is a lifetime counter per channel that never resets, covers both directions, and is enforced in ryco-hub forwarder.ts:245-248. The client treats transfer_limit as non-retryable (relayEngine.ts:376-382). Compressing roughly 8x-compressible JSON would therefore also make each hosted channel last proportionally longer, not just speed up transfers. (4) The hosted screenshot sampler already spaces frames by their payload size (useDeviceScreenshotStream.ts:6-28: 512 KiB/s target, so about 5.8 s per phone frame). That code predates the report. It slows the drain on the budget but does not change the frame count: about 17 phone frames per channel still exhaust it, now over roughly 100 s instead of 13 s.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/NodeE2eeChannelSession.ts:1610 Node-to-client emit() seals the raw RPC bytes with protectRecord(session, E2EE_INNER_TYPE_RPC, bytes). There is no compress step. The legacy branch at :1587 sends the raw bytes too.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeSession.ts:1214 #protectCommitted: plaintext = encodeE2eeInnerRecord(request.innerType, request.body), then aead.seal. No compression.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeWire.ts:107 The inner-type registry is still RPC 0x01, CLOSE 0x02, ERROR 0x03 and CLOSE_ACK 0x04. There is no compressed variant.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayEngine.ts:1230 #deliver hands the result of channel.intercept() (disposition.message), or the legacy bytes, straight to events.onData. No inflate step. A decompressor would go here.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayE2eeChannel.ts:779 On the client send side, the ceiling check and submit under E2EE_INNER_TYPE_RPC (line 811) use the uncompressed size. This is the client-to-node direction.
  • apps/server/src/ws/RpcByteSession.ts:171 Relay RPC is serialized with RpcSerialization.json, so plain JSON goes into the E2EE record.
  • apps/server/src/webSocketCompression.ts:19 WEBSOCKET_PER_MESSAGE_DEFLATE (16 KiB threshold, level 1, no context takeover) from #710 applies only to the server's direct WS (server.ts:265). Its parameters could be reused for relay compression.
  • ryco-hub:origin/main:src/relay/hubSession.ts:453 The Hub sets perMessageDeflate: false (also websocketRuntime.ts:1066). Merged Hub code has no relay payload compression.
  • ryco-hub:origin/main:src/relay/forwarder.ts:245 state.transferBytes counts data payloads in both directions over the channel's lifetime and never resets. The default is 50 MiB (forwarder.ts:22, config.ts:148). Fewer bytes on the wire means the channel lasts longer.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayEngine.ts:376 transfer_limit is classified as a non-retryable protocol failure, so hitting the lifetime budget ends the channel.
  • packages/contracts/src/device.ts:583 DeviceScreenshotResult.bytesBase64 is still base64 PNG over JSON RPC (44 MiB max). computer.ts:559 and :782 are the same at 88 MiB.
  • apps/web/src/components/device/useDeviceScreenshotStream.ts:20 This mitigation predates the report. hostedScreenshotDelayMs spaces frames to about 512 KiB/s (5.8 s for a phone frame), which lowers the rate but not the bytes per frame or the frame count per channel budget.
Remaining

Nothing from the proposal is implemented. (1) Node-to-client relay RPC bodies are sealed uncompressed at apps/server/src/hubConnector/NodeE2eeChannelSession.ts:1610 (E2EE) and :1587 (legacy). The client receive path at packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayEngine.ts:1230-1238 has no inflate step. There is no negotiation or marker for it, either in E2EE inner types (packages/shared/src/relayE2eeWire.ts:107) or at the RPC layer. (2) Screenshot results remain base64 PNG in JSON: packages/contracts/src/device.ts:583-590 and computer.ts:559 and :782, consumed by apps/web/src/components/device/useDeviceScreenshotStream.ts. Even with the existing adaptive cadence, a hosted preview exhausts the Hub's lifetime 50 MiB channel budget after about 17 phone frames or 9 tablet frames.

Implementation sketch

Compression without touching the E2EE wire or the Hub. Put it inside the encrypted payload, at the RPC byte layer, so the Hub sees only opaque ciphertext and needs no change. (a) Add packages/shared/src/relayPayloadCompression.ts with a pure codec. A compressed payload is the byte 0x00, then a 4-byte big-endian uncompressed length, then a deflate-raw body. JSON RPC payloads never start with 0x00, so the marker cannot be mistaken for an uncompressed payload. Include encode/decode helpers and a hard maxInflatedBytes guard. Reuse the 16 KiB threshold and level 1 from apps/server/src/webSocketCompression.ts:19, and use a fresh context per message. (b) Node side: compress in the relay RPC output path before emit(), meaning NodeE2eeChannelSession emit() at :1586 or the RpcByteSession relay writer. Use zlib.deflateRaw on the threadpool, or deflateRawSync for bodies under about 1 MiB. Do it only when the peer advertised support and the body is at least 16 KiB. Keep the original if compression saves less than about 10%. Check the compressed size against plaintextCeiling. (c) Client side: inflate in relayEngine #deliver (relayEngine.ts:1230) after channel.intercept, and on the legacy branch. Chain through the existing #e2eeInbound promise so message order is kept even though the inflate is async. Browsers and desktop use DecompressionStream('deflate-raw'), reading chunk by chunk and aborting once maxInflatedBytes (for example the 4 MiB message limit or an explicit 16 MiB bound) is exceeded. Treat overflow or a corrupt stream as fatal for the channel (fatal_post_key on E2EE). Mobile needs fflate's streaming inflate, or it does not advertise the capability. (d) Negotiation: the client opts in with an in-band first application message or an RPC hello flag inside the encrypted channel. This avoids changing the signed §5.2 capability statement and the Hub's channel.open schema. The node compresses only after seeing the opt-in. Old clients keep getting uncompressed bytes. Client-to-node stays uncompressed. (e) Security: document in docs/relay-e2ee-protocol.md §2.5 and §4.5 that compressed lengths are visible. Exclude message kinds that mix Hub-influenced input with secrets (auth, pairing, tokens, credential-bearing settings). The simplest version is an allowlist: compress only shell, thread-window and server-config streams. Tests: codec unit tests (round trip, marker discrimination, threshold, incompressible skip, truncated or corrupt input, inflate-bomb cap). relayEngine ordering test with mixed compressed and plain messages under slow async inflate. RelayRpcIntegration test where a large shell snapshot crosses the compressed path. Interop tests: a non-opted-in client gets plain bytes, and a compressed payload sent to a legacy client is never emitted. Screenshots (separate, bigger win per byte): stop shipping base64 PNG over JSON for hosted previews. Either route the existing H.264 deviceFrame stream (packages/shared/src/deviceFrame.ts) over the relay, or add a hosted-only lossy downscaled JPEG/WebP screenshot variant in DeviceScreenshotResult (device.ts:583) consumed by useDeviceScreenshotStream.ts. A binary RPC field alone saves only about 25%. Test by checking that bytes per frame and frames per 50 MiB budget improve in useDeviceScreenshotStream.test.ts.

Needs a decision

Compressing before encrypting makes record lengths depend on content in a way the Hub can observe. The Hub is the adversary in the E2EE threat model (§2.1, §2.5), so this needs an explicit security and crypto review and an allowlist of message kinds that may be compressed. It also needs a negotiation design: an in-band RPC opt-in avoids changing the signed capability statement (§5.2) and the Hub protocol, but it is still a client/node wire compatibility decision. Mobile support needs a new dependency (fflate) or must be explicitly deferred. The screenshot part is a product trade-off: lossy or downscaled frames, or routing H.264 over the relay.

Value medium · effort L · risk high

Done#222 First Hub-session ready always re-fetches the directory and every node's thread-cache shell

hub-connection:redundant-ready-invalidation · original impact Low, effort S · Network / RTT

First-pass audit said PARTIAL; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

The fixable part is done: #710 (60633eff3) added structural directory reconciliation and a no-op patch guard, so a re-read that changes nothing no longer publishes a new nodes array or re-renders anything. The auditor's remaining item, skipping the first-ready invalidation with an #everReady flag, rests on a wrong premise and would cause a regression. The first ready is not redundant. On a cold start the directory read (state.ts:752-753) and the routed thread-cache prefetch are sent beside the session restore. The Hub session socket is only created after the store becomes authenticated (hubSession.ts:63,73-99). The Hub adds the socket to its invalidation fan-out (indexSession) only when the upgrade opens, just before it sends ready. Every cold-start read is therefore answered before this browser is subscribed, and a change in that window reaches the browser only through the ready-time re-read. It is the subscribe-then-read barrier. Removing it would save almost nothing. On the directory side, the cold-start read normally finishes before the socket is online, so it schedules the next poll at the unsubscribed 20 s cadence, and nothing reschedules that poll when the subscription comes online. Skipping the ready re-read would only move the same GET /api/nodes to t+20 s and leave the race open until then. On the thread-cache side, the re-reads already present the held version (If-None-Match, so 304/null in the common case). While the subscription is online there is no time-based shell or thread refresh, so dropping the barrier could leave a node's cached shell stale until some other thread-cache invalidation arrives. The existing test (hostedHubSession.test.ts:145-161) and docs/hub-session-protocol.md:54 treat the ready invalidation as intended. Nothing valid remains for this finding.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/hostedHubSession.ts:297 Still calls #notifyInvalidation({directory:true, threadCache:true}) on every ready, the first one included. This is unchanged and serves as the barrier (see below), not waste.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:752 #restoreAccess sends restoreSession and #prefetchDirectory together (752-753). The prefetched directory is committed at 773, after the authenticated patch at 765. #resumeBrowser does the same at 2055-2072. The directory read leaves before any Hub session socket exists.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/hubSession.ts:63 sync() creates and starts the HostedHubSession only once accountStatus is authenticated (63, 73-99), which is after the cold-start directory and thread-cache prefetch reads were sent. onInvalidate at 84-88 forwards to notifyDirectoryInvalidated and to the listeners.
  • ryco-hub:src/relay/hubSession.ts:471 origin/main: the open handler calls indexSession(socket) (471) and then sends ready (473). The fan-out at 278-307 reaches only sockets in sessions/sessionsByScope, so a change made after the Hub answered a cold-start read but before indexSession is never pushed to this browser. The ready-time re-read is the only thing that closes that gap.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:2317 The poll is scheduled at DIRECTORY_SUBSCRIBED_REFRESH_MS (120 s) only if hasLiveHubSubscription() is true when the read completes. Otherwise it is DIRECTORY_REFRESH_MS (20 s, line 488). The only #scheduleDirectory callers are 2223, 2317 and 2352, so nothing reschedules on subscription online. The cold-start read usually finishes before ready, so skipping the ready re-read would only move the GET /api/nodes to t+20 s, not remove it.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/threadReadCache.ts:484 With the subscription online, shells are refreshed only when nextShellRefresh === 0 (484-488), and the 15 s interval re-reads the thread only when !isSubscriptionOnline (521-524). Invalidations are the only refresh trigger while subscribed, so the ready invalidation (514-519) is the thread cache's only barrier against reads answered before the subscription existed. The prefetch at 332-397 is sent beside the access check.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/threadReadCache.ts:246 The barrier re-reads are conditional: readShell gets shells.get(node.id) as held, and readThread gets details...get(threadId) at 294. api.ts:2451/2468 sends If-None-Match. The thread-cache part of the cost is therefore N+1 cheap not-modified round trips, not full bodies.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.ts:2474 listNodes has no If-None-Match, so the barrier directory re-read (like every poll) returns a full body of a few KB at most 16 nodes. That is the only non-trivial residual cost, and it is not specific to this finding.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:429 Fixed part from 60633eff3 (#710). reconcileDirectoryNodes keeps unchanged node objects and returns the previous array when nothing changed. The guard at 2306-2315 publishes no patch when every key is Object.is-equal, and refreshedSelection reuses the selected object (2277-2280). Its doc comment (423-428) names 'the reconnect re-read' as a case it makes cheap, so the authors deliberately kept the barrier and made it cheap.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/hostedHubSession.test.ts:145 The test expects onInvalidate twice (161), from the first ready plus one explicit invalidate, so first-ready invalidation is pinned as intended behaviour. docs/hub-session-protocol.md:54 also documents that reconnection invalidates both domains.
Defects in the shipped fix

None found in the implemented part. reconcileDirectoryNodes handles reordering by id, keeps per-node identity, and returns the previous array when nothing changed. The patch guard compares every key with Object.is. The auditor's own closing change (an #everReady flag that skips the first ready) would itself be a defect if implemented, for the reasons in the summary.

Partial#223 Remember-this-browser cache re-encrypts and writes on every hosted store patch and every 750 ms while an agent streams

hub-connection:read-cache-write-amplification · original impact Low, effort S · CPU WP12B

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

PR #710 (60633eff3) fixed four things. Publishes and catalog writes now happen only on real changes. Each thread's capture is cached by message-list identity. The O(n^2) size trim is now incremental. Saves wait for requestIdleCallback. The per-environment 'skip unchanged record' check, however, does not work in the scenario the finding targets: an agent streaming while its thread is open. The global scrollRevision is one of the skip inputs, and it is bumped on every streaming render. MessagesTimeline re-runs handleScroll through requestAnimationFrame whenever rows change, and LegendList's maintainScrollAtEnd scrolling also fires it. handleScroll calls saveHostedThreadScroll, which calls changed() even when the position has not moved. So every 750 ms save during streaming rebuilds, re-stringifies, encrypts and writes every hydrated environment record (up to 16, each up to 1.9 MB), not only the streaming one. The auditor saw that the global inputs were too coarse but treated it as a minor case triggered by user keystrokes, scrolls or visits. In fact it fires continuously and automatically during streaming. For multi-node users, this cancels much of the per-environment saving.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/readCache.ts:416-427 Confirmed fixed: publish only when sameCatalog or sameItems differ, and the catalog is written only when JSON.stringify(nodes) changes. Covered by apps/web/src/browser/hostedReadCache.browser.tsx (one catalog write across lifecycle patches).
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/readCache.ts:457-484 Confirmed fixed: captureContent reuses captured content and entryBytes per thread while messageIdsByThreadId[id] and messageByThreadId[id] keep their identity.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/readCache.ts:556-569 Confirmed fixed: the trim is incremental. I checked the math: body minus '{}' (2 bytes), plus 2, plus the sum of entryBytes, plus the commas, equals the length of JSON.stringify(record). No unit test covers this equivalence.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/readCache.ts:96,448-451,497-514 scrollRevision is one module-wide counter and is part of every environment's SavedEnvironmentInputs. Any bump makes the skip check fail for all environments.
  • apps/web/src/persistence/hostedReadViewState.ts:10-17 saveHostedThreadScroll calls changed() (that is, onScrollChanged, so scrollRevision++ and scheduleSave) on every call, even when the position is the same as the stored one.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/MessagesTimeline.tsx:470-474,515-524,636-640 handleScroll calls saveHostedThreadScroll(routeThreadKey, scrollTop) unconditionally. Its deps include minimapItems, which is derived from rows. The effect at 636-640 runs requestAnimationFrame(handleScroll) whenever handleScroll or rows.length changes. computeStableMessagesTimelineRows (MessagesTimeline.logic.ts:1477-1495) returns a new array whenever the streaming row changes, so every streaming render bumps scrollRevision.
  • apps/web/src/components/chat/MessagesTimeline.tsx:913-916 maintainScrollAtEnd={liveFollowEnabled} with onScroll={handleScroll}: auto-follow scrolling during streaming also fires handleScroll.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/readCache.ts:501-502,653-654 The drafts inputs (composer.draftThreadsByThreadKey and draftsByThreadKey) are store-wide too. Typing in any composer invalidates every environment's record.
  • apps/web/src/persistence/hostedReadVault.ts:118-157 Each write still stringifies and encodes the whole record, encrypts it with AES-GCM, and calls store.getAll() on the records store, which reads every sealed blob (up to READ_VAULT_MAX_BYTES = 12 MiB) back from IndexedDB just to compute eviction. Unnecessary environment rewrites therefore cost a full vault read each time. This code is unchanged from f1be4abc7.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/readCache.ts:581-602 requestIdleCallback deferral is present. It falls back to a synchronous call where requestIdleCallback is missing, which has historically included Safari.
Remaining

Per-environment write skipping does not work during streaming. In apps/web/src/hostedHub/readCache.ts:497-514 the skip compares global inputs: scrollRevision (line 505) and the composer draft maps (501-502). scrollRevision is bumped continuously while a thread streams. The path is apps/web/src/components/chat/MessagesTimeline.tsx:636-640, then handleScroll at 470-474, then apps/web/src/persistence/hostedReadViewState.ts:10-17, which calls changed() unconditionally, then readCache.ts:448-451. So every 750 ms save rewrites every environment that has state in useStore. For each one it runs readWorkspaceMetadataSnapshot, the body stringify, and vault.write: a full-record stringify of up to 1.9 MB, TextEncoder, AES-GCM, an IndexedDB getAll of every sealed record (up to 12 MiB), and a put. Only the streaming environment's record actually changed. Single-node users are unaffected beyond the inherent rewrite of the active record. No test covers the per-environment skip or the incremental trim.

Defects in the shipped fix

(1) Main defect, more than the 'minor residual' the auditor described: the global scrollRevision is bumped automatically on every streaming render. The cause is MessagesTimeline's requestAnimationFrame handleScroll effect plus maintainScrollAtEnd, combined with saveHostedThreadScroll calling changed() even for an unchanged position. The savedInputs skip therefore never applies to the other environments during streaming. (2) The draft inputs are store-wide, so a keystroke in any composer invalidates all environments. (3) save() stamps each rebuilt metadata with Date.now(), so the next hostedHubStore patch fails sameItems and republishes once. This is bounded. (4) vault.write calls getAll() on all sealed records for every write. This was not caused by the fix, but it multiplies the cost of every unnecessary write. (5) No test covers the savedInputs skip or the byte equivalence of the incremental trim.

Implementation sketch

1. apps/web/src/persistence/hostedReadViewState.ts saveHostedThreadScroll: return early, without calling changed(), when hostedScrollPositions.get(key) === position. Do the same after rounding to whole pixels. Change the callback signature to changed(key) so the cache knows which environment moved. 2. apps/web/src/hostedHub/readCache.ts: replace the global scrollRevision with scrollRevisionByEnvironment: Map<EnvironmentId, number>. onScrollChanged(key) should parse the key with parseScopedThreadKey and bump only that environment; bump all if the key cannot be parsed. SavedEnvironmentInputs.scrollRevision then reads the per-environment value. Clear the map in forgetInMemory and when an environment is removed in reconcile. 3. Scope the draft inputs per environment. Keep a per-environment memo keyed on the store object's identity. When composer.draftsByThreadKey or draftThreadsByThreadKey changes identity, recompute each environment's filtered slice: the keys whose parseScopedThreadKey(key).environmentId or draft.environmentId match, or a draft session key belonging to that environment. Compare each slice shallowly (same keys, same prompt string or draft object) with the previous slice and reuse the previous slice object when equal. Put the slice object, not the store-wide map, into SavedEnvironmentInputs. Visits can be scoped the same way, since they change only on turn completion. 4. Optional and separate: in hostedReadVault.write, stop calling getAll() on every write. Keep sealed byte sizes in a small in-memory or separate metadata index, or use getAllKeys plus a stored size field, so eviction does not read up to 12 MiB of blobs per write. 5. Tests: in apps/web/src/browser/hostedReadCache.browser.tsx, hydrate two environments with the cache enabled and spy on vault.write. Update env A's messages several times and call saveHostedThreadScroll for an env A thread key. Advance past 750 ms plus idle. Assert that the only write calls name env A's environmentId. Also assert that saveHostedThreadScroll with an unchanged position schedules no write. Extract the trim into a pure helper, for example trimContentToBudget(bodyWithoutContent, entries, budget), and add a vitest unit test that compares its byte count with new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(record)).byteLength for random entries, including multi-byte characters.

Done#224 Node (re)connect runs the HTTPS challenge, signing and the WebSocket open strictly in sequence

hub-connection:node-connector-challenge-ws-serial · original impact Low, effort S · Waterfall

Current state

Confirmed DONE. Commit 60633eff3 (#710) changed RelayConnectionSession.#authenticate. It now starts the proof (readOrCreate, key selection, HTTPS challenge, sign) and opens the relay WebSocket at the same time. The auth frame goes out when both are ready, whichever finishes last. If the proof is still pending 4 s after open (RELAY_AUTHENTICATION_DEADLINE_MS 5 s minus 1 s), the early socket is released and the attempt retries in the old order: proof first, then a fresh socket. That is the whole primary proposal. I tried to break it through the timer hand-offs, open() throwing synchronously before the resolved-proof microtask, an error/close before auth while the proof is pending, shutdown during either leg, a Hub error frame before auth, and the PROOF_LATE-then-proof-rejects path. In every case the bytes are wiped, the failure kind is right, and nothing leaks or double-settles. The Hub starts its 5 s auth timer at socket open (websocketRuntime.ts open handler), so the node's 4 s release fits inside it. HubConnector adds a proofFirst mode after a refused proof (429/503/key-store failure), so a refusing Hub does not also get a relay upgrade on every retry. It resets after a successful authenticate. The post-ready steps before state.online (readState, confirmAuthenticatedKey, building the E2EE statement) are local and cached, with no Hub round trip. The only part not done is the optional 'longer-term' Hub change (challenge as the first WS frame). Now that both legs run in parallel it would save about 0 RTT: a fresh HTTPS challenge (TCP+TLS+POST) and the WS open (TCP+TLS+upgrade) are the same length. So it would only remove one TLS connection and one Hub request per reconnect, and is not worth a Hub protocol change.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/RelayConnectionSession.ts:364 #authenticate starts #prepareAuthentication() and, unless proofFirst, awaits #connect(proof, PROOF_AFTER_OPEN_DEADLINE_MS) beside it (377-380); on PROOF_LATE awaits the proof and opens a fresh socket with it in hand (381-388).
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/RelayConnectionSession.ts:159 PROOF_AFTER_OPEN_DEADLINE_MS = RELAY_AUTHENTICATION_DEADLINE_MS - 1_000, which is 4 s (contracts relay.ts:20 sets 5_000).
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/RelayConnectionSession.ts:473 When the proof resolves, the bytes are stored and sent at once if the socket is already open. A proof rejection fails the attempt. Released or closed attempts ignore the proof, and the bytes are wiped by the #authenticate handler at 369-371.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/RelayConnectionSession.ts:489 transport.open is called synchronously without waiting for the proof; the 5 s pre-open stall timer is armed at 613.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/RelayConnectionSession.ts:497 onOpen sends the auth frame if the proof is ready, otherwise it arms the 4 s proof-late timer, which releases the socket and resolves PROOF_LATE (507-511).
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/RelayConnectionSession.ts:438 A socket that fails before auth while the proof is pending is released, and the attempt reports the proof's own failure. The bytes are wiped. Checked against open() throwing before the resolved-proof microtask in the serial path: released=true is set synchronously, so the bytes are wiped once and nothing leaks.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnector.ts:938 The connector passes proofFirst. It resets after a successful authenticate (972) and is set when session.proofRefused (1047). The 1014-1034 steps before online are local reads: readState, confirmAuthenticatedKey, and the cached E2EE statement build.
  • apps/server/src/hubIdentity/HubNodeProofClient.ts:253 The proof still POSTs /api/node/auth/challenges, but this now overlaps the WS handshake. The Hub (origin/main src/http/identityRoutes.ts:259) still serves the route, and the optional first-frame challenge was not implemented.
  • ryco-hub:src/relay/websocketRuntime.ts:1072 The Hub arms its 5 s authentication timer in the socket open handler (origin/main), so the node's 4 s post-open wait leaves about 1 s minus 1 RTT for delivery and verification.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/RelayConnectionSession.test.ts:668 Tests cover send-on-late-proof (668), fallback to serial after the 4 s wait (710), proof failure winning over the early socket failure (780), the shutdown race (616), and proofFirst (888, 914). HubConnector.test.ts:949 and 1015 cover switching proofFirst on and off.
Defects in the shipped fix

None found. Minor non-defect trade-offs: (1) A slow proof (more than 4 s after open, e.g. a keychain prompt) costs one wasted relay upgrade per attempt, and the Hub rate-limits upgrades per peer IP. The proofFirst flag only covers refused proofs, not slow ones, but attempts are backed off, so this is negligible. (2) Under very high RTT (above about 1 s) a proof that lands just before the 4 s release could arrive after the Hub's 5 s timer. The node then gets authentication_timeout and retries. This is an edge case only. (3) The proof-first mode is sticky until an authenticate succeeds, so the first reconnect after a 429/503 refusal is serial. That is intended.
