Done#225 Ticket issuance pays two POSTs on every attempt against Hubs that reject protocolMinor 3

hub-connection:ticket-minor-fallback-memo · original impact Low, effort S · Network / RTT WP15

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The status DONE stands for the performance cost. The auditor understated the fix defect: a session that keeps offering minor 2 after a mid-session Hub upgrade does not just miss an optimisation. The current Hub returns 426 for minor-3 nodes, which the client treats as a terminal 'incompatible' failure, a regression from the old behaviour that recovered on its own. Also, the 'returned minor > offeredMinor' response check is not new; it already existed at f1be4abc7.

Current state

The performance finding is fixed. Since 60633eff3, HostedHubApi.issueRelayTicket remembers a minor-3 refusal per instance in #relayTicketMinorFallback, so later tickets against a Hub that rejects minor 3 cost one POST. The memo is cleared by clearSessionMaterial(), and every ticket caller (web/mobile runtime singleton, desktop coordinator #api) holds one long-lived instance. Origin is fixed per instance: mobile builds a new instance after a Hub profile change. On the current Hub, a minor-3 request gets 400 invalid_request only for body/schema errors, and those would also fail the minor-2 retry, so the memo cannot be set falsely. The fix has one real defect the auditor dismissed. The memo never expires, and the current Hub answers a minor-2 offer for a node live at minor 3 with 426 unsupported_version. The client classifies that as a non-retryable 'incompatible' failure. A session that memoised minor 2 and then sees the Hub upgraded (or rolled back and forward again) is therefore cut off from minor-3 nodes until sign-out or restart. Before the fix, each attempt offered minor 3 first and recovered on its own.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.ts:833 #relayTicketMinorFallback memo field, per HostedHubApi instance.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.ts:2694 offeredMinor starts at 2 when the memo is set. Nothing ever probes minor 3 again for this instance.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.ts:2701-2711 The 3->2 retry only runs when offeredMinor===3 and the error is 400 invalid_request. The memo is set after the minor-2 POST resolves. A memoised minor-2 request that fails (e.g. 426) is rethrown and the memo stays set.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.ts:2713-2722 The check that result.protocolMinor > offeredMinor is rejected already existed at f1be4abc7. It is not new in the fix, contrary to the auditor's wording.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.ts:897-902 clearSessionMaterial() resets the memo. This is the only reset path.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.test.ts:408-451 Tests cover the [3,2,2] sequence, a minor-2 rejection that is not retried, and the reset after clearSessionMaterial. No test covers a memoised minor-2 request getting 426.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:117-138 ticketFailure maps unsupported_version to { kind: 'incompatible', retryable: false }, so a 426 on the ticket POST is terminal. shouldReconnect also stops on terminal-failure (transport.ts:239-247).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:228 Ticket callers (here, transport.ts:356, mobile accountE2eeAttempt.ts:247, desktop desktopHostedIdentity.ts:431) all go through one long-lived HostedHubApi, so the memo persists for the whole app/session lifetime.
  • ryco-hub:src/relay/ticketService.ts:358-368 origin/main Hub rejects a ticket with 426 unsupported_version when the node's live minor (presence.protocol.protocolMinor, ticketService.ts:251) is above the offered minor. The rejection happens inside the issuance transaction, before any ticket exists.
  • ryco-hub:src/http/relayRoutes.ts:14-20,74-75 The current Hub accepts minor 2|3. Its only 400 invalid_request on this route is body/schema/content-type (httpSecurity.ts:160-185). DPoP and CSRF failures use session_invalid or csrf_rejected, so a false memo is effectively impossible against the current Hub.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:470-484 A mobile Hub profile change sets configured=false. The next configureHostedRuntime builds a fresh HostedHubApi, so the memo does not cross Hub origins. Desktop pins the origin per instance (desktopHostedIdentity.ts:64-95).
Defects in the shipped fix

The memo is sticky for the instance lifetime and has no recovery path. Proposal: 'reset on a successful minor-3 issuance'. That reset is unreachable because minor 3 is never offered again once memoised. Scenario: a native (desktop/mobile) client on a self-hosted Hub that rejects minor 3 sets the memo. The Hub is then upgraded, or rolled back and forward, while the app keeps running, and nodes reconnect at minor 3. The client keeps offering minor 2. The Hub answers 426 unsupported_version (ryco-hub ticketService.ts:358-368), and ticketFailure turns that into a terminal, non-retryable 'incompatible' failure (transport.ts:137-138). The user loses relay access to those nodes until sign-out or app restart. Before the fix, every attempt offered minor 3 first and recovered automatically. The window is narrow (the official Hub already accepts minor 3, and web-tier JS is served by the Hub itself), but the consequence is a connectivity failure, not just a missed optimisation, so the auditor's 'None that matter' is too generous.

Implementation sketch

packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.ts, issueRelayTicket (~2694-2712): extend the catch block. When offeredMinor===2 because the memo was set (track `const memoised = this.#relayTicketMinorFallback` before the first request), and the error is a HostedHubApiError with status 426 and code 'unsupported_version', clear #relayTicketMinorFallback and retry once with minor 3. This is safe because the Hub rejects inside the issuance transaction before creating a ticket, which fits the existing 'never retry an uncertain issuance' rule. Leave the existing 3->2 path on 400 invalid_request as is. Optional hardening: give the memo a TTL (e.g. record the timestamp and re-offer minor 3 after ~15-30 min) so a Hub upgrade is picked up even for nodes still at minor 2. Tests in packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/api.test.ts: (1) memoise via [3->400 invalid_request, 2->201 minor 2], then [2->426 unsupported_version, 3->201 minor 3], and assert the offered sequence [3,2,2,3] and that the next call offers 3; (2) a non-memoised minor-3 request that gets 426 is rethrown without retry; (3) a memoised minor-2 request that gets 400/403 is not retried. Validation: focused `bun run test` on the client-runtime api.test.ts only.

A legacy useQuery read with the default retry of 3 that mounts while the session is synchronizing gets refused and sleeps 1 s, then 2 s, in backoff. The post-ready refreshActiveQueriesForEnvironment then calls refetch(force), which joins that sleeping attempt, so the read goes out when the backoff ends rather than right after ready. Example: the WorkItemsTab vcs.listRefs query (apps/web/src/components/projectExplorer/WorkItemsTab.tsx:164-176). Keyed atom queries are not affected (keyedQuery.ts:332-395 has no retry sleep; refreshActiveEnvironment re-runs error states).
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/capabilities.ts:30 Capability hooks pass sessionReady: hostedSessionAdmits(state, method). The same applies at apps/web/src/rpc/sourceControlReadAdmission.ts:51, apps/web/src/components/settings/useDiagnosticsCapability.ts:34 and apps/web/src/lib/threadExport.ts:34. Source-control keyed queries get key null, and so do not fire, until 'ready'.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/primaryConnection.ts:131-147 The native app calls the same admitHostedRequestForState with its per-connection state. Any change to the shared policy changes mobile read admission too.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/shellSnapshotAssembly.ts:51 d2aa947a3 pages the snapshot, but the assembler applies it only at snapshot-end, so 'ready' still waits for every page of a large shell. Because pages are bounded at 1 MiB, admitted reads could now interleave with them on the relay.
  • packages/shared/src/rpcAccessPolicy.ts:285-521 RPC_DELIVERY_EFFECT_POLICY now classifies 116 methods as read, 104 as mutation and 1 as receipted. The finding's 106 is out of date.
Remaining

Every hosted unary read (116 read-effect methods) that a view issues before the shell snapshot is accepted is refused at request start (packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:79,100; packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/protocol.ts:442). It is re-run only by the post-ready refresh (apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:842-855,894-906; apps/web/src/rpc/environmentQueryRefresh.ts:36-50) or by an admission change (source-control keyed queries via apps/web/src/rpc/sourceControlReadAdmission.ts:51). So each first-paint read costs one browser to Hub to node round trip after the full, possibly paged, snapshot instead of being pipelined with it. This happens on cold connect and on every adopted reconnect (state.ts:2624-2656). On top of that, legacy useQuery reads with default retries (apps/web/src/rpc/queryClient.ts:396-399,437-438) can wait out a 1-2 s retry backoff after ready, because a forced refetch joins the sleeping attempt. Impact on the thread view's primary content stays low: shell, thread window, VCS status, server config and terminal events already come through the admitted session-sync subscriptions. The cached Hub shell/thread reads from 8c42d3334 also paint the thread before the relay is up.

Implementation sketch

Part A is cheap, independent and needs no policy change. In QueryClient.fetch (apps/web/src/rpc/queryClient.ts:396-445), do not retry when the error is isAwaitingAdmission(error) (import from @ryco/client-runtime/rpc). Record the error state at once and let the post-ready refreshActiveQueriesForEnvironment re-run it, as keyed queries already do. Alternatively, let a force:true fetch supersede an attempt that is sleeping in backoff (bump fetchId and start a new run). Test: a vitest that mounts a query whose queryFn throws RpcRequestRefusedError('awaiting-session') once and then succeeds, calls refreshActiveQueriesForEnvironment, and asserts the queryFn runs again without the 1 s timer advancing. Part B is the actual proposal and needs a decision. (1) Add a shared predicate such as hostedSessionAdmitsRead(state, method) in packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/capabilities.ts. It is true when rpcDeliveryEffectFor(method)==='read' and sessionStatus is one of 'synchronizing' | 'replaying' | 'stale' (the channel is a fresh or adopted current-generation channel), and false for 'closed'. Keep hostedSessionAdmits unchanged for mutation and receipted methods. (2) In admitHostedRequestForState (packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:72-101), add a branch for !info.stream && rpcDeliveryEffectFor(info.tag)==='read' && transportStatus==='online' && roleFresh && (browserStatus==='current' || browserStatus==='synchronizing') && hostedSessionAdmitsRead(...). This automatically covers mobile (apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/primaryConnection.ts:137). (3) Make the read-only capability callers use the read predicate: apps/web/src/rpc/sourceControlReadAdmission.ts:51, apps/web/src/lib/threadExport.ts:34, and read-only uses of apps/web/src/hostedHub/capabilities.ts:30 and useDiagnosticsCapability.ts:34. Mutation capabilities keep sessionReady===ready. (4) Split isHostedEnvironmentQueryRefreshReady (apps/web/src/rpc/environmentQueryRefresh.ts:36-50) into a reads-may-run gate (session established or synchronizing on the current generation) and keep the post-snapshot refresh. The existing staleness check in refreshActiveQueriesForEnvironment (queryClient.ts:370-386) and keyedQuery refreshActiveEnvironment already skip fresh successful entries, so a read that succeeded before the snapshot is not fetched twice as long as staleTime > 0. Queries with staleTime 0 need a per-generation 'fetched since begin()' mark to avoid the double fetch. (5) Update the tests that encode the current policy: packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.test.ts:543-565 and 586 ('retains only session-sync authority...'), capabilities.test.ts, environmentQueryRefresh.test.ts and apps/mobile/src/connection/hostedConnectionCoordinator.test.ts. Add cases where reads are allowed while synchronizing or replaying, mutations stay 'awaiting-session', and stale-generation reads are fenced. (6) Validate with the hosted browser suite (apps/web test:browser) and a cold-connect trace on a large shell to confirm reads overlap the snapshot pages.

Needs a decision

Part B changes the hosted admission policy that AGENTS.md assigns to the single hosted lifecycle owner. Its tests deliberately encode 'retains only session-sync authority' until the snapshot. Reads before the snapshot is accepted are not mutation authority, but the hosted lifecycle owner still has to sign off. The change also alters native (mobile) admission, because both apps share admitHostedRequestForState. Part A (no retry on awaiting-admission in the legacy QueryClient) involves no policy change and can be done without a decision.

Value low · effort M · risk medium

Done#227 Client NX handshake runs cold, pure-JS noble X25519/Ed25519 on the main thread, about 25 ms on desktop V8 for the first connect

hub-connection:e2ee-handshake-noble-cpu · original impact Low, effort M · Crypto decision

Current state

Confirmed DONE, and now measured. #710 (60633eff3) shipped proposal (a): a once-per-process warmE2eePrimitives(), scheduled in an idle callback when the hosted account becomes authenticated. It also shipped proposal (c), in a more general form: a 128-entry MRU memo of true verdicts inside the single verifyE2eeSignature choke point. In fresh Node 24 (V8) processes, the handshake primitive set (2 keygen + 2 DH + 2 strict Ed25519 verifies) took 21-24 ms cold and 4.7-4.9 ms after the warm-up. The warm-up's own ~20 ms runs off the connect path. A memoized repeat verify took 0.12-0.27 ms against ~1.1 ms for a miss. The web hosted runtime is the only web path that runs the NX handshake, and every signature check goes through the memoized choke point. Only the optional WebCrypto fast path (b) is missing. It would save a few ms, needs the synchronous Noise DH made async, and needs crypto review.

Evidence
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeKeys.ts:760 warmE2eePrimitives(): runs once per process (primitivesWarmed guard). It does a throwaway x25519 keygen x2 plus getSharedSecret, then one strict Ed25519 verify of the RFC 8032 TEST 1 vector (:746-748) through verifyE2eeSignature, which also warms the validators and SHA-512/SHA-256. Errors are swallowed.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/e2eeAttempt.ts:430 scheduleWebE2eeWarmUp() loads the E2EE chunk, then runs the warm-up in requestIdleCallback with a 2 s timeout (:436), or setTimeout 0 where that is missing (e.g. Safari). It is called from watchWebHostedSessionForE2ee (:396-410) on the initial authenticated state and on each later transition to authenticated. It is skipped when the §14.5 randomness check failed.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:37 The watch is registered when the hosted runtime is configured, so the warm-up trigger really runs in production. The warm-up's .then is registered before prepareWebRelayE2ee's continuation (:146), so it is queued before the ticket POST and the WS open.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeKeys.ts:659 verifyE2eeSignature runs the §7.1 validators first, then the memo lookup (:664-667 Ed25519, :673-676 P-256). Only true verdicts are stored. The key (:704-717) is SHA-256 over the length-prefixed algorithm, key, message and signature. The MRU bound is 128 (:701, :719-731). No defect found. On a hit the validator still decompresses the point (~0.1 ms). That is redundant but harmless.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeCapabilityVerify.ts:303 The statement signature goes through the memoized choke point. Time, origin, pin and policy checks (:331 onward) stay outside the memo, as proposal (c) required.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeTranscripts.ts:910 Continuity-chain link signatures (:910) and the prekey cross-signature (:1854) also go through the memoized verifier. The initiator calls verifyNodeE2eeCapabilityStatement at packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayE2eeInitiator.ts:619.
  • apps/server/src/hubIdentity/NodeE2eeCapabilityStatement.ts:333 The node reuses a signed statement until expiresAt minus E2EE_MAX_CLOCK_SKEW. Validity is 600 s and skew is 300 s (relayE2eeConstants.ts:279-281), so a reconnect within ~5 min gets identical statement bytes and a memo hit. Later reconnects re-verify only the statement signature. The prekey and chain-link verdicts still hit.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeNoise.ts:930 The ephemeral keygen (:930) and DH (:971, inside the synchronous #mixDh) still run noble on the browser main thread on every handshake. Browsers and Hermes never install the §14.7 native seam (relayE2eeKeys.ts:333-337). This is the part only proposal (b) would remove.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/e2eeWarmUp.test.ts:91 Tests pin the trigger: no warm-up while signed out or when randomness is unusable, exactly once after authentication, and none on later patches. relayE2eeKeys.test.ts:283-348 covers memo semantics (failures not stored, validation still enforced, bound of 128) and that the warm-up is idempotent.
  • measurement (read-only node one-off, fresh process each, Node v24.21.0) Cold: keygen x2 11.2-12.4 ms, DH x2 1.6-2.2 ms, verify x2 8.4-9.4 ms, total 21.3-24.1 ms. After warmE2eePrimitives (itself 20.3-20.4 ms): keygen x2 0.8-1.0 ms, DH x2 1.5-1.7 ms, verify x2 2.2-2.4 ms, total 4.7-4.9 ms. Repeat verify with a memo hit: 0.12-0.27 ms.
Remaining

Only optional proposal (b) remains. The WebCrypto fast path for X25519 and Ed25519 verify on the browser initiator is not implemented. One ephemeral keygen plus 2 DH (relayE2eeNoise.ts:930, :971), and any memo-miss verify (the statement signature on reconnects more than ~5 min apart, or the first connect), still run noble synchronously on the main thread. That is roughly 2-5 ms on desktop for the first connect, about 1.5 ms per reconnect, and an estimated 4-5x that on a phone. Minor gaps not in the proposal: the warm-up does not warm ChaCha20-Poly1305, HKDF or cborg decode (the finding measured ~0.9 ms cold AEAD). One warm-up pass leaves V8 only partly tiered: 4.7 ms after warm-up versus ~2.6 ms fully warm. The 2 s requestIdleCallback timeout means that on a very busy first load the warm-up can land after the first channel.accept. That first handshake then pays the cold cost and nothing breaks. apps/mobile (Hermes) has no warm-up, but finding 242 covers mobile JS crypto cost, not this one.

Needs a decision

Nothing is required: the finding's described cost (cold noble setup on the first connect, and repeat verifies on reconnect) is removed. The only remaining item, the optional proposal (b), changes which implementation computes E2EE verdicts and DH outputs in browsers (WebCrypto next to the pinned noble primitive under the §14.7 rules), and it would make the synchronous Noise DH path async. That needs crypto/security review and a decision that a few ms per handshake is worth it.

Value low · effort M · risk medium

Partial#228 Server/desktop relay E2EE uses noble where node:crypto is 6-30x faster for the identical algorithms

hub-connection:node-native-crypto · original impact Low, effort M · Crypto WP15decision

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

Commit c1a83bcab fully covers nodes that run under real Node (ryco serve and the CLI node). There, record AEAD for records of 2 KiB or more, X25519, Ed25519 verify and P-256 verify go through node:crypto behind known-answer self-tests, with noble deciding every rejection. The wiring and the parity logic check out, and no correctness bug was found. Two parts of the finding remain. (1) On desktop-hosted nodes, the packaged backend runs under ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE. createCipheriv there has no chacha20-poly1305 (re-verified: Electron 44.7.0 and Bun 1.4.0 report 'Unknown cipher', and support() is chacha20Poly1305:false), so record sealing stays on noble. That was the finding's main cost: per-MiB sealing and about 9.5 ms per 3 MB screenshot frame. Electron 44.7's WebCrypto does provide ChaCha20-Poly1305 with output byte-identical to noble. I measured about 4.5x the throughput (3 MB: 9.55 ms on noble against 1.99 ms wall), and because the work runs on the libuv threadpool, the event-loop cost is only about 0.04 ms at 256 KiB and 0.3 ms at 3 MB. That route is async and experimental in Node 24, so the synchronous seam cannot use it. (2) The proposal's parity gate, which reuses the existing relay E2EE corpus with the provider installed, was not built. Section 14.7 itself says the §16 corpus MUST pass with the native implementations installed and absent, yet no corpus test installs the provider. Section 14.7 is also still marked as awaiting owner acceptance.

Evidence
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeNodeCrypto.ts:18-24,36,149-198,332-409 node:crypto provider: lazy known-answer gates, a 2 KiB AEAD threshold and createCipheriv('chacha20-poly1305'). The comment at lines 21-22 states that Electron's BoringSSL and Bun lack ChaCha20-Poly1305.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeSession.ts:404-444 suiteRecordAead dispatches to native AEAD when it is installed and passed its self-test, and otherwise uses noble. The seam is synchronous. seal is called at :1217 inside async #protectCommitted, and open is called at :1416 inside synchronous #unprotect.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts:105-112 The packaged desktop backend (the server that runs HubConnectorLive and seals relay records for desktop-hosted nodes) runs with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, so the ChaCha known-answer test fails and records stay on noble.
  • apps/desktop/src/desktopHubStack.ts:10-18 The desktop main process installs the provider, but it only runs handshakes (desktopNativeE2ee*.ts) and seals no records. The comment confirms record AEAD stays on the pinned primitive.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorLive.ts:323 installE2eeNodeNativePrimitives() runs when the connector service is built. HubConnectorDeferred loads it, and it runs before any NodeE2eeChannelSession seals.
  • /tmp/v228/support.mjs (one-off probe) makeE2eeNodeNativePrimitives().support() reports all four primitives true on Node 24.21. On Electron 44.7 run as Node and on Bun 1.4 it reports x25519, ed25519 and p256 true and chacha20Poly1305 false.
  • /tmp/v228/bench.mjs (one-off probe) Under Electron 44.7 run as Node, subtle.encrypt ChaCha20-Poly1305 (raw-secret import) matches noble byte for byte. Wall time: 256 KiB 0.197 ms against 0.893 ms on noble, and 3 MB 1.99 ms against 9.55 ms. The synchronous issue cost on the event loop was 0.037 ms and 0.29 ms.
  • docs/relay-e2ee-protocol.md:5071-5078 Section 14.7 is marked 'proposed ... recording owner acceptance ... is REQUIRED' and says 'the §16 corpus MUST pass with the native implementations installed and with them absent'.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeCorpus.test.ts; apps/server/src/hubConnector/relayE2eeNodeCorpus.test.ts Neither file installs the provider. git grep finds installE2eeNativePrimitives and makeE2eeNodeNativePrimitives only in relayE2eeKeys.ts, relayE2eeNodeCrypto.ts and relayE2eeNodeCrypto.test.ts, and the vitest config has no setupFiles. The corpus runs only with the provider absent.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeNodeCrypto.test.ts:177-594 Dedicated parity tests cover X25519 low-order and non-canonical inputs, Ed25519 torsion, S+L and small-order cases, P-256 edge cases, AEAD forgeries, and one E2eeRecordSession run with and without the provider. These are solid, but they do not replace the corpus gate.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeKeys.ts:128-131,495-505,519-533,659-679 On the native Ed25519 path the public key A is decoded twice: once by isValidPublicKey in validateE2eeNodeIdentityPublicKey, and again with isSmallOrder in ed25519NativeVerdictAdmissible. R is also decoded. Measured verifyE2eeSignature: 215 us native against 710 us noble (3.3x). The raw primitive is 55 us against 680 us.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeNoise.ts:12,930,971; relayE2eeHandshake.ts:1712 Handshake DH and keygen go through the dispatchers. The Noise CipherState AEAD (relayE2eeNoise.ts:317,332) stays on noble by design, and its messages are small.
Remaining

(1) Desktop-hosted nodes: the packaged backend runs under Electron as Node (backendLauncher.ts:111), and createCipheriv lacks chacha20-poly1305 there. suiteRecordAead (relayE2eeSession.ts:404-444) therefore always falls back to noble chacha20poly1305 for sealing snapshots, screenshots and streams, which takes about 0.9 ms per 256 KiB and 9.5 ms per 3 MB frame on the event loop. A native route exists (Electron 44.7 WebCrypto ChaCha20-Poly1305), but it is async and the AEAD seam is synchronous. (2) The parity gate in the proposal and in §14.7 (docs/relay-e2ee-protocol.md:5077) is not implemented: relayE2eeCorpus.test.ts and relayE2eeNodeCorpus.test.ts never run with the provider installed. (3) Section 14.7 still awaits owner acceptance (docs:5071-5072), although the fast paths are live in production.

Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness defects found. AEAD seal is deterministic and open is tag-checked, X25519 rejects all-zero output, Ed25519 admits a native true only behind strict decode, small-order and S<L checks, P-256 admits only a native true, and every native false or throw is re-decided by noble. All four self-tests pass on Node 24.21. Gaps: the §14.7 'MUST pass the corpus with native installed' is unenforced by any test, and a minor inefficiency decodes A twice per Ed25519 native verify (relayE2eeKeys.ts:130 and :497), about 50 us of the 215 us native-path cost.

Implementation sketch

A) Desktop-backend record AEAD through WebCrypto (async). In relayE2eeKeys.ts, add an optional member to E2eeNativePrimitives such as chacha20Poly1305Async { minBytes; seal(key, nonce, plaintext, aad): Promise<Uint8Array> }. In relayE2eeNodeCrypto.ts, implement it with crypto.webcrypto.subtle.importKey('raw-secret', key, {name:'ChaCha20-Poly1305'}, false, ['encrypt']) and subtle.encrypt({name:'ChaCha20-Poly1305', iv: nonce, additionalData: aad}, k, plaintext). Import per record and do not cache CryptoKeys, so the key lifetime matches the createCipheriv path (§9.5). Gate it with an async RFC 8439 §2.8.2 known-answer test plus a forged-tag decrypt, started by installE2eeNodeNativePrimitives and unusable until it resolves. Enable it only when the synchronous native ChaCha is unavailable (Electron, Bun). Handle the one-time ExperimentalWarning. In relayE2eeSession.ts, give E2eeRecordAead an optional sealAsync. #protectCommitted (around 1192-1230) should await it for plaintexts at or above a tuned threshold (about 16-64 KiB) and fall back to the synchronous noble seal on rejection. Re-check #erased after the await, and treat an erase during the seal as send_failed without transmitting. Keep the plaintext-erasure finally after the await, and keep the state advance under the existing #sendQueue serialization. Leave the receive path (#unprotect, synchronous) unchanged, since records the node receives are small. Tests: sealAsync parity across sizes against noble, async known-answer failure falling back, erase during an in-flight seal, envelope parity of E2eeRecordSession with sync noble. Benchmark manually with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 apps/desktop/node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron. Update §14.7 and the desktopHubStack.ts comment. B) Corpus parity gate. Wrap the top-level suites of packages/shared/src/relayE2eeCorpus.test.ts and apps/server/src/hubConnector/relayE2eeNodeCorpus.test.ts in describe.each([['pinned', undefined], ['native', makeE2eeNodeNativePrimitives()]]). Use beforeAll(() => installE2eeNativePrimitives(p)) and afterAll(() => installE2eeNativePrimitives(undefined)), and assert that support() is all true on Node in the native leg. Alternatively, export a defineCorpusSuites() and add *.native.test.ts files. C) Optional: skip the second decode of A by having validateE2eeNodeIdentityPublicKey also return the small-order verdict, or by using a small bounded per-key admissibility memo.

Needs a decision

Part A changes E2EE record-sealing semantics on the send path: async AEAD, an experimental WebCrypto algorithm, and CryptoKey lifetime against §9.5 erasure. It needs a crypto and security review, and §14.7 must be updated. Section 14.7 itself is still marked as needing owner acceptance (docs/relay-e2ee-protocol.md:5071), although the native fast paths already run in production. Part B (corpus run with the provider installed) is test-only and needs no decision.

Partial#229 Browser relay data plane does ~7 full copies, a full CBOR re-encode and noble decryption per chunk on the main thread

hub-connection:web-data-plane-main-thread · original impact Low, effort M · CPU decision

Current state

PARTIAL is correct. Parts (a) and (b) are in place and both are in the Hub-vendored Ryco 7bc39eec3. #710 (60633eff3) made the inbound path zero-copy: the WS ArrayBuffer is handed over, the hub-session data payload is borrowed, and the engine's owned, payload and delivered copies are gone. ws.send also no longer copies. 2cb0d3f5e replaced the full canonical re-encode and compare with a spliced prefix/head/suffix check (840 to 32 us per 256 KiB on Node) and stopped copying outbound chunks the engine already owns. Part (c) is not done. There is no Worker for HostedHubSession, HostedRelayEngine or the E2EE channel. On browsers, noble ChaCha20-Poly1305 still runs on the main thread, as one synchronous call per reassembled record (about 9 ms for a 3 MB message on desktop V8). Small copy leftovers remain: the facade copy at relaySocket.ts:244, the assembler copy and concat, and the outbound encodeRelayFrame and hub-session header copies.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.ts:62 Inbound ArrayBuffer is wrapped without slice (was data.slice(0)); changed in 60633eff3.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.ts:90 send passes the view straight to ws.send (was Uint8Array.from(bytes).buffer).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/hostedHubSession.ts:280 decodeHubSessionFrame(bytes, { borrowDataPayload: true }). The codec returns a subarray at packages/shared/src/hubSessionCodec.ts:112. Dropped-data paths zero the payload at :333 and :338.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayEngine.ts:768 decodeRelayFrame runs on the handed-over buffer, which is zeroed at :772; the owned copy is gone. cborg's decode still copies the payload once (byte-utils slice -> data.slice). That is now the single necessary inbound copy.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayEngine.ts:1159 frame.payload is queued as is. #drainInbound hands it to the assembler at :1204 without the delivered copy.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayEngine.ts:593 Outbound chunk copy now runs only when chunk === payload; the same at :1121 (2cb0d3f5e).
  • packages/shared/src/relayCodec.ts:103 isCanonicalEncoding spliced check for byte-string payloads of 1 KiB or more, called at :181. The cborg decode plus the Schema decode at :275 remain, but there is no full re-encode or compare.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.ts:244 this.#engine.send(Uint8Array.from(b)) remains. Hosted RPC uses RpcSerialization.layerJson (packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/protocol.ts:517), so writes are strings and b is already a fresh TextEncoder buffer (:235). Every engine sink copies again: e2ee at relayE2eeChannel.ts:789, negotiating at relayEngine.ts:660, legacy unchunked at :593. The facade copy is only ever zeroed on the legacy error path (relayEngine.ts:582), and that path is the only reason the copy exists for caller-owned views.
  • packages/shared/src/relayMessageChunks.ts:307 The assembler still does Uint8Array.from(body) plus a fill per chunk, then a concat at :319. The input is already engine-owned and is mutated by the assembler anyway. The server caller apps/server/src/ws/RpcByteSession.ts:249 also hands its buffer over.
  • packages/shared/src/hubSessionCodec.ts:70 Outbound data frames are still copied to prepend the 5-byte header. encodeRelayFrame (relayCodec.ts:294-308) still does a Schema decode plus a cborg encode that copies the payload.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeKeys.ts:333 Native fast paths are never installed in browsers; only installE2eeNodeNativePrimitives (relayE2eeNodeCrypto.ts:408) installs them, for server and desktop. Web AEAD is noble (relayE2eeNoise.ts:1).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayE2eeChannel.ts:755 intercept calls session.unprotect(payload) synchronously on the whole reassembled record. A multi-MB message is one long main-thread task.
Remaining

(c) is untouched. The receive path (WS message -> HostedHubSession.#receive -> HostedRelayEngine.#receive/decodeRelayFrame -> RelayMessageAssembler -> relayE2eeChannel.intercept/session.unprotect, which is noble ChaCha20-Poly1305 over the whole record -> onData) and the send path (TextEncoder -> facade copy -> channel.submit copy -> noble seal -> prepareRelayMessage -> encodeRelayFrame -> encodeHubSessionFrame -> ws.send) all run on the web main thread. Leftover copies: (1) apps/web/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.ts:244 redundantly copies the fresh TextEncoder buffer for every RPC write and leaves that plaintext copy unzeroed; (2) packages/shared/src/relayMessageChunks.ts:307/:319 makes a retained copy plus a concat per chunked message; (3) outbound encodeRelayFrame cborg copy and hubSessionCodec.ts:70 header copy. The value of (c) is lower than the report assumed: the web phone tier is frozen behind the get-the-app interstitial (AGENTS.md), so the 50-70 ms phone estimate mostly no longer applies to web. On desktop the cost is about 9 ms per 3 MB message, a single long task during screenshot-sized RPCs.

Defects in the shipped fix

No defects found in the implemented parts. Zeroization holds: the engine zeroes the borrowed buffer after decode (relayEngine.ts:772), the session zeroes dropped data payloads (hostedHubSession.ts:333, :338), and the queue zeroes sent chunks after the synchronous browser ws.send copy. The 5-byte hub-session header in front of the borrowed view is not zeroed, but it only holds the kind and stream id. A data frame for a stream with zero message listeners would skip zeroing, and with several listeners the second would see zeros (hostedHubSession.ts:342). Neither is reachable, because exactly one engine listener is registered per logical stream. Sibling, not part of this web finding: apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.ts:309 still copies inbound with data.slice(0). Its send copy at :383 is deliberate, since React Native may send asynchronously.

Implementation sketch

Small leftovers (S, low risk, no decision needed): (1) In BrowserHostedRelaySocket.send (apps/web/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.ts:232-247), when typeof data === 'string', call this.#engine.send(encoded) on the TextEncoder buffer with no copy, then encoded.fill(0) in a finally. This is safe because every engine sink has already copied synchronously by then (relayE2eeChannel.ts:789, relayEngine.ts:660, :593, and splitRelayMessage), and it improves zeroization. Keep the copy for caller-owned ArrayBuffer/view inputs. Alternatively, drop it entirely and remove the caller-buffer fill at relayEngine.ts:582 so the engine never mutates caller memory. Tests in apps/web/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.test.ts: the engine receives the encoded buffer, it is zeroed after send, a caller Uint8Array is never mutated (including the legacy oversize refusal), and DOMException mapping is unchanged. (2) In RelayMessageAssembler.push (packages/shared/src/relayMessageChunks.ts:305-309), retain the body subarray instead of Uint8Array.from(body) plus fill. The concat loop at :321-325 and reset at :334 already zero the parts. Document that push takes ownership; both callers (relayEngine.ts:1204, apps/server/src/ws/RpcByteSession.ts:249) already hand over. Extend relayMessageChunks.test.ts so the inputs are zeroed after completion and reset. (3) Optional: let encodeHubSessionFrame accept a pre-reserved 5-byte header slot, or have the engine encode the relay frame into a buffer with header headroom, to drop the hub-session copy. Part (c) (L): add a module worker apps/web/src/hostedHub/relayDataPlane.worker.ts (worker.format 'es'). It owns the physical hub-session WebSocket, HostedHubSession, one HostedRelayEngine per logical channel, and the E2EE provider, and posts only decrypted RPC messages as transferable ArrayBuffers, plus status, invalidation and failure events. The main thread keeps hostedHubController and hostedHubStore and a thin proxy that implements the current HostedHubSession surface (resume, probe, createSocket) and the BrowserHostedRelaySocket EventTarget facade. Lifecycle decisions (expireSession, failure, generation checks) stay on the main thread. The worker caches nothing and is terminated on sign-out or disposal. The ticket and DPoP CryptoKeys cross by structured clone. The E2EE verification display, the §12.1 latch and E2eeNxHandshake UI state must be bridged over messages. A cheaper interim, if (c) is too large: an async AEAD seam used only for records of at least about 64 KiB, running noble chacha20poly1305 in a small crypto worker. intercept and protectRecord are already async and serialized, but session.unprotect/protect would have to become async, and session keys would cross threads. Validate with the full web browser suite (apps/web test:browser, including E2eeNxHandshake.browser.tsx and the maliciousRelay tests rerun against the worker), the hosted reconnect and stale-generation tests, and a long-task PerformanceObserver harness that streams a 3 MB RPC.

Needs a decision

Part (c) moves the account Hub-session socket (which owns its own reconnect, backoff and probe) and the E2EE channel with its session keys into a Worker. That touches the AGENTS.md rule that hosted lifecycle recovery has a single owner, moves key material across threads, and changes where the E2EE verification and latch state lives, so it needs owner and security sign-off. The interim crypto-worker option also moves session keys across threads and makes the record-layer API async. The small copy leftovers (relaySocket.ts:244 string branch, assembler copy) need no decision.

Partial#230 Native bearer mode re-hashes the same token per request and re-upserts the enrollment on every launch

hub-connection:dpop-native-connect-overhead · original impact Low, effort M · Crypto decision

Current state

PARTIAL holds. (a) The ath memoization is implemented and tested in createDpopProofSigner (60633eff3, #710). The mobile signer is memoized per key, so the single-slot cache persists across requests. (b) Nothing persists a Hub-confirmed enrollment or treats it as provisionally ready. start() is unchanged since f1be4abc7 apart from the new settled-wait helper, so every native launch still runs the blocking DPoP-signed upsert before any relay ticket. Since #710 the upsert is more exposed than the report says. The directory read now rides beside session restore, while the upsert only starts after restore publishes 'authenticated', so on a cold launch it runs serially (restore, then ensureIdentity and prekey, then the signed upsert RTT, then the ticket). The gate also blocks verified-pin/pairing ('local') relay contexts that never use the enrollment. No Hub change is needed: ticket issuance validates the enrollment itself and does not require an upsert in the current session. The auditor's sketch is directionally right but has gaps (see correction).

Evidence

The per-proof hardware signature (line 149) is inherent to DPoP. Tests are at packages/client-runtime/src/relay/dpop.test.ts:79-125: hash once per token, rehash on rotation, failed digest not remembered.
  • apps/mobile/src/platform/dpopSigner.ts:41-62 The signer is memoized per key (signerPromise), so the cache lives across requests. The expo-crypto digest now runs once per token.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:357-364 On every authenticated launch the coordinator is 'idle', so ensure(accountId) starts the full upsert. Nothing marks a cached enrollment ready first.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts:356-452 start() is unchanged since f1be4abc7. git diff shows only the new awaitNativeE2eeEnrollmentSettled helper at 135-171. It awaits upsertE2eeDeviceEnrollment (429) and publishes 'ready' only at 451. previousRevision (392-396) comes from in-memory state.ready, which is null on a fresh launch.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:749-773 Since 60633eff3 (#710), restoreSession and #prefetchDirectory are issued together. accountStatus 'authenticated' is published only when restore resolves, and only that triggers ensure(). On a cold launch the upsert therefore runs after the directory read rather than beside it, so its signature plus RTT sits fully on the path to the first ticket. The comment at apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/accountE2eeAttempt.ts:105-109 ('upsert runs beside the directory read') is stale.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/accountE2eeAttempt.ts:113-136 prepareMobileRelaySocketContext awaits the settled state (up to MOBILE_ENROLLMENT_GATE_WAIT_MS = 10 s) and throws unless the status is 'ready'. This applies before the trust-record branch, so 'local' verified-pin/pairing contexts (144-150) also wait for the upsert, although issueMobileRelayAttempt's local branch (246-249) never uses the enrollment.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/accountE2eeAttempt.ts:251-254 The account-grant issue path also requires status 'ready' with a matching generation.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts:343-357 The early relay socket (94ec18751) opens beside prepare, but the ticket/grant request waits for prepareSocketContext, and therefore for the enrollment upsert.
  • apps/mobile/src/platform/nativeE2ee.ts:231-249 Only the enrollment id (and, elsewhere, the prekey certificate) is persisted. There is no Hub-confirmed summary. clearEnrollment is a deliberate no-op. The secure-store key set is in apps/mobile/src/platform/e2eeSecureStore.ts:80-106.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/nativeE2eeTrustResolver.ts:231-241 The ticket request carries ready.enrollment.enrollmentRevision and clientPrekeyCertificateDigest. Grant verification (350-357) binds accountAuthEpoch, enrollmentRevision, deviceAuthEpoch and status from ready.enrollment. packages/shared/src/relayE2eeHubDeviceGrant.ts:388-391 checks them. A mismatch returns invalid() (around line 404), which is a non-retryable 'channel_rejected'.
  • ryco-hub:src/e2ee/accountE2eeService.ts:854-877 origin/main 5f656ad. activeEnrollment, used by the account-grant ticket route (src/http/accountE2eeRoutes.ts:117-160), requires an active record with the exact revision and certificate digest and an unexpired certificate. It answers 'enrollment_revoked' for a revoked record. No per-session upsert is required, so a provisional-ready client needs no Hub change.
  • ryco-hub:src/e2ee/accountE2eeService.ts:590-603 A same-identity renew keeps enrollmentRevision and deviceAuthEpoch, and stamps ensureAccountEpoch(). advanceAccountEpoch has no non-test callers. So in the normal case a cached summary's grant bindings stay valid. Identity replacement and post-revocation re-creation bump the revision.
Remaining

The per-launch enrollment upsert (nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts:429, ready published only at :451) is still a hard prerequisite of every mobile relay attempt (accountE2eeAttempt.ts:117-130 and 251-254), local verified-pin contexts included. Since #710 it runs serially after session restore on a cold launch (state.ts:749-773): one hardware DPoP signature, one Hub RTT and secure-store reads before the first ticket or grant. Nothing persists a Hub-confirmed summary (nativeE2ee.ts:231-249). The auditor's fix proposal is incomplete in four ways. (1) It must persist the full AccountE2eeDeviceSummary, not a subset, because grant verification binds accountAuthEpoch, deviceAuthEpoch, enrollmentRevision and status. (2) 'Clear on sign-out' is not enough. A device removed elsewhere loses its sessions, the cold-launch restore then gets 401 and never reaches the coordinator with a namespace, so clearEnrollment is never called and a stale summary would survive into the next sign-in. The summary must be bound to the Hub session id that confirmed it. (3) A provisional ticket answered 'enrollment_revoked' calls invalidate('revoked') (accountE2eeAttempt.ts:273-275). That bumps the generation, which discards the background upsert's result (which, for a session signed in after the revocation, would create revision+1), and leaves the coordinator 'revoked' until the next foreground. (4) A grant-binding mismatch during the provisional window returns a non-retryable invalid(). Minor, unverified side note: nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts:383 still starts refreshDirectory after ensureIdentity. Since #710 the restore already reads the directory, so this may add a second DPoP-signed directory read on launch that queues on the keystore ahead of the upsert's proof. Confirm with a trace before acting. The ath part needs no further work.

Defects in the shipped fix

None in the ath memoization. It is single-slot, keyed by token, drops a rejected digest (the .catch handler does not swallow the caller's rejection), and has tests for all three behaviours. The memoized mobile and desktop signers both benefit.

Implementation sketch

1) Platform persistence. Extend NativeE2eePlatformService (packages/client-runtime/src/platform/index.ts:238) with optional readConfirmedEnrollment(namespace), writeConfirmedEnrollment(record) and clearConfirmedEnrollment(). The record is {hubOrigin, accountId, hubSessionId, enrollment: AccountE2eeDeviceSummary}. Mobile: add E2EE_ACCOUNT_ENROLLMENT_CONFIRMED_KEY to apps/mobile/src/platform/e2eeSecureStore.ts (key union and the exhaustive E2EE_SECURE_STORE_KEY_SET, so reinstall purges it). Implement read/write in apps/mobile/src/platform/nativeE2ee.ts under exclusive(), decode with the contracts schema, and treat any decode failure as null. Desktop (apps/desktop/src/desktopNativeE2ee.ts) returns null or no-ops. 2) Coordinator (packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts). Add input currentSessionId(): string | null; mobile wires hostedHubStore.getState().session?.id in apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:264. In start(), after validateMaterial (391) and building the request, and only for non-retry, non-recovery starts: read the record. Require all of: same namespace, hubSessionId === currentSessionId(), enrollment.enrollmentId === enrollmentId, exactEnrollmentResponse(record.enrollment, request) true, and prekey.expiresAt outside the prekey renewal window. If they hold, publish {status: 'ready', ready: {namespace, enrollment: record.enrollment, identity, prekey}} immediately with an internal provisional flag, and send the upsert with expectedEnrollmentRevision = cached revision in the background under the same issued generation. On success, write the record. If accountAuthEpoch, deviceAuthEpoch or enrollmentRevision changed, bump the generation and republish ready so in-flight attempts fail their generation checks and retry; otherwise keep the generation. On 409 enrollment_revoked or a non-active same-id summary: clear the record and markHubRevoked(). On 409 enrollment_revision: clear the record and re-run a blocking upsert without expectedEnrollmentRevision. On a transient error, keep provisional ready (the Hub re-validates at ticket issuance) and retry in the background. Also write the record after every exact upsert (448-451), and clear it in invalidate() for every reason and in markHubRevoked. 3) Revocation and binding races. In issueMobileRelayAttempt (apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/accountE2eeAttempt.ts:273-275), when the current ready is provisional, clear the record and trigger an immediate blocking re-ensure instead of the foreground-only revoked recovery. In nativeE2eeTrustResolver.ts, when verifyHubDeviceGrant fails on an enrollment binding while the enrollment is provisional, await the background upsert and re-resolve once instead of returning invalid(). 4) Optional narrower step (needs a decision). In prepareMobileRelaySocketContext, resolve trustedRecord(selection) first and skip the enrollment wait for 'local' verified-pin/pairing contexts. 5) Tests. In nativeE2eeEnrollment.test.ts: a matching record publishes ready before the upsert resolves; a different session id, different material or near-expiry certificate falls back to the blocking path; background revoked leads to 'revoked' with the record cleared; a revision or epoch change bumps the generation; invalidate clears the record; a transient background failure keeps ready. In accountE2eeAttempt.test.ts: prepare does not wait for the upsert when provisional, and a provisional 'enrollment_revoked' recovers without a foreground transition. In nativeE2ee.test.ts: round trip, corrupt record returns null, reinstall purge.

Needs a decision

This changes when a native E2EE enrollment counts as 'ready'. A Hub-confirmed record from an earlier launch would authorize account-grant ticket requests before this launch's upsert, which changes the semantics of expectedEnrollmentRevision, revocation and epoch handling in the E2EE/auth path. That needs a security review even though the Hub still validates at ticket and grant issuance. Skipping the enrollment gate for 'local' verified-pin contexts is a separate policy decision.

Not done#231 Connects to nodes that send no E2EE carrier pay a fixed 1.5 s T_ADV wait before any RPC flows, on every connect and reconnect

hub-connection:t-adv-legacy-fixed-wait · original impact Low, effort M · Waterfall decision

Current state

Confirmed NOT_DONE. Since f1be4abc7, nothing in Ryco or the Hub shortcuts the T_ADV wait. T_ADV is still the fixed 1_500. The initiator still arms advTimer at channel.accept, and for a legacy-eligible, legacy-permitted selection with no carrier, timer expiry is still the only path to lockLegacy (row K13). The engine still withholds onTransportStatus('online') and onOpen until #applyModeLock. The node still suppresses the carrier silently. The Hub forwards channel.accept as the node's original bytes and adds no marker. `git log -S` for T_ADV, advTimer and noCarrier only hits the report HTML embedded in #710. Two parts of the finding have changed. (1) The 'x2 per relay drop' multiplier is gone: a38ecac4b adopts the reconnected relay channel instead of rebuilding the client, so a relay drop now pays T_ADV once (1.5 s), not 3 s. (2) The 'undersized-connection' branch cannot happen against the production Hub, which asserts maxDataChunkBytes = 256 KiB, well above the 8,192-byte floor. The affected population is un-upgraded nodes plus nodes whose statement build fails. The cost also applies to apps/mobile legacy-eligible/permitted selections, not only web.

Evidence
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeConstants.ts:251 T_ADV = 1_500, unchanged; still documented as fixed by the L1 keepalive budget.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayE2eeInitiator.ts:566-586 advTimer is armed at machine creation (channel.accept). On expiry with no hello: latched or !legacyPermitted gives P19, unexpected gives P22, otherwise lockLegacy() (K13). There is no hint input or early-lock path. This file has no commits since f1be4abc7.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayEngine.ts:837-850,971-987 channel.accept with an e2ee provider enters 'negotiating' and opens the machine. #applyModeLock flushes the negotiation buffer and only then emits onTransportStatus('online'), 'synchronizing' and onOpen. The engine changes since the report are buffer-ownership and copy-elimination only.
  • apps/server/src/hubConnector/NodeE2eeChannelAdvertiser.ts:203-230,255-268 planFor returns 'suppress' for undersized-connection or statement-unavailable when requireE2EE is false. The suppress announce sends nothing on the wire and only records a node-local §12.5 occurrence.
  • packages/contracts/src/relay.ts:12 RELAY_MAX_DATA_CHUNK_BYTES = 256 KiB, the value the Hub asserts in ready (ryco-hub origin/main src/relay/websocketRuntime.ts:785,925). That is above E2EE_ADVERTISEMENT_MIN_CHUNK_BYTES (8,192), so the 'undersized-connection' suppression is unreachable in production.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/e2eeAttempt.ts:216-217 Web: selectionClass is 'latched' or 'legacy-eligible', with legacyPermitted: true. The only changes since the report are lazy-loading and warm-up of the handshake code.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/e2eeAttempt.ts:590-591 Mobile also runs legacyPermitted from strictLegacyPolicy, which defaults to permitted, so mobile legacy-eligible first-contact selections pay the same K13 wait. The auditor covered web only.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayE2eeInitiator.test.ts:1443-1451 The K13 test still pins mode 'negotiating' at T_ADV-1 and 'legacy' at T_ADV.
  • docs/relay-e2ee-protocol.md:365,1017 The spec still fixes T_ADV at 1,500 ms, and K13 is unamended. The 47 lines added to the spec since the report are §14.7 native fast paths and a §13.6 pending-record note, both unrelated.
  • ryco-hub:origin/main src/relay/forwarder.ts:221-227 channel.accept is forwarded with enqueueOriginal (node bytes verbatim) and gets no Hub-added marker. git grep finds no noCarrier or capability hint. ticketService.ts returns only {ticket, expiresAt, protocolMajor, protocolMinor} for non-account-grant tickets.
  • ryco-hub:origin/main src/relay/websocketRuntime.ts:1126-1141 The Hub does receive node.e2ee.statement frames and acks them (Ryco HubConnector.ts:1159 notes the Hub drops a statement that is not renewed). The Hub therefore holds the 'node has a current statement' fact the proposal relies on, but no API exposes it.
  • commit a38ecac4b Adopts the reconnected relay channel instead of rebuilding the client, removing finding #1's double establishment. A relay drop now pays T_ADV once rather than twice.
Remaining

Every hosted connect and reconnect to a node that sends no E2EE carrier still waits a fixed 1.5 s before any RPC flows. Affected nodes are un-upgraded nodes and nodes whose statement build fails ('statement-unavailable'); 'undersized-connection' cannot happen against the 256 KiB production Hub. The client side is relayE2eeInitiator.ts:566-586 (K13 timer is the only legacy path), with sends held until relayEngine.ts:971-987. Applies to web (e2eeAttempt.ts:216-217) and to mobile legacy-eligible/permitted selections. The node suppresses silently (NodeE2eeChannelAdvertiser.ts:230,255-268). The Hub exposes no 'node has no current statement' signal: forwarder.ts:221 forwards accept verbatim, and the ticket response has no hint. Correction to the finding's cost: since a38ecac4b a relay drop costs 1.5 s, not 3 s.

Implementation sketch

Preferred: a Hub-originated hint on the ticket response, plus a K13 amendment. 1. Hub (ryco-hub) - In src/e2ee/accountE2eeService.ts (acceptNodeStatement ~:791), track per node connection whether a current acked node.e2ee.statement exists. Clear the fact on statement expiry (non-renewal) and on node disconnect. - In src/relay/ticketService.ts issueInternal, add `nodeE2eeAdvertisement: "absent"` to the plain ticket response only when the node's current connection has NEVER published a statement. That is the un-upgraded case and the persistent statement-build-failure case. Do not send it merely because a statement lapsed, so a stale hint cannot silently strip E2EE from an E2EE-capable node behind an honest Hub. - Put the hint on the ticket response, not on channel.accept. The forwarder relays the node's accept bytes verbatim (enqueueOriginal), and adding a field there means re-encoding a node frame. 2. Ryco contracts - Add the optional field to the ticket response schema in packages/contracts/src/relay.ts. - Thread it through packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts into RelayE2eeInitiatorAttempt as e.g. `nodeAdvertisementHint?: "absent"`, set by the web/mobile attempt builders (apps/web/src/hostedHub/e2eeAttempt.ts:webRelayE2eeAttempt, apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/e2eeAttempt.ts). 3. Initiator (packages/client-runtime/src/relay/relayE2eeInitiator.ts ~:566) - Arm advTimer exactly as today. - Lock legacy at creation only when the hint is 'absent' AND selectionClass === 'legacy-eligible' AND legacyPermitted AND !pairingOnly. Use lockLegacy(), which already goes through host.lockMode; the engine's #pendingLock handles a lock issued inside the factory (relayEngine.ts:955-959). - Latched, unexpected, require-E2EE and pairing-only selections keep the timer and fail closed. - A carrier arriving after the early lock is K20 (ignore, never upgrade). Record a diagnostic so a wrong hint is visible. 4. Spec - Amend docs/relay-e2ee-protocol.md §4.4: add a K13a row ('Hub hint absent' at accept, same guard as K13) and a §12.1.1 sentence stating the hint can only shorten the K13 wait for a selection already legacy-eligible and can never move a selection into that class. - Get crypto/owner review. 5. Tests - relayE2eeInitiator.test.ts: hint plus legacy-eligible gives mode 'legacy' and onOpen before T_ADV. Hint plus latched gives P19 at T_ADV. Hint plus pairingOnly gives fatal 'local'. Hint, then a carrier, gives K20 no-op. - A transport test that the ticket field reaches the attempt. - Hub ticketService tests for the field. Cheaper client-only alternative (also a K13 amendment): keep an in-memory per (hubOrigin, accountId, nodeId) 'observed no carrier' bit in apps/web/src/hostedHub/e2eeAttempt.ts. Set it when a channel reaches K13 having seen no carrier at all. Clear it on any carrier (K1-K3, K20) and on page reload. On later channels, lock legacy at accept under the same guards. This removes the wait from reconnects but not from the first connect. Node-only partial alternative, for upgraded-but-degraded nodes only: on 'suppress', emit a harmless legacy JSON record at seq 0 so the client takes K9 immediately. This needs node-row (N16/N17) spec changes, needs proof the RPC parser tolerates the record, and does nothing for un-upgraded nodes. Not recommended. Independently, attribute the delay: when a channel locks via K13 with no carrier observed, publish a client-side diagnostic ('node did not advertise E2EE; connect waited 1.5 s') next to the existing 'legacy' label (apps/web/src/hostedHub/e2eeSession.ts:104).

Needs a decision

Every fix changes §4.4 row K13 of the relay E2EE protocol, the only row besides K9 that releases plaintext. It lets a Hub-supplied hint, or a client-side negative latch, end the negotiation window early. That needs a spec amendment and a crypto/security review: showing that the hint grants no new downgrade power and that a stale hint cannot silently strip E2EE from a capable node behind an honest Hub. The preferred variant is also a Hub protocol change (a new ticket-response field) that needs a Hub deploy and a pin bump. The affected population (un-upgraded nodes, failed statement builds) shrinks as nodes update, so the trade-off between 1.5 s of latency and protocol complexity is a product decision.

All four parts of the proposal are implemented. deriveAppAccess unlocks via direct-node once the direct plane hydrates with a readable credential, without waiting on the hosted plane. ensureMobileHostedSession returns before hostedHubController.bootstrap() when no Hub token is stored. That launch skips the missing-token failure, clearSessionMaterial, the DPoP-minted getBootstrapAvailability request and the Secure Enclave key load. The key load is deferred to first hosted use, and the cost only applies after the gate has opened, on pushed hosted screens (Machines, Settings > Hub, Hub account, E2EE), never on Home. A stored-session launch is also capped at the 8 s hosted launch deadline instead of the 30 s request deadline. The auditor's one flagged defect is not real: the first-run sign-in copy has no production consumer.

The direct plane (lines 84-113) depends only on the catalog KV hydration plus per-environment keychain reads (packages/client-runtime/src/connection/catalog.ts:188-218), not on the hosted plane.

With no stored session, line 455 returns configureMobileHostedRuntime('deferred') before bootstrap(). So the launch makes no network request, does no clearSessionMaterial keychain delete and runs no Secure Enclave op.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:154-192 deferredDpopSigner and ensureMobileHostedDeviceKey load the hardware key on first proof or first hosted-surface mount, with no software fallback.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.test.ts:520-554 Tests pin that bootstrap is not called, the call order is hydrate/trust-hydrate/configure, the account stays signed-out, and createMobileDpopSigner is not called when no session is stored.

Current state

Confirmed DONE. All six proposal parts are in HEAD via 60633eff3 (#710). Scroll offsets live outside React (homeScrollMemory). Some smaller residuals are outside the proposal: `environments` gets a new identity on every Home render, the projects tab has no row stabilization, Home stays mounted and keeps rebuilding under the Thread route, and ThreadDetailScreen over-subscribes through useHomeWorkspaceData. All are low-value follow-ups, not defects in the fix.

Evidence

HomeScreen.tsx:154-161 records through useCallback, and InboxScreen.tsx:253-257 forwards onScroll without setting state.
  • apps/mobile/src/state/homeData.ts:36 useHomeWorkspaceData memoizes each filterEligible result on (slice, eligible set). The slices come from createAcrossEnvironmentsSelector / createSliceRowsSelector (packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:3311-3343), which return the previous array while the id list and record are unchanged, so useShallow sees the same identity.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/home/HomeScreen.tsx:65 The eligible Set is memoized on the joined id string. inboxSections (:89) and projectRows (:122) are built only for the active mode and return frozen empty constants otherwise.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/inbox/inboxModel.ts:357 stabilizeInboxSections reuses row, section and list objects when they are structurally equal at depth 4. That comparison is conservative: deeper differences compare by identity, so rows are never falsely equal. It has a test in inboxSectionStabilizer.test.ts. The impure closure mutation during render is harmless: at worst one extra InboxScreen render after a discarded render.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/inbox/InboxScreen.tsx:159 InboxScreen, InboxThreadMenuRow (:128) and InboxThreadRow (InboxThreadRow.tsx:55) are memo()-wrapped. renderItem is a useCallback (:196). Snooze presets are resolved once per nowMs and kept by value (:187-194).

  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/threadInbox.ts:406 worktreesByProjectKey uses get/push/set, so the quadratic spread is gone.
  • apps/mobile/babel.config.js:6 The auditor did not mention this. React Compiler is on for features/(home|inbox|projects), so HomeScreen, useHomeEnvironments and ProjectsScreen/ProjectRow get auto-memoized JSX on top of the manual memoization.

That is directRows in the final useMemo of useHomeEnvironments (:73-138), so `environments` changes identity on every HomeScreen render. inboxSections (in inbox mode) and projectRows (in projects mode) then rerun buildInboxSections/buildProjectRows even when only a provider-status/serverConfig emit, a preference change or a theme change caused the render. Today they stay fresh only because directRows churns on every render. Memoizing `rows` in useSavedEnvironments would let them go stale until some other dependency changes.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/projects/ProjectsScreen.tsx:117 Projects-mode residual. ProjectsScreen and ProjectRow are not memo()'d and buildProjectRows has no row stabilizer, so every rebuild hands the list all-new row objects. Rebuilds happen on every Home render in projects mode: environments churn, any thread summary change, and the 30s tick, which is not a projectRows dependency but still changes `environments`. The compiler's per-field JSX caching softens the cost, but every visible ProjectRow body still runs.

Each streamed assistant flush (ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:177, every 32ms) bumps the thread's updatedAt (ProjectionPipeline.ts:1176-1180). The shell coalesces this to one thread-upserted per 250ms per thread. The summary is not equal (store.ts:643), so Home still rebuilds the whole inbox model about 4 times per second per streaming thread. Only the changed row re-renders. This is legitimate data change, but the full O(T log T) rebuild remains.
Defects in the shipped fix

No bug or regression in the implemented fix. Residuals are outside the proposal's scope. (1) useSavedEnvironments builds a fresh `rows` array on every call (useConnectionController.ts:60), so `environments` from useHomeEnvironments changes identity on every Home render. inboxSections/projectRows then rebuild even for renders that changed none of their inputs, such as provider-status/serverConfig emits or preference and theme changes. The inbox list itself does not re-render. (2) Projects tab: buildProjectRows has no row stabilizer and ProjectsScreen/ProjectRow are not memo()'d, so every Home render in projects mode, including each thread-summary change, gives every visible project card a new row object. (3) Home stays mounted under Thread with no freezeOnBlur. Because streaming bumps thread updatedAt, coalesced to 250ms per thread on the server, Home rebuilds the full inbox model about 4 times per second per streaming thread even while hidden. (4) Uncovered callers: ThreadDetailScreen.tsx:520, ThreadFileScreen.tsx:612 and ThreadFilesScreen.tsx:213 call useHomeWorkspaceData() for worktrees only, but subscribe to all projects and thread summaries, so they re-render on unrelated threads' summary changes. Two corrections to the auditor's notes. The 30s clock tick is not wasted work in inbox mode, because nowMs is a real inbox dependency; it is wasted only in projects mode. Their suggested fix of memoizing `rows` in useSavedEnvironments would make the imperative readEnvironmentApi/readEnvironmentDescriptor reads in useHomeEnvironments (:88, :101-109) go stale.

Partial#235 Hosted users see a logo until restoreSession AND listNodes finish; offline launches show sign-in instead of the cached workspace

mobile-boot:hosted-gate-waits-for-directory-and-locks-offline · original impact Medium, effort S · Waterfall decision

Current state

PARTIAL is correct. Proposals (a), (b) and (d) are implemented. (a): the gate unlocks on the published `authenticated`, and the directory read is prefetched beside restoreSession instead of after it. (b): an 8 s launch decision deadline in the gate plus an 8 s bearer access-decision deadline in the controller. (d): the native splash is held up to 800 ms for the gate decision. I found no implementation of (c), the read-only cached workspace on a transient Hub failure, in any module, renamed file or Hub change. Offline launches with a stored token still land on the locked identity screen. One small waterfall the auditor missed also remains: on a 401 restore, the gate still waits for a DPoP-signed bootstrap-availability probe whose answer no mobile screen reads.

Evidence
  • apps/mobile/src/features/access/appAccessModel.ts:33-41 deriveAppAccess unlocks on hostedSessionRevalidated alone (proposal a). `locked` still needs both planes hydrated and no grant, so an `unavailable` account with no direct credential is locked (line 40). At f1be4abc7 it returned hydrating until hostedHydrated.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/access/AppAccessGate.tsx:64-82,115-120,157-160 The 8 s HOSTED_LAUNCH_DECISION_DEADLINE_MS timer sets hostedHydrated (proposal b), and hostedAuthenticated feeds hostedSessionRevalidated. The locked branch renders LockedNavigation, whose Access screen is NativeIdentityScreen.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:749-773 #restoreAccess prefetches listNodes beside restoreSession (:753, prefetchHostedDirectory :470-486). It publishes `authenticated` and runs accessSettled before #refreshDirectoryWith (:773). The serial directory RTT is off the critical path.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:518,829-843 HOSTED_ACCESS_CHECK_DEADLINE_MS = 8_000. In bearer mode `unavailable` is published at the deadline with the retry armed, and the request keeps its full deadline so a late answer is still adopted.
  • apps/mobile/src/App.tsx:58-79 and apps/mobile/src/features/access/launchDecision.ts:12,20 SplashScreenCoordinator holds the splash until markAppAccessDecided, capped at SPLASH_ACCESS_DECISION_WAIT_MS = 800 (proposal d).
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:457 and packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:780-789 Residual the auditor missed. The mobile gate settles on hostedHubController.bootstrap(), not bootstrapAccess(). On a 401 (expired or revoked stored session), #restoreAccess clears the token, then awaits getBootstrapAvailability (api.ts:904, dpop: 'mint', so another Secure Enclave signature plus an RTT) before publishing signed-out. The gate stays on the launch surface for that extra request, capped at 8 s.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/hostedHub/hostedAuthModel.ts:432 The only mobile reader of bootstrapAvailable is deriveHostedSignInView, and no non-test mobile screen imports it. runtime.ts:452 itself says no mobile surface reads the probe's answer.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/identity/savedHubSessionModel.ts:63-111 and apps/mobile/src/features/identity/NativeIdentityScreen.tsx:347-371 The offline or early-deadline locked surface is the saved-session view ('Reaching your Hub…', or 'still checking' while the launch check is pending, added in #710). It is not hostedAuthModel's 'Hub unavailable' string, which the auditor cited. No cached workspace and no read-only variant exist, so (c) is not implemented.
  • docs/mobile-native-status.md:21-24 Policy unchanged since f1be4abc7: the workspace navigator mounts only after a revalidated native Hub session or a readable direct credential.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/readCache.ts:614-621 and docs/hosted-hub-client.md:603-609 Precedent for (c). Hosted web already shows an opt-in ('Remember this browser') read-only cached preview while accountStatus is `unavailable` or the bootstrap check is pending, with mutations gated on full revalidation. Mobile has no equivalent.
  • apps/mobile/src/persistence/environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:310-314 Mobile cache policy keeps hosted content across session expiry (purged only on explicit sign-out), so cached content for (c) exists on disk.
Remaining

(1) Main item, proposal (c), needs sign-off. With a stored hosted bearer token and a transient access failure (offline, timeout, 5xx; accountStatus `unavailable`, or still `signed-out` while the check is pending), deriveAppAccess returns `locked` (apps/mobile/src/features/access/appAccessModel.ts:40). AppAccessGate.tsx:158-160 then shows NativeIdentityScreen's 'Reaching your Hub…' view instead of the cached workspace, although the snapshot cache and Hub roster are retained on disk (environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:310-314). (2) Minor, missed by the auditor. On an expired or revoked stored session, the gate waits for the DPoP-signed /api/auth/bootstrap-status probe (state.ts:783-788) after the 401 answer is known. This costs one extra RTT and one Secure Enclave signature before the sign-in surface, for an answer no mobile screen reads (only hostedAuthModel.ts:432, which is unused by screens). It is bounded by the 8 s gate deadline.

Defects in the shipped fix

No real defects in (a), (b) or (d). One correction to the auditor's timing quirk: the gate's 8 s timer starts at mount, before the controller's bearer decision deadline, so the gate can decide `locked` while accountStatus is still the initial `signed-out`. This does not flash a sign-in form or 'Hub unavailable'. NativeIdentityScreen passes checking=true until ensureMobileHostedSession settles, and deriveSavedHubSessionView then shows 'Reaching your Hub… still checking your saved sign-in' (savedHubSessionModel.ts:68-83). A late `authenticated` still unlocks. This is intended behaviour.

Implementation sketch

(c), after sign-off. Mirror hosted web's canShowHostedReadPreview (apps/web/src/hostedHub/readCache.ts:614) in the mobile gate. (1) appAccessModel.ts: add a fact, e.g. `hostedCachedPreviewAvailable`, plus a new verdict { status: "unlocked", via: "hosted-cached-preview" } or a separate `preview` status. Return it only when no plane grants access, hostedHydrated is true, and the preview fact holds; `locked` keeps priority over it once the Hub gives a definite session answer. (2) AppAccessGate.tsx: compute the fact from (a) a stored bearer token (mobileSessionCredentials.readBearerToken, presentation-only today), (b) a non-empty cached Hub roster (getCachedHubNodeRoster / subscribeCachedHubNodeRoster) and (c) accountStatus === 'unavailable' or (initial 'signed-out' while the launch check is pending). Clearing the token on a 401 must drop the preview and re-lock. (3) In the preview, mount WorkspaceNavigation with a 'Reconnecting to Hub' banner driven by accessRecoveryPending. Audit composer, outbox drain, terminals, files and git entry points so none can mutate. They already require a ready directory or a live connection plus a fresh shell snapshot, but check that queued outbox sends stay in the queue, and that ServerStateBootstrap and the hosted connection coordinator do not request relay tickets while unauthenticated. (4) Tests: appAccessModel.test.ts cases for preview-on-unavailable, re-lock on a definite 401 or sign-out, upgrade to via 'hosted-session' on recovery, and no preview without a roster or token. (5) Update docs/mobile-native-status.md:21-24 and the cache section of docs/unified-workspace.md. (2) Minor probe waterfall: let native runtimes skip the bootstrap-availability probe, e.g. a controller or runtime-configuration flag set by configureMobileHostedRuntime that makes the session-failure branch at state.ts:780-789 publish { ...initialState } at once. Alternatively, call accessSettled before the probe and have the gate await a new ensureMobileHostedAccessDecided() that resolves on hostedHubController.bootstrapAccess() rather than bootstrap(). Keep web behaviour unchanged, because web reads bootstrapAvailable for first-run. Test in packages/client-runtime/src/authorization (state tests): with the flag set, a 401 restore publishes signed-out without calling getBootstrapAvailability.

Needs a decision

(c) reverses a documented auth-gate rule (docs/mobile-native-status.md:21-24: the workspace mounts only after a revalidated native Hub session). It also shows account-scoped cached content on the strength of a stored token whose session the Hub has not confirmed. That is a product and security trade-off that touches the hosted lifecycle and mutation-readiness ownership in AGENTS.md, so it needs explicit sign-off. Hosted web's opt-in remembered-browser preview is a precedent, but mobile would turn it on by default. The minor probe skip changes no auth semantics and needs no decision.
