Partial#237 Every projection change triggers a full-environment JSON.stringify + double UTF-8 encode + SQLite write 500 ms later

mobile-boot:snapshot-capture-full-reserialize · original impact Medium, effort S · CPU WP14A

First-pass audit said PARTIAL; the verifier corrected it. The PARTIAL status stands, but the auditor's diagnosis of the remaining gap is wrong. They blame the defeated O(1) skip mainly on detail-stream events (sink.applyOrchestrationEvents). Their fix option (a), dropping projectionChanged there, assumes the shell stream does not cause the same churn. It does. The server sets the projected thread row's updatedAt to event.occurredAt on every thread.message-sent, streaming assistant deltas included (ProjectionPipeline.ts:1160-1181). The shell stream maps every thread-aggregate event to a thread-upserted re-read (orchestrationStreams.ts:343-358, 369-372), coalesced to at most one per thread per 250 ms (orchestrationEventCoalescing.ts:62-74, constants.ts:35). On mobile, writeThreadShellState then replaces both threadShellById and sidebarThreadSummaryById, because both equality checks include updatedAt (store.ts:1138-1146, 1172+, 642, 723). So identity skipping cannot hit while any thread in the environment has agent activity, open in the app or not. Option (a) only removes marks that the debounce already merges. The fix has to target serialization cost (incremental per-thread fragments or per-thread rows), or make an explicit product choice to ignore updatedAt-only churn. Also, the skip test (environmentSnapshotPersistence.test.ts:601-622) only covers two back-to-back captures with no state change, not any real event path. That is why the code comment at :228-230 is wrong and no test catches it.

Current state

Proposal parts 2 and 3 are fully done: no TextEncoder double encode, an allocation-free charCode byte count passed through to SQLite, a 2 s debounce with 10 s max-wait, and a flush on background. Part 1, the identity skip, is implemented but almost never fires in the scenario the finding targets. During any agent activity the shell stream bumps updatedAt on the shell and summary of the active thread up to 4 times a second, so every debounce window still does a full rebuild, a JSON.stringify of up to 2 MiB, a 2 MiB charCode scan, a full-row SQLite upsert and a stats query. That is now at most once per 10 s instead of once per 500 ms quiet gap. Part 4, per-thread rows or incremental writes, is not done.

Evidence
  • apps/mobile/src/persistence/snapshotDb.ts:84-105,186 payloadByteLength is an allocation-free charCode loop with no TextEncoder. saveEnvironmentSnapshot uses the caller's payloadBytes and only measures when none is given. Part 2 is done, but without the payload.length*3 <= cap fast path.
  • apps/mobile/src/persistence/environmentSnapshotCodec.ts:131-141 One stringify and one byte count per bound round, returning {record,payload,payloadBytes}. The whole environment is still stringified on every real capture.
  • apps/mobile/src/persistence/environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:46-47,265-284 2 s trailing debounce with 10 s max-wait (dirtySince) and flushPending on background. Wired at apps/mobile/src/runtime/bootstrap.ts:130-134 and apps/mobile/src/platform/appLifecycle.ts:49-60. Part 3 is done (commit 60633eff3, #710).
  • apps/mobile/src/persistence/environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:121-153,228-251 Identity skip over the seven persisted slices plus a global removalEpoch guard. The comment at :228-230 claims message streaming, session and liveness changes are skipped, which is false (see below). After every real write: full captureEnvironmentSnapshotRecord, bound, save, then evictToCapacity, which calls listEnvironmentSnapshotStats (:188-202).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProjectionPipeline.ts:1160-1181 On every thread.message-sent, streaming deltas included (decider.ts:2880-2900, ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:1413/1759), the projected thread row is upserted with updatedAt: event.occurredAt.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context/orchestrationStreams.ts:343-372 Every thread-aggregate event becomes a thread-upserted re-read of the shell row. The shell feed coalesces message-sent, activity-appended and proposed-plan per thread over 250 ms (orchestrationEventCoalescing.ts:62-74, constants.ts:35). Each active thread therefore pushes a shell upsert with a fresh updatedAt up to 4 times a second.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:1113-1146,1172,3170-3171 The shell-stream thread-upserted goes through writeThreadShellState, which replaces threadShellById when threadShellsEqual fails (updatedAt is compared at :723) and replaces sidebarThreadSummaryById when sidebarThreadSummariesEqual fails (updatedAt at :642, session at :635, backgroundLiveness at :655). This alone defeats samePersistedSlices during any agent activity.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:1589-1611,1871,1958 The detail-stream path does the same: message-sent and activity-appended end in updateThreadShellTimestamp(..., event.occurredAt), which spreads a new threadShellById. This is a second source of the same churn, not the only one.

  • apps/mobile/src/persistence/environmentSnapshotPersistence.test.ts:601-622 The skip test only captures twice with no intervening store change. No test covers a shell-stream or detail event leaving the persisted content unchanged.

The epoch is read before the write, and evictToCapacity can bump it right after written.set, so the next capture of every environment rewrites once even when nothing changed. Inefficient but not incorrect.
Remaining

1) The identity skip (environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:231-239) is effectively dead during agent activity. The shell stream delivers a thread-upserted with a new updatedAt for each active thread every <=250 ms (ProjectionPipeline.ts:1179, orchestrationStreams.ts:343-358, orchestrationEventCoalescing.ts:62-74). writeThreadShellState then replaces threadShellById and sidebarThreadSummaryById (store.ts:1138-1146, 1172+). Detail events add more of the same churn (store.ts:1871, 1958). While any agent runs in the environment, each 10 s max-wait window, or each 2 s quiet gap, still runs captureEnvironmentSnapshotRecord over all threads, JSON.stringify of up to 2 MiB (environmentSnapshotCodec.ts:69-96, 131-141), a 2 MiB charCode scan (snapshotDb.ts:84-105), a full-row TEXT upsert (snapshotDb.ts:171-190) and listEnvironmentSnapshotStats plus eviction planning (environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:188-202, 251). Session or backgroundLiveness changes also force a full rewrite even though those fields are stripped from the payload (store.ts:635, 655 vs codec :86). The finding's expected gain, that most captures during streaming become no-ops, is not achieved. 2) Proposal part 4, per-thread or incremental writes, is not done. 3) Minor: no payload.length*3 <= cap fast path; the global removalEpoch makes one eviction, purge or hydration discard cost every other environment a redundant rewrite; the stats query runs after every write.

Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness defect. Two weaknesses in the implemented skip. (a) The comment at environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:228-230 says message streaming, session and liveness changes are skipped in O(1). Store equality includes updatedAt, session and backgroundLiveness (store.ts:635, 642, 655, 723) on both the shell-stream and detail paths, so none of those are skipped. The only test (environmentSnapshotPersistence.test.ts:601-622) never exercises an event path, so nothing catches this. (b) The global removalEpoch, read at :240 before the write and bumpable by evictToCapacity at :251 right after written.set at :250, and also bumped by every hydration discardRow, invalidates the skip for all environments after any single removal. It costs one redundant full rewrite per environment and is still correct.

Implementation sketch

Recommended, effort S, no product trade-off, payload stays byte-identical: incremental serialization in apps/mobile/src/persistence/environmentSnapshotCodec.ts. 1) Add createEnvironmentSnapshotSerializer(), which holds Map<ThreadId, {shell, summary, json: string, bytes: number}>. For each thread, reuse the cached fragment when shell === cached.shell && summary === cached.summary. Otherwise build JSON.stringify({shell, summary: {...summary, session: null, backgroundLiveness: null}}) and compute payloadByteLength(json). Prune entries for threads that are gone. 2) Assemble the payload as the stringified envelope prefix ('{"schemaVersion":1,"environmentId":...,"capturedAt":...,"projects":[...],"worktrees":[...],"threads":[') + fragments.join(',') + ']}', keeping JSON.stringify's key order. payloadBytes = prefix/suffix bytes + sum(fragment bytes) + commas. 3) Re-implement boundStoredEnvironmentSnapshot's trim loop on fragment byte sums with the same drop order (archived first, then oldest), so trimming never re-stringifies. 4) In environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts keep one serializer per environment next to `written`, and drop it in removeStoredSnapshot and purgeEnvironment. 5) Make removalEpoch a per-environment Map bumped in removeStoredSnapshot(environmentId), so evicting environment X no longer invalidates environment Y's skip. 6) Fix the comment at :228-230 to say what is actually skipped. Tests: a codec property test asserting that the assembled payload === JSON.stringify(boundRecord) and that payloadBytes === new TextEncoder().encode(payload).length, covering non-ASCII text, astral characters, lone surrogates and the trim path; a persistence test that applies a shell-stream thread-upserted changing one thread's updatedAt and asserts only that thread's fragment is re-stringified (inject a stringify counter or spy). Optional follow-ups: (i) mirror per-environment {bytes, updatedAt} in memory after the first stats read so evictToCapacity skips listEnvironmentSnapshotStats when the plan cannot change; (ii) part 4 proper, effort M: an environment_snapshot_threads(environment_id, thread_id, payload, payload_bytes) table plus a header row, schema version 2 with v1 rows discarded, a transactional upsert of only changed thread rows, hydration reading rows grouped by environment, and eviction summing bytes per environment. This also removes the 2 MiB string crossing JSI to expo-sqlite on each write. (iii) Not recommended without a decision: demote updatedAt-, latestTurn-, session-, liveness- and priority-only churn to a low-priority dirty flag with a ~60 s max-wait plus the background flush. The cached sidebar's recency ordering could then lag if the app is killed without being backgrounded.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Done#238 All 25+ screens (and the locked-stack identity/camera/webview screens) are statically imported and evaluated at launch

mobile-boot:eager-screen-registration · original impact Medium, effort M · Bundle size WP14B

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. DONE holds for the launch cost the finding describes. The auditor got two things wrong. (1) They said there were no functional defects, but the Thread prewarm does nothing. 1b8bfd183 (Oct 13, the day after #710) turned on Metro inlineRequires, so ThreadRouteScreen.preload() now evaluates only the 35-line wrapper module. ThreadDetailScreen and everything under it are still evaluated synchronously on the first thread tap, which the proposal wanted to avoid. (2) They said no test guards the launch graph. apps/mobile/src/perf/mobileStartupImports.test.ts:206-251 does: it checks the Stack.tsx and AppAccessGate imports and the lazyRouteScreens requires, and its index.ts graph walk asserts ThreadRouteScreen is not reachable. Minor: there are 23 lazy screens, not 22.

Current state

The launch-graph part is fixed. Stack.tsx and the locked stack in AppAccessGate now register all 23 non-Home screens through lazyScreen(), which defers a function-scoped require() to first render. My static walk from index.ts, resolved like Metro's iOS bundle, went from 633 repo files / 5,869 KiB at f1be4abc7 to 413 / 3,738 KiB. That drop also includes other #710 changes. None of the screen modules, shiki, @pierre/diffs, react-native-webview or expo-camera are still reachable, and mobileStartupImports.test.ts guards this. The defect is the proposed Thread prewarm. It was written when imports were evaluated eagerly. Since 1b8bfd183 turned on inlineRequires, preload() evaluates only ThreadRouteScreen.tsx: running Metro's importExportPlugin and inlineRequiresPlugin on it shows require("./ThreadDetailScreen") inlined into the render function. So the first thread open after launch still evaluates the thread detail graph on the tap. Its static upper bound beyond the launch graph is 136 repo files / ~1.6 MiB of source, plus react-native-webview, expo-video, expo-file-system, @noble and cborg. The shiki highlighter prewarm does work, because it calls a function.

Evidence
  • apps/mobile/src/Stack.tsx:20 HomeRouteScreen is the only route screen imported statically. Every other screen comes from ./navigation/lazyRouteScreens (lines 21-45).
  • apps/mobile/src/features/access/AppAccessGate.tsx:11 The locked stack (lines 23-33) uses the lazy NativeIdentityScreen and ConnectionsNewRouteScreen, so the WebView and camera graphs are no longer evaluated at launch.
  • apps/mobile/src/navigation/lazyScreen.ts:24 lazyScreen caches load() on first render or preload. preload() evaluates only the module the loader requires.
  • apps/mobile/src/navigation/lazyRouteScreens.ts:199 The prewarm calls ThreadRouteScreen.preload(). Under inline requires this evaluates only the wrapper module. The comment at 186-194 still says the Thread route is warmed so the tap stays fast.
  • apps/mobile/metro.config.js:99 inlineRequires: true, added in 1b8bfd183 after 60633eff3. Every module's imports are evaluated at their first use site, not at module evaluation.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/threads/ThreadRouteScreen.tsx:5 ThreadDetailScreen is imported here but only used inside the component (line 29). Running the Metro import-export and inline-requires plugins outputs `_jsx(require("./ThreadDetailScreen").ThreadDetailScreen, ...)` inside the render function, so preload() never evaluates it.
  • apps/mobile/src/perf/mobileStartupImports.test.ts:206 Guard tests the auditor missed: only Home is eager in Stack.tsx (206), AppAccessGate has no identity/connection imports (217), lazyRouteScreens has no static feature imports (222), and the graph walk asserts ThreadRouteScreen is not reachable from index.ts (248). The header comment at 12-13 ('no inline requires') is stale.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/home/HomeRouteScreen.tsx:9 The prewarm is scheduled from Home's mount effect through requestIdleCallback, which RN 0.86 provides in both bridgeless and legacy modes.
Defects in the shipped fix

The Thread route prewarm is a no-op. apps/mobile/src/navigation/lazyRouteScreens.ts:199 calls ThreadRouteScreen.preload(). Since 1b8bfd183 enabled inlineRequires (apps/mobile/metro.config.js:99), that evaluates only apps/mobile/src/features/threads/ThreadRouteScreen.tsx: its ThreadDetailScreen import (line 5) is inlined into the render function (line 29). The first thread open after launch therefore still evaluates the whole thread detail graph synchronously on the tap. The static upper bound is 136 repo source files / ~1.6 MiB beyond the launch graph, plus react-native-webview, expo-video, expo-file-system and the @noble/cborg packages. The code comment says this cost is moved into idle time, and it is not. lazyScreen.test.ts only checks that load() is called, so nothing catches this. Minor issues: ThreadRouteScreen.preload() runs inside an idle callback with no try/catch, while the shiki prewarm has .catch. The comment in mobileStartupImports.test.ts:12-13 still says Metro has no inline requires.

Implementation sketch

1) Measure first, on a release iOS build (Hermes): time from thread tap to the ThreadDetailScreen first commit, or count evaluated modules the way 1b8bfd183 did, with and without a working warm-up. 2) Make the prewarm actually evaluate the thread render graph. Preferred: add apps/mobile/src/features/threads/prewarmThreadRoute.ts exporting an ordered list of thunks. Each thunk does a function-scoped require of a heavy render-path module: ./ThreadDetailScreen, ./ThreadMessage, ./ThreadComposer, ../../native/SelectableMarkdownText, ./ThreadHtmlRender and HtmlRenderWebView (react-native-webview), the approval/user-input cards and the model/composer menus. Pick the modules from the profile. Each module's own imports stay inline-lazy, so list the heavy leaves explicitly. In scheduleWorkspaceRoutePrewarm, run the thunks a few per runWhenIdle slice, each in try/catch, then run the shiki warm-up. Alternative: return `inlineRequires: { blockList }` from getTransformOptions in metro.config.js. Metro 0.84 supports this (metro/src/lib/transformHelpers.js:99-103). Generate the blockList as absolute paths of the thread feature modules, so that requiring ThreadDetailScreen evaluates its imports eagerly again. That is less explicit, and any launch-path import of those files would become eager, so mobileStartupImports.test.ts must keep them out of the index.ts graph. 3) Tests: a unit test that every prewarm specifier resolves to an existing source file. Extend mobileStartupImports.test.ts so that no require target in lazyRouteScreens.ts and no prewarm module is reachable from index.ts (today only ThreadRouteScreen is asserted). Extend metroStartupConfig.test.ts if blockList is used. 4) Fix the stale comments at lazyRouteScreens.ts:186-194 and mobileStartupImports.test.ts:12-13.

Partial#239 Every direct cold connect pays a GET /api/auth/session RTT (and up to 3 keychain reads) before requesting the ws-token

mobile-boot:direct-session-precheck-rtt · original impact Medium, effort M · Network / RTT WP14Bdecision

Current state

Confirmed PARTIAL. 60633eff3 implemented the headline proposal. A persisted, non-secret per-environment session hint (savedSessionHints.ts) lets a direct connect skip the pre-socket GET /api/auth/session whenever the remembered bearer session is at least 1h from expiry and not due for renewal. The connect goes straight to ws-token plus socket and re-asks the session in the background after register. The server answers a rejected bearer on ws-token with 401, which is terminal on the client (store-unavailable is 503, non-terminal), so the skip is safe. This removes one HTTP RTT from the critical path on hinted connects. Not delivered: the proposal's 'read the bearer once per attempt' (kept deliberately) and the expected −1-2 keychain reads. On the hinted path the background check adds a third SecureStore read, so total reads rose by one, off the critical path. Small gaps the auditor missed: in-session renewals (keepRenewed) never refresh the hint; AppAccessGate re-reads the bearer on every registry change, including each socket open; and a narrow window in addSavedEnvironment can re-record the replaced credential's hint after forgetSessionHint. All are low value. Web/desktop keep the same precheck, but that is outside this mobile finding.

Evidence
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/savedSessionHints.ts:49-58 usableSavedSessionHint: bearer-session-token only, at least 1h to expiry, and !shouldRenewSavedSession. This is the proposal's skip condition.
  • apps/mobile/src/runtime/bootstrap.ts:54 createSavedSessionHints(mobileKV) is injected into the mobile driver, so the hint is live in production.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:395-398 Keychain bearer read and hint KV read run in parallel.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:434-441 Hinted path: no pre-socket session GET. The role is patched from the hint.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:466-477 renew() with the hinted session is a no-op (savedSessionRenewal.ts:194-197). The hint is recorded only after a fresh node answer and only when not cancelled.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:536-570 Background session check after register: rejection goes to rejectCredential; success re-records the hint, patches the role and re-arms keepRenewed. It reads the bearer from SecureStore again (:540-541), so the hinted path makes 3 keychain reads (396, resolver 345, 541) where the old non-due path made 2.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:338-347 The URL resolver re-reads the bearer on every attempt, deliberately (superseded-bearer invariant also stated at :302-305). The 'read once per attempt' part of the proposal is not implemented.
  • apps/mobile/src/platform/secretKv.ts:29-41 There is no in-memory caching: every readBearerToken is a SecureStore.getItemAsync call.
  • apps/server/src/auth/http.ts:181-193 The ws-token route authenticates the bearer and maps AuthError through respondToAuthError (http.ts:17-30) to error.status.
  • apps/server/src/auth/Layers/ServerAuth.ts:181-194 A rejected session credential maps to 401 (terminal on the client). An unavailable session store maps to 503 (non-terminal, retried). This confirms the hinted skip relies on a real terminal 401.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/savedEnvironmentSession.ts:105-107 isSavedEnvironmentCredentialRejection is 401 only. It is wired as isTerminalUrlError/onTerminalUrlError at environmentDriver.ts:359-360.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/savedSessionRenewal.ts:209-261 keepRenewed rotates the bearer in-session and re-arms from renewed.session, but has no hook to refresh the persisted hint. After an in-session renewal the hint still describes the old, due session, so the next cold connect pays the precheck once (errs toward checking; not unsafe).
Remaining

1) The proposal's 'read the bearer once per attempt and hand it to the first URL resolution' is not implemented, by design. Hinted connects read the bearer at environmentDriver.ts:396 and again at :345 on the critical path, plus a third read at :541 for the background check. The finding's −1-2 keychain reads were not delivered: the hinted path makes one more read than before, off the critical path. 2) keepRenewed (savedSessionRenewal.ts:240-258) never refreshes the hint after an in-session rotation, so the next cold connect pays one avoidable precheck RTT. 3) AppAccessGate.tsx:106 re-reads the bearer on every registry change, including markConnected on each socket open. 4) There is a narrow window in environmentActions.ts:95 (forget) vs :122-123 (cancel/remove) where the replaced credential's hint can be re-recorded and used by the re-pair connect at :124, giving a transiently stale role. By design and not a gap: the first connect after the session turns 1 day old still runs the full sequential check+rotate+write+read+activation path before ws-token, as the proposal required.

Defects in the shipped fix

Minor and low-severity. In addSavedEnvironment (apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentActions.ts), forgetSessionHint at :95 runs before the awaited persistRecord/writeBearerToken and before cancelPendingSavedEnvironmentConnection/remove at :122-123. During that window an old in-flight attempt is not yet cancelled (environmentDriver.ts:475 checks only !isCancelled()), and an old hinted connection is still current (:552 isCurrent()). Either can call sessionHints.record for the replaced credential, which undoes the forget that the comment at environmentDriver.ts:473-474 says must not be undone. The re-pair connect at :124 can then skip its pre-socket check and show the old session's role until the background check corrects it within one RTT. This is not an auth hole: the new bearer is freshly issued, the ws-token 401 stays terminal, and the server enforces the role. No other defects found. The skip condition, the terminal 401 (confirmed: ServerAuth.ts toCredentialRejection status 401; store-unavailable 503 is non-terminal), serialized hint writes, and non-secret persistence are all sound.

Implementation sketch

Safe, no-decision parts (each S, low risk): (a) Refresh the hint after in-session renewal. In packages/client-runtime/src/connection/savedSessionRenewal.ts, add an optional `onSession?: (session: AuthSessionState) => void` to the keepRenewed request. In renewDue, call it with answer.session when the answer is authenticated, and with renewed.session after a successful rotation (renewed.bearerToken !== bearerToken). In apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts, pass `onSession: (s) => { if (isCurrent()) sessionHints?.record(record.environmentId, s); }` at both keepRenewed call sites (:530, :562). Tests: savedSessionRenewal.test.ts asserts onSession receives the activated session after rotation. environmentDriver.test.ts uses fake timers to drive a keepRenewed rotation, then asserts sessionHints.read returns the new session and a second connectSavedEnvironment registers before fetchRemoteSessionState is called. (b) Close the forget/cancel window. In environmentActions.ts addSavedEnvironment, call registry.driver.forgetSessionHint(environmentId) again after `await registry.driver.supervisor.remove(...)` (:123) and before connect(record) (:124). Keep the early call. Test: an environmentActions test with a fake driver whose pending attempt resolves (and records) during persistRecord. Assert the subsequent connect asks the session before the socket and that the stored hint carries the new session's role. (c) Stop the gate re-reading the keychain on each socket open. In AppAccessGate.tsx:106, subscribe with a key check: remember the sorted environmentId list and call evaluate() only when it changes (lastConnectedAt-only updates are ignored). Test: a gate/unit test that markConnected does not call catalog.readBearerToken again. Needs decision (optional, low value, about 1-5 ms per SecureStore read): (d) read the bearer once per attempt. Option 1: hand the bearer read at environmentDriver.ts:396 to the first resolver invocation (a one-shot `firstBearer` consumed by the URL provider) only when renew() kept that bearer and no rotation is in flight for the environment. Option 2: a write-through in-memory bearer cache in the mobile catalog, which is coherent on mobile because there is a single JS runtime and every write goes through catalog.writeBearerToken/removeBearerToken. rotateAndStore's durable read-back (savedSessionRenewal.ts:179) must bypass it. Either option conflicts with the documented 'never present a remembered bearer' invariant (environmentDriver.ts:302-305, :338-341) and changes locked-keychain behaviour (SavedEnvironmentBearerUnavailableError), so get sign-off first. Tests: extend 'never presents a bearer a renewal superseded' (environmentDriver.test.ts:598) to cover the handed-over bearer.

Needs a decision

This applies only to the leftover 'read the bearer once per attempt' item (d). Reusing a bearer read earlier, or caching it in memory, changes auth semantics around superseded-bearer presentation (the node revokes the pairing on a superseded bearer after grace) and changes locked-keychain behaviour. The code explicitly chose to re-read on every use. Items (a)-(c) are safe, non-secret, conservative changes and need no decision.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Partial#240 React Compiler is enabled for web but not for the mobile app, leaving hand-written memoization fragile

mobile-boot:no-react-compiler-on-mobile · original impact Medium, effort M · Rendering WP14B

Current state

PARTIAL holds. #710 (60633eff3) turned on React Compiler for mobile via experiments.reactCompiler and a babel-preset-expo sources filter, and the wiring works. I ran the repo's real babel.config.js in memory: HomeScreen, InboxScreen, InboxThreadRow, ProjectsScreen and WorktreeRow come out with memo caches (_c(n)). ThreadDetailScreen does not, and neither does anything else in features/threads, components, or the remaining feature directories. Two things the auditor missed. (1) Widening the regex alone will not compile the two hottest thread components. The root ThreadDetailScreen and ThreadComposer both bail on try/finally and on try without catch, so only the row components (TimelineRow, ThreadMessage, ThreadActivityFoldRow) would get compiled. (2) A small defect in the integration: metro.config.js NON_INLINED_REQUIRES names 'react-compiler-runtime', but with target '19' the compiler emits 'react/compiler-runtime'. Inline requires therefore turns every compiled render into (0, require("react/compiler-runtime").c)(n).

Evidence
  • apps/mobile/app.config.ts:167-171 experiments.reactCompiler is true. @expo/cli metroOptions.js:120/203 (export:embed for release builds) and @expo/metro-config rewriteRequestUrl.js:85 (dev server) pass it as transform.reactCompiler. babel-transformer.js:84 then sets supportsReactCompiler.
  • apps/mobile/babel.config.js:6-7 REACT_COMPILER_SOURCES = /apps/mobile/src/features/(home|inbox|projects)/. I transformed every file in those three directories in memory with this exact config. HomeScreen, HomeRouteScreen, InboxScreen (2 sites), InboxThreadRow, ProjectsScreen (3), WorktreeRow (2) and others contain _c(n). ThreadDetailScreen.tsx contains no compiler-runtime import.
  • node_modules/.bun/babel-preset-expo@57.0.11+88441c62a747ee83/node_modules/babel-preset-expo/build/configs/expo.js:121-160 The preset passes target '19' and spreads the user options, sources included. Release builds use panicThreshold 'NONE', so a function that cannot be compiled is skipped instead of failing the build.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/threads/ThreadDetailScreen.tsx:375 In a simulation that compiles all sources, the root ThreadDetailScreen component bails with 'Handle TryStatement with a finalizer' and 'TryStatement without a catch'. The causes are try/finally inside its callbacks at :1041-1049 (applyPolicy), :1329-1396 (send) and :1404-1409. TimelineRow (:206), ThreadCachedBanner, ThreadDeliveryBanner and HeaderActions in the same file do compile.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/threads/ThreadComposer.tsx:37 ThreadComposer bails because of the try/finally at :103-109 in its send handler, so widening the regex alone leaves it uncompiled.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/threads/ThreadMessage.tsx:117 AudioAttachmentRow mutates the useVideoPlayer return value, which the compiler reports as 'This value cannot be modified' (a real rules-of-React diagnostic). It would be skipped. ThreadMessage, ImageAttachment and VideoAttachmentRow compile cleanly.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/threads/useThreadChecks.ts:21 Bails with 'Support value blocks ...'. Simulated totals for features/threads: 47 functions compile, 10 bail. Of the bails, 7 are try/finally or try without catch, 2 are the AudioAttachmentRow mutation, and 1 is this value-block issue.
  • apps/mobile/src/components/OverlayPortal.tsx:36 This is the only bail in src/components ('UpdateExpression' on the module-level nextKey++). Simulated totals for components: 47 functions compile, 1 bails. Widening to this directory is close to free.
  • apps/mobile/metro.config.js:86-93 NON_INLINED_REQUIRES lists 'react-compiler-runtime', the npm polyfill for React 17/18. The compiler emits `import { c as _c } from "react/compiler-runtime"`. Running the Metro worker's import-export plus inline-requires plugins in memory on InboxThreadRow gives `var $ = (0, require("react/compiler-runtime").c)(79);`, so the runtime lookup is inlined into every compiled render. Added in 1b8bfd183.
Remaining

(a) Compiler scope. apps/mobile/babel.config.js:6-7 still excludes src/features/threads, src/components and every other feature directory. Nothing under those paths gets compiled, including ThreadDetailScreen.tsx, ThreadMessage.tsx, ThreadActivityFoldRow.tsx and ThreadComposer.tsx, which re-render during live streaming. (b) Widening the regex is not enough for the hottest components. ThreadDetailScreen (ThreadDetailScreen.tsx:375) bails because of try/finally in callbacks at :1041-1049, :1329-1396 and :1404-1409. ThreadComposer (ThreadComposer.tsx:37) bails because of try/finally at :103-109. useThreadChecks.ts:21 bails on a value block. With a widened regex alone, only the row components (TimelineRow, ThreadMessage, ThreadActivityFoldRow and the cards) would be compiled. (c) Nobody has measured the gain on a device yet.

Defects in the shipped fix

Minor: apps/mobile/metro.config.js:91 keeps 'react-compiler-runtime' eager. Compiled code imports 'react/compiler-runtime' (babel-preset-expo forces target '19'), so the entry does nothing. Metro inline-requires then rewrites every compiled render to `(0, require("react/compiler-runtime").c)(n)`. That costs one metroRequire lookup per render per compiled component. Each lookup is negligible, but the count grows with the scope. The fix is a one-word change. Also minor, and already noted by the auditor: the sources regex is hard-coded to the path segment apps/mobile/src/features, with no test or lint guard. Mobile Vitest does not run the compiler, so existing tests do not cover compiled behaviour.

Implementation sketch

1) apps/mobile/metro.config.js:91: replace 'react-compiler-runtime' with 'react/compiler-runtime' (or keep both). Check: transform a compiled file and confirm the output keeps a single top-level `var _c = ...` binding instead of an inline require at each use. 2) apps/mobile/babel.config.js: widen REACT_COMPILER_SOURCES in two steps, profiling on a device after each one as the existing comment requires. Step A: add src/components, e.g. /[\\/]apps[\\/]mobile[\\/]src[\\/](components|features[\\/](home|inbox|projects))[\\/]/. AppText, GlassSurface, StatusPill and the others all compile, and only OverlayPortal bails. Step B: add features/threads. 3) To compile the thread roots, move try/finally out of component and callback bodies. Options: a module-level async helper such as `async function withBusy(setBusy, fn) { setBusy(true); try { return await fn(); } finally { setBusy(false); } }` called from the useCallback, or promise .catch/.finally chains. Apply this to ThreadDetailScreen.tsx applyPolicy (:1038-1050), the send handler (:1325-1396) and the block at :1404-1409, and to ThreadComposer.tsx :100-110. Optionally restructure useThreadChecks.ts:21, and leave AudioAttachmentRow uncompiled (or add 'use no memo'), since it mutates the player by design. 4) Verify. Add a small Node check script or Vitest test under apps/mobile that runs @babel/core with babel.config.js and caller { supportsReactCompiler: true, isDev: false } over the targeted files. It should use the compiler's `logger` option to assert zero CompileError events for ThreadDetailScreen, ThreadComposer, ThreadMessage and TimelineRow, and assert that the output contains `react/compiler-runtime`. That also guards against the path regex silently going stale. Then run the existing mobile tests and profile thread detail during a live streaming turn with the React DevTools profiler or Hermes sampling profiler, before and after (render counts and commit durations of TimelineRow and ThreadMessage).

Partial#241 Hosted live list waits for a per-launch enrollment upsert and a directory-gated selection restore before the relay ticket

mobile-boot:hosted-relay-turnup-waterfall · original impact Medium, effort L · Waterfall decision

Current state

PARTIAL is correct. (c) is done. (a) and (b) are not implemented, and no Hub-side or renamed implementation exists. Their payoff has largely disappeared, though. Since #710 the directory read runs beside the session restore, so (b) gains about nothing. Since 94ec18751 the relay socket's TCP, TLS and upgrade (about 3 RTT from selection) start beside the enrollment wait and the ticket. On a cold launch the socket, not the upsert, is now usually the critical path. (a) also cannot skip the local identity and prekey reads, because the ready enrollment carries that material into the handshake. It would save at most one DPoP sign plus one upsert RTT, and only when the local work exceeds about 1 RTT. The auditor's sketch for (a) misses one thing: a stale cached summary gets Hub 'forbidden enrollment_unavailable', which maps to a retryable network failure, so the relay would back off forever without re-enrolling. Two smaller observations. First, the enrollment's refreshDirectory call probably sends a redundant listNodes at launch now that the prefetched directory commits early. Second, the hosted primary connection is still held behind full SQLite hydration.

Evidence

  • packages/client-runtime/src/authorization/state.ts:753 #restoreAccess sends listNodes beside restoreSession (prefetchHostedDirectory at :470) and commits it at :773. In bearer/mobile mode too, since 9adb0372c. Directory-ready is now about the same time as authenticated, which removes almost all of (b)'s intended gain.

Ready = {namespace, enrollment, identity, prekey}, so a cached ready would still need the local identity and prekey reads.

When the prefetched listNodes resolved before restoreSession, the commit finishes in microtasks, so this probably sends a second listNodes and DPoP proof at launch, alongside the upsert. Minor.

The mobile coordinator's nodeForId (apps/mobile/src/runtime/bootstrap.ts:145) also reads the directory, so (b) would need a directory-less acquisition path.
Remaining

(a) Not implemented: every authenticated launch runs the DPoP-signed upsert (nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts:381-451, triggered at runtime.ts:357-364) before prepareMobileRelaySocketContext lets the ticket go (accountE2eeAttempt.ts:117-129). (b) Not implemented: restore and selectNode stay directory-gated (selectionPersistence.ts:69-74, state.ts:2359-2366, nodeForId at bootstrap.ts:145). The cost both were meant to remove is now mostly hidden. The directory is prefetched beside the session restore (state.ts:753-773). The relay socket's TCP, TLS and upgrade (about 3 RTT plus one sign, transport.ts:343) start beside the enrollment wait and the ticket (about 2 RTT plus 2 signs plus local key reads). Residual gain from (a) is about max(0, local identity/prekey reads + one sign − 1 RTT): roughly 0 on cellular, maybe 20-60 ms on low-RTT Wi-Fi. Residual gain from (b) is about the gap between listNodes and session restore (near 0). Remaining edges: (1) If enrollment plus ticket exceed the 3.5 s early-socket window (relaySocket.ts:109), or any ticket-stage failure occurs (transport.ts:379), the attempt goes serial again. (2) The hosted primary connect is still deferred until full SQLite hydration (bootstrap.ts:57, environmentDriver.ts:601). (3) The enrollment's refreshDirectory (nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts:383) probably sends a redundant listNodes at launch. The only meaningful lever left is not in the finding: the socket path is now critical, so opening the not-node-specific early relay socket at authenticated time, or with the stored token at launch, rather than after selection could hide 1-2 RTT.

Defects in the shipped fix

None that break correctness in the implemented parts. The early socket carries no authority before its ticket, and the enrollment await grants nothing because ready is still required. Minor, plausible side effect of the #710 prefetch: the enrollment's refreshDirectory (nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts:383) used to join the in-flight launch listNodes. Now the prefetched read often commits before ensureIdentity resolves, so a second listNodes and DPoP proof is sent alongside the upsert on many launches (#refreshDirectoryWith at state.ts:2148 only joins an in-flight read). This is extra launch traffic and Secure Enclave contention, not a correctness bug.

Implementation sketch

Priority is low. If anything is done, prefer the cheaper wins. (1) Redundant launch listNodes. In apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:272, pass refreshDirectory as a call that skips when hostedHubStore.getState().directoryStatus === 'ready' and the last commit was recent. Alternatively add a controller method that joins an in-flight read or reuses one committed within N seconds. Test in runtime.test.ts: bootstrap with enrollment, where the prefetched listNodes resolves before restoreSession, should give exactly one listNodes. (2) Optional, needs decision: open the relay early socket at authenticated time instead of after selection. Add a 'prewarm' in packages/client-runtime/src/relay/transport.ts that an authenticated-account hook calls once (mobile: from watchSelectionForE2ee in runtime.ts when accountStatus flips to authenticated). It keeps one MobileEarlyRelaySocket (relaySocket.ts:259) that the first nextUrl adopts instead of opening its own. It is discarded on generation, account or sign-out changes and after the existing 3.5 s window. Tests in transport.test.ts and relaySocket.test.ts: adoption, discard on account change, no adoption after expiry. (3) Proposal (a), only if measurements show the local work exceeds 1 RTT: - Add a public-only persisted summary to the platform contract (packages/client-runtime/src/platform/index.ts, NativeE2eePlatformService): readEnrollmentSummary/writeEnrollmentSummary. Fields: hubOrigin, accountId, enrollmentId, enrollmentRevision, clientPrekeyCertificateDigest, certificateExpiresAt, status. Implement it in apps/mobile/src/platform/nativeE2ee.ts on the secure store, and clear it on a namespace change and in invalidate('revoked'|'signed-out'). - In nativeE2eeEnrollment.ts start(), after ensureIdentity and ensureClientPrekey (both still needed, because ready carries identity and prekey), compare the cached summary's namespace, enrollmentId and digest with the local prekey, and check the certificate is not within its renewal margin. If it matches, publish ready from the summary plus local material, then run the upsert in the background. On an upsert answer that differs, publish the new ready (generation bump). Write the summary after every successful upsert. - Required fix the auditor missed: in accountE2eeAttempt.ts issueMobileRelayAttempt (around :265-289) and nativeE2eeTrustResolver.ts:252-270, treat Hub forbidden/enrollment_unavailable on the account-grant ticket as stale cached enrollment. Drop the cache and call coordinator.retry() before the next attempt. Otherwise the relay backs off forever on a mismatched revision or digest. Keep enrollment_revoked failing closed. - Tests in nativeE2eeEnrollment.test.ts: cached-ready publishes without an upsert; a background upsert with a new revision republishes; a near-expiry certificate forces a foreground upsert; a namespace change ignores the cache. accountE2eeAttempt.test.ts: enrollment_unavailable triggers a re-upsert; enrollment_revoked invalidates. (b) as proposed is not worth doing: the directory is already prefetched beside the session.

Needs a decision

Proposal (a) changes E2EE enrollment semantics. The device would treat a cached enrollment as ready without a fresh Hub upsert, which needs security review of the cache contents, expiry margin and stale or revoked handling. Proposal (b), and the alternative of prewarming the relay socket before selection or before session validation, change ordering under the single hosted lifecycle owner (AGENTS.md 'Hosted Hub and PWA Boundaries'). Only the redundant listNodes dedupe is a local, decision-free change.

Value low · effort M · risk medium

Not done#242 Every hosted relay frame is base64-decoded in JS (RN WebSocket) and decrypted with pure-JS noble on Hermes

mobile-boot:relay-frames-base64-and-js-crypto · original impact Medium, effort L · CPU decision

Current state

NOT_DONE is confirmed. On mobile, every hosted relay frame still crosses RN 0.86.3's WebSocket as base64. Inbound frames are decoded with base64-js on the JS thread, then opened with pure-JS noble ChaCha20-Poly1305 on Hermes. The Noise handshake stays on noble too. Nothing has been measured: there is no throughput benchmark and there are no snapshot receive, decrypt or apply marks. There is no native crypto module, no JSI or alternate WebSocket, and no compression. Since f1be4abc7 four nearby changes landed, and none of them removes this cost. c1a83bcab added a node:crypto seam, but only the server and desktop install it, and section 14.7 says Hermes never does. 2cb0d3f5e sped up frame equality and canonical CBOR checks. That is per-frame JS work, but not base64 or AEAD. d2aa947a3 pages the shell snapshot into messages of at most 1 MiB. That lowers the peak size of a single message but not the total bytes, and it lets snapshots for very large homes (more than ~2,600 threads) go past the old 4 MiB relay cap. 94ec18751 and 4e07cee4c cut connect latency, not per-byte cost. One correction to the original finding: the '<=2 MiB per environment' bound is the last-known-shell cache bound, not a bound on the live snapshot. A measured 2,000-thread home is 2.9 MB, so the per-snapshot cost may be higher than the finding assumed.

Evidence
  • apps/mobile/node_modules/react-native/Libraries/WebSocket/WebSocket.js:242 RN 0.86.3 (apps/mobile/package.json:81) still decodes inbound binary frames with base64.toByteArray(ev.data).buffer on the JS thread.
  • apps/mobile/node_modules/react-native/Libraries/WebSocket/WebSocket.js:202 Outbound binary frames still go through NativeWebSocketModule.sendBinary(binaryToBase64(data)).
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.ts:285 defaultCreateSocket (:285-297) builds the stock globalThis.WebSocket and passes headers. binaryType is set to 'arraybuffer' at :173, :323 and :502. There is no JSI, Nitro or other WebSocket. The early-socket work in 94ec18751 reuses the same constructor.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.ts:308 classifyInboundMessage copies every inbound frame again (ArrayBuffer.slice(0) at :309, Uint8Array.from at :310/:313). The outbound path copies twice with Uint8Array.from, at :585 (facade to engine) and :383 (engine to socket), before RN's base64 encode.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeSession.ts:409 The record AEAD seal and open (:409-442) use native primitives only if they were installed through e2eeNativePrimitives(). Otherwise they call noble chacha20poly1305 (:422 and :441), which is always the case on mobile.
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeNoise.ts:1 The Noise handshake still imports noble chacha20poly1305, HKDF, sha256 and utils directly (:1-4). Only X25519 is routed through the relayE2eeKeys dispatch (:12).
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeKeys.ts:382 installE2eeNativePrimitives is a synchronous seam from c1a83bcab. A sync JSI or Nitro module could implement it. Its doc comment at :333-337 and :378-381 says 'Browsers and Hermes never install anything' and 'The server and desktop compositions call this once at startup; nothing else may.'
  • packages/shared/src/relayE2eeNodeCrypto.ts:406 installE2eeNodeNativePrimitives is the only installer. It is called only at apps/server/src/hubConnector/HubConnectorLive.ts:323 and apps/desktop/src/desktopHubStack.ts:18. A git grep over apps/mobile finds no caller.
  • docs/relay-e2ee-protocol.md:5069 Section 14.7 limits native fast paths to node and desktop ('Browsers and Hermes never install one', :5081-5082). It keeps Noise CipherState, SHA-256, HMAC and HKDF on noble everywhere (:5108-5110). The section is 'proposed' and 'recording owner acceptance ... is REQUIRED' (:5071-5072).
  • apps/mobile/package.json:58 expo-crypto is used only for getRandomValues (apps/mobile/polyfills.ts:116) and provides no AEAD. react-native-nitro-modules 0.36.5 (:86) is already a dependency for nitro-markdown, so a Nitro crypto module would not add a new runtime. There is no quick-crypto or fast-base64 dependency. apps/mobile/modules has no crypto module, and nothing changed there since f1be4abc7. CryptoKit is used only by the desktop macOS security helper.
  • apps/mobile/src/devtools/e2eeVectorRunner.ts:1 This runner only checks correctness vectors. A grep for bench, MB/s, throughput and performance.now finds nothing. Under apps/mobile/src and packages/client-runtime/src there are no performance marks around relay snapshot receive, decrypt or apply. The only performance.now uses are in shikiReviewHighlighter.ts and platform/frame.ts.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/wsRpcClient.ts:1090 Every client, mobile included, now requests snapshotDelivery: 'paged' (d2aa947a3). Pages are at most 1 MiB (apps/server/src/ws/context/constants.ts:54). This caps how much a single message decrypts at once, but not the total bytes decoded and decrypted.
Remaining

Nothing in the proposal has been done. (1) Measure. Nobody has measured base64 decode, ChaCha20-Poly1305 open or handshake throughput on Hermes. The only dev hook, apps/mobile/src/devtools/e2eeVectorRunner.ts, is correctness-only. There are no receive, decrypt or apply marks in apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/relaySocket.ts (#deliver at ~:547) or in packages/client-runtime/src/relay. (2a) Native AEAD/X25519 on mobile. installE2eeNativePrimitives (packages/shared/src/relayE2eeKeys.ts:382) is never called on mobile. Section 14.7 (docs/relay-e2ee-protocol.md:5069-5110) forbids Hermes from installing a provider. (2b) WebSocket without base64. relaySocket.ts:285-297 still uses RN's base64-bridged WebSocket (WebSocket.js:202/:242). There are redundant copies at relaySocket.ts:309-313 (inbound) and :383 and :585 (outbound). (3) Relay payloads are not compressed. Paged snapshots (d2aa947a3) cap the size of one message, not the total bytes. Large homes can now send more than 4 MiB of shell over the relay. That makes the per-byte cost larger than the finding's '<=2 MiB' assumption.

Defects in the shipped fix

No fix was implemented for this finding. The related changes (c1a83bcab node:crypto seam, 2cb0d3f5e frame equality and canonical check, d2aa947a3 paged snapshot) look correct for their own goals. None of them targets the Hermes base64 or noble cost.

Implementation sketch

Phase 1 (S, no protocol impact, do first). (a) Extend apps/mobile/src/devtools/e2eeVectorRunner.ts, or add a sibling apps/mobile/src/devtools/relayThroughputBench.ts exposed through the same __DEV__ global hook. Benchmark on device with performance.now(): - base64-js toByteArray and fromByteArray at 16 KiB, 256 KiB and 1 MiB. Import base64-js through react-native's dependency, or call the RN WebSocket's path directly. - noble chacha20poly1305 open and seal at the same sizes. - A full NX handshake (relayE2eeNoise) and one Ed25519 and one P-256 verify. - Uint8Array.from(u8) against u8.slice() at 256 KiB. Hermes TypedArray.from may take the iterator path. - decodeRelayFrame at 256 KiB. Report MB/s and ms. Run release builds on a physical iPhone (and on a low-end Android if one is supported). (b) Add marks for: first inbound byte of the shell subscription; record decrypted (relayE2eeSession open); snapshot-end assembled (packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/shellSnapshotAssembly.ts); snapshot applied in the client-runtime shell store. Put them behind a dev or diagnostics flag and log them once per connect. A cheap first step is to wrap the engine's inbound handler in relaySocket.ts #deliver and the relayE2eeSession open callback with a cumulative-ms counter, and dump it after the first snapshot. Phase 2a (L, only if the numbers justify it): a native crypto module. Add apps/mobile/modules/ryco-e2ee-crypto, preferably as a Nitro HybridObject because react-native-nitro-modules is already a dependency. It needs synchronous ArrayBuffer calls, because the seam is synchronous. iOS CryptoKit provides ChaChaPoly (seal/open with AAD and a 12-byte nonce), Curve25519.KeyAgreement (X25519), Curve25519.Signing (Ed25519 verify) and P256.Signing (ECDSA verify). Android would use Tink or BoringSSL via conscrypt, or decline, which falls back to noble. Build an E2eeNativePrimitives object that mirrors relayE2eeNodeCrypto.ts: lazy per-primitive known-answer self-tests (RFC 7748, 8032, 6979 and 8439 vectors plus forgeries), and a minBytes threshold for the AEAD. Then call installE2eeNativePrimitives from the mobile hosted runtime setup (apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts) or from polyfills.ts. Amend docs/relay-e2ee-protocol.md section 14.7 Selection, and the relayE2eeKeys.ts comment at :333-381, to allow a Hermes provider. Get the required owner acceptance. Caveats: - CryptoKit Ed25519 is cofactorless and may reject torsion signatures. Section 14.7 already handles this: a native false is re-decided by noble. - CryptoKit ChaChaPoly.open returns plaintext only after the tag is verified. That satisfies the section 9.5 erasure rule. - If the handshake's own CipherState and HKDF also show up as hot in Phase 1, the 'Unchanged' bullet would have to be revisited. That is unlikely: handshake messages are small. Tests: run the section 16 corpus with the provider installed and absent, the way relayE2eeNodeCrypto.test.ts does, through a JS fake provider in vitest plus an on-device run through e2eeVectorRunner. Phase 2b (M to L, independent of crypto): a WebSocket without base64. Swap defaultCreateSocket (relaySocket.ts:285) for a JSI or Nitro WebSocket that delivers ArrayBuffers natively, for example react-native-nitro-websocket or a small custom URLSessionWebSocketTask module. It must keep custom headers (the DPoP proof and the session cookie handling described at :489-502), close codes, and bufferedAmount semantics. Test it with the existing relaySocket.test.ts suite through the createSocket injection point. Cheap independent cleanup (S): replace Uint8Array.from(x) with x.slice() in relaySocket.ts. Keep one defensive copy where the engine zeroes buffers (:383). Drop the inbound copy at :309 if the engine does not retain or zero the RN-owned buffer, and check that against relayEngine's ownership rules first. Phase 3 (M, node side, separate decision): compression before sealing, for example a negotiated deflate of RPC payloads. This is a protocol and capability change. Note that compression before encryption carries a length side-channel (CRIME-style) risk when secrets and attacker-influenced data share a message. Prefer shrinking the shell snapshot schema itself.

Needs a decision

Phase 2a changes E2EE crypto policy. Section 14.7 of docs/relay-e2ee-protocol.md explicitly says Hermes never installs a native provider, and that section still needs recorded owner acceptance. A mobile native provider needs a protocol-doc amendment and a security review of the CryptoKit and Android equivalence arguments. Phase 3 (compressing before sealing) is a wire or capability change with side-channel trade-offs. Phase 1 (measurement and perf marks) and the copy cleanup need no decision.

Value medium · effort L · risk medium

Done#243 ensureMobileHostedSession runs independent keychain/Secure Enclave steps serially

mobile-boot:hosted-session-serial-local-steps · original impact Low, effort S · Waterfall

Current state

Confirmed DONE for ensureMobileHostedSession, which is the finding's scope. #710 (60633eff3) overlapped the token keychain read, the trust-store load and the signer load. 4e07cee4c then made the signer load conditional. With a stored session it starts when the token read resolves and overlaps the trust read. With no stored session it is skipped and the runtime is configured with a deferred signer. Tests pin both behaviours. One small side effect, not a regression against the report baseline: on a signed-out launch the deferred hardware-key load now runs on NativeIdentityScreen's mount path. There it sits in series after two keychain reads and before an unauthenticated capability fetch that does not need it.

Evidence
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:418 hydrateMobileHubProfile stays first because it resolves the origin. The config is re-resolved and checked before any secret is read (lines 422-423).
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:431 tokenRead starts and is not awaited. signerLoad (lines 434-442) starts createMobileDpopSigner once the token read finds a stored session. The attempt is boxed and its rejection is caught, so there is no unhandled rejection.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:443 Promise.allSettled([tokenRead, mobileE2eeTrustStore.hydrate()]) runs the token read and the trust read together. A token failure still maps to credential-storage (line 445), and trust still loads before configuration.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:455 Signed-out path: configureMobileHostedRuntime('deferred'), so no Secure Enclave load at launch. Stored-session path (line 456): the signer attempt already in flight is joined. Its failure maps to device-security (lines 216-223) and bootstrap runs only after configuration.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.test.ts:501 'overlaps the stored session's key load with the trust read' and 'does not load the hardware key at launch when no session is stored' (line 546) pin the new behaviour. The ordering tests (lines 458-478) still require hydrate -> trust-hydrate -> configure -> bootstrap.
  • apps/mobile/src/platform/dpopSigner.ts:41 createMobileDpopSigner is memoized and clears the memo on failure, so the early start and the later join (or a retry) share one attempt.
  • apps/mobile/src/platform/e2eeSecureStore.ts:242 The install-marker KV read was never inside trustStore.hydrate. It is the memoized custody check (ensureDeviceCustody) that runs before the first E2EE secure-store get, and it still runs inside the trust read. It now overlaps the token read and is required by §6.3, so it is not a defect.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/identity/NativeIdentityScreen.tsx:443 On a signed-out launch, the locked stack mounts this screen. Its effect reads the completion journal (keychain), then the transaction store (line 455), then calls refreshCapability (line 466).
  • apps/mobile/src/features/identity/NativeIdentityScreen.tsx:395 refreshCapability awaits waitForSessionSetup, which calls ensureMobileHostedDeviceKey (line 176). That deferred key load (expo-crypto import, device-key module, ensureKey; key creation on first install) finishes before the capability fetch at line 415 starts. The fetch is unauthenticated (hubCapability.ts:139, credentials: 'omit'), so the two are independent but run in series.
Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness bugs in the fix. Two small notes. (1) As the auditor said, on the stored-session path the signer load starts after the token read, not at t0, because the token read is what proves a session exists. The critical path is max(token+signer, trust), not max(token, trust, signer), so it is slower by at most one keychain read. (2) Side effect of 4e07cee4c: on a signed-out launch the hardware-key load moved out of the gate and into NativeIdentityScreen. It now runs after two keychain reads (lines 443, 455) and before an independent, unauthenticated capability fetch (lines 395 and 415). Against the f1be4abc7 baseline this is still faster to the capability fetch, by about min(token, trust). Against the #710 version it is slower by about min(signer, max(token, trust)), and the identity screen paints earlier. The key load could overlap the journal and transaction reads and the network probe. That would save up to one Secure Enclave round trip (larger on first install, when the key is created) before the sign-in form is ready.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Done#244 Opening a thread on another hosted node always waits a fixed 250 ms trailing debounce before retargeting

mobile-boot:retarget-trailing-debounce · original impact Low, effort S · Waterfall

Current state

The trailing retarget debounce went from 250 ms to 100 ms in 60633eff3 (#710). That is the finding's own fallback proposal (about 80 to 100 ms) and saves 150 ms on every cold cross-node thread open. The leading-edge variant was rejected, and the rejection holds up. If an idle open dispatches immediately, A is dispatched at once, so an A then B tap-through costs two acquisitions. The finding claimed leading edge keeps the one-ticket guarantee, and that claim was wrong. The engine has a single production caller: ThreadDetailScreen through useThreadConnectionRetarget. No production code overrides debounceMs. Web has no equivalent retarget debounce. A regression test keeps the constant at 100 ms or below. The only defects are cosmetic, in comments.

Evidence
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/threadConnectionRetarget.ts:244 THREAD_CONNECTION_RETARGET_DEBOUNCE_MS = 100 (was 250 at f1be4abc7). 60633eff3 is the only commit since f1be4abc7 that touches this file or its test.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/threadConnectionRetarget.ts:237-243 Doc comment records that the leading dispatch for an idle engine was rejected because it would spend a ticket on A in the A to B case. This is correct: with leading edge, A dispatches at once and B queues behind the in-flight A (single-flight at :403), so the pair costs two acquisitions.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/threadConnectionRetarget.ts:270,319-325,365,432 The default debounce is read at :270. open() always calls armDebounce (:432), and evaluate() bails while the timer is pending (:365). Store or roster re-evaluations after the window (for example, the directory becoming ready on a cold deep link) run immediately through scheduleEvaluate, with no second debounce.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/useThreadConnectionRetarget.ts:28 The only production entry point. Its only caller is ThreadDetailScreen.tsx:441. git grep finds no production debounceMs override in apps/mobile/src.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/threadConnectionRetarget.test.ts:650-662 The new test asserts the constant is 100 ms or below and that the default window dispatches at exactly that time. It was inserted between the JSDoc for 'cancels an intent released before the debounce fires' (:645-649) and that test (:664), so the back-swipe JSDoc now sits above the wrong test.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/hostedConnectionCoordinator.ts:325-353 In Wave 3b the actuator (acquireMobileHostedNode, then coordinator.acquire) only refreshes lastAccessedAt and moves the selection cursor for an already-pooled node. The 100 ms therefore adds to a multi-second relay turn-up on cold nodes and is mostly invisible on warm ones. The remaining wait is small next to the measured 5.0 to 6.7 s for a remote Hub thread open.
Defects in the shipped fix

Cosmetic only, no behavioural defect. (1) threadConnectionRetarget.test.ts:645-649: the JSDoc 'Prevents a connection being opened for a thread the user has already navigated away from (a back-swipe inside the debounce window must cost nothing at all)' now sits above the new 'starts a single cross-node open within the default window' test (:650) instead of 'cancels an intent released before the debounce fires' (:664). (2) threadConnectionRetarget.ts:232: the debounceMs prop comment 'Long enough to swallow an A->B tap-through' is slightly stale next to the new rationale at :237-243. (3) threadConnectionRetarget.ts:256-260: the engine doc says every dispatched selectNode 'buys a real teardown and turn-up'. After Wave 3b's bounded pool (MAX_MOBILE_HOSTED_CONNECTIONS) a superseded acquisition holds or evicts a pooled slot instead of tearing down. The conclusion (drop superseded targets before dispatch) still holds; only the wording is dated.

Implementation sketch

Optional comment-only cleanup. In apps/mobile/src/connection/threadConnectionRetarget.test.ts, move the new 'starts a single cross-node open within the default window' test above the back-swipe JSDoc block, so the JSDoc again directly precedes 'cancels an intent released before the debounce fires'. In threadConnectionRetarget.ts:232, change the prop comment to point at THREAD_CONNECTION_RETARGET_DEBOUNCE_MS (for example 'Trailing debounce window; see THREAD_CONNECTION_RETARGET_DEBOUNCE_MS'). Optionally reword :256-260 to say a superseded dispatch costs a relay ticket and a pooled connection slot. Check with: bun run --cwd apps/mobile test -- threadConnectionRetarget. Done#245 Project icons are re-fetched over RPC after every (re)connect because the cache generation is keyed on connectedAt

mobile-boot:project-icon-refetch-per-connection · original impact Low, effort S · Caching WP12AWP14B

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. The status is right: the per-reconnect refetch and the per-render JSON.stringify are gone. The auditor was wrong that the fix has no defects that matter. The peek-on-first-render path added in #710 leaves a row with no latched artwork state. Once the 5-minute TTL passes, the next re-render of that row loses its icon and nothing fetches it again. Mobile also never clears the now environment-keyed cache on hosted sign-out, which web does.

Current state

Confirmed. #710 (60633eff3) removes the described cost: the cache moved from a WeakMap<EnvironmentApi,{generation}> to a module-level Map keyed by environment, then project plus avatar revision, with a 5-minute TTL. Reconnects and remounts no longer re-issue projects.readIcon, the request key is built from plain strings in useMemo, and web and mobile share one helper. However, the fix added a user-visible regression. Both ProjectFavicon components render a cache hit through peekProjectIconSource during render, and their effect returns early on a hit without copying the value into component state. A row that only ever displayed a peeked icon (new inbox rows, rows remounted by FlatList virtualization, NewTaskComposer, ProjectDetail and Projects screens; on web, later-mounted ProjectHero, ProjectBar, InboxRowPreview, NewThreadHero and so on) still shows the icon until the TTL passes. On the first re-render after that (any thread update on a memoized InboxThreadRow, a status or config write, typing in the composer), peek returns undefined and faviconUrl becomes null, so the folder or monogram fallback replaces the icon. The effect deps (api, environmentId, projectId, requestKey, revision, plus visible on web) have not changed, so nothing refetches. The fallback stays until a reconnect or remount. Before #710 every row stored its own fetch result in state, so this did not happen. No test covers TTL expiry for a peek-mounted instance. Minor: mobile never calls clearAllProjectIconCaches on hosted sign-out or Hub change. Web does this at apps/web/src/hostedHub/environment.ts:98. The old WeakMap was GC'd with its API objects, but the new cache keeps up to 16 environments × 8 MiB in memory until the process exits. Display is still gated on a live api for that environment, so this is not a leak.

Evidence
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/projectIconSource.ts:25 Module-level Map<EnvironmentId, EnvironmentIconCache>. Reconnects with a new API object reuse it, so the described refetch per reconnect is fixed (60633eff3).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/projectIconSource.ts:77 peekProjectIconSource returns undefined once expiresAt <= Date.now(). It does the same for an entry evicted by the 64-entry or 8 MiB per-environment LRU.
  • apps/mobile/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:43 cached = peek(...) is computed on every render. It is the only display source for a row whose artwork state is null.
  • apps/mobile/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:47 On a peek hit the effect returns early and never calls setArtwork, so the displayed value is never latched into component state.
  • apps/mobile/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:59 Effect deps do not change when the TTL expires, so no refetch is scheduled after expiry.
  • apps/mobile/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:60 faviconUrl = artwork?.key === requestKey ? artwork.source : (cached ?? null). After expiry this is null, ProjectFaviconImage is re-keyed to 'fallback' and the folder replaces the icon until a reconnect or remount.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/inbox/InboxThreadRow.tsx:55 The row is memo'd but re-renders on every thread update (line 108 renders ProjectFavicon). A new thread row for an already-cached project mounts on the peek path and loses its icon after 5 minutes of activity.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/newTask/NewTaskComposer.tsx:107 Mounted after the inbox filled the cache, so it uses the peek path. It is exposed to the same expiry and re-render loss.
  • apps/web/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:91 Web has the same pattern: peek at line 91, early return at line 95, display at lines 117-119. Later-mounted instances lose artwork after the TTL on any re-render.
  • apps/web/src/components/ProjectFavicon.browser.tsx:161 The remount test checks only the first-pass cached render. No test advances time past PROJECT_ICON_TTL_MS and re-renders a peek-mounted instance.
  • apps/web/src/hostedHub/environment.ts:98 Web drops all icon caches on account teardown. Mobile has no clearAllProjectIconCaches call; it only clears per environment in environmentActions.ts:155 and deviceCache.ts:56.
  • apps/web/src/components/ProjectFavicon.browser.tsx:147 Clearing artwork while disconnected is asserted behaviour. Each reconnect therefore still unmounts and remounts the expo-image (cachePolicy none) and decodes again, so the 'less decode churn' part of the expected gain is not realized by design. The RPCs are saved.
Defects in the shipped fix

(1) Regression from #710: a ProjectFavicon instance that rendered artwork via peekProjectIconSource never latches it into state (apps/mobile/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:43-60, apps/web/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx:91-119). After PROJECT_ICON_TTL_MS, or after LRU eviction, the next re-render shows the folder or monogram fallback, and the effect never refetches because its deps did not change. The icon stays gone until a reconnect or remount. This affects new or virtualized mobile inbox rows, the new-task composer, project screens, and later-mounted web surfaces. (2) Minor parity and hygiene gap: mobile does not clear the environment-keyed icon cache on hosted sign-out or Hub domain change, unlike web hostedHub/environment.ts:98. The artwork stays in memory, bounded at 16 environments × 8 MiB, until the process exits.

Implementation sketch

Fix (1) once for both clients. In packages/client-runtime/src/connection/projectIconSource.ts, split freshness from display. Add readCachedProjectIcon(environmentId, projectId, revision): { source: string | null; fresh: boolean } | undefined, which ignores the TTL for display; or keep peek and add a stale variant. In apps/mobile/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx and apps/web/src/components/ProjectFavicon.tsx: (a) seed artwork state lazily from the cache (useState(() => hit ? { key: requestKey, source } : null)). (b) In the effect, on a cache hit, latch it with setArtwork(prev => prev?.key === requestKey && prev.source === hit.source ? prev : { key: requestKey, source: hit.source }) and refetch only when the entry is not fresh (stale-while-revalidate: keep showing the old value until the RPC answers). (c) Derive display from artwork state first, then the cache. Display then no longer depends on Date.now() at render time, and LRU eviction cannot blank a mounted row. The effect logic is duplicated verbatim in both apps, and client-runtime has no React dependency. So either move the state machine into a small framework-free helper in client-runtime (e.g. resolveProjectIconDisplay plus a subscribe API consumed with useSyncExternalStore), or accept two thin hooks that call the same helpers. Tests: in apps/web/src/components/ProjectFavicon.browser.tsx, render instance A to fill the cache, mount instance B, mock Date.now or use vi.setSystemTime to pass PROJECT_ICON_TTL_MS + 1, re-render B with an unrelated prop change, and assert the img src is still the data URL. Assert readIcon is called at most once more if stale-while-revalidate refetches. Add a client-runtime unit test for the stale read. For (2), call clearAllProjectIconCaches() from the mobile hosted account teardown path (hostedHubController sign-out or expireSession handling and SettingsHubRouteScreen clearLocalHubState), or better from the shared client-runtime hosted teardown so web and mobile cannot diverge, and add a test in the mobile hosted teardown suite. Validate with focused vitest on client-runtime projectIconSource.test.ts, the web ProjectFavicon browser test, and the mobile environmentActions and deviceCache tests.

Done#246 Direct connections wait for full SQLite snapshot hydration (DB open + 1+N sequential reads + full JSON decode)

mobile-boot:snapshot-hydration-barrier-and-n-plus-1 · original impact Low, effort M · Waterfall

Current state

Confirmed DONE. Both proposal parts are on main. Part 1 (60633eff3 #710, refined in 1d55a4132): hydration reads every row with one ORDER BY updated_at DESC query, skips environments that already have state before decoding, and commits in batches of about 64 KiB with a yield between batches. Part 2 (1d55a4132): the startup barrier now has a direct-ready stage, marked right after catalog hydration, and driver.start() runs at that stage. The SQLite open, roster read and decode no longer sit in front of the direct pre-flight. Only the hosted primary still waits for full hydration (admitPrimaryConnection plus a deferred replay). I checked the live-wins assumption the original verifier worried about. Connection registration, the sink and the supervisor write threads-store environment state only from live shell, thread-detail or event data, so the risk of empty state blocking the cache is unfounded. The only gap is a narrow partial-state race, covered in fixDefects. It is low severity and transient.

Evidence
  • apps/mobile/src/runtime/bootstrap.ts:113-139 markDirectReady() runs right after registry.catalog.waitForHydration(). The persistence modules load in parallel, and initializeMobileSnapshotPersistence (SQLite open, roster, rows, decode) runs after the direct stage is open.
  • apps/mobile/src/runtime/bootstrap.ts:187-200 driver.start() is gated by runAfterDirectReady. Only releaseDeferredPrimaryConnection is gated by runAfterHydration. admitPrimaryConnection is wired to isHydrated() at line 57.
  • apps/mobile/src/runtime/startupBarrier.ts:63-128 Two-stage barrier with a generation guard. If hydration fails before markDirectReady, both stages open. Tests cover this at startupBarrier.test.ts:70-112.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:600-614,660-664 createPrimaryConnection returns null and sets a deferred flag while unhydrated. releaseDeferredPrimaryConnection then replays connectPrimary. In supervision.ts:894-896, connectPrimary treats null as a no-op, so nothing is lost.
  • apps/mobile/src/persistence/snapshotDb.ts:151-170 loadEnvironmentSnapshots does a single SELECT environment_id, schema_version, payload, updated_at ORDER BY updated_at DESC. This is proposal part 1 verbatim.
  • apps/mobile/src/persistence/environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:369-458 hydrate() replaces the old stats query plus N per-row SELECTs (f1be4abc7 version) with one read. It skips decode for environments that already have state (line 444) and commits in 64 KiB batches with a yield (lines 63, 428-431). discardRow checks the written map, so a row a live capture replaced is not deleted (lines 402-406).
  • apps/mobile/src/persistence/environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:501-507,549-550 Projection marks that arrive before the runtime exists are buffered and replayed, so an early live snapshot is still captured to disk.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:3792-3806,3935-3955 The live-wins guard returns state unchanged when an environment already has state, and it is applied again per entry at batched commit.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:536-551 Thread-detail subscriptions attach as soon as a connection is registered. isMissingFromShell is false before any shell baseline. This means a bounded thread-window snapshot can land before the shell snapshot (the basis of the minor race in fixDefects).
  • packages/client-runtime/src/state/threads/store.ts:2237-2249,2388-2405 syncServerThreadDetail and syncServerThreadWindow create environment state from initialEnvironmentState with bootstrapComplete=false and no cache stamp. Both the hydrate() hasState skip and the store guard treat that as live.
  • apps/mobile/src/persistence/environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:565-582 listEnvironmentCacheStorage (Settings > device cache) still does stats plus one loadEnvironmentSnapshot and a full decode per environment. It is not on the boot path.
Defects in the shipped fix

No material defect. One narrow, transient race found, plus a few small leftovers. (1) Partial live state blocks the cache. After 1d55a4132 the direct connection can register before the cache commits. A thread-detail subscription retained at cold start (for example a deep link into ThreadDetailScreen, which retains at ThreadDetailScreen.tsx:434) attaches immediately (supervision.ts:549-551). If its window snapshot lands before both the shell snapshot and the cache batch, syncServerThreadWindow creates a one-thread environment state with bootstrapComplete=false (store.ts:2237-2249). hydrate() then skips that environment (environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:444), as does the store guard at store.ts:3799-3806. The environment's list shows only that thread until the live shell snapshot arrives, usually milliseconds later on the same socket. It stays that way only if the shell subscription fails. Before the fix this ordering could not happen. (2) The auditor's leftovers stand, but they now delay only cache paint and hosted-primary admission. Open, PRAGMA WAL and DDL are three sequential native calls (snapshotDb.ts:131-133), and the roster and row reads are sequential (environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:371,394). The single query returns every payload, up to 16 MiB, including rows that live data already owns. (3) The Settings device-cache screen still has the old N+1 plus full-decode pattern (environmentSnapshotPersistence.ts:565-582). It is off the launch path.
