Done#247 Metro inlineRequires is off, so every imported module is evaluated eagerly

mobile-boot:metro-inline-requires-off · original impact Low, effort M · Build config

Current state

Commit 1b8bfd183 turns on Metro inline requires through getTransformOptions (experimentalImportSupport and inlineRequires both true; React and React Native are in nonInlinedRequires). An @ryco/* ESM resolver shim keeps the bundle's module set the same. The import-time configurators stay eager through bare imports in index.ts. The commit message gives release-build measurements: 2,331 -> 1,257 modules evaluated by splash hide, and 283 -> 255 ms median from bundle start to splash hide. I looked for other side effects at module scope in apps/mobile/src. App.tsx has two (preventAutoHideAsync and applyResolvedAppColorScheme), and they run when App is evaluated, which index.ts forces right away through registerRootComponent. hostedHub/runtime.ts registers the trust source and the primary connection factory at module scope. Since #710, which landed before 1b8bfd183, that module has been loaded lazily on purpose, and both of its consumers handle a missing registration: primaryConnectionFactory returns null, and useAuthoritativeNodeTrust handles a null source with a subscription. Deferring them further therefore changes nothing. Barrel re-exports (export *) still evaluate eagerly, as the original verifier noted. That limits how much more inlining can save, but it is not a gap in the fix. Nothing has changed metro.config.js or index.ts since the commit.

Evidence
  • apps/mobile/metro.config.js:86-101 NON_INLINED_REQUIRES (React, react/jsx-runtime, react-compiler-runtime, react-native) plus the getTransformOptions override: inlineRequires true, experimentalImportSupport true.
  • apps/mobile/metro.config.js:48-55 @ryco/* specifiers are resolved with isESMImport:true so the import-only export conditions still match when requires are inlined.
  • apps/mobile/index.ts:1-7 Bare imports of polyfills, threadsRuntime and hostedHub/state come before App, so those registrations stay eager.
  • apps/mobile/src/App.tsx:32-39 Module-scope splash and color-scheme calls run when App is evaluated, which registerRootComponent triggers immediately. Unaffected.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/runtime.ts:66-86 Module-scope configureAuthoritativeNodeTrustSource and installHostedPrimaryConnectionFactory. runtime.ts is already lazy by design (#710), and its consumers tolerate the registrations being absent.
  • apps/mobile/src/hostedHub/primaryConnectionFactory.ts:30-35 Returns null until the hosted runtime loads, which matches the documented pre-load behaviour.
  • apps/mobile/src/features/home/useAuthoritativeNodeTrust.ts:53-73 Handles a null trust source and subscribes for late registration.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/metroStartupConfig.test.ts:34-78 Tests pin the inline-requires options, the ESM resolution of @ryco/* packages, and the order of the bare imports in index.ts.

Partial#248 Effect and @ryco/contracts root barrels pull unused modules into the startup graph, and tree shaking is off

mobile-boot:barrels-and-no-tree-shaking · original impact Low, effort M · Bundle size WP14B

First-pass audit said PARTIAL; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

PARTIAL is right, but one piece of the auditor's evidence is wrong. The finding said the root `effect` and `@ryco/contracts` barrels sit in the mobile startup graph and tree shaking is off. Fixed: the root barrels are gone. There are 0 non-test value imports, down from 3/24/64/14 files in mobile/client-runtime/contracts/shared. A lint rule guards both roots, and e8b023912 measured 2993 -> 2981 bundle modules. Still open: Expo tree shaking is unset, and the `effect/rpc` and `effect/reactivity` sub-barrels remain. I reproduced the auditor's estimate that switching both to deep imports drops 47 effect modules (about 406 KiB raw, about 300 KB once JSDoc is stripped). The auditor was wrong that contracts `rpc.ts` is out of the launch graph. A walker that copies mobileStartupImports.test.ts finds this chain: index.ts -> src/state/threadsRuntime.ts -> client-runtime state/threads/index.ts -> threadFork.ts -> rpc/protocol.ts -> contracts/rpc.ts. Chat forking (#708) added it after the report. Launch-reachable contracts are 56 modules / 890 KiB, not 51 / 707 KiB. Even without that chain, rpc.ts runs when the first environment connects (environmentDriver.ts:333 builds the WsTransport). That pulls in 48 contracts modules / 736 KiB, so lazy schema construction is still a valid low-priority idea, not a moot one.

Evidence
  • vite.config.ts:8 EFFECT_ROOT_IMPORT and CONTRACTS_ROOT_IMPORT (line 19, allowTypeImports) are no-restricted-imports paths. They apply to client-runtime src (125), contracts/shared src (137) and apps/mobile (167). Neither `effect/rpc` nor `effect/reactivity` is restricted.
  • apps/mobile/src/state/preferencesStore.ts:1 Now `import * as Schema from "effect/Schema"`. `git grep 'from "effect";'` finds 0 non-test hits in mobile, client-runtime, contracts and shared. The only remaining hit is packages/client-runtime/test/fakeWebSocket.ts:1, a test helper. Codemod landed in 60633eff3 (#710).
  • apps/mobile/src/features/projects/projectActions.ts:1 One of 5 inline-type-only `import { type X } from "@ryco/contracts"` declarations. babel-preset-expo runs @babel/plugin-transform-typescript with onlyRemoveTypeImports=false (default), so isAllSpecifiersElided removes the whole declaration. No side-effect import of the root is left, so no defect. I found no value imports of either root.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/protocol.ts:8 `import { RpcClient, RpcSerialization } from "effect/rpc"` loads dist/rpc/index.js, which re-exports RpcServer, RpcTest, RpcWorker and others with `export * as`. wsTransport.ts:10 does the same.

That index re-exports AtomHttpApi -> http-api/HttpApiClient and the http server stack. Closure over effect@4.0.2 dist: 235 modules / 4,460 KiB now, 188 / 4,054 KiB with deep imports, 47 fewer. Deep-importing only rpc saves 7 and only reactivity saves 13; most of the saving needs both, because RpcServer/http server and AtomHttpApi/http-api share most of the dropped modules. @effect/atom-react already uses deep reactivity imports; its only barrel reference is in JSDoc.

So contracts/rpc.ts and the effect/rpc barrel are in the static launch graph, contrary to the auditor. Added by 1cc2ab13b (#708, chat forking), after the report. With inline requires the protocol import is deferred to first use, at line 593 inside a function.
  • apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:333 Every saved environment connection runs createWsRpcClient(new WsTransport(...)), which evaluates protocol.ts -> @ryco/contracts/rpc (rpc closure: 48 of 70 contracts modules, 736 KiB) and the effect/rpc barrel. On a paired device this happens right after launch, inline requires or not.

A barrel's `export * as` re-exports are top-level references, so evaluating a barrel still evaluates every re-exported module. No EXPO_UNSTABLE_METRO_OPTIMIZE_GRAPH or EXPO_UNSTABLE_TREE_SHAKING appears anywhere in the repo or in apps/mobile/eas.json build env. @expo/cli metroOptions.js:78-84 still gates tree shaking on both. EAS dashboard env for `environment: production` cannot be checked from the repo.

It never asserts that packages/contracts/src/index.ts is unreachable, so the lint rule is the only guard. Its header still says 'no inline requires', which has been stale since 1b8bfd183.
Remaining

1. Effect sub-barrels: packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/protocol.ts:8 and wsTransport.ts:10 import the `effect/rpc` index. About 10 non-test files import the `effect/reactivity` index: client-runtime connection/atomRpcClient.ts:3, rpc/atomRegistry.ts:1, rpc/invalidation.ts:6, rpc/keyedQuery.ts:2, rpc/requestLatencyState.ts:1, rpc/serverState.ts:12, rpc/wsConnectionState.ts:2, sourceControlDiscoveryState.ts:2, and mobile src/rpc/checkpointDiffAtoms.ts:14 and src/features/newTask/useNewTaskRepository.ts:2. Those modules evaluate when the reactivity index is first touched (module-scope Atom.make in launch state modules) and at first RPC connection. vite.config.ts does not restrict either sub-barrel. 2. Proposal part 3, the Expo tree-shaking release-build experiment (EXPO_UNSTABLE_METRO_OPTIMIZE_GRAPH=1 + EXPO_UNSTABLE_TREE_SHAKING=1), was never run. Tree shaking would also prune the sub-barrels above, since effect is ESM with sideEffects limited to the JIT enable file. 3. It is not moot: contracts/rpc.ts is statically reachable at launch through threadFork.ts:25 and is evaluated at the first environment connection. No functional defects in the implemented fixes. The lint rules correctly allow type-only imports of the contracts root: inline `type` specifiers are fully elided by babel-preset-expo (onlyRemoveTypeImports=false), so no side-effect import survives. The startup guard test has two gaps. It cannot see effect barrels because resolveSpecifier collapses `effect/...` to `pkg:effect`, and it does not assert that packages/contracts/src/index.ts is unreachable, so only the lint rule protects against a regression. Its header comment ('no inline requires') is stale since 1b8bfd183. The auditor's measurement that rpc.ts is out of the launch graph was wrong; the threadFork.ts:25 chain added by #708 puts it back in.

A. Effect sub-barrel codemod (S, low risk). In packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/protocol.ts:8, replace the import with `import * as RpcClient from "effect/rpc/RpcClient"` and `import * as RpcSerialization from "effect/rpc/RpcSerialization"`. Do the same in wsTransport.ts:10. In each reactivity importer, use `import * as Atom from "effect/reactivity/Atom"`, `import * as AtomRegistry from "effect/reactivity/AtomRegistry"`, `import * as AtomRpc from "effect/reactivity/AtomRpc"` and `import * as Reactivity from "effect/reactivity/Reactivity"`. Then add a test asserting staticGraph('index.ts') contains no `pkg:effect`, no `pkg:effect/<barrel-dir>` and no packages/contracts/src/index.ts. Fix the stale 'no inline requires' header. Verify with focused checks: vitest on that test file and oxlint on the touched files. In a scratch worktree outside the repo, compare `npx expo export --platform ios` module count and Hermes bytecode size before and after; expect about 47 fewer modules. B. Tree-shaking trial (M, experiment only). In a scratch worktree, build an iOS release export with EXPO_UNSTABLE_METRO_OPTIMIZE_GRAPH=1 EXPO_UNSTABLE_TREE_SHAKING=1. Compare bundle modules and bytecode size, plus the 1b8bfd183 launch harness (modules evaluated by splash hide, bundle start -> first App commit, splash hide), over 2x10 alternating release-simulator launches. Check that the metro.config.js resolver override forcing isESMImport for @ryco/* and CJS-resolved packages (tabler) still behave, and that the threadsRuntime/hostedHub bare-import registrations survive. Adopt only if the gain is measurable, by setting the env in apps/mobile/eas.json build.{preview,production}.env. C. Optional (M, medium risk). Defer construction of rarely used RPC families in packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts, for example agentControl, atlassian, automationCentre, cliProxy, codexResetCredits, changeRequestReview, acpRegistry and sessionImport payloads, using Schema.suspend. Done#250 Provider event logging is always on, has no off switch and no total-size budget, and nothing in the app reads it (4.1 GB on disk; Diagnostics reads a file that never exists)

gap-logging-io:event-logging-always-on-unbounded · original impact High, effort M · Memory

Current state

Confirmed DONE. 60633eff3 (#710), which is also in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3, delivers every part of the proposal. It adds the providerEventLogs off/lifecycle/full setting with a RYCO_PROVIDER_EVENT_LOGS override; env=off returns NoOpProviderEventLoggers. The default is full in dev and lifecycle when packaged, and changes hot-apply through serverSettings.streamChanges. An age plus total-size sweep runs at boot and then hourly for both logs/provider (30 d, 512 MiB) and logs/terminals (90 d, 256 MiB). Rotated backups are gzipped through zlib. Diagnostics now reads the newest canonical per-thread files instead of the nonexistent events.log. I found no production path that bypasses the mode: no driver passes nativeEventLogPath, so the adapters' own fallback loggers (default mode full) are test-only. ProviderService takes eventLoggers.canonical. The field state matches the code: ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/provider is now 505 MiB in 170 files, down from 4.1 GB in 689. Every rotated .log.N file dates from Oct 10-12, before the update. Files written since are 1-500 KB and contain only lifecycle types (session.*, task.*, turn.*, claude/system/init, claude/result/success), with no deltas. Out-of-scope sibling, not part of this finding: a CLI node installed as a launchd/systemd service sends all console output to logs/service.log in append mode with no rotation (nodeService.ts:141-144, :172-173). That file is unbounded on long-running nodes. In web mode server.log is still never written, which is already tracked as bug-table item 506.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderEventLoggers.ts:154-163 The retention sweep runs for both targets, then repeats every hour (Schedule.spaced(1h)) in a forkScoped fiber. With env=off the layer returns NoOpProviderEventLoggers, so drivers pass no logger.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderEventLoggers.ts:99-105 Mode resolution: env override, then the setting, then the build default (full when devUrl is set, otherwise lifecycle). It is re-resolved on every settings change (:170-183) and read on every write (:186).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderEventLoggers.ts:121-139 logs/provider: 30 d plus 512 MiB. logs/terminals: 90 d plus 256 MiB. Terminal history files are full rewrites capped at 2 MiB (Manager.ts:82, :1264, :1383), so sweeping one only drops old scrollback.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:66-123 sweepLogDirectory: an age pass, then unlink oldest-by-mtime until the total fits maxTotalBytes (:98-110). It never fails (catch at :112-116), so the hourly repeat cannot die.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:430-437 writeRecord checks the mode before resolveWriter, so mode off (or a filtered record) creates no file and does no I/O. The only cost is the mode check.
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.ts:88-160 The lifecycle policy: a canonical type allowlist, native lifecycle-name matching, and exclusion of delta/progress/stream_event/token/item records.
  • packages/shared/src/logging.ts:290-318 Rotation gzips the .1 backup through compressBackup (:382-392, zlib pipeline, tmp file then rename, falls back to the uncompressed backup on failure).
  • apps/server/src/diagnostics/Layers/Diagnostics.ts:735-790 readProviderEventFailures reads the 128 KiB tail of the 8 newest current canonical <thread>.log files and parses runtime.error, failed turns and errored exits. Called at :897.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.ts:1920-1926 The adapter fallback makeEventNdjsonLogger (default mode full, no compression) runs only when nativeEventLogPath is passed. git grep finds no non-test caller that passes it, so the mode cannot be bypassed in production.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:381 The canonical logger comes from the shared ProviderEventLoggers, so the same mode and retention apply.
  • ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/provider (runtime, outside repo) 505 MiB in 170 files, under the 512 MiB budget (4.1 GB in 689 files at report time). Rotated .log.N files all predate the update. A current thread holds 305 KB canonical / 148 KB native with only lifecycle record types.
  • apps/server/src/service/nodeService.ts:141-144 Out-of-scope sibling: the launchd StandardOutPath/StandardErrorPath and the systemd append: (:172-173) send all CLI-node console output to logs/service.log with no rotation.
Defects in the shipped fix

None that reopen the finding. Residuals, all minor or out of scope: (1) The packaged default is lifecycle, not off. The proposal allowed this, and the field data shows delta volume is gone. (2) If off is set through the setting instead of the env var, adapters still call write(), which returns after a mode check. Cost is negligible. (3) There is no web UI control for providerEventLogs; it is reachable only through settings.json or the env var, as documented in docs/observability.md:61-64. (4) ServerDiagnostics.observability.providerEventLogPath still reports the nonexistent provider/events.log path, but the web UI does not display it. (5) Sibling outside this finding: the CLI service's logs/service.log is unbounded, and web-mode server.log is unwritten (bug-table item 506).

Done#251 Canonical log embeds the full native message in every runtime event (11x the native bytes; 87-95% of the canonical file is a copy of the native log)

gap-logging-io:canonical-raw-duplication · original impact Medium, effort S · Other WP16

Current state

DONE holds for the cost the finding describes. Since 60633eff3 (#710), serializeProviderEventLogRecord swaps raw for a reference ({source, method, messageType, nativeId}) on every non-native record before JSON.stringify. The canonical log therefore no longer copies the SDK message on each fan-out event, whatever the provider or event type. Live logs confirm it: canonical files in ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/provider from Oct 14-15 have 0 lines with raw.payload, and raw is 7-16% of bytes, down from 43% typical and 87-95% in bursts. The large-workflow guard test exists. The auditor's line 'nothing is lost' is wrong for the packaged default 'lifecycle' mode. The native lifecycle filter drops most native messages that canonical lifecycle records point to, so on real threads 64-89% of canonical nativeIds point to native records that were never written, and that raw detail is now in neither log. This is a small diagnostics defect, not a performance gap.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.ts:327-346 serializeProviderEventLogRecord: for stream != native it uses withRawReference(record) before JSON.stringify. The over-cap walk and the replacer also run on the stripped value, so raw.payload is never visited.
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.ts:414-428 withRawReference keeps source, method, messageType and nativeId = payload.uuid ?? payload.id. It applies no matter what the log mode is or whether the native log keeps that message.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:358-365 The logger's serialize() calls the shared serializer. writeRecord (430-455) knows the mode but does not pass it on. The canonical delta-run record (providerEventLogRecords.ts:278-289) drops raw entirely.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderService.ts:621-648 publishRuntimeEvent writes the canonical log, then publishes to the PubSub. This is the only canonical write site. Runtime events are never serialized anywhere else; Diagnostics.ts:513-550 reads canonical lines without using raw.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderEventLoggers.ts:99-104 Default mode is 'full' in development and 'lifecycle' when packaged. Native and canonical share one mode (185-197).
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.ts:132-153 The native lifecycle filter keeps a method only if it matches init/start/started/end/complete/result/error and similar. It drops claude/system/status, claude/system/task_notification, claude/system/background_tasks_changed and claude/system/permission_denied, yet these back canonical lifecycle records (session.state.changed, task.completed, subagent.completed, task.started, tool.denied).
  • ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/provider (live user data, not repo) Recent canonical files: 0 raw.payload lines, raw is 6.6-15.8% of bytes. nativeId resolution against the matching .native.log: thread 803309ce 52 found / 433 missing, 76b51201 38/211, 08be3c64 54/85. The misses are almost all session.state.changed<-claude/system/status and task.completed<-claude/system/task_notification.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:2106-2140 The Claude native record id is message.uuid, so canonical nativeId matches it in full mode. In full mode nothing dangles: thinking_tokens and ping, the only native records full mode drops, produce no canonical events (ClaudeAdapter.ts:4534).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:3446-3462 Synthetic turn.started has payload {} and raw.payload {openedBy}, and no native record exists for it. The canonical log now loses whether a turn was opened by a wake signal or by a prompt. The claude.sdk.permission raw payloads (5280-5495) repeat what the canonical payload already holds, so dropping them loses nothing.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.ts:606-625 The Codex canonical eventId equals the native envelope id, so Codex records can be matched by eventId even though nativeId is usually missing (params have no uuid/id). This weakens the auditor's nativeId nit.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:332-334 rawPayloadThreadId is still the only runtime reader of raw.payload. It is unaffected because stripping happens only in the log serializer.
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.test.ts:21-56 Guard test: a 400-member workflow task.progress gives a canonical line under 2,048 bytes, raw becomes the reference, and the native stream keeps the message. It tests only the serializer, not the adapter-to-logger path, and has no lifecycle-mode case.
Defects in the shipped fix

Not a performance defect, but a diagnostics regression in the shipped default. In 'lifecycle' mode, the default for packaged builds, withRawReference (providerEventLogRecords.ts:414-428) strips raw.payload from canonical lifecycle records whose native message the native lifecycle filter (providerEventLogRecords.ts:132-153) does not write: claude/system/status, task_notification, background_tasks_changed and permission_denied. That raw detail (for example permissionMode on status, output_file on task_notification) is therefore in neither log, and on live threads 64-89% of canonical nativeIds point to native records that do not exist. This contradicts the module comment (lines 13-15) and the auditor's 'nothing is lost'. Separately, synthetic raw payloads that never had a native record are now dropped in every mode. The only one carrying unique data is the turn.started {openedBy} at ClaudeAdapter.ts:3458-3462. Minor: the guard test is serializer-only and has no lifecycle case.

Implementation sketch

Keep exactly one copy of each raw message in whichever log keeps it. (1) Pass the mode from EventNdjsonLogger.writeRecord through enqueueRecord and serialize into serializeProviderEventLogRecord(stream, record, mode). (2) In withRawReference, keep raw.payload when mode === 'lifecycle' and the native filter would drop raw.method. Reuse the existing policy: factor the name test out of isLifecycleProviderEventRecord into isLifecycleNativeName(name), and keep the payload when !isLifecycleNativeName(raw.method). Lifecycle records are low volume and task.progress is not lifecycle, so the burst cost does not come back; capping and redaction still apply. Do this only where the native message exists; for synthetic raw sources, also keep a raw.payload that is a small flat record (for example at most 4 own keys, all primitives, checked without stringifying), which saves {openedBy}. Alternatively, move openedBy into the turn.started payload. (3) Tests in providerEventLogRecords.test.ts: lifecycle + canonical task.completed with raw.method 'claude/system/task_notification' keeps payload; lifecycle + session.configured from 'claude/system/init' keeps only the reference; full mode always keeps only the reference; the existing 400-member guard still passes. Optionally add one EventNdjsonLogger test that writes a lifecycle-mode record and checks the file line.

Done#252 Native log writes one ~700 B envelope per streaming delta that carries ~9 B of content (1.2% useful); deltas are 14-58% of native bytes

gap-logging-io:native-delta-coalescing · original impact Medium, effort S · Other WP16

Current state

Confirmed DONE for the Claude and Codex scope. Commit 60633eff3 (#710) added per-writer delta-run coalescing to EventNdjsonLogger on the native and canonical streams. Consecutive deltas of one content stream become one {kind:'delta-run', count, chars, firstAt, lastAt, text} record, closed on a key change, any non-delta record, the 8192-char cap, a run age of 1 s, or close. thinking_tokens and ping are dropped before the run logic, so they do not break runs. The packaged default is lifecycle, which writes no deltas at all. Real logs agree: in the dev log, 23 Codex agentMessage deltas became one ~540 B native record and one canonical record, and the packaged userdata logs from Oct 15 contain no delta records. The code is correct: ordering is preserved, the run is flushed before every non-delta record, idle eviction skips open runs, close drains runs, and secret redaction runs on the concatenated text. What the auditor missed: coalescing only recognises Claude and Codex native shapes. OpenCode, Copilot and the ACP family (Cursor, Grok, registry agents) still write one native record per streaming delta in full mode. ACP writes three per chunk: protocol raw, protocol decoded, and the adapter's session/update. This only matters in full mode (the dev default or an opt-in) and was outside the finding's measured scope.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:398 appendDelta accumulates parts per key. On a key change or the 8192 cap (PROVIDER_EVENT_LOG_STRING_CAP) it calls closeRun (:379).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:430 writeRecord applies the mode filter first, so noise records never close a run. It coalesces only in full mode (:447-451). Any other record closes the open run before being enqueued (:453-454), which keeps file order.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:462 flushWriter closes runs at least DELTA_RUN_MAX_AGE_MS (1 s, :138) old or when closing. Otherwise it reschedules (:475, :519). evictIdleWriters skips writers with an open run (:562), and closeWriter drains late runs (:532).
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.ts:195 extractProviderEventDelta handles canonical *.delta for all providers. Its native branch (:221-249) keys on envelope.method and recognises only Claude content_block_delta (:225) and Codex */delta|*Delta (:235).
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.ts:266 providerEventDeltaRunRecord writes only identifying fields, so the per-delta id/uuid, createdAt, providerThreadId/session_id and full payload are gone. For Codex, the duplicated textDelta and payload.delta go too.
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.ts:156 NATIVE_NOISE_NAMES drops claude/system/thinking_tokens and claude/stream_event/ping (check at :171-174). In lifecycle mode NATIVE_STREAMING_NAME (:134) excludes delta and stream_event names. The auditor cited :160 for this; the correct line is :134.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderEventLoggers.ts:104 Mode resolution is env override, then the setting, then the build default: full in dev, lifecycle when packaged. packages/contracts/src/settings.ts:711 defaults providerEventLogs to null.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:2106 logNativeSdkMessage is now a plain function (no span) and no longer writes createdAt. The payload goes through the per-message cached secretRedactor (:2137), which is shared with the canonical raw.payload.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.test.ts:358 A test covers Claude native runs split by content_block_stop and by index or type, and a canonical content.delta run of 3. providerEventLogRecords.test.ts:147 covers key extraction for Codex native and canonical.
  • local:~/.ryco/dev/logs/provider/5176f8dd-45c3-416d-bc39-e3ebaea44d79.native.log:5548 A real post-fix record: a Codex item/agentMessage/delta run with count 23 (105 chars) in one line, matched by one CANON delta-run (count 23) in the canonical file. The packaged ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/provider files from Oct 15 contain only lifecycle records.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/OpenCodeAdapter.ts:1500 Uncovered caller: every OpenCode SSE event, including each message.part.delta, is written as {observedAt, event:{type, payload:event}}. It has no `method`, so extractProviderEventDelta returns undefined and every delta stays its own record in full mode.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CopilotAdapter.ts:123 Uncovered caller: logCopilotNativeEvent (an Effect.fn span) writes every SessionEvent, including assistant.message_delta and assistant.reasoning_delta (called at :180 and :225). Those are not coalesced, and the per-event span is created even in lifecycle mode (tracked separately under finding 259, logger-effect-spans).
Defects in the shipped fix

No correctness defects in the implemented coalescer. The auditor's 'No real defects' missed one coverage gap. The native branch of extractProviderEventDelta (providerEventLogRecords.ts:221-249) only matches Claude content_block_delta and Codex */delta methods. OpenCode message.part.delta (OpenCodeAdapter.ts:1500), Copilot assistant.message_delta and assistant.reasoning_delta (CopilotAdapter.ts:123/180/225), and ACP chunks (Cursor, Grok, registry) are still one native record per delta in full mode. ACP is triple-logged: protocol raw plus protocol decoded (AcpNativeLogging.ts:60-73, effect-acp protocol.ts:424-455) plus the adapter's session/update (AcpAdapter.ts:717, CursorAdapter.ts:930). The canonical stream is coalesced for every provider. Minor items: (1) Non-delta Claude native records still duplicate id with payload.uuid and providerThreadId with session_id (ClaudeAdapter.ts:2117-2137). ACP native envelopes still carry createdAt equal to observedAt (AcpNativeLogging.ts:25, CursorAdapter.ts:411, AcpAdapter.ts:276). (2) In lifecycle mode, adapters still build and redact a native envelope per delta before the logger drops it. This is cheap for Claude (cached redactor) but uncached for ACP protocol frames and Copilot events. (3) The auditor cited :160 for the lifecycle streaming-name exclusion; it is NATIVE_STREAMING_NAME at :134.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Done#253 Expected failures in hot retry loops are logged as full stack traces and dominate server-child.log and desktop-main.log

gap-logging-io:retry-loop-log-storms · original impact Medium, effort S · Reliability WP07A

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. Status stays DONE, but two auditor claims need correcting. (a) 'VCS remote status refresh failed now goes through logOnceEvery' implies it is deduped, but with the loop's existing 8/15-min backoff the 5-min limiter window passes on every steady failure, so it still logs a full cause each time (37 of 40 in simulation). The auditor's 'fixDefects: None seen' misses this. (b) The renderer HostedReconnectPolicy backoff was not part of the fix: it existed since a8b64ed64 (#695, 2026-10-09), before the report commit f1be4abc7. The Sep 5 storm predates it. The auditor also did not list the latent same-pattern retry loggers (UsageLimitRecovery 30s full stack, CompletionReturnDelivery 2s, chats root probe 30s) or that prepareTransport still rejects over IPC.

Current state

The two log storms that made up 83% of the measured volume and the Electron IPC error-stack storm are gone. SourceControlProviderError: the real cause (deleted worktree directories re-probed on every read) is fixed by recording them once via worktree.checkout.remove (reason 'missing') and skipping removed rows; any other failure is now logged per worktree through logOnceEvery. History recovery: per-thread backoff, with one WARN per failure streak. activate-transport: returns a typed {ok:false} and the desktop log is async. One defect the auditor missed: the 'VCS remote status refresh failed' source (10% of the measured volume) barely shrinks in steady state. The loop's own backoff (8 then 15 minutes) is longer than the limiter's 5-minute window, and the limiter logs every occurrence that arrives after a full window in full. A simulation gives 37 of 40 failures still logged, almost all with the full cause. Latent retry loggers that never showed in the measured logs also still bypass the helper. All leftovers are low value.

Evidence
  • packages/shared/src/logOnceEvery.ts:45-73 admit(): an occurrence after the window with entry.skipped === 0 returns LOG (full cause). So a key that recurs at intervals >= window is always logged in full, never summarised.
  • apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:54-55,164-177,557-565 Failure backoff is 30s*2^(n-1), capped at 15 min (already present at f1be4abc7). The logOnceEvery call uses the default 5-min window. Simulating the real LogOnceEveryLimiter on this delay sequence: 37 of 40 failures logged (0s log, 450s summary, then a full log at 930s, 1830s, 2730s, ...). Steady state is one full-cause WARN per cwd per 15 min, the same as before #710.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:148,173-207 Root-cause fix confirmed: on resolve failure, ENOENT on the checkout (with its parent present) is recorded once as worktree.checkout.remove reason 'missing', and checkoutRemovedAt rows return early. A missing parent (an unmounted volume) still fails, and that failure is rate-limited per worktree by ignoreCauseLogOnceEvery (ws/context.ts:325-330,512,551). Since linkRefresh/discovery timestamps are only set after resolve succeeds, failing worktrees are re-probed on every sweep (5s debounce), which the limiter then dedupes well.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:3503-3584 History recovery: per-thread HistoryRecoveryState with exponential spacing (historyRecoveryPolicy.ts: 30s to 15 min). The WARN with Cause.pretty fires only when previousFailures === 0, then 'failed again' at Debug and an Info line on recovery. This does remove the 37% source regardless of cadence.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3831-3862 activate-transport validates the input and never rejects; it returns {ok:false, reason}, and the desktop log keeps one line per distinct message. Desktop logs now go through AsyncRotatingFileSink (main.ts:1489-1492,1890-1899), so they are no longer sync writes.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:3832-3834 prepareTransport (and reportConnection at ~3895) still throw over IPC, so Electron prints 'Error occurred in handler' with a stack for each rejected attempt. The renderer backoff bounds the rate (at most about 1/min in steady state).
  • apps/web/src/platform/desktopWorkspaceSocket.ts:74-86,206-217 The renderer treats ok:false as a 4401 close. The HostedReconnectPolicy backoff was not added by the perf fixes: it landed in a8b64ed64 (#695, 2026-10-09), before the report commit. The 815/min storm (Sep 5) predates it.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendStartup.ts:211-254 BackendOutputCapture (49d90708a) stops copying backend stdout/stderr into the desktop log once the backend serves. Only a 16 KB in-memory tail is kept.
  • apps/server/src/serverLogger.ts:107-124 Desktop mode adds a batched async logfmt file sink, but Logger.consolePretty() still formats every line to the stdout pipe, which Electron main now just tails into memory. So lines are double-formatted (the optional proposal item).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/UsageLimitRecovery.ts:328-335,382 Latent same-pattern loop that does not use the helper: a full Cause.pretty WARN every 30s (SWEEP_INTERVAL) while the sweep keeps failing.
  • apps/server/src/agentControl/Layers/CompletionReturnDelivery.ts:1031-1032 Latent: 'Completion return recovery will retry.' WARN every 2s on persistent scan failure (no cause, about 43k lines/day if stuck).
  • apps/server/src/project/chatFolders.ts:314,376,549 Latent: 'chats root probe failed' WARN with cause on every 30s retry while the git probe fails.
Remaining

None of the measured storms remain. Leftovers (all low value): (1) Fix defect: VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:557-565 dedupe barely works in steady state, because the loop's 8/15-min backoff exceeds the 5-min window, so each steady failure still logs a full cause. (2) Latent retry loops that bypass logOnceEvery: UsageLimitRecovery.ts:332 (30s, full stack), CompletionReturnDelivery.ts:1031 (2s) and chatFolders.ts:314/376 (30s). (3) desktop main.ts:3832 prepareTransport and reportConnection still reject over IPC (Electron prints a stack per rejection; rate bounded by the renderer backoff). (4) serverLogger.ts:110-111 still runs consolePretty to stdout in desktop mode, alongside the logfmt file sink.

Defects in the shipped fix

VCS remote status refresh: logOnceEvery({key:'vcs.remoteStatusRefresh:'+cwd}) at apps/server/src/vcs/VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:559 uses the default 5-min window. The loop's backoff reaches 480s and then 900s (VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:54-55,164-177). LogOnceEveryLimiter.admit (packages/shared/src/logOnceEvery.ts:61-71) treats every occurrence after a full quiet window as a new burst and logs it in full. A simulation with the real limiter: 37 of 40 consecutive failures emit a line, nearly all as full-cause WARNs. Steady state is unchanged from before #710: one full stack per failing cwd every 15 min. The auditor's claim that this source is deduped holds only for poller churn (re-subscriptions resetting the backoff within 5 min). No correctness bugs found in the other parts of the fix.

Implementation sketch

1) VCS streak logging (S): in VcsStatusBroadcaster.makeRemoteRefreshLoop (~:540-570), mirror ProviderRuntimeIngestion's history-recovery pattern. Log the WARN with exit.cause only when consecutiveFailures === 1 (or when briefCause(exit.cause) differs from the last logged one, kept in a Ref), use Effect.logDebug for later failures, and add an Effect.logInfo('VCS remote status refresh recovered', {cwd, previousFailures}) on success when the previous count was > 0. Keep logOnceEvery keyed per cwd for the streak-start line so poller churn stays deduped. Minimal alternative: pass window: Duration.hours(1) to that logOnceEvery call. Or make it generic: add an optional fullCauseEvery to LogOnceEveryOptions/LogOnceEveryLimiter, so a key whose last full line was within fullCauseEvery gets a summary instead of a full log even after a quiet window. Tests: add to packages/shared/src/logOnceEvery.test.ts a case with occurrences 15 min apart expecting summaries; add a VcsStatusBroadcaster test with TestClock and a failing workflow.remoteStatus that asserts one Warn per streak and Debug afterwards. 2) Latent loops (S): wrap UsageLimitRecovery.ts:332, CompletionReturnDelivery.ts:1031 and chatFolders.ts:314/376 with logOnceEvery (keys 'usageLimit.sweep', 'agentControl.completionReturn.scan', 'chats.rootProbe:'+root), passing the cause, and cover them with the existing layer tests via a fresh makeLogOnceEvery limiter. 3) Desktop (S): make the prepareTransport handler (main.ts:3832) return {ok:true, transportId} | {ok:false, reason}, as activate does. Update DesktopBridge.prepareDesktopWorkspaceTransport in packages/contracts/src/ipc.ts, preload.ts and DesktopWorkspaceIpcSocketFactory.nextUrl (throw a renderer-side error on ok:false so the URL-provider retry/backoff path is unchanged). Optionally route lastWorkspaceActivationFailure through the shared LogOnceEveryLimiter so alternating messages are also bounded. Test in desktopWorkspaceIpc.test.ts and desktopWorkspaceSocket tests. 4) Optional (S): in serverLogger.ts, use Logger.consoleLogFmt (or drop the console logger) when config.mode === 'desktop', since stdout is only tailed into memory after readiness. Keep stderr output for crash tails.

Done#254 Each open thread subscription polls provider history every ~30 s forever; failures are logged without a cause (26k WARNs), and non-live Codex threads spawn codex app-server on each poll

gap-logging-io:history-recovery-poll-storm · original impact Medium, effort M · Process spawns WP02

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it. DONE is right: the poll, the spawn per read, the missing cause and the missing backoff are all fixed. The auditor's 'no concrete defects' is wrong. Removing the 30 s poll also removed the only automatic repair for two failure cases, and the replacement triggers do not cover them (see fixDefects). Minor: the historyRecoveryPolicy.ts range should be 142-178; the file ends at 178.

Current state

The finding's costs are gone. The forever loop of reconcile plus a 30 s sleep (f1be4abc7 orchestrationRpc.ts:68-80) is replaced by withThreadHistoryRecovery. It reads once when an active subscription opens, then once per thread.session-set event that settles the session, with no timer. A spacing gate (5 min after an open, 30 s after a settle) runs before any SQL. Failures back off from 30 s, doubling to 15 min. The cause is logged at Warning once per failure streak, then at Debug. Stored Codex reads share one pooled read-only app-server per instance that closes after 60 s idle. Clients mark prewarmed and retained idle subscriptions passive, so those read nothing. Optional proposal part 2 (a cheap mtime or updatedAt check before thread/read) was not built. That costs little now that reads are spaced and pooled. A verified side effect: the old poll also repaired turns stuck as running. The new triggers cannot fire in that case, and a settle that lands inside the spacing window is dropped rather than deferred.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/ws/orchestrationRpc.ts:85-97 withHistoryRecovery now calls withThreadHistoryRecovery with an active/passive mode and a per-connection registry. The Effect.forever loop is gone. It wraps subscribeThread (:610) and subscribeThreadWindow (:643). setThreadHistoryRecovery (:454-459) only flips the mode for this connection.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/historyRecoveryPolicy.ts:142-178 One forked read on open (only when active, or on a passive-to-active flip). One forked read per stream array that holds a settling thread.session-set event (settlesThreadSession, :46-53). No timer.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/historyRecoveryPolicy.ts:15-43 Spacing is 5 min after an open and 30 s after a settle. After a failure it is 30 s, doubling up to 15 min.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:3517-3527 The spacing gate and the historyReads coalescing set run before resolveThreadShell, getProjectShellById and getBinding. A gated trigger returns Effect.void and nothing is rescheduled. Semaphore(2) bounds admission.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:3557-3585 25 s timeout. Warning with Cause.pretty only on the first failure of a streak; repeats go to Debug with threadId, trigger and failures. State is bounded to 1,000 threads (recordHistoryRecovery, :3504-3516).
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:3298-3345 processHistory returns early on an empty history and uses the bounded getThreadHistoryRepairContext (ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:4409) instead of the full getThreadDetailById.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexStoredThreadReader.ts:61-190 One lazily started read-only app-server per instance, shared by concurrent reads. It closes after 60 s idle (:59) and is retired when the process exits or a transport error occurs. CodexAdapter.ts:2608-2616 uses it for non-live reads. The old per-read readStoredCodexThread (CodexSessionRuntime.ts:1192) is now used only by an integration test.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/connection/supervision.ts:522-566 A subscription sends historyRecovery active only while a view is attached (viewCount > 0). View attach and detach call setThreadHistoryRecovery.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.ts:1145-1156,1200-1225 Defect evidence: a live Codex session emits session.state.changed 'ready' only from session/ready, once at startup (CodexSessionRuntime.ts:2261). thread/status/changed idle maps to thread.state.changed, and ingestion turns that into nothing except compaction (ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:1036-1039). If turn.completed is lost, no settling thread.session-set is ever produced.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/providerTurnLiveness.ts:1-14,93-112 Defect evidence: the liveness sweep settles a running turn only when no live runtime exists ('lost'). On a live runtime it only reports 'unresponsive' once and never acts. Before, the 30 s poll healed this case through the settlesTurn path (ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:3421-3439, decider.ts:2845-2874).
Defects in the shipped fix

(1) Lost turn completion on a live runtime is no longer repaired while the thread stays open. Suppose turn.completed is dropped or fails in processInputSafely (ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:3474-3488) while the Codex runtime stays up. The projected turn then stays 'running', and nothing emits a settling thread.session-set: thread/status/changed maps to thread.state.changed, which is ignored, and session/ready is only emitted at startup. So the session-settled trigger never fires. The liveness sweep only reports 'unresponsive' for a live runtime. Repair now waits for an active subscribe at least 5 min after the last read, a manual stop, or a server restart. Before, the 30 s poll repaired it through the settlesTurn and pending-request clearing paths of processHistory, which exist for exactly this case. A dead runtime is now marked 'lost' (error) after about 2 sweeps, instead of being settled as completed from provider history. (2) A trigger that lands inside the spacing window is dropped, not deferred: reconcileThread returns Effect.void at :3524-3526 and nothing reschedules it. A common case is a thread opened at T0 (read) whose next turn settles before T0+30 s, or two turns that settle within 30 s of each other. The final turn never gets an end-of-turn read until the next settle or a reopen 5 min later. (3) Freshness trade-off, by design of the proposal: an open thread advanced by another writer (the Codex app holding the writer lease, CodexAdapter.ts:2597-2598) no longer picks up those turns within 30 s; it waits for a reopen after 5 min. Minor: the 25 s HISTORY_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT also covers waiting for the Semaphore(2) permit, so a large burst of opens could log a timeout as a failure. Not seen in practice.

Implementation sketch

1) Trailing read instead of a dropped trigger. In ProviderRuntimeIngestion.reconcileThread (:3517-3527), when a 'session-settled' trigger is gated by the success spacing (state.failures === 0), keep a per-thread pendingTrailing set. Fork one Effect.sleep(remaining).pipe(Effect.andThen(reconcileThread(threadId, 'session-settled'))) in the layer scope, deduped per thread and dropped when a read runs first. Or do it in withThreadHistoryRecovery so the subscription scope cancels it: make reconcile report 'gated until X' and schedule one delayed fork. Test in ProviderRuntimeIngestion.test.ts with TestClock: open, then settle at +10 s gives one read now and one at +30 s, never more. 2) Repair a lost completion on a live runtime. ProviderCommandReactor.sweepLiveness (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:3364-3400) already visits every thread with a projected running turn and live runtime activity. When classifyThreadLiveness sees a matching live runtime that has been silent for at least one sweep interval (or the adapter session reports no active turn), call an injected requestHistoryRecovery(threadId). That is ProviderRuntimeIngestionService.reconcileThread with a new 'liveness' trigger: settled spacing plus failure backoff, added to HistoryRecoveryTrigger and historyRecoverySpacingMs. Inject it as an optional layer dependency or reactor option so the reactor does not depend on ingestion internals. It costs nothing for idle threads, since only projected-running threads qualify. Test: drop turn.completed in the ingestion harness, run sweepLiveness, and assert thread.history.restore settles the turn and clears pending requests. 3) Optional, product decision: freshness for external writers. While a view is active, poll a cheap updatedAt probe every 60 s (thread/read includeTurns:false on the shared CodexStoredThreadReader, or a rollout file stat). Do the full includeTurns read only when it changed. This also covers proposal part 2.

Done#255 redactAgentControlSecrets deep-clones every SDK message and every derived runtime event (including the 64-78 KB raw copy) even when there is nothing to redact

gap-logging-io:redact-deep-clone-fanout · original impact Low, effort S · CPU

Current state

Confirmed DONE. PR #710 (60633eff3) moved redaction into agentControl/secretRedaction.ts. Redaction is now copy-on-write, and an includes("rycoac") guard skips the regex for strings without the marker. Clean values come back as the same reference with no allocation. The Claude adapter shares one makeSharedPayloadSecretRedactor, so each SDK message is walked once and every fan-out event, plus the native log, reuses the cached raw.payload by reference. Every Claude event goes through the single Queue.offer, and no downstream stage deep-clones. I found no bypass, no regression and no missed Claude path. Only theoretical semantic changes remain.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/agentControl/secretRedaction.ts:17-18 The marker guard returns strings unchanged unless they contain 'rycoac'. It is case-consistent with SECRET_PATTERN.
  • apps/server/src/agentControl/secretRedaction.ts:26-60 Copy-on-write walk over arrays and objects. Old code (f1be4abc7 ProviderInjection.ts:298-315) used Object.fromEntries/entries, map and replaceAll unconditionally. ProviderInjection.ts:308 now only re-exports.
  • apps/server/src/agentControl/secretRedaction.ts:77-124 A WeakMap caches the redacted result per SDK message. event() sends raw.payload through the cache and walks the other keys copy-on-write. When the payload is clean, the cache maps the message to itself, which is ephemeron-safe and does not leak.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:1932 One adapter-wide redactor.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:1986-1993 secretRedactor.event(event) runs before the only Queue.offer on runtimeEventQueue. The other Queue.offer calls (6064, 6174) go to promptQueue.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:2137 The native log uses secretRedactor.payload(message), which shares the cache with the event path. With no logger it returns early (2110-2112).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:3840-3845, 4366-4395 The workflow fan-out (task.progress per member, subagent.updated) uses raw.payload: message, which hits the cache. Per-event payloads are small, newly built objects, so each fan-out event costs only a small walk with no allocation.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:2018-2099 The subagent emitters also set raw.payload to the SDK message itself (input.raw). I found no code that mutates SDK messages after receipt.
  • apps/server/src/provider/runtimeSession.ts:34-44 stampRuntimeEvent is a shallow spread. ProviderService has no structuredClone, JSON round trip or deep clone (its line 286 fromEntries is an unrelated binding payload).
  • apps/server/src/agentControl/secretRedaction.test.ts:13-65 Tests cover same-reference return, path-local copying, input not mutated, Error flattening, and a shared payload reused across events.
Defects in the shipped fix

No real defects. Theoretical notes only, none actionable: (1) Semantics changed for non-plain values. The old code flattened every object to a plain object, which dropped prototypes, toJSON, Map/Set contents and extra non-index properties on arrays. The new code returns a clean non-plain object as the same reference. A token held only in a Map/Set, behind toJSON or in an extra array property would therefore no longer be stripped. The inputs on these paths are JSON-derived SDK and RPC messages, Schema-typed events, and Error causes (which are still flattened), so this does not happen in practice. (2) There is no ClaudeAdapter-level test asserting that a token inside an SDK message is redacted in both the emitted event and the native log. That coverage was also missing before the change. (3) CopilotAdapter.ts:115/132 and AcpNativeLogging.ts:37/71 still use the uncached walk, but they no longer allocate when clean, and they are outside this Claude finding.

Value none · effort none · risk none

Done#256 Logs write large items uncapped and up to 4 times (a 1.5 MB attachment becomes ~9 MB of logs and 3 MB single lines), while the persistence path caps strings at 16,000 chars

gap-logging-io:uncapped-large-items · original impact Low, effort S · Memory WP16

Current state

Confirmed DONE. #710 (60633eff3) moved every provider log stream (the shared native and canonical loggers, used by all drivers) onto serializeProviderEventLogRecord. That serializer caps strings at 8,192 chars (6 KB head and 1 KB tail), replaces inline base64 with a mime/size/sha256 marker, redacts Agent Control secrets, and turns canonical raw.payload into a reference, so the 3 MB double copy is gone. The writer queue now has 8 MiB per-writer and 32 MiB per-stream character budgets, and drops are counted in providerEventLogRecordsDroppedTotal. Packaged builds also default to 'lifecycle' mode, where item.* and native item/* records are filtered out before serialization, so large items are not even stringified there. Log volume, the memory bound and the privacy goals are met. The one claimed gain that did not materialize is 'removes 2-6 ms stringify stalls': in full mode an over-cap record is still stringified in full, walked, stringified again with a replacer, and sha256-hashed. Measured on a ~1.47 MB base64 image record, the sync cost is about the same as before or slightly higher. This is a minor optimization limited to full mode, not a functional gap.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.ts:315 PROVIDER_EVENT_LOG_STRING_CAP = 8_192, head 6_144 and tail 1_024. This is the capActivityData approach the finding proposed.
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.ts:327 serializeProviderEventLogRecord runs a fast path: an uncapped JSON.stringify (line 337). Only when that output is over the cap and containsOverCapString finds a long string (line 355), or the secret marker is present, does it run a second JSON.stringify with the capLogValue replacer (line 345).
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.ts:380 capProviderEventLogString redacts secrets, then summarizes inline base64 (summarizeInlineBase64, line 393: sha256 over the whole string) or keeps head + '…[N chars omitted]…' + tail. Attachment payloads no longer reach disk.
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.ts:414 withRawReference turns canonical raw.payload into {source, method, messageType, nativeId}, which removes the 'present twice per line' duplicate.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:134 DEFAULT_MAX_QUEUE_CHARS = 8 MiB per writer, DEFAULT_MAX_TOTAL_QUEUE_CHARS = 32 MiB per logger stream.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:335 enqueueLine enforces the record count plus both char budgets and returns queue_full. Both char checks are skipped when this writer's own queue is empty (line 345), so each writer can always add one line, even past the global budget. Lines are now capped, so this is bounded and negligible.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:257 recordDropped increments providerEventLogRecordsDroppedTotal (queue_full / queue_closed).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:358 Every record goes through serialize(), which calls serializeProviderEventLogRecord synchronously on the provider event path. The adapters' own makeEventNdjsonLogger calls only run when nativeEventLogPath is passed; production drivers pass the shared ProviderEventLoggers.native instead (e.g. CodexDriver.ts:180).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderEventLoggers.ts:104 The default mode is 'full' in development and 'lifecycle' when packaged. In lifecycle mode, shouldWriteProviderEventRecord (providerEventLogRecords.ts:161) rejects canonical item.* and native item/* records (the 'item' token is in NATIVE_STREAMING_NAME, line 134) before serialization.
  • apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.test.ts:60 Tests cover capping, base64 summary, redaction, the canonical raw reference (line 22) and long-record fast paths (line 83). EventNdjsonLogger.test.ts:518 covers the per-writer char budget. No test covers maxTotalQueueChars.
  • /tmp/perf3/verify256/bench.mjs Node 24 measurement on a 1.47 MB base64 image record: serialize native 1.92 ms (old pipeline stringify+line+Buffer.from 1.29 ms); serialize canonical 1.99 ms (old plain stringify alone 1.70 ms + copy); serialize 1.5 MB text record 1.09 ms (old 1.07 ms + copy); replacer-only stringify 0.71 ms, of which sha256 is 0.47 ms. Output sizes: 218 B / 302 B / 7.5 KB instead of 1.47 MB / 2.93 MB / 1.58 MB.
Defects in the shipped fix

Minor and limited to full mode (the development default, or an explicit opt-in; packaged builds default to lifecycle and never serialize these records). (1) The finding's 'removes 2-6 ms stringify stalls per large item' gain was not delivered. For an over-cap record, serializeProviderEventLogRecord (providerEventLogRecords.ts:337-345) does a full uncapped JSON.stringify, then the containsOverCapString walk, then a second replacer stringify that sha256-hashes the whole base64 payload (line 405). Measured on a 1.47 MB base64 item: native 1.92 ms vs 1.29 ms for the old stringify+Buffer pipeline; canonical 1.99 ms vs about 1.7 ms + copy. Large text items cost about the same as before (1.09 ms). The four records per large item still cost about 4-8 ms of synchronous time on the provider event path. The downstream 3 MB Buffer copies, writev, rotation and gzip are gone. (2) The per-string cap does not bound total line size: a record with many strings each under 8 KB is written in full. The empty-queue bypass in enqueueLine (EventNdjsonLogger.ts:345) also lets every writer exceed both char budgets by one line. Both are theoretical: no such multi-MB record was observed. (3) The maxTotalQueueChars (global) budget has no test.

Implementation sketch

Optional micro-fix in apps/server/src/provider/providerEventLogRecords.ts, serializeProviderEventLogRecord. Avoid the wasted full stringify for over-cap records. Run containsOverCapString(value, 0) first; it is allocation-free, O(nodes), and never reads string contents. If it returns true, go straight to JSON.stringify(value, capLogValue). Otherwise do the plain stringify and fall back to the replacer only when it contains AGENT_CONTROL_SECRET_MARKER. To keep small records cheap, gate the pre-walk behind a node budget, or keep the current order and pre-walk only when a cheap first-level size hint (e.g. a payload.item / payload.data presence check) suggests an item. In summarizeInlineBase64, replace sha256 over the whole value with a digest of length + head/tail samples (e.g. the first and last 4 KB), or drop the digest; this saves about 0.47 ms per 1.5 MB. Measured result: native base64 record 1.92 ms -> about 0.25-0.7 ms. Tests: extend providerEventLogRecords.test.ts to assert the reordered path gives byte-identical output for capped, base64, secret-bearing and long-but-short-strings records. Add an EventNdjsonLogger.test.ts case with maxTotalQueueChars set low across two thread writers, asserting queue_full drops. If wanted, add a per-line ceiling: after capping, when json.length exceeds e.g. 256 KB, replace the record with a {truncated:true, type/method, chars} stub, and count it.

Done#257 Shared native and canonical loggers are never closed: the last batch is lost on quit, writers are never evicted, and the queue bound counts records instead of bytes

gap-logging-io:shared-loggers-never-closed · original impact Low, effort S · Reliability WP16

Current state

Confirmed DONE by 60633eff3 (#710). ProviderEventLoggersLive registers a finalizer that closes both shared loggers after they are built. It sits below the provider registry, drivers and ProviderService in the server.ts provideMerge chain, so it runs after ProviderService.stopAll and after the instance scopes close. EventNdjsonLogger.close drains every writer and any in-flight evicted closes, then drops later writes as queue_closed. Idle writers are flushed, closed and evicted after 2 minutes, which bounds the writer map and the held file handles. The queue has per-thread and per-stream character budgets on top of the record cap. The shutdown path really releases the layer: NodeRuntime.runMain interrupts on SIGTERM/SIGINT, and desktop sends SIGTERM with a 3 s grace before SIGKILL. A test checks that the finalizer flushes records that are still inside the batch window. I found no defect in the fix, only non-production nits.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderEventLoggers.ts:197-204 Effect.addFinalizer closes native and canonical in parallel. It is registered after both loggers are built and after the forkScoped retention/settings fibers, so it runs before those fibers are interrupted.
  • apps/server/src/server.ts:536-541 Layer.provideMerge(ProviderEventLoggersLive) sits below ProviderInstanceRegistryHydrationLive, ProviderRegistryLive and ProviderRuntimeLayerLive, so the loggers are built first and released last.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderInstanceRegistryLive.ts:564-571 Instance scopes are forked from the registry's layer scope and closed in parallel when that layer is released, so adapters stop before the logger finalizer runs. ProviderService.stopAll is the finalizer at ProviderService.ts:2509.
  • apps/server/src/cliMain.ts:74-75 NodeRuntime.runMain interrupts the program on SIGTERM/SIGINT, which releases the layer scopes and runs the finalizer. No process.exit bypasses it in apps/server/src.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendLauncher.ts:218-256 Desktop sends SIGTERM and waits a 3 s grace before SIGKILL. The comment measures backend exit at 1.0-1.6 s, which leaves room for the logger drain.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:605-613 close() sets loggerClosed, clears writers, stops the eviction timer, and awaits closeWriter for live writers plus closingWriters. writeRecord drops later records as queue_closed at line 435.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:527-554 closeWriter: flush (closing the delta run), mark closed, flush again, await any predecessor close, then sink.close(). All errors are caught, so close never rejects.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:556-590 Eviction only takes writers that have been idle past the TTL and have an empty buffer, no open run and no activeFlush. A replacement writer's first batch and its close wait for the predecessor's close (lines 307, 486-493 and 542-544), so the two sinks never rotate or compress at the same time. The eviction interval is unref'd and stops once the map is empty.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:131-136,335-356,514-518 Per-thread record cap (2048), per-thread char budget (8M) and per-stream char budget (32M) are enforced on enqueue and released in the flush finally. Idle TTL is 2 minutes.
  • packages/shared/src/logging.ts:157,203-219,272-274,349-355 AsyncRotatingFileSink now holds a FileHandle and does one writev per batch. close() drains the write tail and any compression, then closes the handle.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderEventLoggers.test.ts:120-140 Writes inside the 200 ms batch window, closes the layer scope, and checks that both per-thread files contain the record.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.test.ts:518-662 Covers size-bounded queues, idle eviction with reopen, predecessor ordering, close waiting for evicted writers, and drain-on-close then drop-after-close.
Defects in the shipped fix

None material. Non-production or edge nits: (1) The finalizer drain has no time bound. A hung fs write or gzip would stall graceful shutdown. Desktop caps this with SIGKILL after 3 s, but a CLI `ryco serve` stopped with SIGTERM would wait indefinitely. This is unlikely on local disks. (2) ClaudeAdapter and CopilotAdapter never close the logger they build themselves from nativeEventLogPath. That path is test-only. (3) As proposed, there is no explicit release(threadId) on session stop or reap. The idle TTL bounds the writer map instead, so a stopped session's writer and file handle live about 2-3 minutes. The finding allowed this alternative.

Done#258 Electron main writes backend stdout/stderr and its own console with synchronous appendFileSync (3 sync writes per console chunk)

gap-logging-io:desktop-sync-log-sink · original impact Low, effort S · Blocking I/O WP04

Current state

Confirmed DONE. Electron main no longer does any synchronous log I/O. desktop-main.log and server-child.log are both AsyncRotatingFileSink (held append handle, one writev per batch, fs.promises rotation). A captured console chunk is one writeBatch instead of 3 appendFileSync calls. LOG_FILE_MAX_FILES dropped from 10 to 3. In desktop mode the backend writes its own logfmt server.log through a batched async sink, which Diagnostics tails, and Electron stops writing backend output to disk once the backend serves. The user's live log dir shows it working: server-child.log gets one '---- backend serving; its output continues in server.log ----' marker per session, and server.log has been written since Oct 12 at about 150 KB/day. One small defect: PR #710 cut maxFiles from 10 to 3 and, in the same change, replaced the readdir-based overflow prune with a probe of only maxFiles+1..maxFiles+3. Backups .7 to .10 left by the old depth are never deleted on upgraded installs.

Evidence
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1885-1906 initializePackagedLogging creates desktopLogSink and backendLogSink as AsyncRotatingFileSink. No sync RotatingFileSink is used anywhere outside tests (git grep).
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1832-1847 writeDesktopStreamChunk builds [prefix, buffer, optional newline] and calls desktopLogSink.writeBatch once, so one writev per console chunk.
  • packages/shared/src/logging.ts:139-368 AsyncRotatingFileSink opens its handle lazily, appends with handle.writev, rotates through fs.promises rename/rm, and serializes writes through writeTail.
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:315-318 LOG_FILE_MAX_FILES = 3 (was 10 at f1be4abc7). Rotation keeps current + .1..3, so 4 x 10 MiB per log and 80 MiB for both logs, down from about 220 MiB (the auditor's 60 MiB undercounts the current file).
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1909-1936 captureBackendOutput sends each chunk to BackendOutputCapture.push(buffer, readiness.ready). The readiness detector and startup outputTail are only fed while !readiness.ready.
  • apps/desktop/src/backendStartup.ts:213-254 BackendOutputCapture writes to server-child.log only before ready. After that it writes one 'backend serving' marker and keeps a 16 KB in-memory tail, which is written only in recordUnexpectedExit (main.ts handleChildGone, skipped while quitting or on an expected exit).
  • apps/server/src/serverLogger.ts:107-121 In desktop mode the server also pushes makeServerLogFileLogger({filePath: config.serverLogPath}): logfmt, 250 ms / 64-line batches, a 4 MB pending cap that drops lines and counts them, and a 10 MiB x 3 AsyncRotatingFileSink. Logger.consolePretty is still installed, so backend output still goes over the stdout pipe into Electron main after ready, where it only feeds the 16 KB tail (microbench: about 0.46 us per 228-byte chunk).
  • apps/server/src/diagnostics/Layers/Diagnostics.ts:891-896 readFailureLogTail tails config.serverLogPath (logs/server.log), and failureFromLogLine handles the logfmt prefix. The Diagnostics source that used to be dead is now populated.
  • packages/shared/src/logging.ts:307-322,349-350 Defect: pruneOverflowBackups only probes maxFiles+1..maxFiles+OVERFLOW_BACKUP_PROBE_COUNT (3), which is .4..6 for the desktop sinks. Both this and the 10->3 maxFiles cut landed in 60633eff3. The old sync and async sinks used readdir and removed every suffix above maxFiles.
  • ~/.ryco/userdata/logs (user machine, read-only) Live check: server-child.log has 15 'backend serving' markers, the latest session stops right after 'Listening on', and server.log (796 lines since 2026-10-12) exists. No .4+ desktop backups exist on this machine, so the prune gap does not affect it.
Defects in the shipped fix

Low severity: on installs that had rotated deeper than .6 under the old maxFiles=10, desktop-main.log.7..10 and server-child.log.7..10 are never pruned (packages/shared/src/logging.ts:307-322 probes only indices 4..6 when maxFiles=3). That leaves up to 8 x 10 MiB = 80 MiB of static orphaned files, which partly undoes the finding's '~140 MiB lower worst-case disk cap' for upgraded users. Minor, and inherent to the async design: a line logged right before an immediate app.exit (e.g. 'second instance refused' at apps/desktop/src/main.ts:4639-4640) may be lost now that the write is async. Not a perf defect. Also: the sync RotatingFileSink in packages/shared/src/logging.ts:34 is only used by apps/desktop/src/rotatingFileSink.test.ts and could be deleted.

Implementation sketch

Prune gap: in packages/shared/src/logging.ts, add an optional `pruneBackupsUpTo?: number` option to AsyncRotatingFileSinkOptions (default maxFiles + OVERFLOW_BACKUP_PROBE_COUNT). Have pruneOverflowBackups probe indices maxFiles+1..max(that, pruneBackupsUpTo), still with exact-path rm (force), never readdir. In apps/desktop/src/main.ts initializePackagedLogging, pass `pruneBackupsUpTo: 10` (the legacy LOG_FILE_MAX_FILES, kept as a named constant like LEGACY_LOG_FILE_MAX_FILES with a comment) to both desktop sinks. A simpler alternative is raising OVERFLOW_BACKUP_PROBE_COUNT to 8, which costs a few extra async rm calls per sink at startup. Test: extend packages/shared/src/logging.test.ts 'prunes backups left by a deeper rotation' with .7 and .10 (+ .gz) files and maxFiles 3 / pruneBackupsUpTo 10, then assert only .1..3 remain and readdir is not called. Optional cleanup: delete the sync RotatingFileSink and move or delete apps/desktop/src/rotatingFileSink.test.ts. Optional and not worth it at about 150 KB/day: in packaged desktop mode, drop Logger.consolePretty after http-serving so post-ready output stops crossing the pipe. That changes what server-child.log and the crash tail contain, so it would need a product call.

Done#259 Each log write creates 3 exported Effect.fn spans and takes a SynchronizedRef lock shared by all threads

gap-logging-io:logger-effect-spans · original impact Low, effort S · CPU WP16

Current state

The finding is fixed as described. In EventNdjsonLogger, write is now a single span-free Effect.suspend over a synchronous writeRecord: a mode check, a Map lookup with lazy writer creation, one JSON.stringify, and a buffer push. Records are flushed every 200 ms as one writev per batch. The write, toLogMessage and resolveThreadWriter spans are gone, and so is the SynchronizedRef lock. Every Claude helper the finding measured is now a plain function or Effect.fnUntraced: logNativeSdkMessage, ensureThreadId, routeSteerFrame, handleSdkMessage, routeSdkMessage, plus handleStreamEvent and ensureAssistantTextBlock. Codex writeNativeEvent is a plain function. Because every provider shares the logger, the logger-side gain covers all of them. What remains is low-value and outside the finding's measured scope: OpenCode still makes 1 or 2 exported named spans per streamed event, and Copilot still has named spans that are not exported.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:594 write = Effect.suspend(() => writeRecord(...)). No Effect.fn, so no span. It returns a logWarning or recordDropped effect only on the error and drop paths.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:311 resolveWriter is a synchronous Map.get with lazy createWriter (line 274). No SynchronizedRef or semaphore remains in the file. The AsyncRotatingFileSink constructor only starts async initialization (packages/shared/src/logging.ts:161), so creating a writer on the caller does no sync I/O.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:430 writeRecord applies the mode policy, then the writer lookup, delta coalescing and enqueue, all synchronous. File I/O happens in the timer-driven flushWriter (line 457) as a single writeBatch (writev).
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.test.ts:173 Tests cover concurrent first writes, eviction with predecessor ordering (574), close draining (605, 641) and queue bounds (268, 518). These are the races the old lock guarded against.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:2106 logNativeSdkMessage is a plain function (it was Effect.fn at f1be4abc7:2104). ensureThreadId (2357), routeSteerFrame (4771), handleSdkMessage (4864), routeSdkMessage (4898), handleStreamEvent (2900) and ensureAssistantTextBlock (2178) are all Effect.fnUntraced.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CodexAdapter.ts:2791 writeNativeEvent is a plain arrow function (it was Effect.fn("writeNativeEvent") at f1be4abc7). It is called per event from the Effect.gen loop at line 2077.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/OpenCodeAdapter.ts:1468 Uncovered caller: handleSubscribedEvent is still Effect.fn("handleSubscribedEvent"), runs for every OpenCode SSE event (line 2075), and is forked in server context, so its spans are exported. emitAssistantTextDelta (line 1370) is also named and runs for every text-part update (lines 1572 and 1679). Neither changed since f1be4abc7.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/CopilotAdapter.ts:123 Uncovered caller: logCopilotNativeEvent (line 123) and handleCopilotEvent (line 175) are still named Effect.fn around the logger write for every Copilot SDK event. They run through a bare Effect.runPromise (CopilotAdapter.session.ts:344), so the context-scoped LocalFileTracer (Observability.ts:85) is absent and the spans are never written to the trace file. The only cost is a small amount of CPU.
  • apps/server/src/provider/acp/AcpNativeLogging.ts:9 The ACP and Cursor native logging (writeNativeAcpLog, plus logNative in AcpAdapter.ts:264 and CursorAdapter.ts:395) uses plain Effect.gen and adds no spans. The canonical logger write in ProviderService.ts:643 also adds no spans.
Defects in the shipped fix

No bugs or regressions were found in the logger rewrite. There are uncovered callers of the same per-event named-span pattern that 60633eff3 did not touch: (1) OpenCodeAdapter.ts:1468 handleSubscribedEvent and :1370 emitAssistantTextDelta are named Effect.fn that run for every streamed OpenCode event or part. Their spans are exported to server.trace.ndjson, roughly 1 or 2 records of about 380 B each per delta. (2) CopilotAdapter.ts:123 logCopilotNativeEvent and :175 handleCopilotEvent are named per event, but they run through a bare Effect.runPromise without the server tracer, so they cost only CPU. Both are minor and outside the finding's measured Claude and Codex scope.
