Done#260 Web client tracing turns on after auth for every user and POSTs OTLP JSON every 1 s; the server logs the whole body on decode failure

gap-logging-io:client-tracing-always-on · original impact Low, effort S · Network / RTT

Current state

Confirmed DONE. All four parts of the proposal are on main. (1) Export is gated: AuthenticatedTracingBootstrap configures the OTLP exporter only when the primary server advertises observability.browserTracesEnabled (set when otlpTracesUrl is configured or RYCO_BROWSER_TRACES=1) or the build is a VITE_RYCO_PERF_PROFILE build. Otherwise it calls disableClientTracing and spans stay plain NativeSpans. (2) The default export interval is 10 s, matching the server. (3) The server's decode-failure warning logs only the cause and a span count, never bodyJson. (4) OTLP, FetchHttpClient and the serializer moved into clientTracingExporter.ts, which is dynamically imported. Two guards keep them out of the boot graph: a source-level test, and a bundle-budget rule on node_modules/effect/dist/observability/Otlp*. The changes landed in #710 (60633eff3: lazy exporter, 10 s interval, log fix) and 65af92766 (server-advertised gating). Both are in the Hub's vendored pin 7bc39eec3. I searched for missed paths and found none. Mobile uses client-runtime's noop tracer. Hosted-hub, hosted-static and hosted-cached sessions never mount the bootstrap. No other web or client-runtime module imports Otlp*. The server config atom is only cleared on hosted paths, so exportTraces does not flicker during local reconnects. The only leftovers are a few minor latent nits, none of which affect perf.

Evidence
  • apps/web/src/components/RootAppShell.tsx:221-231 AuthenticatedTracingBootstrap computes exportTraces from shouldExportClientTraces and calls configureClientTracing() or disableClientTracing() in an effect keyed on exportTraces. It is mounted only when authGateState.status === 'authenticated' (localTracingAllowed).
  • apps/web/src/observability/clientTracing.ts:45-50 Returns perfProfile || observability?.browserTracesEnabled === true. Older servers omit the field, so their clients export nothing.
  • apps/web/src/perf/perfInstrumentation.ts:10-15 isWebPerfProfileEnabled is a build-time constant from VITE_RYCO_PERF_PROFILE, not a runtime toggle.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:1201-1203 browserTracesEnabled = config.otlpTracesUrl !== undefined || config.browserTracesEnabled === true. The env var is defined at apps/server/src/cli.ts:323 and the schema at packages/contracts/src/server.ts:338.
  • apps/web/src/observability/clientTracing.ts:12 DEFAULT_EXPORT_INTERVAL_MS = 10_000. It was 1_000 at f1be4abc7.
  • apps/web/src/observability/clientTracing.ts:91-94 await import('./clientTracingExporter'). The exporter module (clientTracingExporter.ts:1-3) holds FetchHttpClient and OtlpExporter/OtlpSerialization/OtlpTracer. clientTracing.ts only imports its type.
  • apps/web/src/perf/standardBootGraph.test.ts:160-168 Asserts that clientTracingExporter.ts is not statically reachable from main.tsx.
  • scripts/perf/model.ts:247-249 The bundle-budget rule forbids node_modules/effect/dist/observability/Otlp* in the boot chunks of the real dist.
  • apps/server/src/http.ts:356-403 DecodeOtlpTraceRecordsError now carries spanCount, not bodyJson. The warning logs { cause, spanCount } under the comment 'Never log the payload'. The old code (f1be4abc7 http.ts:291-297) logged bodyJson.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/platform/index.ts:359 The default ObservabilityService tracingLayer is a noop tracer, so mobile and other clients have no OTLP export path.
  • packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/serverState.ts:186-191 clearServerState (which sets the config to null) is called only from hostedHub/environment.ts. Local authenticated sessions do not null the config on reconnect, so the gate does not toggle during reconnects.
  • apps/web/src/observability/clientTracing.ts:65-68 Minor latent nit, not reachable in practice. configure() short-circuits whenever activeConfigKey !== null, even when a disableClientTracing() is still queued behind an in-flight apply. A true->false->true flip inside one exporter load would therefore end disabled. exportTraces only changes when the server's advertised config changes, so this does not happen today.
Defects in the shipped fix

No real defects. Minor non-perf nits: (a) clientTracing.ts:65-68: the configure() fast path ignores a queued disable, so a rapid true->false->true flip during an in-flight exporter load would leave tracing disabled. This is unreachable today because the gate only changes when the server's advertised config changes. (b) clientTracing.ts:95-103: if the dynamic import or exporter start fails, activeConfigKey stays set and later configure() calls never retry. This was already true at f1be4abc7 and only affects diagnostics. (c) RYCO_BROWSER_TRACES is not listed in the docs/observability.md env-var section (around line 519). (d) Intentional behaviour change: the Settings > Diagnostics recent-spans table (DetailedTraceDiagnostics.tsx, source 'browser') no longer shows browser spans by default unless OTLP or RYCO_BROWSER_TRACES is set. The commit message documents this.

Partial#261 Worktrees whose checkout directory was deleted outside Ryco are never marked removed, so every source-control refresh re-probes them and logs a ~2.8 KB stack trace

gap-logging-io:stale-missing-checkouts-reprobed · original impact Low, effort S · Reliability WP07Bdecision

First-pass audit said DONE; the verifier corrected it.

Current state

The core fix landed in #710 (60633eff3) and works in production: on 2026-10-12 it recorded 18 dead checkouts as checkout.remove reason "missing" (once each, which also archives them), and the sweep now skips removed rows. It is not complete, though. checkoutMissingOnDisk only records a checkout when its parent is still a real directory, and stat follows symlinks. A dead row whose parent is also gone, or is a dangling symlink, is never recorded. It stays a live workspace and keeps failing with a full stack on every sweep window. One of the rows the finding measured is in exactly this state on this install. Since the fix it has logged 95 'Source control refresh failed' lines to server.log: 83 full stacks, 198 KB, 47% of the file, in about 2.3 days.

Evidence
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:121 checkoutMissingOnDisk returns true only if stat(path) gives ENOENT and stat(dirname) is a directory. stat follows symlinks, so a dangling-symlink parent, or a removed per-project worktrees folder, counts as 'unavailable' and is never recorded.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:173 When resolve fails and the parent is missing, the code runs Effect.fail(error). The sweep then logs the failure with its full cause on every refresh. Only the parent-present case returns null and dispatches worktree.checkout.remove once, guarded by recordedMissingCheckouts (line 88). That Set is filled before the dispatch, and a failed dispatch is only logged at Debug and never retried in-process.
  • apps/server/src/logOnceEvery.ts:99 ignoreCauseLogOnceEvery logs at Info and writes the full Cause on the first line of every new burst. A failure that comes back on each 5-minute sweep therefore still writes a roughly 2.3 KB stack about every window.
  • apps/server/src/ws/context.ts:470 The sweep skips archived rows, rows with a null path and rows with checkoutRemovedAt set. A dead row whose parent is gone has none of these, so it is still refreshed. The lifecycle (merge) path uses interval 0 and re-resolves it each time.
  • (local, read-only) ~/.ryco/userdata/state.sqlite projection_worktrees 18 rows have checkout_removal_reason='missing' with timestamps 2026-10-12T15:16:56Z and 19:16:20Z, so the mechanism works. One row is still active and missing: worktree-260e10cc-a5a9-47cb-a2e5-15cd1809fe56 (origin pr, PR #663, in the active project rooted at /Users/laurinfrank/Code/ryco). Its path is .../Dropbox/Code/ryco/.claude/worktrees/marketing-site-motion-redesign-49c526, and .claude/worktrees is a symlink to a deleted ryco.pre-local-migration-20261007-153400 directory.
  • (local) ~/.ryco/userdata/logs/server.log From 2026-10-12T15:16Z to 2026-10-14T20:58Z there are 95 'Source control refresh failed' lines, all for worktree-260e10cc: 83 full stacks of about 2,285 bytes and 12 summaries. That is 197,737 of 422,319 bytes (47%). 78 were triggered by ws.rpc.sourceControl.listChangeRequests and 5 by mergeChangeRequest. In the pre-fix server-child.log.1, the same path accounted for 90 of the measured detectProvider stacks, so it was one of the finding's dead rows.
  • apps/server/src/sourceControl/refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.test.ts:640 The missing-parent test asserts exit._tag === 'Failure', so the noisy path (fail, then log the stack) is the tested behaviour. Nothing tests a dangling-symlink parent.
  • apps/server/src/orchestration/decider.ts:2509 worktree.checkout.remove rejects a second removal unless the new reason is 'deleted'. It also emits worktree.archived when the row is not archived, so a 'missing' record auto-archives the workspace.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:1160 Race: Ryco's own remove-checkout runs git worktree remove, checks, completes the fence, and only then dispatches checkout.remove 'removed' (line 1211). A sweep that lands in that window, with a resolve cache miss, dispatches 'missing' first. The lifecycle's record step then fails and reports 'partial'.
  • apps/server/src/workspace/managedWorktreeMigration.ts:189 Race: relocation runs git worktree move first, then finish(). finish() calls refreshRevision, which throws 'manual recovery is required' if checkoutRemovedAt is set, and then dispatches worktree.relocate. A sweep that sees the source path missing in between records 'missing' and archives the workspace. The relocation then ends in 'attention'. The window is narrow.
Remaining

Dead checkouts whose parent directory is also missing, or whose parent is a dangling symlink, are never recorded (refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:121-132, 176-178). Each sweep re-resolves them (one failed git spawn each) and logs a full Info stack through ignoreCauseLogOnceEvery (ws/context.ts:512, logOnceEvery.ts:99-108). They also stay as live workspaces in the project and sidebar UI. On this install one such row, worktree-260e10cc (one of the rows the finding measured), produced 83 full stacks, 198 KB and 47% of server.log, in about 2.3 days after the fix: roughly 500 stacks or 1.2 MB per 2 weeks. The optional boot-time stat sweep was not added.

Defects in the shipped fix

(1) Narrow races with Ryco's own checkout operations. The missing-recorder does not check the storage lifecycle state (fence 'removing' rows, managed_worktree_relocations moving/moved, creation leases). A sweep that fires between git worktree remove and the lifecycle's checkout.remove 'removed' (WorkspaceLifecycle.ts:1160-1215), or between git worktree move and worktree.relocate (managedWorktreeMigration.ts:189-208), records 'missing' and auto-archives the workspace. The lifecycle then reports 'partial', or the relocation needs manual recovery. (2) recordedMissingCheckouts.add runs before the dispatch (refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts:181-182). A failed dispatch is logged only at Debug and never retried until restart, and later refreshes return null silently, so the row stays live with no signal. (3) The missing-parent test (test.ts:640) asserts a Failure exit, which makes the noisy path the tested contract.

Implementation sketch

A (no decision needed): In refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.ts, replace checkoutMissingOnDisk with a three-way checkoutPresence(cwd) returning 'present' | 'deleted' | 'unavailable'. For 'unavailable' (path and parent missing), return null instead of Effect.fail. Log once per worktree with logOnceEvery({ key: `sourceControl.checkoutUnavailable:${worktreeId}`, level: 'Info', window: Duration.hours(1), fields: { worktreeId, path } }) and no cause. Keep a module-level Map<worktreeId, retryAtMs> (cleared in resetWorktreePullRequestDiscoveryForTests) and check it before registry.resolve, so an unavailable checkout is not re-resolved for about 15 minutes. Optionally run a cheap stat in the ws/context.ts:470 sweep loop as well. B (decision: which missing parents count as deletion): in checkoutPresence, lstat the parent. If it is a symlink whose target is ENOENT, or the nearest existing ancestor is the project workspaceRoot or inside it, or is the Ryco worktrees root (resolveProjectWorktreesDir / config worktrees dir), or has the same st_dev as the project root, return 'deleted'. Return 'unavailable' only when the missing component looks like a mount point (the nearest existing ancestor is '/', '/Volumes', '/mnt' or '/media', or st_dev differs). Optionally confirm with `git worktree list --porcelain` from the project root, which reports the path as prunable. C (races): before dispatching 'missing', take storageLifecycleLock.withPermit, re-stat the path, and skip if hasWorktreeCreationLease(canonical), isWorktreeRelocationBlocked(sql, canonical), or a storage_owned_entries row for the canonical path has state 'removing'. Expose this as a small helper in storage/lifecycle.ts or checkoutFence.ts so the refresh does not need its own SQL. Alternatively, dispatch with a lifecycleGuard/expectedUpdatedAt. D: add to recordedMissingCheckouts only after a successful dispatch (or remove the entry on failure), and log a failed dispatch at Warn through logOnceEvery. Tests in refreshWorktreeSourceControlState.test.ts: (1) a parent that is a dangling symlink inside a temp dir yields exactly one checkout.remove 'missing'; (2) an unmounted-volume path succeeds with no failure exit and no dispatch, and a second run inside the backoff does not call registry.resolve (count resolve calls); (3) with a 'removing' fence row or a blocked relocation there is no dispatch; (4) a failed dispatch is retried on the next run. Update the existing missing-parent test so it no longer expects a Failure exit.

Needs a decision

Part B decides which missing-parent cases count as 'deleted'. Recording 'missing' also auto-archives the workspace (decider.ts:2509), so this is a product trade-off: converge stale rows versus never archiving a checkout on a temporarily unmounted volume. Parts A, C and D (stop the stack and re-probe noise, close the lifecycle and relocation races, retry a failed record) change no semantics and can ship without a decision.

Value low · effort S · risk low

Done#262 AsyncRotatingFileSink opens, writes and closes the file once per record, and records are awaited one by one (12-29x more main-thread time than a held handle)

gap-logging-io:appendfile-per-record · original impact Low, effort M · Blocking I/O

Current state

Confirmed DONE (fixed in 60633eff3, #710). AsyncRotatingFileSink now opens one append-mode FileHandle lazily and keeps it until rotation or close(). Each batch is written with one writev, and rotation splits a batch only at the maxBytes boundary. Overflow-backup pruning probes exact paths instead of reading the directory. EventNdjsonLogger hands each flush to one writeBatch call, records attribution once per batch, and closes writers idle for 2 minutes. TraceSink, serverLogger and the desktop main/backend logs use the same sink and close it on shutdown. I ran a copy of the current sink outside the repo (Node 24.21): 12,345 records of about 330 bytes, written in batches of 50, cost about 0.8 us/record of main-thread time with exactly one open() call. The report measured 52.9 us/record for the old per-record appendFile. Nothing else in production writes logs with per-record appendFile: the sync RotatingFileSink is no longer used, and computerAuditLog's appendFile is a deliberate low-rate audit path. The fix has no regressions; the remaining items are minor and the auditor already listed them.

Evidence
  • packages/shared/src/logging.ts:157 The sink keeps a FileHandle and opens it lazily with fs.promises.open(path, "a") at logging.ts:273. The old per-record fs.promises.appendFile is gone (it was at logging.ts:173-191 in f1be4abc7).
  • packages/shared/src/logging.ts:185 writeBatch serializes a whole batch on writeTail. writeNow (logging.ts:234) appends segments with one handle.writev each (logging.ts:274) and tracks currentSize from the buffer lengths. libuv's write-all loop handles more than IOV_MAX buffers (maxQueueSize is 2048) and short writes.
  • packages/shared/src/logging.ts:290 rotate() closes the handle, waits for any gzip still in flight, shifts the backups and renames the file. The next append reopens it. close() (logging.ts:211) drains the queue and compression, then releases the handle.
  • packages/shared/src/logging.ts:327 pruneOverflowBackups rm's the exact paths maxFiles+1..maxFiles+3, plus their .gz files. readdir is gone. Defaults are unchanged (maxFiles 3), so no older deeper backups are left behind, and the hourly sweepLogDirectory reclaims any stragglers anyway.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:481 flushWriter splices the buffer and makes a single writer.sink.writeBatch(lines) call (line 491). recordResourceAttribution runs once per batch with count=lines.length (line 496). The per-message await loop and the per-line Buffer.byteLength from f1be4abc7:EventNdjsonLogger.ts:246-256 are gone.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/EventNdjsonLogger.ts:556 evictIdleWriters closes writers idle for 2 minutes (DEFAULT_IDLE_WRITER_TTL_MS, line 136) through closeWriter -> sink.close(). A writer that replaces an evicted one waits on the old writer's close (predecessor chain, lines 196, 307, 486-492), so two sinks never rotate the same file at once.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ProviderEventLoggers.ts:199 The shared native and canonical loggers are closed by a layer finalizer. All production drivers pass this shared logger (Drivers/*Driver.ts nativeEventLogger), so production has one sink per file.
  • apps/server/src/observability/TraceSink.ts:152 The trace file joins each batch into one sink.write (one writev on the held handle), attributes once per batch, and closes the sink in closeUnsafe (line 203).
  • apps/server/src/serverLogger.ts:68 The desktop server.log writes one batch per window or per 64 lines on the held handle, and sink.close() runs in the scope finalizer (line 86).
  • apps/desktop/src/main.ts:1846 The desktop main log turns each stdio chunk into one writeBatch, one writev on the held handle. Backend stdout is copied only until ready (backendStartup.ts:236). closeDesktopLogs (main.ts:1498) closes both sinks with a 1 s cap.
  • apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:1896 Minor and confirmed: the Claude and Copilot (CopilotAdapter.ts:69) adapters build their own logger from nativeEventLogPath and never close it. Acp, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode do close theirs. Only tests take this path, since drivers inject the shared logger, and idle eviction (an unref'd timer) frees the handles.
Defects in the shipped fix

No functional defect or regression. Minor leftovers, none worth a follow-up. (1) The fd bound is an idle TTL only (2 min TTL, swept every 60 s, so an fd is held up to about 3 min after the last write), with no hard LRU cap. That costs 2 fds per recently active thread, far below the RLIMIT_NOFILE that Node raises at startup. (2) The Claude and Copilot adapters' nativeEventLogPath fallback (ClaudeAdapter.ts:1896, CopilotAdapter.ts:69) never closes its self-created logger. Only tests take that path. (3) Strings are still copied once per line by Buffer.from (logging.ts:188), as writev requires. (4) A sink created with throwOnError whose initialize() rejects leaves a rejected writeTail that can surface as an unhandled rejection through flush(). This pre-dates the fix (f1be4abc7 had the same initialize/flush code) and needs a mkdir or rm failure in a directory that was just created. (5) A held handle means that when something else unlinks or renames the active file, writes go to the orphaned inode until the next rotation or eviction. The only such actor is the sweep's 512 MB budget pass, which removes the oldest mtimes first, so in practice it never hits an active file.

Value none · effort none · risk none

Method and caveats

  • The 263 findings were parsed from the original report, each with its evidence, proposal, verifier notes and old file:line locations.
  • Per finding, a Sonnet auditor located the current code and classified it (done, partial, not done, obsolete) from the code itself, not from commit messages. An Opus verifier then tried to refute that classification: for "done" it looked for missed callers, unimplemented proposal parts and bugs in the fix; for "partial"/"not done" it searched for implementations the auditor missed. 526 agents, no errors, nothing skipped.
  • Both repos were read-only. Hub code was read from origin/main (the Hub working tree is on an unrelated branch). Nothing was measured live in this pass; gains quoted in findings come from the original research or from the verifiers' reading of the code.
  • The Claude SDK defect (#140/#143) was re-checked by hand in @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.296: yT() takes append only from a preset systemPrompt.
  • "Value" is the verifier's rating of the user-visible benefit of the remaining work now, not the original impact.
